Look for cases where evidence_risk score DISAGREES with mom_20 — i.e., names with high mom_20 but low evidence_risk score (likely distribution candidates). If the component flags these and mom_20 does not, evidence_risk is genuinely adding information beyond ranking.

Test evidence_risk's score autocorrelation and its correlation with forward 4-week MAX DRAWDOWN (not return) — a risk-control component should show stronger correlation with drawdown than with return; a ranking component should show the opposite.

Compare evidence_risk score distribution across bull (SPX > 200DMA and rising) vs bear (SPX < 200DMA and falling) regimes — a risk filter should compress toward 'defensive' in bear regimes; a ranking component should not shift.

Identify a specific PIT-safe alternative risk score (e.g., a published RSI-divergence or distribution-day index) and run a head-to-head counterfactual: equal-breadth baskets, same entry triggers, compare ruin rates. Until this is done, the replacement claim is unsubstantiated.
what_would_change_my_mind: A held-out out-of-sample test (post-discovery period, e.g., 2023-2025 data the researcher did not see) where evidence_risk deciles show NO relationship with forward max drawdown or ruin, while mom_20 deciles DO — this would falsify risk-control and confirm ranking-only behavior.

A Shapley or partial-dependence analysis on the actual B0 composite showing that evidence_risk's contribution to the is_b0_pick decision is statistically indistinguishable from a pure mom_20×vol_ratio_5_20 ranking term — i.e., zero residual predictive content once ranking features are partialled out.

A PIT-safe reconstruction of FN/FW labels (using only information available at the decision date) that reproduces the same asymmetry the researcher found — if the asymmetry disappears, the original finding is a label artifact and the risk-control verdict flips back to 'plausible.'

An empirical demonstration that a specific downside-asymmetric alternative score (must be defined, must be PIT-computable, must show >0.05 AUC improvement over evidence_risk on a held-out ruin prediction task) exists and is deployable — only then does the replacement recommendation earn credibility.

Evidence that evidence_risk score does NOT co-move with realized volatility regime (VIX, sector vol, term-structure shifts) in the direction a risk filter should — i.e., it stays high in vol-expansion environments where prudent risk control should down-weight — would confirm it is not risk-aware.

A Monte Carlo simulation: generate 10,000 synthetic names with known mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and true downside risk, run evidence_risk's score formula on them, and show the score's rank correlation with true downside risk is <0.1 while its rank correlation with momentum is >0.5. Until this is done, the claim that the score 'fails as risk control' is unsubstantiated.

tests.name: vol_x_mom_interaction_signature
tests.comparison: Stratify the 27-case archaeology (and any held-out B0 history that surfaces the same PIT fields) into high-vol quartile (vol_ratio_5_20 >= 75th pct) and low-vol quartile (<= 25th pct). Within each vol quartile, split by mom_20 above/below its own median and compute is_b0_pick rate per cell plus 2x2 OR for high-mom vs low-mom. Compare the high-vol OR to the low-vol OR via interaction contrast: delta_logOR_highvol_minus_lowvol. Repeat with px_vs_ma50 substituted for mom_20 as a robustness check (extension proxy).
tests.success_criterion: delta_logOR > 0 AND high-vol-cell shows materially larger mom_20 gap than low-vol-cell (rank-biserial separation in high-vol stratum >= 0.30 while low-vol stratum <= 0.15). A risk-control component must penalize 'high vol without price confirmation' (distribution-day archetype), so the mom_20 differential should widen inside the high-vol regime; this is the signature of asymmetric risk awareness rather than additive strength ranking.
tests.failure_criterion: delta_logOR approximately 0 (|delta| < 0.20) AND mom_20 gap similar across vol strata (within 0.10 absolute). If vol simply amplifies the mom_20 effect additively, the component is treating vol and mom as co-directional ranking features, not as a diagnostic pair.

tests.name: downside_feature_additivity_beyond_ranking
tests.comparison: Fit two nested logistic regressions of is_b0_pick on the discovery+archaeology sample (entity-disjoint from any deployment period): Model_R (ranking-only) = mom_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 + up_day_ratio_20; Model_RR (ranking + risk) = Model_R + pullback_pct + base_depth_pct + atr_14_pct. Compare via likelihood-ratio chi-square, delta-McFadden-pseudo-R^2, and delta-AUC. Also report standardized coefficients and their signs for the three added downside features. Re-run with pullback_pct and base_depth_pct sign-flipped so deeper drawdowns map to 'higher risk,' to ensure coefficient sign is interpretable.
tests.success_criterion: LRT p < 0.05 AND delta-pseudo-R^2 >= 0.05 AND delta-AUC >= 0.04 AND at least one downside feature carries a coefficient in the predicted risk-direction after sign alignment. Confirms the component encodes independent downside-asymmetric information not redundant with momentum/extension/vol-expansion.
tests.failure_criterion: LRT p >= 0.10 AND delta-pseudo-R^2 < 0.02 AND delta-AUC < 0.02. Downside features are statistically and economically redundant with the ranking block, consistent with the 'ranking dressed as risk' claim.

tests.name: asymmetric_dispersion_compression_selected_vs_rejected
tests.comparison: Construct two z-scored composites within each snapshot to remove snapshot-level drift: DOWN_comp = mean(z(pullback_pct), z(base_depth_pct), z(atr_14_pct)) with sign-flipped so higher = more downside-vulnerable; UP_comp = mean(z(mom_20), z(vol_ratio_5_20), z(up_day_ratio_20)). Compute the cross-sectional dispersion (MAD/median) of DOWN_comp and UP_comp separately within is_b0_pick=true and is_b0_pick=false subsets. Form the ratio DOWN_disp/UP_disp per subset and test whether the ratio differs between selected and rejected (e.g., bootstrap entity-level resamples within snapshot, n=10k).
tests.success_criterion: DOWN/UP dispersion ratio is at least 25% LOWER in the is_b0_pick=true subset than in the is_b0_pick=false subset (with bootstrap CI excluding zero). A genuine risk filter should compress the downside tail of its accept set while leaving upside dispersion freer; ranking would compress both or neither.
tests.failure_criterion: Ratio difference < 10% OR bootstrap CI straddles zero. The selected set shows comparable or greater downside dispersion than the rejected set, indicating symmetric (ranking) rather than asymmetric (risk) gating.

leakage_checks: Confirm none of the features in any test is constructed using post-decision-date information; audit each of pullback_pct, base_depth_pct, atr_14_pct, mom_20, mom_60, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50 against the PIT feature allowlist and reject the test if any derived feature requires a forward window.

Block on snapshot_anon: entity rows sharing a snapshot_anon are not independent; apply snapshot-clustered bootstrap (resample snapshots, not entities) for all inference in tests 1 and 3 to avoid underestimating uncertainty.

Outcome labels (false_positive_ruin, false_negative_*) are defined using forward 4w return thresholds per the method_note; this is look-ahead w.r.t. the decision date and must NOT be used as the response variable in tests 1-3. Use is_b0_pick as the response, and treat outcome_label only as a stratification variable for follow-up subgroup diagnostics, never as a target.

Exclude the hybrid entity_6618d3e80c (false_positive_ruin|selected_winner) from any 'ruin' subgroup analysis and run a sensitivity version of test 3 with it removed to confirm the asymmetric-dispersion result is not driven by a single mixed-label case.

For test 2, verify the downside-feature coefficient signs are economically sensible BEFORE interpreting the magnitude: a positive coefficient on raw pullback_pct paired with selection would mean the component rewards deeper drawdowns, which is the researcher's inverted-pullback observation and must be reconciled rather than averaged away.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: On the available 27-case archaeology, the features that best discriminate selected_winners from false_negatives (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5) are all upside-tilted ranking signals, not downside-asymmetric risk signals; however, the inverted pullback_pct pattern (selected winners come from deeper drawdowns) is consistent with base-quality discrimination, which is itself a documented risk-control heuristic. The dataset is too small and too contaminated by forward-return label construction (per method_note) for either the ranking interpretation or the risk-control interpretation to be falsified. The component's behavior at the SCORE level has never been analyzed (no decile of evidence_risk output, no partial correlation holding score constant, no regime-conditional breakdown). Until those score-level and regime-conditional tests run, the historical value cannot be cleanly attributed to downside-risk control versus return ranking; both mechanisms remain simultaneously plausible, and the answer depends on which analytical lens one privileges (cross-sectional medians favor ranking; base-reset logic favors risk control).
falsifiers: F1 (ranking wins): Reconstruct false-negative labels using only PIT-safe proxies (subsequent base-break confirmation, vol-regime shift, distribution-day accumulation over the next 4w) and rerun the numeric_contrasts; if the ranking-feature deltas persist with std|delta| > 0.7 on at least three of {mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50}, ranking is the dominant mechanism.

F2 (risk-control wins): Compute the actual evidence_risk score for every entity, split into deciles, and show that ruin probability DECREASES across deciles with monotone chi-squared trend p < 0.05 AND that mom_20 within the highest-score decile is uncorrelated or NEGATIVELY correlated with subsequent 4w max-drawdown — proving the score penalizes high-mom high-vulnerability names rather than rewards them.

F3 (regime matters): If evidence_risk's score drifts with VIX or cross-sectional dispersion of returns (rank-correlation |rho| > 0.30), then cross-sectional median comparisons are blind to time-varying risk control and the ranking interpretation is misleading; verdict must be CONTEXT_DEPENDENT on regime.

F4 (component isolation fails): Hold the other B0 sub-components constant (residualize is_b0_pick on all non-evidence_risk component scores) and re-test whether evidence_risk's marginal contribution carries any downside-asymmetric coefficient at all — if not, evidence_risk is redundant with another component and the attribution is moot.

F5 (replacement wins out-of-sample): A downside-specific composite built from lower-shadow frequency, downside-vol ratio, close-to-low ratio, and base-quality deterioration must achieve lower ruin-rate at equal or greater selection breadth on held-out data; failure here means the original component is doing something the cleaner replacement cannot replicate.
actionable_design_principles: Score-level before feature-level: any future attribution of evidence_risk must operate on the actual component output (deciles, partial correlations, Shapley attribution on the score itself), not on the marginal association of constituent features with outcome labels.

Regime-conditioning is non-optional: mandate at least three regime partitions (VIX quartile, cross-sectional dispersion quartile, vol-regime shift flag) before claiming the component is 'ranking-style' — a flat cross-sectional median hides regime-dependent risk control.

Label hygiene is a hard precondition: rebuild false-negative labels with PIT-only diagnostics (subsequent base structure, vol-regime confirmation, distribution-day count) before re-running any asymmetry claim, otherwise every numeric_contrast is circular per the method_note definition.

Component orthogonality audit: compute the partial correlation of evidence_risk's score with downside-asymmetric proxies AFTER residualizing on the ranking features (mom_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20); if |partial-rho| < 0.10, the component carries no independent downside information and the ranking interpretation wins on the orthogonality criterion.

Entry-vs-management separation: ruin attribution must be partitioned between entry signal and exit/stop-loss discipline; an entry component cannot be evaluated for risk control without a fixed position-management layer in the counterfactual.

Minimum sample threshold: no claim about evidence_risk should be made on fewer than ~150 entity-decisions (≈5x the 27-case archaeology) with at least 25 ruin events; current 8-ruin sample cannot support chi-squared or decile-based inference.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: evidence_risk_score_decile_monitor
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Operationalizes the score-level diagnostic the prior roles could not perform; tracks ruin-rate by decile of the actual component output rather than by raw feature medians, which sidesteps the label-contamination attack from the skeptic.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance:: Requires per-entity component-score history (not provided in archaeology) and a snapshot-clustered bootstrap to avoid within-snapshot correlation; enables direct falsifier F2 and resolves CONTEXT_DEPENDENT status if decile-monotonicity holds.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: regime_conditional_evidence_risk_gate
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Adds a regime layer that the cross-sectional analysis ignored per the skeptic's regime-dependence attack; lets the same component be ranking-style in calm regimes and risk-controlling in stressed regimes without forcing a single label.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance:: Needs a regime-classification rule (e.g., VIX 75th-pct threshold over trailing 60d) and snapshot-conditional evaluation; directly tests falsifier F3 and lets the policy be regime-aware without redesigning the component.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: orthogonalized_downside_residual
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Constructs a 'pure risk' signal by regressing any candidate risk score on the ranking block (mom_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20) and using the standardized residual; this is the operationalization of the researcher's orthogonalization recommendation in a way the skeptic cannot dismiss as unverified, because the residual carries no ranking information by construction.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance:: Requires all downside-asymmetric features to be confirmed PIT-available (lower_shadow_freq, close_to_low_ratio derivable from OHLC; distribution_day_count needs an explicit rule); the residual itself is the new component, so any downstream policy that compares B0 to a replacement is comparing apples to apples on the orthogonality axis.

cycles.question: For B0 component 'freshness', determine whether its historical value comes from downside-risk control versus return ranking. State what evidence would falsify the component's claimed role and what a cleaner replacement would look like.

researcher.mechanism_claim: B0 'freshness' is functioning as a recent-momentum RETURN-RANKING signal (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, ma10/20_slope_5 cluster) rather than as a DOWNSIDE-RISK CONTROL. The component distinguishes winners from non-selected names via momentum/thrust, but does not reliably suppress picks that subsequently ruin: high-freshness picks can still produce false_positive_ruin, and the worst false positives show that low-freshness cases were not excluded either.
evidence_for: The three largest standardized deltas separating false_negatives from selected_winners are up_day_ratio_20 (std_delta -1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), and mom_20 (-1.00) — all 'freshness/recency' signals, not drawdown or tail-risk metrics.
px_vs_ma50 (-0.85), ma10_slope_5 (-0.68) and ma20_slope_5 (-0.60) also rank among the top discriminators, consistent with freshness capturing trend acceleration, not risk control.

Selected_winners have a higher up_day_ratio_20 median (0.625) than false_negatives (0.500), but the false_positive_ruin cohort sits between them with high up_day_ratio values (e.g., entity_8f0df3d38e at 0.65, entity_4fdc3699fd at 0.60, entity_3472243e0c at 0.65, entity_55c2da490e at 0.65) — i.e., freshness admitted them and they still ruined.

Drawdown/risk proxies that would indicate downside-risk control (base_depth_pct std_delta +0.19, dist_to_52w_high_pct std_delta +0.16, atr_14_pct std_delta -0.28, rv_20 std_delta -0.21) are among the weakest discriminators, confirming risk control is not where the signal lives.

Volatility-based features (rv_20, atr_14_pct) actually have NEGATIVE standardized deltas — winners tend to be calmer, but the component's contribution is via the momentum cluster, not via penalizing tail risk.
evidence_against: Three of eight false_positive_ruin picks had LOW up_day_ratio (entity_84824e6a20 = 0.40, entity_b6bcccdf6a = 0.40, entity_40ea0cfb3b = 0.50) AND sub-1.0 vol_ratio_5_20 for entity_40ea0cfb3b (0.906) — these are not 'fresh' names, yet they were not filtered out, undermining any claim that freshness is currently a downside gate.

entity_8ad5cd4795 is a selected_winner with NEGATIVE ma10_slope_5 (-0.0059), NEGATIVE ma20_slope_5 (-0.0034), and mom_20 ≈ 0.004 (essentially flat) — a counter-example showing low freshness can still win, weakening any tight risk-control interpretation.
entity_2f86543bf6 won with up_day_ratio=0.35 (the lowest in the dataset) and negative ma20_slope_5, again contradicting a 'freshness filters risk' story.

Two false_negatives (entity_de1c657364, entity_d8e8e7b814) had high up_day_ratio_20 (0.65 and 0.45) and decent momentum but were not picked — so even as a return-ranking signal, freshness is necessary but not sufficient, and is confounded with other B0 inputs.
falsifiable_predictions: Replacing the freshness sub-score with a pure 20-day momentum rank (mom_20 + up_day_ratio_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 z-sum) should produce a Spearman correlation > 0.5 with the current B0 freshness contribution across the holdout — confirming it is effectively already a return-ranking score.

Among B0 picks, the freshness score should show NO significant difference (|rank-sum z| < 1.0) between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner cohorts — falsifying any 'freshness protects against ruin' claim. The visible data already suggests ruin cases include both high and low freshness values, supporting this.

Adding a HARD downside-risk gate (e.g., reject if ma20_slope_5 < 0 AND pullback_pct < -10% OR up_day_ratio_20 < 0.45 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0) should reduce the false_positive_ruin count by ≥ 30% in a frozen holdout while leaving the selected_winner median return statistically unchanged — falsifying the existing freshness-as-gate claim.

If freshness were doing downside-risk control, the false_positive_ruin cohort's freshness z-score should be systematically BELOW the selected_winner cohort's z-score (|mean delta| > 0.5σ). The mixed up_day_ratio distribution (ruins at 0.40, 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65) already makes this unlikely; a holdout test with n ≥ 50 picks will resolve it.
A logistic regression of outcome_label on freshness-only features should yield pseudo-R² > 0.10 (return ranking) but AUC for ruin-vs-win separation should be < 0.55 (no downside gating).
policy_implications: Re-label 'freshness' as 'recency_momentum' and use it exclusively for cross-sectional ranking, not as a risk filter.

Add an explicit, separately weighted downside-risk component — candidates that are PIT-observable and not redundant with momentum: negative ma50_slope_10 with high rv_20, deep negative pullback_pct combined with rising vol_ratio_5_20, or dist_to_52w_high_pct > 0 with deteriorating ma20_slope_5.

Convert the new downside-risk component to a HARD GATE (binary) rather than a soft additive score, so that the 8/27 ruin rate is structurally bounded rather than averaged away by blending with momentum.

Track two KPIs going forward: (i) median W4 return of B0 picks conditional on freshness rank quintile — to confirm ranking value; (ii) ruin-rate conditional on freshness quintile — to confirm or refute the falsifiable predictions above.

Investigate whether the soft-additive blending of freshness with other B0 inputs is what allows low-freshness ruin cases (entity_84824e6a20, entity_b6bcccdf6a, entity_40ea0cfb3b) to pass — i.e., other components may be over-compensating, which is a portfolio-construction artifact separate from the predictive mechanism.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: B0 'freshness' is plausibly a HYBRID recency-of-base + minimum-readiness signal whose downside-risk role is being systematically masked by three structural artifacts in the discovery set: (i) Berkson/collider conditioning — only names that pass B0 can enter the false_positive_ruin cohort, biasing observed ruin-freshness upward; (ii) confounding with other B0 sub-scores that rescue low-freshness names, so 'low-freshness ruins passed' understates any threshold-style gate that freshness enforces pre-selection; and (iii) a forward-looking false-negative definition (future W4 ≥ 8%) that mechanically elevates any contemporaneous feature correlated with subsequent return — including features the modeler intended as risk gates. Until an ablation holds other B0 components fixed, the conclusion that freshness is 'purely' a return-ranking score is not warranted by the evidence shown.

attacks.issue: Berkson/collider bias in the ruin cohort construction
attacks.why_it_matters: False positives are conditional on being a B0 PICK. If freshness has even a weak pre-selection gate (e.g., up_day_ratio < 0.30 → reject), then observed ruins are drawn from a truncated distribution that excludes the very low-freshness cases freshness would have filtered. The researcher observes mixed up_day_ratio values (0.40, 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65) among ruins and concludes 'freshness does not gate ruin' — but those are exactly the values that SURVIVED the gate. To claim freshness is not gating, one must compare ruin rates across freshness values in the full pre-selection universe, not within B0 picks. The 5 false-negative cases are pre-selection and provide the only unconditioned evidence, and the data shows false_negatives have systematically LOWER up_day_ratio_20 (median 0.50 vs 0.625) — which is consistent with a weak floor-style gate, not pure ranking.

attacks.issue: Confounding with other B0 sub-scores invalidates the isolation argument
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher explicitly concedes that 'soft-additive blending of freshness with other B0 inputs' may allow low-freshness ruin cases to pass via compensation from other components. But this concession destroys the inference. If entity_84824e6a20 (up_day_ratio 0.40) and entity_40ea0cfb3b (up_day_ratio 0.50, vol_ratio 0.91) reach B0 selection despite low freshness, it could mean (a) freshness is a soft additive that other components overwhelm, OR (b) freshness has no floor at all. Both are consistent with the data. Without ablating other components, the data cannot distinguish 'freshness is irrelevant' from 'freshness is necessary-but-overridable'. The researcher's policy implication to convert to a hard gate is reasonable — but it is also the very experiment needed to falsify the gate claim, which has not been run.

attacks.issue: Forward-looking false-negative labeling contaminates 'return ranking' inference
attacks.why_it_matters: The method note states false negatives are defined as 'future W4 ≥ 8% and ≥ 5pp above B0 selected median'. Any feature measured at snapshot t that correlates with forward return will appear as a 'ranking' discriminator by construction — regardless of whether it was DESIGNED as a ranking signal or as a risk filter. mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, and slope features are forward-predictive partly because they measure persistent drift. The discovery set cannot distinguish 'freshness predicts return because it is a momentum signal' from 'freshness predicts return because names that are quietly base-completing tend to both be safer and to continue higher'. The latter is a risk-control mechanism that ALSO has ranking value.

attacks.issue: Counterexample entity_2f86543bf6 contradicts BOTH hypotheses and is not addressed
attacks.why_it_matters: This selected_winner has up_day_ratio=0.35 (the dataset minimum), negative ma20_slope_5, near-zero mom_20 (-0.008), and px_vs_ma20 only +0.025. If freshness is pure momentum, why did this name win? The researcher's evidence-against cites it as showing 'low freshness can win' (weakening the risk-control story). But the symmetric problem — 'low freshness can rank highly' — weakens the pure-ranking story equally. The honest reading is that freshness, as currently implemented, is NEITHER a tight gate NOR a tight ranker — which suggests it is overweighted by other B0 components, diluted, or being mis-measured. The researcher's binary framing (ranking XOR gating) is itself suspect.

attacks.issue: base_duration_weeks and base_mbox_count are conspicuously absent from the freshness cluster
attacks.why_it_matters: If 'freshness' truly means recency-of-base — the literal IBD-style concept — then base_duration_weeks (std_delta -0.42, winners 52 vs false_negatives 44) and base_mbox_count (+0.34) are the canonical freshness features. They ARE in the data and DO discriminate. The current freshness sub-score appears to use short-window momentum proxies instead. This suggests either (a) the implementation has drifted from the conceptual role, or (b) the conceptual role was always 'recency-of-base' and the proxies are imperfect. Either way, the claim that 'freshness is functioning as momentum' may be a finding about WHAT IS COMPUTED, not about WHAT WAS INTENDED, and these two should not be conflated.

attacks.issue: The falsifiable predictions do not actually test the gate hypothesis under Berkson conditioning
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher proposes: 'Among B0 picks, freshness should show NO significant difference (|rank-sum z| < 1.0) between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner'. This is the wrong test. Under a floor-gate model, ALL B0 picks are by construction above the floor, so the ruin vs winner comparison within B0 is uninformative about the gate. The right test is ruin rate vs freshness in the PRE-SELECTION universe — and that test requires data not in the failure_archaeology snapshot. The proposed ablation (hard gate reduces ruin by ≥30%) is correct in principle but needs a population that includes rejected names, not just B0 picks.

counterexamples_to_seek: Rejected (non-B0) names with very low freshness (up_day_ratio < 0.35, vol_ratio < 0.9, mom_20 < -0.05) that subsequently would have ruined — these would CONFIRM a gate role that is invisible inside B0.

Rejected (non-B0) names with high freshness (up_day_ratio ≥ 0.65, mom_20 ≥ 0.20) that subsequently would have been large winners — these would FALSIFY a pure ranking role (i.e., freshness is missing real winners when low on other components).

B0 picks with freshness z-score in the top quintile that ruined due to factors orthogonal to freshness (e.g., same-sector cluster ruin on a single date, or a gap-down event unrelated to setup) — these would isolate the portion of ruin that freshness COULD NOT have prevented.
Within the same snapshot, pairs of names matched on all other B0 components but differing on freshness by > 1σ — to estimate freshness's marginal effect on ruin and rank, removing confounding.

B0 picks where base_duration_weeks and freshness-cluster features disagree (e.g., long base, weak recent thrust) — to determine whether the model is using recency-of-base or recent-thrust, and which is the better predictor of outcome.

A held-out period in which market regime shifts (high-vol regime, low-vol regime) — to test whether freshness's relationship to outcome is regime-dependent, which would invalidate any static ranking interpretation.
what_would_change_my_mind: An ablation in which freshness is HELD CONSTANT at its median while other B0 components vary, AND vice versa, across the full pre-selection universe: if ruin-rate-vs-freshness slope is flat pre-selection, I accept the pure-ranking claim; if ruin-rate rises sharply below a freshness threshold, I accept a hybrid gate+ranker model.

A pre-selection logistic regression of ruin on freshness alone showing AUC ≥ 0.65 — this would demonstrate freshness is at minimum a useful gate even if not sufficient for ranking. The researcher's predicted AUC < 0.55 threshold is testable but the data presented does not include the pre-selection sample needed to estimate it.

Replacing the momentum-proxy freshness with base_duration_weeks + base_mbox_count + days_since_last_pivot (true recency-of-base features) and observing whether ruin rate drops and/or hit rate rises in a frozen holdout — if the recency-of-base variant dominates the momentum proxy, the original component was mis-specified and the mechanism claim needs revision toward 'recency-of-base' as the conceptual role.

Demonstrating that within B0 picks, the conditional ruin rate given (freshness ≥ median AND other components below median) is materially different from (freshness < median AND other components above median), controlling for snapshot — would show freshness has independent information and therefore is not merely redundant with momentum.

If the discovery sample is expanded to n ≥ 100 picks with non-overlapping snapshots, and the standardized deltas for risk-control proxies (base_depth_pct, dist_to_52w_high_pct, atr_14_pct) remain at |z| < 0.3 while freshness-cluster deltas remain at |z| > 1.0, I would upgrade the researcher's 'freshness is ranking' claim from plausible to probable.

tests.name: pre_selection_freshness_floor_test
tests.comparison: Pool ALL labeled entities in failure_archaeology (false_positive_ruin + selected_winner + false_negative_*) and run a rank-sum test of the freshness z-sum (z-up_day_ratio_20 + z-vol_ratio_5_20 + z-mom_20) between ruin vs non-ruin cohorts. This is the only test that escapes the Berkson/collider conditioning the researcher identified as fatal — because false_negatives are by construction pre-selection.
tests.success_criterion: Rank-sum z ≤ -1.5 AND AUC(pre-selection ruin vs non-ruin on freshness-only logistic) ≥ 0.60 → freshness is a downside-risk floor/gate pre-selection.
tests.failure_criterion: Rank-sum |z| < 0.5 AND AUC ≤ 0.55 → freshness does NOT separate ruin from non-ruin in the unconditioned universe; pure ranking claim survives.

tests.name: within_B0_freshness_quintile_monotonicity_test
tests.comparison: Restrict to is_b0_pick == true. Bin B0 picks into freshness quintiles. Compute ruin-rate (false_positive_ruin / B0_picks) per quintile. Apply Cochran-Armitage trend test across quintiles. This is the direct test of the researcher's prediction #2.
tests.success_criterion: Monotonically decreasing ruin rate from Q1 to Q5 (trend z ≤ -1.5) → supports floor-gate interpretation even conditional on selection.
tests.failure_criterion: No monotonic trend (|trend z| < 0.8) OR U-shape → falsifies gate claim; only consistent with ranking interpretation OR with no freshness role at all.

tests.name: recency_of_base_vs_momentum_proxy_specification_test
tests.comparison: Build two parallel freshness proxies: (Proxy A) up_day_ratio_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 + mom_20 z-sum (current implementation) vs (Proxy B) base_duration_weeks + base_mbox_count + pullback_pct z-sum (literal recency-of-base). Compute pseudo-R² of a logistic regression on outcome_label ∈ {false_positive_ruin, selected_winner} for each proxy. This directly resolves the skeptic's attack #5 (whether the conceptual role is 'recency-of-base' or 'recent-thrust' and which is the mis-specified one).
tests.success_criterion: Proxy B pseudo-R² exceeds Proxy A by ≥ 0.02 absolute → original freshness was mis-specified as momentum when conceptual role is recency-of-base; cleaner replacement is Proxy B.
tests.failure_criterion: Proxy A pseudo-R² ≥ Proxy B → current specification is correctly aligned with intent; no spec revision needed.

tests.name: matched_pair_freshness_marginal_effect_test
tests.comparison: Within snapshots, find pairs of entities matched on the NON-freshness B0 inputs (px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, ma20_slope_5 within ±0.01) but differing on freshness z-sum by ≥ 1σ. Compare ruin/winner rates between the high-freshness and low-freshness member of each pair. This isolates freshness from confounding by other B0 components (skeptic's attack #2).
tests.success_criterion: McNemar odds ratio ≥ 2.0 in favor of high-freshness avoiding ruin → freshness has independent information beyond other components.
tests.failure_criterion: McNemar |OR-1| < 0.5 OR p > 0.3 → freshness is redundant; its observed effect is fully mediated by other B0 inputs.

tests.name: drawdown_proxy_risk_control_discrimination_test
tests.comparison: Compute AUC of a logistic regression using ONLY downside-risk proxies (base_depth_pct, dist_to_52w_high_pct, atr_14_pct) to separate ruin from winner. Then add the freshness z-sum and check whether AUC rises significantly (DeLong test). This separates the 'freshness as risk control' claim from 'freshness as ranking' claim — if risk proxies alone do most of the work, freshness adds little as a gate.
tests.success_criterion: AUC(risk-only) ≥ 0.65 AND adding freshness raises AUC by < 0.03 → risk proxies already do the gating; freshness is NOT the mechanism of downside control.
tests.failure_criterion: AUC(risk-only) < 0.55 AND freshness addition raises AUC by ≥ 0.08 → freshness IS contributing to downside-risk separation, consistent with gate role.

leakage_checks: Verify each feature name resolves to a PIT-observable at snapshot t: confirm up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, ma10/20_slope_5, ma50_slope_10, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, base_depth_pct, atr_14_pct, dist_to_52w_high_pct, ibd_entry_* all use only data available at or before the snapshot timestamp. Reject any test that requires post-snapshot data.

Confirm snapshot_anon and entity_anon are the only join keys — no calendar date, no ticker, no industry classification should be used as a feature or stratification variable. If regime stratification is attempted, use rv_20 or atr_14_pct at snapshot t as the regime proxy, not date.
For matched-pair test (test 4): enforce that pair members come from the SAME snapshot_anon to avoid cross-regime confounding masquerading as freshness effect. Pairs crossing snapshots are rejected.

Confirm no feature in any test is a transformation that uses the outcome label (e.g., 'rank among winners' is forbidden). The labels false_positive_ruin, selected_winner, false_negative_relative may appear ONLY on the LHS, never on the RHS.

For test 3 (specification comparison): verify that base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, pullback_pct are measured at the SAME snapshot t as up_day_ratio_20 / vol_ratio_5_20 / mom_20 — otherwise the comparison conflates measurement timing with mechanism.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The B0 'freshness' component, AS IMPLEMENTED (up_day_ratio_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 + mom_20 cluster with ma10/20_slope_5 satellites), is empirically most consistent with a recent-momentum RETURN-RANKING signal. The three strongest false-negative-vs-winner standardized deltas (-1.19σ, -1.05σ, -1.00σ) all sit inside this cluster, while true downside-risk proxies (base_depth_pct, dist_to_52w_high_pct, atr_14_pct, rv_20) cluster near zero standardized delta (+0.19σ to -0.28σ). Within the observed B0-pick set, false_positive_ruin cases span nearly the entire freshness distribution (up_day_ratio from 0.40 to 0.65), providing no evidence of a floor-style downside gate. However, this verdict is bounded by two structural limits of the data — (1) the B0-conditioning (Berkson truncation) hides any pre-selection floor effect because we never observe the rejected tail, and (2) base_duration_weeks and base_mbox_count are absent from the current implementation despite being the literal IBD-style freshness features. The skeptic's attack #5 is load-bearing: 'freshness' as a label implies recency-of-base, but the implementation measures recent-thrust. These are not the same construct and should not be conflated. The data permits — but does not prove — three concurrent readings: (a) freshness is a ranking score and admits ruin cases by design, (b) a weak soft floor exists but is masked by intra-B0 selection overlap with other components, (c) the conceptual role (recency-of-base) was never operationalized correctly. The verdict is CONTEXT_DEPENDENT because freshness's historical value depends on whether one interprets 'freshness' as intent (recency-of-base) or as effect (momentum ranking), and the two are not interchangeable.
falsifiers: FALSIFIER-1 (gate falsified): Pre-selection cohort analysis. Pool all names evaluated at snapshot t (selected AND rejected). If up_day_ratio_20 quintile Q1 (lowest) shows ruin rate statistically indistinguishable from Q4-Q5 within a frozen holdout (rank-sum |z| < 1.0 AND ruin-rate delta < 2pp), then any downside-floor claim is REFUTED. Conversely, if Q1 ruin rate exceeds Q5 by ≥10pp with rank-sum z ≤ -2.0, the floor-gate reading is SUPPORTED — but this test cannot be run on the current evidence because rejected names are not in failure_archaeology.

FALSIFIER-2 (ranking confirmed): If a frozen holdout shows that pure 20-day momentum rank (mom_20 + up_day_ratio_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 z-sum) yields Spearman > 0.5 with the current B0 freshness contribution AND that B0-pick freshness quintile Q5 produces median W4 return exceeding Q1 by >3pp with rank-sum z ≤ -1.5, the return-ranking interpretation is the dominant mechanism.

FALSIFIER-3 (specification mis-aligned): If base_duration_weeks + base_mbox_count + pullback_pct + pullback_duration_weeks z-sum (Proxy B in the designer's test 3) exceeds the current momentum z-sum (Proxy A) by ≥0.02 absolute pseudo-R² in a logistic on outcome_label, the current freshness is mis-specified — the conceptual role was recency-of-base and the implementation is a wrong proxy.

FALSIFIER-4 (matched-pair independence): Within snapshots, pairs matched on non-freshness B0 inputs (px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, ma20_slope_5 within ±0.01) but differing on freshness z-sum by ≥1σ must show McNemar odds ratio ≥2.0 favoring high-freshness avoiding ruin. If |OR-1| < 0.5 OR p > 0.3, freshness is redundant with other B0 components and its observed effect is confounded.

FALSIFIER-5 (hard gate impact): A hard gate (reject if up_day_ratio_20 < 0.40 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0 OR ma20_slope_5 < 0 AND pullback_pct < -10%) applied to the B0-candidate pool must reduce false_positive_ruin count by ≥30% with non-inferiority on selected_winner median W4 return. If reduction is <10%, no gate mechanism is operating and the component has no downside-control effect, regardless of intent.

FALSIFIER-6 (anomaly resolution): entity_2f86543bf6 (up_day_ratio=0.35, ma20_slope_5<0, mom_20≈-0.008, w4=large_win) and entity_8ad5cd4795 (negative slopes, near-zero mom, large_win) jointly disprove ANY strict version of the freshness claim — whether ranking or gating. They are visible in the discovery set. Their existence alone caps the verdict at CONTEXT_DEPENDENT, not SUPPORTED.
actionable_design_principles: PRINCIPLE-1 (orthogonal decomposition): Decouple three distinct mechanisms that the current single 'freshness' label conflates: (a) recency-of-base (literal freshness — base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks), (b) recent-thrust (ranking proxy — up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, ma10/20_slope_5), (c) downside-risk control (gate — composite of deteriorating slopes + deep pullback + high rv_20). Each must be tested independently because the data cannot refute them jointly.

PRINCIPLE-2 (rank vs gate asymmetry): Ranking signals should remain soft-additive and continuous; downside-risk control should be a HARD BINARY gate, not a continuous contribution. The current architecture blends them, which is the structural reason ruin cases with adequate freshness (entity_8f0df3d38e up_day=0.65) and ruin cases with inadequate freshness (entity_84824e6a20 up_day=0.40) both pass — the blending admits both, but only the latter should have been filtered.

PRINCIPLE-3 (snapshot-matched attribution): Every diagnostic must condition on snapshot_anon. Cross-snapshot averaging is the hidden confound behind why 'freshness correlates with winners' — it may be partly a regime effect. Within-snapshot matched pairs (skeptic's attack #2, designer's test 4) are the only causal-identifying design available with this evidence base.

PRINCIPLE-4 (pre-selection visibility requirement): The next research cycle MUST include the rejected-name universe, not only B0 picks. Until then, the floor-gate claim is structurally unfalsifiable from discovery data alone. A negative result on the pre-selection test would itself be informative — proving 'freshness has no gate whatsoever' rather than the current ambiguous 'we cannot see the gate from inside B0'.

PRINCIPLE-5 (PIT-only feature audit): All four candidate downside-risk features (base_depth_pct, dist_to_52w_high_pct, atr_14_pct, rv_20) are PIT-observable at snapshot t, confirming the gate can be constructed without forward leakage. Their current low discrimination (+0.19σ to -0.28σ) is therefore a real empirical finding, not a measurement artifact.

PRINCIPLE-6 (KPI bifurcation): Forward monitoring should report TWO separate metrics per B0 pick: (i) ranking value — quintile of freshness score vs cross-sectional median W4 return; (ii) gating value — ruin rate within the freshness quintile. A component that does (i) but not (ii) is correctly a ranking signal; a component that does (ii) but not (i) is a risk filter; the current freshness does neither cleanly, which is the failure mode.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: recency_momentum_score (soft-additive ranking)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Replaces the ambiguous 'freshness' label with its empirically dominant mechanism — recent-momentum ranking. Lives in the cross-sectional ranking axis, explicitly NOT a risk control. This makes the false_positive_ruin cases with high recent_momentum (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c) honest outcomes rather than failures of a filter that was never meant to filter.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: HIGH — directly maps to the three strongest false-negative-vs-winner standardized deltas (-1.19σ, -1.05σ, -1.00σ). Empirically the strongest return-prediction signal in the current B0 cluster. Re-uses already-computed features with no new data dependency.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: downside_risk_gate (hard binary filter)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Adds an explicit, separately weighted gate that the current 'freshness' label silently promised but did not deliver. Hard-binary prevents the soft-additive blending problem the researcher flagged (entity_84824e6a20 / entity_40ea0cfb3b passing due to other-component compensation). Lives on the risk-control axis, orthogonal to the ranking axis.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: MEDIUM-HIGH — all four features are PIT-observable and already in the data. Their current weak individual discrimination (+0.19σ to -0.28σ) suggests a composite OR-style threshold will be needed rather than a sum; this is consistent with the gate being a logical OR over distress signals, not a continuous contribution.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: recency_of_base_score (soft-additive, IBD-style freshness semantic)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Resurrects the literal IBD-style 'freshness' meaning the component name implies but the implementation does not measure. base_duration_weeks and base_mbox_count are the canonical features and they ARE in the data with non-trivial discrimination (std_delta -0.42 and +0.34 respectively on base_duration/base_mbox). Without this third axis, the original conceptual role is permanently lost.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: MEDIUM — features exist but base_duration has missing values for several B0 picks (pullback_duration_weeks null in 6/27 cases), so the score requires an imputation or fallback rule. Lower capacity than the other two ideas because of the missingness pattern, but higher semantic fidelity to the original label.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: freshness_quintile_ruin_KPI (diagnostic, not predictive)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Forward-monitoring rule rather than a model component. Tracks ruin rate per freshness quintile stratified by snapshot_anon, exposing whether the historical within-B0 evidence generalizes or is an artifact of the discovery sample. Does not enter the model — its job is to falsify or support the historical claim going forward.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: HIGH for falsification, LOW for prediction. This is the operationalization of PRINCIPLE-6 — the only diagnostic that directly tests whether the current 'freshness' component continues to do either ranking or gating, and which.

cycles.question: For B0 component 'eps_preference', determine whether its historical value comes from downside-risk control versus return ranking. State what evidence would falsify the component's claimed role and what a cleaner replacement would look like.

researcher.mechanism_claim: eps_preference derives its historical lift not from a true earnings-quality screen that suppresses tail losses, but from acting as a proxy for confirmed momentum/leadership (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50) at IBD-style breakout entries. Its B0 value is therefore primarily return-ranking rather than downside-risk control.
evidence_for: Selected winners vs false negatives separate most cleanly on up_day_ratio_20 (+0.125 median, std −1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (+0.245, std −1.05), mom_20 (+0.105, std −1.00), and px_vs_ma50 (+0.071, std −0.85) — all features that empirically co-load with sustained EPS revisions/upgrades in growth-tilt universes, so an eps_preference flag will mechanically select higher-momentum names without measuring EPS directly.

The same winners show deeper, longer pre-breakout pullbacks (pullback_pct −15.9% vs −7.3%, pullback_duration 5.5w vs 4.0w). A stock that has already survived a −15% correction with EPS revisions intact is exactly what 'eps_preference' would tag — the lift comes from having endured a drawdown, i.e., it is a return-ranking selector over already-conditioned bases.

Higher winners' vol_ratio_5_20 (1.42 vs 1.18) and px_vs_ma50 (+12.7% vs +5.6%) mean the eps_preferred cohort is structurally more extended and more volatile entering the trade — the opposite of what a pure risk-control filter would do.
Replicated IBD pullback-base winners require RS-line leadership and accelerating earnings; if eps_preference is highly correlated with RS, it is essentially a momentum filter wearing EPS clothing.
evidence_against: Eight of 27 cases are false_positive_ruin where B0 picked the name; several (e.g., entity_8f0df3d38e mom_20=0.176, up_day_ratio=0.65; entity_4fdc3699fd mom_20=0.185; entity_3472243e0c mom_20=0.242; entity_b6bcccdf6a mom_20=0.176) all carry the same high-momentum / high-up-day signature that eps_preference would lock in — yet they end in ruin. If eps_preference were truly risk-controlling it should veto or downgrade these, which it did not.

entity_40ea0cfb3b and entity_55c2da490e ruined with modest mom_20 (0.024, 0.036) and benign pullback signatures — these look like the kind of names a 'quality earnings' screen should flag safe, yet B0 still selected them and they failed. This contradicts any downside-risk-control interpretation.

false_negative_relative cases (entity_df5478102d mom_20=0.125, entity_d8e8e7b814 mom_20=0.106) had reasonable momentum and were rejected by B0. If eps_preference were the deciding filter, these should have passed — implying eps_preference is being applied with thresholds that reject some winners, consistent with a ranking score rather than a binary risk gate.

entity_6618d3e80c carries both 'false_positive_ruin' and 'selected_winner' labels — the same snapshot-time signal can simultaneously be a pick-quality hit and a tail-loss; this duality is incompatible with a monotonic downside-risk story.

No direct EPS, EPS revision, or earnings-surprise fields appear in the archaeology — the only way eps_preference can drive the observed splits is via correlated price/volume proxies, which by construction is ranking, not risk control.
falsifiable_predictions: If eps_preference is a downside-risk gate: restricting the B0 universe to names with positive eps_preference should reduce the ruin rate (false_positive_ruin share) without materially changing the median W4 return of survivors. Test: compare ruin_rate_with_eps_pref vs ruin_rate_without_eps_pref in the same IBD-pullback cohort; if ruin_rate_with ≥ ruin_rate_without (or differs by <1pp), the risk-control hypothesis is falsified.

If eps_preference is a return-ranking proxy: a regression of W4 return on eps_preference_score conditioned on mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 should show eps_preference's coefficient shrink to ≤0 and become insignificant once the proxy features are partialed out. Test: run W4_return ~ eps_pref + mom_20 + up_day + vol_ratio_5_20 + px_vs_ma50; eps_pref β → 0 falsifies the ranking-proxy claim.

Within the 'is_b0_pick=true' group, ruin cases should NOT have measurably lower eps_preference_score than selected winners; a Mann–Whitney U on eps_pref between ruin vs winner within B0 picks should yield p>0.20 (no separation). A clear separation (p<0.05) would instead support downside-risk-control.

Out-of-sample: in a period where broad EPS revisions turn negative, if eps_preference remains bullish and the ruin rate of its picks rises above the unconditional ruin rate by >3pp, the ranking-proxy interpretation is supported (the signal is not self-protective in regime stress).

Replacing eps_preference with a directly observed earnings-revision breadth score (e.g., % of analysts raising next-quarter EPS over the trailing 8 weeks) and re-running B0 should produce no degradation in selected_winner share > 2pp AND a ruin-rate reduction > 2pp — failure of either half falsifies the replacement as 'cleaner'.

If eps_preference is rank, not risk: the false_negative_relative set should contain names whose eps_pref scores are distributed similarly to (not lower than) the false_positive_ruin set; a Kolmogorov–Smirnov D<0.25 supports rank-only, D>0.45 supports a risk gate that was misapplied.
policy_implications: Stop treating eps_preference as a risk-management lever in B0; doing so creates a false sense of downside defense that the archaeology directly contradicts (ruin cases carry the same momentum signature as winners).

Refactor B0 so the eps component is either (a) replaced by an explicit, PIT-observable earnings-revision breadth / EPS-surprise persistence factor with documented monotone mapping, or (b) demoted to a tie-breaker / secondary weight rather than a gate. This avoids double-counting with mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, and px_vs_ma50, which already carry the same information.

Add an explicit ruin-suppression layer keyed to features that DO separate ruin from winners in this archaeology — the variables where ruin cases diverge from winners (notably low up_day_ratio_20 with positive mom_20, and high px_vs_ma50 combined with high vol_ratio_5_20) are candidates for a true downside filter, not eps_preference.

Track contribution attribution: if removing eps_preference changes the W4-return distribution of B0 picks by <0.5pp median and ruin rate by <1pp, the component is redundant under the proxy interpretation and should be retired to reduce model complexity and overfitting risk.

Implement a cohort-level monitor where eps_preference score deciles are plotted against rolling 4-week max drawdown; if top decile drawdowns are NOT lower than bottom decile drawdowns, escalate to the falsification trigger above and schedule component replacement.

For portfolio construction (separate from predictive mechanism): if eps_preference is purely rank, a small long-short overlay on the eps_preference residual after neutralizing momentum adds no expected alpha; cap exposure to eps_preference-driven tilts accordingly.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The prior conclusion commits an observational-equivalence fallacy: the failure-archaeology sample (n=27, doubly-conditioned on IBD-pullback qualification AND B0 evaluation) is consistent with at least three incompatible mechanisms — (a) eps_preference as a momentum/leadership proxy, (b) eps_preference as a residual earnings-quality filter whose protective effect operated UPSTREAM of IBD screening and is therefore invisible inside this window, and (c) eps_preference as a vestigial feature whose historical lift came entirely from co-loaded variables. The cited evidence does not discriminate between these, and the 'ranking proxy' interpretation is not uniquely supported. The cleaner replacement is not 'swap eps_preference for an EPS-revision factor' but to (i) run a full ablation in an UNCONDITIONED universe, (ii) measure eps_preference against ground-truth EPS revisions at the same snapshot timestamps, and (iii) only then decide whether the slot earns its keep.

attacks.issue: Wrong reference comparison: the numeric_contrasts table contrasts selected_winner medians against false_negative_relative medians, but the relevant test of 'downside-risk control' is whether eps_preference separates false_positive_ruin from selected_winner within is_b0_pick=true cases. The researcher never runs that contrast.
attacks.why_it_matters: If eps_preference IS risk-controlling, the cleanest signature should appear as: ruin cases having lower eps_preference than winner cases within the same B0-pick cohort. By tabulating the wrong contrast, the paper dodges the single most decisive comparison available in the data.

attacks.issue: IBD-pullback conditioning creates an upstream-filter blindness: every name in the archaeology has already passed IBD's own earnings/RS-quality gate. Any downside-protection eps_preference contributes by being even MORE selective than IBD is invisible inside this sample, because those names were excluded before they could become 'false_positive_ruin' candidates.
attacks.why_it_matters: This is a classic Berkson's-selection bias. The 50% ruin rate among B0 picks (8 ruins / 16 picks in the visible sample) is high, but the CONDITIONAL ruin rate given B0 selection is not the same as the MARGINAL effect of eps_preference. To estimate the latter one needs names that B0 evaluated and rejected BECAUSE of low eps_preference, plus their downstream outcomes — neither of which the archaeology provides.

attacks.issue: Post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD) is a confound that flips the researcher's 'momentum proxy' argument: mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, and elevated vol_ratio_5_20 in the post-event window are precisely the signatures a stock leaves AFTER a confirmed earnings beat. Loading on these features is therefore COMPATIBLE with eps_preference measuring earnings revisions, not contradictory.
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher treats co-loading on mom/up_day_ratio as proof eps_preference is not measuring earnings, but the empirical literature shows these features are themselves downstream consequences of earnings surprises. The correlation is consistent with eps_preference capturing the right thing via correlated proxies — exactly the situation that calls for an ablation test, not a mechanism claim.

attacks.issue: Sample structure is non-iid and small: 27 cases drawn from a handful of snapshots (snap_d0d57b1e40 alone accounts for 6 cases, snap_71486ed83c accounts for 6), and a single dual-labeled case (entity_6618d3e80c) carries 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner', demonstrating that the win/ruin dichotomy is unstable for any individual name. Standardized deltas computed on n=5 vs n=11 medians are not reliable enough to anchor a mechanism claim.
attacks.why_it_matters: Statistical inference on rank differences across two tiny, snapshot-clustered samples can yield 'separations' that vanish under bootstrap or under a leave-one-snapshot-out jackknife. The paper's mechanism claim rides on these separations.

attacks.issue: The 'deeper, longer pre-breakout pullback' finding is misframed: the researcher calls survivor-of-drawdown evidence of ranking, but 'the company demonstrated earnings resilience through a 15% correction' IS the canonical earnings-quality / downside-resilience story. The same observation is being used to support opposite mechanisms depending on which label you slap on it.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the observation supports both 'ranking proxy' and 'earnings resilience', it supports neither uniquely. Citing it as evidence for the ranking interpretation only is selection-of-evidence.

attacks.issue: The policy implication 'replace eps_preference with raw earnings-revision breadth' is unsupported: the falsifiable_prediction #5 requires BOTH no degradation in selected_winner share AND >2pp ruin-rate reduction. Failure of EITHER half is supposed to falsify the replacement — but if eps_preference is a momentum proxy (as the researcher claims), the replacement should clearly IMPROVE winners (since it would add real information), making the conjunctive falsifier internally inconsistent with the paper's own mechanism claim.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the paper's claim is right, the conjunctive test should pass on both halves. Constructing a test that can only fail if BOTH halves fail is the wrong design — it should be two independent tests, each capable of falsifying the mechanism on its own.

counterexamples_to_seek: Same-snapshot names with HIGH eps_preference score but located OUTSIDE any IBD-pullback base: if they still cluster with high mom_20 / up_day_ratio_20, the ranking-proxy claim holds; if they do NOT, eps_preference was being driven by the pullback base, not by an independent earnings signal.

Cases within the archaeology where eps_preference is LOW (whatever that means in the data) but the name is a selected_winner: 3 such cases would make the risk-control interpretation untenable and shift weight toward ranking.

Snapshots where the broader EPS-revision breadth for the sector was NEGATIVE: if eps_preference stayed BULLISH in those snapshots and ruin rates spiked, ranking-proxy is supported; if eps_preference correctly turned defensive, the residual-filter interpretation is supported.

B0-rejected (is_b0_pick=false) names with HIGH eps_preference that went on to large_win (entity_05b4c6b1f7, entity_de1c657364 are candidates): if eps_preference was a real risk gate it should have been lower on these, not higher. Document its actual score distribution for this subset.

Cross-sectional check within a single snapshot (e.g., snap_d0d57b1e40, n=6): compute rank correlation between eps_preference and mom_20 within the snapshot. If Spearman rho > 0.6 across names that share macro conditions, eps_preference is at minimum redundant; if rho < 0.3, it carries independent information and the 'pure proxy' claim is weak.

A pre-snapshot earnings-event audit: for each entity, identify whether the trailing 8 weeks contained an EPS release. If 80%+ of high-eps_preference picks had a recent print, the signal is mechanically capturing earnings events — supporting eps_preference, not undermining it.
what_would_change_my_mind: Direct ground-truth: matched PIT EPS-revision-breadth data (e.g., % analysts raising next-Q EPS over trailing 8 weeks) at the same snapshot timestamps as the archaeology. If the rank correlation between eps_preference and this measured variable is < 0.25 across names, eps_preference is NOT capturing earnings and the proxy interpretation stands. If ≥ 0.6, the prior paper's claim is wrong.

Unconditioned ablation: rerun B0 in a universe that includes non-IBD-pullback candidates, then ablate eps_preference. If removing eps_preference changes W4 return of B0 picks by < 0.5pp median AND ruin rate by < 1pp, eps_preference is redundant (consistent with the paper's claim). If ruin rate rises > 2pp, eps_preference was risk-controlling and the prior paper's mechanism claim is falsified.

Within-B0-pick Mann-Whitney on eps_preference score between ruin and winner cases, run with leave-one-snapshot-out jackknife: if separation persists across all jackknife folds (p < 0.05), downside-risk-control interpretation is supported; if it disappears under any fold, the separation was driven by one snapshot's regime, not by eps_preference.

Regime test: split the discovery sample into 'broad EPS revisions positive' vs 'broad EPS revisions negative' subperiods. If eps_preference's lift is concentrated in the negative-revisions regime, it is risk-controlling; if it is uniform or stronger in positive-revisions, it is ranking.

Replacement test, two INDEPENDENT halves (not conjunctive): (a) does the EPS-revision-breadth replacement improve ruin rate by > 2pp? (b) does it preserve selected_winner share within 2pp? Either half failing independently is grounds for rejecting the prior mechanism claim or the replacement, without requiring both to fail simultaneously.

tests.name: Within-B0-pick ruin-vs-winner quadrant monotonicity test
tests.comparison: Restrict to is_b0_pick=true cases (n=16 in archaeology). Compute a composite proxy_score = z(mom_20) + z(up_day_ratio_20) + z(vol_ratio_5_20) per case. Stratify into quartiles of proxy_score. Compute ruin_rate and median w4 outcome-rank per quartile. Also compute Spearman(proxy_score, ruin_indicator) within this subset, with snapshot-blocked permutation p-value.
tests.success_criterion: Downside-risk-control interpretation supported if: (a) ruin_rate decreases monotonically across proxy_score quartiles with top-vs-bottom quartile drop >=25pp, AND (b) Spearman(proxy_score, ruin) <= -0.30 with snapshot-blocked p < 0.15. A clear monotone protection signature within already-selected names is what risk-control would predict.
tests.failure_criterion: Ranking-proxy interpretation supported if: ruin_rate varies by <10pp across proxy_score quartiles OR Spearman(proxy_score, ruin) > -0.10 with snapshot-blocked p > 0.30. Equal ruin exposure across the proxy signature within B0 picks means eps_preference did not protect the names it scored highest.

tests.name: Synthetic-reconstruction redundancy test under 3-slot budget
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot with >=4 cases, regress the eps_preference proxy signal on the 3 candidate slot features. Compute per-snapshot adjusted R^2 and the per-name reconstruction residual. Aggregate across snapshots using snapshot-weighted means. Separately, replace eps_preference in B0 composite with the 3-feature linear reconstruction and recompute the B0 rank ordering; measure Spearman rank correlation between original and reconstructed B0 ranks.
tests.success_criterion: Ranking-proxy/redundancy interpretation supported if median per-snapshot adjusted R^2 > 0.75 AND Spearman(original B0 rank, reconstructed B0 rank) > 0.85. eps_preference is then a near-deterministic repackaging of 3 slot features and earns no independent slot.
tests.failure_criterion: Risk-control / independent information supported if median per-snapshot adjusted R^2 < 0.50 OR Spearman rank correlation < 0.55. A reconstruction that fails to reproduce B0 ordering proves eps_preference carries information outside the 3-slot proxy budget.

tests.name: Berkson-conditioning independence test via base-feature stratification
tests.comparison: Partition the 27 cases into subset P = {cases with documented pullback base (non-null pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks)} and subset N = {cases with null pullback features, i.e., no pullback base documented}. For each subset compute Spearman(eps_proxy_score, outcome_rank) and the proxy-score distribution of selected_winners vs false_positive_ruin. If the eps_preference lift is concentrated in only one subset, Berkson-style upstream filtering is the operative mechanism.
tests.success_criterion: Independent mechanism supported if |Spearman(proxy, outcome_rank)_P - Spearman(proxy, outcome_rank)_N| < 0.15 AND KS distance between selected_winner proxy distributions across P and N < 0.30. Survival of the signal across both conditioning states rules out Berkson bias.
tests.failure_criterion: Berkson/upstream-filter mechanism supported if Spearman(proxy, outcome_rank) differs by >0.40 across subsets, OR the lift vanishes entirely in one subset. eps_preference then operated upstream of IBD-pullback qualification and its in-sample signature is selection-artifact.

leakage_checks: Verify every feature used is PIT-observable at snapshot_anon timestamp: explicitly exclude w4_return_bucket, any forward return, any analyst revision dated after snapshot, and any post-snapshot earnings print from the feature lists.
All inference must use snapshot-blocked resampling (block-bootstrap over snapshot_anon, never case-level bootstrap) to prevent within-snapshot correlation from inflating significance.

Dual-labeled cases (entity_6618d3e80c carries both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner) must be analyzed under two protocols - (i) duplicate the row per label and (ii) drop entirely - and the mechanism claim is robust only if both protocols agree; otherwise flag UNRESOLVED.

Pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks have null values in ~14 of 27 cases; analyses using these must report results under (a) complete-case, (b) null-as-distinct-category, and (c) multiple-imputation, with the mechanism claim valid only if all three agree.
No use of entity_anon, snapshot_anon, pullback-pattern-shape text, or any other ID/calendar field as a predictive feature.

The 3-slot budget must be respected: no test may incorporate a 4th candidate feature into the proxy signal even if it appears more diagnostic in archaeology, because the point of the test is to determine whether eps_preference earns its slot against the 3-feature alternative.

Sensitivity check: rerun each test after removing the snapshot with the single highest ruin count (snap_d0d57b1e40 or snap_71486ed83c) to verify that no single snapshot's regime drives the conclusion.
priority_order: Berkson-conditioning independence test via base-feature stratification

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The archaeology shows eps_preference is failing as a downside-risk gate in its current deployment: 8 of 16 B0-picks ended in ruin (50%), and the ruin cases carry the same high-mom_20 / high-up_day_ratio_20 / elevated-vol_ratio_5_20 signature as the 11 selected winners. This is incompatible with eps_preference acting as a monotone tail-loss suppressor. However, the data cannot cleanly adjudicate the researcher's claim that eps_preference is therefore 'purely' a return-ranking proxy, because Berkson-style upstream filtering means we never observe the names eps_preference (or the B0 gate it sits behind) rejected outright. The visible B0 cohort is a doubly-conditioned slice — IBD pullback qualification AND the eps_preference threshold — so the rank-correlation of eps_preference with mom_20 / up_day_ratio_20 is consistent with BOTH (a) eps_preference being a momentum repackaging and (b) eps_preference measuring earnings-revision persistence via features that themselves drift on earnings news (PEAD-confounded). The Skeptic's dual-labeling critique (entity_6618d3e80c being simultaneously ruin and winner) further destabilizes the binary outcome framing the whole argument rests on. Net: eps_preference is operationally broken as risk control; its historical value likely derives mostly from momentum/RS leadership co-loading, but the marginal-vs-rejected comparison needed to certify that is unavailable in this archaeology.
falsifiers: Within-B0-pick ruin-vs-winner Mann-Whitney on eps_preference proxy score (using mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20 as the proxy as per the experimental designer's test 1): if ruin and winner B0 picks are statistically indistinguishable on the proxy (p > 0.30, |rank-diff| < 0.10), the risk-control interpretation is falsified. This is the single decisive test the researcher did NOT run.

Synthetic-reconstruction under a strict 3-slot budget (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20): if Spearman(original B0 rank, reconstructed B0 rank) > 0.85 and median per-snapshot adjusted R^2 > 0.75, eps_preference is informationally redundant with the proxy trio and earns no independent slot.

Berkson-conditioning test: restrict to cases with documented pullback base (subset P) vs null-pullback cases (subset N) and recompute Spearman(proxy, outcome_rank). If |rho_P - rho_N| > 0.40, the lift is selection-artifact and eps_preference acted upstream of IBD base qualification rather than as an independent risk filter.

Cross-regime test on sector EPS-revision breadth: in snapshots where the broader EPS-revision breadth was negative, if eps_preference's high-score cohort STILL shows 50%+ ruin rate while low-score names did no worse, the risk-control claim is falsified. If eps_preference correctly turned defensive and ruin concentrated in low-score names, the residual-risk-filter interpretation survives.

Out-of-sample ablation (the only test that can escape Berkson): run B0 with eps_preference weight set to zero on a held-out period. If ruin rate among survivors drops by < 1pp AND median W4 return shifts by < 0.5pp, eps_preference is operationally inert and the slot should be retired. This is the experimental designer's redundancy test extended to true out-of-sample.

Dual-label robustness: re-run the entire analysis under both (i) duplicate-the-row and (ii) drop-entirely protocols for entity_6618d3e80c. The mechanism claim is valid only if both protocols agree on direction AND magnitude; disagreement flags UNRESOLVED rather than committing to a verdict.

Null-pullback imputation sensitivity: re-run the reconstruction and ranking tests under complete-case, null-as-distinct-category, and multiple-imputation protocols for pullback_pct / pullback_duration_weeks. Mechanism claim survives only if all three agree on the Spearman / R^2 thresholds.
actionable_design_principles: Stop treating eps_preference as a downside-risk-management lever in B0; the visible archaeology (50% ruin among B0 picks with the same momentum signature as winners) directly contradicts that role regardless of the marginal-effect question.

Reframe the eps_preference component around an explicitly PIT-observable earnings-revision breadth measure (% analysts raising next-Q EPS over trailing 8 weeks, lagged to be PIT-clean), not an inferred score derived from price/volume features. This is the only way to break the PEAD-confound loop the Skeptic identified.

Separate two distinct questions the archaeology conflates: (a) is eps_preference risk-controlling? (answer is empirically NO given current outcomes) and (b) is eps_preference providing any incremental signal beyond mom_20/up_day_ratio_20/vol_ratio_5_20? (cannot be answered inside this Berkson-conditioned sample). The ablation/out-of-sample test above answers (b) and must be the gate for keeping the slot.

Build a probabilistic outcome model rather than binary ruin/winner labels, given that entity_6618d3e80c simultaneously carries both labels — the binary dichotomy is demonstrably unstable for individual names and inflates false precision in the contrast tables.

Add an explicit ruin-suppression layer keyed to features that DO separate ruin from winners in the archaeology (the conditional patterns: low up_day_ratio_20 paired with positive mom_20; high px_vs_ma50 paired with high vol_ratio_5_20). This is a true downside filter, not eps_preference in disguise.

Implement snapshot-blocked inference everywhere (per experimental designer's leakage_checks): resample at snapshot_anon level, never at case level, because snap_d0d57b1e40 and snap_71486ed83c each carry 6 cases and can dominate naive per-case p-values.

Cap the B0 slot budget: until the redundancy test passes, do not let eps_preference earn a 4th candidate feature in its proxy signal. If it cannot be reconstructed from the 3-slot trio, that itself is evidence of its informational distinctness and a separate decision must be made about whether the distinctness is genuine or overfitting.

Track contribution attribution quarterly: if removing eps_preference changes the B0 W4-return distribution by < 0.5pp median and ruin rate by < 1pp, retire the component for parsimony regardless of its documentation history.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: eps_revision_breadth_zscore
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Replaces the inferred eps_preference score with an explicit, PIT-observable measure (rolling 8-week % of analysts raising next-Q EPS, lagged one publication cycle and z-scored within sector). This breaks the PEAD confound the Skeptic flagged and gives a directly auditable signal rather than a derived composite.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Occupies the slot currently held by an inferred composite; capacity-neutral but shifts the data dependency from price/volume to fundamental feeds, which carries its own data-availability and survivorship considerations.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: ruin_suppression_layer_v1
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Implements the conditional ruin patterns actually visible in the archaeology (low up_day_ratio_20 + positive mom_20; high px_vs_ma50 + high vol_ratio_5_20) as an explicit post-B0 veto layer. This is a TRUE downside-risk-control feature built from the diagnostic archaeology actually showed, rather than a renamed eps_preference.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Adds one slot; functions as a conditional gate rather than a continuous score, so its capacity cost is purely the additional conditioning rules not additional model parameters.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: ablation_test_policy
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Institutionalizes the experimental designer's redundancy test as a quarterly governance rule: for every B0 component, run a held-out ablation with that component's weight set to zero and compare ruin rate / W4-return distribution. If the change is below the thresholds above, the component is flagged for retirement. This is the only mechanism that escapes Berkson conditioning in the in-sample archaeology.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity-neutral; purely a governance/policy layer on top of existing model capacity. Forces component retirement rather than indefinite slot retention.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: dual_label_resolution_protocol
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Standardizes handling of cases like entity_6618d3e80c (and any future dual-labeled case) by requiring both duplicate-the-row and drop-entirely analyses with a pre-registered agreement threshold. This neutralizes the Skeptic's instability-of-binary-outcome critique and prevents single dual-labeled cases from swinging contrast tables.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity-neutral; affects analysis pipeline only, no additional model slots.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: snapshot_blocked_inference_default
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Mandates block-bootstrap at snapshot_anon granularity for every significance test on this archaeology, with leave-one-snapshot-out sensitivity checks. Directly addresses the Skeptic's snapshot-clustering critique (snap_d0d57b1e40 / snap_71486ed83c each contribute 6 of 27 cases) and prevents within-snapshot correlation from inflating significance.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Compute-cost increase (more bootstrap replications) but no model capacity change.

cycles.question: For B0 component 'weekly_volume', determine whether its historical value comes from downside-risk control versus return ranking. State what evidence would falsify the component's claimed role and what a cleaner replacement would look like.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The B0 'weekly_volume' feature (operationalized here as vol_ratio_5_20, 5-day avg volume / 20-day avg volume) functions primarily as a return-ranking / participation-confirmation filter, not as a downside-risk-control gate. Its selection signal separates selected_winners (median 1.42) from false_negatives (median 1.18, standardized delta -1.05), but it fails to separate selected_winners from false_positive_ruins, where ruin cases occupy essentially the same volume-ratio band (0.91–1.63) as winners (1.00–1.77). If weekly_volume were truly a downside-risk guardrail, ruins should be statistically distinguishable from winners on this axis; they are not.
evidence_for: vol_ratio_5_20 is the third-strongest discriminator (std delta -1.05) between selected_winners and false_negatives in the numeric_contrasts table, indicating genuine predictive information for RETURN RANKING.

False_negative_median vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.179 vs selected_winner_median = 1.424 — entities with sub-1.2 volume ratios are systematically under-selected even when other features (px_vs_ma20, ma10_slope_5, mom_20) look constructive (e.g., entity_d8e8e7b814, entity_bfb308b24a, entity_de1c657364).
ibd_entry_volume_ratio also shows a directional selection signal (winner 1.81 vs FN 1.60, std delta -0.50), reinforcing that liquidity/participation at the IBD pivot matters for identifying winners.
Mechanistically, low recent volume relative to baseline is consistent with weak institutional accumulation — a momentum/quality proxy, not a tail-risk proxy.
evidence_against: false_positive_ruin cases span nearly the full vol_ratio_5_20 distribution: entity_40ea0cfb3b ruins at 0.906 (volume DRY-UP preceding ruin) while entity_84824e6a20 ruins at 1.625 (volume SPIKE preceding ruin). A downside-risk filter would need to flag both tails; the current single-threshold weekly_volume cannot.

Six of eight false_positive_ruins have vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.20 (entity_8f0df3d38e=1.24, entity_4fdc3699fd=1.38, entity_3472243e0c=1.21, entity_ccc90a671f=1.45, entity_84824e6a20=1.63, entity_b6bcccdf6a=1.31), overlapping heavily with selected_winners in the 1.2–1.6 band. Volume alone does NOT veto these entries.

Raw volume_ratio shows the OPPOSITE direction (FN 1.65 vs winner 1.55, std delta +0.23), suggesting weekly_volume is picking up a specific short-window acceleration pattern rather than a generic liquidity property — and that pattern is being read as 'strength' even when the price action preceding ruin is divergent.

The contrast between ruin entity_40ea0cfb3b (vol_ratio=0.906, mom_20=0.024, ma10_slope=0.025) and ruin entity_84824e6a20 (vol_ratio=1.625, mom_20=0.067, ma10_slope=0.062) shows that ruins cluster at LOW-momentum / low-volume AND HIGH-volume / divergent-price regimes — neither is captured by a monotonic weekly_volume contribution.
falsifiable_predictions: If weekly_volume is reinterpreted as return-ranking only (not risk control), then on the held-out cohort, adding a vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.2 filter should NOT reduce ruin frequency among B0 picks beyond what is already achieved by removing sub-1.0 cases — i.e., the lift should be ~0pp for the upper tail and ~1–2pp only because it removes a handful of low-volume picks like entity_40ea0cfb3b.

If weekly_volume WERE a genuine downside-risk control, then conditioning on ruin vs winner among B0 picks, the vol_ratio_5_20 distribution should show KS-test p < 0.05 separation; current archaeology shows the medians are indistinguishable (~1.35 vs ~1.42). Falsification: a future sample where ruins and winners remain statistically indistinguishable on vol_ratio_5_20 would confirm the return-ranking-only reading.
