tests.success_criterion: Standardized deltas for up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20 against false_positive_ruin remain within ±0.3 of each other across the 5+ distinct snapshot IDs in the dataset—proving stable mechanism rather than regime artifact
tests.failure_criterion: Standardized deltas vary by >0.5 across snapshots, or the direction of the delta reverses in any snapshot—proving the apparent redundancy is snapshot-contingent

tests.name: orthogonality_to_pullback_test
tests.comparison: mechanism_pathway_separation
tests.success_criterion: pullback_duration_weeks shows correlation <0.4 with each of up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, confirming orthogonal coverage—AND conditioning on pullback_duration_weeks adds >10% incremental AUC to false_positive_ruin prediction beyond conviction features alone
tests.failure_criterion: pullback_duration_weeks correlates >0.6 with any conviction feature (suggesting same construct) OR adds <3% incremental AUC—indicating current penalty double-counts patience and conviction

tests.name: mutual_information_test
tests.comparison: information_theoretic_independence
tests.success_criterion: I(outcome_label; up_day_ratio_20) ≈ I(outcome_label; vol_ratio_5_20) ≈ I(outcome_label; mom_20) within ±20%—proving equal marginal information and supporting redundancy hypothesis
tests.failure_criterion: MI differs by >40% between any pair of features, with the highest-MI feature alone accounting for >50% of total mutual information—proving unequal and potentially non-redundant contributions

leakage_checks: All 27 cases are discovery-train artifacts; tests must use only frozen evidence features without accessing post-snapshot outcomes beyond the outcome_label field provided
snapshot_id grouping must be preserved—no cross-snapshot leakage when computing per-snapshot standardized deltas
w4_return_bucket and outcome_label are label fields, not features; they cannot be used as inputs to the predictive mechanism under test
Consolidation test must not use the same 27 cases for both training the conviction_index and evaluating equivalence (use split-half or leave-one-snapshot-out)

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The 'dry_false_penalty' B0 component's three primary inputs (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20) each independently predict false_positive_ruin outcome with standardized deltas of -1.19, -1.05, and -1.00 respectively. This pattern is consistent with either (a) true redundancy through multicollinearity, or (b) three distinct signal surfaces capturing orthogonal facets of institutional accumulation quality. The critical distinction cannot be resolved with the frozen evidence alone. The experimental designer's ablation_independence_test is the essential next experiment: does each feature contribute marginal predictive value when the other two are present, or does any single feature's removal leave false-positive detection statistically unchanged? Until ablation evidence demonstrates near-zero marginal contribution for any single feature, the redundancy hypothesis remains unvalidated. The skeptic's methodological counterpoint is valid: correlated predictions do not prove redundant mechanisms—they may simply reflect a latent construct that loads on multiple observable features.
falsifiers: Ablation test reveals that removing any single feature (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, or mom_20) does NOT significantly increase false_positive_ruin classification error (<2% relative change) when the other two are retained—proving true redundancy

Consolidation test shows that replacing three features with a single equal-weighted z-score conviction_index maintains false_positive_ruin precision within ±3% while matching false_negative_relative rate—proving features were capturing the same variance

Mutual information test demonstrates I(outcome_label; up_day_ratio_20), I(outcome_label; vol_ratio_5_20), and I(outcome_label; mom_20) are within ±20% of each other—proving equal marginal information contribution
A/B out-of-sample test shows that dropping any single feature does not increase false-positive rate by >5% while consolidated score matches multi-feature performance—direct validation of redundancy
Regime stability test reveals standardized deltas for all three features remain within ±0.3 across 5+ distinct snapshot IDs without interaction effects—ruling out snapshot-contingent artifacts
actionable_design_principles: Do not consolidate to a single conviction_score until ablation evidence confirms near-zero marginal contribution for at least one feature—this is a hypothesis, not an established fact
Design the ablation experiment first: hold out one feature at a time and measure McNemar-test-significant (p<0.05) degradation in false_positive_ruin precision across the 27-case archaeological set
If ablation shows significant marginal contribution for ALL three features individually, treat them as orthogonal signal surfaces rather than redundant—consolidation would destroy information

Add ma10_slope_5 to the ablation pool: standardized delta of -0.68 suggests it captures velocity-trap cases (entity_b6bcccdf6a: ma10_slope=0.067, up_day=0.4, mom=0.176) that the current three-feature set misses, implying the penalty is under-parameterized, not over-parameterized

Distinguish pullback_duration_weeks (standardized Δ=-0.73, FN<SW) from conviction features—longer pullbacks predict winners, suggesting patience is a separate mechanism from conviction; current 'dry_false_penalty' may be conflating these
Apply leave-one-snapshot-out cross-validation for any consolidation test to prevent snapshot-regime artifacts from masquerading as generalizable redundancy

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Parameterized conviction_weight vector rather than equal-weighted consolidation
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Rather than assuming redundancy and averaging, learn feature weights that minimize false_positive_ruin classification error; if weights stabilize near equality, redundancy is confirmed; if they diverge significantly, non-redundancy is confirmed
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Tests whether the redundancy hypothesis is structural (equal contributions) or whether differential weighting preserves information from the three-signal construct

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Velocity-divergence detection layer: ma10_slope_5 minus ma20_slope_5 as orthogonal short-term exhaustion signal
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Entity_b6bcccdf6a (selected_winner despite up_day=0.4, mom=0.176) had ma10_slope=0.067 vs ma20_slope=0.045—velocity divergence predicts winners that conviction-only models classify as false-positive-risk; this is additive signal, not redundant
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Captures momentum-trap cases where short-term acceleration exhausts while long-window conviction survives—currently unpenalized by dry_false_penalty

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Patience-reward mechanism separate from conviction-penalty mechanism
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: pullback_duration_weeks correlates with selected_winner (FN median=4.0 vs SW=5.5), opposite of conviction features; this suggests two independent mechanisms: (1) conviction-penalty for entry quality, (2) patience-reward for holding quality—not one redundant component
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: If confirmed orthogonal, splitting into separate penalty components would allow independent calibration rather than conflating entry-quality and holding-patience signals

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Threshold-bucketed conviction rather than continuous z-score
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Continuous penalty is sensitive to measurement noise in correlated feature clusters; bucketing into LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH conviction tiers reduces overfitting to collinear feature precision while preserving the mechanism's categorical intent
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Addresses the skeptic's concern that consolidation may amplify measurement error out-of-sample; bucketing is robust to noise while still implementing the conviction-based penalty

cycles.question: For B0 component 'evidence_risk', determine whether its historical value comes from proxy/redundancy with other B0 components. State what evidence would falsify the component's claimed role and what a cleaner replacement would look like.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The 'evidence_risk' component is a redundant proxy for other B0 signals, primarily reflecting volatility (vol_ratio_5_20), momentum (mom_20) and short‑term trend quality (up_day_ratio_20) rather than providing independent risk information.
evidence_for: In the numeric contrasts, vol_ratio_5_20 (standardized Δ = ‑1.0455), up_day_ratio_20 (Δ = ‑1.1882) and mom_20 (Δ = ‑1.0005) are the top three discriminators between false negatives and selected winners, matching the likely inputs of evidence_risk.

Selected winners (e.g., entity_440e297253, entity_ead73f4390) exhibit high up_day_ratio_20 (0.5‑0.7) and moderate vol_ratio_5_20 (~1.4‑1.8), while false‑positive ruination cases (e.g., entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c) show elevated vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.2) and lower up_day_ratio_20 (0.4‑0.65).
The pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks fields are missing in many cases but when present they co‑vary with vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20, suggesting these are already captured by risk proxies.
evidence_against: No explicit orthogonal risk metric (e.g., realized volatility, ATR, drawdown) appears in the top numeric contrasts; evidence_risk may therefore capture something not fully represented by the listed features, but this cannot be verified without its definition.

A minority of false‑negative cases with high vol_ratio_5_20 still become winners (e.g., entity_2c58cebc59 has vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.619 and is a selected_winner), indicating that a simple combination of volatility and momentum alone does not fully explain the risk signal.
falsifiable_predictions: A model that excludes evidence_risk but includes vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and mom_20 will reproduce the same out‑of‑sample Sharpe (±0.05) and maximum drawdown distribution as the full model.
If evidence_risk is truly redundant, adding it to a model that already contains those three features will yield no statistically significant improvement in bootstrap tests (p > 0.25).

Evidence_risk will have no incremental predictive power for 4‑week drawdown beyond vol_ratio_5_20 and up_day_ratio_20 when both are included as linear predictors (coefficient not significant at α = 0.10).

If evidence_risk is replaced by a direct combination of vol_ratio_5_20 and up_day_ratio_20 (e.g., risk_score = vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20)), the classification accuracy on the 27‑case set will remain ≥ 85%.
policy_implications: If the redundancy hypothesis holds, evidence_risk can be dropped to reduce model dimensionality and over‑fitting risk, with a net reduction in feature count of at least one B0 component.

A cleaner replacement would be a simple composite risk score (e.g., vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20)) that directly encodes the trade‑off between volatility and short‑term trend quality, making the model more interpretable.
If evidence_risk is found to add unique information, the model should retain it but treat it as a higher‑order interaction term (e.g., volatility × momentum) rather than a standalone signal.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The redundancy claim is unfalsifiable without knowing what evidence_risk actually computes. The researcher assumes evidence_risk ≈ f(vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, mom_20) based on the numeric contrasts, but this is circular: using the same 27 cases to both discover which features correlate with failure and to assert that evidence_risk duplicates those features proves nothing. The feature is a black box, and its redundancy cannot be tested without its definition.

attacks.issue: No construct definition for evidence_risk
attacks.why_it_matters: The entire redundancy argument depends on evidence_risk being some function of the top three numeric-contrast features. But evidence_risk has no published formula in the provided data. Claiming it is redundant with vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and mom_20 is an unfalsifiable assertion about an undefined object. The researcher cannot simultaneously use the numeric contrasts to diagnose evidence_risk's inputs AND claim that those same contrasts prove evidence_risk is unnecessary.

attacks.issue: In-sample accuracy on n=27 is not a falsification test
attacks.why_it_matters: The claim that the replacement composite achieves ≥85% classification accuracy on the 27-case set is an in-sample fit statistic, not a falsification. With 27 observations and a composite derived from the same data, this is guaranteed to overstate performance. The true test requires applying the composite to held-out data with a pre-specified decision threshold, which the researcher never performed. The stated falsifiable prediction about Sharpe ±0.05 is a hypothetical out-of-sample claim with zero supporting evidence.

attacks.issue: Bootstrap threshold of p > 0.25 is suspiciously lenient
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher proposes that evidence_risk is redundant if adding it yields p > 0.25 in a bootstrap test. This is backwards: if evidence_risk has genuinely zero predictive power, the null distribution should produce p-values uniformly distributed under the null, yielding p > 0.25 approximately 75% of the time by definition. Using 0.25 as a threshold means three-quarters of truly useless features would be declared redundant. A meaningful test requires p < 0.10 to reject the alternative that evidence_risk contributes anything, not p > 0.25 to accept the redundancy null.

attacks.issue: The replacement composite is an untested, unvalidated alternative
attacks.why_it_matters: The proposed replacement (vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20)) was derived post-hoc from the same failure archaeology data. It has never been backtested on any independent dataset, never evaluated for maximum drawdown performance, and never tested across different market regimes. Asserting it is a 'cleaner replacement' is policy advocacy without empirical support. The composite could systematically underweight tail-risk regimes or miss conditional interactions between volatility and momentum that evidence_risk captures through a different functional form.

attacks.issue: Collinearity masking vs. true redundancy is not distinguished
attacks.why_it_matters: High correlation between evidence_risk and the three proposed features does not establish redundancy in a model sense. In a collinear predictor set, dropping one variable can shift the coefficients and effective degrees of freedom of the remaining variables, changing the decision boundary. The researcher conflates 'predicts similarly' with 'can be removed without consequence.' Even if evidence_risk is 0.9 correlated with the composite, the remaining 10% variance could anchor the model in extreme cases (e.g., high-vol/low-momentum regimes) where the composite and evidence_risk diverge.

attacks.issue: The numeric contrasts identify discriminators, not mechanisms
attacks.why_it_matters: The top standardized deltas (up_day_ratio_20: -1.19, vol_ratio_5_20: -1.05, mom_20: -1.00) are statistical differences between false negatives and selected winners. They are not evidence that evidence_risk is constructed from these features, nor that evidence_risk operates through these channels. Any risk signal correlated with failure will appear as a top discriminator. The researcher has shown evidence_risk is associated with the same outcomes as these features, not that it is redundant with them mechanistically.

attacks.issue: Sample heterogeneity is unexamined
attacks.why_it_matters: The 27 cases span multiple snapshots (snap_724342c280, snap_287267e812, snap_eb3d8128cc, etc.) from what appear to be different market conditions. The researcher never stratifies the analysis by snapshot or regime. An evidence_risk component that is redundant in low-volatility regimes may carry unique signal in high-volatility regimes, or vice versa. Treating 27 pooled cases as a single regime invalidates any generalization about redundancy across the full trading universe.

counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where evidence_risk fires (is_b0_pick = true) but vol_ratio_5_20 and up_day_ratio_20 are both near their false-negative medians — i.e., the composite would NOT predict risk, but evidence_risk does. These are the cases where evidence_risk would be provably non-redundant.

Snapshots where evidence_risk's B0 inclusion changes the final portfolio composition (e.g., a stock selected by B0 because of evidence_risk that would be excluded without it, and that stock's realized outcome contradicts the composite's prediction).

Periods where evidence_risk is consistently high but vol_ratio_5_20 and up_day_ratio_20 are both in the 'safe' range, to test whether evidence_risk captures a regime-level risk factor not present in the three-feature composite.
Cases where evidence_risk is low but the composite is high, to test whether the composite over-predicts risk relative to evidence_risk — indicating the composite is not equivalent.

An out-of-sample dataset of at least 200 cases where the composite and evidence_risk disagree on at least 30% of picks, with realized outcomes tracked, to test whether evidence_risk or the composite is a better risk predictor.
what_would_change_my_mind: A published or observable definition of evidence_risk that shows it is literally computed as a function of vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and mom_20 with no additional nonlinear terms, weighting, or conditioning.

An out-of-sample backtest (minimum 200 unseen cases) demonstrating that dropping evidence_risk and replacing it with the proposed composite produces identical or statistically indistinguishable Sharpe ratio (within 0.03), maximum drawdown (within 2pp), and win-rate distributions.

A bootstrap test on held-out data showing that adding evidence_risk to a model already containing the three proposed features yields a coefficient not significantly different from zero at α = 0.10 AND that the likelihood ratio test p-value exceeds 0.50 (not merely 0.25).

A formal variance decomposition (e.g., variance inflation factor analysis) demonstrating that evidence_risk accounts for less than 5% of unique variance in the B0 scoring function after accounting for vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and mom_20.

Evidence that removing evidence_risk does not change the rank ordering of the top-20 B0 candidates by more than 5% in any held-out test set — demonstrating the signal is genuinely redundant for ranking purposes, not just correlated with outcomes.

tests.name: rank_order_equivalence_test
tests.comparison: Composite (vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20)) vs. evidence_risk B0 selection decisions across all 27 cases
tests.success_criterion: Composite reproduces evidence_risk B0 selection decisions with ≥90% concordance (25/27 cases). Kendall's tau between composite score and evidence_risk binary decision ≥0.70.
tests.failure_criterion: Composite disagrees with evidence_risk on >3 cases OR Kendall's tau <0.70, indicating evidence_risk captures variance not explained by the two-feature composite alone.

tests.name: incremental_information_test
tests.comparison: Logistic regression predicting outcome_label (selected_winner vs. ruin/false_positive_ruin) with and without evidence_risk indicator
tests.success_criterion: Evidence_risk indicator has coefficient not significantly different from zero at α=0.10 (two-sided) AND likelihood-ratio test p-value >0.50 when added to model already containing vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, mom_20. This confirms evidence_risk adds no unique predictive variance beyond the three-feature composite.
tests.failure_criterion: Evidence_risk coefficient significant at α<0.10 OR LRT p-value <0.50. Evidence_risk contributes information not captured by the composite, refuting the redundancy hypothesis.

tests.name: cross_snapshot_regime_test
tests.comparison: Stratified analysis: within each snapshot (snap_724342c280, snap_71486ed83c, snap_d0d57b1e40, snap_b8420124eb, snap_ad495b6705), test whether composite and evidence_risk selection sets are equivalent
tests.success_criterion: Within each snapshot containing ≥4 cases, composite selection set equals evidence_risk selection set. Evidence_risk is uniformly redundant across market regimes.
tests.failure_criterion: At least one snapshot shows composite and evidence_risk disagreeing on ≥1 pick. Evidence_risk captures regime-conditional signal not present in the composite, refuting uniform redundancy.

leakage_checks: The composite formula (vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20)) must be pre-specified before examining evidence_risk's numeric contrasts or case-level feature values in the 27-case set.
All three tests must use the same pre-specified composite without iterative refinement on the 27 cases.
Test significance thresholds (α=0.10, LRT p>0.50, Kendall tau ≥0.70) must be fixed before computing any test statistics on the 27 cases.

The 27 cases constitute discovery data; tests are diagnostic rather than definitive proof. Positive findings require out-of-sample validation on a minimum 50-case held-out set with the same pre-specified thresholds.
Cross_snapshot_regime_test must not use snapshot identity as a predictor—only the numeric features available at each snapshot determine selection decisions.
If any test uses mom_20 or mom_60, these must appear in the PIT feature allowlist; otherwise, replace with available momentum proxy (e.g., px_vs_ma20 or px_vs_ma50) in a pre-specified substitution.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The redundancy claim is plausible but unproven. The numeric contrasts show vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and mom_20 are strong outcome discriminators, which is consistent with evidence_risk encoding some combination of these signals. However, the claim cannot be definitively evaluated because: (1) evidence_risk's functional form is unobserved, making the redundancy hypothesis unfalsifiable in its current form; (2) the proposed replacement composite was derived from the same 27-case discovery set, creating circular validation; (3) case examples like entity_2c58cebc59 (high vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.619, outcome = selected_winner) show the composite's simple interaction does not fully capture outcome variance. The three pre-registered tests are methodologically sound but their diagnostic power is constrained by the absence of an evidence_risk definition and the n=27 sample size. Evidence_risk likely captures at least partial redundancy with volatility and trend-quality signals, but the 10-20% of variance not explained by the composite could be structurally important in tail-risk regimes.
falsifiers: Discovery of an explicit formula for evidence_risk showing it contains terms (e.g., conditional logic, regime thresholds, additional feature interactions) not present in vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20) × mom_20
Out-of-sample test (n ≥ 50 held-out cases) showing composite and evidence_risk disagree on >20% of B0 picks, with evidence_risk's selections achieving materially better Sharpe or lower max drawdown
Within-snapshot analysis showing evidence_risk and composite diverge on ≥1 pick per snapshot, where the evidence_risk pick outperforms the composite's alternative
VIF analysis showing evidence_risk accounts for >5% unique variance after regressing out vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and mom_20
A regime-stratified test showing evidence_risk has significant predictive power in at least one volatility/momentum regime where the composite does not
Bootstrap test on held-out data with p < 0.10 for evidence_risk coefficient, contradicting the redundancy null
actionable_design_principles: Never test redundancy by deriving the replacement from the same cases used to diagnose the original feature; use a two-stage procedure (derive composite on subset A, test on subset B)
Require an observable or inferable construct definition before claiming feature-level redundancy; without this, the hypothesis is about correlation structure, not mechanism
Prefer composite alternatives that are explicitly defined (e.g., 'vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20)') rather than implicit combinations, to enable direct comparison
Stratify all redundancy tests by market regime (snapshot) before claiming uniform equivalence; a component can be redundant in low-vol regimes and essential in high-vol regimes
Use a bootstrap threshold of p > 0.50 (not 0.25) for the LRT to avoid declaring 75% of noise features redundant by construction
Test composite equivalence via rank-order concordance, not classification accuracy on discovery data, to avoid in-sample overfitting

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Decompose evidence_risk into an explicit two-tier signal: a first-tier composite (vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20)) for routine risk screening, and a second-tier residual flag for cases where vol_ratio or up_day_ratio diverge from the composite prediction
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This separates the likely redundant component (first-tier) from the potentially unique signal (second-tier residual), enabling targeted ablation testing without discarding all risk information
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Reduces model dimensionality in routine regimes while preserving capacity to detect non-linear risk interactions in edge cases

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Replace evidence_risk with a conditional risk score: if vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.5 AND mom_20 < 0.10 then flag as high-risk else use vol_ratio_5_20 × (1 − up_day_ratio_20) as continuous score
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This explicitly encodes the regime-conditional logic the researcher suspects evidence_risk captures, making the replacement testable and the difference from a simple composite measurable
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Captures the high-vol/low-momentum regime interactions that a pure multiplicative composite may smooth over

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Introduce an explicit 'evidence_weight' hyperparameter (0 ≤ w ≤ 1) that interpolates between pure composite scoring and evidence_risk-influenced scoring, with w tuned on out-of-sample performance rather than fixed at 0 or 1
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This reframes the redundancy question as a continuous weighting problem rather than a binary keep/drop decision, allowing the model to capture partial redundancy rather than assuming complete equivalence or complete uniqueness
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Preserves model flexibility during regime transitions where evidence_risk may contribute at different magnitudes across market conditions

cycles.question: For B0 component 'freshness', determine whether its historical value comes from proxy/redundancy with other B0 components. State what evidence would falsify the component's claimed role and what a cleaner replacement would look like.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The 'freshness' component is redundant with existing momentum/time features (mom_20, ma10_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20) and captures no independent signal; it is a relabeled proxy for recent price action quality that is already encoded in the selected_winner profile.
evidence_for: Selected winners show mom_20 median of 0.163 vs false negatives 0.058 (standardized_delta=-1.0005), directly encoding 'how much recent acceleration occurred'
Selected winners show up_day_ratio_20 median of 0.625 vs false negatives 0.50 (standardized_delta=-1.1882), encoding 'freshness of directional bias'
Selected winners show ma10_slope_5 median of 0.027 vs false negatives 0.012 (standardized_delta=-0.6815), encoding 'current momentum velocity'

Cases like entity_ead73f4390 (selected_winner, mom_20=0.320, up_day_ratio_20=0.70) and entity_2f86543bf6 (selected_winner, mom_20=-0.008, up_day_ratio_20=0.35) show winners span a range that 'freshness' would flatten, suggesting the feature aggregates rather than distinguishes
The base_duration_weeks contrast (median_delta=-8.0) implies setups that consolidate longer are worse—a temporal effect already partially captured by ma_slope features during the base period
evidence_against: entity_8ad5cd4795 (selected_winner, mom_20=0.004, ma10_slope_5=-0.006, up_day_ratio_20=0.70) is a winner despite weak momentum, possibly indicating a distinct 'freshness' signal from a new base start rather than momentum magnitude
pullback_pct standardized_delta=+0.6404 (false negatives less deep) suggests 'time since pullback' may encode recovery freshness not fully captured by forward-looking slope features

ruin outcomes include cases like entity_6618d3e80c (selected_winner|false_positive_ruin, mom_20=0.251) where high momentum coexists with ruin, implying momentum and freshness may operate in different causal pathways
The feature set lacks an explicit 'days since breakout trigger' variable, which could be the unique 'freshness' signal distinct from ongoing momentum measures
falsifiable_predictions: If freshness is redundant: regression of outcome on (mom_20 + ma10_slope_5 + up_day_ratio_20) will absorb >90% of the variance explained by any freshness proxy constructed from these features
If freshness is unique: adding a 'days_since_ibd_entry_trigger' variable (PIT-observable) will significantly improve classification AUC beyond the existing feature set, with effect size >0.03

If freshness proxies freshness: among entities with identical mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20, those with lower base_duration_weeks will show higher selected_winner rate (specificity test for temporal independence)

Falsification criterion: if Pearson correlation between freshness_score and first principal component of (mom_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20) exceeds 0.85, declare redundancy confirmed
policy_implications: If redundancy confirmed: drop freshness as an independent component; weight its proxy features individually to allow heterogeneous contribution to portfolio construction
If freshness is unique: replace with a cleaner metric: 'trading_days_since_ibd_trigger_entry' (integer, PIT-observable, no lookback bias) rather than a composite of lagged features
If ambiguous: use freshness as a secondary filter (e.g., freshness_score < threshold) rather than a primary feature, reducing its leverage on model decisions while preserving optionality
Avoid 'freshness_score' as a derived composite; instead require PIT-observable atomic features that independently pass the redundancy test

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The researcher's 'redundancy' verdict conflates correlation with causal equivalence. The composite freshness_score may be a suboptimal proxy for a genuine causal mechanism—temporal distance from the last base formation event—that is NOT captured by simultaneous-moment momentum features. The proposed 'cleaner' replacement (trading_days_since_ibd_trigger_entry) would test a cleaner mechanism, NOT redundancy, because it operationalizes the same causal hypothesis with less measurement error.

attacks.issue: The PCA correlation threshold (r > 0.85 = redundancy confirmed) is an arbitrary stopping rule with no theoretical justification
attacks.why_it_matters: If PC1 of momentum features explains 84% of freshness_score variance, the researcher calls it redundant. If it explains 86%, freshness is killed. This threshold is not derived from prediction theory, causal discovery criteria, or information-theoretic bounds on marginal contribution. The researcher is using a convenient cutoff to foreclose investigation rather than a principled boundary.

attacks.issue: The researcher treats base_duration_weeks as 'already partially captured by ma_slope features during the base period' — this is the very claim under test
attacks.why_it_matters: ma10_slope_5 and ma20_slope_5 measure velocity DURING the base consolidation, not the temporal structure of the base itself. A 4-week base and a 12-week base can have identical MA slopes, yet differ fundamentally in how 'stale' vs. 'fresh' the subsequent breakout is. The numeric contrast for base_duration_weeks (standardized_delta=-0.4214) is dismissed with hand-waving rather than tested for independence conditional on momentum features.

attacks.issue: The 'days_since_ibd_entry_trigger' replacement metric does NOT test redundancy — it tests measurement fidelity
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher proposes a cleaner freshness signal as a replacement, but this is not a falsification of the freshness mechanism. It is a refinement. Redundancy requires showing that NO function of temporal distance from base formation improves predictions beyond simultaneous momentum features. The evidence provided does not test this causal boundary.

attacks.issue: The false_negative_median for pullback_pct (+0.6404) is interpreted as supporting 'time since pullback' as a freshness proxy, then immediately declared redundant with slope features
attacks.why_it_matters: pullback_pct standardized_delta=+0.6404 means false negatives have less-deep pullbacks (closer to entry price). This is a temporal-recovery effect: entities that recover slowly are more likely to be missed by B0. This signal is NOT the same as ma10_slope_5 (which measures current velocity) — it measures RECOVERY behavior across a time interval. The researcher quietly concedes this signal exists, then ignores it when concluding redundancy.

attacks.issue: No conditional analysis: redundancy is tested in-sample on the full population, not conditional on momentum regime
attacks.why_it_matters: Freshness may be redundant for high-momentum entities (mom_20 > 0.15) but add signal for moderate-momentum entities. The researcher provides no regime-stratified analysis. The case entity_2f86543bf6 (mom_20=-0.008, selected_winner) is cited as evidence for freshness's irrelevance, but this single case is equally consistent with freshness being critical for low-momentum breakouts and irrelevant for high-momentum ones.

counterexamples_to_seek: Subset of selected_winner entities where mom_20, ma10_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, AND ma20_slope_5 are all at or below false_negative medians, yet the entity is a selected_winner. Does such a set exist? If so, what other feature explains the selection — likely base_duration_weeks or days_since_trigger, supporting a non-redundant freshness mechanism.

Cross-snapshot stability test: for entities appearing in multiple snapshots, compute the correlation between freshness_score and PC1 of momentum features per snapshot. If correlation varies substantially (e.g., 0.55 to 0.92), freshness captures snapshot-specific temporal effects not reducible to a stable PC1.

Paired test: identify entity pairs matched on mom_20 (±0.01), up_day_ratio_20 (±0.05), ma10_slope_5 (±0.005), and ma20_slope_5 (±0.005) but with different base_duration_weeks (e.g., 20 weeks vs 60 weeks). If selected_winner rate differs significantly (chi-square test, p < 0.05), freshness is not redundant — it adds independent explanatory power.

Ruin-within-high-momentum cases: entity_6618d3e80c (mom_20=0.251, selected_winner|false_positive_ruin) and entity_3472243e0c (mom_20=0.242, false_positive_ruin). Both have high momentum. What distinguishes the selected_winner outcome from ruin in this momentum tier? If freshness_score or base_duration_weeks differs systematically, it is not redundant — it filters the high-momentum set.
what_would_change_my_mind: A controlled experiment: holding mom_20, ma10_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, ma20_slope_5 constant (bin-matched), add base_duration_weeks as a separate feature. If AUC improvement is less than 0.005 (not 0.03 — the researcher's threshold is too lenient for a claim of total redundancy), then freshness is effectively redundant.

Causal identification: if an instrumental variable for 'time since base formation' (e.g., natural variation in earnings cadence that systematically lengthens consolidation periods) shows no residual correlation with selected_winner outcome after controlling for momentum features, then the freshness mechanism is causally null — not just statistically correlated.

Information-theoretic test: compute mutual information I(selected_winner; freshness_score | mom_20, ma10_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, ma20_slope_5). If I < 0.01 bits, freshness adds negligible conditional information and the redundancy claim holds. This is a principled test the researcher never performs.

Prospective validation: implement both the composite freshness_score and a pure 'trading_days_since_ibd_trigger_entry' on a holdout temporal window (not the discovery set). If the atomic variable outperforms the composite by any margin, the composite was suboptimal, not redundant — and the researcher's conclusion inverts: freshness is real but poorly measured.

tests.name: conditional_independence_base_duration_vs_momentum
tests.comparison: Among entities binned on mom_20 (±0.02), ma10_slope_5 (±0.005), up_day_ratio_20 (±0.10), ma20_slope_5 (±0.005), test whether base_duration_weeks adds incremental AUC beyond the four momentum/slope features alone. Use logistic regression with momentum features only as baseline, then add base_duration_weeks. Report AUC delta.
tests.success_criterion: AUC improvement < 0.005 when adding base_duration_weeks to momentum baseline, supporting redundancy with base_duration_weeks as the freshness proxy
tests.failure_criterion: AUC improvement >= 0.005, indicating base_duration_weeks captures independent temporal structure not reducible to MA slopes and momentum

tests.name: mutual_information_conditional_on_momentum
tests.comparison: Compute conditional mutual information: I(selected_winner; base_duration_weeks | mom_20, ma10_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, ma20_slope_5) and I(selected_winner; pullback_pct | same conditions). This directly tests whether temporal/freshness signals have residual information after conditioning on momentum features, addressing the skeptic's information-theoretic challenge.
tests.success_criterion: Both conditional mutual information values < 0.01 bits, confirming freshness (via base_duration and pullback) adds negligible information beyond momentum
tests.failure_criterion: Either conditional mutual information >= 0.01 bits, confirming freshness captures independent signal not in momentum features

tests.name: regime_stratified_redundancy_test
tests.comparison: Split the 27 cases into high-momentum (mom_20 > median of 0.163) and low-momentum (mom_20 <= 0.163) regimes. Within each regime, perform the conditional independence test: does base_duration_weeks improve AUC beyond the three momentum features? This addresses the skeptic's concern that freshness may be redundant for high-momentum but critical for low-momentum entities.
tests.success_criterion: AUC improvement < 0.005 in BOTH regimes, confirming unconditional redundancy across the full momentum spectrum
tests.failure_criterion: AUC improvement >= 0.005 in low-momentum regime only, indicating freshness is non-redundant specifically for moderate/low-momentum setups

tests.name: pullback_recovery_signal_test
tests.comparison: The numeric contrast shows pullback_pct standardized_delta=+0.6404 (false negatives have less deep pullbacks), indicating a temporal-recovery effect. Test whether this signal is captured by slope features (current velocity) or represents independent recovery behavior across time. Specifically, test if pullback_pct has significant standardized coefficient after conditioning on all MA/momentum features.
tests.success_criterion: pullback_pct standardized coefficient < 0.05 when added to full momentum feature set, confirming it is redundant with current-slope encoding
tests.failure_criterion: pullback_pct standardized coefficient >= 0.05, confirming pullback recovery captures temporal signal distinct from current momentum velocity

tests.name: ruin_within_high_momentum_cases
tests.comparison: Identify high-momentum entities (mom_20 > 0.20) and test what distinguishes selected_winner from false_positive_ruin outcomes within this subset. Specifically compare entity_6618d3e80c (selected_winner|false_positive_ruin, mom_20=0.251, base_duration_weeks missing) vs entity_3472243e0c (false_positive_ruin, mom_20=0.242, base_duration_weeks missing). If freshness is redundant, no temporal feature should discriminate within high-momentum; if freshness is unique, base_duration_weeks or pullback metrics should differ.
tests.success_criterion: No significant difference in base_duration_weeks or pullback metrics between selected_winner and false_positive_ruin within high-momentum subset, supporting redundancy
tests.failure_criterion: Significant difference in temporal features between outcome classes within high-momentum subset, indicating freshness filters high-momentum cases independently

leakage_checks: All features used are PIT-observable: mom_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, base_duration_weeks, vol_ratio_5_20. No forward-looking features.
selected_winner outcome label is derived from W4 >= 8% AND >= 5pp above B0 selected median OR >= 5pp above worst B0 pick — this is the pre-specified outcome definition, not a leak.
No entity identity features (entity_anon) used as inputs — only numeric features.
No calendar/snapshot features (snapshot_anon) used as inputs — only structural features.
The failure_archaeology case set is discovery-train only per method_note — must not use for final validation.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The freshness component (operationalized via base_duration_weeks, pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) captures a partially non-redundant temporal signal not fully reducible to concurrent momentum features (mom_20, ma10_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, ma20_slope_5). Evidence from the failure archaeology shows pullback_pct has a standardized delta of +0.6404 between false negatives and selected winners—false negatives exhibit shallower pullbacks, indicating slower temporal recovery from retracements. This is not captured by ma_slope features, which encode current velocity, not recovery behavior across time intervals. However, the primary momentum features dominate effect sizes (standardized deltas of -1.00 to -1.19 vs -0.42 for base_duration_weeks), suggesting freshness contributes marginal signal rather than core predictive power. The entity_2f86543bf6 case (selected_winner with mom_20=-0.008) illustrates the lower bound of momentum's reach. The mechanism is better described as 'partial redundancy with measurement contamination' than 'complete redundancy with zero signal'—freshness may encode a real causal structure (temporal distance from base formation) but via suboptimal proxies that overlap substantially with momentum features. Regime-specific effects (freshness may be more critical for low-momentum breakouts) remain untested and unresolved.
falsifiers: Conditional AUC test: adding base_duration_weeks to momentum-only logistic regression improves AUC by < 0.005 when controlling for mom_20 (±0.02), ma10_slope_5 (±0.005), up_day_ratio_20 (±0.10), ma20_slope_5 (±0.005)—this would confirm redundancy with conditional independence satisfied

Conditional mutual information I(selected_winner; base_duration_weeks | momentum_features) < 0.01 bits AND I(selected_winner; pullback_pct | momentum_features) < 0.01 bits—information-theoretic threshold confirming no residual temporal signal

Paired entity analysis: no significant difference (p ≥ 0.10) in selected_winner rate between entity pairs matched on all momentum features but differing in base_duration_weeks by ≥ 20 weeks—would confirm freshness has no discriminative power after conditioning

Prospective holdout test: atomic 'trading_days_since_ibd_trigger_entry' underperforms the current composite freshness_score by any margin—would invert the conclusion: freshness is real but composite is suboptimal, not redundant

Regime-stratified test: AUC improvement < 0.005 in BOTH high-momentum and low-momentum regimes when adding base_duration_weeks to momentum baseline—confirms unconditional redundancy across the full momentum spectrum

Ruin-within-high-momentum test: no significant difference in base_duration_weeks or pullback metrics between selected_winner|false_positive_ruin and false_positive_ruin cases within the mom_20 > 0.20 subset—would confirm freshness filters high-momentum cases redundantly
actionable_design_principles: Decompose freshness into two sub-components: (a) 'recovery_timing' (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) and (b) 'base_staleness' (base_duration_weeks). These have different redundancy profiles—recovery_timing appears non-redundant based on effect size (+0.64), base_staleness appears more redundant (standardized delta -0.42).

Test recovery_timing as a distinct mechanism from momentum: pullback_pct measures depth of correction FROM peak, while ma10_slope_5 measures current upward velocity. These are orthogonal signal dimensions. A composite that blends them conflates distinct causal pathways.

Replace the composite freshness_score with atomic PIT-observable features: trading_days_since_ibd_trigger_entry (atomic temporal distance) and pullback_recovery_rate (pullback_pct / pullback_duration_weeks). This addresses measurement contamination without prejudging mechanism validity.

Implement regime-stratified weighting: allow freshness features higher weight in low-momentum regime (mom_20 < 0.10) where momentum features have lower signal-to-noise, while reducing freshness weight in high-momentum regime (mom_20 > 0.20) where momentum dominates.

Use freshness as a secondary filter rather than primary feature: apply a freshness threshold (e.g., base_duration_weeks < 50 OR pullback_recovery_rate > threshold) to exclude stale setups before momentum scoring, reducing model complexity while preserving optionality.

Treat 'ruin-within-high-momentum' cases (entity_6618d3e80c, entity_3472243e0c) as a diagnostic subset: if freshness features cannot distinguish winner-from-ruin within this subset, confirm freshness is redundant for high-momentum filtering but not necessarily for low-momentum selection.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Regime-conditional freshness weight: dynamically scale freshness feature weight based on momentum regime, with higher weight when mom_20 < 0.10 and lower weight when mom_20 > 0.20
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This addresses the skeptic's attack that redundancy may be regime-dependent. Rather than binary redundancy verdict, this policy admits conditional value in specific momentum contexts while acknowledging redundancy in others.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Captures regime-specific capacity constraints: low-momentum setups may have higher false-negative rates, making freshness-filtering more valuable for universe coverage in that regime.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Atomic temporal distance feature: replace composite freshness_score with trading_days_since_ibd_trigger_entry (integer, PIT-observable) as the primary freshness signal, eliminating proxy contamination from momentum-encoded features
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This directly addresses the researcher's own policy implication. If the atomic variable outperforms the composite on holdout, the composite was suboptimal measurement, not redundancy. This is a cleaner falsification of the measurement-versus-mechanism distinction.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Simplifies feature set and reduces model complexity, potentially improving generalization in low-data regimes where composite features introduce measurement noise.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Recovery velocity composite: construct pullback_recovery_rate = pullback_pct / pullback_duration_weeks (normalized by ATR to handle volatility scaling), testing whether recovery behavior across time intervals adds signal beyond current velocity
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This operationalizes the non-redundant signal suggested by pullback_pct standardized_delta=+0.6404. It measures 'how fast the recovery occurs relative to depth', which is a distinct mechanism from ma10_slope_5 ('current velocity').
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Captures recovery dynamics in volatile markets where pullback patterns are more common, potentially improving selection in high-VIX regimes where base-duration signals may be noisier.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Freshness as exclusion filter: use base_duration_weeks > 60 weeks AND pullback_pct null as a hard exclusion rule rather than a scoring feature, reducing freshness leverage on model decisions while preserving its filtering value
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This aligns with the researcher's ambiguity policy: treat freshness as a secondary filter (reducing leverage) rather than a primary feature, acknowledging its partial redundancy while preserving optionality.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Preserves freshness's utility for eliminating extremely stale setups (likely lower capacity due to base complexity) while preventing freshness from dominating portfolio construction via high-weight composite scoring.

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under pullback versus breakout setup; identify repeated PIT-visible precursors. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-positive B0 picks that ruin under pullback exhibit moderate momentum (0.14-0.18) combined with high volume churn (vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.40) and borderline up_day_ratio_20 (0.50-0.65), producing shallow pullbacks (12-16%) that fail to recover. In contrast, selected winners with high momentum (mom_20 > 0.15) sustain deeper pullbacks (25-42%) that recover. The critical differentiator is up_day_ratio_20 consistency: winners show consistent daily advances (>=0.60), while false positives show erratic internals that cannot absorb the pullback stress.
evidence_for: false_positive_ruin cases (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_ccc90a671f, entity_55c2da490e) show pullback_pct of -12.3% to -16.2% with moderate mom_20 (0.074-0.176) and high vol_ratio_5_20 (1.24-1.45)
selected_winner case entity_3adc078f01 absorbed -42.3% pullback over 9 weeks due to high mom_20 (0.172) and up_day_ratio_20=0.65
selected_winner entity_2c58cebc59 recovered from -25.1% pullback with mom_20=0.321 and up_day_ratio_20=0.60
numeric_contrasts show up_day_ratio_20 has largest standardized_delta (-1.1882) between false_negative_median (0.50) and selected_winner_median (0.625)
vol_ratio_5_20 shows standardized_delta of -1.0455 (false_negative_median 1.179 vs selected_winner_median 1.424)
entity_84824e6a20 (ruin) has up_day_ratio_20=0.40 with vol_ratio_5_20=1.625, showing distribution-prone internals
entity_b6bcccdf6a (ruin) has up_day_ratio_20=0.40 with vol_ratio_5_20=1.312
evidence_against: entity_6618d3e80c is labeled false_positive_ruin|selected_winner with high mom_20 (0.251), vol_ratio_5_20=1.446, up_day_ratio_20=0.55 but large_win outcome—high momentum overcame borderline internals
selected_winner entity_8ad5cd4795 has vol_ratio_5_20=0.996 (below median) with up_day_ratio_20=0.70, suggesting low churn is protective even with lower momentum
Some selected_winner cases (entity_90a828939a, entity_2f86543bf6) have up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.45 but still succeed, indicating other factors (low vol_ratio, weak mom_20) reduce failure pressure
pullback_pct alone cannot distinguish: entity_8f0df3d38e (-16.2%) ruined while entity_2c58cebc59 (-25.1%) recovered
falsifiable_predictions: B0 picks with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60 AND vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.40 will have <15% ruin rate vs current baseline of ~36% (8/22 of is_b0_pick cases ruin)
B0 picks with up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.50 AND vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.45 will have >50% ruin rate under pullback conditions
When mom_20 >= 0.20 AND up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60, pullbacks of any magnitude (test up to -50%) will recover with >80% probability
B0 picks with ma10_slope_5 > 0.05 AND up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.55 will produce 7-week pullbacks in 12-17% range that do not recover (predicts pullback_depth_bucket)
Filtering out is_b0_pick where up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.45 will reduce total picks by ~25% while eliminating ~60% of ruin outcomes
policy_implications: Add up_day_ratio_20 as primary pre-filter: reject B0 candidates below 0.55 threshold
Add vol_ratio_5_20 as secondary filter: reject candidates above 1.45 when up_day_ratio_20 is borderline
For borderline candidates (0.50 <= up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.60, 1.30 <= vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.50), require mom_20 > 0.20 to overcome internal inconsistency
Do not use pullback_pct as entry filter—shallow pullbacks are the failure mode, not a distinguishing success signal
Consider position sizing adjustment: B0 picks with up_day_ratio_20 in 0.50-0.60 range warrant 50% position size even if other metrics pass

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The claimed predictive mechanism conflates stock volatility regime with conditional outcome: high vol_ratio_5_20 at snapshot time is a stable property of volatile stocks, not a causal driver of ruin under pullback. The shallow-pullback pattern in false_positive_ruin cases is trivially explained by vol_mean_reversion (volatile stocks exhibit smaller percentage pullbacks because their baselines fluctuate more), and the up_day_ratio_20 distinction may be measuring momentum decomposition rather than a separate predictive signal. The entire pattern could be a distributional artifact of heterogeneous volatility regimes within the sample, not a filterable precursor.

attacks.issue: Proxy redundancy between up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20
attacks.why_it_matters: Both metrics quantify directional persistence over 20 days. A stock with mom_20 > 0.15 will mechanically tend to have up_day_ratio_20 > 0.50 because positive cumulative returns require more up days than down days. The standardized_delta of -1.1882 for up_day_ratio_20 may simply be re-expressing the momentum contrast (mom_20 standardized_delta -1.0005). If up_day_ratio_20 is a monotonic function of mom_20 with added noise, it provides no independent information and the apparent predictive power disappears under proper collinearity handling.

attacks.issue: Snapshot-conditioned selection artifact
attacks.why_it_matters: All false_positive_ruin cases appear concentrated in specific snapshots (snap_724342c280, snap_71486ed83c, snap_3fc4068e83). Snapshots represent different market regimes where vol_ratio_5_20 and up_day_ratio_20 distributions differ systematically. Comparing false_positive_ruin to selected_winner across snapshots without regime controls means the apparent feature differences reflect when the snapshot was taken, not what predicts ruin. The filter rule derived from pooled cross-snapshot analysis would have different operating characteristics if tested within individual snapshots.

attacks.issue: Trivial mean-reversion explanation for shallow pullbacks
attacks.why_it_matters: A stock with vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.45 has inherently larger daily fluctuations than one with vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.10. When a volatile stock pulls back, the same percentage drop corresponds to a larger absolute price move, which may trigger mean-reversion sooner due to shorter absolute distance to support levels or overshoot detection. The shallow pullbacks (-12% to -16%) in false_positive_ruin cases may be the natural pullback depth for high-volatility stocks, not a pathological failure mode. This mechanism requires no difference in underlying quality—just different volatility baselines.

attacks.issue: Conditioning on the post-snapshot pullback event
attacks.why_it_matters: The analysis selects cases labeled false_positive_ruin, meaning they experienced pullback that led to ruin. But vol_ratio_5_20 and up_day_ratio_20 are computed at snapshot time before the pullback. If pullback_pct is also a post-snapshot measurement, then comparing pre-snapshot internals to post-snapshot pullback depth creates a temporal mismatch: the features and outcomes come from different time windows. The mechanism claim requires that these pre-snapshot features predict post-snapshot events, but this directional assumption is not validated.

attacks.issue: Survivor inclusion bias in the comparison class
attacks.why_it_matters: selected_winner cases by definition survived long enough to be classified as winners. This excludes volatile stocks with similar internals (high vol_ratio_5_20, moderate up_day_ratio_20) that also had shallow pullbacks but failed to recover—these would be labeled false_positive_ruin. The apparent protective effect of up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60 may be an artifact of comparing survivors to documented failures while ignoring unclassified failures that share the same pre-snapshot profile.

attacks.issue: Cherry-picked threshold derivation from N=27
attacks.why_it_matters: With only 8 false_positive_ruin cases, the proposed thresholds (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60, vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.40) are optimized to separate the sample used to generate them. The 36% baseline ruin rate is computed from is_b0_pick cases in this sample, but the sample composition is not demonstrated to be exchangeable with future B0 pick populations. Multiple equivalent threshold combinations could fit this sample equally well, and the specific values selected reflect the researcher's labeling decisions, not statistical stability.

counterexamples_to_seek: B0 picks with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.65 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.50 that subsequently ruined—these would directly contradict the claimed protective effect of consistent up-day ratio even under high churn
B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.60 that recovered from pullbacks exceeding -20% without ruin—this would dissociate vol_ratio from the shallow-pullback-failure mechanism
Temporal holdout validation: apply the proposed filter rules to B0 picks from snapshots not represented in the discovery set and measure whether ruin rates differ as predicted

Within-snapshot validation: for each snapshot containing both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner cases, test whether the up_day_ratio_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 thresholds distinguish outcomes within the same regime

Synthetic counterfactual: construct cases where vol_ratio_5_20 and up_day_ratio_20 are perturbed to cross the proposed thresholds while holding other features constant, and verify the model output changes plausibly
what_would_change_my_mind: Prospective validation: the proposed filter rules (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60, vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.40) applied to a held-out sample of B0 picks with >=50 cases showing ruin rate reduction from baseline at least as large as the in-sample effect with p < 0.05

Mechanistic evidence that vol_ratio_5_20 directly measures something other than baseline volatility—for example, showing that vol_ratio_5_20 correlates with post-entry news sentiment or analyst revision direction rather than merely with stock-specific churn amplitude

Demonstration that up_day_ratio_20 provides incremental predictive power over mom_20 in a proper multivariate model with variance inflation factors < 5, showing the combination captures non-overlapping variance
Replicated pattern in an independent dataset: same feature-outcome relationships observed in B0 picks from a different time period, different market regime, or different scanner criteria

Evidence that shallow pullbacks in false_positive_ruin cases are specifically caused by the high vol_ratio_5_20 (e.g., via intraday analysis showing failed breakout attempts with excessive volume spikes that deplete follow-through), not merely correlated with it via mean-reversion to a higher baseline

tests.name: collinearity_vif_test
tests.comparison: Variance Inflation Factor of up_day_ratio_20 in a multivariate model containing mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 as predictors of ruin outcome
tests.success_criterion: VIF for up_day_ratio_20 < 5, confirming it captures non-redundant variance beyond mom_20
tests.failure_criterion: VIF for up_day_ratio_20 >= 5, indicating proxy redundancy and that the researcher's mechanism conflates momentum decomposition with independent signal

tests.name: volatility_normalized_pullback_test
tests.comparison: Normalized pullback depth (pullback_pct / vol_ratio_5_20) between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner cases
tests.success_criterion: False_positive_ruin normalized pullback depth is significantly shallower than selected_winner (Mann-Whitney p < 0.10), supporting mechanism claim that vol_ratio does not merely proxy baseline volatility
tests.failure_criterion: No significant difference in normalized pullback depth between groups, indicating the apparent failure pattern is a trivial artifact of heterogeneous volatility baselines

tests.name: moment_variance_interaction_test
tests.comparison: Ruin rate conditioned on mom_20 quartile and vol_ratio_5_20 threshold (1.40) cross-tabulation
tests.success_criterion: Within the lowest mom_20 half (<= 0.14), high vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.40) shows ruin rate >50% vs <20% for low vol_ratio_5_20; within the highest mom_20 half, vol_ratio_5_20 does not predict ruin (demonstrating interaction, not main effect)
tests.failure_criterion: Vol_ratio_5_20 predicts ruin regardless of mom_20 level, or mom_20 fully mediates vol_ratio_5_20 effect, indicating vol_ratio is not an independent mechanism

tests.name: within_snapshot_consistency_test
tests.comparison: Outcome proportions for up_day_ratio_20 x vol_ratio_5_20 cell within each snapshot, then aggregated
tests.success_criterion: The up_day_ratio_20 x vol_ratio_5_20 effect direction is consistent across >=3 distinct snapshots (sign test p < 0.10), ruling out snapshot-concentration artifact
tests.failure_criterion: Effect direction reverses or disappears in >50% of snapshots, indicating the pooled pattern arises from snapshot heterogeneity rather than a stable predictor

tests.name: threshold_sensitivity_bootstrap_test
tests.comparison: Ruin rate at researcher's proposed thresholds (0.60, 1.40) versus ±0.05 perturbations, evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation across snapshots
tests.success_criterion: Ruin rate difference between cells remains >=10 percentage points when thresholds vary ±0.05 in any direction (robustness to threshold selection)
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin rate difference collapses to <5 percentage points when thresholds shift ±0.05, indicating the pattern is an artifact of threshold optimization on N=27

leakage_checks: pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are excluded from all test feature sets—they are post-snapshot measurements that would introduce forward-looking bias if used to predict ruin
Feature computation for up_day_ratio_20, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and MA slopes must be completed at snapshot time, not retroactively reconstructed from post-entry price series
Threshold derivation must be pre-specified before inspecting within-snapshot ruin counts to prevent threshold optimization on outcome-concentrated snapshots
Cross-snapshot validation uses outcome labels computed identically across all snapshots—snapshot identity must not influence how outcomes are classified
Interaction test uses only pre-snapshot features (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20) to predict post-snapshot outcomes—no outcome information leaks into feature computation

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The core pattern (high vol_ratio_5_20 + borderline up_day_ratio_20 → ruin under pullback) is directionally present in the 27-case discovery set but rests on insufficient evidence. The experimental designer's collinearity test is critical: if VIF >= 5 for up_day_ratio_20 after accounting for mom_20, the primary predictor is redundant—not independent. The volatility-normalized pullback test addresses the skeptic's strongest attack (trivial mean-reversion); if false_positive_ruin normalized depth is NOT shallower than selected_winner, the entire mechanism collapses to a distributional artifact. With N=27 and only 8 ruin events, threshold derivation is unstable; the 0.60/1.40 values could shift substantially with modest sample changes. Snapshot heterogeneity remains unresolved: if false_positive_ruin cases concentrate in 2-3 snapshots while selected_winners distribute across 6+, the pooled pattern may reflect regime timing rather than a filterable precursor. The proxy-redundancy attack is partially validated by the numeric contrasts (up_day_ratio_20 standardized_delta -1.1882 vs mom_20 -1.0005), suggesting these metrics capture overlapping variance. The mechanism is plausible but not demonstrated as robust, independent, or prospectively validated.
falsifiers: VIF for up_day_ratio_20 >= 5 in a multivariate model containing mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 → mechanism collapses to momentum proxy with no independent signal
Within-snapshot consistency test fails (effect direction reverses in >50% of snapshots) → pooled pattern is regime artifact, not generalizable filter rule

Volatility-normalized pullback depth shows NO significant difference between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner (Mann-Whitney p >= 0.10) → shallow pullbacks are trivial consequence of high-volatility baseline, not a distinct failure mode
Threshold sensitivity bootstrap: ruin rate difference between cells < 5 percentage points when thresholds shift ±0.05 → current thresholds are overfitted to N=27, not stable across sampling variation

Prospective holdout validation: applying proposed filters (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60, vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.40) to held-out snapshot(s) shows ruin rate reduction < 5 percentage points vs baseline → mechanism does not generalize to unseen data
Counterexample found: B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.65 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.50 that subsequently ruined → protective effect of consistent up-day ratio does not hold under high churn conditions
Counterexample found: B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.60 that recovered from pullback exceeding -20% without ruin → vol_ratio dissociation from shallow-pullback-failure mechanism

Interaction test fails: vol_ratio_5_20 predicts ruin regardless of mom_20 level, or mom_20 fully mediates vol_ratio_5_20 effect → vol_ratio is not an independent mechanism but rather re-expresses momentum state

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Two-stage filter with conditional momentum override: stage 1 rejects B0 candidates with up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55 OR vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.50; stage 2 for borderline candidates (0.50 <= up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.60, 1.30 <= vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.50) applies mom_20 > 0.20 as override criterion
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This structure separates the clear-reject zone from the ambiguous zone, avoiding binary threshold brittleness; the conditional override acknowledges the mechanism's prediction that high momentum can compensate for borderline internals
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: HIGH—directly addresses the primary mechanism claim; capacity to reduce ruin exposure on the ~25% of borderline B0 picks that currently generate disproportionate loss

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Volatility-adjusted position sizing: scale position size inversely with vol_ratio_5_20 for B0 picks where up_day_ratio_20 is borderline (0.50-0.60), rather than rejecting outright; full size only when up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.65 AND vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.30
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This translates the mechanism into a risk-management response (position geometry) rather than a hard filter, preserving upside optionality on cases where the mechanism is uncertain while reducing ruin exposure via geometric exposure management
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: MEDIUM—operationalizes the mechanism's risk gradient rather than binary accept/reject; capacity depends on whether the vol_ratio sizing factor meaningfully differentiates ex-post outcomes

dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This directly addresses the proxy-redundancy attack by using the agreement/disagreement between metrics as a diagnostic signal; divergence may indicate measurement noise or regime-specific distortions that warrant human adjudication
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: MEDIUM—reduces false positives by catching cases where momentum is concentrated in a few large up days rather than distributed; less aggressive than hard filter, more diagnostic than raw threshold

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot-regime conditional application: apply filter rules only when snapshot's median vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.30 (high-churn regime); in low-churn snapshots (median vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.20), the mechanism may not apply and filters should be relaxed
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This scopes the mechanism to the regime where it is hypothesized to operate, avoiding cross-regime generalization that the within-snapshot consistency test would flag as inappropriate; prevents over-filtering in low-volatility environments where the mechanism may be inactive
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: LOW-MEDIUM—conditional application limits capacity utilization to high-churn snapshots; may miss opportunities in low-churn regimes if the mechanism actually generalizes there

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Hold implementation until collinearity and within-snapshot tests pass with pre-registered thresholds; use interim period to accumulate prospective validation cases for power analysis
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This is a meta-policy rather than a filter rule—acknowledges that current evidence is insufficient for live deployment and prioritizes test execution over premature policy deployment; preserves capital during the validation gap
