cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under pullback versus breakout setup; separate true signal from correlated proxy. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: B0 false positives that ruin are structurally vulnerable entries: they score as breakout-quality by trend-momentum features but fail because price has already extended beyond the valid base zone (high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct), leaving insufficient room to absorb normal pullback dynamics. The up_day_ratio_20 deficit in false negatives vs winners (standardized delta -1.19) signals weaker intra-bar conviction, but the ruin outcome in flagged false positives is mechanically driven by entry price geometry, not by a separate momentum failure.
evidence_for: false_positive_ruin cases carry elevated ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (median ~0.038-0.069) versus selected_winner cases (median ~0.025-0.028), meaning they enter the breakout at a price already pulled back from the trigger point

entity_3472243e0c and entity_2c58cebc59 share the same snapshot (snap_71486ed83c), identical up_day_ratio_20=0.65 and similar vol_ratio_5_20 (1.208 vs 1.619), yet one ruins and one wins - the ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (0.029 vs 0.034) differentiates them, suggesting structural entry quality dominates over momentum proxy

The numeric_contrasts show up_day_ratio_20 has the largest standardized delta (-1.1882) between false_negative and selected_winner medians, confirming that intra-bar directional conviction is a PIT-observable signal distinguishing signal quality at the population level

Pullback_pct is unavailable at snapshot for 7 of 8 ruin cases; its unavailability itself is a marker of extended price behavior - when px_vs_ma20 and px_vs_ma50 are both elevated without a pullback having occurred, the entry is structurally late

entity_3adc078f01 survives a -42.3% pullback (w4_return_bucket=large_win) because it entered with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.034 - the deep pullback was absorbable from a non-extended entry; by contrast, entity_8f0df3d38e ruins on -16.2% pullback because ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.069 made it doubly exposed
evidence_against: mom_20 alone cannot separate false_positive_ruin from selected_winner: entity_ead73f4390 (mom_20=0.320) and entity_4fdc3699fd (mom_20=0.185) both have strong momentum yet opposite outcomes - indicating momentum is a necessary but not sufficient condition

vol_ratio_5_20 overlaps substantially between ruin and winner groups (range 0.9-1.6 for both), so volume confirmation alone is not the causal mechanism; it correlates with signal quality but does not mechanistically explain ruin under pullback
Pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct are post-snapshot outcomes, not causal drivers - they cannot be used as predictive features at the PIT snapshot

The px_vs_ma20 and px_vs_ma50 features measure price position relative to averages, which is a consequence of prior momentum, not the mechanical cause of ruin; using them as primary predictors risks confounding the causal chain
falsifiable_predictions: B0 picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.025 will have ruin rate < 10% versus > 30% for picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.050, holding up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20 constant

Among B0 picks with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60 and vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.30, adding ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as a filter (threshold 0.030) will reduce false positive rate by at least 40% without reducing true positive recall by more than 15%
When px_vs_ma50 > 0.15 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.045 simultaneously at snapshot, ruin probability exceeds 60% regardless of mom_20 strength
False positives that ruin will show ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct in the top quartile of that snapshot's B0 candidate distribution more than 65% of the time
policy_implications: Replace or augment current B0 selection logic with an entry-quality gate: reject candidates where ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct exceeds the snapshot-level median by more than 2 standard deviations
Treat up_day_ratio_20 as a pre-filter, not a post-hoc rationalization: candidates below 0.45 should be excluded before evaluating momentum or volume features
Do not use px_vs_ma20 or px_vs_ma50 as standalone predictive features - they are outcome proxies for prior momentum and correlate with ruin when entry timing is already compromised

Construct a composite entry-quality score combining ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (weight ≥ 0.4) and up_day_ratio_20 (weight ≥ 0.3) as the primary signal validity check, with momentum features used only as secondary confirmation

Acknowledge that the current feature set cannot fully resolve cases like entity_3472243e0c vs entity_2c58cebc59 at identical snapshots - additional PIT-observable features (e.g., base depth, consolidation symmetry, sector relative strength) are needed to close the residual gap

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct metric is a confounded proxy for extension risk, not a causal mechanism. The data contains entity_3adc078f01 (pullback_pct = -42.3%, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct = 0.034, large_win) and entity_2c58cebc59 (pullback_pct = -25.1%, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct = 0.034, large_win) — both survive extreme pullbacks despite elevated entry extension, while ruin cases (entity_8f0df3d38e: -16.2%, entity_ccc90a671f: -14.4%) ruin on shallower pullbacks. This pattern indicates the researcher's mechanism conflates entry price geometry with an unmeasured variable (likely sector/market regime) that determines whether a pullback becomes destructive.

attacks.issue: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is a mediator, not a cause
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher treats ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as mechanically causal: high values cause insufficient absorption room. But ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is determined by the timing of the entry signal relative to the base formation. The true causal driver is *why* the entry was signaled late — likely deteriorating institutional sponsorship or sector rotation that also independently causes pullback depth. Using ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as a gate without understanding the upstream cause risks rejecting legitimate signals when the real problem is an unobserved regime shift.

attacks.issue: up_day_ratio_20 is a collider, not a pre-treatment covariate
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher uses up_day_ratio_20 (standardized delta -1.19) as a PIT-observable signal, but directional conviction within the 20-day window may be a downstream effect of sector momentum. If market breadth is the common cause of both elevated up_day_ratio_20 and favorable pullback outcomes, conditioning on up_day_ratio_20 opens a collider bias path, artificially inflating the apparent importance of entry quality features while masking that the true driver is market regime.

attacks.issue: 7 of 8 ruin cases lack pullback_pct — data is not missing at random
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher treats missing pullback_pct as an 'unavailability marker' for extended entries. But pullback_pct is likely missing because ruin cases exit before completing a measurable pullback structure (e.g., stop-loss triggered mid-pullback). This creates a selection artifact: ruin cases appear to have 'extended' entries not because they entered late, but because their failure mode prevents the pullback from being fully recorded. The apparent correlation between high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct and ruin may be an artifact of differential data completeness, not a causal relationship.

attacks.issue: The numeric_contrasts compare false_negative to selected_winner, not false_positive_ruin
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher's evidence anchors on contrasts between false_negative and selected_winner medians (up_day_ratio_20 delta = -1.19), but the actual research question concerns false_positive_ruin. The false_negative group represents *missed winners*, which have fundamentally different characteristics than *false losers that ruin*. Applying feature thresholds derived from false_negative vs selected_winner contrasts to predict false_positive_ruin introduces a category error — the feature-outcome relationships may not generalize across these distinct error types.

attacks.issue: No control for market regime or sector at snapshot time
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher cannot rule out that ruin cases occur disproportionately during sector rotations or market-wide distribution days. If entity_8f0df3d38e and entity_ccc90a671f ruin because their sector broke down *after* entry, while survivors like entity_3adc078f01 benefited from sector continuation, then entry quality features are spurious correlates of outcomes driven by an unobserved third variable (sector strength).

counterexamples_to_seek: B0 picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.050 that generated large_win outcomes — these would directly falsify the entry-quality gate recommendation
B0 picks with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.65 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.045 that generated large_win despite px_vs_ma50 > 0.15 — would undermine the 60% ruin threshold claim
Cross-sector comparison: do high-ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct picks in strong sectors (high sector RS) ruin at the same rate as those in weak sectors? If not, sector is the causal variable
Time-period controls: do the same entry-quality thresholds perform differently in up-market versus down-market snapshots?
Entity with low ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct but ruin outcome — would indicate entry geometry is not the causal driver
what_would_change_my_mind: A controlled experiment holding sector relative strength and market regime constant, showing ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct thresholds maintain predictive power for ruin vs success
Replication of the ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.050 → >30% ruin claim on a held-out sample of B0 picks not used in training (n >= 100)
Evidence that the 7 missing pullback_pct ruin cases are not due to early stop-loss triggering (e.g., reconstructed pullback depth from trade logs)

A mechanistic story for ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct that does not invoke 'absorption room' and instead identifies a specific upstream cause (e.g., late-stage base formation, institutional distribution day pattern) that independently predicts both late entry timing and pullback depth
Comparison showing false_negative and false_positive_ruin groups have *different* feature-outcome relationships, confirming the numeric_contrasts apply to the correct error category

tests.name: false_positive_ruin_vs_selected_winner_direct_contrast
tests.comparison: Median and interquartile range comparison between false_positive_ruin (n=8) and selected_winner (n=11) groups at PIT snapshot

tests.failure_criterion: Any momentum feature (mom_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5) shows larger standardized delta than ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct; or up_day_ratio_20 separates groups as effectively as entry extension

tests.name: missing_pullback_pct_selection_artifact_check

tests.success_criterion: No statistically significant difference (p>0.15) in any PIT feature between the two ruin subgroups; confirming missing pullback_pct is random with respect to snapshot observables

If both retain independent predictive power, they are not downstream colliders. If only ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct survives, up_day_ratio_20 may be confounded

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct has real predictive signal for false_positive_ruin vs selected_winner at the sample level (median delta ~0.015-0.040 between groups), but the causal mechanism is unresolved. The feature likely captures entry timing relative to base completion, yet whether this mechanically causes insufficient pullback absorption or is a proxy for upstream sector/institutional deterioration is not disambiguated by current evidence. The same-snapshot contrasts (entity_3472243e0c vs entity_2c58cebc59) suggest entry quality can differentiate within snapshot clusters, but counterexamples (entity_3adc078f01 surviving -42.3% pullback with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.034) indicate absorption capacity depends on unmeasured compensating factors. The missing pullback_pct in 7/8 ruin cases is a genuine selection artifact risk that cannot be dismissed as random unavailability.
falsifiers: Find B0 picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.050 and w4_return_bucket = large_win in a held-out sample—this directly challenges the proposed entry-quality gate threshold

Replicate the ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.050 → >30% ruin rate claim on external data (n >= 100) without sector conditioning; failure to replicate would confirm the skeptic's regime-dependency claim

Demonstrate that ruin vs win outcomes can be predicted by within-snapshot relative ranking of ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct at >65% accuracy, holding sector regime constant—this would support the causal (not merely correlational) status of entry extension

Confirm via trade logs that the 7 missing pullback_pct ruin cases exited via stop-loss before pullback completion (selection artifact); if confirmed, the apparent extension-ruin correlation is methodological, not causal

Test whether high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct picks in top-sector-RelStrength quartile have ruin rates comparable to low ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct picks—if so, sector regime is the true driver, not entry geometry
actionable_design_principles: Use ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as a conditional severity flag, not a standalone rejection gate: the feature predicts ruin better in combination with low vol_ratio_5_20 or weak sector conditions than in isolation

Treat up_day_ratio_20 as a pre-screening covariate only (below 0.45 excludes candidates before evaluating extension features), not as post-hoc confirmation of entry quality—its collider risk under sector breadth common causes is unresolved

Require sector or market-regime stratification when evaluating ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct thresholds; applying a universal cutoff risks over-rejecting in strong-sector regimes and under-rejecting in weak-sector regimes

Do not use pullback_pct or pullback_duration_weeks as predictive features—they are post-snapshot outcomes unavailable at PIT; missingness in ruin cases should be logged as a structural data-quality flag, not treated as a feature itself

Acknowledge the residual gap: same-snapshot pairs with near-identical PIT features can have opposite outcomes (entity_3472243e0c vs entity_2c58cebc59), indicating additional PIT-observable features (base depth symmetry, sector relative strength, institutional sponsorship proxies) are required to close the prediction boundary

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Sector-Conditioned Entry Extension Gate: Reject B0 candidates where ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.045 AND sector_RS_quartile <= 2, but allow candidates with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.045 when sector_RS_quartile >= 3
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Separates the causal role of entry geometry from regime confounding—the researcher treats ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as universally causal, while this design conditions the gate on sector context, directly testing the skeptic's regime-dependency claim
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Reduces false-positive ruin rate in weak sectors where late entries are genuinely higher-risk; preserves legitimate late entries in strong sectors where absorption capacity is institutionally buffered

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Pullback-Absorption Composite Filter: Score candidates on a two-factor composite (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct normalized by snapshot median + px_vs_ma50 normalized by snapshot median); reject if composite > 0.85 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses the missing_pullback_pct artifact concern by reconstructing a proxy for 'structurally late without pullback buffer' from PIT-observable features, rather than treating high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as sufficient cause
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Explicitly models the interaction between entry extension and volume sponsorship that determines whether a pullback becomes destructive; the vol_ratio_5_20 condition acts as a buffer-test for institutional absorption capacity

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Within-Snapshot Rank-Weighted Selection: For each snapshot, rank B0 candidates by ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct; apply a maximum drawdown rule (do not select any candidate in the top ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct quartile if a bottom-quartile candidate exists in the same snapshot)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Controls for cross-snapshot regime variation by using intra-snapshot relative ranking rather than absolute thresholds; tests the experimental designer's entry_extension_holds_across_sector_regimes hypothesis directly
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Operationalizes the within-snapshot ranking test for ruin prediction; if this rule reduces ruin rate by >25% in held-out data, it supports ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as a causal (not merely correlational) entry quality signal

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: False-Negative Informed Recovery Layer: Flag B0 candidates that are excluded by high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct but have up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.65 AND mom_20 >= 0.15; route these to a monitoring queue for manual review rather than hard rejection
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Directly addresses the researcher's evidence that up_day_ratio_20 deficit separates false_negative from selected_winner—candidates with strong up_day_ratio_20 may deserve conditional reconsideration even when entry extension is elevated, preventing systematic false negatives
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Adds a recovery layer for high-conviction candidates that might otherwise be rejected by a strict entry-quality gate; tests whether up_day_ratio_20 acts as a compensating signal (supporting the researcher's pre-treatment covariate claim) or is merely confounded (supporting the skeptic's collider concern)

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under pullback versus breakout setup; propose a counterexample that would invalidate the pattern. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: B0 picks with tight IBD entry proximity (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.025) combined with insufficient momentum reserve (mom_20 < 0.14) and weak recent price action (up_day_ratio_20 < 0.60) signal exhaustion rather than continuation. The price is already close to the trigger at entry, momentum is depleted, and weak recent up-day participation indicates distribution—creating conditions where a pullback becomes ruin rather than a rest.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The observed ruin outcomes are artifacts of position-concentration risk and drawdown sequencing, not stock-level exhaustion signals. The 'false_positive_ruin' label conflates stocks that were structurally sound but destroyed by portfolio-level forced selling, with stocks that had genuine entry-quality deficits.

attacks.issue: 5 of 8 false_positive_ruin cases have null pullback_pct and null pullback_duration_weeks
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher's mechanism explicitly requires a pullback to 'become ruin' versus 'a rest.' With 62.5% of ruin cases missing pullback data, the mechanism cannot be verified for the majority of its own target outcomes. These cases might represent outright catalyst failures (negative news, earnings collapse) with no relationship to the entry-quality features being studied. The claim is unfalsifiable as stated because the key causal pathway is unobserved in most cases.

attacks.issue: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is a confounded proxy for distance-to-resistance
attacks.why_it_matters: A high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct value (entry close to trigger) is operationally identical to 'stock already made most of its move before the signal fired.' This is not an exhaustion signal per se—it is a lagged-entry artifact. The stock may be extended simply because the trader entered late, not because the stock itself lacks continuation potential. Testing this: entity_2c58cebc59 has ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.034 (above the 0.025 threshold) yet achieves large_win with -25.1% pullback survival. The same proximity measure predicts ruin in some cases and survival in others—revealing it as a confounded, not causal, variable.

attacks.issue: The 27-case sample allows feature mining, not pattern discovery
attacks.why_it_matters: With 8 ruin cases and 11 selected_winner cases across ~20 numeric features, the feature space is over-explored relative to sample size. The median deltas reported (e.g., mom_20 standardized_delta of -1.0005) likely reflect in-sample fit rather than stable predictive relationships. For n=27, a standardized delta of -1.0 on one feature is consistent with random sampling variation. The researcher has no out-of-sample validation for the proposed threshold combination (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.030 AND mom_20 < 0.10 AND up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50...).

attacks.issue: up_day_ratio_20 is a likely market-regime proxy, not a stock-specific distribution signal
attacks.why_it_matters: up_day_ratio_20 measures what fraction of the last 20 days were up days. In a broad market rally, nearly all stocks will have up_day_ratio_20 > 0.50. In a choppy or bearish regime, all stocks will score low regardless of their actual accumulation/distribution profile. If the data comes from mixed market periods, the researcher is measuring market beta rather than entry quality. This would explain why false_positive_ruin cases show low up_day_ratio_20 (market was weak when they were selected) rather than indicating distribution-specific weakness.

attacks.issue: Survival of deep pullbacks in selected_winner cases undermines the exhaustion mechanism's internal logic
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_3adc078f01: mom_20=0.172, pullback_pct=-42.3%, survived to large_win. entity_2c58cebc59: mom_20=0.321, pullback_pct=-25.1%, survived. The researcher's own mechanism states 'weak prior momentum provides recovery buffer.' But these cases show that even moderate momentum (0.17-0.32) is sufficient to survive 25-42% drawdowns. If that's true, then the 'depleted momentum' threshold of mom_20 < 0.14 cannot be the operative mechanism—these stocks would need to have negative or near-zero momentum to match the 'ruin' prediction. Yet ruin cases like entity_84824e6a20 (mom_20=0.067) have modest but non-zero momentum. The mechanism requires a sharp momentum cutoff that the data does not support.

attacks.issue: Selection-on-dependent-variable: stocks that ruin under pullback may have been stopped out before completing the pullback, biasing pullback_pct toward smaller values in the ruin cohort
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher observes that ruin cases have 'smaller pullback_pct' than some winners. But this is expected under any exit-trigger mechanism: stocks stopped out at -12% are labeled 'ruin' and contribute pullback_pct=-12%, while stocks that survive to -40% are labeled 'large_win' and contribute -40%. The observed relationship between pullback_pct and outcome is tautological, not causal. The true counterfactual—'would this stock have ruined at -40%?'—is unobserved.

counterexamples_to_seek: A B0 pick with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.035, mom_20 < 0.08, up_day_ratio_20 < 0.45, vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.40, px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 that achieves w4_return_bucket=large_win. This would falsify the composite threshold claim directly.

A B0 pick from the same snapshot_anon cohort that has all the 'winning' features (mom_20 > 0.16, up_day_ratio_20 > 0.65, wide ibd_entry) but still ruins. This would isolate whether the features predict ruin or whether ruin is driven by exogenous factors.

Cross-snapshot comparison: Do the same feature thresholds produce the same ruin rates at different market-regime snapshots? If snap_71486ed83c shows 40% ruin rate for tight-entry+low-momentum picks but snap_287267e812 shows 10%, regime is the dominant variable.

Time-to-event data: For cases with null pullback_pct, what was the time from entry to ruin event? If ruin cases resolve in <2 weeks versus 7+ weeks for observed pullbacks, the mechanism is not pullback-based at all.
what_would_change_my_mind: Replication of the same feature thresholds (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.025, mom_20 < 0.14, up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55) on an independent sample of B0 picks with >50 ruin cases, showing significant ruin-rate elevation.
Time-series validation: Stocks identified by these thresholds in earlier time periods (before the study window) show elevated ruin rates in subsequent periods, demonstrating temporal stability.

Mechanism isolation: Showing that ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct predicts ruin even after residualizing out px_vs_ma50 (distance-to-resistance) and market-regime-adjusted up_day_ratio_20. If the proxy is causal, it should survive deconfounding.
Experimental validation: Real-time application of the pre-filter rule (reject tight-entry + low-momentum picks) over a forward period, with ruin rate reduction as the outcome metric.

tests.name: pullback_mediation_test
tests.comparison: Among B0 picks with non-null pullback_pct, decompose whether ruin prediction from mom_20, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, and up_day_ratio_20 operates through pullback depth or independently
tests.success_criterion: mom_20 and ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct remain significant predictors of ruin (false_positive_ruin vs selected_winner) after conditioning on pullback_pct, confirming exhaustion mechanism is not fully mediated by pullback observation
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin prediction from snapshot-time features is fully explained by pullback_pct; features lose significance when pullback_pct is conditioned on, indicating pullback is the causal variable and features are proxies

tests.name: null_pullback_structural_test
tests.comparison: Compare snapshot-time feature distributions between ruin cases with null pullback_pct versus ruin cases with non-null pullback_pct
tests.success_criterion: No significant distributional difference on snapshot-time features between null-pullback ruin and non-null-pullback ruin, supporting unified mechanism
tests.failure_criterion: Null-pullback ruin cases systematically differ from non-null-pullback ruin cases on snapshot-time features (e.g., lower mom_20, different px_vs_ma50), indicating different causal pathways and invalidating single-mechanism claim

tests.name: up_day_ratio_regime_confound_test
tests.comparison: Test whether up_day_ratio_20 ruin-predictive power persists within snapshot strata or is entirely cross-snapshot (regime-driven)
tests.success_criterion: Within each snapshot_anon, lower up_day_ratio_20 is associated with higher ruin rate among B0 picks, confirming stock-specific distribution signal
tests.failure_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 effect on ruin is entirely explained by snapshot membership; within-snapshot up_day_ratio_20 shows no ruin association, confirming it is a market-regime proxy

tests.name: tight_entry_confound_test
tests.comparison: Test whether ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct ruin-predictive power survives residualization against distance-to-resistance (px_vs_ma50) and momentum (mom_20)
tests.success_criterion: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct remains a significant ruin predictor after controlling for px_vs_ma50 and mom_20, confirming it captures exhaustion beyond lagged-entry and resistance distance
tests.failure_criterion: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct effect on ruin is fully explained by px_vs_ma50 (distance-to-resistance) or mom_20 (momentum), confirming it is a confounded proxy rather than a causal signal

tests.name: composite_threshold_counterexample_test
tests.comparison: Seek any B0 pick satisfying the researcher's tight-entry composite: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.030 AND mom_20 < 0.10 AND up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.30 AND px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 that achieves w4_return_bucket=large_win
tests.success_criterion: Zero cases in the sample satisfy the composite conditions AND achieve large_win, supporting the exhaustion-signal mechanism
tests.failure_criterion: At least one case satisfies all composite conditions AND achieves large_win, directly falsifying the exhaustion-signal mechanism

tests.name: ruin_clustering_test
tests.comparison: Test whether ruin outcomes cluster at specific snapshot_anon values, indicating regime-driven destruction versus stock-specific entry-quality failure
tests.success_criterion: Ruin rate does not significantly vary across snapshot_anon values among B0 picks with matched feature profiles, confirming stock-specific rather than regime-driven ruin mechanism
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin rate significantly varies across snapshot_anon (e.g., >2x ruin rate at some snapshots), indicating portfolio-construction or market-regime factors dominate stock-level features

leakage_checks: w4_return_bucket is outcome variable, not a PIT feature; all tests must use snapshot-time features only
outcome_label is post-hoc classification; tests should not condition on specific label values that would require future knowledge
pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are realized values, not snapshot-time features; tests using these must explicitly address the 62.5% null rate and potential selection bias
snapshot_anon is a grouping variable, not a predictor; it can be used to test cross-regime stability but not as a feature itself
Tests should not use entity_anon or any temporal identifier as a feature

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The exhaustion-signal mechanism (tight IBD entry + depleted momentum + weak up-day ratio → ruin) is structurally plausible and internally consistent. The composite counterexample test (researcher) found zero large_win cases meeting the full threshold, providing weak support. However, the mechanism faces three compounding weaknesses: (1) 5 of 8 ruin cases have null pullback_pct, making the 'pullback-to-ruin' causal pathway unverifiable for the majority of target outcomes; (2) ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is a lagged-entry artifact that correlates with distance-to-resistance, failing the tight_entry_confound_test in at least one case (entity_2c58cebc59 has ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.034 yet achieves large_win); (3) the 27-case discovery sample does not support confident threshold calibration, and standardized deltas of -1.0 at n=27 are consistent with random variation. The evidence supports a weak, context-dependent signal rather than a stable mechanism.
falsifiers: Composite counterexample: A B0 pick with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.030 AND mom_20 < 0.10 AND up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.30 AND px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 achieving w4_return_bucket=large_win. This would directly falsify the exhaustion-signal mechanism. Currently zero such cases exist in-sample.

Cross-snapshot ruin-rate invariance: If B0 picks meeting exhaustion thresholds show ruin rates varying by >2x across snapshot_anon cohorts (e.g., 40% ruin at snap_71486ed83c vs 8% at snap_287267e812), regime effects dominate stock-level features, invalidating the mechanism.

Null-pullback structural divergence: If ruin cases with null pullback_pct differ significantly from non-null-pullback ruin cases on snapshot-time features (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct), the mechanism operates through different causal pathways and the unified claim is false.

Time-to-event falsification: If null-pullback ruin cases resolve in <2 weeks from entry versus 7+ weeks for observed pullback cases, the null cases reflect catalyst events (earnings, news) not entry-quality exhaustion.

Tight-entry survival with depleted momentum: A B0 pick with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.040, mom_20 < 0.08, and up_day_ratio_20 < 0.45 achieving w4_return_bucket=large_win would falsify the composite threshold claim at stricter bounds.
actionable_design_principles: Require non-null pullback_pct for mechanism-based filtering; exclude null-pullback cases from exhaustion-signal logic and treat them as separate risk category (potential catalyst failures)
Prefer ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.020 as necessary condition for confidence in B0 picks; tighter entries require proportionally stronger momentum buffer (mom_20 > 0.20) to compensate
Do not apply up_day_ratio_20 as a standalone filter; it is confounded with market regime and should only be used within snapshot-stratified analysis
Tight-entry B0 picks (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.025) require stop-loss discipline at entry - 8%, as pullback-to-ruin appears to crystallize at -12% to -16% for this cohort

Do not use composite thresholds derived from n<50 without out-of-sample validation; the current threshold calibration (ibd_entry > 0.030, mom < 0.10, up_day < 0.50, vol > 1.30, px_ma50 < 0.08) is likely overfitted

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Exhaustion Composite Pre-Filter with Mandatory Pullback Confirmation
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This is the only policy that explicitly addresses the skeptic's null-pullback attack. Prior designs treat null-pullback cases as missing data; this policy quarantines them as a distinct risk class requiring separate handling.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity-based position sizing: apply exhaustion pre-filter only to cases with observable pullback trajectory; null-pullback cases receive capacity-weighted reduction regardless of other features

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Momentum-Buffffered Entry Proximity Rule
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Instead of rejecting tight entries outright, this policy scales momentum buffer requirements inversely with entry proximity—addressing the skeptic's concern that ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is a lagged-entry proxy rather than a causal signal.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity allocation: assign higher capacity to tight-entry picks with strong momentum buffer (mom_20 > 0.20) or sufficient distance to resistance (px_vs_ma50 > 0.12); reduce capacity for tight-entry picks with low momentum AND low resistance distance

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot-Stratified Exhaustion Threshold
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This directly tests the skeptic's regime-confound hypothesis by deriving separate exhaustion thresholds per snapshot_anon. If thresholds are stable across snapshots, regime concern is minimal; if thresholds diverge substantially, the mechanism is regime-dependent.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Cross-snapshot capacity balancing: if exhaustion thresholds are tighter in certain snapshots (higher ruin rates), reduce capacity allocation to tight-entry picks in those regimes

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under near-buy-point geometry; identify repeated PIT-visible precursors. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-positive B0 picks occur when price is moderately extended above the 50-day moving average (px_vs_ma50 in 0.07-0.12 range) while internal momentum quality is mediocre (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55). This creates an unstable equilibrium where the stock has drifted up enough to trigger a breakout signal but lacks the sustained internal strength to survive the inevitable pullback near the buy point. Winners show px_vs_ma50 > 0.12 with up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.60, giving them structural altitude to absorb pullbacks without violating stop-loss geometry.
evidence_for: entity_8f0df3d38e: px_vs_ma50=0.088 (moderately extended), up_day_ratio_20=0.65 (borderline), outcome=false_positive_ruin with -16.2% pullback over 7 weeks
entity_4fdc3699fd: px_vs_ma50=0.102 (moderate), up_day_ratio_20=0.60, outcome=ruin despite positive momentum
entity_3472243e0c: px_vs_ma50=0.075 (low-moderate), up_day_ratio_20=0.65, outcome=ruin, confirming px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 is dangerous even with decent up_day_ratio
entity_ccc90a671f: px_vs_ma50=0.090, up_day_ratio_20=0.50 (weak), outcome=ruin with -14.4% pullback
entity_84824e6a20: px_vs_ma50=0.068, up_day_ratio_20=0.40 (very weak), outcome=ruin; dual-weakness case
In contrast, entity_ead73f4390: px_vs_ma50=0.185 (high), up_day_ratio_20=0.70 → large_win
entity_3adc078f01: px_vs_ma50=0.131, up_day_ratio_20=0.65 → large_win despite -42.3% pullback (sustained structural altitude)
The numeric_contrasts table confirms this: false_negative median px_vs_ma50=0.056 versus selected_winner median=0.127, standardized_delta=-0.8545, the 4th strongest differentiator
up_day_ratio_20 has standardized_delta=-1.1882 (strongest differentiator): false_negative median 0.50 versus selected_winner median 0.625
evidence_against: entity_b6bcccdf6a: px_vs_ma50=0.182 (high), up_day_ratio_20=0.40 (weak) → outcome=loss, suggesting up_day_ratio alone has predictive floor

entity_2c58cebc59: px_vs_ma50=0.170 (high), up_day_ratio_20=0.60, pullback_pct=-25.1% → still selected_winner (large_win), consistent with mechanism but shows high-extension winners can still have large pullbacks before recovering
entity_40ea0cfb3b: px_vs_ma50=0.014 (very low), up_day_ratio_20=0.50 → ruin, fits mechanism but also suggests extremely compressed price action (near MA50) can fail differently (no momentum at all)

The mechanism does not fully explain entity_2f86543bf6: up_day_ratio_20=0.35 (weak), px_vs_ma50=0.017 (very low) → selected_winner (large_win); this case suggests alternative pathway where low expectations create low-risk entries

Pullback depth alone is not predictive: entity_3adc078f01 had -42.3% pullback but won; entity_8f0df3d38e had -16.2% pullback but ruined. The critical variable is price altitude relative to MAs at entry, not pullback magnitude.
falsifiable_predictions: In a forward B0 sample, stocks with px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55 will have >60% false-positive-ruin rate versus baseline B0 ruin rate
Stocks with px_vs_ma50 > 0.15 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.60 will have <15% false-positive-ruin rate versus baseline

The zone px_vs_ma50 ∈ [0.08, 0.15] AND up_day_ratio_20 ∈ [0.55, 0.65] will show non-linear ruin probability, higher than both the low-extension and high-extension zones, confirming the unstable-equilibrium hypothesis
vol_ratio_5_20 will NOT independently predict false-positive-ruin within px_vs_ma50/up_day_ratio_20 strata (mechanism is structural, not volatility-driven)
If a snapshot shows ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.06 AND the two core predictors are in the danger zone, ruin probability should exceed 70%
policy_implications: Add px_vs_ma50 and up_day_ratio_20 as mandatory pre-trade filters; reject B0 picks when both are in the moderate-weak zone
Do NOT use vol_ratio_5_20 as a filter for this failure mode—it is a confound, not a cause

Consider a three-tier classification: (1) structural winners: px_vs_ma50 > 0.15, up_day_ratio > 0.60 → proceed; (2) unstable zone: px_vs_ma50 0.08-0.15, up_day_ratio 0.55-0.65 → require additional confirmation; (3) structural losers: px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 or up_day_ratio < 0.55 → auto-reject or reduce position size
For existing positions near buy points, if px_vs_ma50 drops below 0.08 while up_day_ratio falls below 0.55, tighten stops preemptively—this is a PIT-observable deterioration pattern
Pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct should NOT be used at snapshot time to predict ruin—they are post-entry labels. Use only pre-entry structural metrics.

The ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct threshold of ~0.07 appears in multiple ruin cases (entity_8f0df3d38e: 0.069, entity_4fdc3699fd: 0.069, entity_84824e6a20: 0.074, entity_40ea0cfb3b: 0.061)—consider combining this with the structural metrics as a composite filter

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The px_vs_ma50 mechanism is a post-hoc artifact of differential move maturity, not a causal structural filter. B0 signals that fire at lower px_vs_ma50 values simply occur earlier in emerging bases—whereas signals firing at higher px_vs_ma50 are late-stage breakouts from extended bases that have already proven strength. The 'structural altitude' interpretation confuses correlation with the true driver: stocks that have already demonstrated sustained internal strength (measured by up_day_ratio) tend to have drifted further from the MA50 before breaking out. The mechanism confuses this natural co-occurrence with a protective effect of altitude.

attacks.issue: Circular mechanism construction: px_vs_ma50 and up_day_ratio_20 are not independent inputs—they are both outcomes of the same underlying process (prior price strength). The mechanism claims altitude protects against pullback, but altitude is simply the accumulated result of the prior strength that up_day_ratio also measures. Testing whether px_vs_ma50 adds predictive power beyond up_day_ratio within strata would require conditioning on up_day_ratio first, which the numeric_contrasts do not perform.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the true predictor is only up_day_ratio (or momentum quality), then px_vs_ma50 is a spurious proxy that will fail out-of-sample when base-building patterns vary. The mechanism attributes protective power to altitude that actually resides in the prior momentum that produced the altitude.

attacks.issue: The unstable-equilibrium zone [0.08, 0.15] for px_vs_ma50 is not a natural regime—it is a measurement artifact of when B0 signals tend to fire. Most valid B0 picks will naturally fall in this range because the IBD entry framework triggers on pullback-to-base patterns that produce moderate extension. The ruin rate difference may reflect that moderate extension picks are simply more common, not that they are structurally unstable.
attacks.why_it_matters: The zone boundaries are derived from the sample distribution, not from an independent structural threshold. If the true base-failure mechanism is something else (e.g., base depth, mbox count), then px_vs_ma50 stratification is capturing nothing but a sampling artifact of signal frequency.

attacks.issue: The labeling of entity_6618d3e80c as both 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' invalidates treating outcome labels as clean binary partitions. If a single entity can carry both labels, the feature-outcome associations computed from labeled groups are contaminated by internal label inconsistency.
attacks.why_it_matters: Any statistical comparison between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner groups is undermined when the group memberships themselves are uncertain. The median contrasts and standardized deltas may be comparing apples to oranges.

attacks.issue: up_day_ratio_20 measures directional frequency, not magnitude. A stock with 7 up days of +0.3% each and 3 down days of -0.1% each would have up_day_ratio=0.70 but negligible actual momentum. The mechanism assumes this metric captures 'internal strength' without accounting for the magnitude asymmetry that determines whether pullbacks are survivable.
attacks.why_it_matters: Two stocks with identical up_day_ratio can have radically different pullback tolerance. The mechanism will misclassify stocks with high frequency but low magnitude (false positive) and low frequency but high magnitude (false negative). The numeric_contrasts do not include magnitude measures, so this confound cannot be detected.

attacks.issue: The vol_ratio_5_20 standardized_delta of -1.0455 (3rd strongest differentiator) is dismissed as a confound, but the researcher provides no analysis of whether it mediates, moderates, or is spurious relative to the proposed mechanism. The rule says to avoid using vol_ratio for this failure mode, but this decision is asserted, not demonstrated.
attacks.why_it_matters: If vol_ratio is a mediator (high vol → larger pullbacks → higher ruin probability given moderate extension), then filtering on vol_ratio would improve the mechanism's accuracy. The dismissal of vol_ratio is not falsifiable from the provided evidence.

counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where px_vs_ma50 > 0.15 AND up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55 but outcome = selected_winner (large_win), to test whether altitude alone predicts survival without internal momentum quality
Cases where px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.65 but outcome = false_positive_ruin, to test whether low altitude is sufficient to cause ruin regardless of internal quality
Cases where vol_ratio_5_20 is very low (<1.0) and px_vs_ma50 is in the 'danger zone' but outcome = selected_winner, to test whether low volatility eliminates the ruin effect

Within a single snapshot, compare B0 picks with identical px_vs_ma50 but different up_day_ratio_20 values—if the mechanism holds, up_day_ratio should predict ruin conditional on altitude, but if the effect disappears, altitude is doing all the work
what_would_change_my_mind: A conditional analysis showing that within px_vs_ma50 quartiles, up_day_ratio_20 retains independent predictive power after residualizing out px_vs_ma50—this would establish up_day_ratio as a genuine moderator rather than a co-conspirator in a single underlying factor

A time-split validation: if the px_vs_ma50/up_day_ratio thresholds derived from one time period predict ruin rates in a held-out period at above-chance rates, this would falsify the sampling-artifact hypothesis

Evidence that px_vs_ma50 thresholds map to distinct base geometries (e.g., flat bases vs. ascending bases) rather than merely reflecting how far along the prior move had progressed—this would establish the mechanism as structurally meaningful

A demonstration that the ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.06 ruin cases are explained by the two-factor mechanism and not by a third unmeasured variable (e.g., sector rotation, market cap, relative strength rank)

tests.name: px_vs_ma50_conditional_independence
tests.comparison: Within up_day_ratio_20 tertiles, does px_vs_ma50 predict false_positive_ruin vs selected_winner? Test H0: px_vs_ma50 coefficient = 0 within each stratum.
tests.success_criterion: px_vs_ma50 coefficient significant (p<0.05) within at least 2 of 3 up_day_ratio_20 tertiles, with ruin probability increasing monotonically with px_vs_ma50 within strata. This confirms altitude has independent protective value beyond internal momentum quality.
tests.failure_criterion: px_vs_ma50 coefficient becomes non-significant within up_day_ratio_20 strata, OR direction reverses. This supports skeptic's circularity claim that altitude is merely a proxy for accumulated momentum.

tests.name: residualized_altitude_predictive_power
tests.comparison: Regress px_vs_ma50 on mom_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20. Use residuals as 'altitude orthogonal to momentum'. Test whether this residual predicts ruin.
tests.success_criterion: Residualized altitude shows significant association with ruin (standardized_delta < -0.3 from selected_winner median to ruin median). This would falsify the claim that altitude is purely a momentum byproduct.
tests.failure_criterion: Residualized altitude has no predictive power (standardized_delta near 0, p>0.10). This confirms altitude is fully explained by momentum features, supporting the skeptic's strongest counterclaim.

tests.name: vol_ratio_mediation_path
tests.comparison: Test whether vol_ratio_5_20 operates as: (a) independent predictor, (b) mediator of px_vs_ma50→ruin, or (c) moderator of the px_vs_ma50/up_day_ratio_20 interaction. Use Baron-Kenny style nested model comparison.
tests.success_criterion: vol_ratio_5_20 adds significant predictive power (ΔAIC > 2) when added to the two-factor mechanism model. This means it should be treated as a genuine third filter, not dismissed.
tests.failure_criterion: vol_ratio_5_20 effect fully absorbed when px_vs_ma50 and up_day_ratio_20 are included (change in coefficient < 10%, no ΔAIC improvement). Confirms researcher's dismissal as confound/spurious.

tests.name: up_day_ratio_magnitude_interaction
tests.comparison: Split selected_winner and false_positive_ruin cases by mom_20 median (0.16). Within each momentum magnitude band, test whether up_day_ratio_20 still differentiates winners from ruin.
tests.success_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 retains predictive power within both high-momentum and low-momentum bands (standardized_delta > 0.5 in both), confirming frequency captures genuine internal strength distinct from magnitude.
tests.failure_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 effect disappears in high-momentum band (standardized_delta < 0.2), only significant in low-momentum band. This supports skeptic's attack that up_day_ratio is inadequate when magnitude is favorable.

tests.name: label_contamination_detection
tests.comparison: Apply k-means (k=2) clustering to features of: (a) pure false_positive_ruin cases, (b) pure selected_winner cases, (c) entity_6618d3e80c. Determine cluster assignment probability for entity_6618d3e80c.
tests.success_criterion: entity_6618d3e80c assigned to a single cluster with >80% probability, clearly aligning with either ruin or winner centroid. This validates clean label separation.
tests.failure_criterion: entity_6618d3e80c has near-50% probability in both clusters (max probability <65%). This validates skeptic's contamination concern and undermines group comparison statistics.

tests.name: snapshot_boundary_stability
tests.comparison: Compute ruin rates for each px_vs_ma50/up_day_ratio_20 zone separately within each unique snapshot. Test whether the 'unstable zone' pattern (high ruin probability in 0.08-0.15 px_vs_ma50, 0.55-0.65 up_day_ratio) replicates across snapshots.
tests.success_criterion: Unstable zone shows ruin rate > 2x baseline in at least 3 of 4 unique snapshots (snap_724342c280, snap_71486ed83c, snap_d0d57b1e40, snap_b8420124eb). This falsifies the sampling artifact hypothesis.
tests.failure_criterion: Unstable zone ruin rate varies widely across snapshots (coefficient of variation > 1.0), or pattern reverses in any snapshot. This supports measurement artifact claim.

leakage_checks: pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct must not appear as test features—they are post-entry labels unavailable at snapshot time
w4_return_bucket is an outer-forward outcome and must not be used as a predictor; only use outcome_label derived at appropriate horizon
Feature engineering for residualized altitude must use only PIT features (mom_20, slopes, ratios) that would be observable at snapshot, not future price derivatives
Snapshot identity (snap_*) must not enter as a feature—test on pooled entity-level observations, not snapshot-level aggregates
Entity identity (entity_*) must not enter as a feature or conditioning variable

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The px_vs_ma50/up_day_ratio_20 mechanism is empirically suggestive but causally underdetermined. False-positive ruin cases do cluster in the moderate-extension/weak-internal-strength quadrant (px_vs_ma50 < 0.10, up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55), consistent with the researcher's unstable-equilibrium claim. However, the skeptic's circularity attack has not been falsified: px_vs_ma50 is causally downstream of prior momentum (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20), so attributing 'protective altitude' to it may conflate correlation with mechanism. The vol_ratio_5_20 standardized_delta of -1.0455 (3rd strongest) is dismissed without mediation analysis, leaving a genuine confound unresolved. The mechanism survives as a useful descriptive pattern for pre-trade filtering, but should not be treated as a proven causal architecture.
falsifiers: residualized_altitude_predictive_power test fails: residualized px_vs_ma50 (orthogonal to mom_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20) shows standardized_delta > -0.2 for ruin vs. selected_winner. This would confirm the skeptic's circularity claim that altitude is purely a momentum byproduct.

px_vs_ma50_conditional_independence test fails: within up_day_ratio_20 tertiles, px_vs_ma50 coefficient becomes non-significant (p > 0.10). This would indicate altitude has no independent protective value beyond accumulated momentum.

vol_ratio_mediation_path test succeeds unexpectedly: vol_ratio_5_20 adds ΔAIC > 2 when added to px_vs_ma50 + up_day_ratio_20 model, with >10% coefficient change. This would falsify the researcher's dismissal and require treating volatility as a genuine third factor.

up_day_ratio_magnitude_interaction test fails: up_day_ratio_20 loses predictive power in the high-momentum band (standardized_delta < 0.3), only active in low-momentum band. This would confirm the skeptic's attack that frequency alone is inadequate.

Snapshot boundary instability: the unstable-zone ruin pattern does not replicate across at least 3 of 4 unique snapshots (coefficient of variation > 1.0). This would support the sampling-artifact hypothesis over structural mechanism.

Counterexample emergence: any case with px_vs_ma50 > 0.15 AND up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55 but outcome = selected_winner (large_win) would falsify the claim that high altitude compensates for weak internal quality.
Counterexample emergence: any case with px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.65 but outcome = false_positive_ruin would falsify the claim that low extension is safe with strong internal quality.
actionable_design_principles: Treat the two-factor pattern as a provisional pre-trade heuristic, not a proven causal mechanism. Use it for soft rejection (increased scrutiny, reduced sizing) rather than hard categorical exclusion.

Reject using vol_ratio_5_20 as an independent filter for this failure mode until the mediation path is resolved empirically. It may be a proxy for pullback magnitude, which is itself a post-entry label.
Never use pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_pct, or w4_return_bucket as predictors at snapshot time—these are post-entry labels that would introduce look-ahead bias.
Do not use entity identity or snapshot identity as features. Test on pooled entity-level observations with outcome labels derived at appropriate horizons.

The ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct threshold of ~0.06-0.07 appears in multiple ruin cases and is orthogonal to the structural metrics. Treat it as a potential composite trigger but validate independently before treating as a filter.

Reserve judgment on the three-tier classification until conditional independence testing is complete. The 'unstable zone' may be a sampling artifact of when B0 signals fire, not a natural structural regime.

Monitor entity_6618d3e80c carefully: its dual-label status suggests either measurement error in outcome assignment or genuine label ambiguity that undermines group-comparison statistics for similar mixed cases.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Structural Loser Soft-Reject Filter: flag B0 picks where px_vs_ma50 < 0.08 OR up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55 for elevated scrutiny, position-size reduction, or confirmation requirement.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Operates on pre-entry structural metrics that are observable at snapshot time, not on post-entry outcomes. Differs from hard exclusion by allowing human override with justification.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Filters B0 candidate universe before position construction; reduces ruin-type false-positive rate at cost of potentially missing some winners.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Unstable Zone Conditional Confirmation: require additional confirmation (e.g., volume spike, sector catalyst, relative strength rank check) when px_vs_ma50 ∈ [0.08, 0.15] AND up_day_ratio_20 ∈ [0.55, 0.65].
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Targets the specific quadrant where ruin and winner outcomes overlap most, without applying blanket restrictions to the full candidate set.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Conditional gate that preserves optionality in the ambiguous middle zone while still filtering clear structural losers.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Composite Entry Quality Score: combine px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, mom_20, and ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct into a single ordinal score, with separate validation that the score predicts ruin at above-chance rates.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Replaces binary accept/reject with graded confidence, allowing position sizing proportional to structural quality. Explicitly tests whether composite score outperforms individual features.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Enables portfolio construction to weight by structural confidence rather than equal-sizing across B0 picks.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Volatility Proportional Stop Adjustment: do not filter on vol_ratio_5_20, but use it to scale stop-loss geometry when in the unstable zone (wider stops in high-vol, tighter in low-vol) to account for noise-driven stop violations.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Treats vol_ratio as a position-construction parameter rather than a filter, avoiding the conflation issue while still using the information.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Preserves optionality while managing post-entry risk through dynamic stop geometry.

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under near-buy-point geometry; separate true signal from correlated proxy. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-positive B0 picks fail not from lack of short-term momentum, but from price extension into declining longer-term trend velocity. The specific failure mode is: (1) weak 20-day momentum (mom_20 < 0.10) combined with price already close to MA20 (px_vs_ma20 < 0.05) leaving no base-building room, or (2) strong momentum but up_day_ratio_20 divergence signaling accumulation exhaustion and imminent distribution. up_day_ratio_20 acts as a correlated proxy for quality rather than a true signal—it captures recent behavior but not the underlying trend architecture that determines whether a pullback is healthy or catastrophic.
evidence_for: false_positive_ruin cases cluster into two distinct geometries: entity_40ea0cfb3b (mom_20=0.024, px_vs_ma20=0.028, up_day_ratio_20=0.5) and entity_55c2da490e (mom_20=0.036, px_vs_ma20=0.058) show weak momentum with price already near MA20—no base depth available for normal pullbacks; entity_8f0df3d38e (mom_20=0.176, up_day_ratio_20=0.65) and entity_3472243e0c (mom_20=0.242, up_day_ratio_20=0.65) show strong momentum but elevated recent up-day ratio signaling divergence from trend
selected_winner median mom_20=0.163 vs false_positive_ruin median ~0.145; winners have meaningful trend substance, not just recent acceleration
selected_winner px_vs_ma20 median ~0.076 vs false_positive_ruin ~0.064; winners have more runway above immediate resistance

numeric_contrasts show standardized_delta for mom_20 at -1.0005 and up_day_ratio_20 at -1.1882—the joint condition of low momentum AND low recent participation is the killer combination, not either alone
entity_8ad5cd4795 (selected_winner, up_day_ratio_20=0.7) disproves high up_day_ratio_20 alone being harmful; it has positive ma10_slope_5=0.044 and good momentum support
evidence_against: up_day_ratio_20=0.65 in entity_8f0df3d38e (false_positive_ruin) vs up_day_ratio_20=0.65 in entity_3adc078f01 (selected_winner with 42.3% pullback but large_win outcome)—the same feature value produces different results depending on base momentum architecture
vol_ratio_5_20 shows mixed signal: false_positive_ruin includes cases with both high (1.449) and low (0.906) volume ratios, suggesting it's not a primary filter
px_vs_ma50 alone doesn't separate: entity_ead73f4390 (selected_winner) has px_vs_ma50=0.185 while entity_8f0df3d38e (false_positive_ruin) has px_vs_ma50=0.088—need joint condition with mom_20
falsifiable_predictions: B0 picks with mom_20 < 0.08 AND px_vs_ma20 < 0.05 will produce ruin outcomes at >60% rate within 4 weeks

B0 picks with mom_20 > 0.15 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 AND ma20_slope_5 < 0.015 will produce ruin outcomes at >50% rate—prediction: adding ma20_slope_5 filter to the divergence condition identifies climax behavior specifically

B0 picks with mom_20 between 0.08-0.20 AND px_vs_ma20 > 0.08 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.5 will produce winners at >65% rate—prediction: the combination of moderate momentum, price not extended, and normal volume defines the survivable base
policy_implications: Reject B0 picks where mom_20 < 0.10 regardless of up_day_ratio_20—the trend foundation is insufficient for normal pullback absorption
Flag (don't reject) B0 picks where up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 but only if ma20_slope_5 > 0.025; if ma20_slope_5 < 0.020 on such picks, treat as high-ruin-risk despite positive momentum signal
Treat px_vs_ma20 as a positional proxy for remaining base depth—require px_vs_ma20 > 0.05 minimum, with tighter requirement (px_vs_ma20 > 0.10) for lower-momentum stocks
up_day_ratio_20 should be used as a risk modifier, not a primary signal—its predictive power is conditional on momentum architecture, not standalone

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The entire classification of false_positive_ruin vs selected_winner is partially defined by post-snapshot W4 returns (method_note explicitly states false negatives require future W4 >=8%), making the snapshot features retroactively correlated with outcomes they did not predict. The researcher is identifying features that describe already-failed picks, not features that would have predicted failure at snapshot time.

attacks.issue: Circular outcome definition
attacks.why_it_matters: The w4_return_bucket directly determines false_positive_ruin classification. A case labeled 'ruin' is ruin because W4 return was bad—not because of any intrinsic failure mode. Features correlated with W4 return are therefore definitionally correlated with the label, not mechanistically causing failure. The researcher never tests whether these features predict W4 return independently of the label construction.

attacks.issue: Proxy-squared problem
attacks.why_it_matters: px_vs_ma20 is claimed to proxy base depth, but base_depth_pct is a separate feature in the numeric_contrasts with weak standardized_delta=0.1942. If base depth matters, use it directly. Conflating position (px_vs_ma20) with structure (base depth) creates a measurement proxy for a measurement proxy—amplifying noise without clear mechanism.

attacks.issue: up_day_ratio_20 classification inconsistency
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_3adc078f01 has up_day_ratio_20=0.65 and is selected_winner, but entity_8f0df3d38e also has up_day_ratio_20=0.65 and is false_positive_ruin. The researcher explains this via 'momentum architecture' but provides no operationalized definition of what constitutes divergent vs coherent architecture beyond post-hoc case fitting.

attacks.issue: Small-N threshold instability
attacks.why_it_matters: With only 8 false_positive_ruin cases, mom_20<0.10 and px_vs_ma20<0.05 thresholds lack power. A single additional case could shift thresholds by 30-50%. Predictions of >60% ruin rates from N=8 are confidence intervals in name only.

attacks.issue: Missing mechanism for why high up_day_ratio_20 causes accumulation exhaustion
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher claims up_day_ratio_20 divergence signals 'imminent distribution' but provides no model of order flow, market microstructure, or volume composition that would make this claim mechanistically plausible. It reads as narrative explanation for a statistical correlation.

attacks.issue: No test of the alternative: mechanical top-capture hypothesis
attacks.why_it_matters: An equally plausible mechanism: B0 picks fire mechanically when price crosses trigger thresholds. Winners happen when that cross occurs during genuine trend continuation; false positives happen when it occurs at momentum exhaustion points. This mechanism requires NO feature-based prediction—only that the trigger itself is placed at varying positions along the trend curve. If true, snapshot features are epiphenomenal.

counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where mom_20<0.10 AND px_vs_ma20<0.05 but outcome was selected_winner—currently missing from evidence, would directly falsify the primary failure-mode claim
B0 picks with identical snapshot features but different market-regime tags (e.g., trending vs choppy) to test whether regime, not features, drives outcomes
Cases where up_day_ratio_20>0.60 AND ma20_slope_5<0.020 that were selected_winner—currently no clear counterexample exists but absence of search doesn't confirm impossibility
A temporal analysis: do false_positive_ruin cases cluster at specific points within their snapshot windows, suggesting entry-timing noise rather than feature-based prediction
what_would_change_my_mind: A controlled backtest showing that the proposed feature-based filter (mom_20<0.10 or up_day_ratio_20 divergence conditions) improves out-of-sample win rate by >10 percentage points vs unfiltered B0 picks across a minimum of 100 cases

Market microstructure evidence that up_day_ratio_20>0.60 corresponds to observable distribution signatures (e.g., closing-price weakness relative to intraday highs, volume imbalance shifts) at or before snapshot time, not just retrospective correlation

A formal separation test: if snapshot features truly predict outcomes, then splitting the 27 cases by median values of the top 3 features should produce statistically significant outcome differences (Fisher's exact test p<0.05) despite small N

Demonstration that base_depth_pct (the direct measure of base quality) outperforms px_vs_ma20 (the proxy) in predicting ruin outcomes, validating the mechanistic claim rather than accepting the proxy's correlation as evidence

tests.name: outcome_independence_test
tests.comparison: Feature-outcome correlation conditional on label construction method
tests.success_criterion: At least one feature achieves p<0.10 (Fisher's exact) in predicting w4_return_bucket when tested across ALL 27 cases as continuous sample, not filtered by is_b0_pick. This establishes features predict outcome independent of the label taxonomy used to define failure modes.
tests.failure_criterion: No feature achieves p<0.15 in Fisher's exact test across full 27-case sample. This would suggest features are descriptive of labeled categories but not independently predictive of the underlying W4 return process.

tests.name: proxy_versus_direct_measurement
tests.comparison: px_vs_ma20 (positional proxy) vs base_depth_pct (structural measure) as predictors of ruin vs winner
tests.success_criterion: base_depth_pct achieves higher AUC or odds ratio than px_vs_ma20 in separating false_positive_ruin from selected_winner. This validates the researcher's mechanistic claim that position proxies underlying structure and that structural measurement is superior.
tests.failure_criterion: px_vs_ma20 matches or exceeds base_depth_pct in predictive power. This falsifies the proxy claim—position becomes the primary signal, not a proxy for base quality.

tests.name: trigger_position_null_hypothesis
tests.comparison: Mechanical trigger position (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) alone vs joint feature model
tests.success_criterion: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct achieves AUC >= 0.60 in separating ruin from winner, OR a model with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct plus any single momentum feature achieves AUC >= 0.75. This supports the skeptic's mechanical-top-capture hypothesis: trigger placement along trend curve is primary driver.
tests.failure_criterion: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct AUC < 0.55 AND feature-only model (mom_20, px_vs_ma20, up_day_ratio_20) achieves AUC >= 0.70. This falsifies mechanical trigger as primary mechanism and validates feature-based prediction.

tests.name: mechanism_separation_test
tests.comparison: Two proposed failure modes—(A) weak momentum + tight price vs (B) momentum divergence—form distinct clusters
tests.success_criterion: False-positive-ruin cases split into two subgroups with non-overlapping feature ranges: Group A with mom_20 < 0.08 AND px_vs_ma20 < 0.05; Group B with mom_20 > 0.15 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 AND ma20_slope_5 < 0.02. If both subgroups exist, the researcher has identified distinct mechanisms. If all ruin cases cluster in one region, only one mechanism is operative.
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin cases distribute across the full feature space without clustering into the two proposed subgroups, OR one proposed subgroup contains zero actual ruin cases. This falsifies the two-mechanism structural claim.

tests.name: up_day_ratio_20_conditionality_test
tests.comparison: up_day_ratio_20 unconditional effect vs conditional on ma20_slope_5 and momentum architecture
tests.success_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 shows ruin association ONLY when ma20_slope_5 < 0.02 AND mom_20 > 0.15. Cases with up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 but ma20_slope_5 >= 0.02 OR mom_20 <= 0.15 are predominantly winners (>=70%). This validates the researcher's conditional mechanism claim.
tests.failure_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 shows ruin association regardless of ma20_slope_5 and mom_20 values. This falsifies the conditional mechanism—up_day_ratio_20 becomes a standalone predictor, not a divergence signal conditional on trend architecture.

tests.name: small_n_robustness_check
tests.comparison: Stability of proposed thresholds (mom_20 < 0.10, px_vs_ma20 < 0.05) under leave-one-out validation
tests.success_criterion: Leave-one-out removal of any single false_positive_ruin case does not shift the optimal mom_20 threshold by more than 30% (i.e., threshold remains between 0.07-0.13), AND does not shift px_vs_ma20 threshold by more than 30% (i.e., remains between 0.035-0.065). This establishes threshold stability despite N=8.
tests.failure_criterion: Removing a single ruin case shifts the optimal threshold by >50%, demonstrating that N=8 provides insufficient power to establish stable thresholds. Claims about >60% ruin rates would then be acknowledged as confidence-interval-in-name-only.

tests.name: counterexample_targeted_search
tests.comparison: Explicit search for the counterexamples the skeptic demands
tests.success_criterion: Find at least 1 case with mom_20 < 0.10 AND px_vs_ma20 < 0.05 that is selected_winner or large_win. This directly falsifies the primary failure-mode claim. Alternatively, find at least 1 case with up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 AND ma20_slope_5 < 0.020 that is selected_winner—this falsifies the divergence condition as sufficient for ruin.
tests.failure_criterion: No counterexamples exist in current 27-case sample. This does not validate the claims—absence of evidence is not evidence of absence—but does establish that current data is consistent with (not proof of) the proposed mechanisms.

leakage_checks: Ensure all tests use features available at snapshot time only (mom_20, px_vs_ma20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, ma20_slope_5, ma10_slope_5, ma50_slope_10, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ibd_entry_volume_ratio, ibd_entry_close_position, ibd_entry_breakout_range_ratio). Pullback metrics (pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_pct) are post-entry outcomes and must not be used as predictive inputs.

Verify w4_return_bucket is used as outcome variable only, never as a feature. The method_note indicates false negatives require future W4 performance—confirm no test inadvertently conditions on this construction rule.
Confirm snapshot_anon is treated as temporal identifier only, never as predictive feature (calendar identity prohibited by rules).

For outcome_independence_test: ensure the 27 cases are treated as a continuous sample rather than filtering by is_b0_pick, which would reintroduce the label-construction circularity by testing features only on cases already classified by the system.

For counterexample_targeted_search: acknowledge this test cannot establish absence—it can only confirm presence of counterexamples if they exist. A failure to find counterexamples requires prospective validation, not retrospective certainty.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: Two distinct false-positive mechanisms were proposed: (A) weak momentum + tight price proximity exhausting base depth, and (B) momentum divergence signaled by elevated up_day_ratio_20. Evidence is WEAK. Counterexample entity_8ad5cd4795 violates Mechanism A (mom_20=0.004, px_vs_ma20=0.007, selected_winner) and counterexample entity_3adc078f01 violates Mechanism B (mom_20=0.172, up_day_ratio_20=0.65, ma20_slope_5=0.063, selected_winner). The strong feature-outcome correlations in numeric_contrasts (up_day_ratio_20 standardized_delta=-1.1882, mom_20=-1.0005) partially reflect label construction circularity, not independent predictive signal. The mechanical trigger-position hypothesis (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct mediating outcomes) was never tested and remains viable given that ruin vs winner medians differ substantially (0.048-0.051 vs 0.025-0.028). Small-N (N=8 ruin, N=11 winner) prevents threshold stability; a single case shift could alter thresholds by 30-50%. up_day_ratio_20 functions as a correlated proxy for trend quality but lacks standalone predictive power—it requires conditional architecture (elevated momentum plus declining MA velocity) that isn't consistently present in the data.
falsifiers: Find at least 2 cases with mom_20 < 0.08 AND px_vs_ma20 < 0.05 that achieve selected_winner or large_win outcome—currently only 1 exists (entity_8ad5cd4795), insufficient to falsify given N=8 baseline

Find at least 2 cases with mom_20 > 0.15 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 AND ma20_slope_5 < 0.020 that are selected_winner—entity_3adc078f01 provides 1 counterexample but ma20_slope_5=0.063 exceeds the proposed threshold, leaving the divergence condition unfalsified

Demonstrate that base_depth_pct outperforms px_vs_ma20 in separating ruin from winner (AUC comparison)—numeric_contrasts show base_depth_pct standardized_delta=0.1942 vs px_vs_ma20=-0.5842, but the proxy claim remains unvalidated
Confirm trigger_position_null_hypothesis: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct alone achieves AUC < 0.55 AND feature-only model achieves AUC >= 0.70—mechanistic test remains pending
Demonstrate outcome_independence: at least one snapshot feature achieves Fisher's exact p < 0.10 across all 27 cases without filtering by is_b0_pick—this test was designed but results not reported
Small-N robustness: leave-one-out removal of any single false_positive_ruin case shifts optimal mom_20 threshold by >30% or px_vs_ma20 threshold by >30%—threshold instability not yet quantified
actionable_design_principles: Treat ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as a primary variable for mechanism testing before accepting feature-based explanations—its median differs substantially between outcome groups and requires controlled testing

Reject any feature-based filter that classifies entity_8ad5cd4795 as ruin-risk: mom_20=0.004, px_vs_ma20=0.007, up_day_ratio_20=0.70, selected_winner with large_win—this case violates both proposed mechanisms and must be incorporated into threshold logic
Acknowledge that up_day_ratio_20 is a risk modifier, not a primary signal: its predictive power depends on trend architecture (ma20_slope_5 direction) that is not reliably measured at snapshot time
Require prospective validation of any ruin-prediction filter across a minimum of 50 additional B0 picks before deployment—N=8 provides insufficient power for actionable thresholds
Do not use post-entry pullback metrics (pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_pct) as predictive inputs; they are outcome-correlated proxies unavailable at entry decision time

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Two-stage conditional filter: Stage 1 rejects mom_20 < 0.08 regardless of other features. Stage 2 flags (not rejects) up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 but only downgrades to reject if ma20_slope_5 < 0.015 AND px_vs_ma20 < 0.08. Otherwise preserves the pick with elevated monitoring.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses the circularity problem by conditioning the up_day_ratio_20 filter on explicit architectural features rather than accepting the feature as a standalone predictor. The entity_8ad5cd4795 counterexample (weak momentum but winner due to strong ma20_slope_5=0.044) demonstrates this conditional structure is necessary.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Moderate—reduces false-positive rate but the conditional thresholds lack robustness validation at N=8

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Trigger position calibration test: for each snapshot, compute ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct percentile within the rolling 20-day distribution. Reject picks where trigger fires in the top quartile (>75th percentile) unless mom_20 > 0.20.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Tests the mechanical top-capture hypothesis directly rather than relying on feature-based prediction. If this simple position rule outperforms multi-feature models, it falsifies the researcher's mechanism claims and supports the skeptic's alternative.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: High—addresses the untested mechanistic alternative. If supported, dramatically simplifies the prediction problem.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Proxy validation layer: whenever px_vs_ma20 < 0.08, require base_depth_pct as a secondary check. If base_depth_pct is not available (null), default to reject rather than accepting the proxy as sufficient.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses the proxy-squared concern by refusing to rely on a proxy when the direct measurement is unavailable or when the proxy's signal diverges from the underlying structural measure.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Low-moderate—adds a missing-data safeguard but doesn't resolve whether base_depth_pct actually outperforms px_vs_ma20 in prediction

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Outcome-independent validation: hold out 5 randomly selected cases from the 27 as a prospective test set. Train threshold logic on remaining 22 cases. Report whether the held-out ruin cases would have been rejected and held-out winners preserved. Repeat across 3 random seeds.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Directly addresses the circularity concern by forcing threshold development to generalize beyond the cases used to define the labels. Any claim of predictive power must survive this cross-validation structure.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Critical—the only design principle that directly falsifies the skeptic's strongest counterclaim about outcome construction circularity

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under near-buy-point geometry; propose a counterexample that would invalidate the pattern. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: B0 picks with weak pre-entry accumulation (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.65) combined with mediocre momentum (0.05 < mom_20 < 0.25) are vulnerable to pullback-induced ruination because the stock lacks the institutional backing to recover from a moderate drawdown (≥10%) taken at full position size.
evidence_for: False-positive ruin cases (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_ccc90a671f, entity_84824e6a20) all exhibit up_day_ratio_20 in range 0.4–0.65 with mom_20 between 0.07–0.24
Selected winners (entity_ead73f4390, entity_2c58cebc59) show up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.6 paired with mom_20 ≥ 0.14

Numeric contrasts confirm false-negative median for up_day_ratio_20 is 0.5 versus selected_winner median of 0.625 (standardized delta = -1.19), the strongest PIT-observable separator in the feature set
Ruin-labeled entities (entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_b6bcccdf6a) have vol_ratio_5_20 in 1.31–1.38 range—elevated but not extreme—consistent with noisy accumulation rather than clean trend
entity_55c2da490e shows moderate up_day_ratio_20 (0.65) but negative ma20_slope_5 (-0.0049), indicating trend degradation at entry
evidence_against: entity_2f86543bf6 is a selected_winner despite up_day_ratio_20 = 0.35 (below false-negative median) and near-zero mom_20 = -0.008, suggesting low-participation but tight base structure can still succeed
entity_3adc078f01 is a selected_winner with pullback_pct = -42.3% (deepest in dataset) but up_day_ratio_20 = 0.65 and mom_20 = 0.172, indicating strong accumulation can survive extreme pullbacks
