entity_8ad5cd4795 is a selected_winner with vol_ratio_5_20 = 0.996 (<1.0) and negative ma10_slope_5, showing below-average volume and declining short-term trend still produced large_win outcome
entity_6618d3e80c is labeled both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner, indicating outcome ambiguity that confounds clean binary classification
falsifiable_predictions: A B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 > 0.75, vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4, and mom_20 > 0.18 that subsequently experiences a pullback ≥15% within 8 weeks will NOT land in the ruin bucket if market-wide returns in that period are neutral-to-positive
A B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 in 0.40–0.55, mom_20 in 0.10–0.20, and px_vs_ma20 > 0.12 (price extended from MA) will have ≥70% probability of ruin-label if pullback_duration_weeks reaches 7+

Finding a B0 pick satisfying all three conditions (up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.75, mom_20 ≥ 0.20, vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.4) that still produces ruin outcome would invalidate the accumulation-vulnerability mechanism
policy_implications: Hard filter: reject B0 picks where up_day_ratio_20 < 0.60 AND mom_20 < 0.15, regardless of other entry signals
Soft filter: apply reduced initial position size (≤50% of standard) when up_day_ratio_20 is 0.60–0.70 with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.25, allowing cost averaging if pullback materializes

Stop-loss trigger: if a B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.65 reaches -12% drawdown before week 4, exit fully rather than averaging—this prevents the 'ruin cascade' where moderate losses accumulate faster than expected recovery
Do not use post-snapshot pullback metrics (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) for entry filtering; these are outcome-correlated noise, not predictive signals

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The up_day_ratio_20 mechanism is a proxy for market-wide momentum regime rather than stock-specific accumulation quality. B0 ruination in the observed sample is driven by adverse market conditions during the holding period, not by pre-entry weakness in institutional backing. The correlation between low up_day_ratio_20 and ruin is spurious—both are downstream of the same market regime variable that the study does not control for.

attacks.issue: up_day_ratio_20 is confounded with market-wide directional bias
attacks.why_it_matters: up_day_ratio_20 measures the fraction of up days over 20 trading sessions—a stock-relative metric that is mechanically lower when the broad market is choppy or declining. If the researcher observes ruin cases with low up_day_ratio_20, this could simply reflect that those B0 picks were made during unfavorable market regimes, not that the stocks lacked institutional backing. The mechanism conflates stock-level accumulation with market-level trend quality. Controlling for S&P 500 or sector index return during the same 20-day window is required before attributing ruination to accumulation failure.

attacks.issue: Selection-on-dependent-variables bias in snapshot composition
attacks.why_it_matters: The 27 cases are drawn from multiple snapshots (snap_724342c280, snap_71486ed83c, snap_d0d57b1e40, etc.) that are themselves time-stamped market conditions. snap_71486ed83c contributes 8 entities including multiple false_negatives and false_positive_ruin. If that snapshot corresponds to a market-wide distribution day failure or sector rotation event, all B0 picks from that snapshot inherit the adverse conditions regardless of their pre-entry accumulation metrics. The apparent predictive power of up_day_ratio_20 may be an artifact of which snapshot a case belongs to, not a stock-picking signal.

attacks.issue: The policy filter using up_day_ratio_20 < 0.60 AND mom_20 < 0.15 would have rejected entity_2f86543bf6 and entity_90a828939a, both large_win outcomes
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_2f86543bf6: up_day_ratio_20 = 0.35, mom_20 = -0.008, ma20_slope_5 = -0.0078 (near-zero or negative on all trend metrics) yet landed in large_win. entity_90a828939a: up_day_ratio_20 = 0.45, mom_20 = 0.036, px_vs_ma20 = 0.018 (tight consolidation, weak momentum) yet also large_win. These are not edge cases—they violate both conjunctive conditions of the hard filter. If the hard filter had been applied historically, it would have eliminated at least 2 of 11 selected_winners, demonstrating that the filter is not just imprecise but actively destructive to the winning subset.

attacks.issue: Pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are used to label outcomes but are not distinguished from causal drivers
attacks.why_it_matters: The mechanism claims weak accumulation causes pullback-induced ruination. But in the data, pullback_pct is an outcome variable (used to construct the outcome_label). The researcher cannot use the same variable as both cause and effect. The true causal chain is: entry conditions → (unobserved) market response → pullback observed → outcome labeled. The mechanism skips the market-response step and attributes it entirely to accumulation quality. If a market-wide -8% event occurs 4 weeks post-entry, every B0 pick from that regime shows a pullback regardless of pre-entry accumulation—this is not a stock-picking failure.

attacks.issue: The vol_ratio_5_20 separator for ruin cases (1.31–1.38 range) overlaps completely with selected_winners
attacks.why_it_matters: Selected winners entity_8f0df3d38e (1.24), entity_ead73f4390 (1.77), entity_2c58cebc59 (1.62), entity_3adc078f01 (1.14), entity_55c2da490e (1.27) span the same 1.1–1.8 range as the ruin cases. vol_ratio_5_20 cannot discriminate winners from ruins. The researcher identifies the 1.31–1.38 range as 'elevated but not extreme—consistent with noisy accumulation' but provides no statistical test for the separation, no p-value, and no holdout validation. This is pattern-matching on a sample of 8 ruin cases.

attacks.issue: The stop-loss rule at -12% drawdown is informationally impossible to execute
attacks.why_it_matters: The policy states: 'if a B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.65 reaches -12% drawdown before week 4, exit fully.' The -12% drawdown is observable only after it occurs. The decision to exit must be made at the point when the drawdown reaches -12%, which means the stop is triggered at the bottom, not before it. This rule cannot prevent the 'ruin cascade'—it can only cap it after the damage is partially done. The rule is a post-hoc position management description, not a predictive filter.

counterexamples_to_seek: A B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.75, mom_20 ≥ 0.20, and vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.5 that experiences a -20%+ drawdown within 6 weeks and lands in the ruin bucket, where the drawdown is clearly sector-specific (sector ETF drops >10% in the same window) rather than stock-unique—this would confirm market regime as the driver, not accumulation quality.

A B0 pick from the same snapshot as a ruin case (e.g., snap_71486ed83c) that has up_day_ratio_20 in the 0.40–0.55 range and mom_20 in the 0.05–0.15 range but still produces a selected_winner outcome—this would directly falsify the hard filter claim.

Cross-snapshot analysis: for snapshots where the majority of B0 picks are false_positive_ruin (e.g., snap_d0d57b1e40 has entity_6618d3e80c as ruin|winner and entity_84824e6a20 as ruin), examine whether sector ETF returns in the subsequent 8 weeks were negative. If so, the ruin outcomes are market-driven.

A B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 in 0.60–0.70, mom_20 in 0.10–0.20, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.1 (low volume, below-average volatility) that still produces a large_win outcome—this would contradict the vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.25 soft-filter recommendation.
what_would_change_my_mind: A controlled analysis matching B0 picks to market returns in the same sector/industry during the 4–8 week post-entry window. If the relationship between up_day_ratio_20 and ruin survives after residualizing on sector returns, then the accumulation mechanism has independent predictive value.

Out-of-sample validation on a separate set of B0 picks from snapshots not used in the discovery sample, showing that the up_day_ratio_20 < 0.60 AND mom_20 < 0.15 filter rejects at least 60% of eventual ruin cases while rejecting fewer than 30% of eventual selected_winners.

A fundamental data point: IBD relative strength rating or institutional sponsorship score at snapshot time. If ruin cases have systematically lower RS ratings than selected_winners with similar up_day_ratio_20, this would confirm that up_day_ratio_20 is a proxy for, but not the cause of, institutional backing.

Evidence that the mechanism generalizes across market regimes: the same up_day_ratio_20 thresholds produce the same ruin rates in both bull-market and bear-market periods, demonstrating that the signal is not regime-dependent.

tests.name: snapshot_regime_inheritance_test
tests.comparison: B0 picks from same snapshot with matched up_day_ratio_20 (±0.05) and mom_20 (±0.03) should have similar ruin rates if up_day_ratio_20 drives outcome; ruin-rate divergence across same-snapshot matched pairs implicates snapshot-level regime effects
tests.success_criterion: Within-snapshot matched pairs show ruin_rate_delta < 0.15 between low and high up_day_ratio_20 strata
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot matched pairs show ruin_rate_delta >= 0.15; OR ruin occurs in high up_day_ratio_20 stratum while low up_day_ratio_20 stratum produces winner—both outcomes in same snapshot would falsify stock-level accumulation mechanism

tests.name: filter_boundary_violation_test
tests.comparison: B0 picks violating the hard filter (up_day_ratio_20 < 0.60 AND mom_20 < 0.15) that still achieve selected_winner status test whether the conjunction is necessary for success
tests.success_criterion: Fewer than 15% of all selected_winners in the dataset violate both filter conditions simultaneously
tests.failure_criterion: 20% or more of selected_winners violate both conditions (entity_2f86543bf6 with up_day_ratio_20=0.35, mom_20=-0.008 and entity_90a828939a with up_day_ratio_20=0.45, mom_20=0.036 are candidate violations in current data)

tests.name: momentum_regime_stability_test
tests.comparison: Skeptic claim that mom_20 is market-biased; test whether directionally-aligned short-term (5-day) and medium-term (20-day) slopes predict outcome better than momentum magnitude alone
tests.success_criterion: B0 picks where ma10_slope_5 and ma20_slope_5 share the same sign as mom_20 have ruin_rate < 0.25; sign-concordant accumulation indicates stable institutional backing
tests.failure_criterion: Sign-concordant picks have ruin_rate >= 0.25 OR sign-discordant picks (opposite slopes) have ruin_rate < 0.20—either falsifies momentum stability as mechanism

tests.name: volume_momentum_interaction_test
tests.comparison: Skeptic notes vol_ratio_5_20 range (1.1-1.8) overlaps completely between winners and ruins; test whether the interaction of volume ratio with momentum strength creates separation
tests.success_criterion: High vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.4) combined with high mom_20 (>0.15) yields ruin_rate < 0.20; low vol_ratio_5_20 (<1.2) combined with low mom_20 (<0.10) yields ruin_rate > 0.50
tests.failure_criterion: Both high-volume-high-momentum and low-volume-low-momentum strata produce similar ruin rates (±0.15)—disconfirms interaction mechanism

tests.name: price_extension_geometry_test
tests.comparison: Near-buy-point geometry claim: false_positive_ruin cases may have price extended too far from moving averages at entry (large px_vs_ma20/50) despite moderate momentum, creating vulnerability to mean-reversion pullbacks
tests.success_criterion: B0 picks with px_vs_ma20 > 0.10 AND mom_20 < 0.20 have ruin_rate > 0.50; extended price without strong momentum is the failure geometry
tests.failure_criterion: Extended-price-but-weak-momentum strata have ruin_rate < 0.35 OR tight-consolidation picks (px_vs_ma20 < 0.05) with same mom_20 range have higher ruin_rate—both would falsify geometry mechanism

tests.name: pullback_response_predictability_test
tests.comparison: Skeptic argues pullback metrics are outcome-correlated noise; test whether PIT features predict whether a pullback, if it occurs, becomes ruinous versus survivable
tests.success_criterion: Among B0 picks that experience pullback (identified via outcome_label containing pullback context), strong accumulation (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.65 AND mom_20 >= 0.15) yields ruin_rate < 0.25; weak accumulation yields ruin_rate > 0.60
tests.failure_criterion: Strong-accumulation pullback cases have ruin_rate >= 0.40 OR weak-accumulation pullback cases have ruin_rate < 0.40—indicates PIT features cannot predict pullback response

tests.name: entry_quality_vs_position_size_confounding_test
tests.comparison: Researcher recommends position-size reduction for weak accumulation; test whether entry tightness (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) interacts with accumulation quality to determine outcome
tests.success_criterion: Tight entries (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.025) with weak accumulation have ruin_rate < 0.35; loose entries (>0.05) with weak accumulation have ruin_rate > 0.50
tests.failure_criterion: Entry tightness does not modulate ruin_rate within accumulation strata (±0.15)—falsifies position-size policy as mechanism

leakage_checks: All test features (up_day_ratio_20, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) must be computed from data available at snapshot time only; no post-snapshot return data included in feature computation
Snapshot identity must not be used as a feature or stratification variable in any test; snapshot_anon is metadata, not a predictive input

Pullback metrics (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) must not appear in test feature lists; these are outcome-correlated variables that would introduce look-ahead leakage if used to predict the outcome they helped create
Outcome labels (selected_winner, false_positive_ruin, ruin) must not appear in test feature lists; these are dependent variables, not inputs
Each test must be executable using only features available at snapshot time; success/failure criteria must reference only the PIT feature values and the outcome label at analysis boundary

Cross-test consistency check: if snapshot_regime_inheritance_test fails (favoring regime explanation), then price_extension_geometry_test and momentum_regime_stability_test must be re-weighted to account for regime confounding before interpretation

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The proposed mechanism—that B0 picks with weak pre-entry accumulation (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.65) combined with mediocre momentum (0.05 < mom_20 < 0.25) are vulnerable to pullback-induced ruination—is directionally supported by the numeric contrasts (up_day_ratio_20 standardized delta = -1.19 is the strongest PIT feature separator), but the causal attribution is confounded. The mechanism conflates stock-level accumulation quality with snapshot-level market regime: ruin cases in the sample (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c) cluster in snapshots that also produce false_negative_relative cases, suggesting the snapshot itself is a confounding variable. The two confirmed large_win violations of the proposed hard filter (entity_2f86543bf6: up_day_ratio_20=0.35, mom_20=-0.008; entity_90a828939a: up_day_ratio_20=0.45, mom_20=0.036) demonstrate the conjunctive filter is not necessary for success. The vol_ratio_5_20 feature shows complete overlap between ruin and winner strata (1.1–1.8), providing no independent discriminative power. Without residualizing on sector-level market returns during the 4–8 week post-entry window, the mechanism cannot be distinguished from a market-regime proxy.
falsifiers: snapshot_regime_inheritance_test fails: Within-snapshot matched pairs (matched on up_day_ratio_20 ±0.05 and mom_20 ±0.03) show ruin_rate_delta ≥ 0.15—ruin cases concentrated in specific snapshots regardless of matched PIT features would implicate regime as primary driver

filter_boundary_violation_test failure threshold met: ≥20% of selected_winners violate both filter conditions (up_day_ratio_20 < 0.60 AND mom_20 < 0.15)—currently 2 of 11 (18%) selected_winners are violations, near the threshold

Cross-snapshot regime analysis: Finding that snapshots contributing multiple ruin cases (e.g., snap_d0d57b1e40) correspond to periods where the relevant sector ETF declined >8% in the 4–8 week post-entry window would confirm market regime as the driver

Strong-accumulation ruin case: A B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.75, mom_20 ≥ 0.20, vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.4 that experiences ruin (w4_return_bucket = 'ruin') despite neutral-to-positive sector ETF returns in the same window would directly falsify accumulation-vulnerability as the mechanism

Same-snapshot winner-within-ruin-range: A B0 pick from a snapshot containing ruin cases, with up_day_ratio_20 in 0.40–0.55 range and mom_20 in 0.05–0.15 range, that produces selected_winner outcome—would falsify the necessity of strong accumulation within adverse regimes
momentum_regime_stability_test failure: Sign-concordant picks (ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, mom_20 all positive) have ruin_rate ≥ 0.25—would falsify accumulation stability as protective mechanism
actionable_design_principles: Do NOT use the conjunctive hard filter (up_day_ratio_20 < 0.60 AND mom_20 < 0.15) as an outright rejection rule—two confirmed large_win outcomes would have been excluded, demonstrating the filter is not necessary for success

Use snapshot-level context as a mandatory stratification variable before interpreting PIT feature predictive power; if a snapshot produces >50% ruin rate across all accumulation strata, that snapshot's regime is the operative variable

Implement position-size modulation (not rejection) based on accumulation quality: reduce initial position size for weak-accumulation picks rather than filtering them out entirely, allowing cost-averaging if pullback materializes
Never use post-snapshot features (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) as policy inputs; these are outcome-correlated variables that cannot predict the outcome they help create

Restrict stop-loss rules to pre-defined percentage thresholds set at entry, not reactive to observed drawdown; a -12% stop triggered only after -12% is reached is a damage-capper, not a ruin-preventer

The vol_ratio_5_20 feature should be treated as a regime volatility indicator (high values = elevated market noise) rather than a stock-picking discriminator, given complete overlap between winner and ruin strata
Reserve the right to escalate to regime-adjusted analysis when the snapshot_regime_inheritance_test indicates snapshot-level confounding is present

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot-regime-adjusted accumulation score (SRA-score) = weighted composite of up_day_ratio_20, mom_20, and vol_ratio_5_20, where the weights are determined after residualizing on snapshot-level outcome rates
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This addresses the core confound: the standard composite would double-count snapshot regime effects. SRA-score residualizes snapshot influence before computing the accumulation metric, providing a stock-specific rather than regime-contaminated signal
features: snapshot_anon (for outcome rate calibration only, not as feature input)
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Position sizing module uses SRA-score to allocate capacity; high SRA-score gets standard position, low SRA-score gets reduced initial position (≤40% of standard), allowing cost-averaging if pullback occurs

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot survival rate gate: compute the historical ruin_rate for B0 picks within each snapshot's cohort; if a given snapshot's cohort ruin_rate > 0.50, apply uniform position-size reduction across all B0 picks from that snapshot regardless of individual accumulation metrics
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This directly addresses the regime confounding without requiring external market data; it treats the snapshot as a regime proxy and adjusts position sizing accordingly, rather than attempting to explain outcomes via stock-specific features that may be confounded
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Risk management module applies snapshot-level position cap; if snapshot cohort ruin_rate exceeds threshold, all positions from that snapshot are capped at maximum 30% of standard size

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Tight-entry compensation rule: when ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.015 (very tight entry), allow up to 1.5x standard position size ONLY if SRA-score is ≥ 0.60; loose entries (>0.05) with weak accumulation (SRA-score < 0.40) trigger automatic exit if drawdown exceeds -8% within first 3 weeks
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This separates entry quality from accumulation quality rather than conflating them; it acknowledges that tight entries can compensate for moderate accumulation only when accumulation is not severely weak, and that loose entries require stronger accumulation to justify holding through drawdowns
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Entry validation module checks entry-tightness against SRA-score thresholds before position sizing; loose-entry-with-weak-accumulation triggers enhanced monitoring with pre-defined exit criteria

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Near-buy-point geometry filter for extended-price entries: B0 picks with px_vs_ma20 > 0.12 AND mom_20 < 0.20 are flagged as geometrically extended; these require up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.70 OR ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.02 to qualify for standard position size, otherwise subject to 50% position reduction
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This directly addresses the near-buy-point geometry hypothesis using only PIT features, without using post-snapshot pullback data; it conditions position size on the geometric relationship rather than predicting whether a pullback will occur
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Entry geometry module applies conditional sizing rule; extended entries with weak accumulation receive reduced initial position, with option to add on pullback if accumulation quality improves post-entry

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under volume confirmation/dry-up; identify repeated PIT-visible precursors. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-positive B0 picks that ruin are characterized by volume expansion WITHOUT momentum acceleration: the 5-day volume surge is present (vol_ratio_5_20 ~1.24) but short-term price velocity (ma10_slope_5) fails to outpace medium-term velocity (ma20_slope_5) by >2x, producing a slope-ratio ceiling that signals distribution rather than accumulation. The PIT-observable signature is modest volume confirmation paired with decelerating price momentum.
evidence_for: False-positive ruin cases show vol_ratio_5_20 median of 1.24 vs 1.42 for selected winners (standardized delta = -1.05), indicating borderline volume confirmation insufficient for sustaining breakouts

False-positive ruin cases exhibit ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 ratios clustered near 1.5-2.0 (e.g., entity_ccc90a671f: 0.0395/0.0111 = 3.6, entity_40ea0cfb3b: 0.0246/0.0018 = 13.9), while selected winners show steeper short-term momentum relative to medium-term (e.g., entity_b00579f203: 0.0531/0.0290 = 1.8, entity_3adc078f01: 0.0635/0.0734 = 0.87)
The numeric contrasts show mom_20 standardized delta of -1.00, with false-positive ruin medians near 0.07-0.18 vs selected winners near 0.16-0.32, indicating weaker underlying momentum baseline
px_vs_ma20 median for false positives (~0.07-0.09) is lower than selected winners (~0.07-0.18), suggesting the breakout lacks sufficient distance from the moving average to absorb normal pullback
up_day_ratio_20 median for false-positive ruin (0.5-0.65) is elevated but does not reflect directional conviction—high values indicate absence of down days, not positive momentum character
evidence_against: entity_8f0df3d38e (false_positive_ruin) shows vol_ratio_5_20=1.24 and ma10_slope_5=0.054/ma20_slope_5=0.037 (ratio=1.46), consistent, but pullback_pct=-16.2 occurred over 7 weeks—volume did confirm initially before drying
entity_4fdc3699fd (false_positive_ruin) has vol_ratio_5_20=1.377, higher than median, yet still failed—volume alone does not predict survival
entity_3472243e0c (false_positive_ruin) shows strong mom_20=0.242 and vol_ratio_5_20=1.21—momentum and volume profiles similar to winners, yet ruin occurred, suggesting additional unobserved factors
Case entity_6618d3e80c is labeled both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner, indicating outcome ambiguity that may conflate distinct mechanisms
falsifiable_predictions: In a validation set, B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.60 AND (ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5) < 2.0 will experience ≥12% drawdown within 6 weeks at >60% frequency
B0 picks where vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.35 AND mom_20 > 0.15 AND (ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5) > 2.5 will be selected_winner at >70% frequency
The slope-ratio (ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5) will have greater classification discriminability than either slope in isolation, measurable by AUC comparison on held-out data
policy_implications: B0 entry signal should be gated: require vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.35 as necessary condition for position sizing above minimum
Slope-ratio < 2.0 flags momentum deceleration risk; recommend reduced position size or earlier stop even if other B0 criteria are met
up_day_ratio_20 should not be treated as a momentum filter; it measures symmetry not direction, and should be combined with mom_20 for conviction scoring
Pullback_duration_weeks null values in false_positive_ruin cases suggest some ruin occurs without observable pullback—volume dry-up may be the primary mechanism rather than gradual mean reversion

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The volume-ratio and slope-ratio signatures are epiphenomenal correlates of momentum baseline rather than mechanistically causal precursors. False-positive ruin occurs when institutional distribution coincides with B0 trigger timing, not because volume confirmation was insufficient or slope ratios fell below 2.0. The observed 1.24 vs 1.42 median vol_ratio_5_20 gap reflects the absence of genuine accumulation (which would produce winners) rather than predicting failure conditional on the trigger event itself.

attacks.issue: The slope ratio (ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5) is a mathematical artifact of momentum baseline, not an independent predictor
attacks.why_it_matters: When mom_20 is lower in false positives (~0.07-0.18 vs 0.16-0.32 in winners), the short-term price velocity mechanically decelerates toward the already-slower medium-term trend. This produces a lower ratio post-hoc without causal force. The ratio does not tell us whether the price will reaccumulate—it merely records that the current momentum cycle is weaker. Testing the ratio as a prospective classifier without conditioning on mom_20 conflates what predicts the label from what causes the outcome.

attacks.issue: up_day_ratio_20 is a symmetry measure, not a momentum filter, yet is treated as if it predicts directional conviction
attacks.why_it_matters: Both false-positive ruin (median 0.5-0.65) and selected_winner (0.625) overlap substantially. A stock gaining +8% on up-days and -1% on down-days yields the same ratio as one gaining +1% on up-days and losing -0.5% on down-days. The prior research explicitly warns against using it as a momentum filter but then uses it to construct the falsifiable prediction, creating an internal contradiction.

attacks.issue: Pullback_duration_weeks nulls in 4 of 8 false_positive_ruin cases directly contradict the proposed 'volume confirmation then dry-up' mechanism
attacks.why_it_matters: The mechanism requires a observable pullback phase where volume confirms support before drying. When pullback_duration_weeks is null, ruin occurs without a gradual drawdown phase—the price simply fails. This suggests the primary mechanism is instantaneous distribution or trigger at a local-top coincidence, not the gradual process the volume-ratio signature assumes. The null cases cannot be reconciled with the mechanism without auxiliary assumptions about 'fast ruin' that are not formalized.

attacks.issue: The comparison class (selected_winner) is not held-out from the B0 selection process, creating circularity
attacks.why_it_matters: 'Selected_winner' means IBD's B0 system chose it AND it performed well. False-positive ruin means B0 chose it AND it failed. Both groups passed the B0 filter. The comparison is therefore between B0 picks that happened to work vs. those that did not—a survivorship comparison within the signal itself. The vol_ratio_5_20 difference (1.24 vs 1.42) does not tell us what volume characteristic causes ruin; it only tells us that the winning subset had stronger volume. This is tautological if volume confirms accumulation.

attacks.issue: Snapshot heterogeneity is uncontrolled: multiple distinct snap_* values span different market regimes
attacks.why_it_matters: The cases come from at least 8 distinct snapshots (snap_724342c280, snap_287267e812, snap_eb3d8128cc, snap_ad495b6705, etc.). A breakout trigger at the start of a rotation sector move has different base rates for success than one near sector exhaustion. The vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20 differences between groups could reflect snapshot-specific regime effects (e.g., some snapshots captured early-cycle breakouts with better fundamentals) rather than feature predictiveness.

attacks.issue: Entity_6618d3e80c labeled both 'false_positive_ruin' AND 'selected_winner' signals classification ambiguity that propagates to all median comparisons
attacks.why_it_matters: This hybrid label suggests the labeling schema conflates multi-phase outcomes or has resolution errors. When 1 of 27 cases cannot be cleanly categorized, and the mechanism requires distinguishing specific causal pathways, the median comparisons across categories inherit this contamination. The numeric contrasts assume clean categorical separation that the data does not support.

attacks.issue: The vol_ratio_5_20 threshold of 1.35 is not derived from a density analysis or ROC optimization on held-out data
attacks.why_it_matters: The standardized delta between false-positive ruin and selected_winner medians is 1.05—a meaningful separation—but this does not establish that 1.35 is the optimal threshold. With only 8 ruin cases, any threshold in the 1.24-1.42 range will have wide confidence intervals. The proposed prediction that vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30 predicts ≥12% drawdown at >60% frequency is not validated; it is a hypothesis derived from the same 8 cases used to motivate it.

attacks.issue: px_vs_ma20 overlap between false positives and winners is extreme (0.07-0.09 vs 0.07-0.18 medians)
attacks.why_it_matters: The prior research cites px_vs_ma20 as indicating insufficient distance from moving averages to absorb pullbacks. However, the interquartile ranges almost certainly overlap heavily. A stock at px_vs_ma20=0.18 (winner) and one at 0.07 (false positive) are both 'above the MA' by modest amounts. The claim that distance predicts survival is not supported by any analysis of the distribution overlap.

counterexamples_to_seek: B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.50 AND slope_ratio < 1.5 that still resulted in selected_winner, demonstrating that high volume does not require high slope ratio to produce winners
B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.20 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.70 that were selected_winner, contradicting the volume-dry-up-is-necessary-for-ruin narrative
Cases where pullback_duration_weeks null co-occurs with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.40, demonstrating that null pullback duration does not imply low volume confirmation

Cross-snapshot validation: do the same vol_ratio and slope-ratio thresholds trained on snap_724342c280 failures predict ruin in snap_71486ed83c with comparable precision? If not, snapshot-specific base rates are the true driver

Momentum-matched counterexamples: among B0 picks with mom_20 in the 0.15-0.25 range (overlapping the winner distribution), do the volume and slope features still separate ruin from winners? If the separation vanishes when conditioning on momentum, the slope ratio is a proxy for momentum baseline
what_would_change_my_mind: A hold-out validation (not derived from these 27 cases) where the slope_ratio threshold of 2.0 applied to vol_ratio_5_20-gated B0 picks produces ruin at >60% frequency within 6 weeks, with the prediction made before outcome observation

A formal mechanism demonstration: show that in false-positive ruin cases, the volume on the B0 entry day is disproportionately from provider/hedge sources (e.g., ITG PIN < 0.3 or equivalent) versus institutional accumulation, separating the vol_ratio signal into its constituent flow types

A conditioning analysis: after matching false-positive ruin and selected_winner cases on mom_20 (±0.02), demonstrate that the slope_ratio or vol_ratio_5_20 retains significant classification discriminability (AUC > 0.70) independent of the momentum baseline

A temporal analysis of pullback_duration_weeks null cases: if null indicates fast ruin (< 1 week to max drawdown), demonstrate that the PIT-observable features at snapshot time distinguish fast-ruin from slow-ruin within the false_positive_ruin group, rather than pooling mechanistically distinct outcomes

Replication across an independent B0 selection universe (different time period or screening criteria) with comparable feature distributions, ruling out snapshot-specific or labeling-algorithm artifacts as the source of the observed contrasts

tests.name: momentum_conditioned_discrimination_test
tests.comparison: Within matched pairs of false_positive_ruin and selected_winner cases where mom_20 difference ≤ 0.02, compute AUC for (a) slope_ratio = ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5, (b) vol_ratio_5_20, and (c) up_day_ratio_20 as binary classifiers
tests.success_criterion: Any single feature achieves AUC > 0.65 in the momentum-conditioned comparison, confirming discriminability independent of momentum baseline
tests.failure_criterion: All features yield AUC ≤ 0.65 when mom_20 is matched, indicating slope_ratio and vol_ratio_5_20 are proxies for momentum baseline rather than independent predictors

tests.name: pullback_null_subgroup_heterogeneity_test
tests.comparison: Within false_positive_ruin cases only, compare PIT feature distributions between pullback_duration_weeks IS NULL (n=4) vs IS NOT NULL (n=4) subgroups using Mann-Whitney U
tests.success_criterion: At least one PIT feature shows p < 0.15 difference between null and non-null subgroups, indicating mechanistically distinct fast-ruin vs slow-ruin pathways
tests.failure_criterion: No significant feature differences between null and non-null subgroups (all p ≥ 0.15), confirming the null status reflects measurement absence rather than distinct causal mechanisms

tests.name: cross_snapshot_holdout_validation_test
tests.comparison: Treat each unique snap_* value as a leave-one-snapshot-out fold. Within each fold, derive thresholds from n-1 snapshots (training set) and apply to held-out snapshot. Use researcher-derived candidate thresholds: vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30 AND slope_ratio < 2.0 predicts ruin
tests.success_criterion: Ruin precision ≥ 0.50 across ≥ 2/3 of held-out snapshots, confirming threshold generalizability beyond discovery snapshot
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin precision < 0.50 in ≥ 2/3 of held-out snapshots, indicating snapshot-specific base rates dominate feature effects

tests.name: volume_dryup_narrative_test
tests.comparison: Examine whether false_positive_ruin cases with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.35 (above winner median) exist and characterize their distinguishing features vs ruin cases with vol_ratio_5_20 ≤ 1.35
tests.success_criterion: At least 2 false_positive_ruin cases show vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.35 but fail anyway, with distinct PIT profiles (e.g., slope_ratio < 1.5 or mom_20 < 0.10) identifying the alternative failure pathway
tests.failure_criterion: No false_positive_ruin cases have vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.35, confirming volume confirmation failure is both necessary and sufficient for ruin within this dataset

tests.name: slope_ratio_mechanical_artifactual_test
tests.comparison: Fit logistic regression: outcome ~ mom_20 + slope_ratio. Test whether slope_ratio coefficient remains significant (p < 0.10) after controlling for mom_20. If not significant, slope_ratio is fully explained by momentum baseline
tests.success_criterion: slope_ratio coefficient p < 0.10 after mom_20 control, confirming slope_ratio carries information beyond momentum baseline
tests.failure_criterion: slope_ratio coefficient p ≥ 0.10 after mom_20 control, confirming slope_ratio is a mathematical artifact of the momentum baseline (skeptic's counterclaim validated)

tests.name: updayratio_symmetry_vs_direction_test
tests.comparison: Compute correlation between up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20 across all B0 pick cases. If correlation > 0.30, up_day_ratio_20 partially reflects directional momentum; if < 0.15, it is primarily symmetry
tests.success_criterion: Correlation < 0.15, confirming up_day_ratio_20 is a symmetry measure orthogonal to directional conviction, explaining overlap between ruin and winner distributions
tests.failure_criterion: Correlation ≥ 0.30, indicating up_day_ratio_20 carries directional information that should be exploited in conjunction with mom_20

leakage_checks: Verify snap_* values used only for fold assignment, never as a feature input to any classification model
Confirm outcome_label determination uses only forward returns, never contemporaneous PIT features
Check that threshold derivation for cross_snapshot_test uses training-fold PIT features and outcome labels only
Ensure matching procedure for momentum_conditioned_test uses only mom_20 for pair matching, not outcome-correlated features

Verify entity_6618d3e80c (labeled both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner) is excluded from threshold derivation and only used in validation if classification is unambiguous for the specific prediction

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The volume-dryup mechanism receives directional support from the 1.24 vs 1.42 vol_ratio_5_20 median gap (standardized delta ≈ -1.0) and from entity_8f0df3d38e's pullback pattern (volume confirmed then dried over 7 weeks), but the proposed slope-ratio discriminator lacks independence from mom_20. The slope ratio (ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5) appears to be a mathematical compression of momentum baseline rather than an independent predictor—lower mom_20 mechanically produces lower slope ratios without adding causal force. The up_day_ratio_20 feature overlaps substantially across outcomes and is misaligned with the falsifiable prediction that uses it, creating an internal inconsistency. Pullback_duration_weeks null in 4 of 8 ruin cases cannot be reconciled with the gradual-dryup narrative without post-hoc 'fast ruin' auxiliary assumptions. The threshold of 1.35 is empirically derived from the same discovery set, not from hold-out density analysis. Overall, volume weakness is plausibly associated with ruin, but the specific PIT-observable discriminator (slope_ratio < 2.0) and the causal mechanism (volume expansion without momentum acceleration) remain unproven.
falsifiers: Cross-snapshot hold-out: vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30 AND slope_ratio < 2.0 fails to predict ≥12% drawdown at >60% frequency in ≥2/3 of held-out snap_* folds
Momentum-conditioned test: after matching false_positive_ruin and selected_winner on mom_20 ± 0.02, slope_ratio yields AUC ≤ 0.65, confirming it is a momentum proxy
High-volume counterexample: a B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.40 AND mom_20 > 0.20 AND slope_ratio < 1.5 results in selected_winner, contradicting the necessity of slope_ratio > 2.0

Pullback_null heterogeneity: Mann-Whitney U shows no PIT feature distinguishes null vs non-null pullback subgroups within false_positive_ruin (all p ≥ 0.15), confirming the mechanism pools mechanistically distinct outcomes
Logistic regression: slope_ratio coefficient p ≥ 0.10 after controlling for mom_20, confirming the skeptic's artifactual counterclaim
actionable_design_principles: Use vol_ratio_5_20 as a monotonic continuous predictor in position-sizing models rather than as a binary threshold; any threshold requires hold-out validation before deployment
Do not condition ruin predictions on slope_ratio without first establishing it retains discriminability after mom_20 control; if it does not, exclude it from the model
Treat pullback_duration_weeks null as a distinct subgroup requiring separate modeling rather than missing-at-random; consider whether 'fast ruin' has a different feature signature at snapshot time
Reserve up_day_ratio_20 for symmetry checks or regime characterization; do not use it as a directional filter without first establishing correlation with mom_20 is < 0.15
Require cross-snapshot hold-out validation before treating any threshold (vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30, slope_ratio < 2.0) as a production signal filter

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Vol_ratio_conditional_entry_gate: require vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.35 for any B0 pick to receive >1x base weight; below 1.35 receives 0.5x or is excluded
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Unlike the slope_ratio threshold, vol_ratio_5_20 shows standardized delta ≈ -1.0 and is not a mathematical function of momentum baseline; however, this remains a hypothesis until cross-snapshot hold-out validation confirms >60% ruin precision
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Position sizing / conviction scoring

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Momentum_exclusion_zone: if mom_20 < 0.10, do not use slope_ratio as a discriminator; treat the B0 pick as low-conviction regardless of slope_ratio value
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: When mom_20 is very low, slope_ratio becomes maximally coupled to momentum baseline, reducing its independent information content; this is a conservative adjustment that reduces false positives at the cost of possibly missing early-stage breakouts
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Entry filter / conviction scoring

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Pullback_null_early_stop: for false_positive_ruin cases where pullback_duration_weeks IS NULL at snapshot time, apply tighter stop-loss (e.g., 8% vs standard 12%) anticipating fast-ruin pathway

dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Risk management / stop-loss timing

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot_regime_interaction: include snap_* as a stratification variable in any threshold validation, or derive snapshot-specific thresholds if ruin base rates vary >20% across snapshots

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under volume confirmation/dry-up; separate true signal from correlated proxy. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-positive B0 ruin occurs when entry coincides with momentum deceleration (low short-term slope) despite prior up-move; the system confuses mean-reversion exhaustion with genuine breakout continuation. Volume ratio distinguishes these: low vol_ratio signals institutional non-confirmation of the pullback entry, whereas moderate-to-high vol_ratio indicates continued participation during the pullback that makes rebound more likely. High-momentum entries (>15% mom_20) survive even without volume confirmation, but moderate-momentum entries (5-15%) require volume confirmation to avoid ruin.
evidence_for: false_negative median vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.18 vs selected_winner median = 1.42 (standardized delta -1.05), indicating low recent volume is associated with missed opportunity, not just low volume causing ruin

false_positive_ruin cases show concentrated values: entity_4fdc3699fd (mom_20=0.185, vol_ratio=1.38), entity_3472243e0c (mom_20=0.242, vol_ratio=1.21), entity_40ea0cfb3b (mom_20=0.024, vol_ratio=0.91) - low vol_ratio even when momentum appears moderate

selected_winner entity_440e297253: vol_ratio=1.59 with modest momentum (0.058) but survives; contrast with false_positive_ruin entity_8f0df3d38e: vol_ratio=1.24, momentum=0.176 (higher) but still ruins

up_day_ratio_20 median delta -1.19 between false_negative and selected_winner: directional conviction matters; low up_day_ratio despite positive momentum suggests volatile reversal rather than sustained advance
ma10_slope_5 median delta -0.68: false positives enter during short-term deceleration even if longer-term (ma20_slope) remains positive

pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are NOT PIT-observable (post-entry outcomes) but observed pullback severity correlates with eventual ruin in winners - suggesting the mechanical stress test is necessary but low vol_ratio entries fail the test more often
entity_2f86543bf6: mom_20=-0.008 (negative momentum), vol_ratio=1.56, selected_winner - negative momentum + high volume indicates fresh accumulation from lower base
evidence_against: entity_3adc078f01: vol_ratio=1.14 (below median for winners), mom_20=0.172, selected_winner large_win - exception where low volume did not predict ruin, possibly due to extreme pullback (-42.3%) resetting the base
entity_8ad5cd4795: vol_ratio=0.996 (sub-1.0, very low), selected_winner - another exception, suggesting vol_ratio is probabilistic not deterministic
entity_b6bcccdf6a: vol_ratio=1.31, false_positive_ruin but w4_return_bucket=loss (not ruin) - some 'ruin' labels may include losses without true catastrophic failure

The vol_ratio feature measures 5-day vs 20-day volume, which may not directly capture whether volume is confirming the pullback rebound or just indicating elevated baseline activity; a ratio below 1.0 could indicate calm accumulation rather than institutional abandonment
mom_20 alone (without vol confirmation) has contradictory signal: both ruin and winner medians overlap in the 0.15-0.18 range
falsifiable_predictions: B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.20 AND mom_20 between 0.05-0.20 will ruin (w4_return_bucket='ruin') with probability >60%
B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.40 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 will achieve selected_winner outcome with probability >70%

Adding ma10_slope_5 > 0.04 as secondary filter to the above will increase ruin-prediction precision; entries where ma10_slope_5 < 0.02 (deceleration) are more likely to ruin even with acceptable vol_ratio

The combination vol_ratio < 1.15 AND ma10_slope_5 > 0.06 (elevated recent slope despite low volume) signals a potential trap: the stock accelerated on thin volume, likely professional manipulation rather than institutional accumulation
Testing: Stratify B0 picks into vol_ratio quintiles; ruin rate should decrease monotonically from lowest to highest quintile; if non-monotonic, the mechanism requires revision
policy_implications: Vol_ratio_5_20 should be elevated to required filter status in B0 entry logic; current threshold may be too permissive (observed ruin cases have ratios 0.91-1.45)
Consider dual-threshold approach: vol_ratio > 1.30 required for entries with mom_20 < 0.15; vol_ratio > 1.15 acceptable when mom_20 > 0.20
Up_day_ratio_20 provides orthogonal signal to vol_ratio; a composite score (e.g., vol_ratio_z + up_day_ratio_z) may better separate true signal from correlated proxy
Pullback entries in the 3-7 week duration range with vol_ratio < 1.25 should be flagged as high-risk; duration itself is post-entry observable but can be estimated from prior base structure at entry
Avoid using mom_20 alone as momentum filter; it correlates with both ruin and winner outcomes; the mechanism requires vol_ratio interaction to disentangle

If backtesting confirms the ruin-prediction accuracy of vol_ratio < 1.20 + mom_20 0.05-0.20, consider shorting the subset of B0 picks that pass momentum but fail volume confirmation on the hypothesis that B0 system overweights momentum and underweights participation

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: vol_ratio_5_20 does not mechanistically cause ruin; it is a correlated proxy for sector/market regime conditions, and the threshold-based predictions are artifacts of snapshot-specific base rate differences rather than causal structure.

attacks.issue: Threshold cutoffs (1.20, 1.40) have no theoretical derivation and are data-snooped from N=27
attacks.why_it_matters: The median deltas reported are <1.05 standardized for vol_ratio. This is weak separation that could easily flip with minor sample perturbations. The researcher proposes binary thresholds at 1.20 and 1.40 with no mechanistic justification for why exactly these values separate accumulation from abandonment. Small changes to the training set would shift these cutoffs by ±0.15 and invert the policy implications entirely.

attacks.issue: False-positive ruin entity_ccc90a671f has vol_ratio=1.45, exceeding the proposed winner threshold
attacks.why_it_matters: This case directly falsifies the mechanism. vol_ratio=1.45 > 1.40, up_day_ratio=0.50, mom_20=0.074. According to the researcher's own falsifiable prediction, this should achieve selected_winner with >70% probability. It did not. The failure is not marginal—it is on the opposite side of the proposed threshold. Any valid mechanism must explain why high volume confirmation fails to prevent ruin.

attacks.issue: False-positive ruin entity_84824e6a20 has vol_ratio=1.63, well above the proposed threshold
attacks.why_it_matters: vol_ratio=1.63 with mom_20=0.067 contradicts both the ruin-prediction rule (vol_ratio < 1.20) and the winner-prediction rule (vol_ratio > 1.40). This entity has the highest vol_ratio in the ruin set yet still fails. The researcher would need to argue some additional interaction, but no interaction is specified in the mechanism. This is a clean counterexample.

attacks.issue: Snapshot contamination: snap_71486ed83c appears in both false_positive_ruin (entity_3472243e0c) and selected_winner (entity_2c58cebc59, entity_3adc078f01)
attacks.why_it_matters: The same snapshot being shared across ruin and winner outcomes suggests the snapshot's base-rate characteristics (which are not observable in the frozen evidence) are driving outcomes, not the vol_ratio at entry. If the snapshot itself is a low-quality market environment, vol_ratio is just picking up that latent snapshot quality, not causal volume dynamics. The mechanism conflates snapshot-level effects with entity-level predictors.

attacks.issue: The method_note explicitly defines false_negative_relative using future W4 performance, making vol_ratio differences between false_negative and selected_winner potentially tautological
attacks.why_it_matters: The median vol_ratio comparison uses outcome-defined groups. If vol_ratio is itself a predictor of W4 return, then comparing vol_ratio between groups that are defined by W4 return is circular. The direction of causality is unclear: does low vol_ratio cause missed opportunity, or does low vol_ratio simply co-occur with low W4 returns because both reflect weak underlying momentum?

attacks.issue: up_day_ratio_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 are both computed from the same 20-day window, creating structural correlation
attacks.why_it_matters: In high-volatility stocks, both up_day_ratio and vol_ratio will be elevated by the same market microstructure (elevated volume on up days vs down days). Using both as orthogonal predictors in a composite score double-counts the same underlying volatility regime. The 'orthogonal' claim in the policy_implications is likely false.

attacks.issue: Pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are rejected as 'post-entry outcomes' but used indirectly in the mechanism claim
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher argues low vol_ratio entries 'fail the test more often' referring to mechanical pullback stress. But this implies pullback severity (which determines ruin vs survival) is already encoded in the vol_ratio measurement. If pullback severity is the true driver, then vol_ratio is merely a noisy proxy for something causally downstream. The mechanism conflates the measurement (vol_ratio at entry) with the causal variable (how deep the subsequent pullback will be).

counterexamples_to_seek: A B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0 (sub-baseline volume) and mom_20 > 0.20 that achieves large_win outcome, demonstrating low volume is not deterministic of ruin even at extreme values
A snapshot where all B0 picks have vol_ratio > 1.40 but none achieve selected_winner, testing whether vol_ratio threshold is spurious when base rates are unfavorable
Entities within the same snapshot where high vol_ratio entity ruins and low vol_ratio entity survives, holding snapshot constant to isolate vol_ratio effect
Time periods where vol_ratio_5_20 distribution for false_positive_ruin overlaps completely with selected_winner, indicating the feature has zero within-period discriminative power
A mechanical test: simulate entries where vol_ratio is inverted (low becomes high, high becomes low) and show ruin/winner rates flip—without this symmetry test, the mechanism is unfalsified
what_would_change_my_mind: A controlled experiment holding snapshot fixed: within-snapshot vol_ratio rank-order correlates with w4_return_bucket monotonicity across at least 15 entities with a Spearman rho > 0.4
Mechanistic derivation of the 1.20/1.40 thresholds from first principles (e.g., bid-ask bounce dynamics, order flow toxicity metrics) rather than empirical fitting

Demonstration that false_positive_ruin cases with vol_ratio > 1.40 (entity_ccc90a671f, entity_84824e6a20) are explained by a second-order interaction (e.g., vol_ratio spike driven by one-off news event rather than sustained institutional participation) that is independently measurable at snapshot time
Out-of-sample test on a separate temporal partition where ruin rate does not simply reflect base-rate changes but vol_ratio explains incremental variance beyond snapshot fixed effects

Causal identification strategy (e.g., difference-in-differences around volume data reporting changes) that distinguishes vol_ratio as causal from vol_ratio as a proxy for unobserved fundamental deterioration

tests.name: within_snapshot_vol_ratio_monotonicity
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot containing both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner outcomes, compute Spearman rank correlation between vol_ratio_5_20 and outcome ordinal (ruin=0, winner=1)
tests.success_criterion: At least 3 qualifying snapshots with N≥3 per outcome class; pooled Spearman rho > 0.35 indicating higher vol_ratio associates with winner outcomes
tests.failure_criterion: Spearman rho ≤ 0.10 OR direction reverses in >50% of qualifying snapshots; this would support the skeptic's snapshot-confounding claim

tests.name: vol_ratio_momentum_threshold_robustness
tests.comparison: Compare continuous (logistic regression with splines) vs threshold-based (researcher's 1.20/1.40 cutoffs) fit on ruin vs winner using AICc; test if threshold positions are stable under leave-one-out jackknife
tests.success_criterion: Continuous model AICc ≤ threshold model AND jackknife threshold stability within ±0.15 of proposed values; suggests mechanism is not threshold-artifact
tests.failure_criterion: Threshold model outperforms continuous by ΔAICc > 4 AND jackknife instability > ±0.30; suggests thresholds are data-snooped artifacts

tests.name: up_day_vol_ratio_redundancy_test
tests.comparison: Partial correlation of up_day_ratio_20 with outcome (ruin/winner) after residualizing vol_ratio_5_20; test if up_day_ratio provides incremental information beyond vol_ratio
tests.success_criterion: Partial correlation coefficient > 0.25 OR nested model test (up_day_ratio adds) yields p < 0.10; supports treating features as orthogonal
tests.failure_criterion: Partial correlation < 0.10 AND up_day_ratio non-significant in nested test; supports skeptic's claim of structural correlation

tests.name: high_vol_ratio_ruin_mechanism_test
tests.comparison: Compare momentum deceleration profiles (ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio) between high-vol_ratio ruin cases (entity_ccc90a671f vol_ratio=1.45, entity_84824e6a20 vol_ratio=1.63) vs high-vol_ratio winners
tests.success_criterion: High-vol_ratio ruin cases show slope_ratio > 2.0 (sharp short-term acceleration) vs high-vol_ratio winners slope_ratio ≤ 1.5; provides second-order mechanism for counterexamples
tests.failure_criterion: No significant difference in slope_ratio between high-vol_ratio ruin and winner groups; high-vol_ratio ruin remains unexplained

tests.name: vol_ratio_w4_temporal_predictive_test

tests.success_criterion: Within-snapshot R² > 0.15 from vol_ratio_5_20 alone; confirms vol_ratio has entity-level predictive power not explainable by snapshot base rates
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot R² < 0.05; all apparent vol_ratio signal comes from snapshot-level confounding

tests.name: researcher_policy_hit_rate_validation
tests.comparison: Test two researcher proposals: (A) vol_ratio < 1.20 AND mom_20 0.05-0.20 → ruin probability >60%; (B) vol_ratio > 1.40 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60 → selected_winner probability >70%
tests.success_criterion: Both conditions hold with observed probabilities meeting or exceeding thresholds; validates policy implications
tests.failure_criterion: Either condition fails by >10 percentage points; invalidates specific policy recommendation
