w4_return_bucket is target variable only; never used as input feature
snapshot_anon not used as predictive feature; only used for grouping in within-snapshot tests
All features must be computable at snapshot time; no forward-looking information in feature construction
base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, ibd_entry_volume_ratio, ibd_entry_close_position, base_depth_pct not in frozen evidence features for this snapshot set and are excluded
No ticker identity or calendar identity used in test design

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: Low vol_ratio_5_20 associates with false-positive B0 ruin at the population level (median delta -1.05 standardized vs selected_winner), but the mechanism is not causal and fails for high-vol_ratio counterexamples. The two most damaging counterexamples—entity_ccc90a671f (vol_ratio=1.45) and entity_84824e6a20 (vol_ratio=1.63)—ruin despite exceeding the researcher's proposed winner threshold, indicating vol_ratio alone does not determine outcome. Snapshot contamination is the central vulnerability: the same snapshot (snap_71486ed83c) produces both ruin and winner outcomes, and up_day_ratio_20 shares structural correlation with vol_ratio_5_20 (both computed over the same 20-day window), contradicting the researcher's orthogonal-signal claim. The true signal is probabilistic: vol_ratio is a regime indicator that modulates ruin probability rather than a deterministic filter, and its predictive power may reflect snapshot-level base-rate variation rather than entity-level causal dynamics.
falsifiers: entity_ccc90a671f (vol_ratio=1.45, ruin) directly falsifies the researcher's vol_ratio>1.40 → winner rule; if this case is driven by an exogenous news event causing one-off volume spike, the rule survives but requires a second-order interaction not specified in the mechanism

entity_84824e6a20 (vol_ratio=1.63, highest in ruin set, ruin) falsifies any monotonic mechanism where higher vol_ratio reduces ruin probability; the experimental designer's high_vol_ratio_ruin_mechanism_test must identify a slope_ratio >2.0 for this entity to rescue the mechanism

within-snapshot vol_ratio rank-order must correlate monotonically with outcome (ruin→winner) in at least 3 snapshots with N≥3 per class; if Spearman rho ≤0.10 or direction reverses in >50% of qualifying snapshots, the mechanism is confounded by snapshot base rates
if continuous (spline logistic) model does not outperform threshold model by AICc ≤4 and jackknife threshold stability exceeds ±0.15, the 1.20/1.40 cutoffs are data-snooped artifacts
if partial correlation of up_day_ratio_20 after residualizing vol_ratio_5_20 is <0.10 and non-significant in nested test, the researcher's composite-score policy implication is invalid
vol_ratio_5_20 explains <5% within-snapshot variance (R²<0.05) would indicate all apparent signal comes from snapshot-level confounding
actionable_design_principles: Treat vol_ratio_5_20 as a soft probabilistic modifier, not a binary gate; any policy using vol_ratio must acknowledge ruin cases at every vol_ratio level

Require second-order interaction terms (slope_ratio = ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5, vol_ratio × mom_20) before deploying vol_ratio thresholds in policy; a slope_ratio >2.0 with high vol_ratio signals potential trap (professional manipulation disguised as institutional accumulation)
Mandatory within-snapshot hold-out: for any vol_ratio-based policy, report within-snapshot hit rates; policies that only work cross-sectionally but fail within snapshots should not be deployed

Decompose vol_ratio into sustained vs transient components using volume-at-price distribution or tick rules; transient spikes (single high-volume day) may explain entity_ccc90a671f and entity_84824e6a20 counterexamples

Do not combine up_day_ratio_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 in a composite score without first orthogonalizing them (e.g., via PCA or residualization); their shared 20-day window creates structural correlation that inflates apparent discriminative power

Pullback severity (depth, duration) is the likely causal variable downstream of vol_ratio; if vol_ratio merely proxies for how deep the subsequent pullback will be, the mechanism is measurement-of-effect rather than cause, and interventions should target entry timing relative to pullback phase rather than volume filters alone

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot-normalized vol_ratio z-score within each snapshot's B0 candidate pool; entry only when entity's vol_ratio exceeds snapshot median by >0.5 SD and slope_ratio ≤1.5
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses snapshot contamination by making vol_ratio relative to snapshot context rather than absolute; adding slope_ratio interaction addresses high-vol_ratio ruin counterexamples by filtering entities where short-term acceleration is disproportionate to longer-term trend
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents systematic over-selection of B0 picks in high-volume snapshots where base rates are favorable; ensures vol_ratio signal is entity-specific, not regime-driven

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Two-tier volume confirmation: (A) vol_ratio > 1.20 required AND (B) 5-day cumulative volume distribution shows >60% of volume occurring on up days within that 5-day window; entities failing condition B are flagged even if condition A passes
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Distinguishes sustained institutional accumulation (up-day volume concentration) from erratic noise-driven volume spikes that produce false-positive high vol_ratio readings like entity_84824e6a20; decomposes the single scalar ratio into directional and magnitude components
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Addresses the structural correlation problem by using a separate 5-day window rather than the 20-day window shared with up_day_ratio_20, allowing orthogonal measurement of volume quality

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Momentum-volume decoupling score: |mom_20 - median_mom_20_in_vol_quintile| / ATR_14; threshold for concern when score < 0.3 (momentum is typical for volume regime) versus score > 0.6 (momentum diverges from volume regime, potential trap)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Tests whether entity's momentum is appropriate for its volume regime; low vol_ratio entities with high momentum scores represent the trap scenario (professional manipulation), while low vol_ratio with low momentum scores may represent genuine accumulation from a lower base
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Provides a single scalar that combines volume and momentum interaction without using hard thresholds; allows continuous risk scoring rather than binary accept/reject

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Within-snapshot win-rate calibration: for each snapshot, compute empirical ruin probability given vol_ratio quintile; use snapshot-specific priors rather than global thresholds
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Explicitly models snapshot as the primary source of outcome variation; vol_ratio becomes a relative rather than absolute predictor, addressing the circularity concern that false_negative groups are defined by future W4 returns that vol_ratio may also predict
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Yields adaptive policy that respects snapshot heterogeneity; if within-snapshot calibration reveals no vol_ratio effect, the policy correctly outputs UNRESOLVED rather than forcing a false positive

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under volume confirmation/dry-up; propose a counterexample that would invalidate the pattern. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: B0 false-positive ruin occurs when volume confirmation peaks at or before the signal snapshot and subsequently contracts, indicating distribution rather than accumulation; the short-term momentum (MA10 slope) decelerates relative to longer-term trend (MA20 slope), creating divergence that predicts failure despite otherwise healthy entry geometry.
evidence_for: false_positive_ruin cases show vol_ratio_5_20 median of 1.21-1.45 (high early confirmation) versus selected_winner median of 1.42-1.58, but this ratio subsequently collapses post-snapshot in ruin cases
ma10_slope_5 standardized delta is -0.6815 between false_negative and selected_winner, indicating short-term momentum decay is a distinguishing feature at snapshot
entity_8f0df3d38e (ruin): vol_ratio_5_20=1.24, ma10_slope_5=0.054, ma20_slope_5=0.037 (ratio=1.46), then pulls back -16.2% over 7 weeks
entity_40ea0cfb3b (ruin): vol_ratio_5_20=0.906 (below median), indicating volume already contracted at snapshot, with mom_20=0.024 (lowest in ruin set)
selected_winner entity_2c58cebc59 sustains vol_ratio_5_20=1.62 and ma10_slope_5=0.013 despite pullback of -25.1% (recovery occurred because volume stayed elevated)
px_vs_ma20 delta of -0.5842 standardized suggests false-positive ruin cases have weaker price proximity to moving averages, consistent with distribution pattern
evidence_against: entity_6618d3e80c labeled both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner with vol_ratio_5_20=1.45 and ma10_slope_5=0.075, showing mixed signal cannot resolve cleanly
entity_b00579f203 (selected_winner) has vol_ratio_5_20=1.58 but also high mom_20=0.23 and ma10_slope_5=0.053, suggesting high volume alone insufficient without momentum context
Pullback metrics are unavailable at snapshot time for 6 of 8 ruin cases, so the failure mechanism must be inferred from pre-snapshot features only
Two ruin cases (entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_84824e6a20) show up_day_ratio_20=0.6 and 0.4 respectively, indicating breadth deterioration is not a consistent predictor
falsifiable_predictions: A B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4 AND ma10_slope_5 > 0.05 AND ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio > 1.2 will NOT produce ruin outcome regardless of other features
A B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0 at snapshot will produce ruin outcome in >80% of cases if other momentum features are weak (mom_20 < 0.08)
A B0 pick showing vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.5 but with ma10_slope_5 turning negative within 2 weeks post-snapshot will produce false-positive ruin despite early volume confirmation

Counterexample to invalidate: Find a B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20=0.85 (volume dry-up) and ma10_slope_5=0.06 (strong short-term momentum) that becomes selected_winner with large_win bucket—this would falsify the claim that volume contraction + strong momentum predicts ruin
policy_implications: Add post-snapshot volume monitoring rule: if vol_ratio_5_20 declines by >30% within first 3 weeks after B0 signal, exit or reduce position regardless of price action
Filter B0 candidates with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0 out of fresh entries; allow existing positions only if ma10_slope_5 > 0.04 and mom_20 > 0.10
Use ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio as entry quality gate: reject B0 picks where ratio < 1.0 even if absolute momentum values appear acceptable
Avoid increasing position size on B0 picks showing vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4 at entry without confirming ma10_slope_5 acceleration in subsequent weeks

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The volume-ratio-to-ruin mechanism is a post-hoc narrative built on unobserved post-snapshot volume data. All proposed 'volume dry-up' is inferred from ma10/ma20 slope divergence and pullback metrics that are unavailable at snapshot time, not from actual volume measurements after the snapshot. This makes the mechanism untestable against the available frozen evidence.

attacks.issue: vol_ratio_5_20 is a backward-looking confirmation indicator, not a forward predictor of accumulation or distribution
attacks.why_it_matters: A volume ratio > 1.4 at snapshot means volume WAS elevated in the recent past, not that it WILL remain elevated. The researcher treats vol_ratio_5_20 as a leading indicator of accumulation health, but it is merely a trailing proxy for prior price momentum. The mechanism of 'volume confirmation peaks at snapshot and then contracts' is asserted, not demonstrated with post-snapshot volume data.

attacks.issue: ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio > 1.2 as an entry quality gate is mechanically circular with vol_ratio_5_20
attacks.why_it_matters: Both vol_ratio_5_20 and ma10_slope_5 are generated from the same recent 5-day window. A high volume ratio in the same window that produced strong ma10_slope_5 means they are not independent discriminators—they co-measure the same recent surge. The researcher treats them as separate filters when they are statistically redundant.

attacks.issue: entity_6618d3e80c carries dual labels false_positive_ruin|selected_winner, contaminating the case base
attacks.why_it_matters: A case labeled both ruin AND winner cannot be used to test the mechanism since its outcome is ambiguous. If the labeling scheme permits hybrid outcomes, the binary pattern between ruin vs. winner groups is unreliable. This entity was used by the researcher as evidence of 'mixed signal cannot resolve,' but it actually reveals the labeling system is insufficient to distinguish the pattern.

attacks.issue: pullback metrics are unavailable at snapshot for 6 of 8 ruin cases, making pullback_depth_pct a post-hoc filter not available at decision time
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher proposes rules like 'if vol_ratio_5_20 declines by >30% within 3 weeks, exit.' No post-snapshot volume data exists in the frozen evidence to validate this. The entire proposed monitoring mechanism is untestable against the available data, yet it is presented as an actionable policy.

attacks.issue: selected_winner entity_3adc078f01 has vol_ratio_5_20=1.14 (below the 1.4 threshold) yet sustains a -42.3% pullback and still wins
attacks.why_it_matters: This directly contradicts the claim that below-threshold vol_ratio_5_20 predicts ruin or that large pullbacks indicate impending failure. The researcher's own evidence shows vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.4 does not prevent selected_winner outcomes even with extreme drawdowns.

counterexamples_to_seek: A B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0 at snapshot, ma10_slope_5 < 0.01 (weak momentum), and mom_20 < 0.05 that becomes a selected_winner with large_win bucket—this would show volume contraction alone does not mechanically cause ruin

A B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4, ma10_slope_5 > 0.05, AND post-snapshot volume data showing volume remained elevated (>1.3 ratio at W1 and W2) that still produced ruin outcome—this would invalidate the claim that volume dry-up is the mechanism

A set of B0 picks from a single snapshot_anon (same market regime) split evenly between selected_winner and false_positive_ruin with nearly identical vol_ratio_5_20 and momentum features—demonstrating the features cannot discriminate within regime
A B0 pick where vol_ratio_5_20 was < 1.0 at snapshot but volume surged in weeks 1-3 post-snapshot and the entity still ruined—showing that post-snapshot volume increase does not save positions
what_would_change_my_mind: Access to actual volume ratios measured at W1, W2, and W3 post-snapshot for the ruin cases showing vol_ratio_5_20 had contracted from snapshot levels
Evidence that the ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio can discriminate ruin vs. winner outcomes within a single snapshot_anon (holding market regime constant)

A controlled experiment showing that filtering out B0 picks where vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4 but ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio < 1.0 would have eliminated >70% of ruin cases without removing >50% of selected_winner cases
Demonstration that pullback_depth_pct for the 6 ruin cases with null pullback data is actually available via a separate data source, making the mechanism testable with actual post-snapshot price data

tests.name: slope_ratio_discrimination_test
tests.comparison: ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio calculated at snapshot; ruination vs selected_winner groups compared via Mann-Whitney U on ratio values
tests.success_criterion: Ratio median for false_positive_ruin cases is statistically significantly lower (p<0.05) than ratio median for selected_winner cases, and ratio threshold of 1.0 achieves >70% separation accuracy
tests.failure_criterion: No significant difference in ratio distributions between outcome groups, OR ratio threshold of 1.0 produces <60% separation—invalidating slope-ratio-as-gate claim

tests.name: volume_ratio_standalone_test
tests.comparison: Direct comparison of vol_ratio_5_20 distributions between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner without conditioning on any momentum features; test whether vol_ratio alone discriminates
tests.success_criterion: vol_ratio_5_20 median for false_positive_ruin is significantly lower (p<0.05) than selected_winner, AND vol_ratio < 1.0 predicts ruin in >75% of applicable cases
tests.failure_criterion: vol_ratio_5_20 distributions are statistically indistinguishable between outcome groups (p>0.1), OR vol_ratio < 1.0 appears in selected_winner cases at comparable frequency to ruin cases—falsifying volume-dry-up mechanism

tests.name: momentum_only_test
tests.comparison: Test whether mom_20 AND ma10_slope_5 together (without volume) can discriminate ruin vs winner; addresses skeptic's claim that vol_ratio_5_20 is backward-looking and redundant with recent momentum
tests.success_criterion: Combination of mom_20 < 0.08 AND ma10_slope_5 < 0.02 predicts false_positive_ruin in >70% of cases where both conditions hold
tests.failure_criterion: Momentum-only features produce no significant discrimination (AUC < 0.6 for ruin vs winner), indicating volume features are necessary for prediction

tests.name: within_snapshot_regime_test
tests.comparison: Identify snapshots containing both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner B0 picks; test whether feature values overlap within regime, directly testing skeptic's claim that features cannot discriminate within market regime
tests.success_criterion: No snapshot contains mixed outcome B0 picks with identical vol_ratio_5_20 (±0.1) AND identical ma10_slope_5 (±0.01) AND identical mom_20 (±0.02)—demonstrating features do discriminate within regime
tests.failure_criterion: At least one snapshot shows false_positive_ruin and selected_winner with overlapping feature values within stated tolerances—falsifying feature discriminability within regime

tests.name: hybrid_label_ambiguity_test
tests.comparison: Quantify contamination from entity_6618d3e80c (dual-labeled false_positive_ruin|selected_winner) and any other multi-outcome entities; test sensitivity of pattern to their exclusion
tests.success_criterion: Removing dual-labeled entities changes ruin vs winner median for vol_ratio_5_20 by <0.05 AND changes slope ratio median by <0.1—demonstrating robustness to labeling ambiguity
tests.failure_criterion: Removing dual-labeled entities flips the sign of median difference between outcome groups for any feature, OR causes statistically significant shift in distributions—revealing pattern is labeling-dependent

tests.name: ibd_entry_distance_decay_test
tests.comparison: Test whether ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (distance from trigger) moderates vol_ratio_5_20's predictive power; addresses researcher claim that entry quality interacts with volume confirmation
tests.success_criterion: Among B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.3, those with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.04 show ruin rate < 20%, while those with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.02 show ruin rate > 50%
tests.failure_criterion: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct does not moderate vol_ratio_5_20's relationship to outcome (no significant interaction in logistic regression)

leakage_checks: pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct excluded from all test features—these are post-snapshot observables unavailable at decision time
w4_return_bucket excluded from test features—it's an outer-forward outcome, not a PIT feature
snapshot_anon used only for regime stratification in within_snapshot_regime_test, never as a predictor feature

All slope ratios computed from same 5-day window (ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5) must be flagged as potentially redundant per skeptic's circularity concern; tests do not claim independence between these features
Tests 1-3 use only pre-snapshot PIT features; no feature represents information that would not be available to a trader at the moment of B0 signal
Test 4 (within-snapshot regime) uses snapshot_anon only to group cases for comparison, not as a predictive feature per rules
Test 5 (hybrid label) is a sensitivity check, not a predictive test; its purpose is to verify the stability of findings under labeling noise

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: Snapshot-level features (vol_ratio_5_20, ma10_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20) show group-level separation between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner outcomes. However, the specific causal mechanism—volume confirmation peaks at snapshot then contracts, causing failure—is not testable with frozen evidence. The proposed volume-dry-up narrative requires post-snapshot volume data that does not exist in this dataset. The ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 ratio and vol_ratio_5_20 are computed from overlapping 5-day windows and lack statistical independence. Entity_3adc078f01 (selected_winner with vol_ratio_5_20=1.14 below proposed thresholds, sustaining -42.3% pullback) demonstrates the mechanism's predictive failure. The strongest observable signal is up_day_ratio_20 (standardized delta -1.1882), not volume ratio. Within-snapshot overlap between ruin and winner groups exists, making regime-conditional prediction unreliable without post-snapshot confirmation.
falsifiers: Find a B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 < 0.9, ma10_slope_5 > 0.06, mom_20 > 0.12, up_day_ratio_20 > 0.6 that produces false_positive_ruin outcome—this would show volume contraction with strong breadth/momentum still leads to ruin

Demonstrate within a single snapshot_anon that B0 picks with identical vol_ratio_5_20 (±0.05) and up_day_ratio_20 (±0.05) split between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner—showing snapshot-level features cannot discriminate within regime
Show actual post-snapshot volume measurements (W1, W2, W3) demonstrating that volume contracted >30% for ruin cases while remaining elevated for selected_winner cases matched on snapshot features
Confirm entity_6618d3e80c's true single-label outcome via external price/volume data beyond W4 return bucket, resolving the dual-label contamination
Find B0 pick with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.5, ma10_slope_5 > 0.05, up_day_ratio_20 > 0.65 that still produces ruin—this would invalidate the threshold-based filter proposed in policy
actionable_design_principles: Use up_day_ratio_20 as primary pre-snapshot discriminator (standardized delta -1.1882 strongest among available features), not volume ratio
Treat vol_ratio_5_20 and ma10_slope_5 as redundant co-measurements of the same 5-day window; do not apply both as independent filters
Accept that post-snapshot volume monitoring cannot be designed from this evidence base; policy must use only snapshot-time features or acknowledge UNRESOLVED status
Apply regime-stratified evaluation: pattern may hold in high-up_day_ratio_20 regimes (breadth thrust) but fail in low-breadth environments
Define clear single-outcome labeling rules; entity_6618d3e80c dual-label reveals labeling system insufficiency for binary pattern analysis
Require >0.125 gap in up_day_ratio_20 (median delta) between candidate and false_negative baseline as necessary condition for selection

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Breadth-gated entry: Accept B0 pick only if up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.6 AND vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.2; otherwise flag for extended monitoring before entry
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Uses breadth (up_day_ratio_20) as primary gate rather than volume ratio alone, addressing skeptic's backward-looking critique by pairing with a forward-looking breadth signal
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Filters low-breadth B0 picks (up_day_ratio_20 < 0.6) which constitute majority of false_negative cases in the evidence base

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Slope divergence alert: Flag B0 pick where ma10_slope_5 < 0.015 AND ma20_slope_5 > 0.025 (negative slope ratio) as elevated-risk despite acceptable volume
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Detects momentum deceleration without claiming volume causation; uses slope relationship as breadth/momentum divergence indicator rather than volume-dry-up mechanism
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Addresses researcher observation that slope ratio differs between groups while acknowledging skeptic's redundancy concern by not pairing with vol_ratio_5_20

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Null-pullback exclusion rule: B0 picks with null pullback_duration_weeks AND null pullback_pct in evidence should not be used to train pullback-depth-based exit rules

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Within-regime validation requirement: Before deploying any B0 filter based on snapshot features, require demonstration of discrimination within at least one snapshot_anon containing mixed outcomes
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Directly addresses experimental designer's within_snapshot_regime_test and skeptic's counterexample about same-regime feature overlap; enforces falsifiability at regime level
features: any snapshot-time feature used as filter
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Ensures no filter passes that produces overlapping feature values for ruin vs winner within market regime

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under industry concentration; identify repeated PIT-visible precursors. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-positive B0 picks that 'ruin' exhibit short-term trend acceleration decoupled from longer-term momentum structure. At entry, the ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratio exceeds 1.5 (median ~2.5), indicating the short-term trend is running materially faster than the medium-term trend—a PIT-visible divergence pattern that precedes mean-reversion failure under sector concentration.
evidence_for: False_positive_ruin cases show ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 ratios of 1.5x to 14x (entity_40ea0cfb3b: 13.9x, entity_ccc90a671f: 3.6x, entity_84824e6a20: 2.95x), while selected_winner cases show ratios below 1.2x or negative (entity_bec51a4227: 0.84x, entity_ead73f4390: 1.07x, entity_d2ca7853ba: 0.79x).
Ruin cases cluster in mom_20 range 0.07-0.24 with up_day_ratio_20 of 0.40-0.65—moderate bullishness without the strong participation (up_day_ratio >= 0.70) seen in many winners.

The vol_ratio_5_20 for ruin cases is elevated (1.21-1.63) but NOT extreme (no ruin case exceeds 1.77), whereas selected_winner cases span 1.01-1.77 with no clear ceiling—implying elevated volatility alone is not the ruin signal.
px_vs_ma20 for ruin cases occupies the moderate band (0.048-0.124), suggesting extended-but-not-explosive price position relative to the 20-week average.

The ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct for ruin cases (0.029-0.074) shows stocks entering with tighter-than-average IBD triggers, consistent with transient momentum spikes rather than confirmed breakouts.
evidence_against: Entity_6618d3e80c is labeled both false_positive_ruin and selected_winner, with a ma10/ma20 ratio of 3.75x (supporting the mechanism) yet achieved a large_win—this indicates the mechanism is probabilistic, not deterministic.
Entity_2f86543bf6 is a selected_winner with ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 = -1.0 (negative short-term slope), demonstrating that low or negative short-term momentum does not exclude positive outcomes.
Entity_8ad5cd4795 is a selected_winner with vol_ratio_5_20 = 0.996 (below 1.0) and up_day_ratio_20 = 0.70, showing that low volatility with strong participation can override the deceleration signal.

The numeric_contrasts table shows mom_20 standardized_delta = -1.0005 for false_negatives vs selected_winners, but the ruin cases have HIGHER mom_20 than many winners—suggesting momentum magnitude is not the differentiating variable.
falsifiable_predictions: In rolling 27-case windows where B0 picks with ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 > 2.0 AND mom_20 between 0.05-0.25 AND vol_ratio_5_20 between 1.15-1.70 exceed 40% of the window's picks, the subsequent 4-week return bucket distribution will show ruin probability > 30% (vs. baseline of ~20% for the overall sample).

The slope_ratio = ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 will exhibit a bimodal distribution separating false_positive_ruin (ratio > 1.5) from selected_winner (ratio < 1.5) at the snapshot level, testable via a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on independent snapshots.

If the mechanism is correct, sector concentration events (measurable as cross-pick correlation in px_vs_ma20 at snapshot time) will amplify ruin probability specifically for high-slope-ratio picks, but not for low-slope-ratio picks—prediction: interaction term slope_ratio × concentration is significant at p < 0.05 in a logistic regression on ruin outcome.
policy_implications: B0 selection filter: reject or reduce weight for picks where ma10_slope_5 > 1.5 × ma20_slope_5, particularly when mom_20 is in the 0.05-0.25 band and vol_ratio_5_20 exceeds 1.15.

Risk sizing adjustment: for picks passing the slope_ratio filter, allocate smaller position sizes when ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05 (indicating tight entry), as this correlates with ruin outcomes in the moderate-momentum cohort.

Snapshot-level concentration check: before constructing a B0 portfolio, compute the median slope_ratio across selected picks—if the median exceeds 1.2, the portfolio contains an above-baseline proportion of the false-positive precursor pattern, suggesting a sector momentum trap environment.

Post-entry monitoring: the ma10_slope_5 decay rate in weeks 1-3 post-entry should be tracked; if ma10_slope_5 crosses below ma20_slope_5 within 2 weeks of entry for a high-ratio pick, the ruin probability should de-escalate (per entity_6618d3e80c mixed labeling).

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The slope ratio (ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5) is a mathematical artifact of dividing by a near-zero denominator, not an independent causal mechanism. The false-positive ruin signal is actually explained by IBD entry tightness (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.045) combined with sector concentration, with the slope ratio merely correlating with these confounders.

attacks.issue: Denominator instability creates spurious ratios
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_55c2da490e has ma20_slope_5 = -0.0049 (negative denominator) producing a slope_ratio of -4.08—a sign-flip artifact that has no mechanical interpretation as 'acceleration.' Similarly, entity_40ea0cfb3b has ma20_slope_5 = 0.0018 (near-zero denominator) producing a ratio of 13.9x that is an artifact of measurement noise in ma20_slope_5, not a real divergence signal. Using ratio metrics with near-zero denominators violates the interval-scale requirement for meaningful division operations.

attacks.issue: IBD entry tightness confounds the mechanism
attacks.why_it_matters: The numeric_contrasts show ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct has a standardized_delta of only -0.6952 between false_negatives and selected_winners, but this understates its importance for RUIN specifically. All 8 false_positive_ruin cases have ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct in the range 0.028-0.074, while selected_winners span 0.001-0.070 with no lower bound constraint. The mechanism conflates 'tight entry' (a known overfitting risk) with 'slope divergence,' when the former is the actual predictive variable and the latter is a consequence of tight entries capturing transient momentum spikes.

attacks.issue: Pullback duration clustering is a sample artifact
attacks.why_it_matters: 6 out of 8 false_positive_ruin cases have pullback_duration_weeks exactly 7.0 weeks (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_ccc90a671f, entity_55c2da490e) or null. This clustering at the 7-week mark is improbable under a continuous mechanism and suggests either (a) a data pipeline artifact where 7 weeks is a default fill value, or (b) the outcome classification itself uses a 7-week threshold to define 'ruin.' If the outcome definition uses a 7-week duration cutoff for ruin classification, the analysis is circular—the supposed PIT-visible precursor is downstream of the classification rule.

attacks.issue: No independent validation set
attacks.why_it_matters: The entire analysis uses 'discovery-train-only' data (method_note: 'Discovery-train-only anonymized error archaeology'). The falsifiable predictions specify testing on 'independent snapshots' and 'rolling 27-case windows,' but the claim is being evaluated on the same 27 cases used to generate it. With n=27 and approximately 20 features, the probability of finding at least one feature with standardized_delta > 1.0 by chance (multiple testing problem) exceeds 60%. The claimed mechanism may be a selection artifact of mining 20+ features across a small sample.

attacks.issue: Entity_6618d3e80c falsifies the deterministic interpretation but the researcher retreats to 'probabilistic' without evidence
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher correctly notes entity_6618d3e80c has slope_ratio = 3.71x AND outcome = selected_winner, then concludes the mechanism is 'probabilistic.' But this concession is unearned—if the mechanism were genuinely probabilistic, the slope_ratio would have documented predictive power conditional on other variables. No such conditional analysis exists in the claim. The retreat to 'probabilistic' is a unfalsifiable hedge that cannot be rejected by any observation in this dataset, violating the Popperian criterion for scientific theories.

counterexamples_to_seek: B0 picks with slope_ratio > 2.0, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05, and industry concentration in the top quartile that do NOT result in ruin (to test if the mechanism requires concentration as a necessary condition).
B0 picks with slope_ratio < 1.2, low mom_20 (0.05-0.15), and high vol_ratio (1.3-1.6) that produce ruin outcomes (to test if slope_ratio is truly necessary vs. optional).
Temporal validation: apply the slope_ratio > 1.5 filter to snapshots NOT used in training (e.g., adjacent time periods) and measure whether ruin probability actually exceeds 30%.

Synthetic counterexample construction: generate random portfolios with the same feature distributions as ruin cases but shuffled outcome labels, and verify the slope_ratio distribution does NOT separate the shuffled groups.
what_would_change_my_mind: Demonstration that slope_ratio > 1.5 retains predictive power (p < 0.05) in a held-out validation set of at least 50 B0 picks where the mechanism was not used to select the training cases.

A mechanistic explanation for why negative ma20_slope_5 denominators (entity_55c2da490e) should be excluded from the ratio calculation, and evidence that the remaining positive-denominator ratio cases still separate ruin from winners.

Confirmation that pullback_duration_weeks = 7.0 is NOT a data pipeline artifact or classification threshold, with evidence that ruin cases with different pullback durations show the same slope_ratio distribution.

A causal model (e.g., instrumental variable or regression discontinuity design) showing that slope_ratio manipulation (if possible) would change ruin probability, not merely that slope_ratio correlates with ruin conditional on other variables.

tests.name: denominator_stability_filter_test
tests.comparison: Within cases where |ma20_slope_5| >= 0.01 (stable denominator), compare ruin_rate between slope_ratio_quartile_4 (top 25%) vs quartile_1-3 (bottom 75%). Compare this to the ruin-rate difference when including near-zero denominators.
tests.success_criterion: Ruin-rate difference between slope_ratio quartile_4 and quartile_1-3 remains statistically significant (p < 0.05) after excluding |ma20_slope_5| < 0.01 cases, with at most 20% attenuation in effect size.
tests.failure_criterion: Statistical significance disappears (p >= 0.05) or effect size attenuates by >50% after denominator filter, indicating the mechanism is a mathematical artifact of near-zero denominators.

tests.name: confounder_decomposition_test
tests.comparison: Fit two logistic regressions on ruin outcome: (A) slope_ratio as sole predictor, (B) slope_ratio + ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as joint predictors. Compare marginal vs. partial R^2 and coefficients. Then swap—use ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as sole predictor vs. ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct + slope_ratio. Test whether slope_ratio adds explanatory power beyond entry tightness.
tests.success_criterion: slope_ratio retains statistically significant coefficient (p < 0.05) after controlling for ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, and adding slope_ratio to a model already containing ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct improves AUC by > 0.05.
tests.failure_criterion: slope_ratio becomes non-significant (p >= 0.10) after conditioning on ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, or adding slope_ratio to a model containing ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct improves AUC by < 0.02, indicating entry tightness is the true predictor.

tests.name: pullback_artifact_check
tests.comparison: Separate false_positive_ruin cases into two groups: (1) pullback_duration_weeks = 7.0 or null, (2) pullback_duration_weeks != 7.0. Compare the slope_ratio distribution between groups using a two-sample test. Also compare the feature distributions to check if the 7-week cluster has systematically different precursor features.
tests.success_criterion: No statistically significant difference (p >= 0.10) in slope_ratio or other precursor features between pullback_duration_weeks = 7.0/null vs. other values, indicating the 7-week cluster is not a data artifact.
tests.failure_criterion: pullback_duration_weeks = 7.0/null cases have significantly higher (p < 0.05) slope_ratio than other durations, suggesting the ruin classification may use a 7-week threshold that creates a self-fulfilling signal.

tests.name: conditional_slope_ratio_test
tests.comparison: Within matched strata defined by ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct buckets (0-0.02, 0.02-0.04, 0.04-0.08, >0.08), test whether slope_ratio separates ruin from non-ruin outcomes. This addresses whether the mechanism is a genuine predictor or an artifact of entry tightness stratification.
tests.success_criterion: In at least 3 of 4 ibd_entry buckets, ruin-rate is higher in slope_ratio > 1.5 subgroup vs. slope_ratio <= 1.5 subgroup, with pooled effect direction consistent across strata.
tests.failure_criterion: The ruin-rate difference by slope_ratio reverses sign or becomes insignificant within most ibd_entry buckets, indicating slope_ratio is not an independent mechanism.

tests.name: probabilistic_interaction_test
tests.comparison: Test whether the 'probabilistic' interpretation is itself falsifiable. If ruin probability is a function of slope_ratio, vol_ratio, mom_20, and up_day_ratio jointly, then for any fixed probability level, there should exist a tradeoff surface. Test: do cases with slope_ratio > 2.0 AND vol_ratio > 1.3 have ruin probability > 0.40, even when mom_20 and up_day_ratio are favorable? If yes, the mechanism is not fully probabilistic—high slope_ratio overrides other factors.
tests.success_criterion: Ruin probability in the high_slope_ratio_high_vol stratum (slope_ratio > 2.0 AND vol_ratio > 1.3) exceeds 0.40 regardless of mom_20/up_day_ratio values, confirming the slope_ratio operates as a threshold override rather than a probabilistic modifier.
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin probability in the high_slope_ratio_high_vol stratum falls below 0.40 when mom_20 > 0.20 AND up_day_ratio >= 0.65, indicating the mechanism is genuinely probabilistic and slope_ratio is not a deterministic override.

tests.name: partial_correlation_test
tests.comparison: Compute partial correlation between slope_ratio and ruin outcome after regressing out mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and up_day_ratio_20. This tests whether the claimed 'decoupling' of short-term from medium-term momentum is genuine (residual correlation) or spurious (correlation explained by other features).
tests.success_criterion: Partial correlation between slope_ratio and ruin remains significant (p < 0.05) after controlling for mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and up_day_ratio_20, confirming the short-term vs. medium-term divergence is an independent signal.
tests.failure_criterion: Partial correlation becomes non-significant (p >= 0.10) after controlling for the medium-term features, indicating slope_ratio is a proxy for mom_20, vol_ratio, or up_day_ratio rather than an independent divergence signal.

leakage_checks: All features must be evaluated at snapshot time only; w4_return_bucket is used only as outcome variable, not as a predictor.
No calendar date features are used as inputs; tests are cross-sectional within snapshots.
Pullback features (pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_pct) are post-entry measurements and must not be used as predictors—only as stratification variables or outcome-adjacent checks.
Entity-level identifiers are not used as predictive features; only anonymized entity IDs for matching.

The 27-case sample is treated as a discovery set; tests should specify whether they are generating hypotheses (exploratory, p < 0.10 acceptable) or testing pre-specified claims (confirmatory, p < 0.05 required).

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The slope_ratio (ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 > 1.5) shows descriptive separation between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner cases in this 27-case discovery sample, but the evidence does not support it as an independent causal mechanism. Three critical confounds undermine the claim: (1) Denominator instability—several ruin cases have near-zero or negative ma20_slope_5 (entity_55c2da490e: -0.0049, entity_40ea0cfb3b: 0.0018), making the ratio an arithmetic artifact rather than a meaningful divergence signal; (2) IBD entry tightness collinearity—the ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct range for ruin cases (0.028–0.074) overlaps with selected_winners, and the confounder decomposition test has not yet been run to separate their independent contributions; (3) Pullback duration artifact—6 of 8 ruin cases have pullback_duration_weeks = 7.0 or null, suggesting the classification may encode a temporal threshold rather than a PIT-visible precursor. The probabilistic retreat by the researcher is unfalsifiable without a documented conditional analysis. The mechanism is better characterized as a hypothesis warranting validation than a supported finding.
falsifiers: The denominator_stability_filter_test fails: if slope_ratio loses statistical significance (p >= 0.05) after excluding |ma20_slope_5| < 0.01 cases, the mechanism is arithmetic noise.

The confounder_decomposition_test fails: if conditioning on ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct eliminates slope_ratio's coefficient significance (p >= 0.10) or adds < 0.02 AUC, the mechanism is redundant with entry tightness.

The pullback_artifact_check fails: if pullback_duration_weeks = 7.0/null cases have significantly higher slope_ratio (p < 0.05), the ruin label encodes a temporal threshold rather than measuring a precursor.
A held-out validation test on 50+ independent B0 picks where slope_ratio > 1.5 does not produce ruin probability > 30%.

Negative ma20_slope_5 denominators (entity_55c2da490e) included in the ratio calculation produce physically meaningless negative ratios that should be excluded, but removing them leaves insufficient sample to establish the mechanism.

Entity_6618d3e80c (slope_ratio = 3.71x, outcome = selected_winner with large_win) remains unexplained under any variant of the mechanism, indicating non-determinism that the researcher has not quantified.
actionable_design_principles: RULE-OUT BEFORE RULE-IN: The denominator_stability_filter_test and confounder_decomposition_test must be executed and published before the slope_ratio enters any production scoring model. Neither has been run.

TREAT PULLBACK_DURATION AS SUSPECT: Treat pullback_duration_weeks = 7.0 as a potential classification artifact until proven otherwise. Exclude null and 7.0 values from any feature engineering pipeline that feeds into the ruin outcome variable.

REQUIRE SYMMETRIC SIGN HANDLING: Any ratio-based feature must document behavior when the denominator is negative or near-zero. The current mechanism implicitly assumes positive denominators, which is violated in at least one case.

DEMAND PROBABILISTIC QUANTIFICATION: If the mechanism is probabilistic, it must specify P(ruin | slope_ratio > 1.5, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20) from a conditional model—not just assert it. Without this, 'probabilistic' is a hedge, not a scientific claim.

MINIMUM VALIDATION THRESHOLD: No slope_ratio-based filter should be deployed unless demonstrated on a held-out set of >= 50 cases not used in hypothesis generation. The current n=27 discovery sample is below the threshold for confirmatory inference.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Two-stage filter: require slope_ratio > 1.5 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <= 0.045 as a combined condition for flagging potential ruin, with a documented justification for why entry tightness should be inverted in this context.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This addresses the confounder concern by explicitly conditioning on entry tightness rather than treating slope_ratio as a standalone signal. It also forces the analyst to articulate why tight entries in high-ratio stocks are acceptable (if they are) or dangerous (if they compound the ruin signal).
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents deployment of slope_ratio as an independent ruin signal when its apparent predictive power may be an artifact of entry tightness stratification.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Denominator stability gate: compute ma20_slope_5 as a rolling 5-day standard error estimate, and only compute slope_ratio when |ma20_slope_5| > 0.01 AND ma20_slope_5 > 0. Exclude negative-denominator ratios from all downstream models.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This directly addresses the denominator instability attack by establishing a mechanical rule for when the ratio is computable, rather than relying on post-hoc exclusion that could introduce selection bias.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Ensures the slope_ratio feature meets the interval-scale requirement for division operations before entering any model. Without this, the feature has no mechanical interpretation.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Temporal hold-out validation protocol: require that any slope_ratio threshold proposed for production be tested on snapshots from a non-adjacent time period that was not used in hypothesis generation, with a pre-specified success criterion (e.g., ruin rate in high-ratio stratum exceeds 25% vs. < 15% in low-ratio stratum, p < 0.05).
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This addresses the 'discovery-train-only' limitation by requiring temporal out-of-sample validation, which is distinct from random hold-out validation and more appropriate for time-series trading signals.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents deployment of features that overfit to the discovery sample's temporal structure. With 27 cases and 20+ features, multiple testing risk is non-trivial; temporal hold-out is a conservative control.

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under industry concentration; separate true signal from correlated proxy. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-positive B0 picks that ruin exhibit an early-stage 'velocity plateau' in price momentum relative to moving average slopes: the short-term slope (ma10_slope_5) decouples from medium-term slope (ma20_slope_5) at a ratio threshold above ~2.5x, signaling unsustainable momentum rather than genuine trend acceleration. This ratio-based decoupling is a correlated proxy for industry rotation risk that becomes ruinous under concentration, but is NOT a causal mechanism itself—industry concentration is the causal amplifier.

entity_84824e6a20 (false_positive_ruin): ma10_slope_5=0.0617, ma20_slope_5=0.0213, ratio=2.90x; mom_20=0.067

entity_2c58cebc59 (selected_winner, large_win): ma10_slope_5=0.0131, ma20_slope_5=0.0139, ratio=0.94x; mom_20=0.321

entity_b00579f203 (selected_winner with large_win): ma10_slope_5=0.0531, ma20_slope_5=0.0290, ratio=1.83x (high ratio yet selected_winner)
Pullback metrics (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) are unavailable at snapshot time and thus cannot be causal—only post-hoc labels
mom_20 alone shows overlap: false_positive_ruin range [0.067, 0.251] vs selected_winner range [-0.008, 0.320]—no clean threshold exists
vol_ratio_5_20 does not cleanly separate: entity_84824e6a20 (ruin) has 1.625 but entity_3adc078f01 (winner) has 1.140
falsifiable_predictions: P1: In a held-out test set of B0 picks, filtering out entries where ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5 > 2.0 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4 will reduce ruin rate by >40% relative to unfiltered B0 picks, while retaining >50% of winners

P2: The slope ratio proxy (ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5) will have zero marginal predictive power after conditioning on ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct quartile within the same snapshot, demonstrating it is a correlated proxy, not a causal feature

P3: Within a single snapshot (snap_*) cohort, false_positive_ruin entities will have systematically higher ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (closer to trigger) than selected_winner entities, because late-stage breakouts (high proximity to trigger) are more likely to reverse under sector rotation

P4: If industry concentration is the true causal amplifier, then replicating the same B0 signal logic across deciles of sector-ETF momentum (e.g., XLE vs XLK positioning) will show ruin concentrated in high-concentration snapshot periods where the sector is rotating out
policy_implications: Do NOT use ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 ratio as a hard filter—it is a proxy for industry rotation risk, not the risk itself. Over-filtering will remove true winners in sectors that are still accelerating

If causal mechanism is industry concentration amplification, then the B0 signal should be conditioned on sector momentum state: same signal near peak sector momentum is ruin-prone; same signal at sector momentum trough is winner-prone

Separate signal quality (true signal vs correlated proxy) from position sizing: ruin occurs when a 'good signal' is oversized under concentration. A proxy-identified risky pick could remain in the portfolio at reduced weight rather than eliminated

The ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct feature is available at snapshot time and shows promise as a cleaner predictor (winners tend to enter earlier: median ~0.030 vs ruin tends to enter late: ~0.069)—investigate this before slope ratio proxies

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 ratio is a confounded proxy for ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (entry proximity to trigger), and the apparent ruin-signal is entirely attributable to late-stage breakout mechanics rather than momentum velocity plateau. In the evidence, every false_positive_ruin case with a high slope ratio (entity_8f0df3d38e at 0.069, entity_84824e6a20 at 0.074, entity_ccc90a671f at 0.070) also has ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct in the upper quartile (>0.065). Conversely, selected_winners with low slope ratios (entity_ead73f4390 at 0.0017, entity_2f86543bf6 at 0.025) have early entries. The slope ratio is epiphenomenal—late breakouts mechanically produce steeper short-term slopes because price is converging on the trigger level from a consolidation, not because momentum is 'unsustainable'.

attacks.issue: Slope ratio confounds with entry timing (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct)
attacks.why_it_matters: A late-stage breakout that snaps toward the trigger level will mechanically produce ma10 > ma20 * k for any k>1, regardless of fundamental momentum quality. The ratio is a kinematic artifact of entry timing, not a discriminator of signal quality. The researcher notes the entry timing contrast (winners median 0.030 vs ruin 0.069) but then ignores this in favor of the slope ratio, which is backwards—the cleaner, more causal feature is being discarded in favor of its own derivative.

attacks.issue: N=27 is insufficient to support a threshold mechanism (2.0x, 2.5x)
attacks.why_it_matters: With 8 ruin and 11 winner cases, any threshold between 1.0x and 3.0x could be cherry-picked. The 'approximately 2.5x' cutoff is post-hoc pattern-matching. A bootstrapped confidence interval on this threshold would be extremely wide, likely spanning 1.5x to >4.0x, making the claim unfalsifiable in practice.

attacks.issue: Snapshot pooling introduces unobserved regime heterogeneity
attacks.why_it_matters: The data aggregates across 10+ different snapshots with no regime controls. Snapshots from different market conditions (e.g., snap_724342c280 vs snap_01d3e2483b) may have fundamentally different base rates of ruin. The slope ratio effect could be entirely confounded by snapshot-level market state—perhaps the ratio happens to be high in snapshots where concentration was elevated, but this cannot be distinguished from the individual-level predictors.

attacks.issue: The industry concentration mechanism is unfalsifiable with this data
attacks.why_it_matters: No sector-ETF momentum data, no concentration index, and no cross-snapshot sector attribution is present. The researcher's P4 prediction (sector-ETF conditioning) cannot be tested with the frozen evidence. Claiming industry concentration as the 'causal amplifier' while providing no evidence for concentration levels is unfalsifiable storytelling—exactly the kind of narrative that survives in small-sample archaeology.

attacks.issue: Pullback metrics are post-hoc outcomes used as if causal
attacks.why_it_matters: pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are observed after the snapshot, yet the researcher uses them to characterize ruin vs winner patterns. These are the outcomes being predicted, not predictors. Any pattern involving pullback (e.g., 'winners have deeper pullbacks') is tautological when comparing selected_winner to ruin labels that were partially constructed using pullback information.

attacks.issue: The vol_ratio_5_20 contrast is non-replicable across cases
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher proposes filtering on vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4, but entity_3adc078f01 (selected_winner, large_win) has vol_ratio = 1.14, below the threshold. Meanwhile, entity_bec51a4227 (selected_winner) has vol_ratio = 1.01. A filter on vol_ratio > 1.4 would eliminate true winners. The standardized delta for vol_ratio is only -1.0455, indicating weak separation at best.

counterexamples_to_seek: A selected_winner case with ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 > 3.0x AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.020 (to isolate slope ratio from entry timing)
A false_positive_ruin case with slope ratio < 1.2x (to test whether slope ratio adds anything beyond entry timing)
A within-snapshot comparison holding ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct constant: do slope ratios still separate ruin from winners?
A sector/market-regime breakdown of ruin vs winner base rates across snapshots to test whether snapshot-level heterogeneity explains the pattern
Replication data from a different time period or universe to test whether the 2.5x threshold holds or is sample-specific
what_would_change_my_mind: A held-out test set (not the 27-case discovery set) where conditioning on ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct quartile leaves significant residual variance explained by ma10/ma20 slope ratio for ruin prediction

Sector-ETF momentum data showing that the same B0 signal in high-concentration snapshots (e.g., XLE peak vs trough) has differential ruin rates, confirming the concentration amplifier hypothesis independently of slope metrics
Bootstrap confidence intervals on the slope ratio threshold showing the 2.0x cutoff is stable across resamples (e.g., <0.3x standard error on the threshold estimate)

A theoretical justification for why 'velocity plateau' (short-term acceleration decoupled from medium-term) mechanically causes ruin under concentration, as opposed to simply being a correlate of late breakout that would fail regardless of market regime

tests.name: entry_timing_vs_slope_ratio_orthogonality
tests.comparison: Within ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct quartile (terciles), test whether ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 ratio retains predictive power for false_positive_ruin vs selected_winner after conditioning out entry timing
tests.success_criterion: Slope ratio OR ma10_slope_5 residualized against ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct has conditional AUC > 0.65 for distinguishing ruin from winner within at least 2 of 3 entry-timing terciles
tests.failure_criterion: Slope ratio becomes non-significant (p > 0.15) after conditioning on entry timing quartile; 95% CI on slope ratio coefficient includes zero within each entry tercile—confirms the skeptic's confounding claim

tests.name: vol_ratio_independence_from_entry_timing
tests.comparison: Partial correlation test: does vol_ratio_5_20 predict ruin conditional on ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct and up_day_ratio_20? This separates whether vol_ratio captures genuine volatility regime vs late-breakout kinematics
tests.success_criterion: vol_ratio_5_20 partial correlation with ruin outcome remains significant (p < 0.10) after regressing out ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct and up_day_ratio_20; standardized partial effect > 0.3
tests.failure_criterion: vol_ratio_5_20 is fully explained by entry timing and up_day_ratio_20; partial correlation CI includes zero—vol_ratio is a derived proxy with no independent signal

tests.name: snapshot_regime_heterogeneity_test
tests.comparison: Test whether ruin base rate differs significantly across snapshots (Q-test for homogeneity). If snapshots are homogeneous, individual-level features are sufficient; if heterogeneous, snapshot-level (regime) features are needed to avoid omitted-variable bias in mechanism claims
tests.success_criterion: Cochran Q-test rejects homogeneity of ruin proportion across snapshots (p < 0.05); within-snapshot ruin rates range from <10% to >40%; confirms regime heterogeneity that could confound individual-level feature claims
tests.failure_criterion: Snapshots are homogeneous in ruin base rate (Q-test p > 0.30); ruin vs winner separation is entirely explained by within-snapshot individual features, not regime effects

tests.name: genuine_momentum_vs_late_breakout_separation
tests.comparison: Cluster the 27 cases into 'genuine momentum' (high mom_20, high up_day_ratio_20, moderate entry timing) vs 'late breakout' (high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, high slope ratio, moderate mom_20). Test if outcome distribution differs across these clusters independently of the entry timing proxy
tests.success_criterion: Late-breakout cluster has ruin rate >60% and genuine-momentum cluster has ruin rate <20%; this separation holds even when comparing within similar entry-timing terciles, confirming a mechanism distinct from entry timing
tests.failure_criterion: Cluster assignment is redundant with entry timing; all genuine-momentum cases also have early entry timing, and all late-breakout cases have late entry timing—no separable mechanism exists

tests.name: skewed_up_day_ratio_as_independent_ruin_predictor
tests.comparison: Test whether up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50 (lower fraction of up days) predicts ruin after conditioning on mom_20 and ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct. This tests if 'choppiness within momentum' is a distinct signal from 'momentum magnitude' and 'entry timing'
tests.success_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50 has OR > 2.5 for ruin vs winner after adjusting for mom_20 quartile and entry timing tercile; confirms choppiness as independent negative signal
tests.failure_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 effect is fully explained by mom_20 and entry timing; low up_day_ratio_20 is merely a correlate of late-stage consolidation with no independent predictive value

leakage_checks: pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are post-hoc outcomes, not snapshot-time features—must be excluded from all predictive tests or treated as outcomes only
w4_return_bucket is the outcome being predicted; cannot be used as a feature in any test

ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 ratio is a derived feature; tests must verify it is not merely a linear transform of ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (correlation < 0.80 required to treat as candidate independent feature)

Snapshot-level aggregation must not use future information; tests requiring sector-ETF momentum or concentration indices cannot be executed with current frozen evidence and should be marked UNRESOLVED
Any threshold proposed (e.g., slope ratio > 2.0) must be pre-specified based on domain theory, not data-snooped from the 27-case sample; bootstrap validation required to confirm threshold stability

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The slope ratio (ma10_slope_5 / ma20_slope_5) is a weak, conditional predictor of ruin that is largely confounded with entry timing (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct). Evidence from the 27-case discovery set shows: (1) all false_positive_ruin cases with high slope ratio (>2.0x) also have ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct in the upper quartile (>0.065), while selected_winners with low slope ratios have early entries; (2) the numeric contrasts show up_day_ratio_20 (standardized delta -1.19) and vol_ratio_5_20 (delta -1.05) as stronger separators than slope metrics (delta ~-0.6); (3) entity_3adc078f01 (selected_winner, large_win) has ratio 0.87x and vol_ratio 1.14—below any proposed threshold—directly undercutting the mechanism. The velocity plateau mechanism is plausible in domain theory but not confirmed by this data. The industry concentration amplifier cannot be evaluated with current frozen evidence and is marked UNRESOLVED. The ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct feature is the dominant predictor; slope ratio adds marginal conditional value only.
falsifiers: A held-out replication where slope ratio retains ruin-predictive power after conditioning on ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct quartile within the same snapshot—current evidence does not establish this orthogonality

Bootstrap instability: with N=8 ruin and N=11 winners, the 2.0x threshold estimate has wide confidence bounds; resampling may shift the optimal threshold substantially, making the specific value a data-snooped artifact
Counterexample survivorship: entity_3adc078f01 is a selected_winner (large_win) with ratio 0.87x and vol_ratio 1.14, below all proposed thresholds—mechanism does not predict this case's success
Vol_ratio non-separation: entity_bec51a4227 (selected_winner) has vol_ratio 1.01 and entity_3adc078f01 (winner) has vol_ratio 1.14; a vol_ratio >1.4 filter would eliminate true winners
Snapshot heterogeneity confounding: ruin base rates may differ systematically across snapshots; if true, individual-level feature claims are confounded by unobserved regime effects

Industry concentration UNRESOLVED: no sector-ETF momentum or concentration index data exists to test the causal amplifier hypothesis—attributing ruin to concentration is currently unfalsifiable narrative
actionable_design_principles: Prioritize ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as the primary ruin risk feature; it is available at snapshot time, has cleaner separation (winners median ~0.030 vs ruin ~0.069), and is not a derived kinematic artifact

Treat ma10_slope_5/ma20_slope_5 ratio as a conditional secondary filter only: apply it AFTER stratifying on entry timing tercile, not as a standalone criterion—its orthogonal contribution is unconfirmed but plausible in domain theory
Use up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50 as an additional negative signal; standardized delta of -1.19 is the strongest feature separation, and it is available at snapshot time
Do not use vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4 as a hard filter; winners exist below this threshold (entity_bec51a4227 at 1.01, entity_3adc078f01 at 1.14)—consider it a soft risk indicator only
Incorporate snapshot-level regime indicators if available; snapshot pooling without regime controls risks omitted-variable bias in individual-level mechanism claims
Avoid pullback metrics (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) as predictive features—they are post-hoc outcomes, not snapshot-time information

If industry concentration is suspected as the causal amplifier, the correct policy response is position sizing reduction on high-entry-proximity picks rather than elimination, to preserve winner capture while limiting ruin exposure

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Two-stage entry filter: Stage 1 uses ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct ≤ 0.040 as a hard screen; Stage 2 applies slope ratio > 2.0 ONLY to cases already in the 0.040-0.080 entry band to catch residual late-breakout risk
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Separates the primary entry-timing signal from the secondary slope artifact; avoids eliminating early-entry winners (like entity_ead73f4390 at 0.0017) while filtering late-entry ruin cases
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Aligns with the finding that entry proximity is the dominant predictor while slope ratio adds conditional marginal value only in the ambiguous middle band

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Choppiness risk penalty: reduce position size by 30% for B0 picks with up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50, independent of entry timing, because low up-day fraction signals weak internal momentum coherence
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: up_day_ratio_20 has the highest standardized separation (delta -1.19) and is orthogonal to entry timing mechanics—targets a distinct signal dimension
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Captures the 'choppiness within momentum' signal that neither entry timing nor slope ratio directly measures; directly addresses the concern that low up_day_ratio cases are more ruin-prone

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Vol-regime conditioning on position size rather than inclusion/exclusion: assign smaller weights (≤50% of base) to B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.5, but retain them in the portfolio to preserve winner capture
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Treats high volatility as a sizing signal, not a binary filter; avoids eliminating winners like entity_bec51a4227 (vol_ratio 1.01) and entity_3adc078f01 (1.14) who coexist with high-vol ruin cases
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Acknowledges vol_ratio has weak separation power (winners span 0.96-1.77) and should modulate exposure, not determine inclusion

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot-stratified validation requirement: any proposed feature threshold (slope ratio > 2.0, vol_ratio > 1.4) must be tested for stability across individual snapshots before deployment, rejecting thresholds that flip direction in even one snapshot
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Directly addresses the unobserved regime heterogeneity attack; ensures the feature-outcome relationship is not an artifact of snapshot pooling

cycles.question: Study false-positive B0 picks that later ruin under industry concentration; propose a counterexample that would invalidate the pattern. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: B0 false positives that ruin exhibit a specific PIT-observable signature: moderate momentum (mom_20 0.024-0.242) paired with elevated recent volatility ratio (vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.2) and sub-maximum up_day_ratio_20 (0.4-0.65), indicating the stock is in a late-stage acceleration phase rather than fresh breakout momentum. This distinguishes them from selected winners (higher mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20 up_day_ratio_20) and false negatives (lower vol_ratio_5_20, lower mom_20).
evidence_for: false_positive_ruin cases (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c) show mom_20 in 0.17-0.24 range with vol_ratio_5_20 1.20-1.38 and up_day_ratio_20 0.6-0.65
selected_winner cases show higher mom_20 (mean ~0.20+) and higher vol_ratio_5_20 (mean ~1.45+), with up_day_ratio_20 often at extremes (0.7 or 0.35)
false_negative cases show distinctly lower vol_ratio_5_20 (median 1.179 vs 1.424 for winners) and lower mom_20 (median 0.058 vs 0.163 for winners)
numeric_contrasts confirm standardized_delta of -1.19 for up_day_ratio_20 and -1.05 for vol_ratio_5_20 comparing false_negatives to selected_winners, indicating false_positives occupy middle ground

pullback_pct contrast: false_positive_ruin shows pullback_pct median around -14 to -16% while selected_winners show deeper pullbacks (median -15.9%), suggesting winners undergo mean-reversion correction while ruins continue deteriorating
evidence_against: entity_6618d3e80c has outcome_label 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' with high mom_20 (0.251), high vol_ratio_5_20 (1.446), and large_win w4_return_bucket, contradicting the simple ruin signature
entity_3adc078f01 shows selected_winner with up_day_ratio_20=0.65, vol_ratio_5_20=1.14, mom_20=0.172 - nearly identical to ruin cases but turned into large_win
entity_b6bcccdf6a ruin case has low up_day_ratio_20 (0.4) but vol_ratio_5_20 only 1.31, overlapping with winner range
The pattern may not hold under industry concentration effects not captured by individual stock features
falsifiable_predictions: A B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.7 AND vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.6 AND mom_20 >= 0.25 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.03 should NOT produce false_positive_ruin under concentrated industry conditions (predicted P(ruin) < 5%)
If a concentrated-industry B0 pick with px_vs_ma20 > 0.10 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.5 still ruins within 7 weeks, the late-acceleration mechanism is invalidated
A ruin case where up_day_ratio_20 drops below 0.4 within 3 weeks post-entry, contradicting the moderate-up_day_ratio_20 signature, would invalidate the temporal stability assumption
If selected_winners and false_positive_ruin cases become indistinguishable on (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20) triple within a future sample of n>=20 per category, the signature is noise
policy_implications: Add pre-entry filter: reject B0 candidates where up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.65 AND vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.2 AND mom_20 between 0.02-0.25, pending concentration adjustment
For concentrated positions, require up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.7 OR vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.6 to distinguish from false-positive late-acceleration signature
If industry concentration is high (not directly in PIT evidence), tighten exit: reduce holding period by 2 weeks for candidates with vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.3 and mom_20 < 0.20
The pullback_duration_weeks null pattern for ruin cases (5 of 8 have null) suggests ruins may not experience classic pullback correction - use this as secondary confirmation

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The 'false-positive ruin signature' is a post-hoc artifact of outcome conditioning rather than a causal mechanism. The three signature features (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20) are collinear measures of the same phenomenon—recent price acceleration—extracted from identical lookback windows. When you condition on future ruin labels to define the signature, you necessarily create features that appear discriminative in-sample but lack structural validity. The mechanism claim of 'late-stage acceleration' is a narrative fitted to correlated noise, not an independent causal channel.

attacks.issue: Outcome-conditioned feature construction
attacks.why_it_matters: The ruin/selected_winner labels are assigned based on W4 returns. Computing features from the same snapshot period and then claiming those features 'predict' the label creates a tautological loop. The features are not exogenous predictors—they are derived from the same price history that generated the outcome. Any observed discrimination is sampling variance around this mechanical relationship, not a generalizable signal.

attacks.issue: Collinear feature bundle
attacks.why_it_matters: mom_20 (20-day return), vol_ratio_5_20 (5-day vs 20-day volatility), and up_day_ratio_20 (% up days) all capture variations of recent price trend and dispersion. When three correlated features are jointly used to define a signature, the apparent specificity is inflated by overfitting. entity_3adc078f01 is a selected_winner with up_day_ratio_20=0.65, vol_ratio_5_20=1.14, mom_20=0.172—firmly inside the claimed ruin range yet produced a large_win outcome.

attacks.issue: Null-valued pullback fields are non-random
attacks.why_it_matters: 5 of 8 false_positive_ruin cases have null pullback_duration_weeks versus 6 of 11 selected_winners. This differential missingness suggests ruin cases may have been assigned before a pullback could occur (immediate collapse), or the pullback tracking logic was terminated upon ruin detection. The researcher uses this as 'secondary confirmation' but it reflects outcome-dependent data availability, not an independent filter.

attacks.issue: No adjustment for industry concentration
attacks.why_it_matters: The question explicitly frames this as 'under industry concentration,' yet no snapshot feature encodes industry concentration, sector beta, or peer-group correlation. If concentration risk drives ruin (e.g., sector rotation triggers cascading stops), the individual stock features are proxies for sector exposure rather than stock-specific signals. The signature may be capturing concentration beta, not late-stage acceleration.

attacks.issue: Sample heterogeneity within snapshots
attacks.why_it_matters: Cases span 15 distinct snapshot_anon values across different market regimes. The 'ruin signature' extracted from snap_724342c280 may not generalize to snap_ad495b6705 or snap_d0d57b1e40. With only 8 ruin cases distributed across 15 snapshots, there is insufficient nesting to distinguish snapshot-specific noise from a stable signature.

attacks.issue: Pullback depth reversal contradicts mechanism
attacks.why_it_matters: The numeric_contrasts show pullback_pct median of -7.3 for false_negatives versus -15.9 for selected_winners (standardized_delta +0.64). This indicates winners experience deeper pullbacks. If ruin cases represent 'late-stage acceleration,' they should show shallower or absent pullbacks—which they do. But this makes the pullback nulls and the pullback_pct contrast indistinguishable from 'no correction opportunity due to immediate collapse.' The mechanism is unfalsifiable with current data.

counterexamples_to_seek: A B0 pick with mom_20 0.15-0.25, vol_ratio_5_20 1.2-1.4, up_day_ratio_20 0.5-0.65 that shows selected_winner or false_negative_big_winner outcome AND has industry_concentration_high = True at snapshot time—this would show concentration alone does not explain ruin
A ruin case where vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.1 AND mom_20 < 0.10, showing low-volatility, low-momentum stocks can also ruin—invalidating the acceleration-based signature

A selected_winner with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.7 AND vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.5 AND mom_20 >= 0.25 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.03 that STILL ruins within 4 weeks—direct contradiction of falsifiable prediction
A snapshot where B0 picks with signature features perform comparably to non-signature picks on a forward basis, demonstrating the signature has zero incremental predictive power beyond base rate
Cross-snapshot replication: if the ruin signature is applied to snapshots not in the discovery set, the discrimination must hold with n>=20 per category to avoid small-sample artifact
what_would_change_my_mind: Replication on a held-out snapshot set where ruin cases (n>=15) are correctly classified at >70% precision using only snapshot-time features, with industry concentration explicitly controlled or randomized

Demonstration that the signature features cause ruin via a proposed mechanism (e.g., late-stage acceleration predicts lower subsequent earnings surprise, or higher future volatility that triggers stop-losses), where the mechanism variable is measured independently of the outcome
A temporal stability test: applying the signature cutoffs derived from snap_X to predict outcomes from snap_Y with comparable accuracy—currently the signature is entirely in-sample

Experimental evidence that filtering on the signature improves out-of-sample Sharpe or win-rate in a portfolio construction that holds multiple B0 picks simultaneously, rather than single-stock case studies

tests.name: cross_snapshot_temporal_stability
tests.comparison: Apply researcher-derived signature cutoffs (up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.65 AND vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.2 AND mom_20 0.02-0.25) to snapshots not used in signature derivation, compute ruin rate differential
tests.success_criterion: Signature-defined subset shows P(ruin) >= 2x baseline P(ruin) in holdout snapshots with n >= 5 ruin cases per snapshot
tests.failure_criterion: No significant ruin rate differential in holdout snapshots, OR signature holds only in discovery snapshots

tests.name: collinearity_decomposition
tests.comparison: Test each feature individually and pairwise for ruin discrimination; compare joint 3-way interaction vs best single feature
tests.success_criterion: A single feature achieves >= 80% of the ruin discrimination power of the 3-feature bundle (i.e., bundle is not multiplicatively more predictive)
tests.failure_criterion: Joint signature achieves >95% of ruin discrimination that no individual feature reaches; confirms bundle inflation rather than genuine signal

tests.name: null_pullback_mechanism_test
tests.comparison: Ruin cases with null pullback vs non-null pullback: test whether nulls show faster pre-entry price acceleration or lower volatility that would mechanically prevent pullback observation
tests.success_criterion: Null pullback cases have (a) higher vol_ratio_5_20 AND shorter base_duration_weeks OR (b) lower mom_20 in the 5 days pre-entry, explaining null as mechanical rather than outcome-dependent
tests.failure_criterion: Null and non-null ruin cases are indistinguishable on snapshot-time features; nulls reflect outcome-dependent tracking termination, not a distinct mechanism

tests.name: falsifiable_prediction_replication
tests.comparison: Search for entity_3adc078f01 analog: B0 pick with up_day_ratio_20 < 0.7 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.5 AND mom_20 < 0.20 that produces selected_winner outcome; test whether this pattern recurs in holdout snapshots
tests.success_criterion: In holdout data, >= 30% of B0 picks matching the signature (up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.65, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.2, mom_20 0.02-0.25) produce selected_winner or false_negative outcomes
tests.failure_criterion: Signature holds with < 15% exception rate across all snapshots, validating the mechanism claim

tests.name: base_rate_incremental_value
tests.comparison: Compare P(ruin) for signature B0 picks vs non-signature B0 picks vs non-B0 picks within same snapshots
tests.success_criterion: Signature B0 picks have P(ruin) that is statistically distinguishable (p < 0.05) from both non-signature B0 and non-B0 subsets
tests.failure_criterion: P(ruin) is indistinguishable across all three subsets; signature adds no incremental predictive value beyond B0 selection itself

tests.name: low_vol_ruin_counterexample
tests.comparison: Search for ruin cases with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.1 AND mom_20 < 0.10; test whether these cases share a different mechanism (e.g., high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct indicating late-stage consolidation)
tests.success_criterion: Low-vol ruin cases (n >= 3) exist and show high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (> 0.04) and lower px_vs_ma20, indicating a distinct 'failed breakout' mechanism separate from acceleration-based ruin
tests.failure_criterion: All ruin cases have vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.1 OR mom_20 >= 0.10; acceleration signature captures the full ruin population

leakage_checks: Ensure snapshot_anon is used only for train/test splitting, never as a feature
Verify w4_return_bucket and outcome_label are never used as inputs to feature computation; they are terminal outcomes only
Confirm pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct are not used to predict themselves (no autogenic leakage)
Check that ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is computed from pre-entry data only, not post-entry price action
Validate that the 3-feature limit per test is enforced; no feature bundles larger than 3 are evaluated
