synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The 'late-stage acceleration' signature (mom_20 0.02-0.25, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.2, up_day_ratio_20 0.4-0.65) captures a statistical association in discovery data but lacks structural validity. Three correlated features measuring the same phenomenon (recent price trend) were extracted from the same snapshot window used to define ruin outcomes, creating outcome-conditioned feature construction. Entity_3adc078f01 (selected_winner with up_day_ratio_20=0.65, vol_ratio_5_20=1.14, mom_20=0.172—firmly inside the claimed ruin range) directly contradicts the mechanism. Industry concentration, the explicit conditioning variable in the research question, is unmeasured. The apparent discrimination may reflect concentration beta, snapshot-specific noise, or overfitting to correlated features rather than a distinct causal channel.
falsifiers: Find >= 3 B0 picks in holdout snapshots with mom_20 0.15-0.25, vol_ratio_5_20 1.2-1.4, up_day_ratio_20 0.5-0.65 producing selected_winner outcomes—this invalidates the signature's specificity
Identify ruin cases with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.1 AND mom_20 < 0.10—demonstrates low-volatility, low-momentum stocks can also ruin, invalidating acceleration-only mechanism

Cross-snapshot replication: applying signature cutoffs from discovery snapshots to predict outcomes in snapshots with n >= 20 per category must achieve P(ruin) >= 2x baseline—currently entirely in-sample
If a single feature (mom_20 or vol_ratio_5_20 alone) achieves >= 80% of the discrimination of the 3-feature bundle, the signature is collinearity-inflated rather than genuinely multi-dimensional

Show that signature-defined subsets have statistically indistinguishable ruin rates from non-signature B0 subsets within the same snapshots—the signature adds no incremental value beyond B0 selection itself

Find a selected_winner with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.7 AND vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.5 AND mom_20 >= 0.25 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.03 that still ruins—this directly contradicts the researcher's falsifiable prediction

Demonstrate that null pullback cases have mechanically different pre-entry features (higher vol_ratio_5_20 OR shorter base_duration_weeks) versus non-null cases—if indistinguishable, nulls reflect outcome-dependent tracking termination
actionable_design_principles: Do not encode the signature as a causal filter until cross-snapshot replication demonstrates temporal stability with n >= 20 ruin cases in holdout
Test each signature feature individually before using the joint bundle—bundle inflation from collinearity can mimic specificity

Separate concentration risk from individual stock features: a stock with the ruin signature in a diversified portfolio may not ruin; the same stock under concentration may ruin due to correlated exit pressure
Treat pullback nulls as outcome-dependent censoring, not as independent confirmation signals
Prioritize tests that falsify the signature's boundary conditions: entity_3adc078f01 analog search and low-vol ruin counterexample are highest priority

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Dual-threshold confirmation filter: accept B0 pick only if (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.7 OR vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2 OR mom_20 > 0.25) to exclude the late-acceleration zone, pending holdout validation
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Differs from researcher's filter by using OR logic (at least one winner-indicator must be present) rather than AND exclusion, reducing false-negative rate while still avoiding the concentrated acceleration zone
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity 2/3: improves signal quality by rejecting outcome-conditioned signatures without requiring full mechanism validation

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Concentration-adjusted exit timer: for B0 picks with vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.3 AND mom_20 < 0.20, reduce maximum holding period by 2 weeks relative to baseline, triggered only when position represents > 15% of portfolio concentration
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Explicitly links the signature to the missing variable (concentration) rather than treating it as an unconditional filter; differs from researcher's concentration adjustment proposal by using position-weight trigger rather than assumed concentration state
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity 3/3: addresses the research question's explicit framing around concentration effects that the current evidence cannot disentangle

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Null-pullback exclusion flag: treat ruin cases with null pullback_duration_weeks as outcome-censored rather than structurally null; exclude from signature computation and use only as secondary confirmation of ruin label
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses skeptic's outcome-dependent missingness attack; researcher treats nulls as secondary confirmation but they reflect data availability bias
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity 1/3: data quality hygiene without requiring new features

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Single-feature triage before bundle: compute ruin P(ruin|vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.2) and P(ruin|mom_20 in 0.02-0.25) separately; only use joint bundle if single features achieve < 70% of bundle's discrimination
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Operationalizes the collinearity_decomposition test from experimental_designer before policy deployment; prevents overfitting from bundle inflation
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity 2/3: test design integrated into policy decision point

cycles.question: Study false-negative non-picks that become large winners under pullback versus breakout setup; identify repeated PIT-visible precursors. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-negative non-picks that become large winners are distinguished by a stealth momentum profile: low short‑term momentum (mom_20 ~0.05‑0.12), modest up‑day fraction (up_day_ratio_20 ≤0.55), subdued short‑term volume (vol_ratio_5_20 <1.30), price close to moving averages (px_vs_ma20 0.04‑0.08, px_vs_ma50 0.06‑0.13), a shallow pullback (‑5% ≥ pullback_pct ≥ ‑15%) lasting 4‑8 weeks, and a tight IBD entry trigger (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <0.025). When these conditions are met, the stock is likely to either consolidate through a pullback and then resume higher, or to break out without a recorded pullback, delivering a large win. The same profile observed in a breakout context (no pullback recorded) also predicts a large win, but the presence of a shallow pullback identifies the ‘pullback‑accumulation’ path.
evidence_for: False‑negative big‑winner entity_535a1beed7 (null pullback) has up_day_ratio_20 = 0.50, vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.174, mom_20 = 0.028, px_vs_ma20 = 0.032, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct = 0.009 – all below the selected‑winner medians yet it delivers a large win.

False‑negative big‑winner entity_de1c657364 (pullback 8 weeks, ‑7.3%) has up_day_ratio_20 = 0.65, vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.147, mom_20 = 0.058, px_vs_ma20 = 0.045, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct = 0.012 – consistent with the low‑momentum, low‑volume, shallow‑pullback profile.

False‑negative big‑winner entity_05b4c6b1f7 (null pullback) shows up_day_ratio_20 = 0.50, vol_ratio_5_20 = 0.964, mom_20 = 0.070, px_vs_ma20 = 0.052, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct = 0.024 – again matching the pattern.

The numeric contrasts show false‑negative medians for up_day_ratio_20 (0.50), vol_ratio_5_20 (1.179), mom_20 (0.058), px_vs_ma50 (0.056), pullback_pct (‑7.3) and ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (0.019) are systematically lower than selected‑winner medians, indicating the pattern is a common property of false‑negative large winners.
evidence_against: False‑negative entity_df5478102d (pullback ‑5%, 4 weeks) has up_day_ratio_20 = 0.60, vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.405, mom_20 = 0.125, yet its outcome is a small win, not a large win – suggesting that a higher vol_ratio (>1.3) can degrade the stealth‑momentum effect.

False‑negative entity_bfb308b24a (pullback ‑12.1%, 4 weeks) has up_day_ratio_20 = 0.45, vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.187, mom_20 = 0.027, but its outcome is a loss, indicating that very low momentum (mom_20 <0.03) combined with a deeper pullback may be insufficient for a large win.

Selected‑winner entity_3adc078f01 (pullback ‑42.3%, 9 weeks) has up_day_ratio_20 = 0.65, vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.140, mom_20 = 0.172, and is a large winner, but its pullback depth (‑42%) is far deeper than the shallow‑pullback range identified, implying that deep pullbacks can also produce large wins when other factors (e.g., stronger mom_20) dominate.
falsifiable_predictions: In a future validation set, false‑negative candidates with up_day_ratio_20 ≤0.55, vol_ratio_5_20 <1.30, mom_20 between 0.05 and 0.12, pullback_pct in [‑15%, ‑5%] (or null pullback), and ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <0.025 will become large‑win outcomes (W4 return bucket ≥large_win) in at least 60% of cases.
If a false‑negative candidate exhibits vol_ratio_5_20 ≥1.40 and mom_20 <0.05, the probability of a large win drops below 30% (i.e., it will more often be a small win or loss).

When the same low‑momentum, low‑volume profile appears but the stock has no recorded pullback, the large‑win hit rate will be comparable to the shallow‑pullback subgroup, confirming that the breakout path is equally viable.

Adjusting the B0 selection threshold to accept candidates with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <0.025 and up_day_ratio_20 ≤0.55 will increase the capture rate of false‑negative large winners by ≥15% without a proportional rise in false‑positive ruin, provided vol_ratio_5_20 stays below 1.30.
policy_implications: Introduce a secondary filter in the B0 pipeline that flags low‑momentum, low‑volume candidates with tight entry distances; these are currently missed but exhibit a distinguishable PIT‑visible signature for large‑win outcomes.

When backtesting, separate false‑negative outcomes into pullback‑accumulation vs. breakout sub‑regimes using pullback_duration_weeks (non‑null) to evaluate whether the predictive signal differs across the two paths.

Consider weighting the B0 score with a modest positive adjustment for stocks where up_day_ratio_20 <0.55 and vol_ratio_5_20 <1.30, while applying a negative adjustment for stocks with vol_ratio_5_20 >1.40, to reduce the false‑negative rate without inflating false‑positives.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The entire 'stealth momentum' mechanism is a sample-composition artifact: the 27 cases are drawn exclusively from observed non-picks that became winners, with no denominator from the full population of non-picks. Any feature profile that characterizes this biased subset is not a predictor—it is a post-hoc description of stocks that succeeded despite being ignored. The proposed thresholds (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30, mom_20 ~0.05-0.12) likely describe a large fraction of the entire non-pick universe, most of which do not become large winners.

attacks.issue: No non-pick failure denominator
attacks.why_it_matters: The 27 cases are drawn from the universe of observed non-picks that became winners (or mixed outcomes). There is no data on how many non-picks with up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55 and vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30 did NOT become large winners. The numeric contrasts compare false negatives to B0-selected winners, not to non-picks that failed. A predictor requires P(win | features, non-pick) >> P(win | non-pick baseline). This baseline is absent.

attacks.issue: Proxy variable conflation: low features describe ignored stocks, not winning stocks
attacks.why_it_matters: Low up_day_ratio_20, low vol_ratio_5_20, and tight ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct are not causal drivers—they are descriptors of stocks that are not yet in favor. The researcher infers that these features predict accumulation and subsequent breakout, but the data only shows they describe resting-phase stocks. Most resting-phase stocks do not subsequently break out large; the analysis cannot distinguish the subset that will.

attacks.issue: Snapshot temporality confusion
attacks.why_it_matters: The snapshot features (e.g., mom_20 = 0.058, vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.179) are measured at the non-pick decision point. The researcher treats these as leading indicators, but they may be contemporaneous descriptions of a base-building phase that has no directional implication. The stock's subsequent large win may be caused by post-snapshot accumulation, news, or sector rotation—not by the low-momentum profile visible at snapshot.

attacks.issue: NULL pullback is not equivalent to 'breakout path'
attacks.why_it_matters: Three of the five false_negative_big_winner cases (entity_535a1beed7, entity_05b4c6b1f7) have null pullback_duration_weeks and null pullback_pct. The researcher treats this as evidence of a 'no-pullback breakout path.' However, null pullback fields may indicate: (a) data not recorded, (b) the stock had not yet entered a pullback phase at snapshot, or (c) the stock did not pull back in the measured window. Conflating null with 'breakout path' doubles the apparent support for the mechanism with data that is operationally undefined.

attacks.issue: Retroactive threshold tuning on a discovery sample
attacks.why_it_matters: The proposed feature ranges (mom_20 0.05-0.12, pullback_pct -5% to -15%, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <0.025) are derived from the same 27-case discovery set used to generate predictions. There is no holdout validation. Any set of features can be tuned to appear discriminating on a small, outcome-biased sample. The 60% hit-rate prediction and the vol_ratio_5_20 ≥1.40 threshold are post-hoc constructions, not out-of-sample hypotheses.

attacks.issue: Feature profiles overlap with confirmed false positives
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_84824e6a20 (false_positive_ruin) has up_day_ratio_20 = 0.40, vol_ratio_5_20 = 1.625, mom_20 = 0.067, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct = 0.074. It violates the proposed thresholds on vol_ratio and IBD entry distance yet is a ruin outcome—not a large winner. This is not a rare outlier: several other false_positive_ruin cases have low up_day_ratio_20 (0.40-0.50) and low mom_20 (0.07-0.10), matching the 'stealth momentum' profile while producing catastrophic losses. The feature profile does not discriminate winners from ruin among non-picks.

attacks.issue: The is_b0_pick flag is endogenous to the features under study
attacks.why_it_matters: B0 selection likely already incorporates (or inversely correlates with) these same features: stocks with low momentum, low volume, and tight IBD entry distances are precisely the stocks B0 is designed to exclude. Treating false negatives as an 'unjustly missed' subgroup while using features that B0 explicitly deweights is circular: B0's rejection of these stocks is the mechanism that defines the false-negative category. The proposed policy change (lowering the B0 threshold) would partially undo B0's filtering, likely increasing false positives proportionally.

counterexamples_to_seek: A random sample of 100 non-picks with up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30, mom_20 between 0.05 and 0.12, and ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.025 that did NOT become large winners (small win, loss, or ruin)—to establish the baseline hit rate without selection bias.

Non-picks with identical 'stealth momentum' profiles at different snapshot dates for the same entity, where one snapshot produced a large win and another produced a loss—testing whether the features are stable predictors or incidental state descriptors.

A time-matched control set: for each false-negative big winner, find 3-5 non-picks from the same snapshot window with similar feature profiles that did not become large winners, to test whether the profile is necessary or merely coincidental.

Stocks that were non-picks due to is_b0_pick = false with high vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.60) and high mom_20 (>0.20) that became large winners—showing that the 'anti-stealth' profile can also produce false-negative big winners, undermining the specificity of the mechanism.
what_would_change_my_mind: A prospective validation study with a held-out set of non-picks from a time period after the discovery sample, showing that applying the stealth-momentum filter (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30, mom_20 in [0.05, 0.12], pullback_pct in [-15%, -5%] or null) selects a subgroup with ≥55% large-win rate, significantly above the baseline large-win rate for all non-picks.

Evidence that the low-momentum profile at snapshot is orthogonal to B0's selection criteria—that B0 is not already filtering on these features in a way that makes their reintroduction redundant or counterproductive.

A mechanistic story that is not purely descriptive: evidence that low up_day_ratio_20 reflects deliberate institutional accumulation (e.g., correlated with off-exchange volume, dark pool activity, or options positioning at snapshot), not merely low retail interest.
A demonstration that stocks with NULL pullback fields are operationally equivalent to breakout-path stocks (e.g., confirmed no-pullback base by independent chart review), rather than data artifacts.
Replication of the numeric contrasts on a second, independent set of false negatives identified by the same methodology, showing consistent median deltas across features.

tests.name: baseline_rate_test
tests.comparison: P(large_win) for all non-picks vs P(large_win) for non-picks meeting stealth profile thresholds
tests.success_criterion: Non-picks meeting stealth profile (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30 AND mom_20 ∈ [0.05, 0.12] AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.025) achieve large-win rate ≥ 2× the baseline non-pick large-win rate
tests.failure_criterion: Stealth-profile non-picks achieve large-win rate < 1.5× baseline, OR the profile captures >60% of all non-picks (floor effect)

tests.name: false_negative_discrimination_test
tests.comparison: Feature medians of false_negative_big_winner vs false_negative_relative vs false_positive_ruin
tests.success_criterion: At least 3 of the 6 features show significant rank-difference (p<0.10, two-sided) between false_negative_big_winner and false_positive_ruin outcomes
tests.failure_criterion: No feature achieves p<0.15 separation between false_negative_big_winner and false_positive_ruin; medians fall within overlapping quartiles

tests.name: null_pullback_mechanism_test
tests.comparison: Null pullback non-picks vs non-null pullback non-picks across feature distributions and outcome rates
tests.success_criterion: Null pullback cases have (a) comparable large-win rate to shallow-pullback cases after matching on other features, AND (b) feature distributions not systematically different from null-missing-data expectation (e.g., are not concentrated in a single snapshot)
tests.failure_criterion: Null pullback cases concentrate in ≤2 snapshots, OR null pullback large-win rate differs by >15pp from matched shallow-pullback cases, indicating NULL is a data artifact rather than a breakout-path indicator

tests.name: b0_orthogonality_test
tests.comparison: Correlation between is_b0_pick flag and stealth-profile features; whether B0 non-picks with stealth profile have same large-win rate as B0 picks with stealth profile
tests.success_criterion: Spearman correlation between is_b0_pick and each stealth feature < 0.30, AND stealth-profile B0 picks have comparable large-win rate to stealth-profile B0 non-picks
tests.failure_criterion: is_b0_pick correlates >0.50 with any stealth feature (B0 already filters these stocks), OR stealth-profile B0 picks significantly outperform stealth-profile B0 non-picks, indicating the profile is not orthogonal to B0

tests.name: pullback_depth_threshold_test
tests.comparison: Large-win rate across pullback_pct bins: (-5%, 0%), [-15%, -5%), < -15%, and null
tests.success_criterion: Large-win rate in [-15%, -5%] bin is ≥ 1.5× the rate in < -15% bin, validating shallow-pullback specificity
tests.failure_criterion: Large-win rate shows no monotonic trend with pullback depth; deep pullbacks (>-15%) produce comparable win rates to shallow pullbacks

tests.name: vol_ratio_threshold_test
tests.comparison: Conditional large-win rate: (vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30 AND mom_20 ∈ [0.05, 0.12]) vs (vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.40 AND mom_20 < 0.05)
tests.success_criterion: Low-vol/low-mom combo yields ≥40% large-win rate; high-vol/low-mom combo yields <25% large-win rate
tests.failure_criterion: Both combos yield similar large-win rates within 10pp, invalidating the vol_ratio threshold as a discriminator

tests.name: cross_snapshot_stability_test
tests.comparison: Stealth-profile feature distributions and outcomes across snapshots with ≥3 non-picks each
tests.success_criterion: At least 3 snapshots show consistent stealth-feature medians (within ±0.05 for mom_20, ±0.08 for up_day_ratio_20) and large-win rates (within 20pp), indicating the pattern is not snapshot-specific
tests.failure_criterion: Feature medians and win rates vary >2× across snapshots, indicating pattern is an artifact of snapshot composition rather than a stable signal

tests.name: ruin_overlap_test
tests.comparison: Mahalanobis distance of false_positive_ruin cases vs false_negative_big_winner cases from stealth-profile centroid
tests.success_criterion: Median Mahalanobis distance of false_positive_ruin from stealth centroid is >1.5× the distance of false_negative_big_winner, OR at least one feature distinguishes ruin from big-winner with AUC >0.70
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin and big-winner cases are equidistant from stealth centroid; no single feature achieves AUC >0.65 for distinguishing them, confirming the profile cannot separate winners from catastrophes

leakage_checks: Confirm that all features (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, pullback_pct, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50) are computed from data available at snapshot time; no forward-looking information embedded
Verify that w4_return_bucket and outcome_label are post-snapshot labels, not used as inputs to feature-based partitioning
Ensure that snapshot_anon is used only for stratification, not as a predictive feature
Confirm that is_b0_pick is contemporaneous with snapshot (pre-decision flag), not a post-hoc classification
Check that pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks nulls are not systematically caused by post-snapshot outcomes (e.g., ruin cases having higher null rates due to truncation)

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The 'stealth momentum' profile (low mom_20 ~0.05-0.12, up_day_ratio_20 ≤0.55, vol_ratio_5_20 <1.30, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <0.025, shallow pullback -5% to -15%) characterizes a non-trivial fraction of false-negative large winners in the discovery sample. However, this pattern is identified on a winner-biased sample (27 cases) with no failure denominator, no holdout validation, and uncertain orthogonality to B0's existing filters. The profile plausibly describes a resting-phase stock state that can transition to large wins, but the same profile appears in ruin outcomes (entity_84824e6a20: ruin with mom_20=0.067, up_day_ratio_20=0.40). The mechanism is plausible but unproven; it describes observed winners without establishing that the profile discriminates winners from non-winners in the full non-pick universe.
falsifiers: A stealth-profile non-pick subset (up_day_ratio_20 ≤0.55, vol_ratio_5_20 <1.30, mom_20 ∈ [0.05,0.12], ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <0.025) achieves large-win rate <2× the baseline non-pick large-win rate in a holdout period
Spearman correlation between is_b0_pick and any stealth feature exceeds 0.30, confirming B0 already filters these properties
False-negative big winners and false-positive ruin cases are equidistant from the stealth-profile centroid; no single feature achieves AUC >0.65 for distinguishing them
NULL pullback cases (entity_535a1beed7, entity_05b4c6b1f7) concentrate in ≤2 snapshots, indicating the null state is a data artifact rather than a distinct breakout path
Applying the stealth profile to a time-period after the discovery sample selects a subgroup with large-win rate not significantly different from baseline non-picks
actionable_design_principles: Do not implement stealth-momentum filtering as a B0 override without first establishing the baseline hit rate: sample ≥100 non-picks with the stealth profile that did NOT become large winners to compute the true conditional probability P(large_win | stealth_profile, non_pick)

Test B0 orthogonality before any policy change: if B0 already excludes these stocks because of their low-momentum/low-volume signature, reintroducing them as a secondary filter is circular and will dilute B0's precision

Distinguish NULL pullback from recorded pullback as separate data-generating processes, not interchangeable signals; NULL pullback requires independent validation (e.g., chart review or confirmed no-base status) before treating it as a 'breakout path' indicator

Run the ruin_overlap_test to quantify Mahalanobis distance: if false-positive ruin cases are not significantly farther from the stealth centroid than false-negative big winners, the profile cannot safely separate winners from catastrophes

Reserve any stealth-momentum signal as a surveillance flag in a secondary non-pick queue rather than modifying B0 selection directly; this preserves B0's false-positive discipline while enabling future signal evaluation

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: A non-pick surveillance queue that flags stealth-profile candidates (up_day_ratio_20 ≤0.55 AND vol_ratio_5_20 <1.30 AND mom_20 ∈ [0.05, 0.12] AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <0.025 AND pullback_pct ∈ [-15%, -5%] OR pullback_duration_weeks IS NULL) for post-snapshot monitoring, without modifying B0 selection criteria
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Operates as a parallel watchlist rather than a B0 override, preserving false-positive discipline while enabling prospective validation of the stealth pattern on held-out non-pick outcomes
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Enables a secondary signal pathway for non-picks that exhibit a repeatable PIT-visible signature without compromising B0's primary selection logic; requires prospective hit-rate tracking before capacity allocation

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: A B0 orthogonality audit layer that computes Spearman correlations between is_b0_pick and each stealth feature across all snapshots; flags any feature with |rho| >0.30 as B0-redundant and excludes it from any future non-pick filter design
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Prevents circular logic where B0's exclusion criteria are re-imported as non-pick rescue criteria; ensures any new signal is additive to, not redundant with, B0's existing filters
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Quality-control checkpoint for signal development pipeline; prevents wasted capacity on signals already embedded in B0's selection logic

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: A stratified failure-denominator sampling protocol that, for each stealth-profile false-negative big winner identified, randomly selects 3-5 time-matched non-picks from the same snapshot window with similar feature profiles that did NOT become large winners, to compute the true hit rate conditional on the profile
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses the critical gap (no failure denominator) by constructing a time-matched control set; this is the minimal evidence required before any stealth-momentum signal can be used for portfolio construction
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Essential calibration step for capacity sizing; without the true hit rate, position sizing and risk limits cannot be responsibly set for any stealth-profile non-pick allocation

cycles.question: Study false-negative non-picks that become large winners under pullback versus breakout setup; separate true signal from correlated proxy. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-negative non-picks that become large winners are distinguished by extended pullback duration (≥8 weeks) combined with elevated short-term volatility (vol_ratio_5_20 >1.4), indicating mean-reversion within a volatile consolidation rather than momentum continuation. The B0 selection signal proxies momentum via up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20, creating a correlated proxy that filters out stocks with high volatility but insufficient directional momentum—these represent a mechanistically distinct subset where shakeout volatility creates entry opportunity.
evidence_for: entity_de1c657364 (false_negative_big_winner): pullback_duration_weeks=8, vol_ratio_5_20=1.15, mom_20=0.058 → large_win outcome despite shallow pullback and weak momentum
entity_535a1beed7 (false_negative_big_winner): vol_ratio_5_20=1.17, mom_20=0.028 → large_win outcome with lowest momentum in dataset
Numeric contrasts show false_negative_median vol_ratio_5_20=1.18 vs selected_winner_median=1.42 (delta=-0.24), confirming non-picks have measurable volatility but lack momentum confirmation

False negatives have longer pullback_duration_weeks median (4.0) vs losing false negatives at similar or shorter duration, suggesting duration distinguishes winners from losers within the false-negative cohort
Selected winners with negative mom_20 (entity_2f86543bf6: mom_20=-0.008) still produce large_win, demonstrating momentum is not necessary for large winners—supporting the proxy hypothesis
evidence_against: entity_2c58cebc59: pullback_pct=-25.1% over 6 weeks with vol_ratio=1.62 and mom_20=0.32 → selected_winner, not false_negative, contradicting the 'missed high-volatility' hypothesis
entity_3adc078f01: pullback_pct=-42.3% over 9 weeks, vol_ratio=1.14, yet is_b0_pick=true → extreme pullback does not prevent selection, challenging the mechanism that pullbacks cause non-selection
entity_bfb308b24a: pullback_duration_weeks=4, pullback_pct=-12.1% → w4_return_bucket=loss within false_negative_relative, indicating pullback duration alone is insufficient predictor
falsifiable_predictions: Non-picks with vol_ratio_5_20 >1.4, pullback_duration_weeks ≥7, and px_vs_ma50 <0.10 will generate ≥8% W4 returns at rate ≥50% higher than non-picks matching momentum proxies (mom_20 >0.15, up_day_ratio_20 >0.6)
Within is_b0_pick=false cohort, the subset with vol_ratio_5_20 in 1.3–1.6 range and ma10_slope_5 <0.015 will outperform those with ma10_slope_5 >0.025 by ≥5pp in W4 returns
Shallow pullbacks (pullback_pct >-8%) in false-negative cohort will show zero correlation between pullback_pct and W4 return, confirming the mechanism is duration-driven not magnitude-driven

Breaking the vol_ratio_5_20 proxy into short-term (5-day) vs medium-term (20-day) components will reveal false-negative winners have elevated 5-day ratio but suppressed 20-day ratio, indicating transient volatility
policy_implications: Introduce secondary signal layer: non-picks passing vol_ratio_5_20 >1.3 threshold and pullback_duration_weeks ≥6 should be flagged as 'volatile consolidation' candidates, regardless of momentum indicators

The up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20 proxy for momentum creates systematic exclusion of high-volatility mean-reversion plays; consider separating signal generation into momentum-track and volatility-track pipelines
Portfolio construction should treat false-negative winners as distinct risk regime (elevated vol_ratio, weaker trend) requiring different position sizing than selected_winner cohort
Avoid using pullback_pct magnitude as entry signal for false-negative candidates; duration-based entries (timed after ≥6 weeks of pullback) may outperform magnitude-based entries

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The proposed mechanism conflates vol_ratio_5_20 (a measure of short-term volatility expansion) with a spurious proxy for directional momentum. The numeric contrasts show FALSE NEGATIVE big winners actually have SHALLOWER pullbacks (median -7.3%) than selected winners (median -15.9%), contradicting the 'extended pullback duration creates shakeout' hypothesis. The false_negative_big_winner cases (entity_535a1beed7, entity_de1c657364) have vol_ratio_5_20 values of 1.17 and 1.15—BELOW the overall dataset median and substantially below selected_winner median of 1.42—meaning these are not high-volatility shakeouts at all.

attacks.issue: Proxy conflation: vol_ratio_5_20 is not measuring what mechanism claims
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher treats vol_ratio_5_20 >1.4 as indicative of 'transient volatility' or 'shakeout.' But vol_ratio_5_20 measures the ratio of 5-day to 20-day average volume. A ratio >1 indicates elevated short-term volume relative to recent norm, which could signal distribution (smart money selling) or accumulation, or simply news-driven noise. There is no mechanism connecting volume ratio to mean-reversion opportunity without directional confirmation. The false_negative_big_winner cases have vol_ratio_5_20 BELOW the feature's own dataset median, directly contradicting the hypothesis that elevated short-term volatility distinguishes them.

attacks.issue: Pullback magnitude paradox: false negatives have shallower pullbacks than selected winners
attacks.why_it_matters: The numeric contrast shows false_negative_median pullback_pct = -7.3% vs selected_winner_median = -15.9% (delta = +8.6pp). This is the OPPOSITE of what the 'extended pullback creates shakeout entry' mechanism predicts. Selected winners experience deeper pullbacks on average, meaning if pullback magnitude were the discriminating factor, selected stocks should be LESS likely to win. The researcher cannot claim pullbacks cause non-selection while simultaneously showing non-selected stocks had shallower pullbacks.

attacks.issue: Snapshot clustering creates temporal confound
attacks.why_it_matters: Five of seven false_negative_relative cases (entity_df5478102d, entity_d8e8e7b814, entity_535a1beed7, entity_bfb308b24a, entity_de1c657364, entity_2c58cebc59) originate from snap_71486ed83c. This snapshot-levl concentration means the false-negative profile may reflect market regime conditions at that specific time (e.g., sector rotation, index-level momentum) rather than stock-specific features. The 'volatility track' vs 'momentum track' separation policy assumes the non-selection is stock-specific, but if snapshot-level clustering drives outcomes, the entire mechanism claim is a temporal artifact.

attacks.issue: Selected winners with negative momentum still win
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_2f86543bf6 (selected_winner, large_win) has mom_20 = -0.008 and up_day_ratio_20 = 0.35—both BELOW false_negative_median values. This stock passed B0 selection despite having negative 20-day momentum and weak up-day ratio, yet became a large winner. This directly undermines the claim that B0 'proxies momentum via up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20.' If the proxy were truly filtering by these features, this stock would have been rejected. Its presence in selected_winner suggests B0 selection includes other features that override negative momentum, and that negative momentum is not a barrier to large_win.

attacks.issue: Pullback duration direction contradicts mechanism claim
attacks.why_it_matters: The numeric contrast shows false_negative_median pullback_duration_weeks = 4.0 vs selected_winner_median = 5.5 (delta = -1.5 weeks). False negatives have SHORTER pullback durations than selected winners. The researcher claims 'extended pullback duration (≥8 weeks) distinguishes false-negative winners,' but the actual median duration for the false-negative cohort is below the selected-winner median. The claim is based on cherry-picked extreme cases (entity_3adc078f01: 9 weeks, entity_de1c657364: 8 weeks) rather than the cohort's central tendency.

counterexamples_to_seek: Stocks with vol_ratio_5_20 >1.6 AND pullback_duration_weeks ≥8 that resulted in ruin or loss (should exist if mechanism is not universal)
Snapshots where is_b0_pick=false stocks with high mom_20 (e.g., >0.20) and high up_day_ratio_20 (>0.6) still produced loss outcomes
False-negative cases from snapshots OTHER than snap_71486ed83c to test temporal vs stock-specific mechanism
Stocks with deep pullbacks (pullback_pct <-20%) that were selected as B0 picks but resulted in ruin (to test if deep pullbacks cause false positives rather than false negatives)
what_would_change_my_mind: A controlled experiment showing that adding vol_ratio_5_20 >1.4 as a selection filter to out-of-sample snapshots increases hit-rate for large_win by >15pp relative to random non-selection, not merely correlating with in-sample outcomes
Evidence that the snapshot clustering effect (snap_71486ed83c concentration) is absent when controlling for market regime (e.g., by matching on VIX regime or index-level momentum)

A mechanistic story for vol_ratio_5_20 that does NOT reduce to 'high volume = accumulation = price rise' (a textbook gambler's fallacy applied to volume), and instead specifies the causal pathway from volume asymmetry to price recovery

Demonstration that pullback_pct sign/direction (i.e., whether stock is above or below prior MA levels) matters more than duration or magnitude, separating mean-reversion plays from continuation failures

Replication of the duration effect using a time-varying threshold (e.g., relative to each stock's own historical pullback duration distribution) rather than an absolute 8-week cutoff that may be confounded with sector or market cap characteristics

tests.name: snapshot_regime_test
tests.comparison: Compute within-snapshot false_negative_large_win_rate versus across-snapshot pooled rate. For each snapshot with ≥3 false-negative cases, compute snapshot-level false_negative_large_win_rate. Then compare variance across snapshots vs. binomial sampling variance.
tests.success_criterion: Within-snapshot variance in false_negative_large_win_rate explains ≥40% of total variance (ICC ≥ 0.40), confirming snapshot-level regime drives outcomes rather than stock-specific features
tests.failure_criterion: Snapshot explains <25% of outcome variance (ICC < 0.25), confirming stock-specific features drive outcomes independent of temporal confounds

tests.name: vol_ratio_directionality_test
tests.comparison: Split is_b0_pick=false cohort at vol_ratio_5_20=1.25 (dataset 25th percentile). Within each vol_ratio stratum, test whether mom_20 OR up_day_ratio_20 predicts large_win vs. loss/ruin using logistic regression. This separates vol_ratio's independent effect from momentum proxy correlation.
tests.success_criterion: Among vol_ratio_5_20 <1.25 (low vol), mom_20 > 0.12 increases large_win probability by ≥20pp vs. mom_20 < 0.05. Among vol_ratio_5_20 ≥1.25, no momentum threshold significantly improves large_win probability, confirming vol_ratio operates via different mechanism.
tests.failure_criterion: Mom_20 predicts large_win equally within both vol_ratio strata (no interaction effect), indicating vol_ratio is a correlated proxy for momentum rather than independent mechanism

tests.name: pullback_magnitude_vs_duration_test
tests.comparison: Within is_b0_pick=false cohort, compute Pearson correlation between pullback_pct and W4_return_bucket (ordinal: ruin=1, loss=2, small_win=3, large_win=4). Then compute same for pullback_duration_weeks vs. W4_return_bucket. Compare absolute correlation coefficients.
tests.success_criterion: Pullback_duration_weeks correlation with outcome ordinal is ≥1.5x the magnitude of pullback_pct correlation, confirming duration is the operative mechanism over magnitude
tests.failure_criterion: Pullback_pct correlation with outcome is equal or greater magnitude than pullback_duration_weeks correlation, contradicting the duration-based mechanism

tests.name: negative_momentum_selected_winner_test
tests.comparison: Examine is_b0_pick=true cases where mom_20 < 0.05 AND up_day_ratio_20 < 0.45. Compute their large_win rate vs. is_b0_pick=true cases with mom_20 > 0.10 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.55. If researcher mechanism is correct, the low-momentum selected cases should be rare or produce poor outcomes.
tests.success_criterion: Selected winners with negative/low momentum (mom_20 < 0.05, up_day_ratio_20 < 0.45) have large_win rate ≤15%, confirming B0 selection does not bypass momentum proxy filtering
tests.failure_criterion: Selected winners with negative/low momentum have large_win rate >30%, demonstrating B0 selection includes non-momentum signals that override mom_20/up_day_ratio_20

tests.name: pullback_depth_within_false_negative_winners_test
tests.comparison: Within is_b0_pick=false large_win cases, compare pullback_pct distributions for vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.20 vs. vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.20. Researcher's mechanism predicts low-vol winners should have shallower pullbacks; skeptic predicts the opposite or no pattern.
tests.success_criterion: False-negative large_win cases with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.20 have median pullback_pct > -8%, confirming the shallow-pullback-with-low-volatility pattern predicted by skeptic
tests.failure_criterion: False-negative large_win cases show no systematic relationship between vol_ratio and pullback_pct, indicating both features operate independently

tests.name: proxy_collapse_test
tests.comparison: Perform principal component analysis on mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5 within is_b0_pick=false cohort. Identify whether PC1 explains ≥70% of variance (proxy collapse) or requires ≥3 components (distinct signals). Then test whether PC1 alone predicts large_win vs. higher-order PCs adding predictive power.
tests.success_criterion: PC1 explains ≥70% of momentum-feature variance AND PC1 alone predicts large_win with AUC ≥ 0.65, while adding PC2/PC3 does not improve AUC by >0.05, confirming mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 are a single proxy rather than independent signals
tests.failure_criterion: Requires ≥3 components to explain ≥80% of variance, OR higher-order PCs improve AUC by >0.08 over PC1 alone, indicating these are distinct signals with different predictive content

leakage_checks: No feature in any test uses information unavailable at snapshot time (all features are trailing or contemporaneous)
Snapshot identity is used only as a grouping variable for regime testing, never as a predictive feature
Outcome labels (large_win, ruin) are computed from future W4 returns and cannot be used as input features
is_b0_pick is a contemporaneous signal, not a forward prediction, so using it to stratify cohorts is valid
pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are computed from price history before snapshot, not from post-snapshot price action

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The proposed mechanism—false-negative large winners distinguished by extended pullback duration (≥8 weeks) combined with elevated vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.4) indicating shakeout volatility—is directly contradicted by the dataset's central tendencies. False-negative big winners (entity_535a1beed7, vol_ratio=1.17; entity_de1c657364, vol_ratio=1.15) have BELOW-median volatility ratios, shallower pullbacks (-7.3% vs selected_winner -15.9%), and only 2 of 27 cases meet the ≥8-week duration threshold. The core claim conflates volume ratio with directional accumulation without specifying causal pathway. The B0 selection proxy claim is undermined by entity_2f86543bf6 (selected_winner with mom_20=-0.008, up_day_ratio=0.35—below false_negative_median values). Snapshot-level clustering (5 of 7 false_negative_relative cases from snap_71486ed83c) introduces temporal confound that the researcher does not address.
falsifiers: Any false_negative_big_winner with vol_ratio_5_20 >1.5 would support the shakeout hypothesis; none observed (FN big winner max vol_ratio = 1.17)
If pullback_duration_weeks ≥8 predicts large_win within FN cohort, the FN median duration should exceed SW median; observed FN median = 4.0 vs SW median = 5.5 (opposite direction)
If up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20 constitute a correlated proxy filtering FN cohort, then B0 selection should never admit negative-momentum winners; entity_2f86543bf6 (mom_20=-0.008) violates this

If snap_71486ed83c concentration is regime artifact, then non-picks from other snapshots with high mom_20/high up_day_ratio should produce similar false_negative profiles; current data cannot test this but the skew is noted
The researcher claims vol_ratio measures 'transient volatility' but provides no mechanistic pathway from 5-day/20-day volume ratio to mean-reversion opportunity independent of price momentum
actionable_design_principles: Do not use vol_ratio_5_20 >1.4 as a standalone entry signal for non-pick re-entry; FN big winners have below-median vol_ratio values
Pullback duration is NOT a reliable discriminator between FN winners and losers; the FN cohort has SHORTER median duration than selected winners
Pullback magnitude is inversely related to outcome—deeper pullbacks correlate with selected_winner outcomes, not false-negative outcomes; avoid magnitude-based entry signals
The up_day_ratio_20/mom_20 proxy hypothesis for B0 selection is unproven; entity_2f86543bf6 demonstrates B0 admits negative-momentum stocks
Snapshot-level temporal clustering must be controlled before attributing FN patterns to stock-specific features
Any 'volatility track' pipeline separated from 'momentum track' must define vol_ratio mechanism explicitly (direction, magnitude, timing) without circular reasoning from outcomes

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Post-hoc regime filter: require that FN re-entry candidates originate from ≥2 distinct snapshots to mitigate temporal confound
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Current FN cohort is heavily clustered in snap_71486ed83c; if regime drives outcomes rather than stock features, uniform application of FN screening to a single-snapshot cohort produces false confidence
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents overfitting to snapshot-specific conditions; requires cross-regime validation before deployment

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Invert the pullback hypothesis: test whether deep pullbacks (pullback_pct < -15%) in is_b0_pick=false cohort predict large_win at higher rate than shallow pullbacks, reversing the researcher's direction
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Numeric contrast shows selected winners have deeper pullbacks; if this pattern holds for non-picks, the mechanism is 'consolidation depth signals base quality' rather than 'shakeout creates opportunity'
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Clarifies whether depth is a positive signal (base-building) or negative signal (distribution) across both cohorts

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Proxy decomposition test: within is_b0_pick=false cohort, test whether vol_ratio_5_20 × mom_20 interaction predicts large_win better than either alone
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The skeptic's strongest attack is that vol_ratio is not measuring shakeout but some correlated-but-distinct phenomenon; interaction testing reveals whether vol_ratio adds signal only when momentum is present
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Distinguishes vol_ratio as independent mechanism vs. correlated proxy for momentum regime

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Duration-relative threshold: replace absolute 8-week cutoff with stock-specific duration relative to its own historical pullback distribution (e.g., ≥75th percentile of that stock's pullback durations)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: An absolute cutoff may conflate market conditions (sector rotation speed) with stock-specific behavior; relative threshold controls for this confound
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: More robust across market regimes; requires historical data per entity but avoids cross-sectional confounds

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: B0 override detection: identify which non-momentum features in B0 selection override negative mom_20/up_day_ratio (e.g., entity_2f86543bf6 case) and test whether these overrides correlate with FN outcomes
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The researcher claims B0 proxies momentum, but entity_2f86543bf6 shows B0 admits negative-momentum stocks; understanding what overrides this proxy clarifies the actual selection mechanism
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents false assumption that B0 selection equals momentum confirmation; informs when non-pick re-entry is or is not justified

cycles.question: Study false-negative non-picks that become large winners under pullback versus breakout setup; propose a counterexample that would invalidate the pattern. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-negative non-picks that become large winners exhibit a specific combination: moderate pullback depth (-5% to -8%) with extended duration (≥4 weeks), low up_day_ratio_20 (0.45-0.50), and nascent momentum recovery (mom_20 ≈ 0.06-0.07). The B0 selector misses these because they fail the breakout-trigger proximity threshold (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.02) while in pullback consolidation, yet they contain enough embedded strength to resume. In contrast, selected_winner breakout setups have tighter trigger proximity and stronger pre-snapshot momentum, making them easier to catch.
evidence_for: entity_de1c657364 (false_negative_big_winner): 8-week pullback of -7.3%, up_day_ratio_20=0.65, mom_20=0.058, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.012 — qualifies as embedded strength during pullback, missed by B0 due to low trigger proximity
entity_535a1beed7 (false_negative_big_winner): up_day_ratio_20=0.50, mom_20=0.028, vol_ratio_5_20=1.174 — low momentum but large_win outcome, indicating pullback-consolidation base building

entity_05b4c6b1f7 (false_negative_relative, large_win): up_day_ratio_20=0.50, mom_20=0.070, vol_ratio_5_20=0.964 — non-breakout profile yet produces large win, suggesting recovery from extended consolidation

Selected winners with pullbacks (entity_3adc078f01, entity_2c58cebc59) show steeper pullback_pct (-25% to -42%) and higher mom_20 (0.171-0.321), confirming the 'missed in deeper pullback' sub-pattern for selected winners

Numeric contrasts confirm false negatives cluster toward lower up_day_ratio_20 (median 0.50 vs 0.625 for selected_winner), lower mom_20 (median 0.058 vs 0.163), and shallower pullback_pct (median -7.3% vs -15.9%)
evidence_against: entity_bfb308b24a (false_negative_relative, loss): has pullback_duration_weeks=4, pullback_pct=-12.1%, up_day_ratio_20=0.45 — similar pullback profile to big-winner false negatives but produces loss, suggesting the pattern alone is insufficient

entity_df5478102d (false_negative_relative, small_win): pullback_pct=-5.0% with 4-week duration but yields only small_win, indicating same pullback characteristics can produce different magnitude outcomes

entity_ad2bfdee3f (false_negative_relative): mom_20=-0.046, px_vs_ma20=0.007, px_vs_ma50=-0.033 — negative momentum with price below MA50, yet only small_win, confirming momentum sign matters for outcome magnitude

False negatives with null pullback data (entity_535a1beed7, entity_d8e8e7b814) complicate the pullback-depth mechanism — some large-win false negatives have no recorded pullback, suggesting alternative paths to embedded strength

Selected winners without pullbacks (entity_28a6ec4601, entity_90a828939a) achieve large_win with moderate momentum and typical trigger proximity, indicating the mechanism does not explain all large-win outcomes
falsifiable_predictions: If a non-pick has up_day_ratio_20 < 0.45, mom_20 < 0.05, and no observable pullback (or pullback_pct > -5%), then it should NOT produce a large_win outcome within 4 weeks

If a non-pick exhibits pullback_pct between -5% and -8% with pullback_duration_weeks ≥ 4, up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.50, and mom_20 ≥ 0.055, then it should produce a W4 return ≥ selected_winner median (prediction conditional on PIT observability of these features)

If ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.03 for a non-pick, the B0 selector should capture it; absence of capture implies other features suppress the pick signal (testable by checking if is_b0_pick=true for all entities with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.03)

Counterexample to invalidate: find a non-pick with up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.55, mom_20 ≥ 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.40, pullback_pct between -5% and -10%, pullback_duration_weeks ≥ 4, that produces a w4_return_bucket of 'loss' or 'ruin' — this would falsify the embedded-strength mechanism
policy_implications: B0 selector could incorporate a secondary pass: for non-picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.02, evaluate whether pullback_duration_weeks ≥ 4, up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.50, and mom_20 ≥ 0.055 as qualifying conditions for a pullback-track watchlist

Portfolio construction: false negatives with shallow pullbacks (-5% to -8%) represent a distinct risk-reward profile vs. deep-pullback selected winners — the former may offer better risk-adjusted entry if momentum recovery is genuine

Risk management: false negatives with low up_day_ratio_20 (< 0.45) and shallow pullback should be treated as lower-conviction signals even if other features appear positive; sizing should reflect the evidence_against cases showing loss outcomes with similar pullback profiles

Snapshot-time filtering: any feature requiring knowledge of future price trajectory (e.g., whether pullback concludes at a specific price level) must be excluded; all qualifying features must be computable from data available at snapshot_anon timestamp

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The embedded-strength pullback mechanism is a post-hoc rationalization of a selection artifact: false-negative big winners are identified AFTER their outcomes are known, so the 'distinguishing features' (pullback depth, up_day_ratio_20, mom_20) are confounded with the outcome rather than causing it. The mechanism cannot explain why entity_535a1beed7 and entity_05b4c6b1f7 achieve large_win despite having null pullback data, nor why entity_bfb308b24a with nearly identical pullback characteristics (-12.1% over 4 weeks, up_day_ratio_20=0.45) produces a loss. The apparent pattern is a statistical mirage from small-sample selection on the dependent variable.

attacks.issue: Endogenous selection: false negatives are defined by their outcomes, not pre-specified criteria
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher labels entities 'false_negative_big_winner' only if they achieve W4 returns >=8% above selected_winner median. This creates look-ahead bias: features like up_day_ratio_20=0.50 and mom_20=0.028 are not predictors—they are artifacts of selecting entities that happened to win. The mechanism cannot be falsified because any entity that fits the thresholds AND produces a large win is classified as confirming evidence; any that fits but fails is not called a false_negative_big_winner. The classification is circular.

attacks.issue: Null pullback data violates the mechanism's premise for 2 of 2 false_negative_big_winner cases
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_535a1beed7 (up_day_ratio_20=0.50, mom_20=0.028, vol_ratio_5_20=1.174) and entity_05b4c6b1f7 (up_day_ratio_20=0.50, mom_20=0.070, vol_ratio_5_20=0.964) are labeled false_negative_big_winner but have null pullback_duration_weeks and null pullback_pct. The mechanism explicitly claims these entities 'missed by B0 due to low trigger proximity while in pullback consolidation,' yet no pullback is observed. Either (a) the pullback occurred before the snapshot and was not recorded, making the feature unobservable at snapshot time (violating the 'do not use information unavailable at snapshot time' rule), or (b) the mechanism is wrong and large_win outcomes occur without pullback.

attacks.issue: Threshold inconsistency between evidence_for cases and falsifiable predictions
attacks.why_it_matters: The falsifiable prediction requires up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55, mom_20 >= 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.40. But the actual false_negative_big_winner cases have: entity_de1c657364 (up_day_ratio_20=0.65, mom_20=0.058, vol_ratio_5_20=1.147), entity_535a1beed7 (up_day_ratio_20=0.50, mom_20=0.028, vol_ratio_5_20=1.174), entity_05b4c6b1f7 (up_day_ratio_20=0.50, mom_20=0.070, vol_ratio_5_20=0.964). Zero of three meet the mom_20 >= 0.12 threshold. The mechanism claims these features explain the outcome, but the evidence contradicts the stated thresholds.

attacks.issue: Contradictory pullback cases with identical profiles produce different outcomes
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_bfb308b24a (pullback_pct=-12.1%, pullback_duration_weeks=4, up_day_ratio_20=0.45, mom_20=0.027) produces 'loss' but is labeled false_negative_relative (not false_negative_big_winner). entity_de1c657364 (pullback_pct=-7.3%, pullback_duration_weeks=8, up_day_ratio_20=0.65, mom_20=0.058) produces 'large_win' and is labeled false_negative_big_winner. The feature differences (longer duration, higher up_day_ratio_20, higher mom_20) are invoked as explanations, but entity_df5478102d (pullback_pct=-5.0%, pullback_duration_weeks=4, up_day_ratio_20=0.60, mom_20=0.125) with similar-or-better features produces only 'small_win'. The mechanism cannot explain why better features sometimes produce smaller wins.

attacks.issue: Up_day_ratio_20 is a lagging indicator that proxies for recent price history, not future direction
attacks.why_it_matters: up_day_ratio_20 measures the fraction of up days in the prior 20 trading days. This is mechanically correlated with recent price trajectory but contains no independent information about future returns. A stock that went up 13 of 20 days (up_day_ratio_20=0.65) is simply a stock that has already gone up recently. The mechanism is claiming that 'recent winners continue to win' dressed in technical analysis language. This is a well-known mean-reversion trap in the opposite direction: high up_day_ratio_20 often precedes reversal, not continuation.

attacks.issue: The vol_ratio_5_20 threshold (>=1.40) contradicts the false_negative median (1.179)
attacks.why_it_matters: The falsifiable prediction requires vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.40 for the mechanism to predict large_win. But the false_negative_median for this feature is 1.179, which is 0.221 below the stated threshold. This means the typical false negative does NOT meet the mechanism's own vol_ratio criterion. The mechanism cannot explain its own canonical cases.

counterexamples_to_seek: A non-pick at snapshot time with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55, mom_20 >= 0.10, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.40, pullback_pct between -5% and -10%, pullback_duration_weeks >= 5, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.02 that produces w4_return_bucket = 'ruin' or 'loss'. This directly falsifies the embedded-strength mechanism by satisfying all preconditions yet failing the predicted outcome.

A false_negative_relative entity (not selected by B0) with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60, mom_20 >= 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.50, but null pullback data (no recorded pullback) that produces only 'small_win' or 'loss' despite strong snapshot features. This would invalidate the claim that these snapshot features are the mechanism by which false negatives become winners.

A period or snapshot cohort where broad market (e.g., SPY) declined >5% in the 20 days prior to snapshot, within which non-picks matching the embedded-strength criteria (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.50, mom_20 >= 0.06, pullback_pct -5% to -10%) uniformly produce 'loss' or 'ruin'. This would reveal that the mechanism is a proxy for market tailwind rather than stock-specific embedded strength.

A selected_winner entity (is_b0_pick=true) with up_day_ratio_20 <= 0.40, mom_20 <= 0.03, vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.00, and no pullback that produces 'large_win' — demonstrating that the B0 selector captures winners using the inverse of the false-negative mechanism's features, which would undermine the claim that those features are necessary for embedded strength.
what_would_change_my_mind: Demonstrate that the mechanism's features (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, up_day_ratio_20, mom_20) are observable and consistently recorded for ALL false_negative_big_winner cases, with no null values and no post-snapshot inference required.

Show that the proposed thresholds (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55, mom_20 >= 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.40, pullback_pct -5% to -10%, pullback_duration_weeks >= 4) were specified BEFORE examining outcomes, not derived from the evidence_for cases post-hoc.

Provide out-of-sample validation: test the mechanism on a separate holdout set of non-picks where the features are pre-specified and the outcome is not used to classify the entity as false_negative_big_winner. Show the mechanism predicts large_win at above-chance rates.

Find at least one entity with null pullback data that is correctly excluded from false_negative_big_winner classification despite having up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20 values consistent with the mechanism's feature profile — demonstrating that the mechanism does not overfit to outcomes.

Identify a causal mechanism (e.g., institutional accumulation detected via specific order flow signatures, options positioning data, sector rotation timing) that links the observable features to the outcome, rather than relying on correlation between snapshot features and future returns.

tests.name: null_pullback_falsification
tests.comparison: false_negative_big_winner cases with null pullback data vs non-null pullback false_negative_big_winner cases
tests.success_criterion: If the embedded-strength mechanism is valid, false_negative_big_winner cases with null pullback data must have null features across ALL entities (i.e., null represents 'no pullback observed' rather than 'pullback unobservable'). Additionally, null-pullback cases must have mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 values within the interquartile range of non-null cases.
tests.failure_criterion: If any false_negative_big_winner has null pullback_pct/pullback_duration_weeks while having mom_20 > 0.10 OR up_day_ratio_20 > 0.60, the mechanism's pullback-consolidation premise is falsified because the entity achieved large_win without an observable pullback, implying an alternative pathway that the mechanism cannot explain using PIT features.

tests.name: threshold_calibration_test
tests.comparison: Distribution of feature values for false_negative_big_winner entities vs stated falsifiable prediction thresholds
tests.success_criterion: At least 2 of 2 false_negative_big_winner cases must meet at least 3 of 5 stated thresholds (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55, mom_20 >= 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.40, pullback_pct between -5% and -10%, pullback_duration_weeks >= 4) if the mechanism is to retain explanatory power.
tests.failure_criterion: If zero of 2 false_negative_big_winner cases meet the mom_20 >= 0.12 threshold (as currently observed), the stated thresholds are contradicted by the canonical evidence. The mechanism must either revise thresholds to match observed data or admit the mom_20 feature is not a causal mechanism for false-negative outcomes.

tests.name: contradictory_profile_counterexample
tests.comparison: entity_bfb308b24a (loss, pullback_pct=-12.1%, pullback_duration_weeks=4, up_day_ratio_20=0.45, mom_20=0.027) vs entity_df5478102d (small_win, pullback_pct=-5.0%, pullback_duration_weeks=4, up_day_ratio_20=0.60, mom_20=0.125)
tests.success_criterion: If the mechanism explains outcome magnitude via pullback depth and duration, then entity_df5478102d (shallower pullback, higher momentum, higher up_day_ratio_20) should produce equal-or-larger returns than entity_bfb308b24a. This would be consistent with the mechanism.
tests.failure_criterion: If entity_df5478102d (better features: shallower pullback, higher momentum) produces only small_win while entity_bfb308b24a produces loss, the mechanism fails to explain within-profile outcome variance. This constitutes a counterexample: the mechanism predicts entity_df5478102d should achieve large_win given superior feature values, but it does not. The mechanism is incomplete.

tests.name: up_day_ratio_lagging_test
tests.comparison: Correlation between up_day_ratio_20 and future mom_20 (5-week forward momentum) vs correlation with past mom_20 (lag-1 autocorrelation)
tests.success_criterion: If up_day_ratio_20 contains forward-looking information (as the mechanism claims), its correlation with future mom_20 must be positive and significant (p < 0.05) after controlling for current mom_20. If it is merely a lagging indicator, correlation with future mom_20 should be no better than correlation with past mom_20.
tests.failure_criterion: If up_day_ratio_20 has stronger correlation with past mom_20 than with future mom_20, or if correlation with future mom_20 is not statistically significant, then up_day_ratio_20 is a lagging indicator that proxies for recent trajectory rather than embedded strength. Any mechanism relying on up_day_ratio_20 as a predictive feature is falsified.

tests.name: market_tailwind_proxy_test
tests.comparison: Cross-snapshot_anon correlation: do false_negative_big_winner cases cluster within specific snapshots (indicating market-wide conditions) vs distributed across snapshots (indicating stock-specific embedded strength)?
tests.success_criterion: If false_negative_big_winner cases are distributed across at least 3 distinct snapshot_anon values with no single snapshot containing >50% of cases, the mechanism is not purely a market-tailwind proxy.
tests.failure_criterion: If all false_negative_big_winner cases share the same snapshot_anon (snap_71486ed83c contains entity_535a1beed7, entity_de1c657364, entity_05b4c6b1f7), this indicates the pattern is confounded by temporal market conditions rather than stock-specific embedded strength. The mechanism would be falsified as a proxy for market tailwind.

tests.name: is_b0_pick_feature_inversion
tests.comparison: Feature distributions for selected_winner (is_b0_pick=true) vs false_negative_relative (is_b0_pick=false)
tests.success_criterion: If B0 selector captures winners via the inverse of the false-negative mechanism (higher trigger proximity, stronger momentum), then selected_winner entities should have ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.025, mom_20 > 0.10, and up_day_ratio_20 > 0.55 more frequently than false_negative_relative entities.
tests.failure_criterion: If selected_winner entities include cases with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.015, mom_20 < 0.05, and up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50 that still produce large_win, then B0 selection is not explained by the inverse of the false-negative mechanism. This would indicate the mechanism is incomplete: B0 captures some winners via different signals, and B0 misses some false negatives despite favorable embedded-strength features.

tests.name: pre_specified_threshold_validation
tests.comparison: Apply pre-specified thresholds (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.50, mom_20 >= 0.06, pullback_pct -5% to -10%, pullback_duration_weeks >= 4, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.02) to ALL non-picks (is_b0_pick=false) regardless of outcome label
tests.success_criterion: The threshold combination must identify a subset of non-picks where large_win rate is statistically significantly higher than the base rate for all non-picks (Fisher's exact test, p < 0.05).
tests.failure_criterion: If non-picks meeting the threshold combination have a large_win rate that is NOT statistically significantly different from non-picks not meeting the threshold, the mechanism's predictive validity is falsified. The apparent pattern would be a selection artifact.

leakage_checks: Verify pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks are computed from data available at snapshot_anon timestamp, not from future price observations post-snapshot
Confirm ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is computed at entry time, not derived from subsequent price action
Ensure mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 are rolling window features backward-looking from snapshot, not forward-looking
Check that w4_return_bucket labels are not used to reclassify entities after feature observation (no outcome-dependent feature engineering)
Validate that vol_ratio_5_20 uses historical volume ratios observable at snapshot time, not contemporaneous volume spikes post-snapshot

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The pullback-consolidation mechanism is directly falsified by the evidence. Both canonical false_negative_big_winner cases (entity_535a1beed7, entity_05b4c6b1f7) have null pullback data—meaning the mechanism's central premise ('missed by B0 due to low trigger proximity while in pullback consolidation') cannot be verified at snapshot time. The stated falsifiable thresholds (mom_20 >= 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.40) are met by zero of two false_negative_big_winner cases. The mechanism cannot explain within-profile variance: entity_df5478102d with superior features (mom_20=0.125, up_day_ratio_20=0.60) produces only small_win while entity_bfb308b24a (mom_20=0.027, up_day_ratio_20=0.45) produces loss. The pattern is an artifact of outcome-biased selection masquerading as a predictive mechanism.
falsifiers: Find a false_negative_big_winner with null pullback data AND mom_20 >= 0.10 AND up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55. Both canonical cases satisfy this: entity_535a1beed7 (mom_20=0.028, up_day_ratio_20=0.50) and entity_05b4c6b1f7 (mom_20=0.070, up_day_ratio_20=0.50). This is already satisfied by the evidence, falsifying the pullback-consolidation premise.

Find a non-pick meeting the stated prediction thresholds (up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55, mom_20 >= 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.40) that produces loss or ruin. Zero of two false_negative_big_winner cases meet even one of these thresholds, let alone the falsifiable prediction. The mechanism cannot explain its own canonical evidence.

Find a non-pick with up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.60, mom_20 >= 0.12, vol_ratio_5_20 >= 1.50, but null pullback data, producing only small_win or loss. This would invalidate the claim that snapshot features (not pullback) drive the outcome—already suggested by the null-pullback winners.
actionable_design_principles: Abandon pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks as causal features for this mechanism. Null values in both canonical cases mean these features are either unobservable at snapshot time or irrelevant to the outcome.

Do not use outcome labels to define the feature space post-hoc. The classification 'false_negative_big_winner' is defined by future W4 returns, then features are inspected to construct a post-hoc narrative. This creates a guaranteed-confirming pattern with no falsification path.
Any valid mechanism must predict without using the outcome variable in feature selection. Pre-specify features based on domain theory, not data-mined associations with known winners.

If up_day_ratio_20 is retained as a feature, validate that it contains forward-looking information independent of current momentum. The skeptic's attack that it is purely a lagging indicator (recent winners continuing to win) must be tested formally, not assumed away.
Threshold calibration must use the same data that defines the mechanism. Using one set of cases to build thresholds and another to validate is circular.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Invert the selection logic: instead of searching for features common to false_negative_big_winner cases, test whether non-picks with features opposite to selected_winner (lower trigger proximity, weaker momentum) have systematically different outcomes from selected winners when controlling for market conditions.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The current mechanism searches for confirmatory evidence among winners. The inversion tests the falsification path: if non-picks with weak features (low trigger proximity, low momentum) still produce large_win at rates comparable to selected_winner, the B0 selector is adding no signal.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Tests whether B0 selection captures a genuine signal or is a selection artifact from the feature space definition.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Test the 'embedded strength' claim by checking if false_negative_big_winner cases have superior ex-ante characteristics (pre-snapshot) vs false_negative_relative cases matched on pullback depth and duration. If no difference exists, the outcome difference is not explained by the mechanism.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Separates the pullback mechanism from pure outcome variance. If matched false negatives with identical pullback profiles produce different outcomes, the mechanism is incomplete regardless of feature values.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Determines whether the mechanism explains outcome magnitude or merely describes post-hoc features of entities that happened to win.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Validate up_day_ratio_20 as a forward-looking signal by testing if it predicts future momentum (mom_future_5) after partialling out current mom_20 and vol_ratio_5_20. If it does not add incremental predictive power beyond current momentum, it is a lagging indicator and must be excluded.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses the skeptic's specific attack that up_day_ratio_20 proxies recent price history without independent forward information. A proper predictive mechanism requires this test.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Determines whether up_day_ratio_20 is a genuine predictive feature or an artifact of outcome-biased selection.

cycles.question: Study false-negative non-picks that become large winners under near-buy-point geometry; identify repeated PIT-visible precursors. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False‑negative non‑picks that become large winners are distinguished by a tight, shallow base: price is less extended from the 20‑day and 50‑day MAs (px_vs_ma20 < 0.07, px_vs_ma50 < 0.10), recent momentum is modest (mom_20 < 0.10), up‑day ratio is low (<=0.5), volume is near or below its 20‑day norm (vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.25), and the entry is very close to the trigger point (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <= 0.025). This combination indicates reduced upside exhaustion and higher continuation potential relative to more extended B0 picks, allowing the non‑pick to accelerate after the snapshot.
evidence_for: Median up_day_ratio_20 for false negatives (0.50) is 0.125 lower than for selected winners (0.625), the largest standardized delta (-1.19).
Median vol_ratio_5_20 for false negatives (1.179) is 0.245 lower than for selected winners (1.424), standardized delta -1.05.
Median mom_20 for false negatives (0.058) is 0.105 lower than for selected winners (0.163), standardized delta -1.00.
Median ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct for false negatives (0.0195) is 0.0105 lower than for selected winners (0.030), indicating a tighter entry proximity.
Median px_vs_ma20 (0.042) and px_vs_ma50 (0.056) for false negatives are roughly half those of selected winners (0.076 and 0.127), showing less price extension.
Median pullback_pct for false negatives (-7.3%) is less deep than for selected winners (-15.9%), consistent with a shallower base.

Case example entity_535a1beed7 (false_negative_big_winner|false_negative_relative) has up_day_ratio_20=0.50, vol_ratio_5_20=1.174, mom_20=0.028, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.009, px_vs_ma20=0.032 – all near the low‑feature cluster and lands in the large_win bucket.

Case example entity_df5478102d (false_negative_relative) exhibits the same low‑feature pattern (up_day_ratio=0.60, vol_ratio=1.405, mom_20=0.125, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.034) and achieves a small_win outcome, illustrating the precursor signature.
evidence_against: Entity bfb308b24a (false_negative_relative, loss) has low up_day_ratio (0.45), low vol_ratio (1.187), low mom_20 (0.027), and near‑trigger ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (0.039) – yet it does not become a winner, showing the low‑feature pattern alone does not guarantee success.

Entity ad2bfdee3f (false_negative_relative, small_win) displays negative momentum (mom_20 = -0.046) and very low price extension (px_vs_ma20 = 0.007), yet the outcome is only a small_win, not large_win, indicating additional factors beyond the identified precursors.
