skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The 'near-buy-point geometry' precursor set defines away the very phenomenon it claims to explain. The thresholds (px_vs_ma20 < 0.07, vol_ratio <= 1.25, mom_20 < 0.10) are calibrated on outcome-selected cases; without the full non-pick population per snapshot, the distributional claim is vacuous—these features may simply describe average non-picks, not discriminative signals.

attacks.issue: Outcome selection conditioning the feature distribution
attacks.why_it_matters: The 27-case sample was assembled using a post-hoc outcome criterion ('future W4 >=8% and >=5pp above B0 selected median'). This guarantees that any feature computed at the snapshot will appear 'lower' for false negatives vs. selected winners by construction, regardless of predictive validity. The standardized deltas (-1.19, -1.05, -1.00) reflect this selection bias, not a causal mechanism. Without the denominator (all non-picks at each snapshot, winners and losers), the numerator statistics are uninterpretable.

attacks.issue: Contradictory cases with near-identical precursor signatures produce divergent outcomes
attacks.why_it_matters: Entity bfb308b24a has up_day_ratio=0.45, vol_ratio=1.187, mom_20=0.027, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct=0.039—dead-center in the claimed precursor cluster—yet produces a loss. Entity ad2bfdee3f has up_day_ratio=0.45, vol_ratio=1.179, mom_20=-0.046, px_vs_ma20=0.007—also cluster-conforming—yet produces only small_win. If the precursor pattern were genuinely predictive, these cases should yield large_win; their divergence shows the pattern is not sufficient and likely not necessary.

attacks.issue: Threshold incoherence: vol_ratio_5_20 <= 1.25 as a 'discriminator' contradicts the selected-winner median
attacks.why_it_matters: The claim proposes vol_ratio <= 1.25 as a discriminating feature, yet the selected-winner median vol_ratio is 1.424—well above this threshold. Most selected winners exceed the proposed cutoff. This means low volume ratio is not what separates false negatives from winners; it separates low-volume stocks from high-volume stocks, a different axis entirely. The mechanism conflates two distinct phenomena.

attacks.issue: Pullback directionality contradicts the 'tight-base continuation' narrative
attacks.why_it_matters: False negatives have median pullback_pct = -7.3% (shallower), while selected winners have -15.9% (deeper). The mechanism claims shallow bases indicate 'reduced upside exhaustion' and higher continuation potential. But technical analysis theory holds that deeper pullbacks produce better resets and more explosive moves. The data shows the opposite pattern the mechanism predicts, suggesting the observed correlation is spurious or confounded by a third variable (e.g., market conditions, sector strength).

attacks.issue: Near-buy-point geometry is operationally self-contradictory
attacks.why_it_matters: The claim requires ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <= 0.025 as a precursor. If the entry is 'near trigger' (within 2.5% of the trigger price), why did the non-pick not trigger? The non-pick status is unexplained and likely reflects an unmeasured variable (sector screening, fundamental filters, market-cap thresholds, or explicit exclusions). Attributing outcome differences to geometric features while ignoring the reason for non-selection introduces an omitted-variable bias.

attacks.issue: Selected winners share the same 'false-negative' feature cluster
attacks.why_it_matters: Entity_28a6ec4601 (selected_winner, large_win) has up_day_ratio=0.60, vol_ratio=1.188, mom_20=0.143, px_vs_ma20=0.086. Entity_8ad5cd4795 (selected_winner, large_win) has up_day_ratio=0.70, vol_ratio=0.996, mom_20=0.004, px_vs_ma20=0.007. These overlap substantially with the false-negative cluster, demonstrating the precursor pattern is not exclusive to non-picks. The predictive power, if any, cannot distinguish picks from non-picks.

counterexamples_to_seek: Non-picks with up_day_ratio <= 0.50, vol_ratio <= 1.25, mom_20 <= 0.10, px_vs_ma20 < 0.07, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <= 0.025 that resulted in loss or small_win (not large_win) — these are absent from the current sample and would directly falsify the predictive claim
Snapshots where the full non-pick population (winners and losers) shows no significant feature difference between outcome groups — this would indicate the observed medians are sampling artifacts
B0 picks with identical 'tight-base' geometry that still produced ruin or loss — to test whether the mechanism applies asymmetrically or not at all

Cases where the reason for non-pick status is documented (e.g., sector exclusion, fundamental screen failure) — if outcomes are explained by these documented reasons rather than geometry, the precursor claim is a proxy variable
what_would_change_my_mind: A controlled study on held-out snapshots showing that the proposed feature set (up_day_ratio <= 0.5, vol_ratio <= 1.25, mom_20 <= 0.10, px_vs_ma20 < 0.07, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct <= 0.025) predicts large_win among non-picks with ≥ 60% precision and ≥ 1.5:1 odds ratio vs. the baseline non-pick win rate
Evidence that the non-pick status itself (sector, market-cap, fundamental exclusion) is orthogonal to the geometric features and does not explain the outcome variance

A mechanism that does not require post-hoc calibration on outcome-selected cases — e.g., a forward-looking measure of 'upside room' that is computable from snapshot data alone and independently validated
Replicated results across ≥ 3 independent snapshot cohorts (each with ≥ 20 false-negative candidates) showing consistent feature separation at p < 0.01

leakage_checks: All feature thresholds must be fixed before outcome inspection; post-hoc threshold adjustment invalidates significance
Snapshot-level aggregation must prevent entity-level cross-contamination in within-snapshot tests
Feature distributions must be computed from snapshot_time only, never from forward-return data
The 27-case discovery set cannot serve as its own validation; external snapshot cohort required
Outcome label 'false_negative_big_winner' construction criterion (W4 >=8% + relative performance) must not influence feature selection

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The 'tight-base continuation' mechanism—claiming that false-negative winners are distinguished by low up_day_ratio (≤0.50), low vol_ratio (≤1.25), modest momentum (mom_20 ≤0.10), tight entry proximity (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct ≤0.025), and low price extension (px_vs_ma20 <0.07)—is directionally plausible based on distributional medians but methodologically compromised. The 27-case discovery set was assembled using post-hoc outcome criteria (future W4 ≥8% and relative outperformance), which creates selection conditioning that guarantees the feature pattern appears 'lower' for false negatives regardless of predictive validity. Standardized deltas of -1.19, -1.05, and -1.00 are numerically large but interpretively vacuous without the denominator: the full non-pick population per snapshot (winners and losers). The skeptic's counterexamples—entity bfb308b24a and entity ad2bfdee3f, both cluster-conforming yet producing loss or small_win—demonstrate the pattern is neither sufficient nor necessary. The vol_ratio threshold incoherence (≤1.25 proposed vs. selected-winner median of 1.424) further undermines the mechanism's internal consistency. Pullback directionality contradicts the 'reduced exhaustion' narrative: false negatives have shallower median pullback (-7.3%) than selected winners (-15.9%), opposite to the expected pattern if deeper resets enable continuation. The unmeasured non-pick exclusion criterion (sector, fundamental, market-cap) introduces an omitted-variable threat that cannot be dismissed. Verdict is UNRESOLVED pending out-of-sample validation using the full non-pick denominator per snapshot.
falsifiers: Out-of-sample test showing non-picks with the tight-base precursor set (up_day_ratio ≤0.50, vol_ratio ≤1.25, mom_20 ≤0.10, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct ≤0.025, px_vs_ma20 <0.07) produce large_win rate NOT significantly above baseline non-pick large_win rate (p > 0.10)
Demonstration that the non-pick exclusion reason (sector filter, fundamental screen, market-cap threshold) is documented and statistically explains outcome variance better than geometry alone
Within-snapshot analysis showing false-negative winners vs. false-negative losers share indistinguishable medians across the claimed precursor features (Mann-Whitney p > 0.30 for ≥4 of 5 features)
Replication of the feature separation pattern across ≥3 independent snapshot cohorts with pre-specified thresholds (no post-hoc adjustment)

Finding that B0 picks sharing identical 'tight-base' geometry (same feature ranges) produce ruin/loss rates comparable to false-negative non-picks, indicating geometry does not distinguish the populations
actionable_design_principles: Do not treat the tight-base pattern as a confirmed filter; use it as an exploratory flag requiring prospective validation before incorporation into selection logic
Require the full non-pick population per snapshot as the denominator for any distributional claim; numerator-only statistics are uninterpretable for discrimination
Distinguish between geometric precursors and the non-pick exclusion criterion—document what caused non-selection before attributing outcomes to geometry
Acknowledge that the proposed vol_ratio threshold (≤1.25) contradicts the selected-winner distribution; consider this an inconsistency requiring resolution rather than a feature boundary
Do not implement policy changes based on post-hoc calibrated thresholds; require forward-looking validation with pre-specified cutoffs

cycles.question: Study false-negative non-picks that become large winners under near-buy-point geometry; separate true signal from correlated proxy. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-negative non-picks become large winners when B0's geometric selection rejects entries that are technically close to the trigger line but structurally distinct: specifically, entities with lower momentum, volume expansion, and price-extension that nonetheless sustain up-day ratio ≥0.5 and exhibit compressed distance between price and MA20/MA50, enabling them to re-enter the buy-point zone post-selection. The false-negative mechanism is a signal-correlated-proxy: B0 uses MA-slope and momentum as proxy discriminators, but these same proxies covary with the wrong subset of the true causal geometry (distance-from-trigger normalized by volatility).
evidence_for: False-negative medians on up_day_ratio_20 (0.5), vol_ratio_5_20 (1.179), and mom_20 (0.058) are uniformly below selected-winner medians (0.625, 1.424, 0.163), with standardized deltas exceeding -1.0 for the first two features, indicating the proxy discriminators successfully stratify momentum magnitude but incorrectly exclude the false-negative subgroup.

Entity 535a1beed7 (false_negative_big_winner) has the lowest vol_ratio_5_20 among all large_win cases (1.174), and entity_ad2bfdee3f (false_negative_relative) has negative mom_20 (-0.0455) and negative ma10/ma20 slopes, yet both achieved positive W4 returns, demonstrating that the proxy discriminators fire in the wrong direction.

False-negative median ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (0.019) is substantially lower than selected-winner median (0.030), indicating the trigger-distance geometry is compressed for non-picks—this is the PIT-observable proxy for the true buy-point geometry, not the geometry itself.

The case entity_2f86543bf6 with ma20_slope_5 = -0.0078 (negative) and mom_20 = -0.008 (slightly negative) still achieved large_win, showing that slope signs in the selected feature set are unreliable separators.

Selected winners with large pullback_pct (e.g., entity_3adc078f01 at -42.3%, entity_2c58cebc59 at -25.1%) generated large wins despite extreme drawdowns, confirming that pullback_pct is not a causal mechanism but a correlated outcome.
evidence_against: False-negative entity_bfb308b24a had pullback_pct = -12.1% and up_day_ratio_20 = 0.45, yet produced a loss outcome (w4_return_bucket = loss), indicating that low up_day_ratio alone is insufficient to generate a false-negative winner—the mechanism requires the specific combination of compressed trigger-distance with moderate momentum continuity.

False-positive ruin cases (entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c) share high mom_20 (0.185, 0.242), high ma10_slope_5 (0.090, 0.030), and up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.6, indicating that the proxy discriminators do correctly identify high-momentum stocks but these high-proxy stocks can still ruin, suggesting the true causal factor (volatility-normalized trigger proximity) is orthogonal to the proxy.

Entity_6618d3e80c is labeled both false_positive_ruin|selected_winner, with high mom_20 (0.251), high px_vs_ma50 (0.337), and high vol_ratio_5_20 (1.446)—its dual outcome suggests the geometry was ambiguous at snapshot, consistent with the mechanism claim that boundary cases are misclassified by the proxy.
falsifiable_predictions: Condition A: Non-pick entities where ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.015, up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.45, and vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.25 will produce W4 returns ≥ 5% at a rate exceeding 60% when the underlying market bucket matches the snapshot's market regime.

Condition B: Adding ma20_slope_5 sign reversal (negative) to the above filter will increase the precision of detecting false-negative big winners by ≥15 percentage points relative to B0's base precision.

Condition C: The proxy `px_vs_ma50` will have zero incremental predictive power over `ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct` for distinguishing false-negative big winners from selected winners when both are conditioned on the same vol_ratio_5_20 bucket.

Condition D: Simulating B0's selection with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct replaced by a volatility-normalized trigger-distance measure (close minus trigger normalized by ATR) will increase false-negative capture by ≥20% without increasing false-positive ruin rate.
policy_implications: B0's screening pipeline should not use ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, or mom_20 as independent selection gates when the primary geometry measure (trigger-distance) is near its own threshold—the proxy gates create correlated exclusions that remove geometrically valid entries.

A secondary filter using only up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.45 and vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.3 (without momentum or slope features) applied to the non-pick pool at each snapshot would capture false-negative winners while excluding the false-negative losses.

Portfolio construction should treat false-negative captures as a separate signal class with position sizing informed by the trigger-distance compression—the more compressed the geometry, the smaller the initial position due to reduced confidence in causal purity.

The policy should avoid using `pullback_pct` as a negative filter for non-pick re-entry decisions, since the evidence shows selected winners with pullbacks exceeding -25% still produced large wins, indicating pullback_pct is an outcome variable, not a causal predictor.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The entire 'false-negative' category is a post-hoc constructed set using forward-looking outcomes (W4 >= 8%, >= 5pp above B0 median), which guarantees that any observed feature distribution is a mixture of predictive signal and outcome-contingent selection bias. The claim that ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct captures 'true geometry' while MA-slopes and momentum are 'proxy discriminators' is circular: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is itself just another proxy, and the researcher never isolates the actual geometric property (spatial position relative to the trigger line at entry) from the correlated price-ratio measures. The mechanism is unfalsifiable because it retrofits geometry post-outcome.

attacks.issue: Outcome-contingent category construction introduces selection bias into all feature distributions
attacks.why_it_matters: The 'false-negative' label requires W4 >= 8% and >= 5pp above B0 median—information unavailable at snapshot time. This means the category is defined by future performance, not snapshot geometry. Any feature contrast between false-negatives and selected-winners is contaminated by having selected on the outcome. The researcher cannot claim these features 'predict' false-negative status when the category was constructed using the very outcome the features allegedly predict. This is textbook circular validation.

attacks.issue: The 'trigger-distance geometry' mechanism is never actually measured
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher claims ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct proxies for 'true geometry' while MA-slopes are 'proxy discriminators,' but provides no evidence that ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct correlates with a distinct geometric property. Both are price ratios derived from the same price series. The actual spatial geometry (where the entry candle sits relative to the trigger line on the chart) is never isolated from these correlated derivatives. Without a causal graph showing why one proxy is 'true' and another is 'correlated proxy,' this is assertion, not mechanism.

attacks.issue: Sample size insufficient for the stated precision claims (27 cases, 2-7 false-negative sub-types)
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher proposes Condition B claiming ma20_slope_5 sign reversal will increase precision by >= 15 percentage points. With at most 7 false-negative cases total (5 relative + 2 big_winner), no statistical test can support a 15pp claim. The 95% confidence intervals on any split would be enormous. The standardized_delta values in the contrasts table (-0.5988 for ma20_slope_5) barely exceed 0.5 SD, indicating weak and likely non-replicable separations.

attacks.issue: Cross-snapshot aggregation obscures regime heterogeneity
attacks.why_it_matters: Cases come from snapshots spanning snap_724342c280 through snap_b8420124eb, with no adjustment for market regime (bull/bear/sideways), sector rotation, or volatility regime changes. The vol_ratio_5_20 contrasts could simply reflect that some snapshots occurred in high-VIX environments where all stocks had compressed volume ratios. Without conditioning on regime, the contrasts conflate time-period effects with the alleged geometric mechanism.

attacks.issue: The policy implication contradicts the mechanism claim
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher recommends 'avoiding ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, or mom_20 as independent selection gates' near trigger-distance thresholds. But the mechanism claim states these proxies 'covary with the wrong subset of the true causal geometry.' If this is true, removing the proxies should either help (if they exclude true winners) or hurt (if they exclude noise). The researcher never demonstrates that including them causes harm—only that winners happened to have lower values. This is selection effect, not causal exclusion.

attacks.issue: pullback_pct nulls undermine the 'compressed geometry' argument
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher correctly notes that selected winners with extreme pullbacks (-42.3%, -25.1%) still won, claiming pullback_pct is an outcome variable. However, the researcher simultaneously uses ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as a causal predictor. If pullback_pct is outcome-correlated, then ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, being a price ratio also derived from the same price series, is equally outcome-correlated. The researcher cannot have it both ways: either price-derived ratios are causal (for ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) or they're outcome-correlated (for pullback_pct).

attacks.issue: The 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' dual-label entity_6618d3e80c is treated as evidence for boundary ambiguity but could indicate label noise
attacks.why_it_matters: A single entity receiving both ruin and winner labels suggests the labeling protocol lacks rigor—perhaps the entity was held through multiple trades, or the label aggregation method is flawed. If labels are noisy, all contrasts are unreliable. The researcher should demonstrate label reliability before claiming any mechanism.

counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.015, up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.45, and vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.25 but W4 returned <= 0% (failed false-negative prediction)
Cases where ma20_slope_5 is negative and W4 was a large win that were NOT labeled false-negative (suggesting the mechanism is outcome-contingent, not geometric)

Snapshots where vol_ratio_5_20 was high (>1.5) but ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct was low (<0.02) and the entity still failed—a test of whether the mechanism is geometry-based or simply a regime effect
B0-selected picks that had compressed trigger-distance (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.02) but still ruined, which would show the 'true geometry' does not protect against loss
A time-period hold-out test: train on snapshots 1-15, test on 16-27, and verify the predicted false-negative capture rate exceeds B0's base capture rate
what_would_change_my_mind: An out-of-sample test showing that applying the Condition A filter (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.015, up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.45, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.25) to a hold-out snapshot set produces >= 60% hit rate on large_win outcomes, with the test set having no overlap with discovery cases

A demonstrated causal graph: (trigger geometry) -> (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) -> (W4 outcome), with instrumental variable evidence that ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct operates through geometry and not through correlated momentum

A within-snapshot randomization test showing that swapping ma10_slope_5 and mom_20 for random noise in B0's selection pipeline changes the false-negative capture rate by >= 20%, proving these are causal exclusions and not spurious correlations

Evidence that the 7-week pullback cases (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_ccc90a671f) are structurally distinct from the no-pullback cases, explaining why the geometry worked for some and not others without reference to post-snapshot information

tests.name: trigger_distance_vs_price_extension_redundancy
tests.comparison: Within vol_ratio_5_20 decile, test whether ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct and px_vs_ma50 are statistically independent vs. redundant. Use Spearman correlation conditioned on vol_ratio decile; pool across snapshots using Fisher Z-transform.
tests.success_criterion: Mean conditional Spearman ρ(ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, px_vs_ma50 | vol_ratio_decile) < 0.60, indicating the features capture distinct variance
tests.failure_criterion: Mean conditional ρ >= 0.60, indicating ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is redundant with px_vs_ma50 and the 'true geometry' claim lacks feature-level support

tests.name: non_pick_momentum_reversal_within_snapshot
tests.comparison: Among non-pick entities (is_b0_pick=false) within each snapshot, compare w4_return_bucket distributions between ma20_slope_5 negative vs. non-negative subgroups, using Fisher's exact test per snapshot, then Stouffer-Z pooled across snapshots.
tests.success_criterion: Pooled odds ratio for large_win/win vs. loss/ruin between negative-ma20_slope and non-negative-ma20_slope subgroups exceeds 2.0, with pooled p < 0.05, confirming ma20_slope sign reversal captures non-pick winners independent of outcome-contingent labels
tests.failure_criterion: Pooled odds ratio <= 1.5 or p >= 0.10, indicating ma20_slope sign reversal has no predictive power for non-pick outcomes and the skeptic's outcome-contingency concern stands

tests.name: trigger_compression_vs_momentum_independence
tests.comparison: Within non-pick entities, test whether ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < median predicts w4_return_bucket=large_win independent of mom_20 quartile, using stratified 2x2 tables per mom_20 quartile per snapshot, pooled Mantel-Haenszel OR across snapshots.
tests.success_criterion: Mantel-Haenszel pooled OR >= 2.5 for large_win vs. non-large_win at low trigger_pct across all mom_20 strata, indicating trigger-distance compression operates as a mechanism distinct from momentum
tests.failure_criterion: Pooled OR < 1.5 or significant homogeneity violation (Breslow-Day p < 0.05), indicating the trigger-distance effect is confounded by or redundant with momentum

tests.name: pullback_pct_temporal_precedence
tests.comparison: Test whether pullback_pct is causally prior to ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct or vice versa by examining their temporal ordering across cases with pullback_pct non-null. Compute cross-snapshot correlation of pullback_pct with subsequent ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct changes to test if pullback_pct predicts geometry, or if both are parallel outcomes of entry quality.
tests.success_criterion: pullback_pct does not predict ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct at next snapshot (partial r < 0.15 controlling for mom_20), supporting pullback_pct as outcome variable rather than causal predictor
tests.failure_criterion: pullback_pct significantly predicts subsequent ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (partial r >= 0.30), indicating it contains forward-looking information and the researcher's outcome-variable claim is false

tests.name: up_day_ratio_threshold_robustness_across_volatility_regimes
tests.comparison: Within vol_ratio_5_20 tertiles (low/mid/high), test whether the up_day_ratio_20 threshold of 0.45 discriminates w4_return_bucket within non-pick cohort. Use stratified chi-square test per tertile, pooled across snapshots, to test if the threshold is regime-invariant.
tests.success_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.45 is positively associated with large_win in at least 2 of 3 vol_ratio tertiles (OR > 1.5 per tertile), confirming the threshold is not regime-dependent
tests.failure_criterion: up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.45 shows OR < 1.0 in high-vol_ratio tertile OR contradicts direction in low-vol_ratio tertile, indicating the threshold is regime-contingent and the proposed Condition A filter is spurious

tests.name: dual_label_boundary_proximity
tests.comparison: For the dual-labeled entity (entity_6618d3e80c), compute its percentile rank within the full sample on each of the three key features. Compare to centroid positions of confirmed false_positive_ruin and confirmed selected_winner clusters using Mahalanobis distance (computed on ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20).
tests.success_criterion: Dual-label entity is closer to the selected_winner cluster centroid than the false_positive_ruin centroid (Mahalanobis ratio < 1.0), indicating dual labeling reflects boundary ambiguity rather than label noise
tests.failure_criterion: Dual-label entity is equidistant or closer to false_positive_ruin centroid (ratio >= 1.0), indicating labeling protocol error rather than geometric boundary case

tests.name: snapshot_regime_vol_ratio_confounding
tests.comparison: Treat snapshot_anon as a random effect. Fit a mixed-effects logistic regression predicting w4_return_bucket=large_win with vol_ratio_5_20 and ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as fixed effects, snapshot_anon as random intercept. Test whether ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct effect persists after accounting for snapshot-level variance.
tests.success_criterion: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct has significant fixed effect (p < 0.05) after controlling for snapshot random effects, with ICC (intra-class correlation) for snapshot < 0.30, indicating the mechanism is not merely a regime artifact
tests.failure_criterion: ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct effect becomes non-significant (p >= 0.15) after adding snapshot random effects, or ICC >= 0.50, indicating the apparent trigger-distance effect is confounded by snapshot-level heterogeneity

tests.name: selected_winner_compressed_trigger_ruin_test
tests.comparison: Among is_b0_pick=true entities, test whether low ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (< 0.025) is overrepresented among ruin/loss outcomes vs. large_win outcomes. This directly tests the skeptic's counterexample that compressed trigger-distance does not protect B0-selected picks from loss.
tests.success_criterion: Among B0 picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.025, ruin/loss rate <= 25%, indicating compressed trigger-distance is not a loss harbinger for selected picks
tests.failure_criterion: Among B0 picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.025, ruin/loss rate > 50%, directly contradicting the mechanism claim that trigger-distance compression identifies geometrically valid entries

leakage_checks: w4_return_bucket and outcome_label must never appear in feature arrays—these are outcome variables used only for test success criteria evaluation
snapshot_anon is a grouping variable for regime control, not a predictive feature—models must not extract snapshot identity as a predictor
All feature thresholds (0.45 for up_day_ratio, 0.025 for ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) must be pre-specified from prior analysis, not tuned to maximize test separation on current data
Tests must not condition on entity_anon identity—no entity-level fixed effects or entity-specific rules

Pullback variables (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) are pre-outcome at snapshot time only for entities where pullback occurred before the snapshot date—proxy must verify temporal precedence before including these as features

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The 'false-negative non-pick becomes large winner under near-buy-point geometry' hypothesis has directional evidence (median contrasts showing lower momentum/volume proxies for false-negatives) but cannot be considered SUPPORTED due to three fatal methodological constraints: (1) the outcome-contingent labeling scheme (requiring W4 >= 8% and >= 5pp above B0 median) contaminates all feature contrasts with circular selection bias—this is not a testable mechanism but a post-hoc category; (2) the mechanistic distinction between 'true geometry' (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) and 'correlated proxy' (MA slopes) is asserted without causal graph support—both are price-derived ratios with no demonstrated orthogonal validity; (3) sample size (27 total, ~7 false-negative subtypes) is structurally underpowered for the precision claims (15pp improvement, 60% hit-rate thresholds). The experimental designer has specified 8 falsification tests, but these remain unexecuted, leaving the core predictions (Conditions A-D) empirically untested. The skeptic's outcome-contingency attack is methodologically correct and cannot be dismissed without test execution.
falsifiers: Execute trigger_distance_vs_price_extension_redundancy test: if conditional Spearman ρ(ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, px_vs_ma50 | vol_ratio_decile) >= 0.60, the 'true geometry vs. proxy' distinction collapses
Execute non_pick_momentum_reversal_within_snapshot test: if pooled OR for ma20_slope sign reversal <= 1.5, the proposed ma20_slope_5 condition in Condition B has no predictive basis

Execute pullback_pct_temporal_precedence test: if pullback_pct predicts subsequent ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (partial r >= 0.30), then pullback_pct contains forward-looking information and the researcher's 'outcome variable only' claim is false

Execute snapshot_regime_vol_ratio_confounding test: if ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct effect becomes non-significant (p >= 0.15) after snapshot random effects, the mechanism is regime artifact not geometry
Find at least one counterexample where ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.015, up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.45, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.25 yet W4 return <= 0%—this directly falsifies Condition A

Execute selected_winner_compressed_trigger_ruin_test: if among B0 picks with ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.025 the ruin/loss rate exceeds 50%, the mechanism claim that trigger-distance compression identifies valid entries is contradicted
actionable_design_principles: Do not use the current false-negative labels for any model training or feature selection—the category is outcome-contingent and creates circular validation

If re-labeling, define 'false-negative candidate' using only snapshot-time features (e.g., ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < threshold AND up_day_ratio_20 >= threshold) without reference to W4 outcome, then evaluate whether those snapshot-time criteria predict subsequent outperformance
Reduce Condition A's hit-rate threshold from 60% to 40% and require minimum 15 false-negative-candidate cases before making precision claims—current N=7 cannot support 15pp precision differentials
Treat vol_ratio_5_20 stratification as mandatory, not optional—cross-snapshot pooling without regime adjustment conflates time effects with geometry effects
Demand causal graph evidence before privileging one price-ratio as 'true geometry' versus another as 'correlated proxy'—the distinction must be structural, not post-hoc

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Redefine false-negative-candidate using only pre-specified snapshot-time thresholds (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct < 0.020, up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.45) without referencing future W4 performance; evaluate forward validity prospectively
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Breaks circular validation by using only contemporaneous geometry as the candidate definition; the outcome test is then genuinely predictive rather than confirmatory
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Enables unbiased estimation of snapshot-geometry → W4 outcome relationship; current labels cannot support this

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Implement dual-stratum analysis: stratum 1 = B0 selected picks (is_b0_pick=true) for ruination risk estimation; stratum 2 = non-pick candidates (is_b0_pick=false) for win-rate estimation; never pool across strata for mechanism claims
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The researcher's mechanism claim conflates two distinct decision contexts (B0's screening vs. non-pick re-entry eligibility); pooling obscures that the relevant question differs: for picks, compressed trigger-distance may indicate entry quality, but for non-picks it indicates a different entry type entirely
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Separates the mechanism question (does trigger-distance compression predict win-rate in non-pick stratum?) from the risk question (does it predict ruination in pick stratum?); conflating these produces policy contradictions

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Add a temporal-holdout validation: train candidate-definition thresholds on snapshots 1 through N-2, test hit-rate on snapshot N-1 and N; require out-of-sample replication before policy deployment
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Current evidence is entirely in-sample; the skeptic's regime-heterogeneity concern means in-sample contrasts may not replicate. Out-of-sample validation across snapshot boundaries is the only defense against regime-contingent spurious correlations
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Addresses the experimental designer's snapshot_regime_vol_ratio_confounding concern before policy claims; current data cannot distinguish mechanism from regime artifact

cycles.question: Study false-negative non-picks that become large winners under near-buy-point geometry; propose a counterexample that would invalidate the pattern. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-negative non-picks that become large winners exhibit compressed near-buy-point geometry: low px_vs_ma50 (<6%), modest mom_20 (<8%), and shallow pullback depth (<=-7.3%), producing a tight consolidation state that B0's selection criteria reject but which subsequently resolves into large winners.
evidence_for: entity_535a1beed7: px_vs_ma50=0.024, mom_20=0.028, up_day_ratio_20=0.5, w4_return=large_win; false negative with maximally compressed geometry
entity_de1c657364: px_vs_ma50=0.054, mom_20=0.058, pullback_pct=-7.3, up_day_ratio_20=0.65, w4_return=large_win; matches compressed geometry pattern despite 8-week pullback duration
entity_05b4c6b1f7: px_vs_ma50=0.056, mom_20=0.070, vol_ratio_5_20=0.964, w4_return=large_win; lowest vol_ratio in large_win FN subset, under-the-radar consolidation

Numeric contrasts show FN median px_vs_ma50=0.056 vs SW median=0.127 (delta=-0.071, -0.85 sigma); FN median mom_20=0.058 vs SW median=0.163 (delta=-0.105, -1.00 sigma); FN median pullback_pct=-7.3 vs SW median=-15.9 (shallow by +8.6pp)

Selected winners entity_2f86543bf6 and entity_90a828939a share this compressed geometry (mom_20=0.008 and 0.036 respectively) yet still produce large_win outcomes, confirming the pattern is not exclusive to false negatives
evidence_against: entity_bfb308b24a: false_negative_relative with px_vs_ma50=0.027, mom_20=0.027, pullback_pct=-12.1, up_day_ratio_20=0.45, w4_return_bucket=loss; compressed geometry but failed to generate large_win
entity_ad2bfdee3f: false_negative_relative with px_vs_ma50=-0.033 (below MA50), mom_20=-0.046, up_day_ratio_20=0.45, w4_return=small_win; negative price-metric relationship, not compressed geometry

entity_df5478102d: false_negative_relative with px_vs_ma50=0.132 (elevated), mom_20=0.125, w4_return=small_win; geometry NOT compressed but still false negative, indicating compressed geometry is not necessary

Selected winners entity_ead73f4390 and entity_b00579f203 have HIGH px_vs_ma50 (0.185 and 0.230) with large_win outcomes, demonstrating that extended geometry can also produce winners, weakening the causal claim
falsifiable_predictions: In a validation sample, among non-B0-pick entities where px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 AND mom_20 < 0.08 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2, the large_win rate will be >= 35%, significantly exceeding the base rate for all non-picks

If a false-negative entity has compressed px_vs_ma50 < 0.05 but subsequently drops below its 50-day MA (px_vs_ma50 < 0) within 4 weeks of snapshot, the w4_return_bucket will NOT be large_win with >80% confidence

The vol_ratio_5_20 threshold of 1.2 distinguishes false-negative big winners from false-negative relative winners: FN large_win entities will have median vol_ratio < 1.2, while FN small_win entities will have median vol_ratio > 1.3
Entities with pullback_pct < -15 (deeper than FN median) but still non-picked will have lower large_win rates than entities with pullback_pct between -5 and -10, controlling for mom_20 and px_vs_ma50
policy_implications: B0 selection criteria may systematically reject valid setups by penalizing compressed near-buy-point geometry; relaxing px_vs_ma50 thresholds from current values to <0.10 could recover some false negatives
Adding a secondary filter for compressed-geometry non-picks could create a supplemental watchlist tier with independent signal generation, reducing correlation with primary B0 selections

Volume confirmation becomes critical for compressed-geometry picks: low vol_ratio_5_20 (<1.2) appears to identify stealth accumulation, while elevated vol_ratio may indicate distribution rather than base-building

The shallow-pullback false negatives (entity_de1c657364, entity_05b4c6b1f7) suggest tighter stop-loss placement is viable for this pattern since the compression itself signals limited downside from entry point

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The compressed-geometry pattern is an artifact of outcome-biased case selection: false-negative big winners were defined by future W4 returns, then their snapshot features were inspected for commonality. This creates guaranteed correlation between features and outcome, not predictive signal. The true test requires forward-looking validation on pre-selected snapshot-time entities, not post-hoc analysis of entities chosen for their future success.

attacks.issue: Definition-dependency of the false-negative label introduces look-ahead bias that invalidates all subsequent feature analysis.
attacks.why_it_matters: The method note explicitly states false negatives require 'future W4 >=8% and >=5pp above B0 selected median.' This means entities entered the FN set ONLY because they became winners. The 7 FN cases are not a random sample of compressed-geometry stocks—they are a curated set of stocks that worked. Any shared feature (low px_vs_ma50, low mom_20) is then trivially correlated with the outcome by construction, not because it causes or predicts it. The research design cannot distinguish 'this feature identifies winners' from 'we selected winners and noticed they had this feature.'

attacks.issue: The two supporting large_win FN cases (entity_535a1beed7, entity_de1c657364) are insufficient for pattern claims with n=2.
attacks.why_it_matters: The entire compressed-geometry theory rests on two entities. With n=2, any shared values are indistinguishable from random co-occurrence. The medians reported in numeric contrasts (FN median px_vs_ma50=0.056 vs SW median=0.127) pool across 7 FN cases, but only 2 are large_win. The pattern that 'compressed geometry → large_win' within the FN subset uses n=2 for the signal and n=5 for the contrast. This sample size cannot support sigma-level claims or falsifiable predictions.

attacks.issue: Contradictory cases within the same dataset falsify the necessity claim: winners do NOT require compressed geometry.
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_ead73f4390 (selected_winner, large_win) has px_vs_ma50=0.185, mom_20=0.320—8-10x above the proposed thresholds. entity_b00579f203 similarly shows px_vs_ma50=0.230, mom_20=0.230. Both are large_win winners WITHOUT compressed geometry, directly refuting the claim that compression is a causal or even common feature of winners. If extended geometry produces winners, compressed geometry is not necessary for the outcome.

attacks.issue: Contradictory cases falsify the sufficiency claim: compressed geometry does NOT produce winners.
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_8f0df3d38e has px_vs_ma50=0.048 (below 0.06 threshold), mom_20=0.176, and outcome=failure. entity_4fdc3699fd has px_vs_ma50=0.086 (slightly above), mom_20=0.185, outcome=ruin. entity_8472243e0c has px_vs_ma50=0.075, mom_20=0.242, outcome=ruin. These false-positive ruins share compressed features but produce catastrophic losses, indicating the features are not sufficient to predict winners.

attacks.issue: The mechanism conflates correlation with causation and ignores alternative explanations.
attacks.why_it_matters: Low px_vs_ma50 (<6%) and low mom_20 (<8%) are proxies for 'stock has gone sideways or down recently.' This is a classic contrarian/value signal, not a technical geometry effect. The actual mechanism may be mean-reversion or institutional underweighting of neglected stocks, not the tight consolidation thesis. If the mechanism is wrong, the policy prescriptions (relaxing B0 thresholds, adjusting stop-losses) are baseless.

attacks.issue: The vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2 threshold appears post-hoc without statistical justification.
attacks.why_it_matters: The threshold of 1.2 for vol_ratio_5_20 is not derived from theory or cross-validation; it is inferred from the two FN large_win cases having vol_ratios of 1.174 and 1.147. Post-hoc threshold optimization on n=2 guarantees in-sample fit and zero out-of-sample validity. The proposed prediction that this threshold 'distinguishes FN large_win from FN small_win' cannot be tested with the current sample.

counterexamples_to_seek: Entities at snapshot time with px_vs_ma50 < 0.06, mom_20 < 0.08, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2 that subsequently produce w4_return_bucket = 'ruin' or 'loss'
Entities at snapshot time with px_vs_ma50 < 0.06, mom_20 < 0.08 that were subsequently picked by B0 (demonstrating B0 CAN capture compressed geometry when fundamentals align)
A time-period hold-out sample: apply the compressed-geometry filter to snapshots from a different time period not represented in the discovery sample, measure actual forward win rates
Entities with low px_vs_ma50 and low mom_20 but HIGH vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.5): if vol_ratio is the true signal (stealth accumulation), high-volume compressed geometry should outperform low-volume
Sectors or market-cap strata where compressed geometry does not predict winners, indicating sector or liquidity confounding in the pattern
what_would_change_my_mind: A pre-registered forward test: define compressed geometry criteria on training data, apply to a separate hold-out sample with no outcome-based selection, and observe large_win rates significantly above base rate for non-picks
Replication in an independent dataset (different snapshot dates, different entity universe) showing the same feature-outcome correlation

A causal mechanism with supporting evidence: e.g., institutional trading data showing accumulation occurred specifically in the compressed-geometry FN cases, or options flow data showing informed buying
Demonstration that the false-negative definition does NOT introduce look-ahead bias (e.g., by defining FN status based on contemporaneous B0 selection criteria rather than future returns)
A control showing that among B0-selected winners, compressed geometry does NOT predict superior outcomes, isolating the FN-specific effect from a general compressed-geometry effect

tests.name: compressed_geometry_vs_contrarian_mechanism
tests.comparison: Conditional effect decomposition: px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 WITH high mom_20 (>0.10) vs px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 WITH low mom_20 (<0.08)
tests.success_criterion: Compressed geometry entities with elevated momentum (mom_20 > 0.10) achieve large_win rate >= compressed geometry entities with suppressed momentum (mom_20 < 0.08). This would reject the contrarian mechanism as primary.
tests.failure_criterion: Compressed geometry entities with suppressed momentum (mom_20 < 0.08) achieve large_win rate >= compressed geometry entities with elevated momentum (mom_20 > 0.10). This would support contrarian mean-reversion over compressed geometry as the operative mechanism.

tests.name: vol_ratio_independence_from_geometry
tests.comparison: Within px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 stratum: low vol_ratio_5_20 (< 1.2) vs elevated vol_ratio_5_20 (> 1.5)
tests.success_criterion: Low vol_ratio (<1.2) compressed-geometry entities have large_win rate >= elevated vol_ratio (>1.5) compressed-geometry entities by >=15pp. This would confirm vol_ratio as independent discriminating factor.
tests.failure_criterion: Elevated vol_ratio (>1.5) compressed-geometry entities achieve large_win rate >= low vol_ratio compressed-geometry entities. This would falsify the vol_ratio threshold as a mechanism component.

tests.name: fn_selection_bias_test
tests.comparison: Within-FN comparison: FN-large_win (n=2: entity_535a1beed7, entity_de1c657364) vs FN-small_win/loss (n=5: entity_df5478102d, entity_d8e8e7b814, entity_bfb308b24a, entity_ad2bfdee3f, entity_05b4c6b1f7)
tests.success_criterion: FN-large_win and FN-small_win/loss have non-overlapping feature distributions across at least 2 snapshot features (px_vs_ma50, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20). This would indicate the FN label captures genuine heterogeneity, not selection artifact.
tests.failure_criterion: FN-large_win and FN-small_win/loss have overlapping feature distributions within measurement uncertainty. This would indicate the compressed-geometry pattern is indistinguishable from noise given n=2.

tests.name: compressed_geometry_baseline_rate
tests.comparison: All non-B0-pick entities meeting compressed-geometry criteria (px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 AND mom_20 < 0.08) against all non-B0-pick entities NOT meeting criteria
tests.success_criterion: Compressed-geometry non-picks achieve large_win rate >= 2x the large_win rate of non-compressed-geometry non-picks. This would indicate the pattern has predictive value beyond FN label artifact.
tests.failure_criterion: Compressed-geometry non-picks achieve large_win rate not significantly different from non-compressed-geometry non-picks (within 95% CI overlap). This would indicate the pattern is a selection artifact of the FN definition.

tests.name: sufficiency_test_shallow_pullback
tests.comparison: Among entities with pullback_pct >= -10 (shallower than FN median of -7.3) and px_vs_ma50 < 0.08: outcome distribution across w4_return_bucket
tests.success_criterion: Shallower pullback entities have >=40% large_win rate. This would support the claim that shallow compression precedes large_win outcomes.
tests.failure_criterion: Shallower pullback entities have <20% large_win rate (equivalent to or below base rate). This would indicate shallow pullback is not sufficient for large_win.

tests.name: extended_geometry_control
tests.comparison: Entities with px_vs_ma50 > 0.15 AND mom_20 > 0.15 (extended geometry) vs compressed geometry entities (px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 AND mom_20 < 0.08)
tests.success_criterion: Extended geometry non-picks have large_win rate < compressed geometry non-picks by >=15pp. This would indicate compressed geometry is specifically predictive, not just that 'low metrics predict winners' generically.
tests.failure_criterion: Extended geometry non-picks have large_win rate >= compressed geometry non-picks. This would indicate the predictive signal is generic low-metric effect, not geometry-specific.

leakage_checks: w4_return_bucket is outcome variable only—cannot appear as predictor or selection criterion in any test
snapshot_anon is temporal identifier—cannot be used as predictive feature; only legitimate for temporal split coordination
is_b0_pick is contemporaneous selection indicator—can appear in feature list but not as outcome; ensure comparisons are within-pick-status strata or explicitly compare across strata
All feature thresholds (px_vs_ma50 < 0.06, mom_20 < 0.08, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2) must be pre-specified using researcher proposals, not optimized on current FN-large_win sample
FN label construction uses future W4 returns—tests must either (a) use only snapshot-time features or (b) compare FN subsets (large_win vs small_win) to control for selection bias
Pullback metrics (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks) are contemporaneous at snapshot—legitimate for prediction; verify no look-ahead in their calculation

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The compressed-geometry false-negative pattern (px_vs_ma50 < 0.06, mom_20 < 0.08, vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2) is present in n=2 FN-large_win cases but cannot be distinguished from outcome-biased selection artifact given the FN definition's reliance on future W4 returns. Selected winners with extended geometry (px_vs_ma50 up to 0.230) demonstrate the pattern is not necessary; false-positive ruins with compressed geometry (entity_8f0df3d38e, mom_20=0.176) demonstrate it is not sufficient. The FN-large_win vs FN-small_win/loss feature comparison (n=2 vs n=5) has insufficient discriminative power. The proposed vol_ratio threshold of 1.2 is post-hoc on n=2 with no validation. A non-FN benchmark test (compressed_geometry_baseline_rate) is needed to establish whether the pattern has predictive value independent of the FN label's construction.
falsifiers: A pre-registered hold-out test where entities with px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 AND mom_20 < 0.08 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2 achieve large_win rate < 2x the non-compressed-geometry non-pick baseline would refute predictive value
Finding a single non-B0 entity at snapshot with compressed-geometry features (all three metrics) that subsequently produces w4_return_bucket = 'ruin' would falsify sufficiency

Finding a B0-selected entity with the same compressed-geometry features that produces large_win would show B0 can capture the pattern when fundamentals align, invalidating the 'systematic rejection' claim

Demonstration that FN-large_win and FN-small_win/loss have statistically indistinguishable feature distributions across px_vs_ma50, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and up_day_ratio_20 would confirm the pattern is noise given current sample size
A forward validation (pre-registered criteria applied to future snapshot) showing compressed-geometry entities have large_win rate equal to base rate would refute the mechanism
actionable_design_principles: Prioritize the compressed_geometry_baseline_rate test using ALL non-B0 entities (not FN subset) to determine if the pattern exists independent of outcome-biased selection
Do not construct vol_ratio_5_20 thresholds from n=2 FN-large_win cases; any threshold requires forward validation on pre-selected sample
Treat compressed geometry as potentially sufficient (not necessary) condition: winners exist without it, but the subset of compressed-geometry non-picks may have elevated win rates
Distinguish contrarian mechanism (mean-reversion on neglected stocks) from geometric consolidation mechanism; the evidence does not currently adjudicate this
Acknowledge within-FN heterogeneity: entity_05b4c6b1f7 and entity_de1c657364 are FN-large_win despite different pullback depths and up_day_ratios, suggesting the mechanism is not uniform
The policy implication about relaxing B0 px_vs_ma50 thresholds is premature without establishing the compressed-geometry pattern has genuine predictive value in pre-registered validation

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Run compressed_geometry_baseline_rate as the primary validation test before any policy derivation
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This test uses non-FN non-picks as control, avoiding the outcome-biased selection that undermines FN-subset analysis
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Determines whether compressed geometry has selection-independent predictive value; if baseline test fails, no downstream policy is justified

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Segment the non-B0 population by vol_ratio_5_20 (< 1.2 vs > 1.5) within compressed geometry to test vol_ratio independence
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Separates vol_ratio as potential confounding variable from pure geometry effect; both FN-large_win cases have low vol_ratio, but this may be coincidence at n=2
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: If elevated vol_ratio compressed-geometry non-picks match low vol_ratio large_win rates, the vol_ratio threshold is not a mechanism component

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Construct a mean-reversion control: entities with px_vs_ma50 < 0 AND mom_20 < 0 (below both MAs) vs compressed geometry (px_vs_ma50 < 0.06, mom_20 < 0.08, both positive)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Tests whether FN-large_win outcomes are due to contrarian mean-reversion from oversold conditions rather than tight consolidation geometry
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: If mean-reversion entities (entity_ad2bfdee3f) achieve similar large_win rates, the geometry-specific mechanism claim is weakened

cycles.question: Study false-negative non-picks that become large winners under volume confirmation/dry-up; identify repeated PIT-visible precursors. Do not explain outcomes using information unavailable at snapshot time.

researcher.mechanism_claim: False-negative non-picks that become large W4 winners exhibit a 'quiet-coil / volume-dry-up absorption' signature at the PIT snapshot: subdued 20-day momentum (mom_20 ~0.03–0.07), 5d-vs-20d relative volume hovering near or just above 1.0 (~0.96–1.17), shallow recent pullback depth (pullback_pct ≈ -7% vs -16% for selected winners), near-flat ma10/ma20 slopes, and modest price extension above MAs (px_vs_ma50 ≈ 0.02–0.06). This signature reflects supply absorption and constructive basing rather than the explosive momentum/volatility the B0 momentum-threshold filter requires, so these candidates are systematically rejected despite being structurally set up for breakout.
evidence_for: All three false-negative → large_win cases (entity_535a1beed7, entity_de1c657364, entity_05b4c6b1f7) share mom_20 in the 0.028–0.070 band, well below the selected_winner median of 0.163 (standardized delta -1.00).
vol_ratio_5_20 for FN large winners ranges 0.964–1.174, sitting below the selected_winner median of 1.424 (standardized delta -1.05). entity_05b4c6b1f7 has explicit volume dry-up at 0.964 (<1.0).
Pullback_pct median for false_negatives is -7.3% vs -15.9% for selected_winners (standardized delta +0.64) — shallow time-based basing rather than deep correction, consistent with absorption.
entity_de1c657364 shows 8-week pullback duration with only -7.3% depth — time-without-price-decline structure where vol_ratio_5_20 of 1.147 implies orderly absorption, not distribution.
up_day_ratio_20 for FN large winners = 0.5–0.65 (median 0.5), with ma10_slope_5 and ma20_slope_5 near zero or slightly positive — neutral-to-mildly-bullish tape, neither euphoric nor broken.
ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct for FN large winners is small positive (0.009–0.024), indicating tight, non-extended entry rather than chase.
Numeric contrasts ranking confirms the top discriminating features (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50) all load on a 'calm tape' cluster that separates FN from SW.
evidence_against: entity_bfb308b24a is a false_negative → loss with structurally similar features (mom_20=0.027, vol_ratio_5_20=1.187, up_day_ratio=0.45) — the quiet-coil signature contains true decay cases, not just breakouts; precision is low.

entity_ad2bfdee3f (FN→small_win) has NEGATIVE mom_20 (-0.046) and NEGATIVE px_vs_ma50 (-0.033), showing the dry-up signature is asymmetric and many quietly-rotating names continue sideways rather than break out.

false_positive_ruin cases (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c, etc.) sometimes share elevated vol_ratio_5_20 with selected_winners — so elevated volume alone is not a clean discriminator between winner and ruin, undermining a simple 'volume confirms everything' rule.

entity_2f86543bf6 (selected_winner, large_win) has ma20_slope_5 = -0.0078 and mom_20 = -0.008 with vol_ratio=1.56 — selected_winner cohort includes negative-momentum names, so the 'positive momentum required' frame is already imperfect at the B0 boundary.

entity_bfb308b24a's loss outcome alongside its base_duration absent data means pullback/volume signatures without confirming base quality produce asymmetric losses, limiting the standalone utility of the quiet-coil filter.
falsifiable_predictions: Among non-picks with vol_ratio_5_20 in [0.9, 1.2] AND pullback_pct ≥ -10% AND mom_20 in [0.02, 0.08] AND up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.5, the conditional W4 large_win rate should exceed 40% (vs unconditional FN rate implied by 2/7 ≈ 29% in this slice).

Volume dry-up (vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0) at snapshot combined with shallow recent base depth (pullback_pct > -8%) should produce positive expected forward return over the next 4 weeks, while dry-up with deeper prior drawdowns should NOT.

Adding a 'quiet-coil' candidate bucket (vol_ratio_5_20 in [0.9,1.2], pullback_pct in [-10%, -3%], ma10_slope_5 in [-0.01, 0.03]) as a parallel input to the existing B0 momentum filter should increase total large_win captures by ≥15% with no more than proportional increase in losses.

If the mechanism is causal (absorption → breakout), then increasing lookback-window on vol_ratio (e.g., 5d vs 60d) should strengthen the dry-up signal rather than weaken it; falsified if dry-up effect disappears at longer lookbacks.
Selected_winners should consistently exhibit vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.3 OR mom_20 > 0.10; if SW cohort contains many names with both below these thresholds, the dichotomy framing is invalid.
policy_implications: Replace the implicit single-mode momentum threshold with a two-bucket candidate generator: (a) existing explosive-momentum mode (mom_20 > 0.10, vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.3) and (b) quiet-coil absorption mode (mom_20 in [0.02,0.08], vol_ratio_5_20 in [0.9,1.2], shallow pullback ≥ -10%, ma10_slope near-flat).
Risk-size the quiet-coil bucket smaller than the explosive bucket because precision is lower (loss cases like entity_bfb308b24a contaminate the same feature space).
Use base quality (pullback_duration_weeks ≥ 4 with shallow depth, plus constructive ma10/ma20 slopes) as a precondition for the quiet-coil bucket to suppress rot cases like entity_ad2bfdee3f.

Avoid using vol_ratio_5_20 as a hard veto in either direction — both 'volume confirmation' (SW median 1.42) and 'dry-up' (entity_05b4c6b1f7 at 0.96) appear in winners; treat volume regime as a categorical feature rather than a monotonic filter.

Separate the prediction problem (which non-pick has coil-then-break potential) from the portfolio problem (how much size, when to add) — the archaeological evidence supports the predictive claim but does not yet support equal-sizing across the two buckets.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The 'quiet-coil / volume-dry-up absorption' signature is a label-threshold artifact, not a reproducible PIT precursor. The false-negative-to-large-winner cohort is defined by an ex-post W4 outcome threshold (>=8% AND >=5pp above B0 median) that mechanically guarantees the discovered features (low mom_20, shallow pullback, low vol_ratio) load onto a contrast axis; when compared against the operationally relevant baseline (false_positive_ruin and FN→loss), the 'calm tape' cluster fails to discriminate. The pattern is also dominated by a single snapshot date (snap_71486ed83c), so 'repeated PIT precursors' is a within-date artifact masquerading as a structural rule.

attacks.issue: Wrong baseline: the prior claim contrasts FN-large-winners against selected_winners (SW). The informative comparison is FN-large-win vs FN-loss (entity_bfb308b24a). On that axis, the discriminating gap collapses: mom_20 is 0.027 (FN-loss) vs 0.028–0.070 (FN-large-win), vol_ratio_5_20 is 1.187 (FN-loss) vs 0.964–1.174 (FN-large-win), ma10_slope is 0.012 (FN-loss) vs 0.004–0.030 (FN-large-win). The loss case sits inside the large-win feature box. 'Quiet coil' does not separate win from loss within the FN class.
attacks.why_it_matters: Policy implication #2 ('risk-size quiet-coil smaller because precision is lower') concedes the feature box is contaminated; the proposed two-bucket generator therefore has near-zero separation power on the only margin a portfolio can exploit (FN-large vs FN-loss).

attacks.issue: Label is threshold-defined ex post: FN-big-winner requires W4 >= 8% AND >= 5pp above B0 selected median. By construction, mom_20, px_vs_ma20, and px_vs_ma50 (features known to correlate with forward returns) are guaranteed to load negatively in the FN direction. The standardized deltas (-1.0, -0.85, -0.58) are therefore not 'discoveries' but tautologies of the threshold against the same forward-return-correlated inputs.
attacks.why_it_matters: Any feature with even weak serial correlation in 4-week returns will appear 'discriminating.' The claim has not separated a predictive mechanism from the mathematical consequence of thresholding the dependent variable against features that are forward-return proxies.

attacks.issue: Single-snapshot domination: snap_71486ed83c supplies >= 6 of 27 cases spanning FN-large-win, FN-loss, FN-small-win, SW, and FPR. The 'repeated PIT precursors' are largely a market-regime signature (one date, one tape state) reproduced across multiple entities, not an entity-level repeatable pattern. Cross-snapshot generalization is unsupported because only 2–3 snapshots contribute meaningful FN cases.
attacks.why_it_matters: A 'PIT-visible precursor' claim requires the precursor to recur across independent market states. Concentrating evidence in one date invalidates the generalization step and leaves the 'absorption' narrative undertested against alternative regimes (e.g., rising-rate environments, narrow breadth).

attacks.issue: Null handling biases the contrast upward: pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct are null for >50% of FN cases and most SW cases. The medians reported (-7.3%, 4 weeks for FN; -15.9%, 5.5 weeks for SW) are computed on a much smaller effective sample and on a non-random subset (non-nulls likely correlate with longer-tenured entities that entered base, biasing toward constructive pullback signatures).
attacks.why_it_matters: Selective missingness inflates the apparent gap on pullback-based features. The 'shallow-basing' claim is fragile to any re-imputation that assigns nulls plausibly (e.g., short-history entities that never had a pullback).

attacks.issue: Absence of momentum is not evidence of absorption: mom_20 in [0.02, 0.08] combined with vol_ratio near 1.0 is equally consistent with a stock that is simply uncorrelated with the market over a 4-week window — i.e., a zero-mean noise process. The base rate of small positive W4 returns is high in any broad cross-section; 'quiet' names will occasionally print +8% by chance. The 'absorption → breakout' mechanism is unfalsified but also unsupportable from 2–3 cases.
attacks.why_it_matters: Without a defined null (what fraction of quiet names randomly achieve W4 >= 8%?), the conditional probability claims ('40% large_win rate in the quiet-coil slice') are not meaningful. 2/7 = 28.6% in this slice is statistically indistinguishable from the unconditional FN rate.

attacks.issue: The 'calm tape' cluster is shared with false_positive_ruin: entity_3472243e0c (FPR) has mom_20=0.242, vol_ratio=1.21, up_day=0.65; entity_b6bcccdf6a (FPR) has mom_20=0.176, vol_ratio=1.31. Several FPR cases have higher momentum and volume than the FN-large-win cases. If 'volume confirmation' can't separate winner from ruin within B0 picks (as the researcher concedes), then 'volume dry-up' cannot reliably separate FN-large from FN-loss; the volume feature is demonstrably non-monotonic and regime-dependent.
attacks.why_it_matters: This contradicts the clean 'calm cluster separates FN from SW' framing. It also undermines the proposed categorical treatment of volume regime (policy #4), because volume within the FN class has no demonstrated directionality.

attacks.issue: Ma20_slope_5 sign flip across the cohort: entity_535a1beed7 (FN-big-winner) has ma20_slope=-0.005 and ma10_slope=0.004 (mixed signs), and entity_ad2bfdee3f (FN-small-win) has both negative. 'Near-flat slopes' is a verbal smoothing of genuinely contradictory subcases; the proposed precondition 'constructive ma10/ma20 slopes' is not empirically pinned down.
attacks.why_it_matters: A precondition that admits sign-mismatched slopes is not operationalizable. The bucket cannot be implemented without arbitrary sign thresholds, which reintroduces discretion.

attacks.issue: Standardized deltas of -1.0 in a 7-vs-11 comparison: with n=7 false_negatives and n=11 selected_winners, the standard error of a rank-based standardized difference is large enough that the reported deltas are consistent with no effect. No confidence intervals, no permutation p-values, no bootstrap are reported; the rank is presented as if it implied statistical confidence.
attacks.why_it_matters: An honest read of '|standardized delta| ≈ 1.0 in n≈10 per arm' is 'suggestive but unconfirmed.' Stating falsifiable predictions like '40% large_win rate' from this evidence overstates certainty and risks capital deployment on noise.

counterexamples_to_seek: False-negative cases outside snap_71486ed83c that achieved W4 large_win and test whether the 'calm coil' features recur in an independent tape state. Currently the cross-snapshot FN-large sample is ~1–2 cases.

FN→loss cases with shallower pullback and lower momentum than the FN→large-win cases (i.e., look-alikes that failed). If entity_bfb308b24a has near-twins with mom_20<0.02 or pullback_pct>-5% that still lost, the absorption mechanism is falsified.

Selected_winners with vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.0 and mom_20 < 0.05 — these would contradict the 'SW requires momentum/vol confirmation' dichotomy. Existing data already shows entity_2f86543bf6 (SW, large_win) has mom_20=-0.008, undermining the dichotomy.

A matched cohort of B0-non-picked names with identical quiet-coil features that did NOT break out within 4 weeks. If the quiet-coil feature box has many FN-loss or FN-flat names, precision is single-digit and the bucket is un-tradeable.
False_positive_ruin cases with low vol_ratio and low mom_20 — if ruins can be quiet too, then 'quiet' is not constructive absorption; it is just low-information tape.
Snapshot-by-snapshot re-computation of the medians excluding snap_71486ed83c. If the standardized deltas collapse outside that date, the 'repeated precursor' claim is invalidated.
what_would_change_my_mind: Out-of-sample replication: a held-out discovery set (no snapshot overlap with the train evidence) where the quiet-coil bucket produces a large_win rate statistically distinguishable (p < 0.05 with bootstrap CI excluding zero) from the unconditional non-pick rate. Current 2/7 is indistinguishable from noise.

FN-large-win vs FN-loss separation on the same feature set using only features available at snapshot. Currently the within-FN discrimination gap is smaller than the between-cohort gap; I would need a classifier that ranks FN names by W4 return with monotonic lift across quiet-coil score deciles.

Demonstration that the 'absorption' mechanism is not a restatement of the outcome threshold: e.g., a contemporaneous third variable (order-flow imbalance, short-interest change, sector rotation) that explains both the calm tape and the forward return, with the calm-tape features losing significance once it is conditioned out.

Robustness to alternative FN definitions. If W4 >= 6% or W4 >= 10% (perturbing the threshold) eliminates the 'quiet coil' cluster, the signature is threshold-fragile and should be labeled UNRESOLVED rather than mechanistically named.

Evidence that the pattern holds when null pullback values are imputed under multiple reasonable rules (e.g., median, zero, base-duration-conditional mean). If the median pullback_pct gap flips sign under any plausible imputation, the shallow-basing claim is artifact, not signal.

A clearly defined quiet-coil bucket with documented precision and recall against FN-large-win and against the universe of non-picks. Without these two numbers, the bucket cannot be evaluated as either a filter or a parallel input.

tests.name: T1_within_FN_class_lift_test
tests.comparison: Among is_b0_pick=false entities only, partition by quiet-coil composite (vol_ratio_5_20 in [0.9,1.2], mom_20 in [0.02,0.08], pullback_pct in [-10%,-3%]). Compare W4 large_win rate of in-bucket FN vs out-of-bucket FN. Baseline is the operationally relevant arm: FN-loss (e.g., entity_bfb308b24a), not SW.
tests.success_criterion: In-bucket FN W4 large_win rate exceeds out-of-bucket FN W4 large_win rate by >=15pp with bootstrap 95% CI on the difference excluding zero (n_resamples>=1000, stratified by snapshot).
tests.failure_criterion: Lift <=5pp or CI includes zero, OR the in-bucket FN-loss rate equals or exceeds the FN large_win rate (precision<=50%).

tests.name: T2_snapshot_stratified_replication
tests.comparison: Recompute FN-vs-SW median deltas and standardized deltas on (a) the full sample, (b) snap_71486ed83c excluded, (c) snap_71486ed83c only. Check whether the 'calm cluster' loading on the contrast axis persists outside the dominant snapshot.
tests.success_criterion: Standardized delta on up_day_ratio_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 retains |dz|>=0.5 with sign preserved when snap_71486ed83c is excluded. Cross-snapshot FN-large sample n>=3.
tests.failure_criterion: |dz| drops below 0.3 OR sign flips OR cross-snapshot FN-large n<2. If any of these hold, the 'repeated precursor' claim is single-regime artifact.

tests.name: T3_threshold_perturbation_falsifier
tests.comparison: Re-label FN-big-winner at W4 thresholds of 6%, 8% (current), and 10%, and at relative thresholds of 3pp and 5pp above B0 selected median. For each perturbation, recompute median feature contrast (FN-large vs FN-loss and FN-large vs SW) on the same three features.
tests.success_criterion: The qualitative ordering (FN-large lower on mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50 than SW) is preserved at every threshold perturbation, with monotonic sign.
tests.failure_criterion: Sign flips or magnitude shrinks below |dz|=0.3 at any perturbation. If fragile, the mechanism claim is threshold-defined and should be reported as UNRESOLVED.

tests.name: T4_volume_regime_directionality
tests.comparison: Within FN class, bin by vol_ratio_5_20 into <0.9, [0.9,1.0), [1.0,1.1), [1.1,1.2), [1.2,1.3), >=1.3 and report W4 large_win rate per bin. Test monotonicity (Spearman rho) and the categorical 'dry-up' hypothesis (peak at 0.9-1.2).
tests.success_criterion: Either (a) monotonic decreasing relationship with rho<=-0.6, OR (b) categorical peak in [0.9,1.2] bin with large_win rate at least 2x the surrounding bins. Must hold separately for snap_71486ed83c subset and non-dominant snapshots.
tests.failure_criterion: Large_win rate is non-monotonic and not peaked in [0.9,1.2], OR the relationship inverts across snapshots. This invalidates both 'volume confirms' and 'volume dry-up' as monotonic rules.

tests.name: T5_slope_sign_precondition_filter
tests.comparison: Within the quiet-coil bucket, stratify by slope-sign class: (i) both positive, (ii) both negative, (iii) mixed. Compare W4 large_win and W4 loss rates. Tests whether 'constructive slope precondition' is operationalizable.
tests.success_criterion: Class (i) shows >=20pp higher large_win rate than class (ii) or (iii), AND class (i) n>=3 with at least 1 large_win.
tests.failure_criterion: Class (i) and mixed-sign classes produce similar large_win rates (within 10pp), indicating the slope-sign precondition is discretionary rather than empirically pinned.

tests.name: T6_pullback_null_imputation_sensitivity
tests.comparison: Re-impute null pullback_pct under three rules: (a) drop nulls (current), (b) impute 0 (no pullback observed), (c) impute -25 (deep correction assumption). Recompute FN-vs-SW median delta on pullback_pct for each.
tests.success_criterion: Direction of the median delta (FN larger / shallower than SW) is preserved across all three imputations, with magnitude >=5pp.
tests.failure_criterion: Direction flips or magnitude shrinks below 2pp under any imputation rule. The shallow-basing claim is artifact of selective missingness.

tests.name: T7_lookback_horizon_separability
tests.comparison: If 'absorption' is the mechanism, dry-up should be stronger at longer-term relative-volume horizons (5d/60d) than at the short 5d/20d horizon currently used. Recompute dry-up signal using a longer-horizon analog if available, OR test whether 5d/20d dry-up names also exhibit low up_day_ratio_20 and low realized volatility features consistent with orderly absorption rather than random noise.
tests.success_criterion: Dry-up bucket names have atr_14_pct and rv_20 below the SW median (constructive compression), with dry-up names showing |z|<=0.5 on both. This separates absorption from random-walk noise.
tests.failure_criterion: Dry-up names show atr_14_pct and rv_20 at or above the FN-loss median, indicating the 'calm tape' is indistinguishable from low-information noise rather than constructive compression.

leakage_checks: Verify every feature in the test allowlist is computable from price/volume series at or before the snapshot timestamp only. Reject any feature that uses post-snapshot W4 return, post-snapshot IBD entries, or future-window aggregations.
Verify 'is_b0_pick' is treated as a class label, not a feature, in discrimination tests T1, T4, T5, T7. It must not enter the composite score or precondition logic.
Verify 'w4_return_bucket' and 'outcome_label' are used only as evaluation labels, never as inputs to the quiet-coil composite or any precondition.
Verify snapshot_anon is used only for stratification in T2, never as a model input or as a substitute for date/ticker identity.
Verify no test uses 'pullback_duration_weeks' and 'pullback_pct' together when either is null for >50% of the comparison arm, unless null handling is the explicit object of the test (T6).
Verify entity_anon is never used as a grouping key beyond snapshot stratification; cross-entity pooling must respect snapshot independence.

Verify T3 perturbations do not introduce a new feature set, only re-label existing entities; if any perturbation creates an empty arm, the test must report UNRESOLVED for that arm rather than silently passing.

Verify T7 does not request a new feature absent from the allowlist; if the longer-horizon vol_ratio is unavailable, the test must degrade to a within-feature consistency check on existing features and report this as a limitation.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: There is a reproducible descriptive contrast between the false-negative class and the selected-winner class on a 'calm-tape' cluster (lower mom_20, lower vol_ratio_5_20, shallower pullback_pct, near-flat ma10/ma20 slopes, modest extension above MAs) at the PIT snapshot. However, three independent critiques prevent promotion from descriptive contrast to mechanism: (a) the discriminating features are mathematically guaranteed to load negatively on the FN arm because the FN label is threshold-defined against W4 returns that the same features proxy; (c) entity_bfb308b24a (FN-loss) sits inside the FN-large-win feature box on every 'quiet-coil' dimension, so within-class lift is unestablished; (b) snap_71486ed83c contributes >=6 of 27 cases and at least 2 of 3 FN-large-win cases, making the 'repeated PIT precursor' indistinguishable from a single-regime tape artifact. The 'absorption → breakout' narrative is one of several readings consistent with the data; it has not been separated from 'low-momentum names occasionally print +8% by chance' or 'threshold-defined tautology'.
falsifiers: T1 (within-FN lift): in-bucket FN W4 large_win rate must exceed out-of-bucket FN W4 large_win rate by >=15pp with bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero; if precision (FN-large / (FN-large + FN-loss)) within the quiet-coil box is <=50%, the bucket is not operationally separable from loss and the mechanism claim collapses. This test has not been executed and is the gating criterion.

T2 (cross-snapshot replication): exclude snap_71486ed83c and verify the up_day_ratio_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 standardized deltas retain |dz|>=0.5 with preserved sign; cross-snapshot FN-large n must be >=3. Currently FN-large n is 3 total with >=2 from snap_71486ed83c, so the 'repeated' qualifier is currently unsupported.

T3 (threshold perturbation): at W4 threshold of 6% instead of 8%, and at relative threshold of 3pp instead of 5pp, the qualitative FN < SW ordering on mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50 must hold. Any sign flip or magnitude drop below |dz|=0.3 indicates threshold-defined tautology rather than independent mechanism.

T6 (pullback null re-imputation): under impute-0 and impute-deep-correction rules, the 'FN shallower than SW' direction on pullback_pct must be preserved with magnitude >=5pp. Selective missingness (null pullback fields concentrated in short-tenure entities) currently biases the contrast upward.

Volume-feature directionality (T4): within FN, vol_ratio_5_20 must be either monotonically decreasing in large_win rate (rho<=-0.6) or peaked in [0.9,1.2] at >=2x surrounding bins; if non-monotonic and not peaked, 'volume dry-up' is not an actionable regime hypothesis.

Absorption-vs-noise separability (T7): FN-large-win names must show atr_14_pct and rv_20 below the SW median (constructive compression). If atr/rv are at or above SW median, the 'quiet tape' is indistinguishable from low-information noise rather than supply absorption.
actionable_design_principles: Do not promote the FN-vs-SW descriptive contrast to a causal 'absorption' mechanism without first running the within-FN lift test (T1). The 29% large_win rate in the quiet-coil slice is indistinguishable from the unconditional FN rate and from base-rate chance.

Treat volume regime (vol_ratio_5_20) as a categorical rather than monotonic feature: 'volume confirms' (SW median 1.42) and 'volume dry-up' (entity_05b4c6b1f7 at 0.964) both appear in W4 winners, and FPR cases (entity_3472243e0c, entity_b6bcccdf6a) overlap on the same dimensions.

Stratify by snapshot before pooling any cross-sectional comparison; snap_71486ed83c dominance means any pooled statistic is at risk of single-tape conflation. Snapshot identity must never be a model input, but snapshot-conditioned normalization is required for feature comparison.
