tests.success_criterion: FN-vs-FN standardized distance is at most 0.75× the median selected_winner-vs-selected_winner distance, indicating a tighter coherent signature than the winners themselves.
tests.failure_criterion: FN-vs-FN distance exceeds the 75th percentile of winner-vs-winner pairwise distances — the two FNs disagree on key claimed features by more than is typical within the winner class, falsifying 'coherent signature'.

tests.name: composite_ruin_contamination_count
tests.comparison: Apply the joint constraint mom_20<0.06 AND vol_ratio_5_20<1.20 AND 0.45<=up_day_ratio_20<=0.70 to the 8 false_positive_ruin entities and to the false_negative_big_winner entities; report capture rate per group.
tests.success_criterion: Zero of 8 false_positive_ruin entities satisfy the joint constraint while both false_negative_big_winner entities satisfy it — composite perfectly discriminates.
tests.failure_criterion: Two or more false_positive_ruin entities satisfy the joint constraint — composite cannot distinguish latent winners from latent ruins at the signal level, regardless of how it performs on winners.

tests.name: pullback_structure_separation_non_null_only
tests.comparison: Restrict to entities with non-null pullback fields: false_negative entities with non-null pullback (entity_df5478102d, entity_bfb308b24a, entity_de1c657364; n=3) versus selected_winner entities with non-null pullback (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_8ad5cd4795, entity_2c58cebc59, entity_3adc078f01, entity_ccc90a671f, entity_55c2da490e; n=6). Compute medians per group.
tests.success_criterion: FN median pullback_duration_weeks exceeds winner median by at least 2 weeks AND FN median base_mbox_count >= winner median AND |FN median base_depth_pct| < |winner median base_depth_pct| — i.e. longer, denser, shallower bases.
tests.failure_criterion: Either the duration gap is <2 weeks OR the FN median base_mbox_count is below the winner median OR |FN base_depth_pct| is not smaller than |winner base_depth_pct|. A failure on any leg falsifies the 'extended shallow base' substrate claim as a necessary feature.

tests.name: entry_footprint_separation_fn_vs_ruin
tests.comparison: Compare false_negative_big_winner entities (n=2) versus false_positive_ruin entities (n=8) on the three entry-context features. Predicted by the mechanism: FNs should have a quieter entry footprint (lower volume ratio, close nearer day midpoint, tighter breakout range).
tests.success_criterion: FN median ibd_entry_volume_ratio is at least 0.30 below ruin median AND FN median ibd_entry_close_position is at least 0.05 below ruin median — entry footprint alone separates latent winners from latent ruins.
tests.failure_criterion: FN median ibd_entry_volume_ratio is within 0.10 of ruin median, OR FN median ibd_entry_close_position exceeds ruin median — ruins share the FN entry profile, so the entry-footprint angle cannot substitute for the composite.

tests.name: within_snapshot_winner_vs_fn_incoherence
tests.comparison: Within snap_71486ed83c, compute standardized 3-D distance between the selected_winner entity_2c58cebc59 (mom_20=0.320, vol_ratio_5_20=1.619, px_vs_ma50=0.170) and each of the two false_negative_big_winner entities in the same snapshot. Then compute the distance between the two FNs themselves. Compare ratios.
tests.success_criterion: Distance from selected_winner to either FN is at least 1.5× the FN-to-FN distance — within-snapshot winners and FNs are more different from each other than FNs are from each other, supporting the skeptic's claim that the snapshot does not host a homogeneous regime.
tests.failure_criterion: Selected_winner-to-FN distance is within 1.2× of FN-to-FN distance — the picked winner and the missed winners in the same snapshot share a recognizable profile, consistent with a shared regime that the B0 filter only partially captured.

leakage_checks: outcome_label and w4_return_bucket appear only as grouping/target variables; they must never enter the feature list of any test.

is_b0_pick is a downstream decision output, not a PIT input feature; it must not be used as a feature in any test or as a grouping variable that conditions the test population beyond the pre-specified entity selection.
snapshot_anon may be used only as a grouping key for population restriction; it must not be treated as a feature and no snapshot-identifying string may be encoded numerically as a feature.
entity_anon is identity and must not be used as a feature; entity selection within groups must be pre-specified by outcome_label membership, not by ad-hoc inspection.
Pullback fields with null values must remain null in every aggregation; no imputation to zero, no exclusion of null entities without explicit pre-specification of the non-null subset.

All momentum features (mom_20, mom_60, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, ma50_slope_10) and base features (base_mbox_count, base_duration_weeks, base_depth_pct) must be verified to be computed from data dated at or before snapshot_anon; any feature that references post-snapshot returns invalidates the test.
ibd_entry_* features reference entry-day data only and must not incorporate post-entry price action; if any entry feature is undefined for a given entity it must be flagged before inclusion.
Standardization (median, MAD) for any distance-based test must be computed on the comparison group specified in the test, not on a pooled sample that includes the units being measured.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: A provisional pattern exists among false-negative large winners: muted 20-day momentum, below-average short-term volume expansion, and modest extension above the trigger. One case resembles a quiet drift with missing pullback fields, while the other shows an eight-week shallow pullback, so the cases share some state features but not a clearly coherent structural profile. The frozen data contains no industry-membership, sector-flow, sector-relative-strength, or portfolio-capacity variables, so industry concentration cannot be identified as the causal mechanism. Repeatedness is also unestablished because only two entities meet the explicit false-negative-big-winner definition, and the broader false-negative group contains losses and small winners. Any policy should therefore be framed as a constrained out-of-sample experiment, not as evidence that a sector-driven quiet-base precursor has been discovered.
falsifiers: On a chronological held-out sample, the proposed low-momentum and low-volume precursor does not achieve a large-win rate or lift above the unconditional non-pick large-win base rate at a prespecified coverage level.

Within the same held-out snapshots, adding industry-concentration or sector-relative-strength confirmation does not improve ranking, coverage, calibration, or large-win precision beyond the stock-level precursor variables alone.
After null pullback fields are excluded, the three observed false-negative big winners do not form a more coherent base structure than matched non-pick controls.

Prospectively relaxing the B0 thresholds captures the expected additional winners but produces a statistically or economically material increase in losses, ruins, or drawdowns that offsets the recovered winners.
The apparent signature disappears when snapshot clustering, regime, industry, or exposure concentration is added as a fixed effect or when the comparison is restricted to contemporaneous candidates.
A materially larger discovery set contains no recurring cell characterized by low mom_20, low vol_ratio_5_20, and small extension above the trigger among false-negative large winners.
Capacity-aware backtests show that the proposed candidates cannot be entered or exited at the modeled prices after spreads, liquidity constraints, position limits, and turnover are applied.
actionable_design_principles: Treat null pullback observations as unknown rather than evidence of a quiet or extended base; preserve missingness and use null-aware branches or explicit non-null analyses.

Define industry concentration prospectively using only PIT-available industry classification and contemporaneous sector breadth, flow, dispersion, or relative-strength measures; do not infer it from a selected-winner count alone.
Use chronological, snapshot-grouped validation to prevent the two large-winner false negatives in snap_71486ed83c from determining rules that are then evaluated on the same snapshot.
Evaluate the stock-level precursor jointly against matched non-picks and false-positive ruins, reporting large-win lift, loss capture, precision, coverage, and calibration rather than case anecdotes.
Require sector confirmation before relaxing B0 momentum thresholds; do not deploy the relaxation as an unconditional low-momentum screen.

Separate stock-selection rules from portfolio construction by testing expected alpha and hit rate first, then applying liquidity, participation, volatility, correlation, and capacity constraints in a second stage.
Prefer continuous ranking or partial dependence analysis over a hard composite whose thresholds can be satisfied on opposite sides of nearly every cutoff.
Freeze all features, transformations, null handling, snapshot definitions, and candidate-universe rules before examining the held-out outcomes.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Define a null-aware quiet-drift candidate branch requiring low mom_20, low vol_ratio_5_20, and small ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, but only permit relaxed eligibility when a contemporaneous PIT sector-confirmation condition is active.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This captures the recurring weak individual-confirmation pattern without converting missing pullback data into a positive structural signal and without asserting that industry concentration is already measured.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Initially cap exposure using existing liquidity and volatility limits; sector confirmation must not bypass capacity checks. Estimate impact and achievable position size in the execution-stage backtest.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Create a shallow-pullback branch for candidates with observed pullback data and prohibit inference when pullback_duration_weeks or pullback_pct is null.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The observed eight-week, minus-7.3% pullback is one of the few concrete structural precedents, but another big winner has no observed pullback record, making null-sensitive branching essential.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Use branch-specific position limits because shallow, longer-duration structures may carry different gap, turnover, and exit-liquidity behavior from confirmed breakouts.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Run an out-of-sample regime-overlay experiment that compares relaxed and baseline B0 rules within strata defined by contemporaneous sector breadth, sector dispersion, and sector relative strength.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This tests whether any incremental value is genuinely attributable to an industry-concentration regime rather than merely replicating a stock-level quiet-drift effect.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Measure whether the overlay changes portfolio concentration, turnover, and drawdown after industry and position caps; predictive lift alone is insufficient for deployment.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Replace the hard composite with a monotonic precursor score validated for incremental lift over snapshot, industry, momentum, and volatility baselines.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: A continuous score avoids dependence on arbitrary joint cutoffs and directly tests whether the apparent pattern generalizes beyond two heterogeneous big winners.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Translate scores into positions only after applying liquidity, participation, volatility, and concentration constraints; keep score generation independent of portfolio-size rules.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Add a ruin-contamination gate that requires the candidate to beat matched weak-momentum ruins on structure, breadth, or sector confirmation before inclusion.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The frozen ruins overlap the proposed quiet signature, so the gate tests whether structural or regime information can distinguish latent large winners from adverse low-momentum names rather than celebrating winner recall alone.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Require lower turnover and smaller initial sizing for any branch that remains materially exposed to ruin outcomes, with promotion based on incremental risk-adjusted capacity rather than hit rate.

cycles.question: For large Top1-vs-Top2 quality gap, determine when cash should dominate filling another slot. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: Under fixed 3-slot capital, a large Top1-vs-Top2 quality gap implies that Top1 carries an asymmetric, concentrated alpha payload (high mom_20, px_vs_ma50, vol_ratio_5_20, ma10_slope_5), while Top2's expected return collapses toward the false_negative_relative distribution (median mom_20 ≈ 0.058, vol_ratio_5_20 ≈ 1.18, up_day_ratio_20 = 0.5, w4_return_bucket = small_win/loss). Marginal slot-filling with Top2 (and Top3) imposes a ruin-risk cost (8/27 ≈ 30% false_positive_ruin rate among B0-style triggers) without compensating expected value, so cash dominates the marginal slot when the Top1-Top2 gap exceeds the realized median feature delta between selected_winner and false_negative archetypes (standardized_delta < -0.5 cluster on mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50).
evidence_for: Selected_winner archetype vs false_negative archetype shows consistent, multi-feature quality gaps: mom_20 median 0.163 vs 0.058 (delta -0.105), vol_ratio_5_20 1.42 vs 1.18, up_day_ratio_20 0.625 vs 0.50, px_vs_ma50 0.127 vs 0.056 — all PIT-observable at entry and all pointing to a 'quality gradient' that maps to large_win vs small_win/loss buckets.

Among the 19 B0-pick (is_b0_pick=true) cases in archaeology, 8 became false_positive_ruin (42% ruin rate), indicating that even threshold-passing entries carry non-trivial ruin tails; Top2 candidates are typically closer to the false_negative distribution and thus inherit non-trivial ruin probability without the upside payload.

false_negative_relative cases (5) all clustered into small_win or loss w4 buckets with mid-range mom_20 (median 0.058) and lower vol confirmation — economically, these are the 'filler' trades that consume slot capacity for negligible expectancy.

Top-pick extension cases (e.g., entity_2c58cebc59 with mom_20=0.32, vol_ratio_5_20=1.62 → large_win; entity_3adc078f01 with deep pullback -42.3% but mom_20=0.17, vol_ratio_5_20=1.14 → large_win) show that concentrated high-momentum/volume Top1s deliver outsized contribution; this is the alpha that gets diluted by slot-spreading.

Mixed case entity_6618d3e80c (false_positive_ruin|selected_winner) demonstrates that a single position can simultaneously realize ruin and selection pay, reinforcing that slot allocation is a portfolio-construction layer separate from per-name signal accuracy.
evidence_against: No direct evidence in this evidence slice quantifies the realized w4 P&L delta between a 1-position, 2-position, and 3-position portfolio built from the same candidate list — the portfolio-construction effect must be inferred indirectly.

Diversification argument: across the 11 selected_winner cases, median mom_20 = 0.163 and not all winners are concentrated mega-wins; some are 'moderate' large_wins, suggesting that even a 2nd-slot position at moderate quality could contribute non-zero expected return in benign regimes.

base_duration_weeks and base_depth_pct show smaller deltas (standardized_delta ≈ -0.42 and +0.19) — base-quality features do not discriminate as cleanly as momentum/volume, so the 'quality gap' may be feature-dependent and not universally large.
The single mixed case (1/27) hints that ruin and winner outcomes can co-occur; this complicates a clean 'Top2 = pure noise' claim and suggests regime-dependent behavior.
falsifiable_predictions: Within the same snapshot, when Top1_mom_20 - Top2_mom_20 > 0.10 AND Top1_vol_ratio_5_20 - Top2_vol_ratio_5_20 > 0.25, the W4 return of a 1-slot portfolio (Top1 only) exceeds the W4 return of a 2-slot portfolio (Top1+Top2) in >60% of matched historical episodes.

When Top1 up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.65 and Top2 up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.50, the conditional ruin probability of the Top2 slot over a 4-week horizon is at least 25% (anchored to the 8/27 false_positive_ruin baseline).

Cash allocation to the marginal 2nd or 3rd slot yields higher Sharpe than deploying Top2 when the standardized Top1-Top2 gap on the {mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50} triplet exceeds 0.5 standard deviations.

Regime test: in episodes where the snapshot's median selected_winner mom_20 > 0.20 (strong-trend regime), the alpha concentration of Top1 is even higher, and the cost of slot-spreading (measured as Top2 contribution / Top1 contribution) falls below 0.3.

Falsifier: if a 2-slot portfolio's median W4 return consistently exceeds the 1-slot portfolio's median by >3pp across the archaeology snapshots, the 'cash dominates marginal slot' claim is invalidated.
policy_implications: Define a pre-entry 'Quality Gap Score' = weighted z-score on {mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5} between Top1 and Top2; when this exceeds a calibrated threshold (e.g., +0.5σ cluster), allocate slot 2 to cash.

Treat N=1 as 'high-conviction concentration' (alpha capture mode), N=2 as 'core-satellite' (Top1 + minimal hedge or pure cash), and N=3 as 'full deployment' reserved for regimes where Top1-Top2-Top3 gaps are all sub-threshold — preserving optionality when the candidate list is shallow in quality.

Do not mechanically fill all 3 slots; the 30%+ ruin rate among B0-pick-triggered entries implies that adding a Top2 that does not clear the same trigger threshold is expected-negative in expectancy terms.

The economic meaning: N=1 maximizes per-slot alpha but maximizes variance; N=3 minimizes variance but forces inclusion of false_negative_relative-style positions; the optimal N is gap-conditional, not fixed.

Implementation: log the Top1-Top2 feature gap at every entry decision; use this gap as a switch between 'concentrate' and 'deploy' modes rather than as a soft weighting — this converts a continuous quality gradient into a discrete capacity decision.

Re-evaluate when base_duration_weeks improves (winners median 52 vs FN 44): longer bases partially compensate for lower momentum, so the abstention rule should weight momentum/volume gaps more heavily than base-quality gaps.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The cash-dominates-marginal-slot rule is wrong because (a) the 30% ruin rate is conditional on already-failing archaeology cases and is therefore an inflated, selected subsample, not the unconditional ruin rate of B0 picks; (b) Top2 is by construction NOT drawn from the false_negative distribution — it passed the same selection screen as Top1 and is merely ranked second; and (c) the framework ignores variance reduction, regime clustering within snapshots, and the ruin rate of Top1 itself, which the archaeology shows is 8/19 ≈ 42%. Concentrating in a single Top1 with a 42% ruin rate is not 'alpha capture' — it is uncompensated tail risk. The correct policy is position-sizing (Top2 smaller than Top1) and regime-conditional deployment, not binary slot->cash.

attacks.issue: Selection bias in the 8/19 false_positive_ruin denominator: the archaeology sample was constructed to find failure modes, so the ruin rate is a posterior failure rate, not a prior per-trade ruin rate for a generic B0 trigger.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the unconditional ruin rate of B0 picks is much lower (say 10-15%), then 'Top2 inherits ruin risk' overstates the marginal cost of slot 2. The gap-conditional policy would activate too often, leaving capital in cash when Top2 is in fact a positive-EV bet.

attacks.issue: Top2 candidates are not from the false_negative distribution by construction — they passed the same screen as Top1, just ranked lower. The mechanism claim that 'Top2 expected return collapses toward false_negative_relative' is a category error: rank #2 ≠ rejected-by-screen.
attacks.why_it_matters: The entire analytical bridge between the gap metric and the cash recommendation depends on this conflation. If Top2 is just a slightly weaker Top1, its expected return is positive and concentrated capital in Top1 alone foregoes free convexity.

attacks.issue: W4 return buckets are an arbitrary truncation horizon. Many 'ruin' and 'loss' outcomes recover by W8-W12 (typical base duration is 44-52 weeks). Treating 4-week ruin as terminal inflates the apparent ruin rate and biases the conclusion toward cash.
attacks.why_it_matters: Even if Top2 has a 30% W4 loss probability, its expected terminal return can be positive if the W4 drawdown is a normal base-building phase. A 4-week stop-loss is a policy choice, not a structural ruin rate.

attacks.issue: Portfolio construction effects are entirely absent from the mechanism: a 2-slot portfolio with low Top1-Top2 correlation has variance reduction independent of mean. Sharpe ratio can rise even when mean falls slightly. The 'cash dominates' rule treats N as if it only affects expected return, not variance.
attacks.why_it_matters: If Top1 and Top2 share <0.3 correlation (different sectors, factor exposures), a 2-slot portfolio can have higher risk-adjusted return than a 1-slot portfolio even when Top2 mean is lower. The cash recommendation ignores this dimension entirely.

attacks.issue: Cash has its own 'ruin' rate: negative real return. In a 2-3% inflation regime, holding cash costs ~0.15-0.25% per 4 weeks. The opportunity cost of cash is non-zero and must be netted against Top2's expected return, which even if modestly positive dominates cash in real terms.
attacks.why_it_matters: The 'cash dominates' claim implicitly assumes cash is a zero-cost option. It is not — cash is a losing real-return position. The break-even threshold for the policy is therefore not zero EV for Top2 but positive EV greater than the negative carry of cash.

attacks.issue: Post-hoc feature cherry-picking in the gap score: the researcher selects {mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5} because these show large standardized deltas in the archaeology. But base_duration_weeks, dist_to_52w_high, and base_depth_pct show smaller deltas — the 'right' gap metric is not uniquely defined, and the threshold (+0.5σ cluster) is tuned to fit the failure set.
attacks.why_it_matters: A policy built on a post-hoc selected feature set with a fitted threshold will not generalize. The threshold is overfit to the archaeology snapshot set and likely to be either too aggressive (cash too often) or too lax (gap not actually predictive) on out-of-sample data.

attacks.issue: Top1 itself ruins 8/19 = 42% of the time in the archaeology. The 'concentrate in Top1' alternative is not a low-ruin regime — it is a high-variance bet with a known ruin tail. The abstention argument must reckon with the fact that abstaining from slot 2 does not save you from Top1's ruin.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the goal is ruin avoidance, the lever is not slot 2 cash but Top1 selection quality or sizing. The cash policy creates an illusion of risk control while leaving the dominant ruin source (Top1) untouched.

attacks.issue: Snapshot clustering: multiple cases per snap_* ID implies a regime effect (market-wide beta) dominates individual name outcomes. In bear-regime snapshots, even Top1 ruins regardless of feature profile. Cash may dominate slot 2 in bear regimes for the wrong reason — the gap metric is acting as a regime proxy.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the gap metric is actually capturing regime (e.g., vol_ratio_5_20 elevates in bear markets as flight-to-quality vol spikes), then the policy is regime-conditional deployment dressed up as quality-gap-conditional deployment. This conflation will fail when quality gap and regime diverge (e.g., bear regime where Top1 has narrow feature gap but Top2 still ruins).

attacks.issue: The 'Top2 = small_win/loss filler' label maps onto 5 false_negative_relative cases that were all REJECTED by the B0 screen. These are not Top2 candidates — they are explicitly the model's misses. Using them as the distribution for 'what Top2 looks like' is double-counting the same selection error.
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher uses FN cases as a stand-in for Top2 because they share feature distributions. But FN by definition is what the model excluded. If Top2 looks like FN, the screen is broken and the fix is screen redesign, not abstention after the screen.

attacks.issue: The mechanism conflates 'large quality gap' (a relative concept between Top1 and Top2) with 'Top2 is bad in absolute terms.' A large gap can arise from an exceptional Top1 with a still-positive-EV Top2. The policy should be relative sizing, not binary abstention.
attacks.why_it_matters: A continuous policy (Top2 size = f(gap)) dominates a binary policy (gap > threshold → cash). Binary abstention loses the convex benefit of partial deployment and produces higher turnover costs as the gap oscillates around the threshold.

counterexamples_to_seek: Episodes where Top1-Top2 gap on {mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50} exceeded 0.5σ but a 2-slot portfolio still outperformed a 1-slot portfolio on Sharpe due to variance reduction — would invalidate the binary cash rule and support continuous sizing.
Cases where Top1 itself ruined (matching the 8 false_positive_ruin profile) despite high gap score, demonstrating that 'concentrate in Top1' does not deliver the alpha capture the mechanism claims.
Regime-divergence episodes: bull-regime snapshots where gap metric is small (compressed Top1-Top2 features) but Top2 nonetheless has positive W4 return, showing that low gap ≠ negative EV.
Recovery trajectories: cases labeled 'ruin' at W4 that closed positive by W12, quantifying how much of the 42% ruin rate is horizon truncation rather than terminal loss.

Cross-correlation matrix of W4 returns for Top1 and Top2 candidates within the same snapshot — if correlation is <0.4, the variance-reduction benefit of slot 2 mechanically exceeds the mean-loss penalty in most realistic scenarios.

An episode where Top3 (third-ranked slot) had higher W4 return than Top2 despite a smaller 'gap' with Top2, breaking the monotonic ranking assumption implicit in 'gap-conditional abstention starts at slot 2.'
what_would_change_my_mind: A matched-pair backtest across all 27 archaeology snapshots showing that 1-slot portfolio W4 median return exceeds 2-slot portfolio W4 median return by >2pp in >65% of high-gap episodes (gap > 0.5σ on the researcher's triplet). Current evidence is inferential; this would be direct.

Demonstration that Top2 candidate expected W4 return, computed unconditionally across the B0-screened universe, is negative in real terms (i.e., worse than the cash carry cost). Until this is shown, the cash recommendation rests on a selected subsample.

Evidence that the Top1-Top2 correlation of W4 returns within snapshots is >0.7, eliminating the variance-reduction argument. If correlation is high, the concentration case strengthens; if low, the binary cash policy is dominated by a continuous sizing policy.

A regime decomposition showing that, conditional on the snapshot's regime (bull/base/bear), the gap metric does NOT act as a regime proxy — i.e., the policy actually identifies quality differences, not market state. Otherwise the cash rule is a regime filter in disguise.

An out-of-sample test where the policy's threshold is calibrated on a holdout set (not the 27 archaeology cases) and still delivers >60% accuracy on the 'cash > Top2' prediction at the 4-week horizon. The current threshold is in-sample tuned.

Quantification of the cash opportunity cost over a multi-quarter horizon showing that, even allowing for ruin-avoidance wins, the foregone Top2 alpha in low-gap episodes exceeds the ruin-cost savings in high-gap episodes at the portfolio level. Without this, partial deployment is at least as good as the binary rule.

tests.name: top2_feature_overlap_with_fn_distribution
tests.comparison: Within each archaeology snapshot, the second-ranked B0-passing candidate (Top2) is projected onto the same 7-feature feature vector; the joint empirical CDF of Top2 across all 27 snapshots is compared against the empirical CDF of the false_negative_relative cases (the researcher's claimed proxy) using a 2-sample KS-style distance per feature. The test resolves which of (i) Top2 and FN come from the same distribution, (ii) Top2 sits between Top1 and FN, or (iii) Top2 sits closer to Top1 than FN. Pre-specify the rule: if median standardized per-feature distance between Top2 and FN is <0.30σ across all 7 features AND < the Top1-to-FN median distance, then researcher's conflation is supported; if Top2-to-FN distance is > Top1-to-FN distance, the conflation is refuted and the mechanism claim collapses.
tests.success_criterion: Top2-to-FN empirical distance (median across 7 features) is < Top1-to-FN distance AND <0.30σ, validating the researcher's claim that Top2 inherits FN-like expectancy.
tests.failure_criterion: Top2-to-FN distance is ≥ Top1-to-FN distance on ≥5 of 7 features, refuting the conflation and supporting the skeptic's claim that rank-2 ≠ rejected-by-screen.

tests.name: variance_reduction_capacity_test_within_snapshot
tests.comparison: Compute the implied per-slot W4 return for every (Top1, Top2) pair in the archaeology using each case's own w4_return_bucket midpoint (large_win=+10%, small_win=+3%, loss=-5%, ruin=-15%, pre-specified map). For each snapshot containing ≥2 B0-pick selected_winner OR false_positive_ruin cases, form the implied 1-slot portfolio (Top1 only) and 2-slot portfolio (Top1 mean+Top2 mean, equal-weighted). The variance-reduction capacity test computes the within-snapshot correlation implied by sharing different cases across slots; since we only observe one slot per realized entity, use the cross-name W4 bucket contingency across paired cases to estimate the upper bound on independent variation. Pre-specify: a 2-slot portfolio's implied variance (over matched cases) ≤ 0.7× the 1-slot variance supports the skeptic's variance-reduction mechanism; ≥0.9× variance leaves only the mean channel active for the researcher.
tests.success_criterion: Implied 2-slot variance ≤ 0.7× 1-slot variance across ≥60% of multi-case snapshots, supporting the skeptic's diversification channel.
tests.failure_criterion: Implied 2-slot variance ≥ 0.9× 1-slot variance across ≥60% of multi-case snapshots, isolating the mean-return channel as the only operative one and keeping the researcher's mechanism live.

tests.name: gap_metric_regime_proxy_discriminator
tests.comparison: Decompose the researcher's proposed gap score (weighted z on {mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5}) into (a) a 'momentum-quality' component and (b) a 'regime-volatility' component using PCA or sign-restricted decomposition on the 7 auxiliary features above. Test whether the gap score co-varies with the regime component across the 6 distinct snapshots (snap_724342c280, snap_287267e812, snap_eb3d8128cc, snap_c7fa0b9bb6, snap_12ebd0d057, snap_71486ed83c, snap_ad495b6705, snap_39b6f2c49e, snap_3fc4068e83, snap_8aa9111909, snap_edaba651c2, snap_d0d57b1e40, snap_01d3e2483b, snap_b8420124eb). Pre-specify: if correlation between gap-score variance and regime-component variance across snapshots is >0.5, the gap metric is acting as a regime filter (skeptic wins); if <0.2, the gap is a true cross-sectional quality discriminator (researcher wins).
tests.success_criterion: Cross-snapshot correlation(gap_score, regime_component) < 0.20 → gap metric is cross-sectional quality, not regime.
tests.failure_criterion: Cross-snapshot correlation(gap_score, regime_component) > 0.50 → gap metric is a regime proxy in disguise and binary policy will fail when gap and regime diverge.

tests.name: concentration_ruin_leak_test
tests.comparison: Compute the unconditional W4 ruin rate (false_positive_ruin outcome) among ALL B0-pick cases in the archaeology (n=19), then stratify by Top1 feature quintile. Pre-specify: if Top1 ruin rate in the highest-quality quintile (top quintile of composite mom_20+vol_ratio_5_20+px_vs_ma50) is still ≥25%, then 'concentration in Top1' inherits substantial ruin risk that the cash-on-slot-2 policy does nothing to mitigate (skeptic's point that abstention ignores the dominant ruin source). The researcher wins only if Top1 ruin rate in the top quintile drops below 10% AND the absolute rate is materially below the 19-case aggregate of 42%.
tests.success_criterion: Top1 W4 ruin rate in top-feature-quintile ≤ 10% (alpha is captured cleanly without comparable ruin tail).
tests.failure_criterion: Top1 W4 ruin rate in top-feature-quintile ≥ 25% (concentration does not eliminate ruin risk; the policy leaves the dominant ruin source untouched).

tests.name: binary_policy_vs_continuous_sizing_w4_sim
tests.comparison: Within each archaeology case, compute the implied W4 return for three portfolio constructions: (P1) N=1, Top1 only with full slot weight; (P2) N=2, equal-weight Top1+Top2; (P3) N=2-continuous, Top1 with weight = 1/(1+gap), Top2 with weight = gap/(1+gap) where gap is the researcher's standardized score on the 5-feature triplet. W4 returns are mapped from w4_return_bucket midpoints. Compare median portfolio W4 across all 27 cases for each construction. Pre-specify: if continuous-sizing median W4 return > binary-cash median W4 return by >1pp in >60% of cases, the skeptic's continuous-policy dominance claim is supported; if binary-cash wins by >1pp in >60%, the researcher's abstention rule is supported (cash is not dominated).
tests.success_criterion: Continuous-sizing portfolio median W4 return exceeds binary-cash (N=1) by >1pp in >60% of matched cases.
tests.failure_criterion: Binary-cash (N=1) portfolio median W4 return exceeds continuous-sizing by >1pp in >60% of matched cases, validating the gap-conditional abstention rule.

tests.name: cash_carry_break_even_proxy
tests.comparison: The researcher's mechanism implies 'Top2 EV ≤ 0' for the cash rule to dominate. The skeptic argues cash carry is negative (~0.15-0.25% per 4 weeks in real terms). Without a direct inflation rate feature in the allowlist, proxy cash carry cost by realized cross-sectional W4 volatility bucket: high-volatility windows (top tertile of vol_ratio_5_20) imply higher cash opportunity cost via the inflation-vol relation. Pre-specify: estimate the minimum-EV threshold for Top2 needed to dominate cash as f(W4 cross-sectional vol) using the empirical distribution of small_win/loss/selected_winner gaps. Test whether the Top2 implied EV (mapped from w4_return_bucket midpoints of the rank-2-distribution analog) clears this threshold. If Top2 implied median EV is positive across the archaeology, the cash rule fails on carry grounds; if Top2 implied median EV is ≤0, the researcher's rule holds in the carry sense.
tests.success_criterion: Top2 implied median W4 EV (across archaeology) is ≤ 0, validating the cash-side dominance on carry grounds.
tests.failure_criterion: Top2 implied median W4 EV is > cash-carry-cost proxy in >60% of archaeology cases, meaning the cash rule sacrifices positive expected return and is dominated even before risk-adjustment.

tests.name: slot3_monotonicity_breaker
tests.comparison: The researcher's gap-conditional abstention rule implicitly assumes rank ordering translates to quality ordering. Within snapshots that contain ≥3 B0-pick cases, compare the W4 bucket of the 3rd-ranked (by feature composite) candidate vs the 2nd-ranked candidate. Pre-specify: if ≥40% of 3rd-ranked cases deliver a strictly better W4 bucket (large_win vs small_win/loss/ruin) than the 2nd-ranked case in the same snapshot, the monotonic ranking assumption breaks and the binary 'start abstention at slot 2' rule is undermined — the optimal deployment point may be slot 3, not slot 2. If 3rd-ranked cases deliver strictly worse W4 buckets in ≥70% of matched snapshots, rank monotonicity holds and the abstention-from-slot-2 framing is defensible.
tests.success_criterion: 3rd-ranked W4 bucket > 2nd-ranked W4 bucket in ≥40% of matched multi-snapshot cases → monotonic rank→quality assumption is violated.
tests.failure_criterion: 3rd-ranked W4 bucket ≤ 2nd-ranked W4 bucket in ≥70% of matched cases → rank monotonicity holds and slot-2-as-abstention-trigger is coherent.

leakage_checks: Verify every feature in every test is point-in-time at the IBD entry decision — no pe-ahead into W4 outcome, no use of w4_return_bucket itself as an input feature, and no use of outcome_label/pulldown characteristics as predictors.

Verify all comparisons use only entity- and snapshot-anonymized joins; no ticker-equivalent identifier is constructed from feature combinations (e.g., a fingerprint of (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50) that uniquely identifies an entity is excluded from the test as identity leakage).

Verify the W4 bucket mapping is fixed in advance: large_win=+10pp, small_win=+3pp, loss=-5pp, ruin=-15pp — and that NO post-W4 fields (W8/W12 recovery, terminal return, max drawdown beyond W4) are queried, used, or inferred as evidence in any test.

Verify no calendar feature (week-of-year, month, quarter, year, day-of-week, holiday-proximity, earnings-proximity in calendar terms) enters any test — only PIT-observable price/volume/volatility/momentum/slope/structure features from the supplied allowlist.

Verify that position-sizing policies compared in test 5 (binary vs continuous) and concentration rules in test 4 use only entry-time features; the W4 outcomes are evaluated only as outcomes, never reused in sizing decisions.

Verify that regime-proxy decomposition in test 3 uses only PIT-computable features (rv_20, atr_14_pct, ma50_slope_10, dist_to_52w_high_pct, mom_60) and not implied regime labels derived from forward-outcome clustering.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The researcher's claim is too strong in its current form but not refuted. The core intuition — that concentrated alpha in Top1 plus a non-trivial ruin tail makes marginal slot-filling conditionally negative-EV — is plausible, but the bridge connecting 'large Top1-Top2 gap' to 'Top2 expected return collapses toward the false_negative_relative distribution' is a category error (Top2 ≠ FN by construction; both passed the screen, only rank differs) compounded by an archaeology-sampling artifact (the 8/19 ruin rate is a posterior failure-mining rate, not a per-trade prior for new B0 entries). Independently, the marginal ruin cost of adding slot 2 is approximately the ruin rate of Top2 itself, not the unconditional 8/19 figure cited for B0 picks; the researcher conflates unconditional and marginal ruin contributions. Cash carry over a 4-week window is small (~-0.2% real, ≈-2.6% annualized) but non-zero, so a Top2 EV positive by even a small margin can dominate cash on carry alone. The genuine economic meaning of N=1, N=2, N=3 under fixed 3-slot capital is therefore: N=1 maximizes per-slot alpha concentration and variance; N=3 minimizes variance but forces inclusion of low-EV fillers; the optimal N is gap-conditional AND regime-conditional AND position-size-conditional. Continuous sizing strictly dominates the discrete N∈{1,2,3} choice set, so any binary 'cash vs fill' policy is suboptimal by construction — the genuine policy is gap-gated continuous weight with a floor that maps to N=1, N=2, or N=3 only as integer-rounded outputs.
falsifiers: If in the experimental_designer's top2_feature_overlap_with_fn_distribution test, Top2-to-FN median standardized distance is ≥ Top1-to-FN median distance on ≥5 of 7 features, the researcher's conflation is refuted and the mechanism collapses to 'gap is a regime proxy, not a quality discriminator'.

If the concentration_ruin_leak_test shows Top1 W4 ruin rate in the top feature quintile still ≥25%, the ruin-tail argument does not uniquely justify concentration — Top1 itself carries substantial ruin risk that gap-conditional abstention does not eliminate.

If binary-cash (N=1) portfolio median W4 exceeds continuous-sizing (Top1 with weight 1/(1+gap)) by >1pp in >60% of cases, the abstention framing beats even the smaller continuous-size alternative, validating a binary rule.
If Top2 implied median W4 EV > cash-carry-cost proxy in >60% of archaeology cases, cash is dominated even before the diversification benefit enters and the policy must be reformulated.

If within-snapshot variance reduction from N=1 to N=2 is ≤0.7× of N=1 variance across ≥60% of multi-case snapshots, the skeptic's diversification channel is operative and weakens the case for concentration regardless of mean.

If 3rd-ranked W4 bucket beats 2nd-ranked W4 bucket in ≥40% of matched multi-snapshot cases, the monotonic rank→quality assumption breaks and slot-2-as-abstention-trigger is the wrong trigger; slot-3 or cumulative-gap rules should replace it.
actionable_design_principles: Separate the two decisions the researcher collapsed: (a) is the marginal slot's EV positive at any sizing? (b) if yes, what continuous weight maximizes risk-adjusted return? Binary N∈{0,1,2,3} is a derived integer output of (a)+(b), not a primitive choice.

Compute the marginal ruin cost of adding slot k as the ruin rate of slot k minus the ruin rate already present in slots 1..k-1, NOT as the unconditional B0-pick ruin rate. The 8/19 figure is a single-slot posterior, not an additive marginal.

The Top1-Top2 gap is a necessary but not sufficient condition for abstention: it must be combined with a regime proxy (vol_ratio_5_20, rv_20, ma50_slope_10) to avoid activating during benign-regime gap events.

Continuous sizing (e.g., slot weight = clip(gap_normalized, 0, 1)) strictly dominates binary cash-or-fill because it captures partial information in the gap magnitude without forcing a discrete cliff.
Cash carry over a 4-week window is small (~-0.2% real) but not negligible; any marginal-slot policy must explicitly model it rather than treating cash as a free default.

The 42% ruin rate among the 19 B0 archaeology cases is an upper bound on per-trade ruin for B0-style triggers, not a point estimate; new-entry ruin rate is materially lower and must be re-estimated on a forward, non-archaeology sample before the gap-conditional rule is committed.

Mixed-outcome cases (ruin|winner co-occurrence) imply the portfolio layer must be evaluated on path-dependent metrics (max drawdown, recovery time) not just W4 bucket means; abstention rules based solely on mean expectancy will understate the variance cost of forced fills.
The 3-slot capital constraint itself is exogenous to the question; if N=1 is optimal under a regime, the correct response is to acknowledge cash deployment rather than to spread across 3 names.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: gap_gated_continuous_sizing: weight_of_slot_k = clip(alpha_k * (1 - beta * gap_normalized_to_baseline), w_min, w_max), where gap_normalized_to_baseline is the standardized Top1-Top2 distance on {mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, ma10_slope_5}. Slots below w_min collapse to cash (binary abstention floor); above w_min, sizing is continuous.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Researcher proposed binary N∈{1,2,3}; skeptic argued continuous sizing dominates. This idea enforces a continuous policy but rounds to integer N as a downstream accounting artifact, not a decision variable. The w_min floor preserves the researcher's abstention intuition without forcing it on every high-gap case.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Directly governs how 3-slot capital is allocated; allows N=1 (one w_max slot + two cash), N=2, or N=3 as continuous-weight roundings.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: regime_conditional_abstention: abstention rule fires only when (gap > threshold) AND (regime_proxy = high_vol_or_low_trend). Regime proxy = composite of {vol_ratio_5_20, rv_20, atr_14_pct, ma50_slope_10, mom_60}. The composite is z-scored; high_vol_or_low_trend = regime_composite < -0.5 OR > +0.5 (two-sided: gap matters in calm trends AND in chaos).
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Researcher's rule fires on gap alone. Experimental designer's test 3 (gap_metric_regime_proxy_discriminator) implies the gap may be a regime proxy in disguise. This idea makes that explicit: the abstention is a joint gate, so a large gap in a benign regime does not trigger cash; a small gap in a hostile regime does not trigger deployment.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Filters which slot configurations are even admissible; under high-vol or low-trend regimes, capacity utilization drops, leaving slots as cash.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: marginal_ruin_adjusted_size: for slot k, expected_loss_k = P(ruin_k) * ruin_magnitude_proxy + P(loss_k) * loss_magnitude. Marginal expected loss of adding slot k = expected_loss_k - expected_loss_(k-1)_portfolio. Position size inversely scaled by marginal expected loss: weight_k ∝ 1 / (1 + gamma * marginal_expected_loss_k).
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses the synthesis insight that unconditional ruin rate ≠ marginal ruin contribution. The 8/19 figure cited by the researcher is unconditional; this idea uses only the marginal increment. This corrects both the researcher's over-statement and the skeptic's under-statement.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Drives the per-slot weight; slots with high marginal ruin contribution are shrunk toward w_min (cash-equivalent) even if their mean EV is positive.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: cumulative_gap_deployment_curve: rather than triggering at Top1-Top2 gap, compute cumulative_gap = sum of consecutive rank-pair gaps (Top1-Top2, Top2-Top3, ...) for the active candidate list. Cash fraction = clip(cumulative_gap / baseline_cumulative_gap, 0, 1 - 1/N_max).
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Experimental designer's slot3_monotonicity_breaker test implies slot-2-as-trigger may be wrong. This idea replaces the discrete slot-2 trigger with a cumulative metric that responds to rank-order breaks anywhere in the candidate list, making the policy robust to violations of the monotonic rank→quality assumption.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Directly maps to N (number of deployed slots): if cumulative_gap is large, only Top1 deploys (N=1); if moderate, N=2; if small, full N=3 deployment.

cycles.question: For large Top1-vs-Top2 quality gap, determine what PIT statistic can measure confidence without future leakage. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: For a large Top1-vs-Top2 quality gap, the PIT-safe confidence proxy is the Composite Confidence Margin (CCM): the z-scored differential between Top1 and Top2 on a multi-factor conviction bundle [up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50], all computable from the snapshot's pre-entry bars. CCM > ~1.0 indicates decisive Top1 conviction and should gate a 1-slot concentrated bet; CCM in [0.3, 1.0] indicates genuine Top2 merit and licenses a 2-slot split; CCM < 0.3 indicates no meaningful rank separation, so the 3-slot equal-weight allocation is preferred as implicit variance reduction rather than as alpha expression. Under a fixed 3-slot capital budget, slot count is not a risk-budget dial but a confidence-band selector: 1 slot = 67% cash + high-conviction alpha, 2 slots = 33% cash + hedged alpha, 3 slots = 0% cash + diversification beta.
evidence_for: Across the 27 error-archaeology cases, the four features up_day_ratio_20 (std Δ -1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), mom_20 (-1.00), and px_vs_ma50 (-0.85) show the largest separation between selected_winner and false_negative cohorts, all PIT-observable at the snapshot bar.

Selected winners consistently sit above the B0 cohort median on these features (mom_20 median 0.163, up_day_ratio_20 0.625, px_vs_ma50 0.127), while false negatives cluster below (mom_20 0.058, up_day_ratio 0.500, px_vs_ma50 0.056) — meaning a positive CCM signals genuinely differentiated conviction, not just absolute level.

False_positive_ruin cases (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c, entity_ccc90a671f, entity_84824e6a20, entity_b6bcccdf6a, entity_55c2da490e, entity_40ea0cfb3b) carry B0_pick=true but show *moderate* CCM-equivalent profiles (mom_20 ranging -0.01 to 0.23 with weaker px_vs_ma50 of 0.06-0.18), suggesting the gap-to-Top2 — not Top1 absolute level — is what distinguishes real conviction from overconfident selection.

Entity_2c58cebc59 (selected_winner, large_win, mom_20=0.32, px_vs_ma50=0.17, up_day_ratio=0.6) versus entity_3472243e0c (false_positive_ruin, mom_20=0.24, px_vs_ma50=0.07, up_day_ratio=0.65) shows nearly identical absolute features yet opposite outcomes; only the relative gap to a notional Top2 would resolve whether entity_2c58cebc59 was a true outlier or a marginal pick — confirming CCM is the discriminating signal.

The pullback_pct standardized delta (+0.64) and pullback_duration_weeks (-0.73) for false negatives vs winners indicate that deeper, longer consolidations precede genuine breakouts; these enter CCM indirectly through px_vs_ma50 since deep bases produce larger px_vs_ma50 dispersion between candidates.
evidence_against: Entity_440e297253 was a selected_winner (large_win) despite modest mom_20=0.058 and px_vs_ma50=0.073 — features that look like a false negative by the same medians, so a pure CCM > 1.0 rule would have wrongly under-allocated to it; CCM is necessary but not sufficient without absolute-floor gating.

Entity_6618d3e80c carries outcome=false_positive_ruin|selected_winner simultaneously, with very high conviction features (mom_20=0.25, px_vs_ma50=0.34, up_day_ratio=0.55) — a high CCM here would trigger full concentration yet the position later ruined, exposing CCM's blindness to regime/event risk not encoded in price-only bars.
Vol_ratio_5_20 is elevated (>1.2) for nearly all cases regardless of outcome, limiting its discriminative power as a single feature; the composite may overweight a noisy axis.

Only 27 cases anchor the false-negative definition; the contrast medians have wide confidence intervals and the method note explicitly conditions on outer-forward W4 outcomes, so the gap is structurally optimistic — CCM thresholds must be cross-validated, not trusted from this sample alone.

Some selected winners have *negative* ma20_slope_5 (entity_8ad5cd4795, entity_2f86543bf6) yet still won, implying trend-slope features (intentionally excluded from the proposed CCM bundle) carry information that a 4-factor margin would discard.
falsifiable_predictions: On held-out snapshots where CCM(z-scored margin on {up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50}) exceeds 1.0, a 1-slot allocation on Top1 yields higher 4-week Sharpe than a 3-slot equal-weight allocation on the same candidate set, after transaction costs.
When CCM is in [0.3, 1.0], the 2-slot (Top1, Top2) allocation's hit rate on Top2 should exceed 0.50 *conditional on Top1 winning*, confirming Top2 carries independent alpha rather than being a hedge.

When CCM < 0.3, the 3-slot portfolio's variance should be at least 30% lower than the 1-slot Top1-only variance, but expected return should not exceed 1-slot return by more than the cash-drag penalty — confirming diversification is variance-control, not alpha.

An absolute-confidence floor (e.g., Top1 raw score below 25th percentile of historical winners) should override CCM and force abstention (0 slots deployed) regardless of gap size, since entity_440e297253-like cases can produce large CCM from a weak Top2.
Calibration check: quintile-bucketed CCM should be monotonically related to Top1 win-rate; violation indicates the z-score weights are misspecified for the live distribution.
policy_implications: Adopt CCM as the slot-count gate: high CCM → 1 slot + 2/3 cash (yield plus optionality), mid CCM → 2 slots + 1/3 cash, low CCM → 3 slots fully invested. This converts the 3-slot budget from a fixed-allocation rule into a confidence-conditional one.

Pair CCM with an absolute conviction floor on Top1 (e.g., require Top1 z-score on the conviction bundle above -0.5) before any deployment; below the floor, hold cash in all 3 slots — this is the capacity-abstention trigger.

Treat cash held in 1-slot or 2-slot states as a deliberate position with its own expected return (yield), not as 'idle capital' — economic PnL attribution must split alpha return, diversification discount, and cash yield.

Use Top2 as an *information source* about Top1's regime, not as an independent alpha bet when CCM is small — small CCM means Top2 is nearly indistinguishable, so the 3-slot allocation is paying full transaction cost for variance reduction that could be cheaper achieved via position sizing on Top1.

Monitor false_positive_ruin rate stratified by CCM quintile; if high-CCM cases still ruin at >10%, CCM is insufficient and a regime filter (e.g., market-breadth or sector-relative features) must be added to the bundle.

Do not extrapolate the 27-case medians to live thresholds without bootstrap confidence intervals on CCM cutoffs; the discovery-train sample is small and the false-negative definition embeds an outer-forward criterion that biases the contrast.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The CCM (Composite Confidence Margin) framework is a circular restatement of the B0 selection model. The 'gap between Top1 and Top2' on mom_20/up_day_ratio_20/vol_ratio_5_20/px_vs_ma50 is not an independent confidence signal — it is, by construction, a function of the very features B0 used to pick Top1 in the first place. The 27-case error-archaeology contrast (selected_winner vs false_negative_relative) is therefore not measuring a PIT-safe conviction proxy; it is measuring how strongly the existing ranker separates the names it decided to deploy from the names it declined. The four-feature bundle was cherry-picked from 20+ candidates by post-hoc standardized delta, the threshold cuts (0.3, 1.0) are unanchored to any empirical quantile or cross-validated cutoff, and vol_ratio_5_20 is admitted by the proposer to be elevated (>1.2) across virtually every case — i.e., noise. The slot-count mapping (1 → 67% cash, 2 → 33% cash, 3 → 0% cash) further conflates two orthogonal decisions: how many positions to hold and how much of the 3-slot capital to deploy per position. A concentrated bet is not the same as deploying 1 of 3 slots; it is a position-sizing choice. The mechanism thus fails on three independent grounds: (a) the proxy is endogenously selected, (b) the threshold values are free parameters, and (c) the slot-to-cash identity ignores that 1-slot with full capital and 3-slot with full capital are both possible states.

attacks.issue: Endogeneity / circular contrast definition
attacks.why_it_matters: Selected_winner requires is_b0_pick=true; false_negative_relative requires is_b0_pick=false. B0 is selected using exactly this feature family (momentum, relative-to-MA, volume ratio, up-day share). The CCM margin on these features between the B0-deployed and B0-skipped cohorts is therefore an identity, not a discovery. Any model that ranks via mom_20+px_vs_ma50+up_day_ratio will show a CCM-shaped gap for the same reason. The framework proves the ranker works, not that a new confidence proxy has been found.

attacks.issue: Post-hoc feature selection from 20+ candidates
attacks.why_it_matters: The frozen evidence shows standardized deltas for ~23 features; the proposer picked the top 4 by |Δ|. With multiple-testing, the largest gap is expected to be ~1.2 by chance even when no feature carries signal. The 4-feature bundle is therefore a multiple-comparisons artifact; its components need pre-registration or holdout confirmation, neither of which is present.

attacks.issue: vol_ratio_5_20 is noise inside the bundle
attacks.why_it_matters: The proposer concedes vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.2 for ~all cases. Substituting a near-constant feature for one dimension of a margin score cannot help discriminate; it at best shifts the z-scoring weights of the remaining 3 features. Including it gives a false sense of multi-factor robustness.

attacks.issue: Unanchored threshold values (0.3 and 1.0)
attacks.why_it_matters: No quantile, no bootstrap, no train/test split produced 0.3 or 1.0. They read as round-number defaults. With 27 cases, even a stratified split would put ~5 cases per bucket — quintile monotonicity is unestimable. Any threshold picked on this sample inherits its variance.

attacks.issue: Exclusion of the actually most discriminative contrarian features
attacks.why_it_matters: pullback_pct (+0.64 std Δ) and pullback_duration_weeks (-0.73) separate winners from false negatives in directions consistent with deep-base continuation. Ignoring these in the conviction bundle throws away the contrarian component. The claim that px_vs_ma50 'indirectly' captures this is unsubstantiated — a deep pullback can produce large px_vs_ma50 OR small, depending on when the snap was taken.

attacks.issue: Date-cluster confounds (snap_71486ed83c dominates false negatives)
attacks.why_it_matters: Most false-negative cases come from a single snapshot. Within one snapshot's candidate set, all names have correlated features and small pairwise margins. The CCM is artificially small for the snapshot, not because confidence is low. Quoting snapshot-pooled CCM statistics mixes this regime effect with conviction.

attacks.issue: Conflation of slot count with cash allocation
attacks.why_it_matters: '1 slot = 67% cash' presumes a fixed 3-slot budget where unfilled slots become cash. But 1 slot could carry 100% of capital (concentrated) or 33% (cautious); 3 slots could be 3×33%, 3×10%, or pyramid-sized. The economic meaning of slot count under a fixed capital budget is not what the proposer claims; the slot count is a portfolio-construction dial separate from sizing and from confidence.

attacks.issue: Self-contradicting labels (entity_6618d3e80c: selected_winner AND false_positive_ruin)
attacks.why_it_matters: This case simultaneously won and ruined at different horizons/buckets. CCM cannot be assigned a single outcome, so thresholding on outcome labels is unstable. Any decision rule derived from such labels inherits an oscillation.

attacks.issue: 'Top2 as information source about Top1' lacks mechanism
attacks.why_it_matters: Top2 is a peer from the same universe scored by the same feature family. Its margin to Top1 reflects scoring noise and ranking ties, not regime. Modeling Top2 as a regime diagnostic requires a separate generative story the proposer does not supply.

attacks.issue: Sample labels embed future information
attacks.why_it_matters: selected_winner and false_positive_ruin are W4 outcomes. While CCM itself is computed on pre-entry bars, the *thresholds* are calibrated on outcome-conditioned labels. The gap between 'Top1 deployed = won' and 'Top1 deployed = ruined' is forward-aware by construction; generalizing thresholds to live PIT data is a transfer-learning problem the proposer does not address.

attacks.issue: Internal contradiction — absolute floor alongside a relative-gap rule
attacks.why_it_matters: Proposing an absolute-floor override (Top1 must clear 25th-percentile raw score) implicitly admits the relative CCM is insufficient. If a large gap from a weak Top1 is still invalid, then CCM alone is not the confidence statistic — and the slot-count mapping is no longer purely confidence-driven.

counterexamples_to_seek: A snapshot where Top1 and Top2 share nearly identical vectors on the 4 CCM features (so margin ≈ 0) yet both subsequently deliver large positive W4 returns — CCM < 0.3 would force 3-slot deployment even though conviction is path-dependent, not gap-dependent.

A snapshot where the entire candidate pool has low up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20, making every candidate's CCM score uniformly depressed regardless of relative ordering. CCM predicts low confidence; live outcome may show the small-gaps regime is precisely where consensus matters more.

A Top1 with high CCM (large gap) coming from a thin-volatility regime where vol_ratio_5_20 ≈ 1 across all names — the apparent conviction is an artifact of vol_ratio contributing ~0 to every margin, so the std Δ on the *bundle* is engineered.

Selected winners with negative ma20_slope_5 (entity_8ad5cd4795, entity_2f86543bf6) where the CCM bundle ignores slope direction — these are wins the relative-gap framework would not specifically endorse and could 'accidentally' approve.
Cases where snap_71486ed83c had a high-CCM Top1 that subsequently failed — this would refute the bundle's claim that high gap = high conviction, demonstrating snapshot-cluster contamination.

Top2 candidates with higher absolute mom_20 than Top1 (legitimate ranking inversion at the snapshot) — current CCM correctly flags this as low margin; the framework has no fallback when both the ranker and the gap are wrong.
what_would_change_my_mind: A pre-registered feature bundle (chosen before seeing the contrast table) plus a held-out snapshot sample of >100 cases showing monotonic quintile-level win-rate on Top1 by CCM — this would falsify the multiple-comparisons critique.
Demonstration that CCM margin carries incremental AUC beyond B0's raw score on a leave-one-snapshot-out CV — i.e., the gap is informative above and beyond the underlying feature magnitudes.
A causal/structural story for why vol_ratio_5_20 specifically should enter the bundle when its range is narrow across all cases — i.e., economic mechanism, not just 'it loaded in a PCA-like view'.

Empirical threshold selection (bootstrap percentile or constrained optimization on a separate sample) for the 0.3 and 1.0 cut-points, with sensitivity analyses showing the slot-count policy is stable across reasonable perturbations.

Evidence that the slot-count mapping (1, 2, 3) is truly confidence-conditional rather than a sizing dial — e.g., a controlled comparison where 1 slot with 100% capital outperforms 1 slot with 33% capital at high CCM, and 3 slots with 100% capital outperforms 3 slots with 33% at low CCM.

Inclusion of pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks in the bundle improves out-of-sample hit-rate over the 4-feature CCM, confirming the contrarian information component is captured rather than ignored.

Demonstration that false_positive_ruin rate conditional on high-CCM is below the unconditional ruin rate, ideally below 10% — currently the claim is unfalsified because the bundle was selected post-hoc on the very sample it must outperform.

tests.name: within_snapshot_margin_compression_test
tests.comparison: Distribution of CCM (Top1-Top2 z-scored margin on the 4-feature bundle) computed once across the pooled candidate pool versus once within each individual snapshot. Compare within-snapshot variance to across-snapshot variance and to the pooled variance.
tests.success_criterion: Within-snapshot CCM variance is within 50% of the pooled variance, AND the rank order of (Top1, Top2, Top3) by absolute conviction is stable across within-snapshot and pooled scoring. This would indicate the gap statistic is not a pooling artifact.
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot CCM variance is less than 30% of the pooled variance, OR the within-snapshot Top1 differs from pooled Top1 in more than 25% of snapshots. Failure shows that low-CCM readings partly arise from same-snapshot candidate similarity, not from genuine low conviction.

tests.name: counterfactual_bundle_indistinguishability_test
tests.comparison: Construct K=5 alternative 4-feature bundles sampled from the PIT allowlist excluding the proposed CCM features. For each, compute within-snapshot CCM-style margin. Test whether the empirical distribution of (Top1-Top2) margins is statistically indistinguishable from the proposed CCM bundle's distribution (e.g., Kolmogorov-Smirnov on the absolute margins, and Mann-Whitney on the signed margins).
tests.success_criterion: At least 4 of 5 counterfactual bundles produce margin distributions that are significantly different from the CCM bundle's (two-sided KS p<0.05). This would indicate the CCM feature choice carries non-generic structural content.
tests.failure_criterion: More than 2 of 5 counterfactual bundles produce indistinguishable margin distributions. Failure demonstrates that any 4-feature z-score margin has the same shape — meaning CCM is a generic statistic dressed in a specific feature set, not a mechanism-specific signal.

tests.name: vol_ratio_contribution_bound_test
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot, compute the coefficient of variation (CV) of vol_ratio_5_20 across candidates. Then compute the marginal contribution of the vol_ratio_5_20 dimension to the CCM margin as: |z-score(Top1) - z-score(Top2)| * (1/sqrt(K)) where K=4 features. Compare this contribution's expected magnitude to the contributions of the other three features.
tests.success_criterion: Across snapshots, the vol_ratio_5_20 contribution to the CCM margin exceeds 25% of the average per-feature contribution in more than 50% of snapshots. This would indicate vol_ratio is doing real discrimination work, contradicting the noise critique.
tests.failure_criterion: Vol_ratio contribution falls below 15% of average per-feature contribution in at least 75% of snapshots, OR its CV across snapshots is below 0.15 in more than 70% of snapshots. Failure confirms the feature is structurally near-constant and contributes only via z-scoring arithmetic, not via signal.

tests.name: top2_dominance_inventory_test
tests.comparison: For each snapshot, count on how many of the 4 CCM features Top2 strictly exceeds Top1. Bucket snapshots into {Top2 wins 0/4, 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4}. Test whether the CCM margin correlates negatively with the count of features where Top2 dominates (gap shrinks when Top2 wins features).
tests.success_criterion: In at least 60% of snapshots, Top2 wins on at most 1 of 4 features, and the CCM margin shows positive correlation (rho > 0.3) with Top2's loss-margin (i.e., margin tracks the bundle's joint configuration). This supports CCM as a meaningful joint statistic.
tests.failure_criterion: Top2 wins on 2+ features in more than 40% of snapshots, AND the CCM margin fails to correlate with bundle-joint configuration (|rho| < 0.2). Failure shows the gap is mechanically dominated by single-feature outliers rather than joint conviction — undermining the multi-factor framing.

tests.name: absolute_floor_gap_orthogonality_test
tests.comparison: Compute two PIT statistics per snapshot: (a) Top1 absolute conviction = mean z-score of Top1 on the 4 features, (b) CCM margin = z-score differential between Top1 and Top2. Tabulate the joint distribution across snapshots. Test rank correlation between (a) and (b), and identify the four quadrants {high level, high gap}, {high level, low gap}, {low level, high gap}, {low level, low gap}.
tests.success_criterion: Rank correlation between Top1 absolute level and CCM margin exceeds 0.4 within snapshots, indicating they carry overlapping (not independent) information. The {high level, low gap} and {low level, high gap} cells should be sparsely populated (combined <30%).
tests.failure_criterion: Rank correlation falls below 0.2, OR the {low level, high gap} cell holds more than 25% of snapshots (the entity_440e297253-like scenario dominating). Failure shows the gap and the level are decoupled, which means CCM cannot stand alone as a confidence statistic and the Researcher's own absolute-floor override is structurally required, not optional.

tests.name: contrarian_feature_redundancy_test
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot, compute partial correlation: residualize pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks against the 4 CCM features (using all candidates in the snapshot), then test whether the (Top1-Top2) margin on pullback residuals adds variance beyond the CCM margin. Use the increase in R^2 when adding pullback-based margin to CCM margin as the test statistic.
tests.success_criterion: Adding pullback-based margin to CCM margin raises R^2 by less than 0.05 across snapshots (i.e., pullback information is already redundant with the 4-feature bundle). This supports the Researcher's claim that px_vs_ma50 indirectly captures deep-base structure.
tests.failure_criterion: Adding pullback-based margin raises R^2 by more than 0.10 in more than 50% of snapshots. Failure shows the contrarian features carry non-redundant information that the proposed bundle silently discards, supporting the Skeptic's claim that an incomplete bundle biases the gap statistic.

tests.name: slot_count_sizing_decomposition_test
tests.comparison: Enumerate the 3-slot budget under all combinations of (slot count) x (sizing rule). For slot count in {1,2,3}, define sizing rule S_uniform (equal weight across deployed slots) and S_proportional (slot weight = bundle z-score). For each (slot_count, sizing) combination, compute: (i) total capital deployed, (ii) cash fraction, (iii) per-position weight, (v) within-snapshot dispersion of per-position weights. Test whether the Researcher's stated mapping {CCM>1 → 1 slot + 67% cash; 0.3<CCM<1 → 2 slots + 33% cash; CCM<0.3 → 3 slots + 0% cash} corresponds to one unique point on this matrix or to a curve of possibilities.
tests.success_criterion: The mapping uniquely determines both slot count AND sizing, such that fixing CCM fixes a single point in (slot_count, per-position-weight) space — i.e., the 67% cash / 33% cash / 0% cash outputs are inseparable from the 1-slot / 2-slot / 3-slot counts. This would confirm slot count IS a confidence dial in this accounting.
tests.failure_criterion: Multiple (slot_count, sizing) pairs yield the same cash fraction and per-position weights, OR the mapping leaves per-position weight under-specified. This refutes the claim that slot count alone determines confidence under a fixed capital budget, since the same slot count can be paired with different sizing rules without changing deployed capital.

leakage_checks: Verify that every feature listed is computable from the snapshot bar and prior history only; reject any feature whose definition requires the bar at, after, or beyond the IBD entry trigger.
Verify that vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, mom_20, and px_vs_ma50 are defined using only bars strictly before the snapshot timestamp — no lookahead into the breakout or post-entry window.
Verify that pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks, when used, are measured from the most recent completed base, not from the entry or post-entry period.

Confirm that no test outcome depends on W4 return buckets, w4_return_bucket, outcome_label, or any outer-forward label — all evaluations must be structural (distributional, correlational, geometric) rather than outcome-conditioned.

Confirm that no test uses snapshot_anon, entity_anon, or is_b0_pick as a feature or stratum — these encode forward-conditioned labels or sampling structure that would re-introduce the selection bias the framework is meant to avoid.
Confirm that 'within-snapshot' computations exclude the snapshot identity itself (snap_71486ed83c-style cluster effects must not become features) — use candidate identity only.
Confirm that the counterfactual bundle test does not draw features already in the proposed bundle and then claim independence; rejection of overlap is part of the design.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The Researcher's CCM proposal — z-scored Top1-minus-Top2 margin on {up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50} — captures a real and PIT-safe question ('is Top1 an outlier or the best of a tight pack?'), but it cannot stand alone as a confidence statistic for three converging reasons: (i) the bundle was selected from a ~23-feature contrast conditioned on outcome labels that the B0 ranker itself uses, so the gap is partially a tautology with the ranker rather than an independent check; (ii) within a 27-case discovery sample the standardized deltas and CCM thresholds (0.3, 1.0) are not pre-registered and lack bootstrap support; (iii) the slot-count mapping conflates position concentration with confidence — under fixed 3-slot capital, going from 3 slots to 1 slot quadruples per-position weight and quintuples idiosyncratic exposure, so fewer slots is the HIGHEST-risk state for any given conviction, not the safest. The mechanism therefore survives only as a relative gap indicator that must be paired with an absolute conviction floor, a regime overlay not in the bundle, and an explicit recognition that 'cash held' is itself a position whose contribution to risk-adjusted return is positive in the 1-slot state. The Experimental Designer's seven tests are appropriate but most will require an out-of-sample snapshot set larger than the 27 discovery cases to deliver adjudicating power; on the current evidence base they cannot confirm or refute the mechanism, only bound where it could fail.
falsifiers: On a held-out snapshot set of >=200 candidates drawn from a period disjoint from snap_71486ed83c and snap_d0d57b1e40, the within-snapshot CCM margin fails to correlate (Spearman rho < 0.15) with the actual 4-week forward Top1-minus-Top2 return spread — falsifying that the gap statistic is informative about realized conviction differential.

The counterfactual_bundle_indistinguishability_test (4 of 5 random 4-feature bundles producing KS-indistinguishable margin distributions from CCM) passes — falsifying the claim that the specific feature choice carries non-generic structural content and showing CCM is just a z-score artifact dressed in a familiar feature set.

Quintile-bucketed CCM on held-out data fails to be monotonically related to Top1 win rate (a non-monotonicity, e.g., highest CCM quintile with win rate below the median quintile) — falsifying the calibration claim that higher gap implies higher conviction.

vol_ratio_5_20 contribution to CCM margin falls below 15% of per-feature mean contribution in >75% of held-out snapshots AND its CV across snapshots is <0.15 — confirming the feature is structural noise and that CCM effectively reduces to a 3-feature weighted margin.

Adding pullback-based margin (residualized pullback_pct + pullback_duration_weeks) to CCM margin raises out-of-sample R^2 for the Top1-vs-Top2 return spread by >0.10 in >50% of snapshots — confirming the bundle silently discards non-redundant base-structure information.

Under live transaction costs, the 1-slot allocation in the CCM>1 regime does NOT dominate the 3-slot allocation by Sharpe after the cash-drag penalty is subtracted — falsifying the slot-count-as-confidence-dial claim and showing concentration premium is illusory.

False_positive_ruin rate in the CCM>1 quintile exceeds 10% on held-out data — falsifying the implicit regime-invariance assumption baked into the bundle and showing CCM is blind to the same event/regime risk that already produced entity_6618d3e80c.

The absolute_floor_gap_orthogonality_test shows rank correlation between Top1 absolute level and CCM margin <0.2 AND the {low level, high gap} cell holds >25% of snapshots — falsifying CCM as a usable standalone proxy and confirming the Researcher's own absolute-floor override is structurally mandatory, not optional.

Permutation test: randomly reassigning is_b0_pick labels within each snapshot destroys the contrast between selected_winner and false_negative cohorts on the 4 CCM features (standardized delta collapses to |Δ|<0.3 for all four) — falsifying the discovery itself as a selection-on-feature artifact.
actionable_design_principles: Treat CCM strictly as a RELATIVE gap diagnostic, never as a confidence proxy in isolation. Any deployment decision must require THREE independent confirmations: (a) CCM above its regime-specific threshold, (b) Top1 absolute z-score on the bundle above a pre-registered floor, and (c) a regime/sector filter (e.g., market breadth or sector-relative momentum) outside the bundle. Single-criterion deployment is forbidden.

Pre-register the CCM feature bundle, the z-scoring reference window, and the slot-count thresholds BEFORE the next out-of-sample window opens. Any re-selection of features or thresholds on observed failure rates constitutes re-introducing the same endogeneity the framework is meant to eliminate.

Recognize that under fixed 3-slot capital, 'fewer slots' means HIGHER per-position risk, not lower. The 1-slot regime is the most concentrated exposure state; cash held is not zero-risk but earns the risk-free rate plus optionality. Risk attribution must decompose PnL into alpha, diversification discount, and cash yield as three separate legs.

Decouple slot count from sizing. The Researcher's mapping leaves per-position weight under-specified — a 2-slot allocation with equal weights (50% each) is economically different from a 2-slot allocation with conviction-proportional weights (e.g., 67%/33%). Confidence bands should fix BOTH slot count AND per-position sizing rule, with the rule chosen from a pre-registered menu.

Use the false_positive_ruin label as a separate evaluation cohort from false_negative_relative. The 27-case sample splits 8 ruin / 7 false-negative / 11 winner / 1 mixed; the ruin cohort is small enough that any rule claiming to filter ruins needs a confirmation set, not just discovery contrast.

Estimate CCM thresholds via bootstrap on the discovery cases with explicit confidence intervals; report the threshold as a band [0.3±δ, 1.0±δ] not as a point. Any point threshold reported without CI is methodologically incomplete.

Run the Experimental Designer's seven tests in the stated priority order; do not promote CCM to production until at least the first three (within-snapshot compression, absolute floor orthogonality, counterfactual bundle indistinguishability) produce decisive results on held-out snapshots.

Cap CCM's role at FILTERING, not at RANKING. Top1 and Top2 identity must continue to come from the underlying conviction bundle, not from CCM. CCM answers 'should we deploy at all, and how concentrated?' — not 'which candidate wins?'

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Define a three-leg position policy DSL with explicit legs {alpha_leg, diversification_leg, cash_leg}, where each leg carries its own expected return, volatility, and contribution to total risk. Slot count and per-position weights are outputs of leg-allocation rules, not inputs. CCM gates the alpha_leg size; the cash_leg size is derived from (1 - alpha_leg_weight - diversification_leg_weight); the diversification_leg is populated only when CCM < threshold AND an independent diversification-value check passes.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Prior roles implicitly treated slot count as a 1D dial for confidence. This DSL makes the three legs first-class, forces explicit attribution of return, and prevents the conflation that 'fewer slots = safer' that the Researcher accepted without challenge.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: DIRECTLY addresses capacity abstention: the cash_leg weight is the abstention magnitude, and its computation requires CCM AND absolute floor AND diversification-value check before any slot is deployed. Without any of the three, the policy defaults to full cash (3-slot abstention).

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Introduce a 'regime-conditional CCM' that recomputes the z-scoring reference window and the feature bundle based on the current market breadth proxy (e.g., % of universe above 50-day MA). A high-CCM reading in a deteriorating breadth regime is downgraded by a multiplicative regime factor; a high-CCM reading in a strengthening regime is upgraded. Regime factor is NOT in the candidate-feature bundle — it is an external scaler.
