dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The Skeptic's core attack on the bundle was that it is blind to regime/event risk (entity_6618d3e80c-style ruins with strong feature profile). The Researcher's proposed regime filter was mentioned as a 'must be added if high-CCM ruins persist' but not formalized. This DSL makes the regime scaler a first-class operator that sits between CCM computation and slot allocation, satisfying the separation-of-mechanism requirement.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Addresses the failure mode where CCM signals full deployment right before a regime shift that produces ruin in otherwise strong-feature candidates. Capacity abstention becomes regime-aware: abstain not because of weak candidates but because of a hostile macro envelope.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Define an 'abstention-as-position' DSL primitive: when the policy abstains (0 slots deployed or all-cash state), it must declare (a) the cash_leg return assumption (e.g., short-rate + X bps for optionality value), (b) the re-entry trigger condition (which snapshot statistic, at which threshold, would re-enable deployment), and (c) the maximum abstention duration before mandatory re-evaluation. Abstention is not a null state — it is an active position with explicit entry/exit logic.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Neither the Researcher, Skeptic, nor Experimental Designer treated abstention as a state with its own lifecycle. The Researcher's policy treats 1-slot and 2-slot states as having a 'cash held' leg but does not specify when cash becomes a position vs. a residual. This DSL makes abstention an explicit state machine, which is the only way to evaluate whether abstention is capacity-driven (insufficient high-CCM candidates) versus regime-driven (hostile environment) versus discovery-driven (insufficient evidence).
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: This is the core capacity-abstention primitive: it separates 'cannot deploy' from 'choose not to deploy' from 'do not yet know if we can deploy'. Each reason code triggers a different recovery path, preventing the conflation of evidence-absence with evidence-of-absence.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Define a 'bundle-indistinguishability guard' DSL operator that, given any candidate confidence statistic, automatically tests it against K=5 counterfactual bundles sampled from a pre-registered feature allowlist. If more than 2 of 5 counterfactuals produce statistically indistinguishable margin distributions, the candidate statistic is flagged as 'non-mechanism-specific' and downgraded to informational status (logged but not policy-binding). This codifies the Experimental Designer's counterfactual_bundle_indistinguishability_test as a mandatory pre-deployment check.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The Skeptic's strongest attack was multiple-comparisons / non-specificity of the bundle. The Researcher's proposed bundle is just one of many 4-feature subsets that would produce a CCM-like statistic. This DSL operator turns the 'any bundle could have produced this' critique into an automatic gate, rather than a one-time philosophical objection.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents the system from over-committing capital to a confidence proxy that is actually a generic z-score margin. Capacity abstention becomes the safe default whenever the guard fires: if the statistic is non-specific, do not let it gate capital, default to cash or to the most conservative rule in the pre-registered menu.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Define a 'concentration-cost DSL' that, given a target slot count n in {1,2,3}, a sizing rule S in {equal, conviction_proportional, kelly_capped}, and a fixed capital C, computes the realized per-position risk contribution including cross-position correlation from the snapshot's own candidate covariance. The output is the policy's actual risk budget, not its nominal slot count. The DSL rejects any (n, S) pair whose realized risk exceeds a pre-registered ceiling, regardless of CCM signal.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The Researcher's mapping {CCM>1 → 1 slot, ...} implicitly assumed slot count equals confidence equals risk. This DSL makes risk explicit and rejectable. It also surfaces the case where CCM says '1 slot' but the candidate pool has correlated Top1/Top2 such that 1 slot carries 80% of the pool variance — a configuration where the policy should downgrade to 2 slots despite the high-CCM signal.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Concentration risk is the primary mechanism by which 'high confidence' becomes 'high ruin' (as seen in the false_positive_ruin cohort where B0_pick=true implied full concentration). This DSL prevents CCM from forcing concentration in configurations where concentration is structurally dangerous, which is the operational form of capacity-aware abstention.

cycles.question: For large Top1-vs-Top2 quality gap, determine how to falsify an adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: Under a large Top1-vs-Top2 quality gap, the marginal PIT-observable alpha of slots 2 and 3 is negative-expectancy because (a) the false-negative pool is structurally weaker on the same features that predict Top1 success (up_day_ratio, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50; standardized deltas −0.6 to −1.2), and (b) ruin probability compounds with position count while Top1 conviction capital shrinks. An adaptive rule that still fills 2 or 3 slots during high-gap regimes violates a regime-conditional Kelly logic and is falsifiable.
evidence_for: Numeric contrast table shows false_negatives sit below selected_winners on every momentum/quality proxy: up_day_ratio_20 (0.500 vs 0.625), vol_ratio_5_20 (1.179 vs 1.424), mom_20 (0.058 vs 0.163), px_vs_ma50 (0.056 vs 0.127), ma10_slope_5 (0.012 vs 0.027) — so Top2/Top3 candidates in high-gap regimes are not just 'slightly worse' but measurably degraded across the same PIT features that identify Top1.

8 of 27 archaeology cases are false_positive_ruin on B0 itself; ruin exposure scales multiplicatively with slot count (3× ruin probability for 3 slots vs 1× for 1 slot under independent ruin), so a high-gap regime that still fans out to 3 slots triples tail-loss surface.

pullback_pct median delta is +8.6pp (false_negatives at −7.3% vs winners at −15.9%) — the false-negative pool includes stocks with shallow pullbacks that look 'safe' but lack the deep-base momentum signature, reinforcing that gap-driven skipping is empirically supported.

is_b0_pick=false cases still achieve w4_return_bucket = large_win (e.g., entity_de1c657364, entity_535a1beed7), but only n=2 qualify as 'big winner' (≥8% AND ≥5pp above B0 median) — the rare payoff does not compensate systematic quality decay.

Base_duration_weeks median delta is −8 weeks for false_negatives; longer bases are characteristic of established leaders, so filling slots with shorter-base candidates violates base-effect compounding.
evidence_against: The single false_positive_ruin|selected_winner case (entity_6618d3e80c) shows Top1 can both win and ruin in different windows — concentration on 1 slot does not eliminate ruin, only reduces its frequency.

11 selected_winner cases demonstrate that B0 selection itself is reliable in >40% of archaeology; a 'concentrate to 1' rule still accepts ruin risk and forgoes positive-skew outcomes from slot-2 hits.
Diversification counterargument: 1-slot portfolio has higher variance than 3-slot under non-zero Top2 win rate; if Top2 win rate is even modest, variance reduction may dominate expected-return loss.

Method note restricts false-negative labeling to ≥8% W4 AND ≥5pp above B0 selected median — under that bar, false-negative rate is small (n=2 of 27), suggesting the gap-skipping penalty is rare rather than pervasive.

The numeric_contrasts are false_negative vs selected_winner, not Top1 vs Top2 directly — we lack an explicit Top2 quality score, so the 'gap' is inferred from a downstream cohort rather than measured at the time of selection.
falsifiable_predictions: Regime-conditional test: stratify all live candidates by Top1-Top2 quality gap (e.g., top-decile vs bottom-decile) and compare equal-weight-3 vs concentrated-1 vs concentrated-2 Sharpe. Predicted outcome: concentrated-1 dominates concentrated-2 dominates equal-weight-3 in the high-gap decile; rank order inverts or flattens in the low-gap decile.

Ruin incidence test: count false_positive_ruin events per slot deployed in high-gap regimes. Predicted outcome: ruin-event rate per dollar of capital deployed is non-increasing in position count only when the gap is large; under small gaps, ruin-event rate per dollar decreases with more positions (diversification benefit dominates).

W4 return variance test: portfolio W4 return std-dev should fall monotonically with slot count in high-gap regimes (1 > 2 > 3 in std-dev) but expected W4 return should fall faster than std-dev for slot 3 vs slot 1, producing lower Sharpe for the 3-slot allocation.

Interaction test: regression of realized W4 return on (slot_count × gap_bucket) should produce a significant negative coefficient on slot_count restricted to the high-gap bucket. A non-significant or positive coefficient falsifies the gap-conditional concentration hypothesis.

PIT-feature falsifier: if pre-entry up_day_ratio_20 of slot-2 candidate exceeds 0.6 AND vol_ratio_5_20 exceeds 1.4, then the 'large gap' classification should be overridden and slot 2 included — otherwise the rule is over-fit to the Top1-only cohort and will miss the entity_535a1beed7 / entity_de1c657364 archetype.

Ruin clustering test: false_positive_ruin cases cluster on snapshot_anon (e.g., snap_71486ed83c, snap_b8420124eb, snap_d0d57b1e40 each contain multiple ruins); a regime-aware capacity rule that throttles to 1 slot on those snapshots should reduce ruin-cluster P&L impact by >50% versus a 3-slot allocation.
policy_implications: Capacity rule should be encoded as a regime filter: capacity = 1 when Top1−Top2 gap > threshold τ (high-gap), capacity = 2 or 3 when gap ≤ τ (low-gap). Threshold τ should be set so the upper-tail false-negative rate (≥8% W4 AND ≥5pp gap) is below a calibrated break-even probability.

Economic meaning under fixed 3-slot capital: '1 position' = full Top1 conviction, max idiosyncratic risk, minimum ruin-multiplier; '2 positions' = Top1 + quality-tier hedge, partial ruin-multiplier, intermediate Sharpe profile; '3 positions' = forced dilution including a Top3 that by gap definition is the weakest, producing the worst risk-adjusted profile in high-gap regimes.

Distinguish capacity from sizing: capacity 1 means 100% of capital in Top1; capacity 2 with equal-weight means 50/50; the rule must specify allocation as well as count, because filling 3 slots at 33% each is economically different from 60/30/10 weighted.

Refutation protocol: any adaptive rule that defaults to 3 slots in high-gap regimes should be rejected a priori; empirical defense requires showing 3-slot allocation has higher Sharpe than 1-slot in that regime, which the archaeology does not support.

Reject the rule if a single high-gap snapshot shows 3 simultaneous false_positive_ruins (the worst outcome class for fixed-3-slot capital) — the archaeological frequency of ruin-clustered snapshots (≥3 ruins per snap_anon) implies 3-slot deployment in those snapshots is the dominant tail-loss path.

Monitor false_negative_big_winner rate as the cost of concentration; if it exceeds a calibration ceiling (e.g., >5% of high-gap regimes produce a missed ≥8% Top2), the gap threshold τ should be tightened to widen the 2-slot allocation band.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The 'high-gap → concentrate to 1 slot' rule rests on a tautological feature comparison (false_negatives look weak on the SAME features B0 used to select winners), ignores that 1-slot concentration triples position size (so ruin severity per dollar is NOT lower than 3-slot), and assumes ruin events are independent across slots when the archaeology shows they cluster by snapshot_anon — meaning a 3-slot allocation in a single bad regime and a 1-slot allocation in that same regime both bear nearly the full ruin tail. The prior claim of 'negative-expectancy marginal alpha' for slots 2/3 is asserted, never derived: the false-negative W4 buckets are large_win, not loss, so the cohort is winners-by-construction rather than losers-by-mechanism.

attacks.issue: Selection-on-observables / tautological contrast: the false_negative cohort is defined as B0 REJECTIONS, and the 'numeric contrasts' measure them against selected_winners on the SAME features B0 uses for selection. The standardized deltas of −0.6 to −1.2 are not evidence of degraded alpha — they are the mechanical footprint of the selection rule. Using them to justify abstention from the rejected tier is circular.
attacks.why_it_matters: The whole falsification logic depends on slots 2/3 being 'structurally weaker.' If that weakness is definitionally guaranteed by what B0 rejects, then any rule that fills slots with B0-rejected stocks will look 'bad' on these features by construction, regardless of whether the stocks actually underperform at W4. The mechanism is not identified.

attacks.issue: Position-sizing confound ignored: under 'fixed 3-slot capital,' moving from 3 slots (≈33% each) to 1 slot (100%) triples per-name exposure. The prior argues ruin PROBABILITY per name is 3× higher with 3 slots, but ruin DOLLAR magnitude per dollar deployed is unchanged (independent ruin) or WORSE (correlated ruin). The 1-slot rule therefore does NOT reduce tail-loss per dollar of capital — it concentrates it.
attacks.why_it_matters: Economic meaning of capacity is conflated with economic meaning of sizing. A 1-slot 100% position and a 3-slot 33% position have identical ruin probability per dollar under independence; under positive correlation the 1-slot is strictly worse. The 'capital preservation' justification collapses once position size is restored.

attacks.issue: Ruin clustering by snapshot_anon violates the independence assumption. snap_71486ed83c, snap_b8420124eb, snap_d0d57b1e40 each contain MULTIPLE false_positive_ruin cases (and one snapshot also contains a selected_winner). Ruin is correlated within regime. Diversification across 3 slots within a single regime therefore buys little variance reduction if all candidates share the same macro shock.
attacks.why_it_matters: If ruin is correlated across slots within a snapshot, then 1-slot concentration in that snapshot actually INCREASES portfolio ruin severity. The archaeology data — not a model assumption — shows the ruins cluster. The adaptive rule needs to throttle by snapshot regime, not by candidate gap, or it misallocates risk.

attacks.issue: Labeling asymmetry: false_negative requires W4 ≥8% AND ≥5pp above B0 selected MEDIAN (a strict bar); selected_winner requires only is_b0_pick=true (a permissive label). The two cohorts are not symmetrically constructed, so a head-to-head feature comparison is biased against the rejected tier. entity_535a1beed7 and entity_de1c657364 achieve large_win but only the 'big_winner' sublabel counts toward the contrast — this is conditioning on the outcome that makes the prior claim look strongest.
attacks.why_it_matters: The prior's claim that 'rare payoff does not compensate systematic quality decay' is partially an artifact of the asymmetric label definition. With a symmetric label (e.g., both require ≥8% W4), the false-negative rate among B0 rejects would rise and the apparent gap would shrink.

attacks.issue: B0's own hit rate is weak: 11 selected_winner vs 8 false_positive_ruin among 19 is_b0_pick=true cases → ≈58% win rate, ≈42% ruin rate. If Top1 itself ruins 42% of the time at full position size, then 'concentrating on Top1' in a high-gap regime concentrates a coin with substantial ruin probability. The 'Top1 conviction' narrative is empirically thin.
attacks.why_it_matters: The adaptive rule assumes Top1 alpha is large enough that concentrating 100% of capital into it is superior to diversification. With a 42% ruin rate at full size, expected-value calculations are dominated by ruin-tail magnitude and need explicit dollar-weighting, which the prior did not perform.

attacks.issue: Missing data is MNAR: 11 of 27 cases have null pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct (no base yet formed). The numeric contrasts on pullback_pct (Δ=+8.6pp) and pullback_duration_weeks (Δ=−1.5wk) therefore describe a non-random subset — likely the candidates whose bases have already broken out and pulled back, biasing the 'deep base' signature toward B0 picks.
attacks.why_it_matters: The 'deep base = winner' mechanism is inferred from a sub-sample that excludes stocks currently forming one. A rule that abstains from these stocks will systematically miss fresh breakout candidates whose pullback history has not yet accumulated.

attacks.issue: Sample size n=27 is severely underpowered for the claims made. The numeric_contrasts table contains ~24 features; with this n, multiple-comparison corrections would shrink most standardized deltas. A delta of −0.5 to −1.2 σ on individual features is consistent with noise across a 20+ feature screen.
attacks.why_it_matters: Without a pre-registered feature subset or holdout validation, the 'structural weakness' claim is statistically fragile. A skeptic should demand that the gap-threshold τ be derived on a separate sample before the rule is treated as falsifiable rather than exploratory.

attacks.issue: Gap magnitude is post-hoc, not PIT: the 'Top1-Top2 quality gap' is inferred from the false_negative cohort's feature deltas, not from a contemporaneous quality score on the ranked Top2 candidate at the time of selection. There is no measurable τ that an algorithm can apply at decision time without reconstructing the rejection cohort.
attacks.why_it_matters: An adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule requires a decision-time computable gap. If the gap is only knowable after-the-run, the rule is unfalsifiable in production — every outcome can be reinterpreted as consistent with whatever gap bucket it lands in.

counterexamples_to_seek: A high-gap regime where the B0-rejected slot-2 candidate had up_day_ratio_20 > 0.6 AND vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.4 AND mom_20 > 0.15 AND won W4 by ≥10% — entity_535a1beed7 and entity_de1c657364 are near-misses under the strict labeling but should be re-examined under a symmetric label to test whether the gap rule systematically excludes these archetypes.

A snapshot_anon (e.g., snap_d0d57b1e40) where one B0 pick was a selected_winner AND another was a false_positive_ruin (entity_6618d3e80c carries both labels) — this demonstrates that within-snapshot ruin is not eliminated by Top1 focus; the same Top1 conviction that wins in one window ruins in another.

A snapshot with ≥3 false_positive_ruin cases (snap_71486ed83c qualifies) where a 3-slot allocation across DIFFERENT sectors within that snapshot would have hedged the regime — proving that within-snapshot diversification can be constructed even when cross-snapshot regime is hostile.

An out-of-time period where the 1-slot concentration rule produced lower Sharpe than the 3-slot equal-weight rule in a high-gap regime — falsifies the regime-conditional concentration hypothesis directly.

A case where the 'Top1' pick had shallower pullback (closer to 0%) and shallower base_duration_weeks than the B0-rejected slot-2 candidate — this would show that B0 selection is not strictly dominated on the 'deep base' axis and that the gap-rule misses valid bases still forming.

A large-gap regime where 3 independent candidates (different sectors, different supply/demand signatures) had ruin probability BELOW the single Top1's ruin probability — i.e., diversification benefit dominates even when individual Top2/Top3 features look weak.
what_would_change_my_mind: Demonstration that ruin events are statistically independent ACROSS candidates within a snapshot (correlation test within snap_anon) — without this, 3-slot deployment cannot be claimed riskier per dollar than 1-slot.

A pre-registered, decision-time computable Top1-Top2 quality gap (e.g., a specific z-score on a PIT ranking) that produces higher Sharpe for capacity=1 vs capacity=3 in an out-of-sample test of ≥50 high-gap regime observations.
Re-analysis with symmetric labeling (both false_negative and selected_winner require W4 ≥8%) showing the standardized feature deltas persist at ≥0.5 σ — currently the asymmetry is a confound.

Evidence that B0's selected_winner cohort's W4 returns are robust to position-sizing (i.e., a 100% allocation in Top1 doesn't ruin 42% of the time as the raw archaeology suggests), so that concentration is not a tail-risk amplifier.

A within-snapshot counterfactual showing realized W4 return distribution of the equal-weight-3 portfolio vs the 100%-Top1 portfolio in the SAME snapshot — currently we have no joint outcomes, only marginal labels.

Multiple-comparison correction applied to the 24-feature contrast table (e.g., Benjamini-Hochberg) leaving at least 5 features with FDR-adjusted q < 0.1 — currently the feature-level deltas are exploratory.

An MNAR-adjusted analysis of pullback_pct / pullback_duration_weeks that accounts for the 11/27 missing-value cases, showing the +8.6pp delta survives imputation rather than being a selection artifact.

tests.name: within_snapshot_joint_realized_counterfactual
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot_anon, treat co-occurring entities as a candidate pool and compute equal-weight-1 (100% Top1), equal-weight-2 (Top1+Top2), and equal-weight-3 (Top1+Top2+Top3) realized W4 bucket mixtures using w4_return_bucket mapped to numeric payoffs (ruin=-1.0, loss=-0.5, small_win=+0.5, large_win=+1.0). Average across snapshots stratified by within-snapshot Top1-Top2 feature gap (z-score on mom_20+up_day_ratio_20+vol_ratio_5_20+px_vs_ma50).
tests.success_criterion: In the high-gap stratum (top tercile of within-snapshot gap), mean 1-slot payoff > mean 3-slot payoff by ≥0.20 AND 1-slot hit rate of 'large_win' > 3-slot hit rate.
tests.failure_criterion: 3-slot payoff ≥ 1-slot payoff in the high-gap stratum, OR the gap-stratified difference is not monotone (low-gap ≤ high-gap in reverse).

tests.name: position_sizing_adjusted_ruin_per_dollar
tests.comparison: For each snapshot, compute ruin event rate (w4_return_bucket=='ruin') and ruin magnitude per dollar deployed under four capital accounting schemes: (A) 1-slot at 100%, (B) 2-slot at 50/50, (C) 3-slot at 33/33/33, (D) 1-slot at 60% + cash 40% (capacity-1 with sizing haircut). Ruin-per-dollar = P(ruin) × ruin_magnitude × slot_weight.
tests.success_criterion: In high-gap snapshots, ruin-per-dollar for (A) ≤ ruin-per-dollar for (C) by ≥30% (concentration genuinely reduces ruin exposure per dollar).
tests.failure_criterion: Ruin-per-dollar for (A) is equal to or greater than (C) — i.e., concentrating does NOT reduce ruin exposure per dollar of capital, falsifying the 'ruin-multiplier' mechanism.

tests.name: snapshot_ruin_clustering_independence_test
tests.comparison: Compute (i) the empirical probability that two independent candidates within the same snapshot_anon both ruin (P_ruin^2 under independence), (ii) the observed co-ruin rate among all pairs of co-snapshot entities, and (iii) a Fisher exact / chi-square test of within-snapshot ruin independence. Restrict to snapshots with ≥3 entities.
tests.success_criterion: Observed co-ruin rate ≤ P_independent × 1.5 (no meaningful positive dependence; diversification within snapshot is well-defined).
tests.failure_criterion: Observed co-ruin rate ≥ 2× P_independent (ruin is correlated within snapshot; 3-slot deployment within a hostile snapshot provides little variance reduction, and the diversification half of the prior's logic collapses).

tests.name: PIT_computable_gap_score_construction
tests.comparison: Construct a decision-time computable Top1-Top2 gap = |z(Top1) − z(Top2)| where z is the cross-sectional z-score of a fixed composite (mean of z-scored mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50) computed only from PIT features observable before entry. Verify gap is (i) finite and non-degenerate for ≥80% of snapshot×Top2 pairs, (ii) uncorrelated with w4_return_bucket at the Top2 level (i.e., the gap itself is not a leak of the outcome), and (iii) monotone in the false_negative cohort's standardized deltas.
tests.success_criterion: Gap is computable for ≥80% of candidate pairs AND its tercile partition reproduces the false-negative vs selected_winner cohort separation with standardized delta ≥0.5 σ on at least one of mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20.
tests.failure_criterion: Gap is undefined for >20% of pairs, OR its tercile partition fails to separate the two cohorts (delta <0.3 σ on all four composite features), demonstrating the rule is not operationalizable at decision time.

tests.name: symmetric_labeling_contrast_retest
tests.comparison: Re-compute the numeric_contrasts table under symmetric labeling: restrict BOTH is_b0_pick=true and is_b0_pick=false cohorts to w4_return_bucket in {large_win} AND apply the same ≥8% W4 + ≥5pp-above-cohort-median rule used for the false-negative bar. Re-derive standardized deltas on all 10 PIT features.
tests.success_criterion: Standardized delta of false_negative_minus_selected_winner remains ≤-0.5 σ on at least 5 of 10 features under symmetric labeling (the alpha-decay claim survives label-symmetry correction).
tests.failure_criterion: Standardized deltas compress to between -0.3 and +0.3 σ on ≥7 of 10 features — the apparent gap is an artifact of asymmetric cohort construction.

tests.name: FDR_corrected_feature_persistence
tests.comparison: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at q=0.10 to the full set of 23 standardized deltas in the false_negative vs selected_winner contrast. Count features that survive.
tests.success_criterion: ≥5 features survive FDR q < 0.10 with absolute standardized delta ≥0.5.
tests.failure_criterion: <3 features survive FDR correction — the 'structural weakness' signature is exploratory noise across a wide screen.

tests.name: ruin_cluster_snapshot_throttle_test
tests.comparison: Identify snapshots with ≥2 false_positive_ruin cases (the clustered-ruin snapshots in the archaeology: snap_71486ed83c, snap_b8420124eb, snap_d0d57b1e40). Within those snapshots, compute realized payoff under three regime-aware rules: (i) throttle to 0 slots (full abstain), (ii) throttle to 1 slot (Top1 only), (iii) maintain 3 slots equal-weight. Compare aggregate payoff.
tests.success_criterion: Throttle-to-0 OR throttle-to-1 yields strictly higher aggregate payoff than 3-slot in clustered-ruin snapshots (regime throttling adds value beyond simple slot count).
tests.failure_criterion: 3-slot aggregate payoff ≥ throttle-to-1 in clustered-ruin snapshots — the ruin damage is concentrated within Top1 itself and slot-count throttling does not address it.

tests.name: MNAR_sensitivity_pullback_signature
tests.comparison: Among the 11/27 cases with null pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct, impute using available base_* and ibd_entry_* features via median imputation stratified by is_b0_pick and snapshot_anon cluster. Re-derive the false_negative vs selected_winner pullback_pct delta and pullback_duration_weeks delta with imputed values included.
tests.success_criterion: Pullback_pct delta remains ≥+4pp (i.e., false_negatives still show shallower pullbacks after MNAR imputation) and pullback_duration_weeks delta remains ≤-1 week.
tests.failure_criterion: Pullback_pct delta collapses to <+2pp OR reverses sign after imputation — the 'deep base = winner' mechanism is selection-biased by missingness.

tests.name: top1_ruin_tail_capacity1_falsifier
tests.comparison: Compute the empirical ruin rate (w4_return_bucket=='ruin') and loss rate (w4_return_bucket in {loss, ruin}) among is_b0_pick=true entities, both unconditionally and conditioned on the high-gap strata (using the PIT-computable gap from test 4). The capacity=1 rule assumes Top1 ruin rate is low enough that full concentration is tolerable.
tests.success_criterion: Top1 ruin rate <25% AND loss+ruin rate <50% in the high-gap stratum (concentration is empirically defensible).
tests.failure_criterion: Top1 ruin rate ≥35% OR loss+ruin rate ≥60% in the high-gap stratum — concentration of full capital on Top1 amplifies a tail that is itself ruin-prone, so the 'Top1 conviction' premise of the adaptive rule is violated regardless of Top2/Top3 quality.

tests.name: high_gap_within_snapshot_diversification_within_sector_breaker
tests.comparison: Within each high-gap snapshot, partition entities into 'high-feature-coherence' (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50 all above snapshot median) and 'low-feature-coherence' subsets. Compare 3-slot equal-weight payoff on the high-coherence subset vs the snapshot-wide 3-slot allocation. Tests whether diversification across high-coherence candidates within an otherwise hostile regime rescues the 3-slot outcome.
tests.success_criterion: Within-snapshot high-coherence 3-slot payoff > snapshot-wide 3-slot payoff AND > high-gap 1-slot payoff (diversification can be reconstructed along a feature-coherence axis).
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot high-coherence 3-slot payoff ≤ snapshot-wide 3-slot payoff — the high-coherence subset ruins together (feature-coherence = correlation), confirming the snapshot-level correlation finding from test 3.

leakage_checks: Verify no test uses w4_return_bucket, outcome_label, entity_anon, or snapshot_anon as an input feature (only as stratification or outcome variables).

Verify the PIT-computable gap construction (test 4) does NOT include any feature whose value is determined by or updated after the entry trigger (ibd_entry_* features are entry-time and acceptable; w4_* and post-W4 features are excluded).
Verify that the imputation in test 8 does not use w4_return_bucket, outcome_label, or any feature whose value is only defined post-outcome.
Verify that snapshot_anon is used only as a grouping/stratification variable, never as a numeric input or one-hot encoded into the model.
Verify no test introduces outer-forward outcomes (no W4 returns beyond the frozen w4_return_bucket labels, no forward-looking labels beyond what's in the archaeology).
Verify that is_b0_pick is treated as a cohort label (not a feature) in tests 5, 6, 8 to avoid tautological selection-on-observables leakage.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: Under large Top1-Top2 quality gaps, the adaptive capacity rule hypothesizes that the marginal PIT-observable alpha of slots 2 and 3 is negative-expectancy because (i) false-negative pools show systematic decay on the same features that identify Top1 success (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50; standardized deltas −0.6 to −1.2 σ), (ii) ruin probability compounds multiplicatively with slot count under independent ruin (3× surface for 3 slots vs 1× for 1 slot), and (iii) base-duration and pullback-depth decay signals suggest structural rather than transient weakness. However, the contrast is a downstream cohort signature (false_negative_minus_selected_winner), not a direct Top1-vs-Top2 measurement at decision time; the rule therefore stands or falls on whether the gap is PIT-constructible AND monotone in the same cohort signal under symmetric labeling. The architecture must separate predictive mechanism (gap estimation) from portfolio-construction effect (slot count × sizing × ruin-cluster correlation), because concentration to 1 slot and dilution to 3 slots trade off in a regime-conditional way that is not currently identifiable from n=27 with n=2 false-negative big-winners and snapshot-level ruin clustering on only 3 snapshots.
falsifiers: PRIMARY FALSIFIER — PIT_computable_gap_score_construction (Experimental Designer test 4): if the decision-time-computable gap (z-score difference on the 4-feature composite) is undefined for >20% of Top1×Top2 pairs OR its tercile partition fails to reproduce the false_negative-vs-selected_winner cohort separation with ≥0.5 σ on any single composite feature, the rule has no operational anchor at decision time and must be rejected. This is the load-bearing test because the entire adaptive logic depends on a measurable, pre-entry gap.

SECONDARY FALSIFIER — symmetric_labeling_contrast_retest (test 5): if recomputing the 10 PIT-feature standardized deltas under symmetric B0-vs-non-B0 labeling restricted to w4_return_bucket=='large_win' compresses the deltas to the [−0.3, +0.3] band on ≥7 of 10 features, the apparent quality gradient is a tautological artifact of the asymmetric outcome-based cohort construction, not an empirical signal.

TERTIARY FALSIFIER — top1_ruin_tail_capacity1_falsifier (test 9): if Top1 ruin rate in the high-gap stratum is ≥35% OR loss+ruin rate is ≥60%, then concentrating to 1 slot under high-gap conditions amplifies a tail that is itself ruin-prone; the 'Top1 conviction' premise of capacity=1 collapses and the rule must instead throttle to 0 (full abstain) or apply sizing haircuts.

QUATERNARY FALSIFIER — snapshot_ruin_clustering_independence_test (test 3): if observed co-ruin rate among snapshot-co-occurring entities is ≥2× the independence null P_ruin^2, then diversification across slots within a hostile snapshot provides little variance reduction; the diversification benefit that could justify capacity=2 or 3 disappears, and capacity must become a regime throttle (0 or 1) rather than a conviction expression.

INTERACTION-TERM FALSIFIER: if a regression of realized W4 return on (slot_count × gap_bucket) restricted to the high-gap bucket produces a non-negative or statistically insignificant coefficient on slot_count, the gap-conditional concentration hypothesis fails empirically and the adaptive rule is no better than a fixed-capacity baseline.

MNAR FALSIFIER — test 8: if pullback_pct delta collapses to <+2pp or reverses sign after median-imputation of the 11/27 null pullback cases stratified by is_b0_pick and snapshot_anon, the 'deep-base = winner' mechanism is selection-biased by missingness and cannot anchor the gap definition.
actionable_design_principles: Separate the predictive mechanism (PIT-computable Top1−Top2 gap) from the portfolio-construction effect (slot count × per-slot weight × ruin-cluster correlation). The rule must be expressible as gap(g) → capacity(c) → sizing(w), and each step must be independently falsifiable.

Distinguish capacity (number of slots) from sizing (per-slot weight). Capacity=1 with 100% allocation is economically different from capacity=1 with 60% allocation + 40% cash; capacity=2 equal-weight is different from capacity=2 with 60/40 Top1-heavy. The archaeology supports slot-count analysis but does not yet justify any specific weight scheme.

The adaptive rule must encode a 0-slot fallback. The evidence that B0 itself ruins in 8/27 cases (≈30% ruin rate on the selected cohort) and that ruin clusters within snapshots (snap_71486ed83c, snap_b8420124eb, snap_d0d57b1e40) means even Top1 conviction is not a sufficient condition for deployment; the rule must allow full abstain when both Top1 ruin-tail probability AND snapshot-cluster ruin probability are simultaneously elevated.

Treat the false-negative cost (missed big winners like entity_535a1beed7 and entity_de1c657364) as an explicit calibration ceiling. With n=2 false-negative big-winners under the strict ≥8% W4 AND ≥5pp-above-median bar, the cost-of-concentration is empirically small; the rule must not over-weight it relative to the n=8 false-positive-ruin cost.

The rule should be expressed as a tiered regime: (a) high-gap + low-snapshot-ruin-cluster → capacity=1, full weight; (b) high-gap + high-snapshot-ruin-cluster → capacity=0; (c) low-gap → capacity=2 or 3 with equal weight. This separates regime throttling from conviction expression.

Any deployment of the adaptive rule must include a holdout validation step on the symmetric-labeling retest before live use. The tautology risk is the dominant epistemic threat and must be closed before the rule is trusted.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: regime_gap_capacity_policy
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Encodes the gap-thresholded capacity logic with explicit separation of gap estimation, capacity selection, and sizing; allows 0-slot abstain as a first-class state rather than treating it as a corner case.
features: pit_gap_score = abs(z_composite(Top1) - z_composite(Top2)) computed on {mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50} via cross-sectional z-scoring within snapshot_anon
snapshot_ruin_cluster_rate = count(w4_return_bucket=='ruin') / count(co-occurring entities in same snapshot_anon)
top1_ruin_tail_prob = empirical ruin rate of Top1 conditioned on pit_gap_score tercile == 'high'
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Outputs capacity ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3} via piecewise rule: capacity=0 if snapshot_ruin_cluster_rate ≥ 0.4 OR top1_ruin_tail_prob ≥ 0.35; capacity=1 if pit_gap_score ≥ τ_high; capacity=2 if τ_low ≤ pit_gap_score < τ_high; capacity=3 if pit_gap_score < τ_low. Sizing is then applied within the chosen capacity (equal-weight within slot count by default).

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: capacity_with_sizing_haircut_policy
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Holds slot count at the adaptive output but applies a per-slot weight haircut proportional to ruin-tail probability; this is the test-2 (position_sizing_adjusted_ruin_per_dollar) operationalization and lets the rule express 'capacity=1 with conviction' vs 'capacity=1 with reduced exposure' as distinct economic choices.
features: ruin_per_dollar_estimate = empirical ruin rate × ruin magnitude (ruin = -1.0) conditioned on gap tercile and snapshot cluster
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: When the adaptive capacity rule outputs capacity=1 but ruin_per_dollar_estimate is elevated (e.g., 0.5), the effective deployment becomes 50% Top1 + 50% cash; this is economically distinct from capacity=1 with full weight and should be tracked as a separate outcome class in any backtest.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: snapshot_regime_throttle_policy
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: A pure regime throttle that ignores the Top1-Top2 gap and instead conditions capacity on snapshot-level ruin clustering alone; this is the test-7 (ruin_cluster_snapshot_throttle_test) operationalization and serves as a falsification benchmark — if this throttle alone outperforms the gap-based rule, the gap component adds no value.
features: snapshot_ruin_count = count(w4_return_bucket in {'ruin', 'loss'} for entities in snapshot_anon)
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: capacity=0 if snapshot_hostility ≥ 0.5; capacity=1 if 0.25 ≤ snapshot_hostility < 0.5; capacity=3 otherwise. This policy is intentionally gap-blind and is the cleanest comparison benchmark for the gap-conditional rule.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: adaptive_capacity_with_concentration_premium
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Augments the gap-conditional capacity rule with an explicit concentration-premium adjustment: when capacity=1 in a high-gap regime, the policy adds a conviction-multiplier to the slot weight (e.g., 1.0–1.3×) financed by reducing future capacity in adjacent regimes; this operationalizes the economic meaning that 1-position deployment under high gap is 'full Top1 conviction' rather than 'default minimum'.
features: concentration_premium = 1.0 + α × pit_gap_score where α is calibrated against historical Top1 hit rate in high-gap regime
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Makes capacity=1 economically meaningful as concentrated conviction (not just undiversified default) by encoding that the high-gap signal is itself the rationale for both reducing slot count AND increasing per-slot conviction — the two effects are coupled rather than independent.

cycles.question: For weak third candidate, determine when cash should dominate filling another slot. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: Under a fixed 3-slot capital structure, the marginal third candidate carries asymmetric tail risk: when its feature profile intersects the false-negative-relative region (lower up_day_ratio_20 ≤ ~0.55, mom_20 ≤ ~0.08, vol_ratio_5_20 ≤ ~1.25, weaker ma10/ma20 slopes), the conditional ruin probability rises faster than the conditional winner payoff because ruin magnitudes (w4 bucket 'ruin') exceed winner magnitudes ('large_win'/'small_win') on average. Forced inclusion of this weakest link therefore depresses the 3-position portfolio's expected value below both the 2-position portfolio (top-2 concentrated) and the 1-position portfolio (highest-conviction concentrated), making cash the dominant third-slot decision.
evidence_for: false_positive_ruin accounts for 8/27 (~30%) of archaeology cases, all with w4_return_bucket='ruin' — the ruin bucket is the largest single negative terminal state, confirming ruin is a heavy-tailed, asymmetric outcome, not a small drawdown.

Selected winners (11/27) cluster in 'large_win' while false-positive ruins cluster in 'ruin' with no overlapping w4 bucket — the terminal distribution of accepted names is bimodal between ruin and large_win, with little middle ground.

Numeric contrasts show false_negative vs selected_winner separations on up_day_ratio_20 (Δ-0.125, z=-1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (Δ-0.245, z=-1.05), mom_20 (Δ-0.105, z=-1.00) and px_vs_ma50 (Δ-0.071, z=-0.85): a weak third candidate by these definitions is essentially the same feature signature as a false-negative reject, meaning the marginal candidate has both elevated ruin probability AND weakened expected upside.

Among b0 picks, the false_positive_ruin|selected_winner case (entity_6618d3e80c) had identical setup features to entity_84824e6a20 (both strong momentum, high px_vs_ma50) yet terminal outcomes diverged — indicating that even top-tier feature profiles carry irreducible ruin risk, which compounds when forced into the weakest slot.

entity_2f86543bf6 (selected_winner, 'large_win') entered with NEGATIVE mom_20 (-0.008), negative ma20_slope, no pullback — a profile that any slot-quality filter would reject, demonstrating the existence of 'surprise winners' but these are exceptions, not the modal weak-slot profile.

Pullback_pct median for selected_winner is -15.9 vs -7.3 for false_negative — winners often came from deeper bases; a shallow, short pullback (weak-third signature) is associated with the rejection region, not the winner region.
evidence_against: Several false_negative_relative cases had 'large_win' buckets (entity_535a1beed7, entity_de1c657364) — names that the system rejected but produced large upside, implying that rejecting marginal candidates has its own opportunity cost that can rival ruin magnitudes.

entity_8ad5cd4795 reached 'large_win' despite near-zero momentum (mom_20=0.004), flat ma10/ma20 slopes, and only 5w/-6.7% pullback — a textbook weak-third profile that won big, weakening any strict-feature threshold rule.

False_negative_relative false-negative set has 5 cases with 'small_win' or 'loss' buckets, showing rejected candidates are mixed quality, not systematically superior — so 'always reject weak thirds' overweights the missed-large-winner tail.

The numeric_contrasts table has only 2 false_negative_big_winner cases, making the opportunity-cost side of the trade statistically thin; claim of asymmetric ruin-vs-winner magnitude is directionally supported but not robustly measured in this archaeology sample.

Fixed 3-slot rule may itself be the artifact: if portfolio construction were conviction-weighted (e.g., 60/30/10 or 50/30/20), the 'third candidate' question dissolves and the comparison of 1/2/3 equal-weight positions becomes moot — the asymmetry may be construction-induced, not intrinsic.
falsifiable_predictions: If we bucket archaeology cases into 'weak third candidate' profiles (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55 AND mom_20 ≤ 0.08 AND vol_ratio_5_20 ≤ 1.30 simultaneously), the ruin probability in this bucket should exceed 40%, versus <25% for the strong counterpart — falsifiable by re-scoring the archaeology set under the proposed rule.

A simulated 2-slot portfolio that holds only the top-2 names per snapshot and leaves the third slot in cash should produce higher risk-adjusted return (Sharpe or Sortino) than the equal-weight 3-slot portfolio on the same discovery-train set, given that the 8 ruin cases would have been avoided by the 2-slot rule.

The 'cash dominates' decision boundary should fall at a feature composite (e.g., normalized sum of up_day_ratio, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, ma10_slope_5) below approximately the 35th percentile of selected winners — falsifiable by computing the empirical ruin rate by composite-score decile.

If the third candidate's px_vs_ma20 < 0.04 AND px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 AND pullback_duration_weeks is null (no base), the ruin probability should be ≥50% — a narrow, testable weak-base rule derived from the FN-region medians.

The expected value of adding a weak-third (profile matched to false_negative_relative region) to a 2-position portfolio should be negative in-sample: E[Δportfolio] = p_win × avg_win + (1-p_win) × avg_ruin < 0, verifiable directly on the archaeology outcomes.

Sharpe ratio of 1-position (top-1 only, 2/3 cash) should exceed 3-position (equal weight) when top-1 is in the upper-half of selected_winner feature composites — falsifiable by ranking archaeology by top-1 score and comparing portfolio constructions.
policy_implications: Replace the fixed 3-slot equal-weight rule with a conviction-weighted allocation (e.g., 50/30/20 or 40/30/30) so that a weak third candidate receives a smaller position rather than equal weight, preserving most of the diversification benefit while shrinking ruin exposure.

Adopt a 'cash buffer' rule: when the marginal candidate's composite score falls below a threshold calibrated to the false_negative_region median, leave the slot in cash. Threshold should be tuned on the discovery set (e.g., up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55 OR mom_20 ≤ 0.08 as a soft veto).

The economic meaning comparison: 1 position = high-conviction concentration, lowest diversification, highest opportunity cost; 2 positions = best risk-adjusted when third is weak (top-2 quality + 1/3 cash drag); 3 positions = only justified when ALL three candidates clear the composite threshold — otherwise the weakest link is a hidden short-vol bet.

Explicitly model the ruin-vs-win magnitude asymmetry in position sizing: since ruin magnitude exceeds winner magnitude (per the bimodal w4 bucket distribution), Kelly-style sizing should reduce the marginal third position below equal weight even when expected value is positive.

Track a 'weak third' rejection counter as a real-time policy variable — if rejection rate of marginal thirds exceeds ~50% of weeks, the slot-filling rule is structurally biased toward ruin and needs recalibration.

Consider widening the snapshot evidence to include b0-rejected but not-yet-bucketed names so the opportunity-cost side of the cash-vs-fill trade has statistical parity with the ruin side; current archaeology under-samples false_negative_big_winner (n=2).

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The 'cash dominates the weak third slot' claim is probably wrong because the conditioning set is circular, the ruin label is sample-clustered rather than candidate-driven, and the opportunity-cost side is under-powered to within statistical noise. The 27-case discovery-train archaeology cannot distinguish a feature-based ruin probability from a snapshot-regime artifact, and the proposed 1/2/3-slot ranking is an unverified counterfactual against a construction rule (equal-weight 3-slot) that may not exist in the live system.

attacks.issue: Label leakage in the false_negative_relative conditioning set: cases are defined as 'false negatives' BECAUSE they subsequently produced W4 >= 8% return AND >=5pp above B0 median. Conditioning ruin probability on a feature signature drawn from this selection-on-outcome set is circular — the 'weak third' threshold is calibrated on the very rejections that won, so any rule derived from it is overfit by construction.
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher's central mechanism (marginal ruin probability exceeds marginal winner probability given the false_negative region) is built on a sample whose definition depends on future returns. The conditional probabilities cannot be interpreted as forward-looking expectations.

attacks.issue: Snapshot clustering confounds candidate-level inference: at least 6 of 27 cases share snapshot snap_71486ed83c, and most ruin cases concentrate in 3-4 snapshot ids. If macro regime (vol regime, sector rotation, breadth) drove those outcomes, candidate features are proxies for snapshot id, not independent ruin signals.
attacks.why_it_matters: Treating 8 ruin observations as 8 independent candidate-level events inflates apparent ruin precision. The effective sample size for candidate-conditioned ruin probability may be 3-4, not 8, making the 'ruin rate' claim unestimable.

attacks.issue: Proxy variable contamination across up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, and px_vs_ma50: all four are jointly driven by short-horizon return autocorrelation, so the 'multi-feature' composite score that distinguishes weak from strong is mostly one latent factor. Median deltas (z-scores -1.19 to -0.85) suggest collinear signals, not orthogonal evidence.
attacks.why_it_matters: If features collapse to one momentum factor, the 'cash dominates when multiple weak features coincide' rule is equivalent to 'cash dominates when momentum is low' — and momentum is known to be regime-dependent and mean-reverting at the extremes. The composite rule is no more robust than a single-feature momentum filter.

attacks.issue: Counterfactual construction is unverified: the claim that a 2-position (top-2 + cash) portfolio beats a 3-position portfolio requires comparing realized PnL on the same discovery-train set under both constructions. The archaeology shows only single-name outcomes, not slot-aggregated portfolio returns. With only 2 false_negative_big_winner cases, the 'missed large winner' cost cannot be quantified against the 8 ruin cases.
attacks.why_it_matters: The headline policy recommendation (cash > weak third) is an unevaluated counterfactual. The researcher offers a falsifiable prediction ('Sharpe of 2-slot > 3-slot') but has not run it. The claim rests on aggregating single-name outcomes without addressing position-correlation within a portfolio, nor the cash drag of holding 1/3 of capital idle for extended periods.

attacks.issue: Bucket boundary artifact in the 'bimodal' ruin-vs-large_win claim: 'ruin' and 'large_win' are categorical outcomes, and the apparent absence of middle buckets is partly a function of how thresholds were set. entity_bfb308b24a is 'loss' (not 'ruin') with -12.1% pullback but small-win bucket; this case sits at the boundary. Without the threshold values, the magnitude asymmetry claim (ruin > winner) cannot be checked.
attacks.why_it_matters: If 'ruin' is defined as W4 < -10% and 'large_win' is W4 > +8%, the apparent asymmetry could be entirely a thresholding choice. The economic meaning of the slot comparison depends on actual return magnitudes, which are hidden inside bucketed labels.

attacks.issue: Endogeneity of the 'weak third' tier: the very existence of a weak-third candidate presupposes a ranking procedure. If we replaced that ranking with a different one (e.g., mean-reversion-aware scoring), the candidate currently labeled 'weak third' could become 'strong second'. The claim is conditional on a specific scoring function that itself may be misspecified.
attacks.why_it_matters: Attributing ruin to the candidate's intrinsic quality, rather than to the ranking procedure that placed it third, conflates two distinct failure modes. The same stock could be 'avoid' under one ranking and 'must-buy' under another, so the cash-vs-fill decision is a property of the ranker, not the slot.

attacks.issue: Contradictory cases are not explained: entity_2f86543bf6 won large with negative mom_20, negative ma20_slope, no pullback base; entity_6618d3e80c carried an identical strong-momentum profile to entity_84824e6a20 yet diverged in terminal outcome (large_win vs ruin). The researcher cites these as 'exceptions' but does not account for why features failed to discriminate within the same snapshot/momentum regime.
attacks.why_it_matters: Two cases of identical feature signature, opposite terminal outcomes, suggest an unmodeled factor (idiosyncratic event, intraday path, news flow) dominates candidate features. If so, the conditional ruin probability given features is far from deterministic and the slot-decision rule will misclassify frequently.

attacks.issue: Fixed 3-slot equal-weight rule may be a strawman: the prior literature the researcher cites ('replace fixed 3-slot equal-weight with conviction-weighted') implies the live system may already be conviction-weighted, in which case the entire 'cash vs fill the third slot' question is moot because the third slot already receives less than 1/3 capital.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the construction rule is already 50/30/20, the marginal ruin exposure of the third slot is 20% of capital, not 33%. The cash-vs-fill trade-off changes qualitatively, and the headline recommendation (avoid the third slot) becomes a position-sizing tweak rather than a slot abandonment.

counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where a 'weak third' profile (low up_day_ratio_20 + low mom_20 + low vol_ratio_5_20) produced 'large_win' in a snapshot NOT dominated by macro drift (i.e., outside snap_71486ed83c and similar clustered snapshots). If such cases exist in test data, the conditional ruin probability claim fails out-of-sample.

Snapshots in the test set where the 2-position (top-2 + cash) portfolio underperformed the 3-position portfolio by more than the ruin-tail would predict. Specifically: snapshots containing 2+ winners among the rejected names, with no ruin among accepted names.
Sector-decomposed ruin rates: if ruin cases concentrate in one or two sectors within a snapshot, the candidate-feature model is incomplete and a sector-controlled ruin rate is the right comparator.

Regime split: bull-vol vs bear-vol vs chop snapshots, with ruin rate recomputed per regime. If ruin is concentrated in one regime, the 'weak third' rule is essentially a regime filter, not a candidate feature.

Time-decay of the false_negative signal: if the false_negative_relative region only predicted winners in the first 2 weeks of W4 but not later (W8-W12), the forward-window claim is unstable and the opportunity cost of cash is deferred rather than avoided.

The 'strong but ruined' counterpart: cases with high up_day_ratio_20, high mom_20, high vol_ratio_5_20 that STILL ruined (entity_84824e6a20, entity_b6bcccdf6a, entity_3472243e0c). Their frequency relative to weak-but-ruined cases bounds the maximum precision of any candidate-feature rule.
what_would_change_my_mind: An out-of-sample test on at least 100 test snapshots, with the candidate-feature composite score computed on the train-set false_negative_relative median, showing ruin rate in the bottom-quintile composite exceeds 35% and winner rate in the same quintile is below 15%, with confidence intervals that exclude the null of equal ruin/win probabilities.

A regime-stratified analysis showing that, conditional on snapshot macro factors (VIX regime, breadth, sector dispersion), candidate features still contribute marginal explanatory power for ruin beyond what snapshot id alone provides.

A direct A/B comparison of 3-position equal-weight vs 2-position + cash vs 1-position + 2/3 cash portfolios on the same out-of-sample set, with Sharpe ratios and maximum drawdown reported. If 2-position + cash does NOT beat 3-position with statistical significance, the core claim is falsified.

Resolution of the bucket-boundary ambiguity: showing actual W4 returns (not categorical buckets) for ruin cases vs large_win cases. If average ruin magnitude is not materially larger than average large_win magnitude, the 'asymmetric tail' mechanism dissolves.

A re-scored archaeology with snapshot-fixed effects removed, so candidate-level features are evaluated against within-snapshot variation only. If the candidate-feature signal vanishes under within-snapshot scoring, the rule is a regime proxy.

Evidence that the live portfolio construction rule is in fact fixed equal-weight 3-slot (not conviction-weighted), so the policy recommendation is addressing a real rule rather than a hypothetical one.

tests.name: within_snapshot_feature_discrimination
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot id (e.g., snap_71486ed83c), compute per-snapshot z-scores of each feature across that snapshot's candidate pool, then compare the within-snapshot z-score distribution between w4_return_bucket='ruin' and w4_return_bucket='large_win'. This isolates candidate-level signal from snapshot-level (regime) signal.
tests.success_criterion: Median within-snapshot z-score for 'ruin' cases is ≤ -0.5 (below the snapshot median) for at least 3 of the 7 features, AND the rank-sum p-value between ruin and large_win z-score distributions is <0.10 for at least 2 features. This would confirm candidate-level discrimination survives snapshot demeaning.
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot z-scores for ruin cases are statistically indistinguishable (p>0.30) from large_win cases for all 7 features. This would mean features are pure regime proxies and the candidate-level mechanism collapses.

tests.name: composite_orthogonality_audit
tests.comparison: Compute the full Spearman rank-correlation matrix across these 7 features on all 27 archaeology cases. Perform PCA and report the proportion of variance explained by the first principal component. Test whether any pair has |ρ|>0.70.
tests.success_criterion: First PC explains <60% of variance AND no feature pair has |ρ|>0.70. This would justify a multi-feature composite as more than a momentum re-label.
tests.failure_criterion: First PC explains ≥75% of variance OR ≥3 feature pairs have |ρ|>0.70. This would confirm the skeptic's collinearity attack and invalidate any multi-feature composite as additive evidence.

tests.name: prespecified_weak_third_quintile_test
tests.comparison: Pre-specify the weak-third rule (decision-time only, no outcome peeking) as: a candidate is 'weak' if at least 3 of 5 features fall in the bottom tertile of the cross-sectional distribution. Compute ruin rate and large_win rate for the weak bucket vs the strong bucket, using the same numeric_contrasts medians as the threshold seeds. Do NOT use false_negative labels in defining the bucket.
tests.success_criterion: Weak bucket ruin rate ≥35% AND strong bucket large_win rate ≥50%, with at least a 25pp gap on each tail. A non-overlapping confidence interval on ruin rates between buckets.
tests.failure_criterion: Weak bucket ruin rate <20% OR the ruin/large_win ratio is statistically indistinguishable between weak and strong buckets (binomial p>0.20). This would falsify the 'weak third = elevated ruin probability' mechanism.

tests.name: counterfactual_portfolio_construction_within_snapshot
tests.comparison: For each snapshot that has ≥3 candidates in the archaeology, simulate three portfolio constructions on the same set of cases: (A) 1-position — invest 100% in the highest-mom_20 candidate; (B) 2-position — invest 50/50 in top-2 by composite; (C) 3-position — 33/33/33 across all three. Use w4_return_bucket as ordinal proxy (ruin=-1, loss=-0.5, small_win=0.5, large_win=1) to compute portfolio score per construction. Compare mean portfolio score and worst-case score across constructions, restricted to within-snapshot comparisons.
tests.success_criterion: Mean portfolio score for (B) ≥ (C) by at least 0.2 ordinal units AND worst-case (B) ≥ worst-case (C). This would justify 'cash dominates weak third' as an empirical portfolio statement, not just a candidate-level claim.
tests.failure_criterion: Mean (C) > mean (B) by ≥0.1 OR worst-case (C) > worst-case (B). This would mean filling the third slot adds expected value on average, falsifying the cash-dominance claim at the portfolio level. Caveat: small snapshot count limits power — report effective N.

tests.name: identical_signature_outcome_divergence
tests.comparison: Identify all pairs of cases within the same snapshot whose 5-feature vector has Euclidean distance in the bottom quartile (most similar profiles). For each such pair, compute the difference in ordinal w4_return_bucket score and report the median absolute divergence and the count of pairs with opposite-sign outcomes (ruin vs large_win).
tests.success_criterion: Among near-identical pairs within the same snapshot, ≤20% have opposite-sign outcomes. This would indicate features carry meaningful signal even at the within-snapshot level.
tests.failure_criterion: Among near-identical pairs within the same snapshot, ≥40% have opposite-sign outcomes. This would confirm an unmodeled factor dominates features, bounding any feature-based rule's maximum precision.

tests.name: snapshot_concentration_bound
tests.comparison: Compute the ruin concentration: fraction of all 'ruin' cases that come from the single most-ruinous snapshot id. Also compute effective independent ruin sample size n_eff = (Σ_k p_k)^(-1) where p_k is ruin share of snapshot k. Compare n_eff to the naive n=8.
tests.success_criterion: No single snapshot contributes >40% of ruin cases AND n_eff ≥ 5. This would justify treating ruin cases as independent candidate-level observations.
tests.failure_criterion: One snapshot contributes ≥60% of ruin cases OR n_eff < 3. This would invalidate candidate-level ruin probability estimates and confirm the regime-proxy interpretation.

tests.name: magnitude_asymmetry_via_bucket_anchoring
tests.comparison: Anchor on the two cases with the most extreme positive mom_20 (large_win-candidates) and two with the most extreme negative setup profiles within the ruin set. Compute the implied return-magnitude asymmetry using pullback_pct (where available) as a directional proxy: large_win cases have median pullback_pct of -15.9, ruin cases (when pullback exists) average -12.0. Test whether the candidate-feature profile that selects large_win is compatible with higher expected magnitude than the profile that selects ruin, using only features that DON'T require knowing the bucket.
tests.success_criterion: Average pullback_pct magnitude (deep base) for selected_winner-feature-signature cases exceeds average magnitude for ruin-feature-signature cases by ≥3pp. This would support the 'winner magnitude > loser magnitude' asymmetry that underpins Kelly-style position sizing on the third slot.
tests.failure_criterion: Magnitudes are within 2pp or invert (winner base shallower than loser base), in which case the 'asymmetric tail' mechanism that justifies avoiding the third slot collapses to a magnitude-symmetric bet where equal-weight is defensible.

tests.name: rank_procedure_invariance_of_weak_third
tests.comparison: For each snapshot with ≥3 candidates, define 'weak third' under THREE independent rank procedures: (i) pure mom_20, (ii) equal-weight composite of 6 features, (iii) px_vs_ma50 only. Compute the overlap (Jaccard index) of which candidate is labeled 'weak third' across the three rankers. Then test whether ruin rate is elevated within each ranker's 'weak third' set.
tests.success_criterion: Mean Jaccard ≥0.5 across ranker pairs AND ruin rate is elevated (≥30%) within each ranker's weak-third set. This would mean 'weak third' is a property of the candidate, not the ranker.
tests.failure_criterion: Mean Jaccard <0.30 OR ruin rate is elevated for one ranker but not the others. This would confirm the 'weak third' tier is ranker-induced, and the cash-vs-fill question must be reframed as 'which ranker do we trust' rather than 'is this candidate weak'.

leakage_checks: Verify that no feature in any test uses the w4_return_bucket, outcome_label, is_b0_pick, or any boolean label that was constructed using forward returns. The labels in the archaeology set were created using future W4 return thresholds per method_note; using them as predictors in a new rule would be label leakage.

Confirm the weak-third composite in 'prespecified_weak_third_quintile_test' is derived from feature distributions within the archaeology set WITHOUT conditioning on outcome bucket. Threshold tertiles must be set on the joint feature distribution, not on ruin-vs-win splits.
For 'within_snapshot_feature_discrimination', verify that snapshot id is used only as a fixed-effect control (demeaning/grouping variable) and never as a feature input to the predictive model.

Check that 'counterfactual_portfolio_construction_within_snapshot' does not assume the candidate pool within a snapshot is exchangeable — if the top-2 by composite have correlated outcomes, the 50/50 portfolio's variance is understated. Report pairwise outcome correlation within snapshot.

Verify 'magnitude_asymmetry_via_bucket_anchoring' does not circularly use the w4_return_bucket='ruin' label to select 'ruin-feature-signature cases'. Instead, define the ruin-feature signature from the PIT feature medians of the negative-outcome cluster computed BEFORE consulting bucket labels.
Ensure no test depends on calendar identity (week, month, year, day-of-week) as a feature or threshold. Snapshot id is acceptable only as a clustering/regime variable.
Confirm that 'identical_signature_outcome_divergence' uses only PIT features for the signature, and that 'outcome' is the ordinal bucket which is the only forward information accessed.
Check that no test requires outer-forward outcomes beyond the W4 bucket already in the frozen archaeology evidence; flag any test that would require new forward data collection as invalid.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: Under a fixed 3-slot equal-weight capital structure, cash dominates a third position only when the marginal candidate's PIT feature vector intersects the false_negative_region (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ ~0.55, mom_20 ≤ ~0.08, vol_ratio_5_20 ≤ ~1.25, weak ma10/ma20 slopes) AND the within-snapshot regime does not concentrate ruin disproportionately. Economic meaning of position counts under fixed 3-slot capital: 1-position = high-conviction concentration with ~67% cash drag, lowest diversification but tightest dispersion if conviction is calibrated; 2-position = top-2 quality plus 1/3 cash, expected best risk-adjusted when third is weak, trades opportunity cost for ruin protection; 3-position equal-weight = only justified when all three clear composite threshold, otherwise the weakest link is an asymmetric-tail bet (ruin magnitude plausibly exceeds winner magnitude per bimodal w4 buckets) compounded by forced 1/3 weight. The cash-dominance claim is conditional, not categorical — it requires the construction artifact (equal weight) to be intrinsic rather than incidental, the FN-region feature signature to generalize beyond a label-leakage-conditioned set, and the snapshot regime to support candidate-level rather than regime-level inference. None of these preconditions is yet verified.
falsifiers: Snapshot_concentration_bound: if any single snapshot contributes ≥60% of ruin cases OR effective n_eff < 3, the candidate-level ruin probability claim collapses to a regime proxy.

Within_snapshot_feature_discrimination: if ruin and large_win within-snapshot z-score distributions are statistically indistinguishable (p>0.30) on all 7 features, the candidate-level mechanism is unsupported regardless of cross-sectional differences.

Counterfactual_portfolio_construction: if mean portfolio score for 3-position ≥ 2-position by ≥0.1 ordinal units on snapshots with ≥3 candidates, cash does not dominate the third slot at the portfolio level (effective N may be small; caveat).

Magnitude_asymmetry_via_bucket_anchoring: if winner pullback depth does not exceed loser pullback depth by ≥3pp on features computable without the bucket label, the asymmetric-tail justification for cash fails and equal-weight becomes defensible.

Rank_procedure_invariance: if mean Jaccard across ranker pairs is <0.30, the 'weak third' tier is ranker-induced and the cash-vs-fill question must be reframed as 'which ranker do we trust' rather than 'is this candidate weak'.

Composite_orthogonality: if first PC explains ≥75% of variance across the 7 features OR ≥3 pairs have |ρ|>0.70, any multi-feature composite collapses to a momentum re-label and the threshold-based rule is not robust.

Label leakage audit: if rerunning the FN-region rule with the w4 outcome-conditioning step removed still produces the same ruin-rate separation, the mechanism claim survives the leakage attack; if not, the directional evidence is artifact.

Conviction-weighted alternative: if a 50/30/20 allocation on the same archaeology set produces higher risk-adjusted score than either 3-position equal-weight or 2-position + cash, the 'cash vs fill third' framing is dominated by a construction-alternative solution and the candidate-quality question becomes secondary.
actionable_design_principles: Separate candidate-quality identification (a feature signature question) from portfolio-construction effects (an allocation question); the weak-third claim conflates these and should be partitioned in any policy specification.

Treat 'weak third' as a tier, not a binary: a candidate triggers soft veto when composite score falls below the false_negative_region median on ≥3 of 5 features, with the veto defaulting to cash unless conviction-weighting rules apply.

Reframe position counts under fixed 3-slot as a conviction surface, not a count: 1-position means capital allocated 100% to highest-composite name (cash elsewhere is reserve, not lost opportunity); 2-position means top-2 with the remaining 1/3 conditional on composite threshold; 3-position means all three cleared a shared composite gate.

Use within-snapshot z-scores (snapshot-demeaned features) as the operational weak-third signal, not cross-sectional ranks, until snapshot_concentration_bound confirms regime independence; cross-sectional ranking will systematically overweight snapshot-level ruin concentration.

Track a 'weak-third rejection counter' and a 'weak-third composite distribution' as real-time policy variables; if rejection rate exceeds ~50% of decision weeks, the slot-filling rule is structurally biased and needs recalibration rather than tighter thresholds.

Model ruin-vs-win magnitude explicitly even if uncertain: the bimodal w4 bucket distribution (ruin vs large_win, no overlap) suggests Kelly-style reduction of the marginal third position below equal weight is appropriate as a default, not an aggressive bet on cash.

Do not commit to a single fixed threshold until the experimental_designer tests (especially within_snapshot_feature_discrimination and snapshot_concentration_bound) have been executed; current evidence supports directional belief, not calibrated threshold.

Expand the evidence base on the opportunity-cost side (false_negative_big_winner sample is n=2 in archaeology) before firm policy commitment; the cash-vs-fill trade is only well-posed when ruin and missed-large-winner samples are both adequately powered.

Operationalize capacity-abstention as a three-state decision per slot: FILL (composite above gate), CASH (composite below weak-third threshold), and SHRINK (composite between thresholds, apply sub-equal-weight conviction sizing); this dissolves the 1/2/3-position framing into a continuous policy.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Weak-third soft veto with composite gate: declare weak-third when snapshot-demeaned composite of {up_day_ratio_20, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5} falls below the false_negative_region median on ≥3 of 5 features; veto defaults to cash with a 1/3 reserve.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Differs from researcher policy by using snapshot-demeaned inputs and a soft 3-of-5 veto rather than a hard OR rule (up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.55 OR mom_20 ≤ 0.08); also incorporates ma10_slope_5 which the researcher's proposal omitted.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Direct capacity-abstention: defines when the marginal candidate's profile triggers non-deployment of the third slot, preserving 1/3 capital as cash reserve against asymmetric ruin tail.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Conviction-weighted 3-slot allocation: replace equal-weight with allocation proportional to composite percentile rank (e.g., 50th-percentile weight scaled by score), so a weak third receives a smaller position rather than forced equal weight or full cash.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Rejects the binary cash-vs-fill framing of the research question and offers a continuous alternative; this is the 'construction-alternative solution' that the skeptic's analysis implies but does not formalize.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity-abstention at the margin: position size itself becomes the abstention variable; a weak-third gets partial deployment (e.g., 10-15%) rather than full 33% or full 0%.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Bimodal Kelly sizing on the third slot: condition position size on the empirical ruin-vs-large_win bucket probability conditional on composite score, using magnitude estimates from pullback_pct and dist_to_52w_high_pct as Kelly inputs.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Differs from conviction-weighting by being magnitude-aware rather than score-rank-aware; explicitly models the asymmetric tail rather than treating composite as a proxy for expected return.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity-abstention calibrated to tail risk: when conditional ruin probability × ruin magnitude exceeds win probability × win magnitude, Kelly fraction falls below equal-weight and may fall to zero, generating cash.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Ranker-ensemble weak-third identification: compute weak-third label under three independent rankers (pure mom_20, equal-weight 6-feature composite, px_vs_ma50-only) and require ≥2-of-3 agreement before declaring a weak-third veto; this bounds ranker-induced fragility.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Operationalizes the rank_procedure_invariance_of_weak_third test as a policy rather than a falsification step; if rankers disagree, the candidate is in a 'contested weak' zone and defaults to cash rather than triggering veto.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity-abstention as consensus failure — disagreement among conviction sources is itself a veto trigger, framing weak-third identification as an epistemic rather than purely feature-based call.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Regime-conditional weak-third threshold: scale the weak-third composite threshold by snapshot-level ruin concentration; when within-snapshot historical ruin rate exceeds a calibration value, raise the composite gate (more vetoes, more cash) rather than relying on the same threshold across regimes.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Directly addresses the snapshot_concentration_bound concern by making the threshold regime-conditional rather than universal; if ruin is regime-driven, the gate should react to regime rather than be fixed.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity-abstention that tracks regime risk: in high-ruin regimes, abstain more aggressively; in low-ruin regimes, the third slot fills more readily, making the cash decision regime-adaptive.

cycles.question: For weak third candidate, determine what PIT statistic can measure confidence without future leakage. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: A PIT-only composite confidence score built from the strongest false-negative/selected-winner separators (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5) — specifically a 'minimum-feature-floor' statistic (worst z-score among the top features, computed against the false-negative median, not the selected-winner median, to avoid ex-post leakage) — can flag the weak third candidate as a likely false_negative_relative before capital is deployed. Under fixed 3-slot capital, selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions is economically equivalent to choosing how much of the budget is exposed to the marginal candidate's downside asymmetry: 1 slot concentrates on maximum-conviction alpha but caps diversification, 2 slots is the marginal-efficiency frontier when #3's PIT composite falls below the false-negative cluster centroid, and 3 slots is only justified when #3 clears the floor because the marginal position carries the highest probability of underperforming the B0-pick median (false_negative_relative pattern) while offering limited diversification payoff (correlated momentum factors).
evidence_for: Numeric contrast table shows the false_negative cluster sits at lower mom_20 (0.058 vs 0.163, std δ = -1.001), lower up_day_ratio_20 (0.5 vs 0.625, δ = -1.188), lower vol_ratio_5_20 (1.18 vs 1.42, δ = -1.046), lower px_vs_ma50 (0.056 vs 0.127, δ = -0.854) — all of these are PIT-observable on entry snapshot, no future window needed.

False_negative cases are predominantly is_b0_pick=false (entity_df5478102d, d8e8e7b814, 535a1beed7, bfb308b24a, de1c657364) and have w4_return_bucket in {small_win, loss, large_win} — i.e., the #3 slot would have captured underperformance relative to B0 winners, exactly the case where the 3rd slot dilutes portfolio alpha.

False_positive_ruin cases (8 instances) often share strong PIT features with selected_winners (e.g., entity_8f0df3d38e has mom_20=0.176, ma10_slope=0.054 — comparable to entity_b00579f203 SW with mom_20=0.230), confirming that absolute PIT strength alone cannot separate winners from ruiners; the relevant gate is the floor under the FN cluster, not absolute conviction.

Selected_winner entity_8ad5cd4795 (ma10_slope=-0.006, mom_20=0.004) shows even weak PIT can win when base structure is favorable (5-week pullback, up_day_ratio=0.7), implying the floor-statistic must be multi-feature AND-conditioned, not single-threshold — a single weak feature is insufficient for abstention.
ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is PIT-observable (entry day's close vs pivot), shows δ = -0.695 — a tighter trigger extension correlates with false_negative, useful as a tie-breaker in the composite.

27-case base rate: 11 SW / 8 FP_ruin / 7 FN_relative+big_winner. The asymmetric downside of taking a weak #3 is dominated by FN_relative events (relative drawdown vs B0 median), not ruin events, so abstention economics hinge on relative underperformance, not catastrophic loss.
evidence_against: Selected_winner entity_2f86543bf6 had ma10_slope=0.0076, mom_20=-0.008, up_day_ratio=0.35 — well below FN medians on multiple features yet won large_win, indicating the PIT floor has false-abstention cost: missing a winner by being too strict.

False_positive_ruin entity_6618d3e80c has both selected_winner and ruin labels, mom_20=0.251, ma10_slope=0.075, px_vs_ma50=0.337 — extreme PIT strength that nevertheless produced ruin, so a high composite score does NOT immunize against the FP_ruin tail; the floor logic only addresses the FN-relative dilution, not catastrophic ruin.

pullback_pct shows δ = +0.640 (FN med -7.3, SW med -15.9) — deeper pullbacks correlate with WINNERS, contradicting the naive 'weak = bad' reading; a 3rd candidate with shallow pullback may still be the right pick. The composite must avoid penalizing this feature.
vol_ratio_5_20 standardization (-1.046) uses a small-N contrast; with 27 cases the delta is suggestive but not statistically definitive — confidence intervals on the median floor are wide.
