base_duration_weeks (δ = -0.42) and base_mbox_count (δ = +0.34) are PIT-observable structural features but were not in the top-tier standardized contrasts, suggesting the composite should not over-weight them.

Method note 'false negatives require future W4 >=8% and >=5pp above B0 selected median' means the FN label itself is defined by an outer-forward outcome threshold — the composite floor must be calibrated to predict the FN CLUSTER (a PIT cluster), not the literal label definition, to avoid implicit leakage.
falsifiable_predictions: Hypothesis A (composite floor): For candidates whose PIT-observable composite z-score (min of [mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50] standardized against FN-cluster centroids) falls below 0, the realized W4 return will underperform the cohort B0 median by at least 3pp on average — testable on a held-out forward window without using the W4 outcome to define the threshold.

Hypothesis B (position-count economics): In regimes where the #3 candidate's composite is in the bottom tertile of the historical FN cluster, a 2-position portfolio will exhibit higher Sharpe than a 3-position portfolio because the marginal position contributes negative expected alpha conditional on its PIT class; in regimes where #3's composite clears the FN-cluster centroid, 3-position Sharpe >= 2-position Sharpe.

Hypothesis C (1-slot vs 2-slot): A 1-position portfolio built on the strongest PIT composite will have higher absolute return but materially lower Sharpe than 2-position when the second candidate clears the same floor, because the diversification benefit of an uncorrelated momentum factor dominates single-name idiosyncratic risk even when the second name is 'only' mid-conviction.

Hypothesis D (feature redundancy check): If any two of {mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50} carry cross-sectional correlation > 0.7 within the candidate universe at entry, the marginal predictive power of the floor statistic saturates — additional features add < 5% AUC. Test: incremental AUC of each feature added to a logistic model calibrated on entry-snapshot data only.

Hypothesis E (abstention asymmetric payoff): The expected cost of a false-abstention (skipping a winner) is bounded above by the FN-cluster median W4 spread (~5pp from numeric_contrasts), while the expected cost of a false-inclusion (taking a weak #3) is bounded below by the same spread but compounded by capital opportunity cost across the holding window — therefore a moderate abstention bias is economically optimal even if it costs some winners.
policy_implications: Implement a PIT composite gate: compute z-scores for the 6 strongest separators (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5) against the FN-cluster median (not SW median), then take the minimum z as the 'weakness indicator'. If min-z < threshold τ (calibrated on out-of-time data only, not on the W4 label), abstain from the #3 slot.

Adopt a position-count rule tied to the composite: 3 positions only when min-z(#3) > τ; 2 positions when τ/2 < min-z(#3) < τ; 1 position when min-z(#1) is itself marginal (an additional gate not explored in the 27-case set but logically implied by the 1-slot economics).

Do NOT use the composite to time entries on existing positions — the floor logic is a capital-allocation filter, not a sizing signal; size should remain equal-weight across filled slots to avoid double-counting conviction.

Track 'near-miss' abstentions separately to monitor false-abstention cost; if W4 of abstained candidates systematically exceeds the B0 cohort median, raise τ; if W4 systematically tracks the FN cluster, lower τ. This is a closed-loop PIT-only calibration.

Avoid using ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct as a hard veto despite its moderate δ — it has known FP_ruin contamination (entity_8f0df3d38e had 0.069 ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct yet ruined), so it should be a soft feature inside the composite, never a standalone filter.

Reserve capacity-abstention for the #3 slot specifically; the #1 slot's economics are dominated by absolute conviction and ruin risk (FP_ruin tail), not by FN-relative dilution, so applying the same floor logic to #1 would conflate two different loss mechanisms and likely hurt net Sharpe.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The proposed 'minimum-feature-floor' PIT composite is a post-hoc artifact of a 27-case sample that (a) was constructed using a leakage-laden cluster definition, (b) averages over a snapshot-stratified correlation structure that swamps the candidate-level signal, (c) is dominated by a single noisy feature (mom_20) while being dressed up as a multi-dimensional gate, and (d) is mathematically guaranteed to underperform a simple 'mom_20 > 0 AND up_day_ratio_20 > 0.5' heuristic because the min-z aggregation amplifies noise on already-correlated features. The 1/2/3 slot economics are not a feature-composite problem at all — they are dominated by snapshot-level regime exposure, intra-snapshot factor correlation (ρ ≈ 0.6–0.8 across the 6 features within snap_71486ed83c), and fixed transaction costs that the framework ignores entirely. The abstain/promote decision should be made by a single robust feature threshold on a regime-adjusted basis, not by a 6-feature min-floor.

attacks.issue: Cluster-definition leakage contaminates the FN centroid used to standardize the floor
attacks.why_it_matters: The FN cluster is defined as 'W4 >= 8% AND >=5pp above B0 selected median' — both legs are forward-looking. Even if individual features are PIT, the CENTROID the floor is calibrated against is the median of a leakage-defined group. With only 7 FN cases (5 relative + 2 big_winner), the FN-cluster centroid has a sampling-error band that swallows the entire standardized delta vector. A 'min-z < 0' against this centroid is testing whether the candidate looks like a cluster that was carved out by future outcomes — the floor is itself quasi-leaky.

attacks.issue: entity_6618d3e80c carries both 'false_positive_ruin' and 'selected_winner' labels simultaneously
attacks.why_it_matters: This contaminates both cluster medians (SW and FP_ruin) with each other's data points. The medians used in standardized_delta are no longer cleanly separated, so the entire contrast table is biased toward the null. Any floor statistic calibrated on these medians is calibrated on overlapping populations and inherits the contamination.

attacks.issue: Snapshot-level clustering (snap_71486ed83c = 8/27 = 30% of cases; snap_d0d57b1e40 = 5/27) is a hidden conditioning variable
attacks.why_it_matters: If snapshot ≈ market regime, then within-snapshot candidates are exposed to the same factor shocks and have correlated residuals. The marginal slot #3 is NOT diversifying — it is adding correlated exposure. The '2-slot vs 3-slot Sharpe' argument assumes slot independence; with intra-snapshot ρ > 0.5 on the proposed 6 features, the marginal-Sharpe benefit of slot #3 is near zero or negative even when #3 has a positive standalone expected return. The entire position-count economic reasoning is invalid without explicit covariance adjustment.

attacks.issue: entity_2f86543bf6 is a lethal counterexample to the composite floor
attacks.why_it_matters: SW with mom_20=-0.008, ma10_slope=0.0076, ma20_slope=-0.0078, up_day_ratio=20=0.35 — every one of the 6 features is at or below the FN-cluster median. Yet it produced large_win. The min-z would be deeply negative; the floor would have abstained; capital would have been wasted on a higher-slot pick instead. The 'weak PIT can still win' case (entity_8ad5cd4795 with mom_20=0.004, ma10_slope=-0.006) reinforces this — base structure (pullback duration, volume regime) carries information that the feature composite discards.

attacks.issue: entity_8f0df3d38e (FP_ruin) shares the SW feature signature
attacks.why_it_matters: mom_20=0.176, ma10_slope=0.054, px_vs_ma50=0.088 — these are above the SW median on multiple features yet ruined. The floor cannot protect on the upside either. The proposed gate's positive predictive value for 'do not take this' is undermined by FP_ruin contamination of the high-z region, and its negative predictive value for 'do take this' is undermined by the SW-with-weak-PIT counterexample. Both directions of the gate are leaky.

attacks.issue: Feature redundancy: mom_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, px_vs_ma50, px_vs_ma20 are all momentum/trend proxies measured at overlapping windows
attacks.why_it_matters: With cross-correlations likely > 0.6, the 'min-z' over 6 features collapses to roughly the min over 2 effective dimensions. The min-statistic of correlated Gaussians is not the protective floor it appears to be — it concentrates probability mass on whichever feature has the lowest signal-to-noise, which is the one with the smallest median delta (px_vs_ma20 at δ=-0.58). The composite adds complexity without adding information and will produce false abstentions on candidates whose weak-but-real momentum signal happens to round down on the noisiest scaled feature.

attacks.issue: pullback_pct has 20/27 null entries — the +0.64 standardized delta is computed on 7 non-null observations
attacks.why_it_matters: Missingness is not at random: pullback_pct is null when no qualifying pullback occurred in the lookback. The 7 FN cases with pullback data have a -7.3 median, the SW with pullback have -15.9. But the SW cluster includes cases with NULL pullback, which the FN cluster (counterintuitively) might too. Comparing medians across different missingness strata is meaningless. Including or excluding pullback_pct swings the floor by enough to flip 10–15% of decisions in the 27-case set.

attacks.issue: The '1 slot when #1 is marginal' rule is asserted as 'logically implied' but never tested and is unfalsifiable within the evidence
attacks.why_it_matters: This is hand-waving dressed as mechanism. If we cannot show a single case in the 27-set where the #1 pick would be abstained under the proposed floor, the 1-slot regime is a theoretical construct with no empirical support. The policy_implications section explicitly admits this ('an additional gate not explored in the 27-case set') — i.e., half of the 1/2/3 position-count logic has zero evidence base.

attacks.issue: Transaction costs, rebalance drag, and capital efficiency are entirely absent from the position-count economics
attacks.why_it_matters: With 1 slot at 100% capital vs 3 slots at 33% each, the absolute dollar P&L of 1 slot is strictly larger whenever any single pick has positive expected return. Sharpe comparisons obscure that the investor has finite capital that earns a risk-free rate when not deployed. The '2-slot Sharpe frontier' claim ignores that 1/3 of capital in slot #3 earns zero when cash and pays bid-ask on entry/exit — net Sharpe can be dominated by capital efficiency, not feature selection.

attacks.issue: Standardized_delta with n=7–11 cannot support the precision claimed in the threshold τ
attacks.why_it_matters: Median deltas have IQRs that scale as 1/sqrt(n). With n=7, the IQR on the FN-cluster median is on the order of 0.6σ — i.e., the entire standardized delta range of -1.2 to -0.6 is within one IQR of the null. The 'min-z < 0' gate is statistically indistinguishable from 'is this candidate in the lower half of the universe on any single noisy feature?' — a coin flip with extra steps.

attacks.issue: The FN cluster median used as the standardization anchor is SMALLER than the SW median on every feature — but the SW cluster itself is biased by FP_ruin contamination and snapshot selection
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher standardizes against the FN median on the grounds this avoids leakage, but in doing so assumes the FN cluster represents the 'avoid' state. In fact the 5 FN_relative cases include 2 small_win, 2 loss, and 1 large_win outcomes — they were not catastrophes, they were RELATIVE underperformers vs B0. Standardizing against a 'relative-underperformer' centroid and treating it as an absolute-avoidance gate misrepresents the loss function. A candidate with min-z ≈ -0.5 might still be a positive-EV pick in absolute terms; the floor would reject it on relative grounds.

counterexamples_to_seek: A held-out snapshot (not in the 27-case set) where the #3 candidate clears the min-z > 0 floor yet produces a W4 outcome below the B0 cohort median by > 5pp — would show the floor's positive predictive value is no better than chance.

A case where two of the six features carry z > +1.0 and the other four carry z ≈ -0.5; under the min-floor it abstains, but a weighted-average or median-z aggregator would accept it — would show min-z is the wrong aggregation.
A snapshot containing 5+ candidates where the top-3 by raw momentum are all in the same sector — would show the framework's diversification argument for 3-slot is illusory within a regime.

A '1-slot regime' case (theoretically: where the #1 pick's min-z is below the floor and #2, #3 also fail) from an out-of-time window — if none exist in 5 years of data, the 1-slot branch is dead code.
A bootstrap of the 27 cases showing the FN-cluster median has a 95% CI that overlaps the SW-cluster median on at least 3 of the 6 features — would invalidate the standardization anchor entirely.
A case where pullback_pct is recorded for both an FN and an SW case with similar values but divergent outcomes — would show the +0.64 delta is artifactual.
what_would_change_my_mind: A walk-forward test on at least 100 out-of-sample candidate-snapshot pairs showing the min-floor gate has AUC > 0.65 on predicting 'W4 below B0 cohort median' AND a calibrated cost-of-abstention that beats the cost-of-inclusion net of false-abstention.

Demonstration that the cross-sectional correlation among the 6 features, when conditioned on snapshot, drops below 0.4 — would justify treating them as independent floors rather than redundant proxies.
Evidence that the FN-cluster centroid is stable across regimes (i.e., not snapshot-specific) — would justify using a single global threshold τ rather than a regime-conditional one.
A case where the #3 candidate has min-z < 0 yet the 2-slot portfolio's Sharpe is materially LOWER than the 3-slot portfolio's Sharpe — would refute the 'abstain when min-z < 0' rule.

Inclusion of pullback_pct, base_duration_weeks, and base_depth_pct with full coverage (no nulls) showing they re-rank the floor in ways that flip 2-slot vs 3-slot decisions in < 10% of cases — would show the current feature set is approximately sufficient.

A transaction-cost-adjusted Sharpe comparison showing 2-slot beats 3-slot by > 0.1 Sharpe units net of round-trip costs on at least 50 candidate-snapshot pairs — would validate the marginal-efficiency-fronier claim that 2 slots is the economic optimum.

tests.name: T1_min_z_floor_dual_leakage_stress_test
tests.comparison: Within the frozen 27-case set, compute the minimum z-score across the six proposed separator features against the FN-cluster median. Count (a) SW cases whose min-z < 0 (false-abstention rate) and (b) FP_ruin cases whose min-z > 0 (false-inclusion rate on the ruin tail). Compare both rates to the naive base rate of picking the strongest feature alone (max-z).
tests.success_criterion: If the proposed min-z floor is genuinely informative, false-abstention rate on SW plus false-inclusion rate on FP_ruin must both be < 15% and strictly lower than the max-z single-feature baseline (Mechanism A: genuine multi-feature signal beats single-feature).
tests.failure_criterion: Either rate > 25% OR not lower than the max-z baseline: the min over correlated features concentrates on noise; the apparent gain from six features is an artifact of redundancy (Mechanism C).

tests.name: T2_within_snapshot_variance_decomposition
tests.comparison: Compute the share of total cross-sectional variance for each of the six features that is explained by snapshot identity (snap_*) vs by entity identity, using an ANOVA decomposition on the frozen 27 cases. Then compute the pairwise within-snapshot Spearman correlation among the six features and compare to cross-snapshot correlation.
tests.success_criterion: For the slot-independence assumption required by the 1/2/3 position-count economics to hold, within-snapshot variance share must be < 40% for at least 4 of 6 features AND average within-snapshot |ρ| must be < 0.5. If both conditions hold, three-slot diversification can be evaluated as roughly uncorrelated capital deployment.
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot variance share ≥ 50% for a majority of features OR average within-snapshot |ρ| ≥ 0.55: snapshot ≈ regime and slot #3 is loading correlated factor exposure, invalidating Mechanism D's diversification claim regardless of any per-candidate PIT statistic. The position-count economic comparison must then be reformulated under a within-snapshot covariance penalty.

tests.name: T3_FN_anchor_contamination_sensitivity
tests.comparison: Re-derive the FN-cluster median for each of the six features under three exclusion rules: (i) drop cases with multi-label contamination (entity_6618d3e80c type), (ii) drop any case where pullback_pct is null AND the comparator cluster median uses non-null subsamples only, (iii) the strictest intersection of (i) and (ii). Recompute the min-z statistic for each of the 27 entities under each rule and count how many entities flip from abstain to include or vice versa.
tests.success_criterion: Fewer than 3 entities (≤ 11%) flip decisions across the three anchors. The floor is robust to the cluster-definition leakage the skeptic flagged.
tests.failure_criterion: ≥ 4 entities flip OR the sign of the median delta reverses on ≥ 2 features across the three anchors: the FN-cluster centroid is unstable in the n=5–7 regime and any min-z < 0 gate is a leakage artifact (Mechanism B dominates A). Standardization must be redone against a leakage-free anchor or the floor must be abandoned.

tests.name: T4_pullback_pct_missingness_null_model
tests.comparison: The +0.64 standardized delta on pullback_pct was computed on n=7 non-null observations (5 SW + 2 FN). Draw 10,000 bootstrap samples of size 5 (SW non-null) and size 2 (FN non-null) from the empirical null where the null is 'pullback_pct median is exchangeable across clusters'. Compute the distribution of standardized delta under the null and locate the observed +0.64 in that distribution.
tests.success_criterion: Observed +0.64 standardized delta falls in the upper 5% tail of the null distribution (one-sided p < 0.05): the pullback_pct separation is unlikely to arise from missingness-driven subsample selection alone, justifying its inclusion in the composite.
tests.failure_criterion: Observed delta falls in the central 50% of the null distribution (p > 0.25, two-sided): the +0.64 figure is a small-sample artifact of differential missingness. Pullback_pct must be either (a) dropped from the composite or (b) paired with an explicit missingness indicator, and the composite recomputed without it.

tests.name: T5_vector_negative_control_pairs
tests.comparison: Within the frozen 27 cases, find all pairs of entities (i, j) such that the Euclidean distance in the 6-feature standardized space is below the 20th percentile of all pairwise distances. Among these near-neighbor pairs, count how many pairs have the SAME outcome label and how many have DIFFERENT labels.
tests.success_criterion: Same-label share ≥ 60% among near-neighbor pairs: the 6-feature space produces locally consistent outcome groupings, supporting the composite's representational validity.
tests.failure_criterion: Same-label share ≤ 40% (i.e., near-neighbors disagree more often than they agree): the 6-feature space is locally inconsistent about the W4 bucket. Entity_2f86543bf6-type and entity_8f0df3d38e-type micro-counterexamples dominate the surface. The min-z floor's apparent discrimination is averaging over a locally incoherent signal.

tests.name: T6_position_count_within_snapshot_covariance_accounting
tests.comparison: For each snapshot with ≥ 3 candidates, compute the empirical within-snapshot feature-correlation matrix among the six features. Then simulate the per-snapshot W4 variance of (a) 3-slot equal-weight portfolio, (b) 2-slot portfolio (drop the bottom by raw min-z), (c) 1-slot portfolio (top by raw max-z). Use the frozen W4 buckets as the realized return input — this is observation, not forward prediction. The test is structural, not predictive: it asks whether the variance ordering of slot-counts is determined by within-snapshot correlation rather than per-candidate PIT strength.
tests.success_criterion: Within-snapshot average |ρ| < 0.4 AND 3-slot variance ≤ 2-slot variance ≤ 1-slot variance: the diversification hierarchy is real and the PIT composite affects only the ranking, not the slot-count structure. Position-count economics reduces to a ranking problem.
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot average |ρ| ≥ 0.55 OR 2-slot variance < 3-slot variance: the third slot adds correlated exposure rather than independent alpha, and the 1/2/3 economic comparison must be reformulated as a covariance-weighted marginal-alpha question, with τ potentially set even tighter to compensate for correlated residual risk.

tests.name: T7_single_feature_baseline_AUC_inequality
tests.comparison: Compute the rank-AUC of each single feature (in isolation) for separating SW from FN using only PIT values. Then compute the rank-AUC of the min-z composite (six features, against FN median). Pre-specify the inequality that must hold for the multi-feature floor to be a justified addition over the simplest possible baseline.
tests.success_criterion: AUC(composite) ≥ AUC(best single feature) + 0.05 AND AUC(composite) > 0.6: the composite captures information not in any single feature, justifying the added complexity and the min-floor aggregation logic.
tests.failure_criterion: AUC(composite) ≤ AUC(best single feature): the multi-feature floor is parsimony-violating. The mechanism dissolves to a single dominant feature (likely mom_20). Recommend collapsing the policy to a single threshold on the best-feature direction with a calibration guardrail, not the six-feature min-z.

tests.name: T8_abstention_asymmetric_payoff_evidence_check
tests.comparison: Among is_b0_pick = false cases (the candidate pool for the #3 slot), compute the median W4 bucket position for those whose min-z < 0 (floor-abstained) vs min-z > 0 (floor-included). Then ask whether the abstention asymmetry Hypothesis E requires is observable in the data at all, given how few is_b0_pick = false cases exist (7 in the frozen set).
tests.success_criterion: The asymmetry is observed with the expected sign AND the magnitude exceeds the IQR of the bucket distribution: the abstain/promote economic argument has empirical backing at the candidate-pool level.
tests.failure_criterion: Direction is correct but magnitude is within IQR, OR direction is wrong, OR the is_b0_pick = false sample is too small (n=7) to support any direction claim. Mark Hypothesis E UNRESOLVED pending a larger candidate-pool sample; the position-count policy must default to the conservatism branch (1 or 2 slots) until evidence accumulates.

leakage_checks: Verify that no test requests W4 return magnitudes beyond the frozen snapshot_anon labels — every success_criterion references existing bucket labels or PIT-only statistics, never new forward inference.
Confirm that snapshot_anon and entity_anon are used only as group identifiers for variance decomposition and never as inputs to any predictive PIT feature.

Confirm that ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, despite being PIT, is treated as a soft composite input only and never as a hard veto (skeptic flagged FP_ruin contamination in entity_8f0df3d38e at 0.069).
Confirm pullback_pct is excluded from any composite until T4 resolves the missingness artifact, regardless of its standardized delta.

Confirm that the FN-cluster median used as the standardization anchor is the cluster that excludes entity_6618d3e80c (dual-label contamination) before T3 is run; report the pre-removal and post-removal anchors side by side.
Confirm no test uses ticker identity, calendar identity, day-of-week, month, or quarter as a feature.

Confirm the 3-slot accounting is fixed at the test level: equal-weight deployment of capital across the N filled slots is not a feature, and the test outcome does not depend on position sizing within the filled set.
Confirm that within-snapshot correlation in T2 and T6 is computed only on the frozen 27 cases; no cross-snapshot extrapolation is implied as predictive input.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The hypothesis that a minimum-z PIT composite (across {mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5}, standardized against the false-negative cluster median) can directionally identify a weak third candidate at entry is plausible but uncalibrated in the frozen 27-case window. The directional signal is supported (FN cluster sits ~0.6–1.2 standardized units below SW on the top-4 PIT features), but three distinct layers of evidence undermine a calibrated threshold claim: (i) the FN-cluster centroid is partly defined by an outer-forward outcome rule ('W4 ≥ 8% AND ≥ 5pp above B0 median'), so the anchor is a hybrid PIT/forward object rather than a clean PIT object — this is implicit leakage at the centroid definition, not at the candidate observation; (ii) the cross-feature correlations, the snapshot-cluster structure, and the missingness pattern of pullback_pct introduce correlated-noise and small-sample artifacts that the static standardizations cannot disentangle; (iii) the 1/2/3-slot economic comparison is fundamentally a covariance question (correlated momentum factors in #2 and #3 reduce diversification benefit) that the frozen sample cannot resolve because within-snapshot covariance estimation requires per-snapshot degrees-of-freedom the data does not contain. The most defensible reading is that an AND-conditioned floor on 4 (not 6) top-features, anchored at a hand-tuned percentile rather than the empirical FN median, gives a directional abstention signal useful at the policy-as-prior level, but the SNR is not high enough to support a deterministic threshold rule.
falsifiers: T1 outcome: if min-z false-abstention rate on SW exceeds 25% OR is not lower than max-z baseline, the apparent multi-feature gain is redundancy-not-signal (composite fails the parsimony test and collapses to single-feature dominance).
T3 outcome: if ≥ 4 entities flip decision across the three FN-anchor rules, the floor's mean is unstable at n=5–7 and any min-z<0 gate is anchor-leakage rather than signal.

T6 outcome: if within-snapshot average |ρ| ≥ 0.55 across the six features, the 1/2/3 economic ordering is determined by covariance, not per-candidate alpha — the position-count policy must be reformulated under a within-snapshot covariance penalty, and τ becomes correlation-conditional.

T7 outcome: if AUC(composite) ≤ AUC(best single feature, likely mom_20 or up_day_ratio_20), the multi-feature floor is parsimony-violating and should collapse to a one-threshold rule with a calibration guardrail.

Calibration falsifier: if a held-out forward window (n ≥ 30 new candidates, observed forward only AFTER entry) shows the floor's lift over a no-floor baseline has 95% CI crossing zero, the directional signal does not survive sample extension.

Label-anchor falsifier: an explicit re-labeling of the 'false_negative' cluster using a non-W4-anchored definition (e.g., bottom-quartile by base_depth_pct AND bottom-quartile by mom_20) yields a centroid that does NOT rank-order the existing 27 cases the same way, indicating the current FN centroid is label-coupled and the floor inherits that coupling.

Position-count falsifier: across all snapshots with ≥ 3 candidates in the held-out window, the Sharpe ordering 3-slot ≤ 2-slot ≤ 1-slot is reversed from the theory's diversification prediction, implying correlated residual dominates the diversification payoff and the 3-slot default is structurally sub-optimal.
actionable_design_principles: Pre-specify the floor statistic computation BEFORE seeing any candidate: Z_floor(c) = min over k in {1..K} of [ (x_k(c) − μ_k(FN_anchor)) / σ_k(FN_anchor) ], where K starts at 4 (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50) and is recursively reduced by Held-out AUC gain ≥ 0.03 per added feature.

Anchor contamination control: the FN cluster definition must be re-expressed as a PIT-only proxy (bottom-quartile by base_depth_pct AND bottom-quartile by mom_20, for example) for at least one sensitivity branch; report the floor thresholds and SW/FN flip counts under both anchor rules side by side.

Separate the two distinct policy questions: (a) whether to abstain on #3 given a PIT composite (a ranking/abstention problem), and (b) whether 1, 2, or 3 slots is optimal under marginal-correlation structure (a portfolio construction problem). Do not let one resolve the other.

Do not use pullback_pct in the composite until its missingness-driven positive delta is decomposed against an explicit null model (T4); if the +0.64 delta collapses to null-distribution noise, drop the feature from the floor entirely rather than imputing.

Calibration guardrail: any floor-driven abstention must be paired with a separate 'conviction ceiling' check (absolute minimum on mom_20 OR px_vs_ma50) to avoid the false-abstention failure mode already observed in entity_2f86543bf6, where low PIT readings paired with favorable base structure produced a large_win.

Snapshot heterogeneity: treat each snap_* as a regime marker in policy documentation; if the held-out extension shows floor behavior reverses across snapshots, the floor should become snapshot-conditional (regime-gated) rather than universal.

Capital-allocation rule under unresolved covariance: when the within-snapshot |ρ| cannot be estimated with confidence, default to 1- or 2-position deployment rather than 3, on the basis that the downside of correlated residual is asymmetric (FN_relative compounds across the holding window whereas FP_ruin is concentrated in single names).

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Z_floor_AND_gate_with_conviction_ceiling_v1
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Combines the minimum-z AND-condition (the Researcher's mechanism) with an absolute floor on a single high-AUC feature to bound the false-abstention failure mode (entity_2f86543bf6-type). Operates strictly on PIT values, with the FN-cluster centroid computed under a PIT-only proxy branch in parallel to the original (mixed-anchor) branch.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Directly operationalizes the 'weak third candidate' abstention signal under a fixed 3-slot capital budget. By AND-conditioning across the top-4 features and OR-conditioning with a single-feature ceiling, the policy preserves the FR-defined direction while hedging against the false-abstention tail observed in the frozen set. The dual-anchor branch addresses the implicit-leakage concern raised by the Skeptic without requiring a relabeling of the full dataset.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot_regime_conditional_slot_allocator_v1
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Reframes the 1/2/3-slot choice as a regime-conditional decision: when within-snapshot covariance among the top-4 PIT features is above a sentinel threshold (estimated on a rolling window), the policy allocates ≤ 2 slots regardless of individual PIT strength; otherwise it allocates up to 3 slots gated only by the Z_floor. This explicitly decouples the per-candidate alpha question from the portfolio-construction question, which the prior analysis conflated.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Maps directly to the position-count economic question (1 vs 2 vs 3 slots) by making the covariance regime observable and policyable, rather than assuming independence between slots. Avoids the dominant-mode failure where the third slot loads correlated factor exposure and adds residual rather than alpha.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: PIT_only_FN_anchor_proxy_branch_v1
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Replaces the mixed PIT/forward FN-cluster anchor with a pure-PIT proxy (e.g., bottom-quartile by base_depth_pct AND mom_20 cross-quartile) and runs the Z_floor statistic against both anchors in parallel. The capacity decision is made on whichever anchor yields the higher held-out AUC, with a mandatory dual-anchor disagreement audit when the two floors give conflicting abstention calls on the same candidate.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Provides a falsifiable, auditable handling of the implicit-leakage concern at the centroid definition. The disagreement audit creates a documented uncertainty band that maps onto an explicit capacity reduction (e.g., demote 3-slot to 2-slot when anchors disagree on the third candidate) rather than silently inheriting the leakage into the threshold.

cycles.question: For weak third candidate, determine how to falsify an adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: With three fixed capital slots, a weak third candidate should usually be assigned capacity 0 rather than mechanically filling the third slot. Capacity 1 represents a concentrated bet on a single high-conviction candidate, capacity 2 trades one unit of concentration for diversification, and capacity 3 should be reserved for a third candidate whose point-in-time quality is comparable to the first two. A weak candidate is characterized by low 20-day up-day participation, subdued near-term volume expansion, weak 20-day momentum, and proximity to the 20- and 50-day moving averages. Adding that candidate can reduce average quality and increase the chance that an apparently valid breakout fails or produces ruin, while 0 and sometimes 1 preserve optionality for future candidates. This claim concerns the incremental information carried by the third-ranked candidate, not ticker identity or calendar effects.
evidence_for: The archaeology identifies eight false-positive-ruin cases and one case carrying both false-positive-ruin and selected-winner labels; these show that breakout-like observations can be selected at entry and subsequently fail.

Several selected-winner cases have weak-looking point-in-time features, so observable weakness is not proof of future failure. For example, entity_2f86543bf6 had mom_20 near zero, slightly negative ma20_slope_5, and small px_vs_ma20, yet its later bucket was large_win. This supports abstention as a risk-control hypothesis but also argues for uncertainty rather than a deterministic cutoff.

Relative to selected winners, false negatives have materially lower median up_day_ratio_20 (0.500 versus 0.625), vol_ratio_5_20 (1.179 versus 1.424), mom_20 (0.058 versus 0.163), and px_vs_ma50 (0.056 versus 0.127). The adaptive rule should therefore treat a weak third candidate as low-priority, not as a claim that the candidate will necessarily lose.

The false-positive-ruin examples often show moderate entry extension without uniformly stronger breadth, volume, or momentum. For example, entity_84824e6a20 had ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct 0.0738, up_day_ratio_20 0.40, mom_20 0.067, and a later ruin bucket. This pattern is consistent with a low-quality third slot diluting the portfolio's stronger signals.

The archaeological label method itself uses future W4 performance, so selected_winner, false-positive-ruin, false-negative-relative, and false-negative-big-winner are outcome labels and must not be used as if available at the decision date. The falsification test must use only entry-time candidate features and known portfolio state.
evidence_against: Weak point-in-time features are not sufficient to justify capacity 0. Entity_2f86543bf6 was weak on up_day_ratio_20 and momentum yet later classified as a large winner, while entity_3adc078f01 had modest up-day participation and volume ratio but later a large winner bucket.

The supplied evidence contains no simultaneous, matched observations of the same candidate under capacities 0, 1, 2, and 3. It therefore cannot identify the causal effect of changing capacity or establish that capacity 0 dominates capacity 1 or 2.

The 27-case sample is small, discovery-train-only, and includes only a limited number of explicit false-negative and false-positive cases. It cannot support a stable numerical threshold, guarantee monotonic returns, or establish that weak candidates should be excluded in all market states.

The evidence does not provide the complete ranking distribution, cross-sectional candidate universe, contemporaneous competing candidates, or the later performance of all alternatives. Consequently, a weak third candidate may be inferior to the held candidates but still superior to leaving capital uninvested or to a future replacement.
Outcome labels include future W4 returns and relative comparisons, so using their patterns to define a present-time policy risks lookahead bias and outcome-based selection.
falsifiable_predictions: For third-ranked candidates below prespecified thresholds for up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, and distance above ma20 and ma50, the observed next-period performance distribution should be shifted toward lower returns and higher loss frequency than for third-ranked candidates above the thresholds. A failure of this ordering would falsify the proposed weak-candidate abstention mechanism.

Within the weak-third stratum, a policy that leaves the slot open should outperform a policy that always allocates the third slot on mean return per unit risk, and should avoid the largest observed ruin outcomes. The comparison must use identical dates, candidate universe, transaction costs, and capital sizing.

Conditional on a weak third candidate, capacity 1 should be chosen when the first candidate has substantially stronger point-in-time breadth, momentum, volume confirmation, and moving-average separation than the second and third candidates. Capacity 1 should deliver lower drawdown or better return concentration than capacity 2 or 3, while accepting lower diversification.

Capacity 2 should dominate capacity 3 when the second candidate is materially stronger than the third on the same entry-time quality features. If adding the third slot does not improve return per unit risk, this would falsify the proposed diversification benefit and support abstention.

Capacity 3 should only be selected when the third candidate is close to the first two on quality and its incremental entry evidence is strong. In such a high-quality third-candidate stratum, capacity 3 should not produce significantly worse risk-adjusted performance than capacity 2, after controlling for transaction costs.

The adaptive rule is falsified if, after controlling for candidate quality and contemporaneous portfolio composition, capacity has no relationship with incremental next-period return, loss probability, or drawdown, or if the estimated value of the third slot is the same for weak and strong third candidates.

The mechanism is also falsified by a reproducible exception: weak third candidates whose point-in-time breadth, volume, and momentum are weak but whose subsequent return consistently exceeds the corresponding strong-third-candidate group after costs. Such a result would indicate that the proposed quality dimensions are mis-specified or temporally unstable.
policy_implications: Do not fill all three slots solely because a candidate satisfies a generic breakout trigger. Use capacity as a ranked, testable decision variable: 0 for a clearly weak third candidate, 1 for one dominant setup, 2 for two comparably strong setups, and 3 only for three similarly strong setups.

Estimate capacity effects with a fully entry-time-defined policy and causal or quasi-causal comparisons. Use date-level blocking, matched candidate ranks, and identical capital scaling; do not evaluate capacity using outcome labels as input features.

Use calibration and walk-forward validation to set thresholds for weak versus strong candidates. Avoid embedding the observed false-positive and false-negative labels directly in the rule, because those labels depend on future returns.

Interpret capacity 0 as preserving capital and avoiding dilution, not as a prediction of an immediate market decline. A weak third candidate can still win, so the policy objective should emphasize incremental risk-adjusted portfolio value and the opportunity cost of not holding a replacement.

The current evidence is insufficient to implement a definitive capacity assignment. The appropriate conclusion is UNRESOLVED pending a matched entry-time experiment capable of separating candidate-selection quality from the portfolio-construction effect of adding one, two, or three positions.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The proposed adaptive capacity rule is not falsifiable from this evidence because (a) the 'weak' label itself is partially defined by future outcomes (the false-negative definition uses W4 >= 8%), (b) the archaeology cannot separate candidate-quality effects from portfolio-diversification effects, and (c) capacity 0 is not a true abstention but a deferred selection whose opportunity cost is unmeasured. The null hypothesis that the third slot should always be filled cannot be rejected; in fact the selected-winner cases entity_2f86543bf6 (mom_20 = -0.008, up_day_ratio_20 = 0.35) and entity_8ad5cd4795 (negative MA slopes) are direct entry-time counterexamples that the prior mechanism accommodates only by retreating to 'weak ≠ certain loss', which is materially weaker than the abstention claim.

attacks.issue: Target leakage in the 'false negative' definition itself
attacks.why_it_matters: The archaeology requires false negatives to have future W4 >= 8% AND >=5pp above the B0 selected median. This makes 'false negative' a post-hoc construct that selects entities which were rejected at entry but would have been large winners. The standardized deltas (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20) that allegedly characterize 'weak' candidates are computed on a population that was filtered precisely because they won. Any threshold derived from these medians inherits the W4 conditioning and cannot be used entry-time without re-introducing the leakage.

attacks.issue: Conflation of candidate-quality effect with slot-filling/diversification effect
attacks.why_it_matters: All 27 cases are B0 picks observed together. The evidence never contrasts a regime where slot 3 is filled with the same candidate against a regime where slot 3 is left open (or filled with an alternative). Capacity 1, 2, and 3 cannot be disentangled from one another: there is no within-snapshot, within-rank, within-date comparison where the only difference is whether slot 3 is occupied. The 'rule' therefore cannot be empirically tested on this evidence regardless of threshold choice.

attacks.issue: Capacity 0 is not a real abstention; it is an unmodeled deferred fill
attacks.why_it_matters: If a portfolio maintains a target of 3 slots, capacity 0 today implies the slot will be filled tomorrow or next week by whatever candidate is available then. The archaeology provides no evidence on (i) the quality of replacement candidates, (ii) the timing cost of waiting, or (iii) whether the replacement is systematically better or worse than today's weak third. The 'preserves optionality' framing in the prior output is untested and could easily be wrong — replacements during rising regimes may be weaker than the abstained weak third.

attacks.issue: Selected-winner cases with weak entry features directly refute a hard abstention threshold
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_2f86543bf6 (mom_20 = -0.008, ma20_slope_5 = -0.008, up_day_ratio_20 = 0.35) and entity_8ad5cd4795 (ma10_slope_5 = -0.006, ma20_slope_5 = -0.003) would be classified 'weak' on the proposed dimensions yet both became large_win. If these were third-ranked candidates under fixed 3-slot capital, abstention would have left return on the table. The prior researcher's escape — that 'weak ≠ certain loss' — collapses the abstention claim into noise tolerance, at which point the rule has no decision content.

attacks.issue: Median standardized differences conflate magnitude with policy thresholding
attacks.why_it_matters: Standardized deltas of -1.19 (up_day_ratio_20) and -1.05 (vol_ratio_5_20) are computed on small, non-i.i.d. samples with heteroscedastic features across snapshots. A delta of -1σ in 27 mixed-snapshot cases does not imply a policy-relevant cutoff exists at, say, up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50. Bootstrap intervals would almost certainly overlap the false-positive-ruin and selected-winner medians, especially because 8 false-positive-ruin cases also exhibit moderate up_day_ratio_20 (0.40–0.65).

attacks.issue: The 'weak third' stratum is never isolated; the rule's conditioning variable is missing
attacks.why_it_matters: The evidence does not record candidate rank (1st, 2nd, 3rd) within B0. Some false-positive-ruin cases may have been the strongest pick of the day; some selected-winners may have been the weakest. Without rank conditioning, the claim 'capacity 0 for weak third' cannot be evaluated: the same feature profile on a #1 candidate may have entirely different implications than on a #3 candidate. The prior policy implication collapses without this conditioning.

attacks.issue: Survivorship in label assignment biases the false-positive-ruin count
attacks.why_it_matters: Eight false-positive-ruin cases share the snapshot snap_d0d57b1e40 / snap_b8420124eb / snap_71486ed83c cluster. If a single bad regime produced multiple ruins (e.g., a sharp drawdown window), the 'weak candidate → ruin' mechanism is actually a 'bad-regime → ruin' mechanism, and the abstention rule would not generalize. Snapshot clustering is not controlled for.

attacks.issue: The 'adaptive 0/1/2/3' framing implies ordinality of conviction, but capacity may be a latching constraint, not a belief
attacks.why_it_matters: If portfolio construction is constrained (e.g., sector exposure limits, cash buffer rules, margin requirements), capacity 0/1/2/3 may be mechanically determined by constraints rather than belief strength. Treating capacity as a free ordinal signal of candidate quality introduces a category error: the same 'weak third' could legitimately be capacity 0 due to a cash rule rather than a conviction rule, and the archaeology cannot separate belief from constraint.

counterexamples_to_seek: A weak-on-features third-ranked candidate that produced a top-decile W4 return despite low up_day_ratio_20, low vol_ratio_5_20, and proximity to MA20/MA50 (the entity_2f86543bf6 archetype) — demonstrates that entry-time weakness does not bound forward return.
A 'strong-on-features' third-ranked candidate that subsequently produced a ruin or loss bucket — demonstrates that the proposed quality dimensions do not guarantee success.

A matched pair of identical snapshots where slot 3 was filled vs left open, with measurable incremental Sharpe, max drawdown, and replacement-candidate quality — the only design capable of falsifying the rule.
False-positive-ruin cases where the same entity's rank within B0 was #1 rather than #3, demonstrating that the ruin is candidate-independent of slot position.

A regime where weak third candidates systematically outperformed strong third candidates (e.g., late-stage bull market where breadth is already narrowing) — would invalidate the directional claim of the abstention hypothesis.
Cases where the entity had weak entry features, was correctly abstained (capacity 0), and the replacement candidate subsequently lost — direct evidence that capacity 0 is not free.
what_would_change_my_mind: A within-snapshot, within-date, matched experiment where for each B0 pick day we observe (i) the candidate quality features of all 3 B0 slots, (ii) the candidate that would have replaced slot 3 if left empty, and (iii) the W4 outcome under both 'fill slot 3' and 'leave slot 3 / fill replacement' policies. If 'leave slot 3' dominates on risk-adjusted return after costs, the abstention claim is no longer UNRESOLVED.

An entry-time-only threshold (no future return in its construction) for 'weak third' that, when applied prospectively out-of-sample, produces monotonically lower mean W4 return and higher loss frequency for the 'weak third fill' group vs the 'weak third abstain' group, with statistically significant separation after multiple-testing correction.

Evidence that false-positive-ruin cases predominantly occur at rank 3 within B0 (i.e., that ruin is conditional on slot position, not just on candidate quality). Without this, rank-conditioning of the rule has no empirical anchor.

A demonstrated monotonic relationship: capacity 0 > capacity 1 > capacity 2 > capacity 3 in average next-period risk-adjusted return, holding first-two-slot quality fixed. Any deviation (e.g., capacity 2 > capacity 1) would falsify the ordinal conviction interpretation.

Replacement-candidate evidence showing that candidates available on day t+1 are systematically higher-quality than the abstained weak third, AND that this replacement advantage persists across regimes. This is what 'preserves optionality' actually requires to be true.

Decomposition of the false-positive-ruin population into 'regime-driven' vs 'candidate-driven' failures, demonstrating that abstaining on weak features would have prevented the ruin in the latter case only.

tests.name: Within-date capacity marginal contribution
tests.comparison: For each B0 pick date, simulate three fixed-slot portfolios: capacity 1 (top-ranked slot only), capacity 2 (top two slots), capacity 3 (all three slots). Hold candidate identity and entry timing identical. Compute the incremental W4 risk-adjusted return (Sharpe, max drawdown, ruin probability) of slot 3 over the slot 1-2 baseline. Compare this incremental contribution across weak-third vs strong-third strata defined entry-time by the composite quality threshold.
tests.success_criterion: Slot 3's incremental risk-adjusted return is positive and statistically significant (after multiple-testing correction) only within the strong-third stratum, and negative or insignificant within the weak-third stratum. The gradient between strata is significantly negative.
tests.failure_criterion: Slot 3's incremental contribution is statistically indistinguishable between weak-third and strong-third strata, OR is negative in both strata (rule is anti-information).

tests.name: Rank-conditioned weak-quality threshold
tests.comparison: Apply the weak-quality composite threshold separately to candidates ranked #1, #2, #3 within each B0 snapshot. Compare mean W4 return, ruin probability, and max drawdown for threshold-pass vs threshold-fail cases at each rank. Test for an interaction between rank and threshold-pass status using a rank × weak-quality fixed-effects regression with cluster-robust standard errors at the snapshot level.
tests.success_criterion: Weak-quality threshold-fail at rank 3 produces significantly lower mean W4 return and higher ruin probability than weak-quality threshold-pass at rank 3, while weak-quality threshold-fail at rank 1 produces returns indistinguishable from threshold-pass at rank 1. The rank × weak-quality interaction term is significant.
tests.failure_criterion: Weak-quality threshold-fail produces similarly poor outcomes at rank 1 and rank 3 (no interaction), OR weak-quality threshold-fail at rank 3 produces no worse outcome than threshold-pass at rank 3 (threshold is non-discriminating at rank 3).

tests.name: Snapshot-cluster regime decomposition
tests.comparison: Group snapshots into clusters by entry-time realized volatility regime (rv_20 quantile × breadth regime defined by median up_day_ratio_20). Within each cluster, decompose false-positive-ruin cases by slot position (rank 1, 2, 3) and by weak-quality status. Test whether ruin attribution to rank 3 is concentrated in specific regimes or distributed uniformly.
tests.success_criterion: Within adverse-volatility or narrowing-breadth regimes, ruin is disproportionately concentrated at rank 3 and the weak-quality threshold predicts it. Within benign regimes, ruin does not concentrate at rank 3 and the threshold does not predict it. Regime × rank interaction is significant.
tests.failure_criterion: Ruins distribute evenly across slot positions within any single regime cluster, OR the weak-quality threshold predicts ruin uniformly across regimes (no regime interaction), indicating the rule captures regime rather than slot-position-specific candidate quality.

tests.name: Monotonic capacity gradient under matched slot-1/2 quality
tests.comparison: Construct matched pairs of B0 pick dates where the top-two slot candidates have near-identical composite quality (within ±0.5σ). Within each pair, compare the W4 return distribution under capacity 1, capacity 2, and capacity 3 policies. Test for a monotone ordering: μ(capacity 1) ≥ μ(capacity 2) ≥ μ(capacity 3) on risk-adjusted return.
tests.success_criterion: The matched-pair differences satisfy capacity 1 ≥ capacity 2 ≥ capacity 3 in mean risk-adjusted return with non-significant reversals. The marginal cost of adding slot 3 is non-positive when slot 3 is weak.
tests.failure_criterion: Any reversal of monotonicity (e.g., capacity 2 > capacity 1, or capacity 3 > capacity 2) in more than 10% of matched pairs, OR no significant capacity ordering after matching.

tests.name: Slot-3 replacement quality differential
tests.comparison: For each simulated capacity-0 case, identify the first B0-eligible candidate that would have filled slot 3 within a defined entry window (e.g., 1, 3, 5 trading days). Measure the replacement candidate's composite quality at its own entry time using only PIT features. Compare the paired (abstained quality, replacement quality) distribution.
tests.success_criterion: Replacement candidates exhibit systematically higher composite quality than the abstained weak-third candidates (paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank with p < 0.05 after Bonferroni). The quality gap is largest when the abstained candidate is in the bottom quality quartile.
tests.failure_criterion: Replacement candidate quality is statistically indistinguishable from abstained quality, OR replacement quality is lower than abstained (capacity 0 destroys value).

tests.name: Capacity-0 optionality realization test
tests.comparison: Among simulated capacity-0 paths, stratify by the realized replacement candidate's composite quality (top half vs bottom half). Compare W4 ruin probability, mean return, and max drawdown of the high-replacement-quality paths vs low-replacement-quality paths.
tests.success_criterion: High-replacement-quality paths achieve significantly lower ruin probability and higher mean W4 return than low-replacement-quality paths, demonstrating that capacity 0's economic content depends on the realized optionality distribution.
tests.failure_criterion: Replacement candidate quality has no significant relationship with subsequent portfolio performance, indicating capacity 0 is decision-noise rather than value-preserving.

tests.name: Within-weak-stratum feature heterogeneity
tests.comparison: Restrict the sample to candidates classified as weak by the composite threshold. Within this stratum, fit single-feature logistic regressions of ruin (PIT-computable proxy only) on each component feature individually. Compare out-of-fold AUC of the composite threshold vs each single-feature threshold.
tests.success_criterion: No single feature within the composite predicts ruin significantly better than the composite itself (composite AUC > any single-feature AUC by at least 0.05, with DeLong test p < 0.05). The composite captures non-redundant information.
tests.failure_criterion: One single feature predicts ruin as well as or better than the composite (composite is over-specified), OR the composite AUC is statistically indistinguishable from random within the weak stratum (the threshold does not separate winners from losers even among 'weak' candidates).

leakage_checks: Verify that 'weak third' thresholds are derived exclusively from entry-time PIT features (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, MA slopes) without reference to w4_return_bucket or outcome_label.

Confirm that 'false_negative' and 'false_positive_ruin' labels (which depend on future W4 returns) are used only as post-hoc analysis outputs and never as inputs to threshold construction or capacity assignment.
Block all cluster-robust inference at the snapshot level; do not treat multiple B0 picks within the same snapshot as independent observations because regime exposure is shared.

For the replacement-candidate test, measure replacement quality at the replacement candidate's own entry time using only that candidate's PIT features — do not use features measured retrospectively or smoothed across multiple dates.

Verify that capacity simulation uses identical entry timing, transaction-cost assumptions, and capital scaling across capacity 1/2/3 conditions within the same date (the only varying input is which slots are occupied).
Confirm that no test uses entity_anon, snapshot_anon, or any calendar-based identifier as a predictive feature; these are permitted only as blocking/clustering variables.
Exclude is_b0_pick from feature lists — it is a selection label, not a PIT measurement of the candidate's intrinsic quality.
For the matched-pairs monotonicity test, verify that the matching procedure is defined entry-time (e.g., composite quality at t=0) and not retroactively adjusted using W4 returns.
Confirm that the regime-decomposition test uses entry-time rv_20 and up_day_ratio_20 to define regimes, not realized forward volatility.
Apply Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all within-test multiple comparisons to prevent false discovery from fishing across the seven proposed tests.
priority_order: Monotonic capacity gradient under matched slot-1/2 quality

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule hypothesizes that the third-ranked candidate carries incremental information beyond slots 1 and 2, and that when this candidate is weak on entry-time point-in-time features (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, MA slopes), capacity 0 (abstain) or capacity 1 (concentrated bet) dominates capacity 3 (full fill) on risk-adjusted return. The economic meaning is: capacity 1 trades diversification for concentration on highest-conviction signal, capacity 2 trades one unit of concentration for modest diversification if the second slot is comparable in quality, and capacity 3 requires three comparable-quality setups or it dilutes the portfolio with an inferior signal that increases ruin probability without proportional expected return. The 27-case archaeology is consistent with this mechanism (false-positive-ruin candidates cluster at weak-to-moderate PIT feature values; selected winners show higher medians on the same features), but the evidence is too small, too outcome-leaked in label construction, and lacks the matched within-date capacity counterfactuals needed to causally attribute outcomes to capacity rather than to candidate selection or regime. Therefore the mechanism is theoretically coherent and economically meaningful but not empirically established.
falsifiers: Matched-pair within-date test (Test 4): construct B0 pick dates where slots 1 and 2 have near-identical composite quality (±0.5σ) at entry. If μ(capacity 3) ≥ μ(capacity 2) ≥ μ(capacity 1) on risk-adjusted return in more than 10% of pairs after Bonferroni correction, the weak-third abstention rule is refuted because the marginal slot adds value even when its quality is below slot 1 and 2.

Rank × quality interaction test (Test 2): a regression of W4 return on rank × weak-quality-pass status, with snapshot-clustered standard errors, must show a significant negative interaction. If weak-quality-fail at rank 1 produces outcomes statistically indistinguishable from weak-quality-pass at rank 1 (no rank interaction), the rule's premise that quality matters more at rank 3 than rank 1 is false.

Replacement quality differential (Test 5): for abstained capacity-0 cases, the paired (abstained quality, replacement quality) distribution must show replacement quality > abstained quality at p < 0.05. If replacement quality is equal or lower, capacity 0 destroys expected value and the rule's 'optionality' justification collapses.

Within-weak-stratum composite discrimination (Test 7): within the weak stratum, the composite threshold's out-of-fold AUC for ruin prediction must exceed the best single-feature AUC by ≥0.05 (DeLong p < 0.05). If any single feature (e.g., up_day_ratio_20 alone) matches the composite, the composite is over-specified and the multi-feature justification for abstention is unjustified complexity.

Regime concentration test (Test 3): if ruin at rank 3 distributes uniformly across regime clusters (rv_20 × up_day_ratio_20 quantiles), the rule captures regime rather than slot-position-specific candidate quality and should be reformulated as a regime filter, not a capacity rule.

Capacity-0 optionality realization (Test 6): high-replacement-quality paths must show significantly lower ruin probability than low-replacement-quality paths. If replacement quality has no relationship to subsequent performance, capacity 0 is decision noise rather than value preservation.

Reproducible counter-example: if a stable population of weak-third candidates (below all prespecified thresholds) consistently achieves W4 ≥ median(selected winners) after costs across out-of-sample periods, the proposed quality dimensions are mis-specified and the mechanism is refuted on construct validity.

Sharpe monotonicity test: incremental Sharpe ratio of slot 3 over slots 1-2 baseline must be significantly negative in the weak-third stratum and non-negative in the strong-third stratum. Failure of either sign in either stratum refutes the adaptive rule.
actionable_design_principles: Treat capacity as a ranked, testable decision variable, not a default fill-rate: assign capacity 0 for clearly weak third candidates, capacity 1 for one dominant setup, capacity 2 for two comparable setups, and capacity 3 only when three candidates are similarly strong on entry-time PIT features.

Construct all thresholds and capacity assignments exclusively from point-in-time entry features (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5); never use outcome labels, w4_return_bucket, or future W4 returns as inputs.

Block inference at the snapshot level: cluster standard errors by snapshot_anon, treat multiple B0 picks within a snapshot as non-independent because regime exposure is shared, and avoid calendar- or ticker-based features.

Run capacity counterfactuals within the same date with identical entry timing, capital scaling, and transaction-cost assumptions; the only varying input is which slots are occupied. Construct matched-pairs comparisons when slot 1/2 quality is held fixed.
Use walk-forward validation and Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all within-test multiple comparisons to prevent threshold fishing and false discovery from the seven proposed tests.

Separate the candidate-selection decision (is this a B0-eligible setup?) from the capacity-allocation decision (do we deploy 0, 1, 2, or 3 slots to this universe?). Conflating them obscures whether observed ruin is attributable to weak selection or to portfolio dilution.

Quantify the opportunity cost of capacity 0 by estimating replacement candidate quality at defined future entry windows (1, 3, 5 trading days) using only that candidate's PIT features, never retrospective features.
Document regime context (entry-time rv_20 and up_day_ratio_20 quantile) for every capacity decision, and test regime × capacity interactions before generalizing the rule across market states.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Adaptive capacity assignment keyed on rank-3 composite quality
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Translates the adaptive 0/1/2/3 rule into a DSL operator that consumes the third-ranked candidate's entry-time PIT composite and outputs a capacity integer. Distinct from a generic fill policy because it conditions on rank-3 quality relative to slots 1-2, not on absolute threshold alone.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Direct: emits capacity ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3} as the policy output. Capacity 0 when rank-3 composite falls below weak threshold AND relative gap to slot-2 exceeds δ; capacity 1 only when slot-1 composite strongly exceeds slot-2 and slot-3; capacity 2 when slot-1 and slot-2 are comparable and slot-3 is below weak threshold; capacity 3 only when all three slots clear the strong threshold.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Within-date marginal slot contribution estimator
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Computes the incremental risk-adjusted return of slot 3 over a slot-1-2 baseline using only contemporaneous matched observations and snapshot-clustered inference. Distinct from a static rule because it estimates the causal marginal effect of capacity choice rather than asserting one.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Inputs include the composite quality of all three slots and outputs a marginal Sharpe estimate for slot 3. Capacity decision follows from the sign and significance of this marginal; abstention (capacity 0) when marginal is negative or insignificant.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Capacity-0 replacement quality differential
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Simulates abstention by estimating the quality of the first B0-eligible replacement candidate in a forward entry window (1/3/5 trading days) and outputs the paired quality gap. Distinct because it makes the opportunity cost of abstention explicit and testable rather than treating capacity 0 as free optionality.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Feeds back into the capacity decision: if replacement quality systematically exceeds abstained quality, capacity 0 is value-preserving; if not, capacity 0 destroys value and the rule should default to capacity ≥ 1.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Regime-conditioned capacity multiplier
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Applies a regime scalar to the capacity decision based on entry-time realized volatility (rv_20) and breadth (up_day_ratio_20) quantile. Distinct because it captures the regime interaction documented in the archaeology (ruin concentrates at rank 3 in adverse regimes) rather than applying a uniform rule across market states.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Scales the weak-third threshold: in adverse regimes (high rv_20, low up_day_ratio_20), the weak threshold tightens, biasing toward capacity 0 or 1; in benign regimes, the threshold relaxes toward capacity 2 or 3. Tests whether regime × rank interaction is significant.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Rank-conditioned weak-quality interaction regressor
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Embeds a rank × weak-quality interaction term into the DSL so that the same weak-quality signal at rank 1 vs rank 3 produces different capacity recommendations. Distinct because it explicitly tests the claim that quality matters more at lower ranks, not just whether weak quality predicts poor outcomes.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Outputs an interaction coefficient that, if significant, validates the asymmetric treatment of weak quality across ranks. If insignificant, refutes the premise that rank-3 abstention is fundamentally different from rank-1 abstention.

cycles.question: For single-industry crowding, determine when cash should dominate filling another slot. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: Under fixed 3-slot capital with single-industry crowding, cash dominates filling slot N+1 when the marginal candidate's expected information ratio falls below the risk-free baseline because (a) industry beta forces effective correlation toward 1, negating diversification benefit of additional slots, and (b) the surviving pool after slot 1 and 2 selection is biased toward less-mature bases (lower mom_20, shallower pullback_pct, lower px_vs_ma50, lower vol_ratio_5_20) that the historical record shows convert to wins at sub-baseline rates. The economic meaning is not 'more positions = more diversification' but rather: slot 1 = full concentrated Kelly exposure; slot 2 = pseudo-diversification whose variance reduction is ~industry_correlation²·σ²; slot 3 = option-cost-only addition whose expected return is dominated by selection-pool decay, not by independence.
evidence_for: Selected pool ruin rate is 8/20 (40%) plus 1 mixed = 45% non-pure-winner, meaning the marginal slot carries significant loss-of-capital probability independent of slot count.

False-negative set (rejected candidates that won) median mom_20 = 0.058 vs selected-winner 0.163 — survivors after the first two slots show degraded momentum signal, indicating the slot-3 pool is structurally weaker than the slot-1 pool.

False-negative median pullback_pct = -7.3% vs selected-winner -15.9% (delta +8.6pp) — shallower bases in the rejected-but-winning cohort confirm that 'looks weaker at snapshot' is not equivalent to 'will underperform', so the slot-3 filter inherits false-negative risk on top of single-industry correlation.

False-negative median px_vs_ma50 = 0.056 vs selected-winner 0.127 — candidates farther below the 50-day MA are more frequently rejected, meaning the surviving slot-3 candidates in a crowded industry tend to be price-action weaker, not stronger.

False-negative median up_day_ratio_20 = 0.50 vs selected-winner 0.625 — internal barometric pressure is lower in the rejected-winners cohort, supporting the claim that slot-3 marginal candidates carry inferior tape characteristics.
vol_ratio_5_20 standardized_delta of -1.05 between false-negative (1.18) and selected-winner (1.42) shows volume-confirmation decay in the post-selection pool.

Numeric contrast base_duration_weeks median 44 (FN) vs 52 (SW) indicates younger bases disproportionately populate the rejection pool, so the slot-3 marginal candidate is more likely to be in an earlier-stage base that the rules are structurally biased against.
evidence_against: Sample size of 27 is too small to estimate slot-3-specific ruin rates with statistical confidence.
Direct industry-correlation coefficient between simultaneous positions is not measured in this dataset, so the claim that 'effective correlation → 1' is mechanism-level inference, not empirical.
11 of 20 selected winners did produce large_win outcomes, so the slot-1 pool is not ruin-dominated — the framework must not imply 'never deploy' but 'deploy only when marginal conditions hold'.

false_positive_ruin cases (e.g., entity_40ea0cfb3b) had relatively low momentum/vol signals too (mom_20 = 0.024, vol_ratio = 0.91), suggesting some rejected-pool features are also present in ruins — features are not cleanly separable into 'slot-3 good' vs 'slot-3 bad' buckets.
No direct slot-N marginal-elasticity calculation is possible from this archaeology alone because cases are single-entity snapshots, not paired slot-add comparisons.
falsifiable_predictions: In backtests of 3-slot portfolios, when slots 1 and 2 share a GICS sub-industry, the realized return variance of slot 3 will be at least 70% of single-position variance (correlation > 0.84), falsifying the assumption that '3 positions = diversification' under crowding.

The conditional expected 4-week return of slot-3 candidates with up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.3 will be statistically indistinguishable from zero or negative, after controlling for industry exposure — supporting cash dominance.

When the best two available candidates share industry, the expected return of substituting cash for slot 3 will exceed the median large_win bucket return by ≥2pp on a risk-adjusted basis, because industry-correlation destroys the convexity benefit of the third bet.

The ruin probability of a 3-slot single-industry portfolio will be ≥ 1 - (1 - 0.40)^3 ≈ 78% if ruin events are industry-correlated, versus ~64% if independent — this gap is the quantified cost of crowding and is the threshold above which cash strictly dominates.

If industry beta is introduced as a feature, the coefficient on slot-3 dummy will be negative and significant in a return regression, whereas slot-1 dummy will be positive and significant, confirming slot-asymmetric information content.
policy_implications: Treat the 3-slot architecture as 1 concentrated slot + 1 partial-diversification slot + 1 option slot whose expected value depends on industry-orthogonality, not as '3 independent bets'.

When slots 1 and 2 are in the same industry, hard-rule slot 3 = cash unless the marginal candidate simultaneously exceeds selected-winner medians on at least three of: up_day_ratio_20 (>0.625), vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.42), mom_20 (>0.163), and pullback_pct (<-15.9%).

Define cash dominance threshold as: P(ruin|marginal) × max_loss > E[return|marginal] - cash_yield. With observed P(ruin) ≈ 0.40 in selected pool, the threshold for cash is triggered when marginal expected return falls below roughly cash_yield + 0.40 × tail_loss.

Use the standardized_deltas in this archaeology to construct a slot-3 eligibility score that explicitly penalizes industry crowding (e.g., requires industry-orthogonality or feature-superiority), and backtest whether abstention from slot 3 under crowding improves Sharpe vs full deployment.

Because false-negative rate appears high (7/7 in this sample, though small-N), the policy should treat the option value of unfilled slots as non-zero and explicitly price the cost of forcing slot 3 in crowded conditions.

Reframe '1, 2, or 3 positions' as a convexity question: slot 1 buys market exposure + Kelly upside; slot 2 buys modest variance reduction if cross-industry; slot 3 buys only convexity, which is destroyed under single-industry crowding.
If UNRESOLVED on the exact correlation coefficient: require forward measurement of intra-industry pairwise correlation of held positions before relying on diversification math.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The 'cash dominates slot 3 under single-industry crowding' claim is mostly an artifact of (a) comparing selected winners against a pool whose 'false negatives' are defined as ex-post winners (selection-on-outcome tautology), (b) attributing generic slot-rank decay to industry crowding when no industry correlation is actually measured, and (c) assuming slots 1 and 2 are exogenously forced into the same industry when slot 2's industry assignment is an endogenous choice that the framework never prices. The genuine empirical content — that the post-selection pool is feature-weaker — holds for ANY rank-order selection rule, not specifically for crowded industries.

attacks.issue: Selection-on-outcome in the FN vs SW comparison
attacks.why_it_matters: The numeric contrasts compare 'false negatives' (defined as rejected candidates with W4 >=8% and >=5pp above B0 median) against 'selected winners' (positions that were actually entered and won). By construction, the FN bucket is ex-post sorted on performance; the SW bucket mixes survivors with the same definition. The standardized deltas therefore reflect what differentiates winning late-bloomers from already-known winners — not what differentiates good from bad pre-snapshot signals. The 'slot-3 pool is structurally weaker' conclusion cannot be drawn from this contrast without an ex-ante control group of rejected non-winners, which is absent.

attacks.issue: Mechanism conflation: feature decay ≠ industry-induced correlation
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher attributes slot-3 weakness to industry beta forcing correlation → 1, but none of the measured features (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, pullback_pct) are industry-correlation proxies. A pure rank-ordering mechanism (best X go first, slot 3 is by construction lower-quality) would produce the same feature deltas without any industry effect. The 'single-industry crowding' framing adds zero explanatory power over a baseline 'third pick is weaker' model. The claim is therefore not specifically about crowding at all.

attacks.issue: The 78% ruin probability is not specific to crowding
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher computes ruin probability ≥ 1 - (1 - 0.40)^3 ≈ 78% under independence and claims that exceeding this threshold is 'the cost of crowding'. But this formula IS the independence case. For correlation > 0 the probability is higher; for correlation < 0 it is lower. The 78% figure is the floor, not the threshold that cash must beat. A 3-slot independent portfolio already 'cash dominates' in this accounting, so the entire mechanism reduces to: 'more positions in one industry aren't independent, which is true of any third position regardless of industry.'

attacks.issue: Counterexample entity_3adc078f01: -42.3% pullback, large_win
attacks.why_it_matters: This selected winner survived a 42.3% pullback to deliver a large W4 return, contradicting the policy implication that pullback_pct < -15.9% is a 'superior-feature' requirement for slot 3. If a single position with such an extreme drawdown base can be a winner, the argument that 'deeper pullback = safer' is undermined. The policy rule (require pullback_pct < -15.9%) would have explicitly rejected this winner from slot 1, suggesting the filter is overfit to the median contrast and brittle at the tails.

attacks.issue: Mixed label entity_6618d3e80c exposes ambiguous ruin definition
attacks.why_it_matters: This entity is labeled 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' — i.e., simultaneously a ruin and a winner. If 'ruin' is portfolio-level (e.g., drawdown against cost basis) and 'selected_winner' is per-position, then the ruin rate of 8/20 is being counted on a different denominator than the win rate of 11/20, and the 40% ruin figure mixes per-position and portfolio-level events. The cash-dominance arithmetic depends on this P(ruin) and is therefore not comparable to a portfolio-level benchmark.

attacks.issue: Endogeneity of slot-2 industry assignment is ignored
attacks.why_it_matters: The claim treats 'slots 1 and 2 share a GICS sub-industry' as an exogenous constraint. In practice, slot 2 is a choice: if the second-best candidate is in the same industry as slot 1, the operator can substitute the third-best cross-industry candidate. The framework therefore overstates the frequency of the crowded state and consequently overstates how often cash should dominate slot 3. A 3-slot same-industry portfolio requires the operator to reject a cross-industry alternative, which is itself an unmodeled opportunity cost.

attacks.issue: The 'option-cost' framing of slot 3 assumes slot 3 is sized like slots 1 and 2
attacks.why_it_matters: If slot 3 is half-sized or smaller, its variance contribution is mechanically reduced and 'correlation → 1' matters less. The framework's strong cash-dominance conclusion depends on equal-weighting, which the data does not specify. Under any sensible fractional Kelly or vol-targeted sizing, the slot-3 ruin probability is closer to the slot-1 ruin probability scaled by position size, not the unconditional 40%.

counterexamples_to_seek: A 3-slot same-industry portfolio where slot 3 is the dominant contributor to portfolio return (e.g., one position rugged 30%+ while the other two chopped) — would falsify 'slot 3 = option-cost-only addition' under crowding.
