An industry-orthogonal 3-slot portfolio that nonetheless shows slot-3 feature decay relative to slots 1 and 2 — would falsify the industry-specific mechanism and support the generic rank-ordering alternative.

A backtest in which 3-slot same-industry deployment beat 1-slot + cash in 2019–2021 (low cash-yield regime) but lost in 2022–2024 (high cash-yield regime) — would show the result is driven by cash-yield opportunity cost, not by industry-crowding mechanics.

Pairwise return correlations of the 8 false_positive_ruin entities vs other selected positions: if these are all from different sub-industries yet co-ruined, the 'industry forces correlation → 1' claim is false.
A held-position history showing slot 2 industry is frequently switched within 4 weeks of entry — would show that 'single-industry crowding' is a transient snapshot artifact, not a structural state.
what_would_change_my_mind: A backtest with N ≥ 500 three-slot portfolios, stratified by sub-industry overlap (0, 1, 2 shared), where the same-industry stratum shows slot-3 marginal contribution that is statistically indistinguishable from zero after controlling for slot-3 feature rank. Without this, the mechanism is unfalsifiable inference.

Direct measurement of intra-sub-industry pairwise return correlation across held positions showing the median correlation ≥ 0.6. The current dataset does not contain return series for held portfolios, only per-position snapshots.

An ex-ante rejection control: a matched set of rejected non-winners with the same feature distribution as the false negatives, used to estimate the false-positive rate of the proposed slot-3 eligibility score. Currently the score's precision is unmeasurable because the negative class is undefined.

Decomposition of the 40% per-position ruin rate into (a) signal-quality component and (b) market-regime component. If regime dominates, the cash-dominance rule is time-varying and not a structural property of slot 3.

Replication on an out-of-sample period with different industry-correlation regime (e.g., 2020 COVID where intra-tech correlation briefly approached 0.95). The current snapshot-only archaeology cannot speak to regime dependence.

tests.name: within_portfolio_rank_decay_by_overlap_stratum
tests.comparison: Within each 3-slot portfolio compute (slot_1_feature - slot_3_feature) and (slot_2_feature - slot_3_feature). Stratify portfolios by industry-overlap count (0, 1, 2 shared GICS sub-industry among the three candidates). Compare the within-portfolio rank-decay gaps across strata.
tests.success_criterion: Industry-crowding mechanism supported if the within-portfolio slot_1-to-slot_3 feature gap widens monotonically with overlap stratum (median gap in 2-shared stratum ≥ 0.5 standardized units larger than 0-shared stratum, on at least 3 of the 5 features).
tests.failure_criterion: Generic rank-order mechanism supported if the gap is approximately constant across strata (delta < 0.2 standardized units), indicating slot 3 is uniformly weaker regardless of industry structure.

tests.name: slot_position_dummy_with_overlap_interaction
tests.comparison: Fit W4 outcome (large_win / small_win / loss / ruin buckets as ordered) on slot_position dummy (slot_1, slot_2, slot_3) plus slot-3 absolute feature level plus overlap × slot_position interaction. The interaction coefficient isolates industry-specific marginal contribution after stripping rank and quality effects.
tests.success_criterion: Industry mechanism supported if the slot_3 × overlap_2 coefficient is significantly negative (p < 0.10) AFTER controlling for slot-3 absolute feature level, meaning crowding adds penalty beyond feature decay.
tests.failure_criterion: Generic mechanism supported if the interaction coefficient is statistically indistinguishable from zero, meaning slot-3 weakness is fully explained by absolute feature level with no industry-specific contribution.

tests.name: absolute_threshold_failure_odds_ratio_by_overlap
tests.comparison: Define binary indicator I_thresh = 1 if slot-3 candidate falls below selected-winner median on ≥2 of 4 features. Compute odds ratio of ruin outcome (w4_return_bucket == 'ruin') given I_thresh=1 vs I_thresh=0, separately for crowded (overlap=2) and uncrowded (overlap=0) portfolios.
tests.success_criterion: Industry mechanism supported if OR_crowded ≥ 2 × OR_uncrowded, i.e., absolute-quality failure is doubly destructive under crowding because the high industry correlation prevents offsetting winners elsewhere in the portfolio.
tests.failure_criterion: Generic mechanism supported if OR_crowded ≈ OR_uncrowded (within 25% relative tolerance), indicating quality failure hurts the same regardless of crowding.

tests.name: pairwise_base_similarity_co_ruin_test
tests.comparison: Within each 3-slot portfolio, compute pairwise Mahalanobis-style distance in base-feature space between all (i,j) candidate pairs. Test whether low-distance pairs (bottom quartile) co-ruin (both w4_return_bucket == 'ruin') more often than high-distance pairs (top quartile). Base features are pre-snapshot and not contaminated by W4 timing.
tests.success_criterion: Industry mechanism supported if co-ruin rate in low-distance pairs ≥ 2× co-ruin rate in high-distance pairs, consistent with shared base structure implying shared downstream vulnerability.
tests.failure_criterion: Generic mechanism supported if co-ruin rate is statistically indistinguishable across distance quartiles, indicating base similarity is not a usable proxy for return co-movement.

tests.name: pre_specified_abstention_rule_targeted_stratum_test
tests.comparison: Pre-specify abstention rule R: if slots 1 and 2 share GICS sub-industry AND slot-3 candidate fails ≥2 of 4 selected-winner median thresholds, replace slot 3 with cash. Apply R to historical 3-slot portfolios. Compare per-portfolio W4 outcome distribution under R vs full-deployment baseline, stratified by overlap.
tests.success_criterion: Policy supported if R improves per-portfolio ruin rate by ≥10 percentage points in the 2-shared stratum AND does not degrade ruin rate by more than 5 percentage points in the 0-shared stratum (asymmetric benefit is the signature of crowding-specific value).
tests.failure_criterion: Policy not supported if improvement in 2-shared stratum is matched or exceeded in 0-shared stratum (i.e., abstention helps regardless of crowding), in which case the rule is industry-blind and the 'crowding triggers abstention' claim is spurious.

tests.name: snapshot_level_controlled_rank_ablation
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot, rank the top-3 candidates by feature composite (z-score average of 4 features). Track whether the selected 3-slot portfolio follows rank-order exactly. Test: among snapshots where the actual 3-slot selection deviates from rank-order (e.g., slot 3 holds a higher-feature candidate than slot 2), is W4 outcome better or worse than rank-ordered selection? This separates 'slot position is causal' from 'slot position is just an index of quality'.
tests.success_criterion: Slot-position-asymmetry mechanism supported if rank-order violation yields NO W4 improvement (i.e., swapping a higher-feature candidate into slot 3 does not raise slot-3's W4 outcome), meaning slot position carries independent cost under crowding.
tests.failure_criterion: Quality-only mechanism supported if rank-order violation improves slot-3 W4 outcome, indicating slot position is purely a quality index and not an independent state.

leakage_checks: Verify w4_return_bucket is computed strictly from post-snapshot W4 prices and never enters any feature derivation; it is the outcome label only.
Verify snapshot_anon is used solely as a grouping key for paired-within-snapshot tests and is never included as a model feature or proxy.
Verify is_b0_pick is treated as a policy decision (selection outcome) and excluded from feature set; it is not a market-state descriptor.

Verify ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ibd_entry_volume_ratio, ibd_entry_close_position, ibd_entry_breakout_range_ratio, current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct are confirmed point-in-time at snapshot date and do not embed any post-snapshot return information.
Verify base_depth_pct, base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, dist_to_52w_high_pct are pre-snapshot base descriptors and not contaminated by intra-base forward return.
Verify no test derives a feature from a function of two snapshots' W4 buckets simultaneously (would leak cross-snapshot outcome structure into a single-snapshot feature).

Verify the abstention rule R uses only point-in-time features (no peeking at W4 bucket to tune thresholds); thresholds are taken from selected-winner medians disclosed in the archaeology and frozen before outcome evaluation.
Verify no feature is calendar-derived (e.g., year, quarter, month) in violation of the calendar-identity ban.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The synthesis reconciles three layers. Layer 1 (well-supported by archaeology): under fixed 3-slot capital, the third slot inherits a structurally weaker candidate pool because selection-from-rank depletes mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50 and inflates the proportion of immature bases — the slot-N marginal information ratio is mechanically lower than slot-1's. Layer 2 (mechanismally conflated in researcher output): the additional claim that single-industry crowding specifically destroys slot-3 diversification benefit via ρ→1 is not directly measured in the 27-case archaeology; the observed feature deltas are consistent with both an industry-correlation mechanism AND a pure rank-order mechanism. Layer 3 (asymmetric slot economics, analytically defensible): slot 1 buys concentrated Kelly exposure; slot 2 buys variance reduction proportional to (1−ρ) only when cross-industry; slot 3 buys convexity that requires ρ<1 to clear the cash hurdle. Under single-industry crowding, ρ→1 implies slot 3's variance reduction approaches zero while its candidate-pool quality is already degraded — the two penalties compound, which is the novel economic finding beyond either layer alone. The verdict is CONTEXT_DEPENDENT because Layer 1 is empirically grounded, Layer 3 is economically rigorous but parametrically untested, and Layer 2 conflates them — policy can be drafted from Layer 1+3 but should not claim Layer 2 as proven until the experimental designer's interaction tests are executed.
falsifiers: If the experimental designer's slot_position × overlap interaction test returns a coefficient indistinguishable from zero after controlling for absolute feature level (p > 0.10 on the overlap_2 × slot_3 term), the industry-specific crowding mechanism is REFUTED and only the generic 'slot 3 is weaker' effect remains — policy should then reframe as a uniform rank-depletion rule independent of industry structure.

If forward measurement of realized intra-industry pairwise correlation across held positions shows ρ < 0.5 in same-sub-industry 3-slot portfolios, the ρ→1 hypothesis is REFUTED and cash dominance under crowding is no longer categorically supported.

If the pairwise_base_similarity_co_ruin test shows co-ruin rate statistically indistinguishable across distance quartiles (chi-square p > 0.20), the claim that base similarity proxies for shared downstream vulnerability fails and the abstention rule loses its industry-specific foundation.

If a same-industry 3-slot portfolio in historical backtest shows ruin rate ≤ 55% (i.e., not appreciably above the 40% single-position ruin rate × independence adjustment), the compounding penalty thesis is REFUTED and cash's expected-loss advantage disappears.

If entity-class counterexamples (deep-pullback winners like entity_3adc078f01 with -42.3% pullback delivering large_win) accumulate to >10% of same-industry slot-3 cases, the pullback-depth filter as a feature-superiority requirement is OVERFIT and the policy should drop pullback_pct as a binary gate, retaining it only as a soft scoring input.

If the pre_specified_abstention_rule_targeted_stratum_test shows improvement in 2-shared stratum matched or exceeded in 0-shared stratum, the rule is industry-blind and the 'crowding triggers abstention' causal chain is REFUTED.

If false-negative rate in a larger sample (>200 cases) drops below 20%, the 'slot-3 pool is structurally weaker' claim loses its option-cost framing because the rejected pool contains too many winners to justify treating unfilled slots as positive option value.

If the ruin-rate label definition (per-position vs portfolio-level) cannot be reconciled for the mixed-label entity_6618d3e80c case in a consistent accounting framework, all P(ruin)-driven thresholds in the policy become numerically undefined and cash-dominance arithmetic collapses.
actionable_design_principles: Reframe the 3-slot capital allocation as three distinct economic instruments rather than three symmetric bets: slot 1 = concentrated Kelly exposure (priority: max expected return), slot 2 = variance-reduction slot (priority: cross-industry ρ reduction), slot 3 = convexity option (priority: positive option value conditional on candidate-pool quality AND industry orthogonality). This is the core analytical contribution and survives whether Layer 2 is later confirmed or refuted.

Decouple the policy into two independent gates: (a) a quality gate that applies to all three slots uniformly using selected-winner medians as soft thresholds (mom_20 > 0.163, vol_ratio_5_20 > 1.42, up_day_ratio_20 > 0.625, pullback_pct < -15.9% as scoring inputs not binary cutoffs), and (b) a crowding gate that applies only to slot 3 and triggers cash abstention when slots 1+2 share GICS sub-industry AND slot-3 candidate fails the quality gate on ≥2 features. The two-gate structure ensures that the generic rank-depletion effect is enforced even when industry data is unavailable.

Treat slot-3 abstention as a state-dependent option whose strike price is the candidate's marginal expected return minus cash yield plus a crowding premium: cash dominates when E[R₃] < r_f + λ·P(ruin|crowded)·L_max, where λ scales with the empirical same-industry ruin penalty (currently unmeasured, treat as a free parameter until calibrated).

Enforce a measurement prerequisite before deploying any same-industry slot-3 rule: require N ≥ 30 same-industry 3-slot portfolio outcomes with realized W4 returns and intra-portfolio pairwise correlations to calibrate ρ̂ and the ruin multiplier, otherwise default to the conservative position of abstaining from slot 3 when slots 1+2 share sub-industry.

Preserve the option value of unfilled slots explicitly in the policy: a cash slot in a crowded 3-slot configuration should be logged with its option value estimated as max(0, E[R|marginal_candidate] - r_f) conditional on the candidate pool at decision time, so that abstention is not treated as a free action but priced against the foregone convexity.

Avoid the overfit trap flagged by entity_3adc078f01: deep pullback_pct is evidence of base maturity but not a sufficient cause of large_win — therefore pullback_pct enters the policy as one input among several, never as a standalone disqualifier, and the threshold direction (more negative = better) should be tested against tail behavior, not just median contrasts.

Separate the predictive mechanism (Layer 1: slot-3 pool is weaker) from the portfolio-construction effect (Layer 2: crowding compounds the penalty) so that policy updates to one layer do not contaminate the other — the quality gate can be recalibrated on outcome data without disturbing the crowding-gate structure.

Build the abstention trigger around observable, point-in-time features only (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50, GICS overlap) and exclude any feature that embeds forward return information, snapshot identity, calendar variables, or the is_b0_pick decision variable, per the experimental designer's leakage checks.

Parameterize the policy so that the industry-specificity coefficient is a tunable input rather than a fixed assumption: the rule fires when overlap_count × quality_failure_count ≥ k, where k is calibrated on out-of-sample data; this preserves the analytical claim while preventing overcommitment to a specific overlap threshold.

Maintain a continuous audit of the ruin label definition (per-position vs portfolio-level) and resolve the entity_6618d3e80c ambiguity before deploying the policy at scale, because mixed labels corrupt the empirical ruin rate that anchors the cash-dominance arithmetic.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: AsymmetricSlotAllocator: a stateful policy that classifies each candidate into one of three slot roles (anchor, diversifier, option) and applies role-specific quality thresholds rather than a uniform 3-position filter. The anchor role inherits the standard selected-winner median thresholds with no quality discount; the diversifier role applies a 10% discount on mom_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 to allow cross-industry variance reduction; the option role applies a 25% discount on all four core features but additionally requires either cross-industry orthogonality to slots 1+2 OR simultaneous superiority on ≥3 of 4 features. If neither condition holds, the option role is set to cash.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This differs from the researcher's uniform threshold proposal by encoding slot-asymmetric economics directly: the diversifier gets a relaxed threshold because its purpose is variance reduction not return maximization, while the option gets a stricter threshold because its expected return must clear both the rank-depletion hurdle AND the crowding hurdle. The researcher's policy would treat all three slots identically and therefore either over-filter slot 2 (killing legitimate variance-reduction candidates) or under-filter slot 3 (allowing weak candidates through). The experimental designer's within_portfolio_rank_decay test would be the validation instrument for the role-specific discount magnitudes.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Directly encodes the abstention logic: capacity is preserved by allowing slot 1 to deploy at full quality, slot 2 to deploy at relaxed quality when cross-industry, and slot 3 to abstain (cash) when both quality and orthogonality fail. The policy's abstention frequency is a learnable parameter that should decrease as candidate pool quality improves and increase as crowding intensifies.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: CrowdingPenaltyMultiplier: a continuous abstention-score modifier that computes slot-3 expected value as E[R₃] = base_3_return_estimate − κ · (overlap_count²) · quality_failure_magnitude, where κ is calibrated from same-industry ruin-rate data and quality_failure_magnitude is the standardized distance below selected-winner medians. Cash dominates when this adjusted E[R₃] falls below cash_yield + transaction_cost_buffer. The policy abstains from slot 3 when the multiplier-adjusted score is non-positive, regardless of absolute feature levels.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This differs from a binary industry-overlap threshold (researcher's proposal) by making the abstention decision continuous in both overlap depth and feature weakness. It directly addresses the skeptic's mechanism-conflation concern by not claiming a specific ρ value but instead letting the empirical ruin-rate calibration drive κ. This avoids the overfit trap of hard-coding 'overlap ≥ 2 = abstain' while still penalizing crowding proportionally. It also operationalizes the researcher's cash-dominance threshold formula (P(ruin) × max_loss > E[return] - cash_yield) in a learnable, point-in-time form.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Enables graduated abstention: in mild crowding (overlap_count=1) with high slot-3 quality, the policy still deploys; in severe crowding (overlap_count=2) with marginal slot-3 quality, it abstains; this preserves more capacity than a binary rule. The same_industry_ruin_rate_estimate should be updated periodically from realized outcomes to keep κ calibrated.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: ConvexityOptionGate: a policy that explicitly prices the option value of holding slot 3 unfilled (cash) versus filled (risky asset), and abstains only when the marginal candidate's expected information ratio fails to clear the convexity hurdle under the specific crowding state. The gate computes option_value_filled = E[R₃] − VaR_0.05(filled) and option_value_cash = r_f − VaR_0.05(cash) ≈ r_f, then abstains when option_value_filled < option_value_cash AND overlap_count ≥ 1. The key novelty is the explicit pricing of the unfilled slot as a positive option rather than zero-value cash drag.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This differs from the researcher's option-cost framing (which treats abstention as a foregone bet) by inverting the valuation: abstention itself is the position with measurable expected return (r_f) and zero variance, and the question is whether filling slot 3 produces positive risk-adjusted value above that baseline. This is the economically rigorous form of the 'cash dominates' claim and avoids the binary framing of threshold rules. It also addresses the skeptic's endogeneity concern: the operator who would otherwise substitute a cross-industry candidate into slot 2 is implicitly captured because such substitution changes overlap_count and therefore the gate's decision.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Maximizes capacity utilization by deploying slot 3 whenever its risk-adjusted information ratio exceeds cash, even under moderate crowding, while abstaining when crowding is severe enough that the option value of cash exceeds any plausible slot-3 deployment. This is the most capacity-preserving of the three policies because it abstains only when economically justified.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: RankDecayEligibilityFilter: a policy that bypasses the crowding question entirely and instead enforces a uniform rank-decay filter: across all three slots, require candidate quality score (z-score composite of 4 features) to exceed max(0, top_candidate_score − decay_factor × slot_index), where decay_factor is calibrated to the empirical slot-1-vs-slot-3 quality gap from archaeology. If slot 3's candidate falls below this decaying threshold, abstain to cash regardless of industry overlap.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This is the skeptic-aligned policy: it accepts Layer 1 (rank-depletion) as the operative mechanism and rejects Layer 2 (crowding-specific penalty) until empirically validated. It differs from the researcher's crowding-triggered abstention by treating the abstention as a quality-decay phenomenon rather than an industry phenomenon. The advantage is robustness: the policy works even when industry classification is unavailable or noisy, and it makes no claim about ρ values. The disadvantage is that it may over-abstain in cross-industry configurations where slot-3 candidates are legitimately strong.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Industry-blind abstention: abstention frequency depends only on the candidate pool's quality distribution across slots, not on industry structure. This is the conservative baseline against which the crowding-aware policies should be benchmarked; if a crowding-aware policy cannot outperform this baseline in out-of-sample tests, the crowding mechanism is REFUTED and this becomes the deployed policy.

cycles.question: For single-industry crowding, determine what PIT statistic can measure confidence without future leakage. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: Single-industry crowding inflates apparent independence among B0 candidates. A PIT-only statistic that captures confidence without future leakage is the cross-sectional dispersion (e.g., standard deviation or interquartile range) of the composite signal {up_day_ratio_20 + z(vol_ratio_5_20) + z(mom_20)} across the same-industry candidate cluster at snapshot time — call it 'cluster_dispersion'. When cluster_dispersion is LOW, candidates are redundant expressions of the same industry factor, so slot 2 and slot 3 contribute near-zero marginal diversification; when cluster_dispersion is HIGH, candidates carry idiosyncratic alpha and additional slots are genuinely additive.
evidence_for: Numeric contrast table shows up_day_ratio_20 (std Δ −1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (std Δ −1.05) and mom_20 (std Δ −1.00) as the three largest discriminators between selected_winner and false_negative classes — all PIT-observable at snapshot, no future leakage.

Label distribution (11 selected_winner vs 8 false_positive_ruin) shows the model already admits substantial ruin risk on B0 picks despite positive PIT features, consistent with feature agreement being necessary but not sufficient under crowding.

entity_3472243e0c (false_positive_ruin, w4=ruin) has mom_20=0.242, up_day_ratio_20=0.65, vol_ratio_5_20=1.21 — all 'good' individually but cluster likely shared these levels with same-industry peers, illustrating why absolute features mislead under crowding.

entity_6618d3e80c carries dual label 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' on the SAME snapshot with mom_20=0.251, px_vs_ma50=0.337 — the strongest absolute features in the set still produce heterogeneous outcomes, evidencing that redundancy within a cluster inflates single-name confidence incorrectly.

Pullback_duration_weeks median delta of −1.5 weeks (std Δ −0.73) and pullback_pct reversed delta (+0.64) indicate base-formation heterogeneity IS captured PIT, meaning dispersion-style statistics are constructible without future info.

Entity_2f86543bf6 (winner) has ma20_slope_5 = −0.0078 yet won — supports the claim that ABSOLUTE single-name signals are noisy; what matters is whether the candidate DIFFERS from its industry peers at snapshot.

False_negative cases show systematically lower vol_ratio_5_20 (−0.24 median delta) — a low-vol candidate embedded in a high-vol industry cluster is exactly the redundancy signal cluster_dispersion would expose PIT.
evidence_against: Cluster dispersion is NOT directly observable in the provided feature set — we only see per-entity snapshots, not peer-group composition or industry tags, so the proposed statistic requires construction that this evidence alone cannot validate.

Some ruin cases (entity_84824e6a20, entity_b6bcccdf6a) carry high ma10_slope_5 (>0.06) AND high mom_20 (>0.17) yet failed, suggesting even DIVERSE-looking candidates within a cluster can co-fail — cluster_dispersion may UNDERSTATE true same-industry correlation.

pullback_pct has POSITIVE standardized delta (+0.64), meaning selected_winners had DEEPER pullbacks than false_negatives — opposite of naive intuition; this complicates any linear composite and warns that simple z-score addition may mis-rank under regime shifts.

False_negative_big_winner|false_negative_relative label exists (n=2), showing missed big upside on PIT-fuzzy candidates — abstention cost is real and asymmetric, so aggressive 1-slot-only policy under crowding has opportunity cost.

The data contains no explicit 'industry_group' or 'cluster_id' field; identifying 'same-industry' clustering itself requires an auxiliary PIT mapping (e.g., IBD sector tags) that is not validated within this frozen evidence.
Case count is only 27 with mixed snapshot IDs — statistical power to detect dispersion thresholds is limited; the claim is mechanistic rather than empirically confirmed.
falsifiable_predictions: If cluster_dispersion (std of {up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20}) across same-industry candidates at snapshot is computed PIT, then candidates with cluster_dispersion below the 25th percentile will exhibit pairwise 4-week return correlation ≥0.6, versus <0.3 for candidates above the 75th percentile.

Under fixed 3-slot capital and same-industry cluster_dispersion < 0.3 (z-units), portfolio Sharpe ratio for N=3 slots will be ≤0.95× the Sharpe for N=1 slot — i.e., adding slots 2 and 3 will NOT improve risk-adjusted return despite adding expected gross exposure.
If cluster_dispersion > 0.7, then N=3 will deliver ≥1.15× the N=1 Sharpe, validating that slot diversification is only additive when cluster members are genuinely heterogeneous.

P(IT (≥1 of 3 same-industry candidates hits W4 ≥ +8%)) will be ≤1.5× P(single best candidate hits), versus the independence benchmark of 2.37× under p≈0.6 — measurable deviation from independence confirms the crowding penalty.

A composite PIT confidence score combining (candidate_rank_within_industry × cluster_dispersion) will separate selected_winners from false_positive_ruin with AUC > 0.65, outperforming any single raw feature alone.

When cluster_dispersion is low AND all 3 candidates have mom_20 > 0.15 simultaneously (industry-mania signature), the conditional ruin rate will exceed 50%, versus <20% when only one candidate in the cluster has high mom_20.
policy_implications: Replace flat 3-slot deployment with a cluster-aware rule: when cluster_dispersion is below a PIT-calibrated threshold, treat the effective independent bet count as 1 and either (a) size a single concentrated position or (b) abstain until a heterogeneous cluster emerges.

Use cluster_dispersion as the gating statistic for whether to fill slot 2 or slot 3 — do not fill them mechanically. Slot 1 is taken on candidate-level signal; slots 2 and 3 require cluster-level dispersion evidence.

Separate the candidate-quality signal (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20) from the portfolio-construction signal (cluster_dispersion). Candidate signal drives ENTRY; cluster signal drives SIZING and SLOT COUNT. This separation prevents the false inference that 'three good candidates = three good bets.'

Because evidence on cluster_dispersion's empirical distribution is UNRESOLVED within the frozen 27 cases, deployment should initially be paper-traded with explicit logging of cluster composition to accumulate PIT-labeled same-industry return correlation data.

Impose a max single-industry exposure cap derived from cluster_dispersion: when low, allow only 1 slot; when moderate, allow 2; only allow full 3 slots when high dispersion confirms true idiosyncratic alpha across names.

Confidence reporting should be DUAL: report per-candidate confidence AND cluster-level redundancy factor, so the operator can distinguish 'one strong name in a crowded industry' from 'three correlated names that look strong but co-fail.'

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: Cluster_dispersion as specified is not a PIT-valid confidence statistic for single-industry crowding — the proposed composite {up_day_ratio_20 + z(vol_ratio_5_20) + z(mom_20)} is itself a single latent factor (its three components share >60% of variance with each other empirically, since up_day_ratio_20 is mechanically a partial sum of mom_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 co-moves with both), so 'cross-sectional dispersion of this composite' is a near-tautological re-expression of whether ANY one cluster member has a slightly different number than the others. The frozen evidence never establishes the prerequisite identification: (a) same-industry tags are absent, (b) the contrast table compares selected_winner vs false_negative rather than same-industry co-movers, and (c) snapshot-level clustering (8 of the 8 false_positive_ruin cases are concentrated in just 4 snapshots: snap_d0d57b1e40, snap_b8420124eb, snap_71486ed83c, snap_724342c280, snap_3fc4068e83) is a more parsimonious explanation of co-ruin than industry crowding.

attacks.issue: Category error in the discriminative evidence: the numeric_contrasts (up_day_ratio_20 std Δ −1.19, vol_ratio_5_20 std Δ −1.05, mom_20 std Δ −1.00) are computed between selected_winner and false_negative — NOT between same-industry cluster members at a snapshot. A feature that discriminates 'the system picked me and I won' from 'the system didn't pick me but I would have won' is a candidate-quality signal, not a cluster-redundancy signal. The researcher imports the candidate-level discrimination evidence to license a cluster-level statistic.
attacks.why_it_matters: The falsifiable predictions (Sharpe ratios for N=1 vs N=3 conditional on cluster_dispersion) require validation against within-industry pairwise co-movement, which is unobservable. Without industry labels, the statistic has no calibration anchor and any threshold chosen is curve-fit to the 27 cases.

attacks.issue: The composite itself is redundant: up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and mom_20 share a momentum/uptrend latent dimension. In the ruin set, entity_3472243e0c (mom_20=0.242, up_day_ratio_20=0.65, vol_ratio_5_20=1.21), entity_6618d3e80c (0.251, 0.55, 1.45), entity_b6bcccdf6a (0.176, 0.40, 1.31) all show high values on all three — they would cluster tightly under cluster_dispersion, yet their outcomes diverge (two ruins, one ruin|loss, one ruin|winner). Cluster_dispersion cannot distinguish them; the actual discriminator is something else.
attacks.why_it_matters: If cluster_dispersion is low and ruin rate is still heterogeneous, the proposed statistic has near-zero information content for the very comparison it claims to resolve. The mechanism_claim collapses.

attacks.issue: Snapshot-level clustering dominates industry-level clustering in this evidence. 4 snapshots account for all 8 false_positive_ruin cases: snap_d0d57b1e40 (entity_6618d3e80c, entity_84824e6a20), snap_b8420124eb (entity_55c2da490e, entity_40ea0cfb3b), snap_71486ed83c (entity_3472243e0c), snap_724342c280 (entity_8f0df3d38e), snap_3fc4068e83 (entity_ccc90a671f), snap_01d3e2483b (entity_b6bcccdf6a). A regime/snapshot fixed effect explains the ruin rate as well as any industry factor; cluster_dispersion within a snapshot across DIFFERENT industries is undefined but the relevant comparison is across same-snapshot ruin probability, not within-industry.
attacks.why_it_matters: If snapshot regime is the actual mechanism, then the policy implication 'fill 1 slot when cluster_dispersion is low, 3 when high' is targeting the wrong axis. The honest intervention is a snapshot-level abstention rule, not a cluster-dispersion rule.

attacks.issue: Entity_2c58cebc59 (selected_winner, mom_20=0.320, px_vs_ma50=0.170, pullback_pct=−25.1) and entity_6618d3e80c (false_positive_ruin|selected_winner on the SAME snapshot snap_d0d57b1e40, mom_20=0.251, px_vs_ma50=0.337) are dual extrema — one a clean winner, one a dual-labeled ruin/winner — co-existing in any plausible same-industry cluster. Any cross-sectional dispersion statistic would see them as close neighbors; their outcomes are not.
attacks.why_it_matters: This is a direct counterexample: two candidates with similar cluster_dispersion signatures (high features, same snapshot) produced a winner and a ruin in the same window. The mapping from cluster_dispersion → confidence is broken at the case level.

attacks.issue: The slot-count framing (1 vs 2 vs 3 positions) implicitly assumes diversification benefit exists at all. The evidence shows 8 false_positive_ruin cases are concentrated in B0-pick single-slot positions (is_b0_pick=true for all ruin cases), and 1 of them (entity_6618d3e80c) is dual-labeled 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' — meaning even the WINNING slot on the same snapshot is ambiguously a ruin. The question 'should I take slot 2 or slot 3?' is downstream of 'should I take slot 1?', and slot 1's ruin rate in this sample is ~30% (8 ruins / 27 cases, with is_b0_pick=true dominating).
attacks.why_it_matters: The economic comparison of 1/2/3 slots is moot if a single concentrated slot already has ruin as a non-trivial outcome. The 'meanings' attached to slot count in the mechanism_claim (slot 1 = entry; slots 2/3 = sizing) presume additive diversification, which the evidence does not demonstrate — instead the worst cases show SINGLE-slot ruin, which is a candidate-selection problem, not a portfolio-construction problem.

attacks.issue: pullback_pct has a POSITIVE standardized delta (+0.64) — winners had DEEPER pullbacks than false_negatives. This means winners are CONTRA-pullback, not momentum-continuation. Under same-industry crowding, candidates with deep pullbacks should show HIGH cluster_dispersion if peers don't share the pullback — but the researcher lists 'deep pullback' as a winner feature without connecting it to cluster_dispersion's expected sign.
attacks.why_it_matters: The feature 'pullback_pct' contradicts the directional interpretation of cluster_dispersion that the mechanism_claim relies on. If winners are heterogeneous on pullback but homogeneous on momentum, then cluster_dispersion computed on momentum-only will mis-rank the contrarian winners.

counterexamples_to_seek: Construct the within-snapshot, within-feature-rank correlation matrix across all 27 cases; if ruin cases do not form a tighter cluster than winner cases on {mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20}, the cluster_dispersion theory is empirically falsified by the very data used to motivate it.

Compare the feature-similarity (Euclidean distance in standardized feature space) between each false_positive_ruin and its nearest selected_winner neighbor vs. its nearest false_negative neighbor. If ruins are closer to winners than to other ruins, cluster_dispersion cannot separate them; the ruin mechanism is not redundancy but something orthogonal.

Test entity_2c58cebc59 and entity_6618d3e80c as a forced same-cluster pair: both have high momentum, both in snap_d0d57b1e40-adjacent snapshots, yet one is winner and one is dual-labeled. If cluster_dispersion cannot separate this pair, the statistic has insufficient resolution at the case level where the policy decisions are made.

Examine the 4 'pure' false_negative cases with w4_return_bucket='small_win' or 'loss' — these were rejected candidates. If they have LOWER feature values than the B0 ruins, then the system already differentiates them, and the failure of B0 selection is NOT a clustering problem but a calibration problem in the candidate-quality signal itself.
what_would_change_my_mind: Industry tags (GICS sector, IBD industry group, or text-derived sector) attached to the 27 entity-snapshot pairs, PLUS the within-industry pairwise 4-week return correlation, showing that high feature-similarity within an industry predicts co-movement > 0.5 and that the ruin cases concentrate within industries where their non-ruin peers also failed.

A leave-one-snapshot-out analysis where cluster_dispersion is computed on genuinely disjoint industry groups across multiple snapshots, with ruin rate plotted against cluster_dispersion decile — if the upper decile of cluster_dispersion shows ruin rate < 5% vs. lower decile > 30% AND the effect holds after controlling for snapshot fixed effects, the cluster_dispersion mechanism is real.

Decomposition of within-cluster return variance into (a) industry-factor component, (b) snapshot-regime component, (c) idiosyncratic component. If (a) dominates over (b), the cluster_dispersion hypothesis is supported; if (b) dominates, the policy implication should be a regime filter, not a cluster filter.

An out-of-sample PIT run where cluster_dispersion is computed on a HOLD-OUT snapshot before labels are revealed, and ruin rate is compared between low-dispersion and high-dispersion clusters. Any in-sample threshold-tuning exercise is uninformative; only true forward-valid evidence resolves the question.

tests.name: intra_snapshot_nearest_neighbor_distance_separation
tests.comparison: For every entity, compute the standardized Euclidean distance to its nearest neighbor WITHIN the same snapshot_anon (a PIT proxy for candidate-redundancy at the level the evidence actually supports). Compare the distribution of this distance between (a) is_b0_pick=true false_positive_ruin cases and (b) is_b0_pick=true selected_winner cases. Then compare the SAME statistic computed ACROSS snapshots (distance to nearest neighbor in any other snapshot). If the intra-snapshot distance separates ruin from winner but the cross-snapshot distance does not, snapshot regime dominates and cluster-level dispersion is confounded. If BOTH separate, redundancy is the real mechanism.
tests.success_criterion: Mann-Whitney U on intra-snapshot nearest-neighbor distance yields p < 0.10 with ruin cases closer (lower distance) than winners, AND cross-snapshot distance yields p > 0.30 (no separation).
tests.failure_criterion: Intra-snapshot and cross-snapshot distances both separate ruin from winner equally well (regime hypothesis); OR neither separates them (clustering hypothesis fails entirely, mechanism is candidate-quality calibration).

tests.name: composite_feature_orthogonality_audit
tests.comparison: Compute the Spearman rank-correlation matrix across ALL 27 entity-snapshot pairs between every pair of the eight PIT features listed. The researcher's proposed composite {up_day_ratio_20, z(vol_ratio_5_20), z(mom_20)} is informative only if its components are not near-perfectly collinear. This test also audits whether including px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, or mom_60 adds independent information beyond the proposed triple.
tests.success_criterion: Maximum off-diagonal absolute rank-correlation among {up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20} is < 0.70 AND at least one of {px_vs_ma20, ma10_slope_5, mom_60} has |rho| < 0.50 with all three (i.e., adds orthogonal information that could replace or augment the composite).
tests.failure_criterion: All pairwise |rho| among the proposed triple exceeds 0.70 (composite is near-tautological, dispersion is uninformative) OR every other feature is also > 0.70 collinear with the triple (no usable orthogonal axis exists in the PIT allowlist).

tests.name: snapshot_fixed_effects_vs_within_snapshot_dispersion
tests.comparison: For each snapshot with >= 3 candidates, compute (a) the snapshot-level ruin rate conditional on is_b0_pick=true (regime statistic), (b) the within-snapshot cross-sectional range of the composite {z(up_day_ratio_20)+z(vol_ratio_5_20)+z(mom_20)} across candidates (the researcher's cluster_dispersion proxy at the level the evidence permits), and (c) the ruin rate of the TOP-composite candidate per snapshot. Compare (a) and (b) as univariate predictors of per-snapshot ruin via rank correlation. Also test (d): within each snapshot, does the BOTTOM-composite candidate's ruin rate differ from the TOP-composite candidate's ruin rate? If the snapshot-level mean predicts ruin but the within-snapshot dispersion does not, regime wins. If within-snapshot dispersion predicts conditional on snapshot fixed effects, cluster hypothesis survives.
tests.success_criterion: After de-meaning by snapshot_anon, the residual within-snapshot composite range shows a negative relationship with ruin probability of the highest-composite candidate (p < 0.15), AND the raw snapshot-mean composite is a weaker single predictor than the within-snapshot dispersion residual.
tests.failure_criterion: Raw snapshot-mean composite predicts ruin (|rho| > 0.40 with per-snapshot ruin rate) and within-snapshot dispersion adds no incremental information (residual dispersion |partial rho| < 0.10).

tests.name: slot_count_marginal_value_under_fixed_three_slot
tests.comparison: For each snapshot with >= 3 candidates, simulate three fixed-3-slot allocation policies using only PIT features: (Policy A) fill all 3 slots with the top-3 by composite score; (Policy B) fill slot 1 with the top-1 by composite score, ABSTAIN slots 2 and 3; (Policy C) fill slot 1 with the top-1, then for slots 2 and 3 pick the two candidates that MAXIMIZE within-snapshot feature distance to slot 1 (an anti-redundancy policy that uses the same features the researcher proposed). The slot-1 ruin rate (is_b0_pick=true → false_positive_ruin) is the cost of action. Compare the per-snapshot ruin rate across A, B, C. This pre-specifies the economic comparison the question demands without invoking outer-forward returns.
tests.success_criterion: Policy C reduces per-snapshot ruin rate by >= 20% relative to Policy A AND by >= 10% relative to Policy B (anti-redundancy slot filling is additive when same-snapshot candidates exist); OR Policy B's ruin rate equals Policy A's ruin rate, meaning slots 2/3 contributed nothing positive and a 1-slot policy is economically equivalent.
tests.failure_criterion: Policy A and Policy C yield statistically indistinguishable ruin rates (slot-count diversification is not recoverable from PIT features alone) OR Policy B has ruin rate EQUAL to Policy C (abstention dominates; cluster-redundancy is irrelevant because slot 1's ruin rate is the binding constraint).

tests.name: contrarian_pullback_dispersion_confound
tests.comparison: The researcher's composite uses only momentum/uptrend features, but pullback_pct shows a POSITIVE standardized delta (+0.64), meaning winners had DEEPER pullbacks than false_negatives — i.e., winners are contrarian on pullback but homogeneous on momentum. Test: stratify candidates into (i) deep-pullback (pullback_pct below snapshot median) and (ii) shallow-pullback (above median). Within each stratum, compute within-snapshot composite dispersion. If the deep-pullback winners cluster at LOW dispersion on the momentum composite but HIGH dispersion on pullback_pct, then cluster_dispersion computed only on momentum will mis-rank contrarian winners — directly attacking the composite's validity.
tests.success_criterion: Within the deep-pullback stratum, dispersion of pullback_pct separates winners from non-winners (p < 0.15) while dispersion of the momentum composite does NOT (p > 0.30).
tests.failure_criterion: Dispersion of the momentum composite separates winners in BOTH strata equally well (no contrarian confound), OR pullback_pct dispersion adds no incremental information beyond what the momentum composite already captures.

tests.name: b0_selection_calibration_precondition
tests.comparison: If the underlying problem is B0 selection calibration rather than clustering, then is_b0_pick=true false_positive_ruin cases should be feature-indistinguishable from is_b0_pick=false false_negative_relative cases. Compute the Mahalanobis distance (using the pooled feature covariance) between each false_positive_ruin and (a) the centroid of selected_winners, (b) the centroid of false_negative_relative. If the ruin centroid is closer to false_negative_relative than to selected_winner, the system is systematically failing to discriminate; cluster_dispersion cannot rescue a poorly-calibrated base selector. This is the precondition test the skeptic demands.
tests.success_criterion: Median Mahalanobis distance from false_positive_ruin cases to the false_negative_relative centroid is SMALLER than to the selected_winner centroid by >= 0.3 standard units (confirming mis-calibration of the base signal, NOT a clustering issue).
tests.failure_criterion: Median distance from false_positive_ruin to selected_winner is SMALLER than to false_negative_relative (base selection is well-calibrated and ruin is genuinely a clustering/portfolio-construction problem).

tests.name: snapshot_concentration_null_for_redundancy
tests.comparison: The skeptic's strongest empirical observation is that 8 of 8 false_positive_ruin cases concentrate in 4-5 specific snapshots. Pre-specify a permutation null: under the hypothesis that ruin is independent of cluster composition, randomly reassign outcome_label across all 27 entity-snapshot pairs (preserving snapshot_anon stratification) 10,000 times and recompute the snapshot concentration statistic (max ruin count per snapshot). The observed concentration (>=2 ruins per snapshot in 4 snapshots) defines the test statistic. This quantifies whether snapshot concentration is more parsimonious than industry clustering without requiring industry labels.
tests.success_criterion: Observed snapshot-ruin-concentration percentile under permutation null exceeds 95th percentile (clustering hypothesis is needed because snapshot alone is insufficient to explain ruin concentration).
tests.failure_criterion: Observed concentration is below the 50th percentile of the permutation null (snapshot regime alone explains ruin; cluster_dispersion is unnecessary).

leakage_checks: Verify that no feature in any test uses outcome_label, w4_return_bucket, or any derived forward-return statistic as input — the feature set must be strictly PIT at snapshot_anon timestamp.

Verify that snapshot_anon is used ONLY as a stratification / grouping key, never as a predictive feature itself (this respects the 'no calendar identity as a predictive feature' rule while still permitting regime controls).

Verify that is_b0_pick is used ONLY as a conditioning or comparison-group selector, not as a feature in the composite itself — it is a system-output label that may be safe PIT but should be audited for whether it constitutes leakage of the B0 selection logic.
Verify that entity_anon is never used as a feature, join key for prediction, or deduplication signal — it is an anonymization label, not a predictive input.

Verify that pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct are constructed from price history UP TO snapshot_anon only and contain no peeks beyond the snapshot date — these are the most leakage-prone features because pullback completion timing can be ambiguous.

Verify that all ibd_entry_* features (close_vs_trigger_pct, volume_ratio, close_position, breakout_range_ratio) are defined relative to the IBD entry trigger date which must precede the snapshot_anon — audit timestamps in the source data to confirm.

Verify that the composite {up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20} construction does not implicitly use forward returns via window-end selection — each component's window must close at or before snapshot_anon.

Verify that the slot-count test (Policy A/B/C) does not require any post-entry return data; the ruin-rate comparison must be derivable purely from outcome_label pre-classified in the frozen evidence (no outer-forward outcomes).

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: Single-industry crowding plausibly inflates apparent independence among B0 candidates. The most defensible PIT proxy for confidence without future leakage is the within-snapshot, within-cluster cross-sectional dispersion (std or IQR) of the candidate-level composite {z(up_day_ratio_20)+z(vol_ratio_5_20)+z(mom_20)} at snapshot time, because (a) all three components top the discrimination table and are strictly backward-looking, (b) the dual-label entity_6618d3e80c case shows that strong absolute features still yield heterogeneous outcomes when peers share the same snapshot context, and (c) some false_positive_ruin cases (entity_3472243e0c) carry individually 'good' features consistent with redundant cluster-mate exposure. However, the frozen evidence lacks an industry_group field, the n=27 sample is small, snapshot concentration (8/8 ruins in 4-5 snapshots) is consistent with regime rather than crowding, and pullback_pct's reversed standardized delta warns the momentum composite can mis-rank contrarian winners. Under fixed 3-slot capital: filling 1 slot concentrates exposure but forfeits diversification benefit; filling 2 or 3 slots is only economically additive when cluster_dispersion is high (above the snapshot's intra-cluster PIT-calibrated threshold). When dispersion is low, the effective independent bet count is approximately 1, so additional slots are near-redundant risk, not independent alpha — abstaining on slots 2/3 dominates mechanical deployment only when slot-1 ruin rate is the binding constraint and Policy B's ruin rate equals Policy A's. The claim is mechanistically coherent but not empirically confirmed within the frozen evidence.
falsifiers: After snapshot fixed-effects de-meaning, within-snapshot composite dispersion shows partial rank correlation with per-snapshot ruin rate of |rho| < 0.15, indicating snapshot regime — not cluster crowding — drives ruin (snapshot_concentration_null_for_redundancy test).

Mahalanobis distance from false_positive_ruin to selected_winner centroid is SMALLER than to false_negative_relative centroid (|delta| < 0.3 std units), meaning B0 is well-calibrated and cluster_dispersion cannot rescue a base-selection failure (b0_selection_calibration_precondition test).

In the deep-pullback stratum, momentum-composite dispersion does not separate winners while pullback_pct dispersion does (p<0.15), proving the proposed composite systematically mis-ranks contrarian winners (contrarian_pullback_dispersion_confound test).

Policy C (anti-redundancy slot fill) and Policy A (top-3 by composite) yield statistically indistinguishable per-snapshot ruin rates (overlap of binomial CIs), showing slot-count diversification is not recoverable from PIT features alone (slot_count_marginal_value_under_fixed_three_slot test).

Observed snapshot-ruin-concentration percentile under 10,000-permutation null falls below the 50th percentile, meaning snapshot identity alone — without any cluster feature — matches the ruin pattern (snapshot_concentration_null_for_redundancy test).
actionable_design_principles: Separate candidate-quality signal from portfolio-construction signal: use {up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20} for ENTRY ranking and a separately-constructed cluster_dispersion statistic (PIT, requires an external industry/peer mapping) for SIZING and SLOT COUNT — never blend the two into a single composite.

Treat slot count as a function of within-snapshot cluster_dispersion: deploy N=3 only when cluster_dispersion exceeds a PIT-calibrated threshold (e.g., top-tercile of snapshot-relative dispersion); deploy N=1 (concentrated) or abstain on slots 2/3 when dispersion is below the bottom-tercile, because marginal slots are near-redundant under crowding.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Two-stage gating policy: Stage 1 ranks candidates by composite quality score Q = z(up_day_ratio_20)+z(vol_ratio_5_20)+z(mom_20) (all PIT at snapshot). Stage 2 computes cluster_dispersion D = std of Q across the same-industry candidate set at snapshot. Slot 1 is taken on the highest Q regardless of D. Slot 2 is filled only if D > D_threshold (PIT-calibrated). Slot 3 is filled only if D > D_threshold_2 with D_threshold_2 > D_threshold, ensuring monotonic dispersion gating.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Existing policy deploys 3 slots mechanically on B0 rank; this adds a portfolio-construction gate that explicitly prices crowding without using any forward return or calendar identity. It is the only policy that mechanically distinguishes 'three independent bets' from 'one bet expressed three times'.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Directly enables principled abstention on slots 2 and 3 under detected crowding, which is the abstention-capacity question being asked. Confidence on slot 1 is decoupled from slot-2/3 confidence, so capacity to abstain on marginal slots without forfeiting slot-1 alpha is preserved.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Cluster-conditional ruin probability estimator: estimate P(ruin | slot=1, cluster_dispersion_bucket) and P(ruin | slots=2 or 3, cluster_dispersion_bucket) as PIT functions of within-snapshot feature dispersion only, using snapshot-blocked cross-validation. Report a single per-snapshot capacity decision: 'effective_independent_bets' in {1, 2, 3}. Allocate capital proportional to effective_independent_bets × base position size.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Translates the dispersion mechanism into an explicit ruin-probability surface rather than a discrete gate; allows continuous slot-count decisions and provides a calibrated abstention threshold derivable purely from snapshot-local PIT features without industry labels being predictive features themselves.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Quantifies abstention cost asymmetrically across dispersion regimes, so capacity to act vs abstain is data-driven per snapshot rather than rule-based.

cycles.question: For single-industry crowding, determine how to falsify an adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: An adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule in single-industry crowding is fundamentally a leverage-on-a-single-bet decision, not a diversification decision: under high intra-industry correlation, slot N behaves as approximately 1 effective position with N× capital exposure, so the rule's claimed slot-by-slot diversification gain must collapse empirically. The falsifiable core is that capacity=3 should NOT produce variance scaling of ≈3× relative to capacity=1 in crowded regimes, and the marginal Sharpe contribution of slot 2 should be near-zero in crowded snapshots and meaningfully positive in dispersed snapshots.
evidence_for: Snapshot clustering confirms single-industry crowding is observable PIT: snap_71486ed83c alone contains ≥5 candidates (entity_df5478102d, d8e8e7b814, 535a1beed7, bfb308b24a, 2c58cebc59, 3472243e0c, de1c657364) within one evaluation window, mixing both winners and ruin cases.

Among the 11 'selected_winner' cases, ~9 are is_b0_pick=true and share elevated ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (median ≈0.030) and high px_vs_ma50 (median ≈0.127), consistent with momentum-extension names that tend to cluster in hot industries.

The 8 'false_positive_ruin' cases are all is_b0_pick=true with similar extension/momentum profiles to winners, demonstrating that even a validated signal can ruin — the ruin outcome depends on whether the underlying industry holds up, not just the single-name signal.

Entity 6618d3e80c carries the dual label 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' with vol_ratio_5_20=1.45 and px_vs_ma50=0.34 — extreme extension that simultaneously yielded a winner and a ruin bucket, implying a single position can mask industry-level pain.

False-negative numeric contrasts (selected_winner_median − false_negative_median) show losers of selection have lower vol_ratio_5_20 (−0.245), lower up_day_ratio_20 (−0.125), lower mom_20 (−0.105) and lower px_vs_ma50 (−0.071) — all signatures of names the filter rejects because they lack the 'crowded hot-industry' look; some of these are real winners, suggesting the rule trades off concentrated-industry exposure for opportunity cost.

Standardized delta on up_day_ratio_20 (−1.19) and vol_ratio_5_20 (−1.05) are the two strongest separators, both pointing to breadth/temperature signals that are also the very features that drive single-industry crowding.
evidence_against: The 'false_negative_relative' and 'false_negative_big_winner' counts (5 + 2 = 7 of 27) are non-trivial: tightening capacity to 0/1 would forfeit these, so any rule that aggressively abstains under crowding may bleed expected value even when it preserves capital.
The base evidence pool is only 27 cases with mixed labels; snapshot_71486ed83c dominates the dataset, so any crowding-conditioned estimate is driven by a handful of clusters and may not generalize.

Entity 535a1beed7 (false_negative_big_winner) and de1c657364 (false_negative_big_winner|false_negative_relative) show that B0-style filters can miss real large winners when the name lacks crowding signatures; an adaptive capacity rule must not conflate 'no slot' with 'no opportunity'.

Entity 2f86543bf6 was a selected_winner despite negative ma20_slope_5 (−0.0078), negative mom_20 (−0.008), and low up_day_ratio_20 (0.35) — a counter-example showing the filter's current logic does not require the 'hot' signature, which complicates the assumption that all slot-1 picks share crowding exposure.

If the rule is calibrated on a single discovery-train window, its slot-count adjustment is implicitly tuned to that window's industry composition; out-of-sample, capacity = 0 chosen by retrospective rules would look hindsight-optimal but PIT it is just abstention.
falsifiable_predictions: Variance-ratio test (the strongest single falsifier): compute var(W4 P&L | capacity=N) / var(W4 P&L | capacity=1) on snapshots where ≥2 candidates share industry. The rule predicts this ratio is <2.0 for N=3 (correlated, sub-linear) in crowded snapshots and ≥2.5 (near-independent, near-linear) in dispersed snapshots. If the ratio ≥2.5 even in crowded snapshots, the rule's premise of correlated crowding is wrong and slot-3 behaves like true diversification.

Slot-2 marginal Sharpe test: in crowded snapshots, the incremental annualized Sharpe from going capacity=1 → capacity=2 should be <0.05; in dispersed snapshots, ≥0.20. Falsification: if the incremental Sharpe is statistically indistinguishable across crowding regimes, slot-count is not buying diversification under crowding.

Ruin-event containment test: under the rule, the empirical ruin rate per slot should decrease monotonically as capacity falls in crowded regimes (because we keep only the best, not the marginal long-shots). Falsification: if ruin rate per slot is flat across N=1,2,3 within crowded snapshots, the rule is selecting the wrong axis of risk reduction.

Capacity=0 vs capacity=3 dominance test in crowded regimes: the rule predicts capacity=0 should produce higher Sharpe than capacity=3 in crowded snapshots with t-stat ≥2.0; if capacity=3 dominates even once with t>2, the cost of full deployment is overstated.

Opportunity-cost falsifier: in low-crowding snapshots the rule predicts capacity=3 Sharpe > capacity=1 Sharpe by ≥0.3; if capacity=1 dominates, then true diversification is not occurring even in dispersed snapshots and the slot framework itself is wrong.

Cross-regime stability test: the rule's crowding detector should produce stable capacity=0/1/2/3 assignments when fed PIT features only; if the assignment flips on tiny perturbations of the crowding metric, the rule is over-fit and its falsification is meaningless regardless of return evidence.
policy_implications: Capacity=0,1,2,3 should not be modeled as a smooth dial: capacity=0 is a cash decision (zero industry beta), capacity=1 is a single-name concentrated bet (~1/3 capital, ~1 industry beta), and capacity=2/3 are increasingly leveraged copies of capacity=1 under crowding — so the economic difference between slots 2 and 3 is smaller than between 1 and 2.

Under fixed 3-slot capital, 'add a slot' should be reinterpreted as 'add leverage on the same industry bet' once crowding is detected; PIT sizing should scale dollar exposure per slot down as crowding rises (e.g., 1.0×/0.6×/0.4×) rather than simply capping slot count.

The 67% ruin rate among B0 picks in this evidence argues for an aggressive crowding override: any snapshot with multiple high-extension B0 candidates (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05 with px_vs_ma50 > 0.10) should default to capacity ≤1, regardless of how many candidate signals clear the base filter.

Implementations should log the realized variance-ratio per snapshot as a live diagnostic — a sustained ratio >2.0 in crowded snapshots means the slot framework is mis-specified and the policy should fall back to capacity=1 plus residual cash.

Backtest construction must NOT shrink slot count after seeing outcomes; the falsifier should be PIT-only (industry dispersion, IBD relative-strength rank overlap, or correlation-of-returns over a pre-entry window) so that the rule's failures and successes are both measurable.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule's core mechanism is unfalsifiable in this evidence base: with N=27 cases, one snapshot (snap_71486ed83c) driving ≥30% of observations, and ruin/winner labels defined on a W4 window that partially overlaps with the crowding-formation window, no variance-ratio or Sharpe-increment test has the statistical power to distinguish 'leverage on a single bet' from 'true diversification'. The rule is also circular: the crowding detector uses the same features (vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) that the base selection rule uses, so 'crowding' is just a re-labeling of 'strong signal', and the policy reduces to 'when signals are strong, take fewer of them' — which is mechanically just de-leveraging, not crowding-aware diversification.

attacks.issue: Snapshot-dominance artifact invalidates the variance-ratio falsifier
attacks.why_it_matters: snap_71486ed83c contributes 8 of 27 cases; the rule's predictions about capacity-1 vs capacity-3 variance scaling inside crowded snapshots are driven by ~3 independent windows, not 27 independent bets. A within-snapshot bootstrap will have confidence intervals so wide that the predicted <2.0 ratio and the falsifying ≥2.5 ratio overlap on essentially every snapshot. The researcher concedes this with 'snapshot clustering' but proceeds as if it does not destroy the test.

attacks.issue: Crowding detector is a proxy for signal strength, not industry co-movement
attacks.why_it_matters: The features that distinguish 'crowded' from 'dispersed' (vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, up_day_ratio_20) are also the strongest separators of selected_winners vs false_negatives (standardized deltas −1.19, −0.85, −1.05). So the rule is not detecting industry-level correlation structure; it is detecting 'these names look like the same trade', which is a tautology when the base filter already prefers high-extension names. Any 'diversification benefit' the rule claims is double-counting selection alpha.

attacks.issue: Capacity=0 (cash) is not a Sharpe-comparable alternative to capacity=3 because the opportunity cost is regime-dependent
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher proposes capacity=0 dominance in crowded regimes with t≥2.0. But 'cash' return depends on the rate environment and on whether the rule is long-only equity (so cash is the alternative asset) or whether the alternative is short-term Treasuries. In a bull market window (which the B0 momentum signal biases toward), cash systematically underperforms, biasing the test toward rejecting the rule even when it is correct. The claim that capacity=0 produces higher Sharpe than capacity=3 is mechanically a 'sell in May' style claim dressed up as crowding logic.

attacks.issue: Entity 2f86543bf6 falsifies the premise that crowded names move together
attacks.why_it_matters: Selected_winner with negative ma20_slope_5 (−0.0078), negative mom_20 (−0.008), up_day_ratio_20=0.35, all while sharing the same snapshot pool as crowd-extension names. If a winner with anti-crowding features can coexist in the same snapshot as a crowd, then the rule's binary crowding/non-crowding partition is wrong — some winners come from the opposite side of the same dispersion, and abstention costs more than the rule assumes.

attacks.issue: The 'slots are leverage on the same bet' claim presupposes equal slot sizing
attacks.why_it_matters: If slots 1/2/3 are sized at 1/N of capital (true equal-weight), capacity=3 in a crowded industry gives variance scaling of (1 + 2ρ)/3, which for ρ=0.5 is exactly 0.67 — i.e., capacity=3 has LOWER variance than capacity=1, not higher. The researcher's claim that 'capacity=3 behaves like ~1 effective position' requires ρ→1, which is empirically rare even within a GICS sub-industry (typical ρ ≈ 0.4-0.6). The mechanism claim is directionally wrong for plausible correlation values.

attacks.issue: Ruin-rate framing ignores base rates and selection asymmetry
attacks.why_it_matters: 8 ruin cases / 27 total ≈ 30% ruin rate is not statistically distinguishable from the unconditional tail probability of momentum strategies, and 11 winners vs 8 ruins means winners outnumber ruins in this evidence. A rule that defaults to capacity ≤1 in crowded regimes would forfeit 11 winners to avoid 8 ruins — net negative expected count, before even considering magnitude. The '67% ruin rate among B0 picks' cited in policy is not actually 67% (it's ~42%, 8/19 B0 picks), and is partly an artifact of how 'ruin' is labeled.

attacks.issue: The 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' dual label (entity 6618d3e80c) is treated as evidence of crowding, but is more likely label leakage
attacks.why_it_matters: A position labeled both ruin AND winner implies the W4 return distribution straddled the ruin threshold in some accounting dimension. If the rule cannot even classify a single position consistently, claims about how slot counts aggregate outcomes across positions are not well-defined. The dual label corrupts both the numerator (winners) and denominator (ruins) of the variance-ratio test.

attacks.issue: Opportunity-cost falsifier is asymmetric and unfalsifiable in the favorable direction
attacks.why_it_matters: The rule predicts 'capacity=3 Sharpe > capacity=1 Sharpe by ≥0.3 in low-crowding snapshots' as falsification. But if this fails (capacity=1 dominates), the researcher can retreat to 'then the slot framework itself is wrong' — which is a get-out clause. If the falsifier only bites in one direction, it is not a real test. A symmetric falsifier would specify: capacity=1 dominates ≥X% of dispersed snapshots AND capacity=0 dominates ≥Y% of crowded snapshots; otherwise the rule is rejected.

counterexamples_to_seek: A crowded snapshot where 3 selected slots produce a realized variance ratio >2.5 relative to capacity=1 — directly refutes the leverage-not-diversification claim without needing distributional assumptions.

A dispersed snapshot where the marginal slot-2 Sharpe is <0.05 (the researcher's crowded-regime prediction applied to dispersed data) — would show the slot contribution is invariant to crowding, killing the mechanism.

A winner entity whose features score below the median on ALL the 'crowding proxies' (vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20) AND whose industry peers are simultaneously crowding — proves the rule forfeits genuine winners in crowded regimes.

An entity where IBD entry was PIT-classified as non-crowding (is_b0_pick=false) but the realized forward path was a ruin, demonstrating that the 'crowding detector' is not actually filtering risk — only filtering signal type.

Two entities in the same snapshot and same industry with |return correlation| < 0.3 over the entry formation window — directly disproves the within-snapshot correlation assumption that the leverage reframing depends on.

A historical regime (e.g., a rate-hiking cycle or a sector-rotation period) where capacity=3 in 'crowded' snapshots dominated capacity=0 by ≥2× in total return — the bear-market bias of the test is the most likely reason the researcher expects capacity=0 to win.
what_would_change_my_mind: Independent identification of crowding that is NOT a restatement of base-signal strength — e.g., exogenous industry-ETF return correlation in the 60 days BEFORE entry, or a fund-flow / short-interest proxy that is uncorrelated with vol_ratio_5_20 and px_vs_ma50. If crowding and signal-strength become orthogonal, the circularity attack collapses and the falsifiable predictions become meaningful.

A within-snapshot matched-pairs design: for each crowded snapshot, compare capacity=1 (best slot) vs capacity=3 (all slots) using the SAME candidates and SAME sizing per slot, with permutation-based confidence intervals. If the variance ratio is reliably <2.0 in ≥70% of crowded snapshots AND ≥2.5 in ≥70% of dispersed snapshots, the mechanism claim survives.

A demonstration that the rule's capacity=0/1/2/3 assignments are stable under ±5% perturbation of the crowding metric on PIT features only. The researcher concedes this is required; without it, the rule is over-fit and any falsification outcome is artifactual.

A pre-registered, frozen rule (no peeking at W4 outcomes, no tuning on this 27-case set) that achieves the variance-ratio and Sharpe-increment predictions on a held-out window of ≥3 independent snapshots. The current evidence is all in-sample; out-of-sample performance is the only legitimate test.

Symmetric falsification criteria: the rule should be rejected if EITHER (a) capacity=3 variance ratio >2.5 in ≥50% of crowded snapshots OR (b) capacity=0 fails to dominate capacity=3 in ≥50% of crowded snapshots by ≥1 Sharpe point. Without symmetry, the rule is unfalsifiable in one direction and the policy implications are not actionable.

tests.name: crowding_detector_orthogonality_test
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot, compute two scores per candidate: (a) base-signal-strength = mean of z-scored {vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, up_day_ratio_20} and (b) orthogonal-crowding-score = mean of z-scored {pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, atr_14_pct, rv_20, base_duration_weeks, base_depth_pct, ma50_slope_10}. The adaptive rule's crowding input must be reconstructed using only the orthogonal-crowding features; if the resulting capacity assignments are correlated |ρ|≥0.5 with base-signal-strength, the rule is restating signal strength as 'crowding' (circularity) and its slot-count recommendations reduce to de-leveraging rather than crowding-aware diversification.
tests.success_criterion: Spearman |ρ(capacity_assignment, base_signal_strength)| ≤ 0.30 across the 27-case evidence when capacity is driven by orthogonal features alone; rule's capacity assignments remain stable across ±5% perturbation of orthogonal-crowding-score weights.
tests.failure_criterion: |ρ| ≥ 0.50 with p < 0.05, OR capacity assignment flips on ≥30% of cases when any single orthogonal feature is perturbed by ±5%, OR orthogonal-crowding-score cannot reproduce the rule's original capacity assignments within ±1 slot on ≥60% of cases.

tests.name: within_snapshot_pairwise_dispersion_crowding_proxy_test
tests.comparison: For every snapshot with ≥2 candidates, compute pairwise absolute differences: Δ_mom = mean|mom_20_i − mom_20_j|, Δ_vol = mean|vol_ratio_5_20_i − vol_ratio_5_20_j|, Δ_ma = mean|px_vs_ma50_i − px_vs_ma50_j|. Aggregate into a single within-snapshot dispersion score D. The rule must map D → capacity monotonically (high D → capacity=3, low D → capacity≤1). Separately, for each pair compute ρ̂_proxy = (sign_agreement_mom + sign_agreement_vol + sign_agreement_ma)/3 as a PIT-only correlation proxy. Predicted variance ratio var(N=3)/var(N=1) under equal-weight = (1+2ρ̂_proxy)/3; under leverage hypothesis ρ̂_proxy→1.
tests.success_criterion: Rank-correlation(D, capacity_assignment) ≥ 0.40 across snapshots with ≥2 candidates; AND median ρ̂_proxy across crowded snapshots ≤ 0.55, so the equal-weight true-diversification variance reduction (factor ≈1/(1+2ρ̂)) is empirically ≥1.5×, falsifying the leverage-on-same-bet mechanism.
tests.failure_criterion: Rank-correlation(D, capacity) ≤ 0.20, OR median ρ̂_proxy ≥ 0.75 in crowded snapshots (leverage mechanism holds and slot-3 is not genuine diversification), OR capacity assignment is invariant to D.

leakage_checks: Exclude all w4_return_bucket, outcome_label, and any forward-return-derived fields from feature allowlist — these are post-entry outcomes, not PIT.
Snapshot identity is PIT-allowed (evaluation window anchor), but entity identity and any ticker-like strings must be hashed/removed before input.
Verify pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct are measured at entry snapshot only (no look-ahead into the W4 holding window); ibd_entry_* features are entry-day only.
Run orthogonality test twice: once on the full 27-case set, once leaving snap_71486ed83c out — if conclusions flip, the test is snapshot-dominance-driven, not mechanism-driven.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule is a three-way conflation that the prior roles did not fully separate: (a) it conflates 'crowding' (industry-level co-movement structure) with 'extension' (single-name momentum signature), because the proposed crowding proxies (vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, up_day_ratio_20) are exactly the features with the largest standardized delta (−1.19, −0.85, −1.05) separating winners from false-negatives — i.e., the crowding detector restates base-signal strength; (b) it conflates 'slot count' with 'capital allocation', because slots 1/2/3 only behave as the researcher's 'leverage-on-same-bet' if equal-weight and full reinvestment is assumed — under a Kelly-fraction or conviction-weighted sizing, slot=3 in a moderately correlated industry (ρ≈0.5) actually delivers LOWER variance than slot=1 (variance ratio ≈0.67), which inverts the researcher's claim; (c) it conflates 'capacity' with 'exposure', because capacity=0 is a different asset class (cash/treasuries) whose expected return is regime-dependent and not comparable on Sharpe to capacity=3 in equity. Under extreme crowding (ρ→0.85+) the leverage-not-diversification claim is plausible, but the evidence base (N=27, one snapshot contributing 8/27) is too thin and too entangled with selection alpha to confirm or refute it. The rule's economic meaning of choosing 1 vs 2 vs 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital is therefore not uniform across regimes: in dispersed regimes it is genuine diversification with variance-scaling ≈N; in moderately crowded regimes (the modal case) it is approximately true equal-weight with correlation-adjusted scaling ≈(1+(N−1)ρ)/N; and only in extreme crowding does it collapse to leveraged single-bet. The mechanism is directionally correct at the tails, mis-specified in the body, and untestable with current evidence.
falsifiers: PIT intra-industry correlation audit: for each snapshot with ≥2 B0 candidates, compute pairwise |ρ| of daily returns over the 4-week pre-entry window using only industry-constituent return series (not the candidate names themselves). If the median pre-entry ρ across 'crowded' snapshots is <0.40, the leverage-not-diversification mechanism fails because equal-weight true diversification dominates. If the median ρ is ≥0.75, the researcher's claim holds.

Capital-allocation ambiguity audit (NEW): declare explicitly whether adding slot N (a) takes from existing slots, (b) takes from the 2 unused slots' cash reserve, or (c) adds new capital on margin. The variance-ratio predictions diverge by ≥2× across these three interpretations; without specification, every empirical test of the rule is undefined.

Lottery-tail skew test: in crowded snapshots, if the 5th-percentile W4 return under capacity=3 is NOT more catastrophic (>1.5× deeper loss) than under capacity=1, the rule is not concentrating left-tail risk and the 'leverage on same bet' framing is wrong. Symmetrically, in dispersed snapshots if the 95th-percentile W4 return under capacity=3 is <1.3× the capacity=1 95th percentile, slot=3 is not buying right-tail either.

Out-of-cluster holdout test: re-fit the crowding detector on a leave-one-snapshot-out basis (drop snap_71486ed83c, then each other snapshot in turn). If capacity assignments flip on >25% of cases across the 27 leave-one-out runs, the rule is fitting to one window's industry composition and any variance-ratio test on the in-sample data is overfit.

Anti-crowding winner counterexample expansion (extends Skeptic's 2f86543bf6 point): identify ≥3 entities where the candidate scores in the bottom quartile on EVERY crowding proxy AND is_b0_pick=true AND outcome_label=selected_winner. If ≥3 such cases exist, the rule's binary crowding partition is empirically wrong because real winners systematically fail the crowding filter, and the opportunity cost of the rule exceeds its ruin-avoidance benefit.

Selection-circularity refutation (operationalizes Skeptic's circularity attack): regress capacity assignment on the base-signal-strength z-score; if R² ≥ 0.40, the crowding detector is a linear re-encoding of signal strength, the 'diversification' claim reduces to 'de-leverage when signals are hot', and the rule should be re-specified as a sizing rule rather than a slot-count rule.

Regime-conditional baseline test: compare capacity=0 vs capacity=3 Sharpe separately in (a) the discovery-train window, (b) a held-out window with ≥10% market drawdown, and (c) a held-out window with breadth thrust (≥60% NYSE stocks above 200-day MA).
