If capacity=3 dominance appears only in breadth-thrust regimes (the natural habitat of momentum signals), the rule's falsification in regime (b) shows the 'cash is better' conclusion is a regime-bias artifact and capacity=0 is not a robust alternative.
actionable_design_principles: Separate three orthogonal layers explicitly in any implementation: (1) selection — which names pass the base filter, (2) crowding — independent measure of industry co-movement PIT, (3) capacity/sizing — dollar exposure per slot and total capital deployed. Conflating layers makes the rule untestable.

Define 'slot' as a dollar fraction of allocated capital with a documented reinvestment policy (e.g., slot N takes 1/(N+N_unused) of remaining cash reserve, NOT a proportional cut of existing slots). Without this specification, capacity=2 and capacity=3 have no defined economic meaning.

Use orthogonal crowding features only — features NOT in the base-signal-strength set. Concrete candidates: IBD relative-strength rank percentile overlap across candidates, GICS sub-industry constituents' average 20-day correlation, sector ETF return dispersion, breadth-of-advance within sub-industry. These are industry-structure features, not single-name extension features.

Prefer continuous sizing (e.g., dollar exposure = f(orthogonal_crowding_score)) over discrete capacity=1/2/3 buckets. The discrete bucket boundary at slot=2 implies a discontinuous risk jump that has no economic justification in the evidence and makes the rule brittle to perturbation.

Always log the realized pairwise correlation between co-slot candidates at entry (using pre-entry daily returns). This is a PIT-only audit that lets you distinguish leverage-mode from diversification-mode slot behavior in real time without waiting for W4 outcomes.

Distinguish capacity=0 (cash/treasuries) from capacity=1 explicitly in any Sharpe comparison. Capacity=0 has different return distribution, different variance, and different regime dependence; comparing it to capacity=3 on raw Sharpe conflates asset-class choice with industry choice.

Reject any backtest that uses post-entry W4 outcomes in the capacity assignment decision — this is the most common source of hindsight-bias in capacity-rule research and is explicitly forbidden by the PIT constraint.

Maintain a minimum sample threshold (e.g., ≥30 independent snapshots) before drawing mechanism conclusions. The current 27-case evidence with 8 from one snapshot does not meet this bar; treat all current findings as hypothesis-generating only.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: orthogonal_crowding_gate
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Replaces the proposed crowding detector (which reuses vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, up_day_ratio_20 — the same features that select winners) with industry-structure features only: sub_industry_pairwise_corr_20d (pre-entry), sub_industry_breadth_pct (fraction of constituents above 20-day MA), sector_etf_dispersion_5d, ibd_rs_rank_overlap_count (how many of the B0 candidates fall in top-decile industry RS). This breaks the circularity that the Skeptic identified.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Outputs a continuous crowding score 0–1; maps to capacity as 0→0 slots, <0.33→1 slot, 0.33–0.66→2 slots, >0.66→3 slots, but with explicit dollar allocation defined separately (see sizing_per_slot policy).

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: sizing_per_slot
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Decouples slot count from dollar allocation. Defines per-slot capital fraction as 1/(active_slots + reserved_cash_slots) with explicit reserved_cash_slots ≥ 1 always. This makes capacity=2/3 economically meaningful (they take from cash reserve, not from slot-1), and prevents the equal-weight → leveraged-bet collapse that the Skeptic's ρ<1 argument exposes.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity=1 with reserved_cash=2 means 33% deployed, 67% cash. Capacity=3 with reserved_cash=0 means 100% deployed across 3 names. Capacity=0 means 100% cash. The economic distinction between slots is now continuous and auditable.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: pit_correlation_audit
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Requires logging the realized pre-entry pairwise correlation of returns between co-slot candidates. This converts the assumed ρ (from crowding proxies) into an observed ρ at entry time, enabling live verification of whether the rule is operating in leverage-mode (ρ>0.7) or diversification-mode (ρ<0.4) — the central unresolved empirical question.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: If observed_ρ > 0.7, the rule overrides to reduce capacity by 1 (or shrink per-slot sizing by 50%) regardless of what the orthogonal_crowding_gate said. This is the operational mechanism for the variance-ratio falsifier — instead of waiting for W4 outcomes, the rule self-corrects at entry based on measured correlation.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: lottery_tail_monitor
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Tracks the realized left-tail (5th percentile) and right-tail (95th percentile) of slot combinations vs single-slot outcomes, separately in crowded and dispersed regimes. This explicitly tests the 'slot=3 is leverage on left-tail' vs 'slot=3 buys right-tail' alternative, which is the empirical question the researcher's variance-ratio test cannot cleanly answer.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: If left-tail worsens >1.5× when going from capacity=1 to capacity=3 in crowded regimes, capacity is mis-specified for that regime and the rule should default to capacity=1 with residual cash. If right-tail improves <1.3× in dispersed regimes, slot=3 is not buying meaningful upside either and the framework should be re-examined.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: anti_crowding_winner_lot
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Carves out a minimum capacity=1 override slot for any candidate that scores in the bottom quartile on the orthogonal crowding features but in the top quartile on base-signal strength (e.g., mom_20 in top quartile, sub_industry_breadth_pct in bottom quartile). This directly addresses the Skeptic's entity 2f86543bf6 counterexample — winners that come from anti-crowding trades.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Forces the rule to keep at least one slot open in every snapshot regardless of crowding reading, but limits it to one. Prevents full capacity=0 abstention when genuine anti-crowding opportunities exist, which the evidence (2 winners with negative momentum slopes) suggests is non-trivial.

cycles.question: For low setup density, determine when cash should dominate filling another slot. Compare the economic meaning of selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital.

researcher.mechanism_claim: In low setup-density regimes, the candidate pool is shifted toward marginal profiles whose PIT-observable features (up_day_ratio_20 ≈ 0.40–0.65, vol_ratio_5_20 ≈ 1.0–1.6, mom_20 ≈ 0.02–0.25, px_vs_ma50 ≈ 0.05–0.15) overlap materially with the false_positive_ruin region of historical outcomes; cash dominates the unfilled slot because (a) the marginal candidate's expected return net of asymmetric ruin risk is negative, and (b) holding cash preserves option value for the next higher-quality setup without paying a ruin tax. Selecting 1, 2, or 3 positions under fixed 3-slot capital therefore has non-linear economic meaning: slot 1 captures the highest-quality setup (positive EV), slot 2 captures the second-best (often breakeven to slightly positive), and slot 3 captures the marginal candidate (expected negative EV, dominated by ruin tail).
evidence_for: 8 of 27 archaeological cases are labeled false_positive_ruin despite passing the b0 entry filter; their PIT features sit in a band that partially overlaps selected_winners (e.g., entity_8f0df3d38e: mom_20=0.176, vol_ratio_5_20=1.24, up_day_ratio=0.65, yet w4_return=ruin; entity_3472243e0c: mom_20=0.242, vol_ratio=1.21, up_day_ratio=0.65, w4=ruin).

Numeric contrast: false_negatives vs selected_winners show standardized deltas of -1.19 (up_day_ratio), -1.05 (vol_ratio_5_20), -1.00 (mom_20), -0.85 (px_vs_ma50), confirming that the very features that distinguish true winners from non-winners are concentrated in the high-density tail.

The median up_day_ratio for selected_winners (0.625) sits above the false_negative median (0.50); the false_positive_ruin cases cluster between these values, indicating they enter the portfolio from the ambiguous middle of the distribution.

Pullback_pct median delta (+8.6, standardized 0.64) shows winners had deeper, longer-duration pullbacks (median 5.5 weeks vs 4.0), meaning many marginal candidates fail the deeper-base confirmation that requires time to develop — so in low-density snapshots the pullback-confirmed cohort is small.

Ruin outcome bucket outcomes (w4_return=ruin) imply asymmetric losses: one ruin can erase the gains of multiple winners in a 3-position portfolio, making the variance contribution of the lowest-quality slot disproportionately negative.

Only 1 case carries the dual label 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' (entity_6618d3e80c), showing that even setups with strong features (mom_20=0.251, px_vs_ma50=0.337) can bifurcate — indicating the feature filter is necessary but not sufficient.
evidence_against: Several false_negative_relative cases (e.g., entity_de1c657364: pullback_pct=-7.3, mom_20=0.058, up_day_ratio=0.65) became large winners despite mid-tier features, implying that abstaining on marginal setups forgoes real upside and the opportunity cost of cash is non-zero.

2-position diversification could theoretically reduce portfolio variance if position failures are weakly correlated; the archaeology does not directly test cross-position correlation in low-density snapshots.
Cash has no explicit yield modeled here; in regimes where the benchmark drifts upward, 2/3 idle capital may underperform even a marginal 3rd slot — the data does not net out this benchmark drift.

Selected_winners themselves sometimes have only modestly above-threshold features (entity_90a828939a: mom_20=0.036, up_day_ratio=0.45, w4=large_win), showing that high-conviction gating on the listed features would have skipped real winners.
Sample size (n=27, of which only ~11 selected_winners and 8 false_positive_ruin) is small; the apparent separation between winner and ruin distributions may shrink with more data.
falsifiable_predictions: If fewer than 3 candidates in a snapshot satisfy ALL of {up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.60, vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.40, mom_20 ≥ 0.15}, then a 3-slot full-deployment portfolio will underperform a 1-slot portfolio on risk-adjusted return over W4 because the 3rd slot's ruin probability exceeds ~35%.

If the marginal (lowest-feature) candidate has up_day_ratio_20 < 0.55 OR vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.30, the contribution of that slot to portfolio expected value is negative and dominated by the ruin tail; cash strictly dominates deployment of that slot.

In low-density snapshots (≤2 qualifying setups), the conditional probability of w4_return_bucket='ruin' for any slot whose up_day_ratio_20 falls in [0.40, 0.60] AND vol_ratio_5_20 in [1.0, 1.5] is ≥30%, versus ≤10% for slots with all three features above the thresholds.
Sharpe ratio ordering in low-density regimes: 1-position ≥ 2-position > 3-position; this ordering should reverse (3 > 2 > 1) in high-density regimes where all slots meet the feature thresholds.

The 2nd slot's marginal value (ΔEV of moving from 1 to 2 positions) is positive only when the 2nd-best candidate has up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.60 AND mom_20 ≥ 0.10; below these, the 2nd slot is net-negative.
policy_implications: Adopt a slot-deployment quality gate using PIT-observable features only: require up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.60, vol_ratio_5_20 ≥ 1.40, and mom_20 ≥ 0.15 for any slot to be filled; below these thresholds the slot defaults to cash.

In low setup-density snapshots, cap deployment at min(N_qualifying, 2) positions; explicitly prohibit forcing the 3rd slot when only 1 or 2 setups clear the gate, because the historical false_positive_ruin band coincides with the marginal-candidate range.

Treat cash as a position with explicit option value: the cost of an unfilled slot equals the expected EV of the best future setup discounted by arrival probability, not zero — this should be netted against any marginal candidate's expected return before deployment.
When only 1 setup qualifies, prefer single concentrated deployment over forcing diversification; when 2 qualify, deploy both; reserve the right to hold 1–2 slots in cash without penalty.

Track per-slot feature overlap with the false_positive_ruin profile (up_day_ratio in [0.40,0.65], vol_ratio in [1.0,1.6], mom_20 in [0.02,0.25]) as a pre-trade risk flag; if the marginal candidate lands in this band, abstain regardless of slot count.

Re-evaluate the feature thresholds quarterly using expanding archaeology: if the winner/ruin separation weakens over time, raise the thresholds rather than lowering them, because the ruin tail is asymmetric and dominates the loss profile.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The prior mechanism claim is unfalsifiable as stated because (a) the feature-threshold gate is derived from the wrong comparison group (false_negatives vs selected_winners rather than false_positive_ruin vs selected_winners), (b) ruin events are demonstrably regime-clustered within snapshots (snap_71486ed83c and snap_b8420124eb each contain multiple ruin cases), which destroys the diversification assumption that slot 2/3 ruins are approximately independent, and (c) the 'option value of cash' double-counts the same marginal-feature problem by deferring it to the next snapshot rather than resolving it. The non-linear slot-EV ordering (slot1>slot2>slot3>cash) is therefore not an intrinsic property of low-density regimes — it is an artifact of (i) feature-based ranking that has already been shown to bifurcate on strong setups (entity_6618d3e80c: mom_20=0.251, px_vs_ma50=0.337, BOTH ruin and winner), and (ii) pooling across heterogeneous regimes that drives the apparent ruin tail.

attacks.issue: Threshold derivation uses the wrong reference distribution. The numeric contrasts compare false_negatives (rejected setups) against selected_winners, but the marginal-slot decision is between DEPLOYING a passing setup or holding cash — i.e., the relevant comparison is selected_winners vs false_positive_ruin (8 cases). The false_positive_ruin median up_day_ratio is in [0.50–0.65], overlapping the selected_winner median of 0.625; the gates derived from the false_negative comparison (≥0.60) would fail to exclude a meaningful fraction of ruin cases.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the thresholds cannot separate the actually-risky cohort from the winning cohort on the demonstrated sample, the policy implication 'cash dominates slot 3' is unsupported. The signal-to-noise in the discrimination is much weaker than the researcher claims.

attacks.issue: Regime-driven ruin correlation within snapshots. snap_71486ed83c contains at least 4 false_positive_ruin/false_negative cases; snap_b8420124eb contains 2 false_positive_ruin cases plus a selected_winner. This is consistent with a market-regime effect (e.g., a sector drawdown week) that hits multiple slots simultaneously. The 'diversification across 2–3 slots reduces variance' assumption baked into the slot-EV ordering is therefore likely false.
attacks.why_it_matters: If ruins are correlated across slots within a snapshot, the marginal variance reduction from slot 1→2 is small, and the comparison should be '1 concentrated slot vs 3 correlated slots,' which inverts the policy. The 'slot 2 is breakeven, slot 3 is negative' ordering collapses under correlated ruin.

attacks.issue: Omitted-variable confound on the ruin label. The feature set shown (up_day_ratio, vol_ratio, mom_20, px_vs_ma50, ma slopes, pullback stats) does not include earnings-date proximity, sector beta, market-cap, ADV liquidity, or borrow availability — common causes of idiosyncratic W4 ruin. entity_2c58cebc59 had pullback_pct=-25.1 yet produced large_win; entity_3adc078f01 had pullback_pct=-42.3 and large_win. The 'ruin' label may be driven by variables orthogonal to the PIT feature gate.
attacks.why_it_matters: If ruin is driven by omitted variables, capping deployment at 2 slots based on observable features does not actually reduce ruin exposure — it just reduces exposure to the same marginal setups that were going to fail anyway. The cash buffer provides no insurance against regime-wide or event-driven ruin.

attacks.issue: Circular 'option value of cash'. The researcher claims cash has option value equal to 'expected EV of best future setup discounted by arrival probability.' But the next setup available in the same regime will have the same marginal-feature profile (low density is itself a regime property). Deferring deployment to the next snapshot does not escape the marginal-candidate problem; it just delays it.
attacks.why_it_matters: This makes the policy 'prefer 1 concentrated slot + cash' unfalsifiable: any period of cash holding can be retrospectively justified by 'waiting for the next setup,' while no deployment decision is ever proven wrong because future outcomes are not observed. The option-value argument is rhetorical, not empirical.

attacks.issue: Magnitude of 'ruin' is unknown. The w4_return_bucket='ruin' label could be -20% or -80%. Without the underlying return magnitude, the EV arithmetic for the marginal slot is impossible. If ruin = -25% with probability 30% and large_win = +30% with probability 50% with breakeven otherwise, the slot has EV = 0.5*30 + 0.3*(-25) + 0.2*0 = +7.5% — positive, not negative. The asymmetry claim is asserted, not computed.
attacks.why_it_matters: The entire 'cash dominates slot 3' conclusion rests on ruin being catastrophic enough AND frequent enough to swamp winner gains. With n=27 and undefined ruin magnitude, this is an unsubstantiated claim. The mechanism_claim is a story, not a calculation.

attacks.issue: Bifurcation on strong setups invalidates the gating logic. entity_6618d3e80c has features well above the proposed thresholds (mom_20=0.251, px_vs_ma50=0.337, up_day_ratio=0.55) and carries the dual label 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' — meaning the same setup produced both a ruin-cohort outcome and a winner-cohort outcome. This shows the feature gate has a non-trivial false-positive rate even at the strong end.
attacks.why_it_matters: If even setups that pass the gate can bifurcate into ruin vs winner within the same snapshot, the gate is necessary-but-insufficient for the researcher's stated policy. The 'slot 1 positive EV' claim is conditional on a regime axis the gate does not measure.

attacks.issue: Density is never operationalized. The mechanism_claim and policy_implications both reference 'low setup density,' but the archaeology data contains no density field — snapshots are identified by hash only. The researcher infers density from sample composition without defining it, measuring it, or stratifying by it. The falsifiable predictions reference density thresholds that cannot be checked against the evidence.
attacks.why_it_matters: A claim that depends on a regime variable that is neither measured nor defined in the data is not testable. The policy 'cap deployment at min(N_qualifying, 2)' presupposes a definition of qualifying that the data does not support.

attacks.issue: Sample artifact: n=27 discovery-train only. With 8 false_positive_ruin, 11 selected_winner, 5 false_negative_relative, 2 false_negative_big_winner, 1 dual-label, the per-bucket n is below any reasonable statistical-power threshold. The standardized deltas shown (max ~1.2) are moderate, not strong; small-sample deltas of this magnitude are consistent with random variation around zero.
attacks.why_it_matters: An effect size of 0.6–1.2 standardized units in a 27-case archaeology is suggestive, not conclusive. The 'asymmetric ruin dominates' narrative is built on point estimates whose confidence intervals would likely include zero or reverse sign with another 27 cases.

counterexamples_to_seek: A snapshot where the 2nd-best setup by the researcher's feature rank produced the largest W4 gain of the three slots — demonstrating that slot ordering by EV is not monotonically decreasing in feature rank.

A held-out snapshot where 3 marginal slots (all below the proposed thresholds) collectively produced a higher W4 return than the 1-slot 'concentrate on best' alternative — falsifying the slot3-dominance claim.
Cross-snapshot ruin correlation: cases from different snapshots but the same calendar week that all show false_positive_ruin, isolating regime from features.
A ruin case where the failing slot's features all CLEAR the proposed thresholds (up_day_ratio≥0.60, vol_ratio≥1.40, mom_20≥0.15), demonstrating gate-bypass.
A bull-regime snapshot where the researcher-classified 'marginal' 3rd slot produced large_win despite features in the false_positive_ruin band — showing regime overrides feature signal.
A negative benchmark-drift period where holding 2/3 in cash produced a portfolio return below even a single moderate-win slot — falsifying the option-value-of-cash claim.
A snapshot where selected_winners had lower median features than false_positive_ruin cases — demonstrating the ordering can reverse.
what_would_change_my_mind: A held-out test (n≥30 low-density snapshots) where 1-slot deployment strictly dominates 2- and 3-slot deployment on Sharpe with p<0.05, AND where ruin magnitudes are reported (not just bucketed) so that EV arithmetic is verifiable.

Evidence that within a single snapshot, ruin outcomes across multiple slots are approximately uncorrelated — measured either by sign-correlation of W4 returns or by feature-conditional independence tests — supporting the diversification assumption.

A regime-stratified analysis (bull vs bear vs neutral snapshots) showing the ruin probability of marginal slots is materially lower in regimes where the marginal slots also have high features, not just lower marginal-feature counts overall.

Calculation of cash option value using a stated discount rate and arrival probability, showing that the option value exceeds the marginal slot's expected EV with statistical significance across multiple held-out snapshots.

Demonstration that the proposed gates (up_day_ratio≥0.60, vol_ratio≥1.40, mom_≥0.15) actually exclude a majority of false_positive_ruin cases while including a majority of selected_winner cases on the discovery sample — i.e., that the gates work on the correct reference comparison.

Evidence that features not shown in the archaeology (earnings proximity, sector exposure, liquidity, beta) do not dominate the ruin signal — i.e., that the visible feature set is sufficient for the gating logic.

tests.name: T1_correct_reference_gate_discrimination
tests.comparison: Distinguishability of selected_winner (n=11) vs false_positive_ruin (n=8) cohorts under the researcher's proposed gate {up_day_ratio_20>=0.60 AND vol_ratio_5_20>=1.40 AND mom_20>=0.15}; contrast with the existing false_negative-vs-selected_winner contrast that originally motivated the threshold.
tests.success_criterion: On the selected_winner vs false_positive_ruin comparison (the deployment-decision-relevant pair), at least 0.50 of selected_winners fall inside the gate and at most 0.50 of false_positive_ruin cases fall inside it; plus a sign-rank/median separation of mom_20 or up_day_ratio_20 at standardized delta >=0.5 between the two cohorts.
tests.failure_criterion: Gate passes <=0.40 of selected_winners OR >=0.60 of false_positive_ruin cases; OR the median direction of mom_20/up_day_ratio_20/vol_ratio_5_20 between the two cohorts does not have the same sign as in the false_negative-vs-selected_winner contrast.

tests.name: T2_within_snapshot_cross_slot_dependence
tests.comparison: Across all snapshots that contain >=2 slots (selected_winners AND/OR false_positive_ruin AND/OR false_negative labels): compute per-snapshot the cross-slot dispersion of up_day_ratio_20 and vol_ratio_5_20, and the cross-slot dispersion of W4 return bucket (encoded as ordinal); then test whether low feature dispersion predicts low return dispersion (independence) vs high feature dispersion predicting correlated ruin/winner clustering (regime dominance). This separates 'marginal-slot EV is intrinsically negative' (independence assumed) from 'regime hits slots simultaneously so diversification does not help' (dependence observed).
tests.success_criterion: Within snapshots where feature dispersion is small (e.g., IQR of up_day_ratio_20 across slots <=0.10), W4 outcomes across slots are uncorrelated (sign agreement <=60%); within snapshots where feature dispersion is large, ruin labels are NOT clustered on the same snapshot (at most 1 false_positive_ruin per snapshot when snapshot's mean up_day_ratio_20 >=0.60).
tests.failure_criterion: Two or more snapshots contain >=2 false_positive_ruin cases each despite homogeneous within-snapshot features; OR any snapshot shows >=3 slots sharing the same w4_return_bucket='ruin' with cross-slot feature IQR<=0.10.

tests.name: T3_marginal_band_ruin_concentration
tests.comparison: Compute ruin/winner rate within the joint marginal feature band {up_day_ratio_20 in [0.40,0.65] AND vol_ratio_5_20 in [1.0,1.6] AND mom_20 in [0.02,0.25]} vs all slots outside this band. Separates 'this band is the ruin zone' from 'this band is just where most candidates fall regardless of density'.
tests.success_criterion: Slots inside the marginal band show false_positive_ruin rate >=2x the rate of slots outside the band; slots outside the band show selected_winner rate >=2x the rate of slots inside the band. Sample sizes inside vs outside must both be n>=3.
tests.failure_criterion: Inside-band ruin rate is not statistically distinct from outside-band ruin rate given the small samples (Fisher's exact p>0.20 OR deltas in opposite direction); OR ruin rate inside band <= outside band.

tests.name: T4_density_proxy_stratification
tests.comparison: Construct a per-snapshot density proxy from PIT features alone (not from snapshot_anon identity): specifically, the count of slots per snapshot whose up_day_ratio_20>=0.55 AND mom_20>=0.10. Stratify snapshots into 'low density' (0-1 qualifying) and 'high density' (>=3 qualifying) under this proxy and compare the slot-EV ordering (median w4_return_bucket ordinal, where ruin<loss<small_win<large_win) for slot 1 (best-feature), slot 2, slot 3 (worst-feature) within each density class.
tests.success_criterion: In the low-density proxy class, slot 1 median ordinal > slot 3 median ordinal by >=1 bucket rank (one-sided Wilcoxon or median test on >=3 snapshots each with at least 2 slots labeled). In the high-density class, slot 1 median ordinal is not significantly lower than slot 3 (diversification partially works).
tests.failure_criterion: In low-density proxy class, slot 3 median ordinal >= slot 1 median ordinal; OR the proxy fails to stratify (low- and high-density classes yield indistinguishable slot-EV orderings).

tests.name: T5_volatility_regime_vs_feature_gate
tests.comparison: Test whether rv_20 (realized volatility) and atr_14_pct (price-range volatility) dominate the winner/ruin separation above and beyond up_day_ratio_20 and mom_20. Fit a simple ordinal regression (logit on ruin-vs-winner) with (a) up_day_ratio_20 + mom_20 only, (b) rv_20 + atr_14_pct only, (c) all four. This separates 'high-feature gates work' from 'ruin is actually a volatility-regime phenomenon that the proposed gate mislabels as marginal features'.
tests.success_criterion: (a) Model with up_day_ratio_20+mom_20 explains ruin/winner with pseudo-R^2 >=2x the (b) volatility-only model; OR adding vol features to (a) does not improve pseudo-R^2 by >0.05.
tests.failure_criterion: (b) Volatility-only model has pseudo-R^2 >= (a) feature-only model; OR adding rv_20/atr_14_pct to (a) improves pseudo-R^2 by >=0.10.

tests.name: T6_slot_ordering_monotonicity_within_snapshot
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot with >=2 slots, rank slots by composite feature score (e.g., equal-weighted z-score of up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50) and check whether higher-ranked slots actually achieve better w4_return_bucket. Separates 'features predict slot EV monotonically' from 'feature ranking is unreliable within a snapshot, so slot ordering by features is meaningless even when marginal features predict ruin on aggregate'.
tests.success_criterion: Within-snapshot Spearman correlation between composite feature rank and w4_bucket rank (ruin<loss<small_win<large_win) is >=0.30 averaged across snapshots with n_slots>=3; at least 0.60 of within-snapshot comparisons show higher-feature slot >= lower-feature slot.
tests.failure_criterion: Within-snapshot Spearman is <=0.10 OR sign-flips across snapshots; OR >0.40 of within-snapshot rank-order comparisons contradict monotonicity (e.g., entity_6618d3e80c-style bifurcation where features are strong yet ruin AND winner appear).

tests.name: T7_counterfactual_cash_replacement_of_marginal_slots
tests.comparison: For each snapshot in archaeology, identify the marginal (worst-feature) slot per the composite rank in T6. Compute a counterfactual w4_return of replacing that slot's outcome with the median outcome of the 'cash cohort' — operationally defined as the w4_return_bucket=null-valued or non-deployed outcomes pooled across snapshots. Compare the count of times cash-replacement strictly improves the snapshot's worst-outcome vs degrades it. This tests 'cash dominates the marginal slot' on the existing archaeological sample (no outer-forward required) without assuming zero cash return.
tests.success_criterion: Cash-replacement strictly improves the worst outcome in >=0.60 of multi-slot snapshots; aggregate w4_bucket ordinal sum across marginal slots drops (more ruin replaced) vs aggregate drops only when forced into a worse bucket.
tests.failure_criterion: Cash-replacement does not improve outcome in >=0.50 of multi-slot snapshots; OR the marginal slot's median w4_bucket ordinal is not significantly worse than the median of higher-feature slots (Wilcoxon p>0.30).

leakage_checks: snapshot_anon and entity_anon are hash IDs, NOT PIT features — exclude from any feature list; using them would be a de-anonymization/timestamp-proxy leak.
outcome_label and w4_return_bucket are labels, never features — confirm they appear only in the comparison/output side of each test, never on the input side.
ibd_entry_* features are PIT (point-in-time relative to entry) and acceptable; verify no ibd_entry_* feature describes post-entry information (e.g., peak-during-W4 attributes).
pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct: confirm these measure the pullback that preceded entry, not the drawdown during W4 holding period; flag for re-verification.
No calendar-derived features: exclude any feature that binarizes day-of-week, month, or relative-to-event-window without an explicitly PIT interpretation.
base_duration_weeks and base_mbox_count: confirm these are measured as of the snapshot date, not retrospectively after the W4 outcome window.
Sample composition: the archaeology is explicitly discovery-train-only per method_note — confirm T1-T7 do not introduce cross-fold or held-out claims that contradict the in-sample scope.

Feature subset audit: T5 uses rv_20 and atr_14_pct which appear only in the numeric_contrast metadata (not in every entity row); confirm these features are present for the comparison subsample before declaring the test runnable, otherwise mark UNRESOLVED rather than imputing.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The 'cash dominates the marginal slot in low-density regimes' thesis has partial empirical support but is not cleanly separable from confounders. Within the discovery-train archaeology (n=27), false_positive_ruin cases (8) cluster in a marginal feature band (up_day_ratio_20 ≈ 0.50–0.65, vol_ratio_5_20 ≈ 1.0–1.6, mom_20 ≈ 0.02–0.25, px_vs_ma50 ≈ 0.05–0.15) that also contains a non-trivial fraction of selected_winners (e.g., entity_90a828939a at up_day_ratio=0.45/mom_20=0.036 → large_win; entity_2f86543bf6 at mom_20=-0.008 → large_win). This means the candidate band is genuinely ambiguous: ruin probability is elevated versus the high-feature tail, but the absolute ruin rate is not 100% and the upside of marginal setups is non-zero. The economic meaning of 1 vs 2 vs 3 slots under fixed capital is therefore NOT a simple monotonic EV ordering. Slot 1 is plausibly positive-EV (concentrated highest-feature setup), but the slot 2/slot 3 distinction collapses once we accept the Skeptic's point that ruin events co-occur within snapshots (snap_71486ed83c has 4+ ruin/false_negative labels, snap_b8420124eb has 2 ruins + 1 winner) — implying regime-correlated draws that defeat variance-reduction arguments. The mechanism is best characterized as: marginal-band candidate EV is approximately zero with a left-tail dominated by asymmetric ruin risk, AND the marginal slot's ruin probability is partially correlated with other slots' ruin probability, so diversification gain across slots 2 and 3 is smaller than naive independence would predict. Cash therefore dominates a marginal slot only when (a) the slot's composite feature score falls in the ruin-cluster band AND (b) the snapshot's cross-slot feature homogeneity is high enough that diversification offers minimal variance reduction.
falsifiers: T1 fails: the proposed gate {up_day_ratio≥0.60 AND vol_ratio_5_20≥1.40 AND mom_20≥0.15} cannot separate selected_winners from false_positive_ruin with median-direction agreement on mom_20/up_day_ratio/vol_ratio (i.e., ruin cases inside the gate are not reduced below ~50% of in-band cases).

T2 fails: a snapshot with cross-slot up_day_ratio_20 IQR ≤0.10 produces ≥3 slots sharing w4_return_bucket='ruin' — directly demonstrating that diversification across 3 slots does not reduce ruin incidence and cash-dominance over the marginal slot is undermined by the lack of independent ruin draws.

T4 fails: in low-density-proxy snapshots, the slot-3 (worst-feature) median w4 ordinal is ≥ slot-1 median ordinal, showing the within-snapshot feature ranking does not reliably identify which slot is 'marginal' and which is 'core', so 'cash should replace slot 3' becomes undefined.

Discovery of additional selected_winners in the marginal feature band (up_day_ratio<0.55 OR mom_20<0.10) at rates exceeding the false_positive_ruin rate inside the same band — entity_90a828939a and entity_2f86543bf6 are early warnings that the ruin band is not exclusive.
Out-of-sample (held-out fold) replication where the gate-passing cohort has W4 ruin rate ≥20% — falsifying the claim that the gates themselves reduce ruin probability.

Regime-variable (sector-relative strength, market breadth) explains more outcome variance than the candidate-level PIT features, in which case the cash-dominates-marginal-slot claim is true at the snapshot level but not the slot level, and the policy prescription changes from 'gate individual slots' to 'gate entire snapshots'.
actionable_design_principles: Treat cash as a first-class position with explicit non-zero cost equal to (benchmark drift over holding window) × (probability of no replacement setup arriving within that window); never treat cash as free.

Use a composite PIT-feature quality score (z-scored combination of up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50, pullback_pct, ma10_slope_5) rather than binary thresholds; binary thresholds discard ordering information and force winners like entity_90a828939a out of the portfolio while admitting ruinations like entity_8f0df3d38e.

Distinguish 'slot N is filled' from 'slot N is filled with a qualifying candidate' — deployment is conditional on candidate quality, not on slot index. The number of deployed slots (1/2/3) is a derived quantity, not a policy input.

Stratify snapshots by within-snapshot feature homogeneity (IQR of up_day_ratio_20 across slots); when homogeneity is high (cross-slot features look similar), assume correlated draws and cap deployment at 1 slot even if 3 candidates nominally exist, because diversification gain is empirically small in that regime.

Log every abstention (cash-held slot) with the candidate's composite score and the ruin-band membership flag, so that quarterly archaeology can detect drift in the ruin band location without confusing it with sample-size noise.

Do not derive gates from the false_negative-vs-selected_winner contrast — that contrast is about candidate rejection, not deployment decision; the deployment-relevant contrast is selected_winner vs false_positive_ruin, which has much smaller median separation.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: slot_deployment_gate: returns max(0, min(3, count(slots where composite_score ≥ quality_threshold AND slot NOT in marginal_band))) where marginal_band = (up_day_ratio_20 ∈ [0.40, 0.65]) AND (vol_ratio_5_20 ∈ [1.0, 1.6]) AND (mom_20 ∈ [0.02, 0.25]).
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Combines a quality floor AND an explicit ruin-band exclusion; the band exclusion addresses the regime where marginal candidates pass the quality floor but have ruin-overlap features. Does NOT force 3-slot deployment when only 1–2 candidates clear both gates.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Maps directly to the 1/2/3 slot decision by counting qualifying candidates; the cap at 3 preserves the original portfolio constraint while letting cash fill the gap.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: within_snapshot_dispersion_filter: compute IQR(up_day_ratio_20 across slots) per snapshot; if IQR ≤ 0.10 then cap deployment at 1 slot regardless of candidate count, on the hypothesis that low-dispersion snapshots have regime-correlated draws.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Operates at the snapshot level, not the candidate level; addresses the Skeptic's correlated-ruin objection directly by recognizing that diversification gain is conditional on cross-slot feature dispersion. Does not appear in the Researcher's policy list.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Reduces deployment count in homogeneous-snapshot regimes, so effective capacity (= number of deployed slots) becomes endogenously state-dependent rather than fixed at 3.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: cash_position_explicit_carry: log cash holdings with opportunity_cost = benchmark_return_window × (1 - setup_arrival_probability_window); surface this as a per-decision cost on the abstention side, so that the policy does not over-abstain when benchmark drift is steeply positive.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Forces the abstention decision to be evaluated against an explicit alternative use of capital rather than zero; addresses the Researcher's own caveat that 'cash has no explicit yield modeled here' without requiring an outer-forward benchmark test. The capacity implication is that '1 slot deployed + 2 cash' carries an explicit carry cost.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Couples deployment count to opportunity cost; in steep uptrend regimes, the policy may justify forcing slot 2 or 3 even with marginal features, raising effective capacity temporarily.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: marginal_band_ruin_flag: per-slot pre-trade flag = 1 if candidate's features fall in the ruin-cluster band AND the snapshot contains another slot already in the same band; flag triggers automatic abstention for the lower-quality slot (cash substitutes).
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Conditional abstinence based on portfolio-level ruin concentration rather than slot-level score alone; recognizes that ruin correlation within the marginal band amplifies left-tail risk. Operates as a tie-breaker when two slots are both in the marginal band.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Further reduces the 3rd slot probability when slots 1 and 2 are already in the ruin band, lowering effective capacity in the worst regime (homogeneous marginal).

cycles.question: Test the hypothesis 'Lane has independent predictive information' specifically in fresh breakout weeks. Give discriminating predictions for B0_LANE, LANE_NEUTRAL, and SCORE_BEFORE_LANE.

researcher.mechanism_claim: In fresh breakout weeks (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct typically 0.01-0.07), Lane's apparent predictive edge is largely the reflection of a few base SCORE inputs (mom_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20). Lane's independent contribution is concentrated in a single interaction: it suppresses names where ma10_slope_5 is elevated but up_day_ratio_20 is low (≤0.5), a bull-trap regime that the raw SCORE permits. Outside that interaction, B0_LANE is essentially isomorphic to a high-quintile SCORE_BEFORE_LANE bucket; LANE_NEUTRAL is functionally a wider, noisier version of the same SCORE distribution.
evidence_for: Selected_winner median up_day_ratio_20 = 0.625 vs false_negative_median = 0.500 (std delta -1.19) — Lane's winners share a breadth signature absent from non-picks.

Selected_winner median mom_20 = 0.163 vs false_negative_median = 0.058 (std delta -1.00) and px_vs_ma50 = 0.127 vs 0.056 (std delta -0.85) — Lane's winners cluster at the high-momentum/RS corner; SCORE captures the same corner.

Among is_b0_pick=true cases, false_positive_ruin entries (entity_8f0df3d38e up_day 0.65+ but ruin; entity_84824e6a20 ma10_slope 0.062 but up_day 0.4 → ruin; entity_b6bcccdf6a ma10_slope 0.067 but up_day 0.4 → loss) show Lane is fooled by momentum bursts when breadth is thin — i.e., Lane DOES add an interaction filter (slope × breadth) that raw SCORE does not.

Entity_6618d3e80c carries the rare compound label false_positive_ruin|selected_winner — a high-conviction Lane name (px_vs_ma50 0.337, ma10_slope 0.075) that produced a large_win within the ruin window, indicating Lane's strongest conviction tier does carry genuine edge.

False_negative_relative cases (entity_df5478102d, entity_d8e8e7b814, entity_bfb308b24a) all sit in the moderate-feature band (mom_20 0.027-0.124, up_day 0.45-0.60) — exactly the band Lane abstains on. These represent Lane's 'LANE_NEUTRAL' miss set and demonstrate Lane is conservative, not selective.
evidence_against: The numeric_contrasts ranking is led by up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50 — all SCORE primitives. Lane's incremental column would have to appear as a higher-order interaction or a residual; the available contrasts do not isolate one.

Selected_winners and false_positives_ruin share nearly identical median ma10_slope_5 ranges (0.027 vs ~0.030-0.060) and overlapping px_vs_ma20 distributions — Lane cannot separate these classes with first-order features alone, weakening the claim of independent signal.

Entity_440e297253 is a selected_winner with up_day 0.50 (at the false_negative level) yet still produced large_win; entity_2f86543bf6 won with up_day 0.35 and negative ma20_slope — counter-examples to any deterministic Lane filter on breadth.

Sample is 27 cases with 8 false_positives_ruin and only 7 false_negatives; the power to detect a small but real Lane interaction is limited. No feature shows a standardized delta > |1.2|, the classic threshold for an independent signal in this archaeology.
falsifiable_predictions: In a held-out fresh-breakout sample, the Spearman correlation between B0_LANE's rank and SCORE_BEFORE_LANE's top-quintile rank will exceed 0.70 — falsified if it falls below 0.50 (i.e., Lane is doing something uncorrelated and genuinely independent).

The hit rate (w4_return ≥ +5pp vs benchmark) of B0_LANE minus the hit rate of the top-quintile of SCORE_BEFORE_LANE in fresh breakout weeks will be in the range [-3pp, +5pp]. A delta > +8pp would falsify the 'Lane ≈ SCORE' claim; a delta < -5pp would falsify 'Lane adds value at all'.

Among fresh-breakout B0_LANE picks, the conditional ruin rate given (ma10_slope_5 > 0.04 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.50) will exceed 55%. Falsified if the conditional ruin rate is statistically indistinguishable from the unconditional ruin rate (Lane is NOT filtering the bull-trap interaction).

LANE_NEUTRAL in fresh breakout weeks will have a bimodal forward-return distribution: probability of w4_return ≥ +8% will be ≥ 18% (matching selected_winner rates for moderate features) AND probability of w4_return ≤ -8% will be ≥ 22%. Falsified if LANE_NEUTRAL forward returns concentrate near zero (Lane's abstention carries no information).

A logistic model of w4 win/loss using only {mom_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, ma10_slope_5, ma10_slope_5×up_day_ratio_20} will produce an AUC within ±0.03 of a model that adds a B0_LANE dummy in fresh breakout weeks — testing whether the slope×breadth interaction absorbs Lane's information.

In fresh breakout weeks, the false_negative_relative rate inside LANE_NEUTRAL will be ≥ 2× the false_negative_relative rate inside the bottom three SCORE_BEFORE_LANE quintiles, since Lane's abstention is more conservative than SCORE's bottom tail.
policy_implications: If the predictions hold (Lane ≈ SCORE in fresh breakouts), portfolio construction should treat B0_LANE and top-quintile SCORE_BEFORE_LANE as substitutes in fresh breakout weeks and not double-count exposure. Lane's perceived alpha is largely a labeling artifact of the SCORE primitives.

The slope×breadth interaction is the actionable kernel: explicitly encode ma10_slope_5 × up_day_ratio_20 as a penalty/bonus rather than relying on Lane to filter implicitly. This makes the 'Lane' logic transparent and backtestable.

LANE_NEUTRAL in fresh breakouts is best treated as a HIGH-VARIANCE bucket, not as a 'do-not-trade' signal. The base SCORE should still rank LANE_NEUTRAL names; abstention should lower position size, not eliminate the trade.

Because the sample is thin (27 cases, 8 ruins, 7 misses) and no feature crosses |1.2| std delta, any deployment decision should be gated on a larger out-of-sample archaeology. Until then, mark the Lane-independent-information hypothesis as UNRESOLVED with a weak prior toward 'minimal independent contribution'.

Separate the 'directional filter' (Lane picks/not) from the 'sizing filter' (conviction tier). In fresh breakouts, sizing should be driven by SCORE_BEFORE_LANE magnitude, not by Lane conviction — Lane conviction adds at most a small tilt, per the predicted delta band of [-3pp, +5pp].

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The researcher's claim that 'Lane is essentially isomorphic to a high-quintile SCORE bucket in fresh breakout weeks' is an artifact of three compounding analytical errors: (1) collapsing Lane into a single binary flag (is_b0_pick) while SCORE is treated as a multi-feature vector, producing a guaranteed asymmetry; (2) testing the hypothesis on a sample whose labels are constructed AROUND Lane's hardest cases (false_positive_ruin and false_negative_relative), so a null finding is over-determined by selection; and (3) omitting the Lane-specific feature families that were never tested (base/pullback morphology, IBD-entry timing ratios, conviction tier). When these are corrected, the most plausible reading of the archaeology is that Lane has MEANINGFUL independent information that the analysis is structurally unable to detect.

attacks.issue: Selection bias in the label construction: the 27 cases were explicitly chosen to be Lane's worst and most ambiguous outcomes, then used to test whether Lane adds value
attacks.why_it_matters: If you sample the bottom of Lane's accuracy distribution and then ask 'does Lane add value?', a null answer is tautological. The false_positive_ruin (8) and false_negative_relative (7) labels exist precisely BECAUSE Lane failed there. Showing Lane ≈ SCORE on Lane's failure set cannot generalize to the broader population, and the researcher treats this failure-conditioned sample as representative.

attacks.issue: Category asymmetry: is_b0_pick is a single binary column, while SCORE is implicitly a continuous composite of ~25 features; comparing a flag to a distribution biases the conclusion toward 'Lane adds little'
attacks.why_it_matters: A binary signal with a 65-70% hit rate in fresh breakouts would already carry independent information by virtue of being correct 2:1 over chance. The numeric_contrasts ranking shows selected_winner up_day_ratio_20 = 0.625 vs false_negative 0.500 — but is_b0_pick is the actual decision variable and the analysis never directly asks 'what is the AUC of is_b0_pick alone?'

attacks.issue: Missing Lane-specific feature families in the SCORE primitives tested
attacks.why_it_matters: The numeric_contrasts include pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_pct, base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, base_depth_pct, ibd_entry_volume_ratio, ibd_entry_close_position, ibd_entry_breakout_range_ratio, current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct, dist_to_52w_high_pct — none of which are standard momentum/breadth SCORE inputs. These are the features Lane is most plausibly using; lumping them into 'SCORE' and then concluding 'Lane ≈ SCORE' is circular if Lane's information is concentrated exactly there.

attacks.issue: Snapshot non-independence inflates apparent feature importance
attacks.why_it_matters: Snap_71486ed83c alone contains 6 entities and snap_d0d57b1e40 contains 6 entities. With 27 cases spread across only ~12 snapshots, effective sample size for inference is roughly 12, not 27. The standardized deltas in numeric_contrasts are computed treating entities as independent when they share market-regime covariance, which inflates every reported effect size and creates spurious 'Lane ≈ SCORE' alignment within-regime.

attacks.issue: The slope×breadth interaction is a post-hoc rationalization from ~20 candidates on n=27
attacks.why_it_matters: With 20 candidate interactions and 27 cases, at least one will produce a standardized delta near |0.7| by chance. The researcher presents 'ma10_slope_5 × up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.5' as THE Lane mechanism, but no multiple-testing correction, no held-out validation, and no pre-registration. The bull-trap filter claim is a single fishing expedition.

attacks.issue: Reverse conditioning: Lane only emits picks when IBD publishes, so 'fresh breakout weeks' is doubly conditioned on (a) IBD editorial timing and (b) Lane's binary flag
attacks.why_it_matters: IBD's decision to publish a fresh-breakout trigger is itself an information event. SCORE_BEFORE_LANE applied to the same conditional set is also IBD-conditional, so the comparison Lane vs SCORE_BEFORE_LANE within this set is contaminated by a shared collider. The asymmetric conditioning means SCORE_BEFORE_LANE may have an unfair advantage because it can be computed on the full universe, while B0_LANE is restricted to IBD-published names.

attacks.issue: Entity_6618d3e80c (false_positive_ruin|selected_winner) is an in-sample refutation of the 'Lane filters the bull-trap' mechanism
attacks.why_it_matters: This compound label means Lane flagged the name as a ruin candidate (likely post-entry weakness flag) but the name STILL produced a large_win within the window. The mechanism claim that 'Lane suppresses names with high slope + low breadth' predicts Lane would NOT produce winners from the bull-trap regime; entity_6618d3e80c has ma10_slope_5 = 0.075 (high) and up_day_ratio_20 = 0.55 (moderate) — Lane tagged it as ruinous yet it won. The slope×breadth filter did not fire when it should have, weakening the entire mechanistic story.

attacks.issue: The [-3pp, +5pp] delta window is too wide to falsify 'Lane ≈ SCORE' and is asymmetric (allows 5pp Lane edge but only 3pp Lane loss)
attacks.why_it_matters: An 8pp acceptance band swallows any effect smaller than 8 percentage points. A real Lane edge of 6pp would pass this test as 'Lane ≈ SCORE.' The prediction is unfalsifiable in the direction that matters for deployment — the researcher chose a window that protects the null.

attacks.issue: Power collapse: 8 false_positive_ruin + 7 false_negative cases is far below the threshold to detect even a 2× interaction effect
attacks.why_it_matters: Detecting a 2× ruin-rate multiplier in the (ma10_slope_5 > 0.04 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.50) cell with α=0.05 and power=0.80 requires ~50 events in the conditioned cell. With 8 ruins total, the conditional test is underpowered by an order of magnitude. Reporting 'no significant interaction found' on this sample is uninformative, not evidence of absence.

attacks.issue: LANE_NEUTRAL destruction-of-alpha is ignored: false_negative cases (entity_de1c657364, entity_535a1beed7, entity_05b4c6b1f7, entity_ad2bfdee3f) suggest abstention cost ~15-20pp of large-win rate
attacks.why_it_matters: If Lane abstained on 5-7 names that became large winners within the window, the policy implication is not 'LANE_NEUTRAL is high-variance' but 'Lane is leaving real alpha on the table.' The researcher frames abstention as informational; the data shows abstention as costly. These are contradictory policy framings of the same evidence.

counterexamples_to_seek: Fresh-breakout B0_LANE picks where ma10_slope_5 ≤ 0.02 and up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.65 (low-slope, high-breadth regime the slope×breadth filter would not catch) that produced large_win — tests whether the proposed interaction is the ONLY Lane channel

Fresh breakout weeks where B0_LANE abstained (LANE_NEUTRAL) on a name with px_vs_ma50 ≥ 0.10 and ibd_entry_volume_ratio ≥ 2.0 that subsequently became a large winner — tests whether Lane's abstention mechanism is captured by SCORE
Held-out snapshots where multiple B0_LANE picks share the same IBD entry trigger week (true cross-section, not snapshot-dominated) — tests whether the 27-case analysis is a single-regime artifact
Cases where Lane's conviction tier (not captured in is_b0_pick) ranks stocks and lower-tier B0 picks underperform higher-tier ones by ≥5pp w4 — tests whether the binary collapse hides monotone edge
False_positive_ruin cases where the ruin occurred AFTER the w4 measurement window but BEFORE the typical holding period exit — tests whether the false_positive label is itself a look-ahead artifact

Snapshots where the base/pullback features (pullback_pct, base_depth_pct, base_mbox_count) cleanly separate selected_winner from false_positive_ruin but the SCORE momentum features do not — tests whether Lane's 'independent' signal lives in base morphology, which was never isolated
what_would_change_my_mind: A pre-registered out-of-sample test on ≥200 fresh breakout weeks with explicit isolation of Lane's base/pullback/IBD-entry feature families (not lumped into SCORE) AND a direct AUC comparison of (a) is_b0_pick alone, (b) SCORE primitives alone, (c) base/pullback features alone, (d) full feature set — if (c) or (d) does not dominate (a)+(b) by ≥0.05 AUC, the 'Lane ≈ SCORE' claim survives

Replicating the archaeology on data AFTER the discovery cutoff and finding the same slope×breadth interaction with p<0.01 after multiple-testing correction on ≥5 pre-specified interactions — this would convert the post-hoc fishing expedition into a real mechanism

Demonstrating that Lane's conviction tier (continuous, not binary) is redundant with SCORE_BEFORE_LANE quintile via a calibration plot showing <2pp hit-rate spread across conviction tiers within each SCORE quintile — this would support the 'Lane ≈ SCORE' reading

Showing that the 27 cases are i.i.d. with respect to snapshot by re-running the analysis with one case per snapshot and obtaining the same numeric_contrasts rankings — currently the snapshot non-independence is unaddressed
Evidence that IBD's publication timing has zero correlation with subsequent 4-week returns after controlling for the entry features, which would close the reverse-conditioning loophole

tests.name: AUC isolation of B0_LANE flag vs feature families in fresh breakouts
tests.comparison: Three nested logistic models on fresh-breakout weeks: (A) is_b0_pick alone, (B) SCORE_momentum = {mom_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, ma10_slope_5}, (C) base_pullback = {pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, base_depth_pct, base_mbox_count, ibd_entry_volume_ratio}. Compare AUC(A), AUC(B), AUC(C), AUC(B∪C), AUC(B∪C∪is_b0_pick).
tests.success_criterion: AUC(B∪C∪is_b0_pick) − AUC(B∪C) ≤ 0.02 AND AUC(C) ≤ AUC(B) − 0.03: Lane adds nothing beyond primitives and base/pullback family carries no incremental signal.
tests.failure_criterion: AUC(B∪C∪is_b0_pick) − AUC(B∪C) ≥ 0.05 OR AUC(C) ≥ AUC(B) + 0.02: Lane (or its base/pullback substrate) is not captured by SCORE momentum primitives.

tests.name: Slope×breadth bull-trap conditional ruin inside B0_LANE only
tests.comparison: Within B0_LANE picks in fresh breakout weeks, partition into cell (ma10_slope_5 > 0.04 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.50) vs complement. Compute w4_return bucket ruin rate per cell. Repeat for SCORE_BEFORE_LANE top quintile.
tests.success_criterion: Conditional ruin rate in the cell ≥ 1.8× unconditional B0_LANE ruin rate AND ≥ 1.5× the same cell's ruin rate within SCORE top quintile: Lane-specific bull-trap suppression exists.
tests.failure_criterion: Conditional ruin rate in cell ≤ 1.1× unconditional OR ≤ 1.0× SCORE-cell rate: the slope×breadth penalty is not Lane-specific; researcher's mechanism collapses.

tests.name: LANE_NEUTRAL vs SCORE bottom quintile destruction-of-alpha
tests.comparison: In fresh breakout weeks, compare large_win rate (w4_return ≥ +8pp vs benchmark) for LANE_NEUTRAL names vs the bottom-three SCORE_BEFORE_LANE quintiles. Also compute large_win rate for LANE_NEUTRAL names with px_vs_ma50 ≥ 0.10.
tests.success_criterion: LANE_NEUTRAL large_win rate ≤ bottom-quintile large_win rate + 3pp: abstention is informationally equivalent to bottom SCORE — researcher's 'high-variance bucket' reading holds.
tests.failure_criterion: LANE_NEUTRAL large_win rate ≥ bottom-quintile large_win rate + 10pp, OR ≥ 18% in the px_vs_ma50 ≥ 0.10 subset: abstention is costly and Lane's neutral state destroys recoverable alpha — skeptic's counterclaim holds.

leakage_checks: Cluster cases by snapshot_anon and recompute each test statistic using one-case-per-snapshot jackknife; report range vs point estimate to bound snapshot non-independence inflation.

Verify ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is used only as a freshness filter (< 0.07) and never as a predictive regressor in the AUC tests, since it is a trigger-relative metric that can leak editorial timing.
Hold out the entity_6618d3e80c compound-label case and re-estimate the slope×breadth cell to ensure the bull-trap mechanism is not driven by a single counter-example.
priority_order: AUC isolation of B0_LANE flag vs feature families in fresh breakouts
LANE_NEUTRAL vs SCORE bottom quintile destruction-of-alpha
Slope×breadth bull-trap conditional ruin inside B0_LANE only

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: In fresh breakout weeks (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct ∈ [0.01, 0.07]), Lane's apparent predictive edge overlaps substantially with a high-quintile SCORE_BEFORE_LANE bucket on the momentum/RS/breadth axis (mom_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20). The candidate independent contribution is localized to a single higher-order interaction: a slope×breadth bull-trap suppression (high ma10_slope_5 ≥ 0.04 paired with thin up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.50), which raw SCORE primitives do not capture first-order. However, with effective sample size n_eff ≈ 12 after snapshot-cluster correction, 8 ruin events and 7 miss events, this interaction is (i) post-hoc on ~20 candidate interactions (no multiple-testing adjustment), (ii) underpowered by roughly an order of magnitude to detect a 2× ruin-rate lift at α=0.05/power=0.80, and (iii) not robust to a single counter-example (entity_6618d3e80c, compound-label, sat in the bull-trap quadrant yet produced large_win). LANE_NEUTRAL in fresh breakouts behaves as a wide, partially-informed variance bucket — empirically not equivalent to the bottom SCORE quintile (it has higher false_negative density) but also not a clean 'do-not-trade' state. The discriminating question is therefore not 'Lane yes/no' but 'Lane ≈ SCORE_BEFORE_LANE top quintile ± delta on the population mean AND does the slope×breadth interaction survive cross-snapshot validation.' Both questions are unresolved at the current sample scale. Verdict: UNRESOLVED with a weak prior toward 'partial, interaction-localized independent contribution,' explicitly gated on out-of-sample archaeology.
falsifiers: Collider-free replication: in a held-out fresh-breakout sample where SCORE_BEFORE_LANE is computed ONLY on IBD-published names (not the full universe), |AUC(is_b0_pick) − AUC(SCORE_BEFORE_LANE top quintile)| < 0.025 AND DeLong p > 0.20 — falsifies any Lane-independent-information claim. If Lane carries no signal beyond SCORE, restricting SCORE to the same conditional set should drive AUCs to equivalence.

Out-of-sample slope×breadth interaction: in ≥3 fresh-breakout weeks not in the discovery set, ruin rate given (ma10_slope_5 > 0.04 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.50) inside B0_LANE must be ≥ 1.8× unconditional B0_LANE ruin rate AND ≥ 1.5× the same cell's ruin rate within SCORE_BEFORE_LANE top quintile. Falsified by either cell ruin rate ≤ 1.2× unconditional OR ≤ 1.0× the SCORE-cell rate.

Snapshot-jackknife stability: leave-one-snapshot-out re-estimation of the Spearman(B0_LANE_rank, SCORE_BEFORE_LANE_top_quintile_rank) must remain in [0.50, 0.85] across ALL folds. If the jackknife range includes values < 0.40 in any fold, the apparent Lane–SCORE alignment is a single-regime artifact.

LANE_NEUTRAL baseline check: in fresh breakouts, LANE_NEUTRAL large_win rate (w4_return ≥ +8pp vs benchmark) must be ≤ bottom-three SCORE_BEFORE_LANE quintiles' large_win rate + 3pp. Falsified (Lane-needs-different-treatment) if LANE_NEUTRAL large_win rate ≥ bottom-quintile rate + 10pp — abstention is then measurably costly.

Pre-registered interaction enumeration: if the slope×breadth interaction is one of ≥20 candidate feature×feature interactions, the strongest interaction's standardized delta must exceed |1.5| on the discovery set AND exceed |1.0| in held-out validation. Falsified by a top interaction whose held-out standardized delta falls below |0.7| — confirms fishing-expedition status.

Conviction-tier monotonicity: if Lane's conviction tier (not collapsed into is_b0_pick) shows monotone edge across ≥4 tiers with top-tier − bottom-tier w4 return ≥ +5pp, the binary-flag-only analysis is provably lossy and any 'Lane ≈ SCORE' claim from a binary collapse is artifactual.

Base/pullback family isolation: AUC(base_pullback_only) ≥ AUC(SCORE_momentum_only) + 0.03 in fresh breakouts — falsifies the implicit assumption that Lane's information lives in momentum/breadth SCORE primitives. If true, it shows Lane's independent channel is in pullback/base morphology that was never isolated by the original SCORE lump.

Freshness-decay falsification: if B0_LANE hit rate in the narrow freshness band [0.02, 0.05] (NOT the full [0.01, 0.07]) is statistically indistinguishable from hit rate in [0.05, 0.07] at p < 0.10, then 'fresh breakout week' is not the discriminating scope and the hypothesis framing is wrong.
actionable_design_principles: Encode slope×breadth explicitly as ma10_slope_5 × up_day_ratio_20 with a non-linear penalty when slope > 0.04 AND breadth ≤ 0.50; treat this as a FIRST-CLASS feature rather than relying on Lane to filter the interaction implicitly. This makes the candidate Lane-mechanism backtestable, falsifiable, and removable.

Compute SCORE_BEFORE_LANE on the same IBD-published universe as B0_LANE (collider correction). Never compare a flag defined on a conditional set against a continuous score defined on the full universe — this guarantees spurious Lane-edge or spurious SCORE-edge depending on conditioning direction.

Snapshot-clustered jackknife (leave-one-snapshot-out) is MANDATORY before reporting any standardized delta. Effective sample size ≈ number of distinct snapshots ≈ 12, not 27. All effect sizes and p-values must be jackknife-corrected; otherwise every reported contrast is over-stated by roughly √(27/12) ≈ 1.5×.

Power-gate interaction tests: at n_eff=12 and 8 ruin events, the minimum detectable odds ratio for an interaction at α=0.05/power=0.80 is ≈ 4–5× (not 2×). Either collect ≥50 fresh-breakout cases OR restrict interaction claims to OR ≥ 4. The current 'slope×breadth penalty' claim does not survive this gate.

Separate Lane's three semantic components before testing: (a) directional flag (is_b0_pick), (b) conviction tier (multi-level), (c) base/pullback substrate (Lane's most plausible independent feature family). Collapsing all three into is_b0_pick destroys information and biases the comparison toward 'Lane ≈ SCORE'.

Treat LANE_NEUTRAL as a sizing signal, not a blocking signal: empirical false_negative density inside LANE_NEUTRAL (entity_de1c657364, entity_535a1beed7, entity_05b4c6b1f7, entity_ad2bfdee3f) suggests 15–25% recoverable large_win rate, materially above bottom-quintile SCORE. Use LANE_NEUTRAL to scale position down by 30–50%, never to zero.

Freshness scope discipline: hypothesis tests must be stratified by ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct bands ([0.01,0.03], [0.03,0.05], [0.05,0.07]). The 'fresh breakout week' scope is 3× wider than typical IBD timing precision; the discriminating signal, if any, likely lives in the tightest band only.

Multiple-testing correction: of the ~20 candidate feature interactions in the discovery archaeology, at least one will produce standardized delta near |0.7| by chance. Bonferroni-adjusted threshold at α=0.05/20 = 0.0025 corresponds to |z| > 3.0; current top interaction at |1.19| does NOT survive this. Pre-register interactions before examining w4 outcomes.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: fresh_breakout_slope_breadth_penalty
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Encodes the slope×breadth bull-trap interaction (ma10_slope_5 > 0.04 AND up_day_ratio_20 ≤ 0.50) as an explicit position-size penalty in fresh breakout weeks. Distinct from Lane's implicit binary because the penalty is continuous, regime-conditional, and removable; distinct from raw SCORE because no first-order momentum/RS feature captures this interaction.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Operates only in the freshness band where the interaction was observed; can be toggled or weighted independently of B0_LANE. Useful as a counterfactual probe to test whether the interaction's predictive lift survives without Lane conditioning.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: lane_vs_score_collider_aligned_score
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: SCORE_BEFORE_LANE computed only on the IBD-published universe (collider-corrected) and ranked against B0_LANE flag. Distinct from raw SCORE because it conditions on the same publication event that defines is_b0_pick, eliminating the asymmetric conditioning that biases the prior analysis toward Lane-equals-SCORE or Lane-beats-SCORE artifacts.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Critical for any cross-comparison of Lane vs SCORE. Without this alignment, every Lane-vs-SCORE policy inherits the collider bias. With this alignment, the residual delta is interpretable as genuine independent information.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: lane_neutral_variance_sizer
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: LANE_NEUTRAL in fresh breakouts is NOT a 'do-not-trade' bucket — it is a high-variance, partially-informed bucket with empirically non-trivial large_win density. This policy scales LANE_NEUTRAL positions to 30–50% of the B0_LANE notional, distinguished from a hard veto by allowing participation when SCORE_BEFORE_LANE rank is in the top tercile of the conditional distribution.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Allocates risk capital across the LANE_NEUTRAL bucket in proportion to expected variance-adjusted return rather than zeroing exposure. Resolves the researcher/skeptic tension on LANE_NEUTRAL by treating it as informative-but-noisy rather than informational-or-zero.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: conviction_tier_monotone_decay
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Treats Lane's conviction tier as an ordinal signal (≥4 tiers) rather than collapsing to is_b0_pick. Tests whether top-tier B0 picks earn ≥5pp w4 return over bottom-tier B0 picks. If monotone, every binary-flag analysis to date is provably lossy and the 'Lane ≈ SCORE' conclusion is artifactual.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Restores information discarded by the binary collapse. Allows position sizing to vary smoothly across conviction tiers rather than step-functioning at is_b0_pick. Particularly important because the compound-label case (entity_6618d3e80c) is plausibly a high-tier signal that the binary flag mangles.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: freshness_band_stratified_score
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Splits 'fresh breakout weeks' into three tightness bands ([0.01,0.03], [0.03,0.05], [0.05,0.07]) and scores Lane independently per band. Distinct from a pooled fresh-breakout analysis because if the discriminating Lane signal exists only in the tightest band, pooling dilutes it to noise.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Provides per-band AUC and ruin-rate estimates so deployment can be tuned to the tightness of the IBD trigger rather than the average. Also a power-recovery device: tighter bands have smaller n but larger per-case signal; wider bands have larger n but diluted signal.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: base_pullback_family_isolator
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Treats Lane's base/pullback/IBD-entry feature family (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, base_depth_pct, base_mbox_count, ibd_entry_volume_ratio, ibd_entry_close_position, ibd_entry_breakout_range_ratio, current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct) as a separate SCORE sub-family, not lumped with momentum/breadth primitives. Tests whether this family dominates momentum primitives in fresh breakouts.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Skeptic's strongest attack — Lane's independent channel plausibly lives in base/pullback morphology that was never isolated by momentum/RS SCORE primitives. This isolator probes whether the lumped 'SCORE' comparison was circular. If this family alone outperforms is_b0_pick, Lane has clear independent information.

cycles.question: Test the hypothesis 'Lane is only a proxy for freshness/geometry/volume' specifically in fresh breakout weeks. Give discriminating predictions for B0_LANE, LANE_NEUTRAL, and SCORE_BEFORE_LANE.

researcher.mechanism_claim: In fresh breakout weeks, if Lane (B0_LANE / LANE_NEUTRAL / SCORE_BEFORE_LANE) is merely a re-encoding of freshness (up_day_ratio_20), geometry (mom_20, px_vs_ma20, base shape), and volume (vol_ratio_5_20, ibd_entry_volume_ratio), then conditioning on those three axis-features, Lane bin assignments must carry near-zero W4 return differential and SCORE_BEFORE_LANE must retain essentially all of SCORE_AFTER_LANE's predictive variance.
evidence_for: Frozen contrasts rank up_day_ratio_20 (std delta -1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), and mom_20 (-1.00) as the three largest separators between selected_winners and false_negatives, while px_vs_ma20/ma20_slope_5 also show mid-sized deltas; this leaves little residual axis for Lane to occupy that is not already in those proxies.
evidence_against: Multiple false_positive_ruin B0 picks (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_3472243e0c, entity_84824e6a20, entity_ccc90a671f) display proxy readings that match or exceed winners (mom_20 0.18, up_day_ratio_20 0.65, vol_ratio_5_20 1.21-1.63), indicating residual risk that up_day_ratio_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 + mom_20 cannot fully localize and that a Lane-style assessment of entry context could plausibly capture.
falsifiable_predictions: P1 (proxy holds): within fresh-breakout-week triples matched on up_day_ratio_20 (±0.05), vol_ratio_5_20 (±0.10), mom_20 (±0.05), the W4 return gap B0_LANE minus LANE_NEUTRAL is <1.0pp and SCORE_BEFORE_LANE explains ≥90% of SCORE_AFTER_LANE's W4-return cross-sectional R^2; also, the false_positive_ruin rate in LANE_NEUTRAL rows that pass on the proxy composite equals the B0_LANE ruin rate within ±1pp.

P2 (proxy refuted): under the same matched triples, B0_LANE minus LANE_NEUTRAL W4 return exceeds 2.0pp, OR SCORE_BEFORE_LANE explains <70% of SCORE_AFTER_LANE R^2, OR false_positive_ruins cluster disproportionately in a single Lane bin independent of the composite — any one of these rejects the pure-proxy hypothesis.
policy_implications: If P1 holds in the next discovery-cycle matched triple test, retire Lane and replace it with an explicit composite z(up_day_ratio_20) + z(vol_ratio_5_20) + z(mom_20) in the B0 selector; if P2 holds, keep Lane as an orthogonal residual and re-weight SCORE_AFTER_LANE so the fresh-breakout-week B0 priority list downweights Lane-Neutral rows that otherwise screen clean on the proxy composite.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The proxy hypothesis is methodologically untestable in this evidence base: the false_negative sample is constructed by selecting on future W4 returns (>=8% and >=5pp above B0 median, or >=5pp above worst B0 pick), which makes ANY correlation between feature axes and 'false_negative' status a tautology of future returns — not evidence that the features 'cause' winners versus losers. Lane cannot be reduced to proxies when the proxies themselves were fished from a forward-selected sample. Furthermore, the matched-triple design the prior role proposes is statistically dead: with N=27 cases and the request to match on three continuous features at ±0.05/±0.10/±0.05 tolerances, expected cell occupancy is well below 1 per stratum, so neither P1 nor P2 can be reached at conventional power.

attacks.issue: False_negative sample is constructed using FUTURE W4 returns, biasing every feature coefficient
attacks.why_it_matters: The method_note explicitly states false negatives require future W4 >=8% and >=5pp above B0 selected median. Selecting on the dependent variable produces spurious feature separation. The 'top three separators' (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20) are not 'proxies for Lane' — they are features correlated with momentum that will also correlate with any future-return-weighted label. The proxy hypothesis becomes circular: if Lane is correlated with momentum (which it plausibly is in fresh-breakout weeks), Lane would also separate false_negatives purely because the label is future-return-based.

attacks.issue: Matched-triple test has effectively zero statistical power at N=27
attacks.why_it_matters: Matching three continuous features at ±0.05/0.10/0.05 tolerances over a 27-case archaeology yields near-empty cells. Even if Lane is purely a proxy, sampling noise in W4 returns (which can be ±10pp for individual 4-week windows) will swamp any 1.0pp or 2.0pp differential the predictions reference. The researcher sets thresholds without any power calculation, so P1 and P2 are unfalsifiable in either direction — any outcome is consistent with 'not enough data.'

attacks.issue: The three proxy features are near-collinear and proxy for one latent momentum factor, not three independent axes
attacks.why_it_matters: up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and mom_20 are mechanically linked: rising prices (mom_20) produce more up days (up_day_ratio_20) on higher relative volume (vol_ratio_5_20). Matching on all three is matching on essentially one dimension. If Lane captures an orthogonal axis — e.g., base quality, distribution-day count in the breakout week, sector RR, sponsorship flow, or close position relative to the breakout range — these collinear proxies cannot substitute for it, and the matched test will falsely conclude 'no Lane effect' because the matched triples all share the same momentum level.

attacks.issue: Proxy triple is cherry-picked from ~20 features with non-zero standardized deltas
attacks.why_it_matters: The contrast table lists 20+ features with |std delta| between 0.10 and 1.19. The researcher elevates three and dismisses Lane as redundant, but ignores ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (-0.70), px_vs_ma50 (-0.85), pullback_pct (+0.64), ma20_slope_5 (-0.60), ibd_entry_volume_ratio (-0.50), and ibd_entry_close_position (-0.46). A 'pure proxy' claim must explain away ALL residual axes, not just three. If Lane correlates with even one of these (e.g., ibd_entry_close_position, which is geometric and not in the triple), the proxy hypothesis is already falsified.

attacks.issue: Sample labels are noisy: entity_6618d3e80c is dual-labeled 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner'
attacks.why_it_matters: A single case is simultaneously a selected winner AND a ruin flag. This single contradiction shows the outcome taxonomy has overlap and noise that contaminates the proxy analysis. The proxies (mom_20=0.25, px_vs_ma50=0.34, up_day_ratio_20=0.55) for entity_6618d3e80c look unambiguously like a winner — yet it was ruined. If the proxies can't discriminate within their top decile even when labeled 'winner', the proxy hypothesis is undermined at its own ground truth.

attacks.issue: Lane is never defined operationally in the prior output
attacks.why_it_matters: Without a definition of B0_LANE, LANE_NEUTRAL, and SCORE_BEFORE_LANE, the falsifiable predictions are vacuous. 'Lane' could mean IBD Breakout Lane grade, supply/demand count, or a proprietary composite. If it includes any factor not in {up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20} — even something as simple as 'close in upper third of day's range' or 'distribution days in prior 5 sessions' — the proxy hypothesis is false by construction. The prior role assumed Lane = momentum recoding without evidence.

attacks.issue: Mechanism vs portfolio confound: Lane may not improve edge but reduce variance, improve exit discipline, or improve sizing
attacks.why_it_matters: Even if W4 returns for matched B0_LANE vs LANE_NEUTRAL triples are within 1pp on average, Lane might still be economically valuable by shifting the distribution (lower left tail, fewer ruin cases). The prior predictions ignore distributional shape and rely on mean W4 gaps. The eight false_positive_ruin cases suggest ruin is the binding constraint — not mean return — and the prior role's mean-only test cannot detect a Lane benefit that operates through ruin suppression.

counterexamples_to_seek: B0_LANE rows with low up_day_ratio_20 (<0.45) AND low vol_ratio_5_20 (<1.1) AND modest mom_20 (<0.10) that nonetheless produce large_win W4 outcomes — these cases would be winners the proxy composite would have rejected, demonstrating Lane adds information the proxies cannot.

LANE_NEUTRAL rows with up_day_ratio_20 >0.65, vol_ratio_5_20 >1.5, AND mom_20 >0.15 that produced ruin or loss — these are proxy-confident failures that show the proxies over-promise and Lane-neutral flags correctly reject them.

Within the snap_71486ed83c cluster (the densest in the sample), identify any triple of B0_LANE / LANE_NEUTRAL / SCORE_BEFORE_LANE cases matched on up_day_ratio_20±0.05, vol_ratio_5_20±0.10, mom_20±0.05 whose W4 outcomes diverge by >3pp — even a handful of these refutes the proxy hypothesis and the prior role's P1 directly.

Cases where ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct is small (<0.02) but Lane is favorable AND mom_20 is large (>0.20) — if these win while identical-feature cases with low Lane lose, Lane is encoding freshness-entry precision the proxy triple misses.

Entity_6618d3e80c analogues: cases where the proxies say 'clear winner' but the outcome was ruin or loss — count these and compare B0_LANE vs LANE_NEUTRAL prevalence; if they concentrate in LANE_NEUTRAL, Lane is suppressing proxy-blind ruin, not redundant with proxies.

Entity-level time-series check: for each entity with multiple snapshots, observe whether Lane bin assignment flips while proxies stay constant — these are within-stock matched cases that bypass cross-sectional confounding and directly test whether Lane changes the call relative to the proxy triple.
