The researcher and designer identified that the false_positive_ruin cluster sits in high-mom regimes (mom_20 ≈ 0.15–0.23), so a momentum-conditional gate concentrates the penalty where the mechanism is most plausible and avoids penalizing names where the interaction may not exist.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Neutral; momentum gating narrows where the penalty applies, not what is eligible.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: outcome_channel_separated_eval: instead of a single W4-return-bucket target, evaluate any chase penalty on three separate outcome channels (w4_return, max_drawdown_to_w4, pullback_pct) and require the penalty to improve at least two of three before activation.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Addresses the label-construction critique (W4 ≠ ruin protection) by making the multi-channel evaluation explicit. A penalty that helps W4 but hurts drawdown protection should not activate, and vice versa.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Neutral; changes evaluation, not eligibility.

cycles.question: Explore a conditional ranking plus adaptive capacity using ibd_entry_close_position and ibd_entry_volume_ratio. Explain the mechanism, likely failure regime, and how to encode it without expanding the B0 eligible universe.

researcher.mechanism_claim: ibd_entry_close_position and ibd_entry_volume_ratio jointly measure breakout conviction: a close in the upper portion of the day's range confirms that buyers defended the breakout, while a volume ratio >1 confirms participation rather than thin-air drift. When the two agree (high-high), the B0 candidate is a real institutional accumulation pivot and earns full adaptive capacity; when they disagree (one high, one low), the breakout is fragile (thin breakout or distribution) and should receive a reduced or zero position even though it passes the B0 filter. Encoding this preserves the eligible universe but re-weights exposure by cross-sectional conviction rank, so marginal B0 picks degrade gracefully instead of being hard-rejected.
evidence_for: Numeric contrasts show false_negative medians trail selected_winner medians on both features (close_position delta -0.039, volume_ratio delta -0.215), and standardized deltas are among the larger moves (close_position std=-0.46, volume_ratio std=-0.50), consistent with the joint signal discriminating survivors from misses.

False-positive ruin cases cluster where close_vs_trigger_pct is elevated (0.06-0.07) but vol_ratio_5_20 sits only mid-pack (~1.2-1.6) with up_day_ratio often ≤0.5 (entity_84824e6a20 up_day=0.4, entity_b6bcccdf6a up_day=0.4) — i.e. price pushed to trigger on weak/contradictory tape.

Selected winners with very high close_vs_trigger and very high vol_ratio_5_20 (entity_b00579f203: 0.0465/1.58, entity_ead73f4390: 0.0017/1.77, entity_2c58cebc59: 0.034/1.62) correspond to large_win buckets, supporting the high-high = full-capacity hypothesis.
evidence_against: entity_6618d3e80c is dual-labeled selected_winner|false_positive_ruin with a high volume_ratio (1.45) and strong px_vs_ma50 (33.7%), showing the high-high combination is not sufficient when downstream drawdown control is missing — adaptive capacity can shrink ruin magnitude but cannot fully prevent it under distribution regimes.

entity_55c2da490e and entity_40ea0cfb3b are ruins with relatively low close_vs_trigger (0.028, 0.061) yet still destroyed; ruin is achievable from sub-trigger-grade entries, so the rule must not over-trust mid-range close_position as safe.

False-negative cases (entity_de1c657364, entity_535a1beed7) sometimes carry decent up_day_ratio (0.5-0.65) but low vol_ratio_5_20 (1.15-1.17), indicating that absent volume confirmation, B0 currently filters them out — the same feature that causes FNs can be repurposed for capacity rather than eligibility without changing the universe.
falsifiable_predictions: Among B0-eligible picks, those with close_position > 0.85 AND volume_ratio > 1.5 (top-tertile of a composite conviction rank) will realize W4 returns above the cross-sectional median of B0 picks at a hit rate materially higher than picks satisfying only one of the two thresholds.

Reducing position size to ~50% on picks where the two features disagree (high-low or low-high) will shrink aggregate ruin rate (large_loss + ruin bucket frequency) more than it shrinks aggregate large_win rate, i.e. the convexity of the payoff improves without shrinking upside participation.

In regime slices where up_day_ratio_20 < 0.5 at entry, the high-high conviction subset will still underperform its in-regime baseline because the close/volume joint signal does not substitute for trend quality; capacity rule should be gated by trend filter rather than applied unconditionally.
policy_implications: Encode a conviction score = zscore(close_position) + zscore(volume_ratio) computed on the B0-eligible cross-section only, then map to a position scalar (e.g. 0x below threshold, 0.5x when one leg passes, 1.0-1.25x when both pass) so the eligible universe is unchanged but capital is concentrated where buyers and participation agree.

Add a regime gate: when 5-day MA10 slope or 20-day up_day_ratio falls below the cross-sectional median, clip the conviction scalar to 1.0 so adaptive capacity does not amplify exposure in deteriorating tape.

Track capacity-adjusted W4 outcomes by conviction bucket to validate whether the high-high bucket earns a convexity premium; if not, collapse to a binary eligibility gate rather than continuous sizing.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: ibd_entry_close_position and ibd_entry_volume_ratio are contemporaneous, mutually-redundant proxies for 'it was a strong breakout day.' They do not encode institutional accumulation versus thin-air drift in any way that survives extension, regime, or post-decision path; the high-high subset in the archaeology is dominated by extended-price blowoffs that the dual-labeled entity_6618d3e80c (and the ruin cases entity_84824e6a20 and entity_ccc90a671f, both with close>0.07 and vol_ratio>1.4) make explicit. The proposed encoding is therefore a sizing rule that concentrates capital on the most extended, most overbought B0 picks exactly when ruin risk is highest; 'adaptive capacity' here is structurally anti-adaptive.

attacks.issue: Redundancy / proxy substitution: close_position and volume_ratio are not orthogonal. Both spike on the same breakout session. The joint standardized deltas vs selected winners are only -0.46 and -0.50, far weaker than up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), or mom_20 (-1.00). Adding two weak, collinear signals does not recover what stronger trend features already encode; this is a textbook case of redundant feature stacking.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the high-high subset is just a re-weighted subset of 'already-momentum-extended names,' then the position-sizing rule is not adding conviction differentiation, it is amplifying exposure on extended entries. This inverts the intended convexity improvement.

attacks.issue: Direct counterexample to the high-high = safe mechanism: entity_84824e6a20 has the highest close (0.074) and very high volume_ratio (1.63) in the archaeology — by the researcher's own metric this is the highest-conviction B0 pick — and it is a ruin. entity_ccc90a671f (close 0.070, vol 1.45) is also ruin. entity_8f0df3d38e (close 0.069, vol 1.24) is ruin. The 'institutional accumulation' interpretation collapses under these cases.
attacks.why_it_matters: These are not edge cases; they sit at the extreme of the proposed conviction distribution. If the researcher's encoding sizes UP here, ruin magnitude increases proportionally. The mechanism predicts the opposite of what the evidence shows for the top of the proposed ranking.

attacks.issue: Snapshot clustering: snap_71486ed83c alone contributes at least 5 of the 27 cases, and snap_d0d57b1e40 and snap_b8420124eb each contribute multiple. Within a snapshot, close_position and volume_ratio share common regime drivers (single-session tape direction, single-day breadth). Any 'joint signal' is partially a snapshot-id confound masquerading as a feature.
attacks.why_it_matters: Cross-sectional rank within a snapshot is not the same as cross-sectional rank across snapshots. A high-high conviction rank computed on the full B0 universe pools regimes where volume has opposite meaning (climactic accumulation vs climactic distribution). Without snapshot-stratified evaluation the within-B0 ranking is partly noise.

attacks.issue: Capacity ≠ alpha: even if high-high wins more often than low-high, sizing up after the breakout day means paying the full premium. The archaeology is computed at the IBD entry snapshot, which already incorporates the breakout move. Adaptive sizing into extended entries is a classic late-stage momentum trap, especially in cases like entity_6618d3e80c (px_vs_ma50 = 33.7%) and entity_b6bcccdf6a (px_vs_ma50 = 18.2%) where the breakout is layered on already-extended structure.
attacks.why_it_matters: Sizing rules have a separate failure mode from eligibility: they improve Sharpe when payoff is convex in the signal, but worsen it when ruin risk is also convex in the signal. Here ruin risk appears to rise with the same conviction rank as the upside, which is the worst case for the proposed scaling.

attacks.issue: Dual-label entity_6618d3e80c explicitly shows that high conviction does not resolve dual-path outcomes: a high-close, high-volume, strong-trend B0 pick realized BOTH selected_winner and false_positive_ruin. A continuous position scalar assumes a single latent quality; the evidence is consistent with branching outcomes (win or ruin with comparable probability) at the top of the ranking.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the best B0 picks have binary outcomes rather than graded ones, the right policy is binary (full or skip), and shrinking position size on 'disagreement' picks does nothing to address the dominant risk.

counterexamples_to_seek: Within snap_71486ed83c, snap_d0d57b1e40, and snap_b8420124eb, compute the high-high vs low-low ruin rate difference to determine whether the joint signal discriminates within a fixed regime or merely reflects snapshot-level differences.

Re-rank B0 picks by close+volume conviction after conditioning on px_vs_ma50 (extension) and on ma20_slope_5 (trend). If the high-high conviction premium disappears inside these strata, the proposed encoding is just a proxy for 'extended momentum'.

Identify any selected_winner with both close_position > 0.85 AND volume_ratio > 1.5 that subsequently had a meaningful pullback (e.g., pullback_pct worse than -15%). entity_2c58cebc59 (close 0.034, vol 1.62, pullback_pct = -25.1%) is a candidate — verify whether high conviction coexists with deep drawdowns even on winners.

Check whether false_positive_ruin cases systematically have HIGHER close_position than selected_winners. If ruins dominate the upper tail of close_position (as entity_84824e6a20 and entity_ccc90a671f suggest), the proposed rank is mis-specified: highest conviction = highest ruin probability.
what_would_change_my_mind: Stratified-by-snapshot ruin frequencies in which the high-high bucket has materially lower ruin incidence than the low-low bucket across at least three different snapshots, with n >= 10 per cell.

Demonstration that the high-high conviction premium survives controlling for px_vs_ma50 and ma20_slope_5 (i.e., is not pure extension / pure trend), with effect size that exceeds the strongest single-feature alternative (up_day_ratio_20 alone).

Out-of-sample evidence where the conviction score is computed BEFORE the breakout completes (e.g., using prior-day close_position and volume_ratio) and still predicts W4 outcomes — currently the evidence is purely contemporaneous, which is contaminated with the post-breakout move itself.
A payoff-convexity diagnostic showing that ruin rate decreases faster than large_win rate as the conviction score rises; without this, scaling up the high-high bucket is unjustified.

tests.name: Within-snapshot_ruin_isolation
tests.comparison: Restrict to snapshots with n>=8 B0-eligible picks. Within each such snapshot, rank picks by a composite conviction score = zscore(close_position)+zscore(volume_ratio) computed strictly within the snapshot's B0 cross-section. Compare the top tercile (high-high) vs bottom tercile (low-low) ruin incidence (large_loss + ruin bucket frequency). Pooled-snapshot comparison is NOT used.
tests.success_criterion: Across at least three qualifying snapshots, the within-snapshot top-tercile has a ruin rate at least 30% lower than the within-snapshot bottom-tercile (relative reduction), AND this sign is consistent (no snapshot where bottom tercile outperforms top tercile by more than noise).
tests.failure_criterion: In >=2 of the qualifying snapshots, the top tercile ruin rate is equal to or higher than the bottom tercile, OR the effect reverses sign within snapshot (i.e., the joint signal is a cross-snapshot proxy rather than a within-regime discriminator). If snapshot-level sample sizes are insufficient, mark UNRESOLVED.

tests.name: Extension_and_trend_stratified_premium
tests.comparison: Bin B0 picks by px_vs_ma50 tercile (low/medium/high extension) AND by ma20_slope_5 tercile (weak/medium/strong trend) forming a 3x3 strata grid. Within each cell with n>=5, test whether high-high conviction (close_position > snapshot median AND volume_ratio > snapshot median) still earns a positive W4-return spread vs the low-low counterpart. Compare the size of this within-cell spread to the unconditional pooled spread.
tests.success_criterion: At least 4 of 9 cells with n>=5 show a positive high-high minus low-low W4 spread, AND the median within-cell spread is >=50% of the pooled spread (i.e., the joint signal retains meaningful information after stripping extension and trend).
tests.failure_criterion: In >=6 of 9 cells the within-cell spread is zero or negative, OR the within-cell median spread is <25% of the pooled spread. This indicates the joint signal is mostly a proxy for 'already-extended-momentum' and the encoding is anti-adaptive.

tests.name: Convexity_diagnostic_ruin_vs_win_gradient
tests.comparison: Rank all B0 picks by the composite conviction score into 5 quintiles. For each quintile compute (a) large_win hit rate, (b) ruin hit rate (ruin+large_loss). Plot ruin_rate(q) vs large_win_rate(q). Fit a Spearman rank correlation between quintile index and ruin rate, and separately between quintile index and large_win rate. The PAYOFF CONVEXITY criterion requires ruin rate to fall with quintile AT LEAST AS FAST as large_win rate falls (or rise).
tests.success_criterion: Spearman(quintile, ruin_rate) <= -0.5 AND Spearman(quintile, ruin_rate) <= Spearman(quintile, large_win_rate) (ruin declines at least as steeply as upside). The minimum between (large_win_rate Q5 - large_win_rate Q1) and (ruin_rate Q1 - ruin_rate Q5) must be positive and the ruin differential must be >=50% of the upside differential.
tests.failure_criterion: Spearman(quintile, ruin_rate) > 0 (ruin rate RISES with conviction), OR ruin_rate Q5 >= ruin_rate Q1, OR the ruin differential is <25% of the upside differential. Any of these means scaling UP the high-high bucket worsens aggregate ruin magnitude more than it gains upside — the policy is structurally anti-adaptive regardless of overall hit rate.

tests.name: Three_slot_encoding_head_to_head
tests.comparison: Implement three 3-slot sizing encodings on the same B0 universe and compare aggregate risk-adjusted outcomes WITHOUT changing eligibility: (Encoding A) Researcher's proposal — 0x / 0.5x / 1.0-1.25x slots keyed on the composite conviction score, gated by ma10_slope_5 and up_day_ratio_20 regime filter (clip to 1.0x when regime weak). (Encoding B) Pure binary — 0x for non-high-high, 1.0x for high-high (no continuous scaling). (Encoding C) Equal-weight 1.0x for all B0 picks (capacity-control baseline). Compute ruin-burden per unit of large-win upside for each.
tests.success_criterion: Encoding A produces a ruin-burden-per-upside ratio that is at least 15% lower than both Encoding B and Encoding C, while preserving >=85% of Encoding C's large-win capture. This demonstrates the continuous scaling genuinely adds convexity beyond a binary rule.
tests.failure_criterion: Encoding A's ruin-burden-per-upside is NOT meaningfully lower than Encoding C (equal-weight baseline), OR Encoding B (binary) is statistically indistinguishable from or superior to Encoding A. This means the 3-slot structure adds complexity without convexity improvement; collapse to the better of binary-or-equal.

tests.name: Disagreement_leg_attribution
tests.comparison: Within B0 picks, isolate the two disagreement quadrants: (Q2) high-close / low-volume and (Q3) low-close / high-volume, defined relative to within-snapshot medians. Compute ruin rate of Q2, Q3, and compare to (Q1) low-low and (Q4) high-high. Test whether one disagreement leg carries the ruin signal disproportionately.
tests.success_criterion: Exactly one disagreement quadrant (Q2 or Q3) has ruin rate materially elevated above Q1, AND the high-high quadrant has ruin rate <= both disagreement quadrants. This identifies which leg is the real discriminant and whether the joint rule is parsimonious.
tests.failure_criterion: BOTH disagreement quadrants have ruin rates >= Q1 (ruin distributed across all non-high-high picks, so the 0.5x slot is over-broad), OR Q4 ruin rate is >= either disagreement quadrant (high-high does not improve over disagreement, collapsing the 3-slot to a 2-slot rule).

tests.name: Regime_gate_effectiveness
tests.comparison: Partition B0 picks by whether up_day_ratio_20 is below the in-snapshot median ('weak-tape' regime). Within the weak-tape regime, compare Encoding A (with the regime gate clipping capacity to 1.0x) vs Encoding A without the gate (unconditionally scaling). Measure ruin-burden-per-upside in the weak-tape subset.
tests.success_criterion: The regime-gated version reduces ruin-burden-per-upside in the weak-tape subset by >=20% relative to the un-gated version without reducing large-win capture by more than 10%. Demonstrates the gate prevents capacity amplification specifically where the joint signal is least reliable.
tests.failure_criterion: The gate provides <10% reduction in ruin-burden-per-upside, OR it costs >15% large-win capture, OR the weak-tape subset is too small (n<10) to support inference — in the latter case mark UNRESOLVED rather than confirming the gate.

leakage_checks: Confirm ibd_entry_close_position and ibd_entry_volume_ratio are computed using only data available at the IBD entry snapshot timestamp (intraday or close-of-day). Reject any test where the close_position uses post-entry window data.

Confirm pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, base_depth_pct, base_duration_weeks, and base_mbox_count are NEVER used as predictive features — these are path/outcome descriptors and would constitute look-ahead even if pre-breakout in name.
Confirm snapshot_anon is used ONLY as a stratification/blocking variable, never as a direct predictive feature or proxy.

Confirm the composite conviction score (zscore close_position + zscore volume_ratio) is recomputed within the B0-eligible cross-section and within each snapshot for stratified tests — never pooled across regimes.
Confirm no outer-forward W4, W8, or beyond-snapshot-window outcomes enter the training signal. W4 from the archaeology snapshot is admissible only as an evaluation target, never as a feature.

Confirm 3-slot accounting is preserved exactly: tests may not introduce a 4th or 5th position-size bucket under any encoding, and the eligible B0 universe must remain identical across Encoding A, B, and C comparisons.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: ibd_entry_close_position and ibd_entry_volume_ratio carry a modest median-level discriminant (FN medians trail selected-winner medians by z=-0.46 and z=-0.50), but the archaeology fails to confirm tail separation: three of the four highest close_position ruins sit at extreme high values (entity_84824e6a20 close=0.074 vol=1.63; entity_ccc90a671f close=0.070 vol=1.45; entity_8f0df3d38e close=0.069 vol=1.24) and entity_6618d3e80c is dual-labeled winner+ruin at close=0.051 vol=1.45. Both standardized deltas are markedly weaker than up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), and mom_20 (-1.00) — features already implicit in the regime context. The joint signal behaves as a partial proxy for 'breakout-on-strong-tape day' that splits the B0 mass around the median but does NOT identify the upper tail as safe; ruin and large_win rates both appear to rise with conviction (convex-in-both-directions), so scaling UP into the high-high bucket amplifies ruin magnitude at least as fast as upside. The defensible reading is: the joint signal is a DAMPER against low-low and disagreement-leg picks, not an AMPLIFIER into high-high. Regime/snapshot stratification is mandatory because most of the evidence clusters in 3 of the visible snapshots (snap_71486ed83c, snap_d0d57b1e40, snap_b8420124eb) and a snapshot-level cross-sectional rank pools climactic-accumulation with climactic-distribution regimes. Net: the proposed continuous encoding (0x/0.5x/1.0-1.25x) is not warranted by the evidence; a strictly bounded binary-ish sizing (0.5x or 1.0x, never above) is the most that the evidence supports, and only with a regime gate and an extension partial-out.
falsifiers: Within snap_71486ed83c, snap_d0d57b1e40, or snap_b8420124eb, the within-snapshot top-tercile (z-close + z-vol, computed inside the snapshot's B0 cross-section) shows ruin rate >= bottom-tercile ruin rate OR sign reversal across two of three snapshots — refutes the within-regime discriminant and reduces the encoding to a snapshot-id proxy.

Spearman(quintile, ruin_rate) over composite-conviction quintiles is > 0 (ruin RISES with conviction), OR ruin_rate(Q5) >= ruin_rate(Q1), OR the ruin differential across quintiles is less than 25% of the upside differential — refutes any convexity claim and indicates scaling up amplifies ruin more than upside.

In the 3x3 px_vs_ma50 × ma20_slope_5 strata grid, fewer than 4 of 9 cells with n>=5 show positive high-high minus low-low W4 spread, OR median within-cell spread is <50% of the pooled spread — refutes the signal's informativeness after stripping the extension/trend confound.

Encoding A (researcher's 0/0.5/1.0-1.25x with regime gate) fails to achieve a ruin-burden-per-upside at least 15% lower than Encoding C (equal-weight 1.0x) while preserving >=85% of Encoding C's large-win capture; OR Encoding B (binary 0/1.0x) is statistically indistinguishable from or superior to Encoding A — refutes the value of continuous-vs-binary scaling and collapses the encoding to a simpler rule.

Among selected_winners with close_position > 0.85 AND volume_ratio > 1.5, pullback_pct worse than -15% occurs in >=50% of cases (entity_2c58cebc59 already qualifies at -25.1%) — refutes the 'high-high = reduced path risk' interpretation and supports a binary-or-skip conclusion.

After partialing out px_vs_ma50 and ma20_slope_5, the residual rank of close+volume no longer correlates with W4 bucket (Spearman |rho|<0.1 or ruin rate differential collapses to within noise) — confirms the joint signal is a proxy for extension/trend, not an independent conviction axis.

In the weak-tape subset (up_day_ratio_20 < in-snapshot median) the regime gate provides <10% reduction in ruin-burden-per-upside OR costs >15% large-win capture — weakens (does not necessarily refute) the gate, but if combined with weak-tape sample n<10, mark the gate UNRESOLVED.
actionable_design_principles: Do not adopt the researcher's 1.0-1.25x upper slot. Cap adaptive capacity at 1.0x regardless of conviction. The continuous-up direction is contradicted by the upper-tail counterexamples (entity_84824e6a20, entity_ccc90a671f, entity_8f0df3d38e) where highest conviction co-occurs with ruin.

Read the joint signal as a DEFENSIVE damper (downscale disagreement and low-low picks toward 0.5x) rather than as an OFFENSIVE amplifier (upscale high-high picks above 1.0x). This is the only direction the evidence supports without overfitting on 27 cases.

Compute the conviction score strictly WITHIN each snapshot's B0-eligible cross-section (no pooling across snapshots). Pooling biases the rank toward snapshot-id because the visible evidence clusters in snap_71486ed83c, snap_d0d57b1e40, and snap_b8420124eb.

Require Encoding A, B, and C head-to-head comparison before adopting any scaling. Encoding C (equal-weight) is the explicit control — if it is statistically indistinguishable from A or B in ruin-burden-per-upside, the simplest rule wins (Occam).

Lock the eligible B0 universe across all three encodings. Adaptive capacity MUST come from within-universe re-weighting; the research question explicitly forbids eligibility expansion, and the contrast test mechanically enforces that.

Never use pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, base_depth_pct, base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, snapshot_anon-as-feature, or forward W4/W8 outcomes as predictive inputs. They are path descriptors or evaluation targets and would constitute look-ahead leakage even if renamed.

Treat entity_6618d3e80c (dual selected_winner | false_positive_ruin at high conv+strong trend) as a structural reference case: it shows that even a confluence of close+volume+trend can produce BOTH outcomes, so the policy must not assume graded underlying quality at the top of the rank.

If the convexity diagnostic (Spearman quintile-ranks) returns rho(ruin) > 0 OR rho(ruin) > rho(large_win), DO NOT scale up — instead collapse the proposal to binary or equal-weight and document the failure mode.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Within-snapshot conviction damper (no upscale)
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Restricts the composite conviction score to B0 within each snapshot_anon and applies ONLY a downward damper (0.5x on disagreement, 1.0x elsewhere). Distinct from researcher's proposal because it caps the upper slot at 1.0x and removes the 1.0-1.25x band, which the upper-tail counterexamples make unjustifiable. Preserves the eligible universe and 3-slot structure without crossing the safety line.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Adaptive capacity DOWN only — reduces position size when the two conviction legs disagree, leaves exposure unchanged when they agree. Avoids amplifying ruin magnitude at the top of the conviction rank.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Disagreement-leg explicit demotion with hard 0.5x floor
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Tags a pick as disagreement when close_position and volume_ratio are on opposite sides of the within-snapshot median, and forces capacity = 0.5x regardless of any other composite score. Distinct from a smooth z-sum because it makes the 'one leg fails' condition an explicit categorical event rather than a continuous penalty. Testable directly by the Disagreement_leg_attribution comparison.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Caps disagreement picks at half-size, isolating which leg carries the ruin signal. If ruin concentrates in only one disagreement quadrant, this rule alone may suffice and the continuous upscale can be dropped entirely.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Regime-bounded scaling with 1.0x ceiling in weak tape
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Adds a regime filter keyed on up_day_ratio_20 and ma10_slope_5 medians. Distinct from unconditional scaling because any encoding that would yield >1.0x is clipped to 1.0x inside the weak-tape subset. Direct counterweight to the snapshot-level confound where close+volume may signal opposite things under different breadth conditions.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents adaptive capacity from compounding in deteriorating tape. Without this gate, the conditional cross-sectional scaling amplifies exposure exactly where it is least reliable.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Extension partial-out conditioning before conviction scoring
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Regresses close_position and volume_ratio on px_vs_ma50 and ma20_slope_5 within snapshot, then computes conviction score from residuals. Distinct from raw z-sum because it strips the dominant trend/extension component that is already redundant with features the B0 filter and regime context already capture. Directly addresses the standardized-delta weakness (only -0.46/-0.50 vs -1.19/-1.05/-1.00 for the underlying trend features).
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: If the residual conviction still earns a convexity premium, the signal is genuinely incremental and scaling is justified; if the residual does nothing, the researcher is invited to drop the encoding entirely rather than persist with a redundant proxy.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Ruin-burden-per-upside diagnostic as a guardrail metric
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Defines a composite metric ruin_burden_per_upside = (weighted_ruin_loss) / (large_win_capture) computed within-snapshot and pooled across snapshots with snapshot-as-random-effect. Encodes the policy-level question — does the encoding buy more upside than ruin? — directly into the DSL evaluation. Distinct from raw hit-rate metrics because it penalizes ruin magnitude, not just ruin frequency, and tracks the convexity-criterion that the standard hit-rate approach misses.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Provides the explicit objective function for evaluating any capacity scaling proposal. A policy that does not reduce ruin-burden-per-upside relative to Encoding C (equal-weight baseline) cannot be justified by hit-rate gains alone.

cycles.question: Adversarially attack the apparent industry-allocation advantage: construct the strongest alternative explanation. Prefer a concrete diagnostic over generic caution.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The apparent industry-allocation advantage is not an industry effect; it is a proxy for a momentum-stage/regime factor that the IBD-style B0 selection already concentrates on, but does not adequately filter. Industry tag is downstream of the underlying features (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5) that actually differentiate winners from ruins and false negatives in the failure archaeology. Any marginal return attributed to 'industry' should vanish once those features are properly controlled or matched.
evidence_for: The largest standardized deltas separating false_negative_relative from selected_winner are feature deltas, not industry: up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19σ, median 0.50 vs 0.625), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05σ, 1.179 vs 1.424), mom_20 (-1.00σ, 0.058 vs 0.163), px_vs_ma50 (-0.85σ, 0.056 vs 0.127). These are momentum/quality signals, not sector labels.

Selected_winner and false_positive_ruin cases share 'extended late-stage entry' signatures that are sector-agnostic: e.g., entity_6618d3e80c (winner) and entity_4fdc3699fd (ruin) both have ma10_slope_5 ~ 0.075–0.090 and px_vs_ma50 > 0.10; entity_b6bcccdf6a (ruin) and entity_2c58cebc59 (winner) both have ma10_slope_5 in 0.013–0.067 and strong mom_20. The discriminator is not industry — it is entry tightness and momentum maturity.

Pullback features (pullback_duration_weeks median 5.5 vs 4.0; pullback_pct -15.9 vs -7.3) differentiate winners from false negatives but are stock-specific base characteristics, not industry-typical. Industry cannot explain why one stock with a deeper, longer base works and another does not.

Cases cluster by snapshot_anon (e.g., snap_71486ed83c contributes 6 of 27 archaeology rows, snap_d0d57b1e40 contributes 4). Snapshot-tagged clustering is consistent with a regime/timing explanation rather than a structural industry explanation.

B0 selection (is_b0_pick=true) is itself a filter that, by construction, over-samples names in momentum-confirmed leadership; leadership names cluster in 1–3 sectors per regime, so any portfolio factor correlated with leadership will look like an industry effect.

False positives with steep ma10_slope_5 and high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (e.g., entity_8f0df3d38e: ma10_slope_5=0.054, ibd_entry gap=6.85%; entity_84824e6a20: ma10_slope_5=0.062, gap=7.38%) are textbook 'buying the 8th inning of momentum' failures — a timing failure mode that operates identically across sectors.
evidence_against: The numeric_contrasts table is truncated, so I cannot verify whether any sector-level feature was even recorded or tested in this archaeology; the case-level features available are all sector-agnostic, which is silent rather than disconfirming on industry per se.

It is possible (not demonstrated in this evidence) that certain industries systematically exhibit different distributions of the discriminating features (e.g., biotech having lower up_day_ratio_20), in which case 'industry' would be a valid coarse-grained feature even if reducible to its constituents — falsification must come from the matched-pair test below, not from armchair reasoning.

The 11 selected_winners include some with extreme strength (entity_ead73f4390: mom_20=0.32, px_vs_ma50=0.185) that could in principle be sector-tagged in ways the truncated feature table hides; the visible evidence is consistent with but does not exhaust the possibility of an industry residual.

Snapshot concentration could alternatively indicate a structural shift in industry leadership that was correctly captured, rather than a regime artifact — distinguishing these requires the time-stability test, which the frozen evidence does not contain.
falsifiable_predictions: Matched-pair sector test: within a (mom_20 quintile × vol_ratio_5_20 quintile × ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct quintile × up_day_ratio_20 quintile) bucket, the W4 return difference between B0-pick industry A and B0-pick industry B will have |t| < 1.0 and a sign inconsistent across buckets. If industry is the true driver, the sign should be stable across buckets.

Sector HHI of B0 winners minus sector HHI of B0 ruins should be near zero in any single snapshot_anon bucket; the cross-snapshot variation in sector concentration will explain more W4 return variance than any sector dummy in a within-snapshot regression.

Adding sector fixed effects to a regression of W4 return on (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5) will increase adjusted R^2 by less than 2 percentage points; without the features, sector dummies will look powerful (the trap to avoid).

A sector-neutralized portfolio that matches each B0 winner on (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20) will retain ≥ 80% of the un-neutralized W4 alpha, and the residual 20% will be concentrated in 1–2 calendar quarters rather than spread across the sample.

Replacing the 'industry tilt' with a 'momentum-stage penalty' rule (down-weight or skip names where ma10_slope_5 > 0.05 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05) will reduce the false_positive_ruin rate by more than re-weighting toward any single industry.
policy_implications: Remove explicit industry tilts from allocation and replace them with explicit controls on the features that the archaeology actually flags: up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5.

Add a momentum-stage filter (penalize or skip when steep ma10_slope_5 is combined with extended ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) — this directly attacks the largest false_positive_ruin signature without invoking industry.

Tag every pick with snapshot_anon / macro-regime and report performance stratified by regime before reporting industry-stratified performance; if regime explains the spread, industry is a label, not a lever.
Run the matched-pair sector test as the gating diagnostic: do not allocate by industry unless the test shows |t| > 2 stable across at least three non-overlapping time windows.

If industry is retained as a soft prior, cap its weight and require that the industry tilt be justified by a documented, feature-reducible mechanism (e.g., 'biotech systematically shows lower up_day_ratio_20, so we tilt to balance the missing signal') rather than by raw sector return differentials.

UNRESOLVED on whether a residual industry effect exists once features are properly controlled; the frozen evidence does not contain a sector field, so the falsification must be carried out in a downstream diagnostic rather than asserted from this archaeology.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The prior researcher treats the seven discriminating features (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5) as primitive, but these features are computed from price series whose noise structure is itself industry-conditioned (event-driven binary-catalyst sectors vs. commodity/rate-sensitive sectors). Quintile-matching on features matches rank within a pooled, industry-contaminated distribution, not the underlying risk exposure — meaning the matched-pair diagnostic is mathematically incapable of distinguishing 'no industry effect' from 'industry effect that has already been absorbed into the quintile boundaries.' The proposed falsification test therefore cannot falsify the original industry claim; it can only confirm a tautology.

attacks.issue: Feature endogeneity under industry conditioning invalidates the matched-pair design.
attacks.why_it_matters: Two stocks assigned to 'mom_20 quintile 4' may sit there for entirely different absolute reasons — a biotech recovering from a -80% binary drawdown and a staples name grinding up 5% both rank high, but their forward variance, catalyst path, and base-rate of regime shift are categorically different. Quintile matching on a feature whose distribution is industry-shifted is not neutralization; it is partial double-counting. A null result from the proposed test therefore proves nothing about industry.

attacks.issue: The archaeology sample (n=27, 5 outcome labels, multiple snapshot_anon strata) is wildly underpowered for any sector-stratified inference; a null is uninformative rather than confirmatory.
attacks.why_it_matters: Splitting 27 cases across likely 5+ GICS sectors leaves 3-6 observations per cell. A 3pp W4 difference in that regime has a confidence interval easily spanning ±15pp. The researcher proposes |t|<1.0 as the bar, but the realized power to detect a 5pp industry effect at α=0.05 is under 15%. Citing a null here as evidence 'industry is a label, not a lever' inverts the proper statistical reading.

attacks.issue: The argument confuses a portfolio-construction effect (factor exposure that happens to load on industry) with a predictive mechanism.
attacks.why_it_matters: Even if 'industry tilt' is reproducible, removing it without replacing it with an equivalent factor exposure (e.g., explicit value/growth/size/momentum tilts that survive the within-quintile matching) will degrade realized alpha purely as a portfolio-construction artifact. The policy to 'remove industry tilts and replace with feature controls' assumes the features are orthogonal to the factor the industry tilt was harvesting — which is exactly the assumption the endogeneity attack above denies.

counterexamples_to_seek: Within the archaeology, find a 'selected_winner' from an industry whose feature baselines are structurally low (e.g., biotech or small-cap medical) that nonetheless wins with below-median mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 — this falsifies 'features alone drive outcomes' and re-opens industry as a residual.

Find a 'false_positive_ruin' from a sector where comparable feature readings (matched on the seven-feature vector) typically win — a single such case breaks the within-quintile invariance that the prior researcher's mechanism relies on.
what_would_change_my_mind: A within-quintile matched-pair test using ABSOLUTE (not rank) feature thresholds — e.g., pair only on mom_20 within ±0.05 absolute, not within the same quintile — with at least 50 pairs spanning ≥4 sectors and showing industry dummies add <1pp to R^2 after the seven-feature set. The quintile-based version proposed by the researcher would not move me, for the reasons above.

A feature-decomposition showing that the seven discriminating variables are themselves industry-invariant in second moments (variance, skew, autocorrelation structure of residuals) across at least 4 sectors. Without this, feature-controlling remains industry-confounded.

tests.name: Absolute-feature near-twin discordance test
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot_anon bucket, pair observations whose absolute feature vectors are near-identical: |Δmom_20|≤0.05 AND |Δma10_slope_5|≤0.01 AND |Δibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct|≤0.02 (with up_day_ratio_20 and px_vs_ma50 reported as covariates, not gating). For each near-twin pair, record whether outcome_label is concordant (both selected_winner, both false_positive_ruin, etc.) or discordant. Aggregate discordance rate across all snapshot_anon strata and tabulate discordance pattern by feature-residual gap (the residual vector in the four non-gating features).
tests.success_criterion: Near-twin concordance ≥80% across all snapshot_anon strata, and the residual feature vector in discordant pairs does not exhibit a coherent non-gating signature (i.e., adding up_day_ratio_20 / px_vs_ma50 / vol_ratio_5_20 to the matching rule pushes concordance toward 100%). This confirms the seven-feature set (including ma20_slope_5) is sufficient and no industry residual is required.
tests.failure_criterion: Concordance <65% with discordance concentrated in a feature-residual signature that survives the gating rule (e.g., discordant pairs consistently differ in up_day_ratio_20 by ≥0.10 OR in px_vs_ma50 by ≥0.05 even when the gating features match). A residual that survives is admissible evidence of a non-feature mechanism consistent with the skeptic's industry-conditioning claim. Also FAIL if concordance is high but driven by a single snapshot_anon stratum — that indicates the match collapsed into a trivial sub-sample rather than discriminating.

tests.name: Cross-snapshot stage-score concordance stability
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot_anon, z-score mom_20, ma10_slope_5, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20 using that snapshot's own mean/SD (intra-snapshot standardization, not pooled). Construct a composite stage_score = unweighted mean of the five z-scores. Compute Spearman rank correlation between stage_score and an ordinal outcome severity ladder (large_win > small_win > loss > ruin), restricted to cases within that snapshot. Compare ρ across all snapshot_anon strata that have ≥3 cases.
tests.success_criterion: Spearman ρ ≥ 0.55 in at least 3 non-overlapping snapshot_anon strata AND sign of ρ is consistent across all strata with ≥3 cases AND the cross-snapshot dispersion of ρ (max−min) ≤ 0.4. Stable cross-snapshot ρ supports a regime-/stage-driven mechanism that travels with the features themselves.
tests.failure_criterion: ρ varies by ≥0.6 across strata (sign flip or near-zero ρ in ≥2 strata). Failure indicates that the same feature composite predicts opposite outcomes in different snapshots, which is the signature of an industry-leadership-shift mechanism — i.e., the features are picking up the industry of the regime rather than the stage of the stock. Also FAIL if only one snapshot_anon has ≥3 cases (insufficient cross-regime evidence to support either claim — mark UNRESOLVED).

tests.name: Snapshot-feature-dispersion vs outcome-variance coupling
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot_anon, compute the coefficient of variation (CV) of mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma20, and ma20_slope_5 across the snapshot's entities, and independently compute the variance of an ordinal w4_return_bucket encoding (large_win=4, small_win=3, loss=2, ruin=1). Test the rank correlation between per-snapshot feature-CV and per-snapshot outcome-variance. Then, conditional on is_b0_pick=true subset, recompute. If a snapshot happens to be industry-concentrated, the feature vector is expected to be bimodal and outcome-variance elevated; a regime-only mechanism predicts no such coupling.
tests.success_criterion: Spearman ρ between feature-CV and outcome-variance across snapshot_anon strata is |ρ| ≤ 0.25 (no coupling) AND the conditional distribution of outcomes within each snapshot is consistent with a unimodal 'stage' rather than a bimodal 'industry' composition. This would indicate that snapshot-level outcome heterogeneity is not driven by feature-distribution heterogeneity, undercutting the industry-concentration explanation.
tests.failure_criterion: ρ ≥ 0.55 between feature-CV and outcome-variance, OR outcome distribution within ≥2 snapshots is bimodal (Hartigan dip test on ordinal outcome, or simply two clusters separated by ≥2 levels). Bimodal within-snapshot outcomes co-located with elevated feature-CV is direct evidence that snapshot composition (industry leadership shift) — not stage — drives dispersion. Also FAIL if most snapshot_anon strata have <3 cases; the test is undefined.

leakage_checks: Verify that mom_20, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_pct, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, and ibd_entry_volume_ratio are all computed using data strictly at-or-before the IBD entry trigger timestamp for each entity — reject the test if any rolling-window end date extends past entry. This is the primary PIT gate.

Confirm snapshot_anon is a calendar/regime tag assigned using only information available pre-entry for the entities in that snapshot, not a post-hoc label assigned using the outcome distribution. If snapshot_anon construction is opaque, demote any test that conditions on it and report UNRESOLVED.

Confirm w4_return_bucket and outcome_label are frozen at the archaeology timestamp (do not require an outer-forward 4-week window beyond the archaeology date). No test in this design requests any new forward measurement.
Verify is_b0_pick is computed deterministically from a published, pre-entry rule (e.g., IBD-style leadership screen) and is not retroactively flipped after outcome is known.

Check that pullback_duration_weeks and pullback_pct are not missing-not-at-random in a way that correlates with outcome (currently several false_negative_relative cases have nulls while several false_positive_ruin cases have values — pattern is suspicious and must be tabulated before relying on these features in any test). If MNAR is detected, restrict the matched-pair test to features with complete data.
Confirm that the entity-level archaeology table is a strict subset of the universe evaluated at the same PIT — no survivorship bias introduced by dropping delisted entities pre-emptively.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The strongest alternative to the industry-allocation advantage is a three-layer confound: (1) B0-style leadership selection is, by construction, an industry-clustering screen — leadership names concentrate in 1-3 GICS sectors per macro regime, so the 'industry tilt' is a label applied to a portfolio that B0 already concentrated by sector. (2) Within those concentrated picks, the archaeology's discriminating signal is the seven-feature vector (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5), not the sector tag. Winners and false_positive_ruins cluster within similar late-stage entry signatures (e.g., entity_6618d3e80c winner and entity_4fdc3699fd ruin both have ma10_slope_5 ~0.075-0.090 and px_vs_ma50>0.10), and the discriminating residual is feature-based, not industry-based. (3) The dominant cross-strata variance comes from regime (snapshot_anon clustering), which is calendar-driven and shifts industry leadership — explaining why snapshot_anon concentrates cases (snap_71486ed83c=6/27, snap_d0d57b1e40=4/27) more than any sector variable. Industry is therefore the shadow cast by (B0 selection × regime × momentum-stage factor); it is not an independent lever. The skeptic's valid endogeneity caveat tempers confidence: the seven features are themselves industry-conditioned in second moments, so quintile-matching on them is tautological. Direct adjudication requires sector-tagged archaeology, which this evidence lacks.
falsifiers: Within an absolute-threshold (not quintile) matched-pair test across ≥4 GICS sectors, where pairs are matched on |Δmom_20|≤0.05, |Δma10_slope_5|≤0.01, |Δvol_ratio_5_20|≤0.20, |Δup_day_ratio_20|≤0.10, and |Δibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct|≤0.02, adding a sector dummy to a W4-return regression on those five features increases adjusted R² by more than 1 percentage point and the sector coefficient is significant at |t|>2.0 across at least 3 non-overlapping snapshot_anon strata. A positive finding here falsifies the feature-only mechanism and re-opens industry as a residual lever.

A sector-neutralized portfolio that matches each B0 winner on (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) retains less than 70% of the un-neutralized W4 alpha, and the lost alpha is distributed across ≥3 distinct sectors rather than concentrated in one regime. This would demonstrate industry as a real factor exposure that the features do not subsume.

In a within-snapshot_anon regression with sector fixed effects, the seven-feature vector's standardized coefficients each shift by more than 25% (in magnitude) when sector dummies are added, indicating that the feature coefficients were silently absorbing an industry component. Stable coefficients refute this falsifier.

Cross-snapshot_anon variance in industry HHI of B0 winners minus B0 ruins explains more than 15% of W4-return variance in a hierarchical regression, after the seven-feature vector is conditioned on. This would re-open industry leadership shifts as a within-snapshot mechanism distinct from regime.
actionable_design_principles: Treat industry as a derived, observable label rather than a primitive input — compute sector tag at PIT but do not use it as a feature in any selection or scoring model. Report it post-hoc for attribution only.

Mandate that any industry-tilt policy be expressed as a feature-reducible rule (e.g., 'we tilt away from biotech because the seven-feature vector's typical biotech reading fails the ma10_slope_5 > 0.05 + ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05 gate'); raw sector return differentials are not admissible as a policy lever without such a reducible mechanism.

Stratify every reported performance number by snapshot_anon (regime) BEFORE stratifying by industry. If regime explains the within-industry return spread, industry is a label not a lever. Report both stratifications and a partial-correlation table.

Separate predictive-mechanism gates (per-name feature conditions: ma10_slope_5, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, up_day_ratio_20) from portfolio-construction constraints (industry caps, exposure limits). Removing an industry tilt without replacing its factor exposure is a mechanical alpha loss, not a refutation — design the replacement, then remove the original.

Refuse industry-based allocation unless the absolute-feature matched-pair diagnostic passes the falsifier bar above. Until it does, treat the industry-allocation advantage claim as an unproven post-hoc narrative that conflates B0 selection bias, regime timing, and momentum-stage factors.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Momentum-stage penalty gate: skip or down-weight entries where (ma10_slope_5 > 0.05 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05) — directly attacks the largest false_positive_ruin signature in the archaeology without invoking industry. Applied at PIT, no forward look.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This is the smallest, most directly archaeology-supported rule. It targets the actual failure mode (entity_8f0df3d38e, entity_84824e6a20, entity_b6bcccdf6a) rather than a sector aggregate. Industry cannot explain why a stock with steep late-stage slope fails while one with shallow slope succeeds, but this rule can.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Two-feature, single-comparison gate — O(1) per pick at PIT, trivially O(N) across a universe. No calendar, no ticker, no forward look. Fits inside any scoring layer without portfolio-construction overhead.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Regime/snapshot tag as a stratification variable, not a feature — compute snapshot_anon at PIT using only pre-entry information, tag every pick with it, and require that any sector-stratified performance report first condition on snapshot_anon. Industry-stratified claims that do not condition on regime are inadmissible as policy inputs.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Separates the predictive layer (per-name feature gates) from the attribution/portfolio-construction layer (regime + industry stratification). This prevents the common error of attributing regime-driven returns to industry. Also prevents calendar identity from leaking as a predictive feature.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Snapshot_anon is a categorical label, not a numeric feature; it cannot drive a forward prediction on its own. Used only as a stratification axis for reporting and partial-correlation diagnostics. Zero predictive capacity cost.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Industry exposure cap with feature-reducibility justification: cap any sector concentration at the B0-screen's pre-entry sector HHI plus a documented epsilon, and require each cap be expressed as a feature-reducible constraint (e.g., 'cap biotech at HHI+5% because biotech systematically shows up_day_ratio_20 < 0.50 and the entry-gate above already excludes 70% of biotech names'). If the constraint cannot be reduced to a feature rule, it is removed.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Operationalizes the 'portfolio-construction effect vs predictive mechanism' separation. Industry caps are allowed as portfolio-construction artifacts only when they are explicit substitutions for the factor exposure the industry tag was harvesting — preventing silent double-counting and the mechanical alpha loss that pure removal would cause.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Cap is a portfolio-level constraint, not a per-pick feature — runs once after the universe is scored. Feature-reducibility justification is a documentation gate, not a runtime cost. Capacity: O(1) post-screening.

cycles.question: Adversarially attack the apparent within-industry stock-selection advantage: construct the strongest alternative explanation. Prefer a concrete diagnostic over generic caution.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The apparent within-industry stock-selection edge is dominated by co-exposure to industry-group trend continuation; the model's discriminating features (mom_20, ma10/ma20 slopes, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20) are common-momentum proxies that load on the same factor across peer names. The act of 'picking one B0 name inside a hot group' is largely identifying the tightest technical expression of an industry rotation that is already underway, so the PnL should be attributed to industry-timing beta, not firm-level alpha.
evidence_for: All top separating features between selected_winners and false_negatives (mom_20: 0.163 vs 0.058; px_vs_ma50: 0.127 vs 0.056; ma10_slope_5: 0.0268 vs 0.0122; ma20_slope_5: 0.0204 vs 0.0089; up_day_ratio_20: 0.625 vs 0.500; vol_ratio_5_20: 1.424 vs 1.179) are group-coherent momentum/relative-strength features that, by construction, correlate within an industry and are NOT firm-idiosyncratic.

False_negatives with muted stock signals (entity_de1c657364: mom_20=0.058, up_day_ratio=0.65, w4_return_bucket=large_win; entity_535a1beed7: mom_20=0.028, ma20_slope=-0.005, w4_return_bucket=large_win; entity_05b4c6b1f7: mom_20=0.070, up_day_ratio=0.50, w4_return_bucket=large_win) still became winners — indicating the stock-level signal was unnecessary, consistent with industry tailwind doing the work.

False_positive_ruins carried stock-level signals as strong as winners (entity_8f0df3d38e: mom_20=0.176, ma10_slope=0.054, up_day_ratio=0.65, ruin; entity_3472243e0c: mom_20=0.242, ma10_slope=0.030, ruin; entity_4fdc3699fd: ma10_slope=0.091, mom_20=0.185, ruin; entity_b6bcccdf6a: mom_20=0.176, ma10_slope=0.067, ma20_slope=0.045, ruin). If the signals truly isolated firm-level quality, a stock with mom_20>0.17 and positive dual-MA slopes should not have produced an 8-count ruin bucket — implying the stock-level signal provided no protective information.

ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (PIT-observable) is higher for winners (median 0.0300) than false_negatives (0.0195), but this is a breakout-execution feature, not a firm-quality feature — winners entered closer to the group's collective breakout level, again consistent with riding the group move.

The mixed-outcome case entity_6618d3e80c (w4_return_bucket=large_win but also false_positive_ruin) had extreme px_vs_ma50=0.337 and mom_20=0.251 — the W4 win came from the group, and the later ruin came from the firm. This single case cleanly separates the two effects and supports attributing W4 PnL to the group.

Pullback profile of winners (deeper median -15.9%, longer 5.5 weeks) vs false_negatives (-7.3%, 4.0 weeks) indicates the model selects names mid-pullback inside an established uptrend — the textbook signature of group-rotation entries, not idiosyncratic base-breakout timing.
evidence_against: vol_ratio_5_20 separation (1.424 vs 1.179, standardized delta -1.05) is a name-relative-volume feature that can carry some firm-specific information not perfectly shared by the group.

Within any snapshot (e.g., snap_71486ed83c), not every candidate with similar group-level signals is selected (entity_df5478102d and entity_d8e8e7b814 are both rejected false_negatives with moderate mom_20=0.12 and 0.11 respectively), implying some within-group discrimination is occurring.

base_mbox_count is higher for false_negatives than selected_winners (4 vs 3.5), and base_duration_weeks is shorter (44 vs 52) — a count/duration-of-base feature is partially firm-pattern-specific and partially a proxy for cycle phase.

Some winners have very weak technical footprints (entity_8ad5cd4795: ma10_slope=-0.006, ma20_slope=-0.003, mom_20=0.004, up_day_ratio=0.70 → large_win; entity_2f86543bf6: ma10_slope=0.0076, ma20_slope=-0.0078, mom_20=-0.008, up_day_ratio=0.35 → large_win) — if the group were the only driver, such weak technical names should not be disproportionately represented among winners.
falsifiable_predictions: Compute, for each of the 27 cases, the median W4 return of the industry peer set (PIT-defined at snapshot date). The Pearson correlation between stock W4 return and peer-median W4 return should exceed 0.6 across cases; partial correlation holding peer-median W4 constant should drop the apparent selected-vs-not edge to statistical insignificance (bootstrap p>0.10).

A 'buy-every-name-in-top-quintile-industry' naive sleeve, rebalanced at the same snapshot cadence, should capture ≥70% of the selected-sleeve's W4 mean return; if it does, the residual cannot bear a fees+slippage budget for a long-short or factor-pricing premium.

False_positive_ruins should concentrate in snapshots where the industry peer-median W1 return (PIT-observable at entry) is negative or bottom-decile; conversely, false_negatives that became winners should concentrate in snapshots with top-decile peer-median W1 return. A 2x2 contingency test (signal-strength quartile × peer-W1 quartile) should show peer-W1 as the dominant explanatory axis, with signal-strength insignificant conditional on peer-W1.

If the model is rerun with industry-peer-median features included (mom_20, slope, px_vs_ma50 measured on the peer median instead of the stock), the within-sample hit rate on selected_winners should fall below 50% (i.e., the model is learning the group, not the name).

Among snapshots where group momentum is positive but the rejected name has stronger firm signals than the selected name, the rejected name's W4 return should not be statistically lower than the selected name's — falsifying firm-level discrimination.

The 8-count false_positive_ruin bucket should, by W4-end, exhibit peer-median drawdown in 6+ of 8 cases; absence of that pattern (ruins without group drawdowns) would re-favor the within-industry-skill hypothesis.
policy_implications: Do not pay alpha fees for the within-industry sleeve. Capacity, risk budget, and benchmark should be sized against an industry-rotation neutral factor, not a market-neutral long-short; the apparent edge is mostly group beta in disguise.

Add an explicit industry-peer-median W1/W4 PIT feature as a hard pre-filter or position-size scaler. If peer-median is bottom-quartile, the selection signal should be ignored or shorted, since the ruin concentration in strong-signal names confirms strong stock-level signals do not protect against group breakdowns.

Risk management should monitor industry-group drawdown in real time; position-level stops are insufficient because the largest PnL shocks come from correlated peer moves (false_positive_ruins had peer breakdowns despite strong stock signals).

Re-evaluate the false_negatives that became winners (7 cases) as a missed-industry-timing cost, not a missed-stock-picking cost — broadening the candidate set to capture group rotation, rather than tightening the firm-level filter, is the indicated improvement.

If the diagnostic tests above confirm the industry-proxy hypothesis, the 'within-industry advantage' should be reclassified as a known factor exposure (industry momentum / relative rotation) and hedged or beta-priced rather than marketed as security-selection skill.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The failure archaeology is not measuring industry-group beta; it is measuring a snapshot-cluster / regime confounder. The 27 cases collapse into 1-2 dominant snapshots (snap_71486ed83c alone accounts for >=6 cases, snap_d0d57b1e40 for >=5), and the 'false_negatives that became winners' concentrate in those very snapshots. A snapshot with broad-market rally characteristics (top-decile SPY/QQQ W1 return, VIX contraction, or post-FOMC drift) will produce winners from any reasonable candidate pool regardless of firm-level skill, and a snapshot with a sector-rotation initiation will produce industry-coherent winners regardless of selection. The prior researcher's industry-beta reframe is therefore a special case of a more general sample-artifact problem: the apparent 'within-industry edge' is confounded by snapshot identity, not by industry identity, and the firm-level signal may be doing real, small-sample work that is invisible once you condition on snapshot.

attacks.issue: Snapshot clustering dominates case distribution. snap_71486ed83c and snap_d0d57b1e40 together hold >=11 of 27 cases (~41%); the 'industry proxy' hypothesis and the 'within-industry skill' hypothesis are both under-identified because snapshot fixed effects are not partialled out. A concrete diagnostic: compute, within each snapshot, the W4 hit rate of all candidates (selected + rejected) against the median peer and against SPY. If the within-snapshot hit rate of REJECTED candidates equals or exceeds the selected candidates' hit rate, the signal is snapshot-driven, not name-driven or industry-driven.
attacks.why_it_matters: If rejected candidates in the same snapshot as the false_negatives also became winners at similar rates, then the 'missed winners' were not missed due to firm-signal weakness — they were missed because any name in that snapshot worked. This single test, computed on the existing 27-case data plus the rejected-but-not-winner pool, falsifies the researcher's mechanism claim more directly than any peer-median W1/W4 feature engineering.

attacks.issue: The false_negative definition is circular and contaminates the contrast. Per method_note, a false_negative requires future W4 >=5pp above the B0 selected median. Therefore the 'missed winners' are, by construction, the right tail of the candidate-pool W4 distribution; they were never representative of the typical rejected name. The 11 selected_winners vs 8 false_positive_ruins contrast is the only unbiased comparison in the dataset, and on that contrast the win rate is 11/19 = 58% with the rest being ruin — a coin-flip-with-tails, not a clean edge. The 'industry beta' reframe cannot rescue a sample whose positive class is defined relative to itself.
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher treats the 7 false_negatives as a uniform counterfactual ('these names would have won'). They are not — they are a selected-on-outcome subsample. The honest comparison is selected (11 W, 8 R, 1 mixed) vs all-other-rejected (must be reconstructed), and until that comparison is run, every downstream attribution to industry momentum is built on a tautology.

counterexamples_to_seek: A selected winner in a snapshot whose SPY W1 return is bottom-decile AND whose industry-peer-median W4 return is bottom-decile, yet the name returns top-decile W4 — this isolates firm alpha from both market beta and industry beta. Conversely, a false_positive_ruin in a snapshot where peer-median W4 is top-decile would falsify firm-level discrimination.

A rejected candidate in the same snapshot as a false_negative that ALSO became a W4 large_win with similar mom_20 / slope / vol_ratio — this directly shows the 'missed winner' was not signal-weak, only snapshot-lucky.
what_would_change_my_mind: If, within each snapshot, selected candidates' W4 hit rate conditional on snapshot fixed effects is statistically distinguishable from the rejected-pool hit rate (bootstrap p<0.05 on a per-snapshot basis), the firm-level signal is real and the industry-beta reframe collapses.

If the snapshot-cluster pattern disappears after restricting to snapshots with neutral market-regime dummies (SPY W1 in [40th, 60th] percentile, VIX change |dVIX|<5%), AND the selected-vs-rejected gap survives that restriction, then within-industry selection skill is supported and the researcher's mechanism claim is wrong.

tests.name: industry_beta_partial_out
tests.comparison: For each of the 27 cases, compute the snapshot-defined industry peer-set median (PIT, pre-entry) of {mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50}. Regress selected-vs-rejected outcome label (w4_return_bucket collapsed to win/loss) on (stock_feature - peer_median_feature) and on peer_median_feature separately, then jointly. If the firm-residual coefficient is insignificant (p>0.10) while peer-median coefficient is significant, industry beta dominates. If both significant, both mechanisms operate.
tests.success_criterion: Stock-feature residual (after peer-median subtraction) shows significant marginal association with selected_winner vs false_positive_ruin (p<0.10) AND odds ratio >1.5 in same direction as raw feature — firm-skill hypothesis supported.
tests.failure_criterion: Peer-median feature retains significant association with outcome label after conditioning on stock-feature residual (p<0.10), and raw stock-feature significance collapses (p>0.10) — industry-beta hypothesis supported.

tests.name: snapshot_regime_stratification
tests.comparison: Stratify the 27 cases into snapshot-regime bins using snapshot-aggregate pre-entry vol_ratio_5_20 (terciles) AND snapshot-aggregate base_duration_weeks (median split) as regime proxies. Within each bin, compute selected-vs-rejected hit rate. If selected outperforms rejected only in top-tercile vol_ratio bins (high-vol expansion regimes), the edge is regime-confounded, not firm-skill.
tests.success_criterion: Selected hit rate exceeds rejected hit rate by >=20pp within AT LEAST 2 of 3 vol_ratio_5_20 terciles (firm signal robust across regimes) — within-industry skill supported.
tests.failure_criterion: Selected-vs-rejected gap is concentrated (>2x larger) in a single vol_ratio_5_20 tercile AND is statistically indistinguishable from zero in the other two terciles — regime-confounded, firm-skill claim falsified for this sample.

tests.name: pullback_signature_orthogonality
tests.comparison: Test whether the selected_winners' deeper/longer pullback signature (median pullback_pct=-15.9%, pullback_duration_weeks=5.5) is driven by industry-cycle phase or by name-specific basing. Compute partial correlation of pullback_pct with selected_winner indicator, controlling for peer-median px_vs_ma50. If pullback signature disappears once peer-trend strength is controlled, the model is selecting mid-pullback in a group uptrend (rotation entry), not identifying firm-specific bases.
tests.success_criterion: Pullback_pct retains significant association with selected_winner (p<0.10) after conditioning on peer-median px_vs_ma50 — firm-specific base timing is being captured.
tests.failure_criterion: Pullback_pct loses significance (p>0.10) once peer-median px_vs_ma50 is partialled out, and pullback_pct correlates >=0.5 with peer-median px_vs_ma50 — pullback signature is a group-trend proxy, not firm-skill evidence.

leakage_checks: Peer-median features for tests 1 and 3 must be computed from anonymized peer-set snapshots dated <= the case snapshot date; no use of outcome_label or w4_return_bucket in any peer-aggregate construction.

Snapshot-regime bins in test 2 must be defined by pre-entry aggregates only (vol_ratio_5_20, base_duration_weeks computed at or before entry); vol_ratio_5_20 itself is a stock-relative ratio so snapshot-aggregate here means mean across all PIT-candidates at that snapshot, used only as a regime dummy, never as a name-level feature.

All three tests must be reproducible on the existing 27-case dataset without invoking W4 outcomes as inputs; if any test requires W4 of the peer set as input, it must be reframed using PIT peer momentum features instead (mom_60 as forward-direction proxy is forbidden).

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The apparent within-industry stock-selection advantage is best characterized as a partially-identified edge in a heavily snapshot-clustered, small sample, where the discriminating features (mom_20, ma10/ma20 slopes, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20) are all common-momentum proxies that load on the same factor across peer names. The strongest alternative explanation is NOT exclusively industry-group beta (Researcher's frame) — it is a more general snapshot-regime / cross-sectional-cluster confounder that subsumes industry beta as a special case (Skeptic's frame). snap_71486ed83c and snap_d0d57b1e40 together hold ~41% of cases, the false_negative definition is right-tail-of-its-own-distribution (circular), and the unconditional 11W/8R/1mixed selected hit rate of 58% is not distinguishable from a regime-driven coin flip plus tail-selection artifact. The within-industry skill claim is therefore neither supported nor refuted by the current evidence; it is dominated by a sample-structure problem that any honest re-analysis must partial out before either the industry-beta or the firm-skill interpretation can be evaluated.
falsifiers: Sequential nested-model test: regress W4 outcome on (a) firm features alone, (b) firm + snapshot fixed effects, (c) firm + snapshot FE + industry-peer-median features, (d) firm + snapshot FE + industry-peer-median + snapshot×industry interactions. If (b) wipes out the firm-feature coefficient (R² drop >50% in firm block) and (c) and (d) add nothing, snapshot regime is the dominant confounder and BOTH firm-skill and industry-beta reframe collapse. The firm-skill claim survives only if firm features retain p<0.10 conditional on snapshot FE.

Within-snapshot W4 hit-rate comparison: for each snapshot with >=3 candidates, compute the W4 hit rate of rejected candidates vs selected candidates. If rejected hit rate >= selected hit rate in >50% of multi-candidate snapshots, the edge is snapshot- and not name-driven. This is the cleanest test of the Skeptic's strongest counterclaim and is computable on the existing 27 cases plus the rejected-non-false-negative pool.

Peer-W1-PIT-conditional stratification: partition cases by industry-peer-median W1 return (PIT-observable at entry, computed from peer set dated <= snapshot). If the selected-vs-rejected hit-rate gap is concentrated in the top-tercile of peer-W1 and is statistically zero in the bottom two terciles, the edge is industry-timing, not firm-skill. If the gap is concentrated in a specific snapshot within each peer-W1 tercile, the edge is snapshot-regime.

Drop-tail robustness: rebuild the contrast by either (a) randomly sub-sampling 1 case per snapshot to balance snapshot exposure, or (b) re-defining false_negative as W4 >= 8% absolute (not relative to B0 selected median), then re-run the median-delta contrast table. If the standardized deltas of the top 5 separating features all shrink by >40%, the contrast was being driven by right-tail selection bias, not by a real feature-outcome relationship.

Idiosyncratic-residual construction: regress each candidate's mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50, vol_ratio_5_20 on snapshot FE + industry FE (using a PIT industry map) and use the residual as the firm-specific feature. The within-industry skill claim survives only if (firm-residual → selected_winner) odds ratio >2.0 with p<0.10. A null result on the residual with the raw feature still significant is the cleanest signature that the model is learning snapshot/industry, not the name.

Counterexample search: enumerate the snapshot × industry cells in the data. The firm-skill claim is supported if at least one cell contains both a selected winner and a rejected large_win with the rejected name having strictly weaker firm features (mom_20, up_day_ratio, vol_ratio) than the selected name. Absence of such a cell in the existing data, or a cell where the rejected name has stronger features but equal/better W4, would directly refute within-snapshot name discrimination.
actionable_design_principles: Partial out snapshot fixed effects before evaluating ANY firm-level signal; snapshot identity is the highest-order confounder in this dataset and must be the first covariate entered, not the last.

Treat industry-peer-median features as a second-order control layered on top of snapshot FE; do not regress firm features on peer medians alone, as that conflates snapshot regime with industry regime.

Use only PIT-observable features (features computable from data dated <= snapshot date) in any diagnostic; mom_60 used as a 'forward-direction proxy' is forbidden per the experimental designer's leakage check and must not be smuggled in via a renaming.

Balance snapshot exposure in any re-analysis (one case per snapshot, or weighted by inverse snapshot frequency) before computing median-delta contrasts; the current contrast is over-weighted toward snap_71486ed83c and snap_d0d57b1e40.

Replace the right-tail-relative false_negative definition with an absolute-threshold definition (e.g., W4 >= 8% absolute return) for any cross-comparison; the current definition is circular with respect to the selected-pool W4 distribution and contaminates every downstream attribution.

Separate the mechanism question (does the firm-feature → outcome link exist at all?) from the portfolio-construction question (is the magnitude, after costs and capacity, large enough to monetize?) — they require different evidence and should not be conflated in policy recommendations.
Report the within-snapshot selected-vs-rejected hit-rate gap with bootstrap CIs as a primary statistic; the cross-snapshot pooled 58% win rate is not an adequate summary and is regime-confounded.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: snapshot_fe_first_residual_then_industry
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Inverts the researcher's proposed industry-partial-out by conditioning on snapshot first and industry second. This addresses the Skeptic's stronger counterclaim (snapshot > industry as a confounder) and prevents the industry-beta reframe from being mis-attributed when the real driver is snapshot regime. It is a nested-covariate ordering, not just another feature.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity estimate must shrink by the R² attributable to snapshot FE; if snapshot FE alone explains >40% of the W4 variance, the strategy's scalable alpha is far smaller than the raw hit-rate gap suggests, and capacity should be benchmarked against a snapshot-regime-timed sleeve, not a market-neutral long-short.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: peer_w1_pit_conditional_filter
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Uses only PIT-observable peer W1 return (computable at entry from peer set dated <= snapshot, NOT future peer W4) as a hard regime gate. Distinct from the researcher's peer-W1 use as a stratification feature because it is implemented as a binary pre-filter that disables the signal when peer momentum is bottom-quartile. This is a policy-level commitment, not a diagnostic.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Restricts capacity to regimes where peer-W1 is top-tercile; in bottom-tercile regimes, the signal is shorted or ignored, which both reduces expected drawdown (as observed in the false_positive_ruin cluster, where peer breakdowns coexisted with strong firm signals) and concentrates capacity in the regime where the signal has the most evidence. Capacity is therefore regime-gated, not name-gated.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: snapshot_balanced_bootstrap_oos_test
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: A re-sampling policy, not a feature. Rebalances the 27-case archaeology by drawing one case per snapshot with replacement, then re-computing the median-delta contrast and the firm-feature → outcome logistic regression. This directly tests whether the cross-feature separation observed in the researcher's contrast table survives snapshot-exposure equalization. Distinct from the researcher's falsifiable predictions because it does not require constructing a peer-W4 feature (which is forbidden by the leakage rule) and does not require re-running the model on a new dataset.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Capacity decision is gated on bootstrap CI: if the 95% CI of the firm-residual odds ratio includes 1.0 after 1000 snapshot-balanced resamples, the strategy is not allocated alpha capacity. If the CI excludes 1.0 with lower bound >1.5, capacity can be sized at the magnitude the lower bound supports, not the raw hit-rate gap.

cycles.question: Adversarially attack the near-parity of SCORE_BEFORE_LANE: construct the strongest alternative explanation. Prefer a concrete diagnostic over generic caution.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The near-parity of SCORE_BEFORE_LANE is an artifact of the score being dominated by a single vol-confirmed-momentum factor (vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20 carry the load), so that downstream lanes (base/pullback filters) operate on a residual that the pre-lane score cannot resolve; the score's apparent equality across outcomes is structural truncation, not informational content.
evidence_for: Numeric contrasts show the largest standardized deltas between false_negatives and selected_winners are exactly the vol/momentum cluster: up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), mom_20 (-1.00), px_vs_ma50 (-0.85); pre-lane scores built from these features will therefore produce near-parity between a ruin like entity_8f0df3d38e (vol_ratio 1.24, mom 0.18) and a winner like entity_440e297253 (vol_ratio 1.59, mom 0.06) only because a heavier feature (pullback_pct median -15.9 vs -7.3) is excluded from the pre-lane score.

Base/pullback structural features show opposite-signed deltas (pullback_duration_weeks +0.73, base_depth_pct +0.19, base_duration_weeks +0.42), confirming a residual axis the score cannot read; 8/8 false_positive_ruins and all 5 false_negatives occur in samples where pullback_duration_weeks or pullback_pct is null or shallow (>= -7.3%), so the lane does real work the score ignores.
