evidence_against: Entity_6618d3e80c (false_positive_ruin|selected_winner) and entity_2c58cebc59 (selected_winner with pullback_pct -25.1%) show that high pre-lane-style features can co-occur with both ruin and win, so a pure vol+momentum score is necessary but not sufficient explanation.
Counter-sample size is small (n=27) and snapshots cluster (snap_71486ed83c contributes 7 cases), so the parity could partially reflect snapshot-period regime rather than score construction.
falsifiable_predictions: Within-quartile bins of vol_ratio_5_20, the W4 outcome distribution across SCORE_BEFORE_LANE deciles should remain near-parity (Kolmogorov-Smirnov D < 0.15) while pullback-adjusted residual deciles should show monotonic separation (D > 0.25); if separation holds within quartiles, the score-dominance claim is wrong.

Replacing SCORE_BEFORE_LANE with a residual = score - beta*vol_ratio_5_20 - gamma*mom_20 should flip the near-parity: winners and ruins should separate by >=0.4 standardized delta on this residual, whereas the raw score shows <=0.2.
policy_implications: Stop relying on SCORE_BEFORE_LANE as a marginal gate; treat it as a coarse vol-confirmed-momentum filter and route base/pullback information into a separate post-lane residual score to avoid double-counting or canceling signal.
Run the within-vol-quartile KS diagnostic on the next 50 B0 picks before trusting any parity-based lane equivalence claim.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The near-parity of SCORE_BEFORE_LANE is a selection-on-collider artifact, not a feature of the score itself: every false_negative in the archaeology has is_b0_pick=false (lane-rejected), every false_positive_ruin has is_b0_pick=true (lane-accepted), and selected_winners also have is_b0_pick=true. Because the cases are sampled AFTER lane-decision, the SCORE_BEFORE_LANE distributions being compared are truncated on a downstream variable that the score cannot read, so observing similar score medians across error types reveals nothing about the score's true discrimination in the untruncated candidate pool.

attacks.issue: Collider conditioning on is_b0_pick breaks the pre/post-lane separation the researcher assumes
attacks.why_it_matters: The claim requires that SCORE_BEFORE_LANE comparisons are unconfounded, but 8/8 false_positive_ruins are is_b0_pick=true and 7/7 false_negatives are is_b0_pick=false. The score is computed pre-lane but sampled post-lane-decision; matching winners and ruins on opposite sides of that filter means the parity test is contaminated by the very lane the researcher claims is doing the work the score cannot.

attacks.issue: Case-level inversions contradict the vol-confirmed-momentum mechanism the researcher attributes the parity to
attacks.why_it_matters: Entity_440e297253 (selected_winner, large_win) has mom_20=0.058 and vol_ratio_5_20=1.59, while entity_8f0df3d38e (false_positive_ruin) has mom_20=0.176 and vol_ratio_5_20=1.24 — the winner has lower momentum and higher vol; entity_2c58cebc59 wins despite pullback_pct=-25.1%; entity_6618d3e80c is dual-labeled false_positive_ruin|selected_winner. Median contrasts hide rank inversions that directly falsify the single-factor story.

counterexamples_to_seek: Within is_b0_pick=true (snap_d0d57b1e40 has 4 such cases mixing false_positive_ruin, selected_winner, and the dual-labeled entity), test whether SCORE_BEFORE_LANE still shows parity when the collider is held fixed — if separation emerges, the prior claim collapses.

Construct an unconditioned control set of candidates that satisfy SCORE_BEFORE_LANE thresholds but were never evaluated as B0 picks, and compare W4 outcome distributions to the lane-filtered set to test whether the score carries any pre-lane information.
what_would_change_my_mind: Re-estimating the false_negative vs selected_winner standardized deltas after restricting both groups to is_b0_pick=true (or both to false) and finding |d|>0.3 persists on SCORE_BEFORE_LANE — that would defeat the collider explanation and support the vol-confirmed-momentum artifact story.
Showing that on the full pre-lane candidate pool the score's KS distance between winners and ruins is <0.15 with no conditioning, i.e., the parity is not created by the lane-truncation.

tests.name: collider_cohort_stratification
tests.purpose: Decide whether near-parity of SCORE_BEFORE_LANE between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner survives conditioning on the B0-pick decision (skeptic's collider) or collapses once lane decision is held fixed (researcher's residual-axis claim).
tests.comparison: Within each is_b0_pick stratum, build a SCORE_BEFORE_LANE proxy as the equally-weighted z-sum of vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50 (the four features with |standardized_delta| > 0.85 in the archaeology). Compute Slot1-vs-Slot3 standardized rank separation (Hodges-Lehmann delta / pooled sd) within each stratum, and compare to the unconditioned separation across strata.
tests.success_criterion: Within is_b0_pick=true stratum, |SlotA_minus_SlotC standardized delta| on the proxy >= 0.30 AND within is_b0_pick=false stratum, |SlotA_minus_SlotC standardized delta| on the proxy >= 0.30. Researcher mechanism (residual-axis claim) wins because the score still carries discrimination once the collider is held constant.
tests.failure_criterion: Within both strata |SlotA_minus_SlotC standardized delta| < 0.15 while the unconditioned cross-stratum delta > 0.40. Skeptic mechanism wins because the apparent separation was entirely created by is_b0_pick truncation.

tests.name: vol_quartile_residualization
tests.purpose: Test whether the researcher's vol-confirmed-momentum residual-axis mechanism actually exists: within fixed vol_ratio_5_20 bins, does a SCORE_BEFORE_LANE proxy stripped of vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20 still separate SlotA from SlotC?
tests.comparison: Bin all 27 cases into vol_ratio_5_20 quartiles (bin boundaries set PIT using quartile medians of the 27 cases themselves to avoid outer-forward leakage). Within each bin, regress the SCORE_BEFORE_LANE proxy on mom_20 alone and compute the residual. Compare KS distance between SlotA and SlotC on (a) the raw proxy and (b) the vol+mom-stripped residual. Report per-bin and pooled-within-bin (weighted by sqrt(n_bin)) statistics.
tests.success_criterion: Pooled-within-quartile KS distance on the vol+mom residual between SlotA and SlotC >= 0.25, while the raw-proxy KS distance pooled-within-quartile is < 0.15. Researcher mechanism wins: vol+mom are the dominant load and the residual contains orthogonal signal that pre-lane score can in principle carry.
tests.failure_criterion: Pooled-within-quartile KS distance on the residual is < 0.10 (i.e., no improvement over the raw-proxy KS < 0.15). Then vol+mom dominance is the entire story and the residual is empty noise within quartiles; this is the skeptic-adjacent null and weakens the researcher's mechanism without endorsing the collider claim.

tests.name: snapshot_blocked_re_estimation
tests.purpose: Test whether the apparent near-parity is a snapshot-period regime artifact (both roles flagged snap_71486ed83c with 7/27 cases) by re-estimating the SlotA-vs-SlotC deltas within snapshot_anon blocks.
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot_anon block containing >= 3 cases and at least one SlotA and one SlotC outcome, compute the SlotA-vs-SlotC standardized delta on the SCORE_BEFORE_LANE proxy. Report (i) median block-level delta, (ii) sign consistency (fraction of blocks with same sign as the global delta), (iii) range of block deltas.
tests.success_criterion: At least 2 of 3 snapshot_anon blocks with sufficient SlotA+SlotC coverage show |block delta| > 0.20 and sign agreement with global delta. Parity is regime-robust, not a snapshot artifact.
tests.failure_criterion: Block-level deltas are sign-inconsistent OR > 50% of blocks contain only one slot (insufficient within-block contrast). Outcome is UNRESOLVED on the snapshot-artifact question, with explicit caveat that small-n archaeology cannot distinguish mechanism from sampling.

leakage_checks: snapshot_anon may be used ONLY for blocking / stratification. It must not enter the SCORE_BEFORE_LANE proxy or the residual. Using it as a feature would amount to calendar identity leakage.
is_b0_pick is a post-lane-decision label and may be used ONLY as a conditioning / stratification variable. It must not be used as a predictive feature inside the proxy.
entity_anon is a row identifier. It must not be used as a feature or as a cluster variable that implicitly carries forward-return information.

The SCORE_BEFORE_LANE proxy must be constructed exclusively from features that are point-in-time at the IBD entry snapshot (ma slopes, momentum, vol ratio, up_day_ratio, px_vs_ma). It must not include pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_pct, base_depth_pct, base_duration_weeks, or base_mbox_count, because those are the lane-residual features whose omission is exactly the mechanism under test.

w4_return_bucket is the only outcome slot and must be applied as a 3-level categorical (large_win / small_win / loss_or_ruin). Do NOT split loss and ruin into separate slots — n is too small and it double-counts the 'false_positive_ruin' label which is already encoded in the archaeology.

Quartile bin edges for vol_ratio_5_20 must be computed from the 27 archaeology cases themselves (PIT-safe for the archaeology); do not import external quartile boundaries which would inject outer-forward distributional information.
Pre-specify all thresholds (0.30 / 0.15 / 0.25 / 0.20) before looking at within-stratum results to avoid post-hoc threshold fishing.
Apply Holm correction across the 3 tests' success/failure decisions to keep family-wise error <= 0.10 given the small n.
experimental_designer.notes_on_3_slot_accounting: Each test uses the same fixed 3-slot W4 outcome partition (large_win / small_win / loss_or_ruin) so that slot membership is identical across tests and per-slot case counts can be cross-tabulated. The 3-slot structure is pre-registered; collapsing to 2 slots (win/non-win) would erase the small_win informative middle that currently distinguishes false_negative_relative from false_positive_ruin and is central to the contrast in the numeric_contrasts table.
experimental_designer.outcome_if_all_tests_fail: UNRESOLVED: the 27-case archaeology cannot separate a vol+mom residual-axis mechanism from a lane-decision collider artifact, and any parity claim about SCORE_BEFORE_LANE should be treated as descriptive rather than causal until either (a) within-stratum n >= 30 per slot per is_b0_pick cohort is collected, or (b) an unconditioned pre-lane candidate pool is exposed.

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The near-parity of SCORE_BEFORE_LANE between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner is contaminated by two non-mutually-exclusive artifacts that the 27-case archaeology cannot separate: (a) a collider on is_b0_pick — every false_positive_ruin is is_b0_pick=true and every false_negative is is_b0_pick=false, so score distributions are truncated by the very lane whose work the score is supposed to evaluate; and (b) vol+mom feature dominance — the largest standardized deltas load on vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20, so any pre-lane proxy built only from these features will mechanically compress to near-parity across error types. The researcher's residual-axis claim and the skeptic's collider claim both predict the same observation, so the observation cannot adjudicate between them.
falsifiers: Within either is_b0_pick stratum, the SlotA-vs-SlotC Hodges-Lehmann delta on the SCORE_BEFORE_LANE proxy exceeds 0.30 in absolute value — this would refute the collider explanation and shift weight toward the vol+mom residual-axis story.

Pooled-within-vol_ratio_5_20-quartile KS distance between SlotA and SlotC on the vol+mom-stripped residual falls below 0.10 — this would refute the residual-axis claim and leave the collider as the dominant explanation.

Sign-inconsistent block-level deltas across snapshot_anon blocks, or >50% of blocks containing only one slot — outcome UNRESOLVED on regime robustness, demanding either extended archaeology or a held-out pre-lane candidate pool.
actionable_design_principles: Do not treat SCORE_BEFORE_LANE parity as a causal claim about the score; gate any parity-based lane equivalence statement on a successful collider_cohort_stratification test with n>=30 per stratum per slot, and route base/pullback information into a separate post-lane residual score rather than collapsing it into a marginal pre-lane gate.

Run the three pre-registered tests (collider stratification, vol-quartile residualization, snapshot blocking) on the next 50 B0 picks with Holm-corrected alpha=0.10 before any policy change, and explicitly pre-specify the unconditioned pre-lane candidate pool comparison as the tie-breaker if stratum tests are inconclusive.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Add a SCORE_BEFORE_LANE_PARITY_AUDIT operator that requires is_b0_pick-stratified re-estimation of SlotA-vs-SlotC deltas before the score can be used as a marginal filter, and emits UNRESOLVED if either stratum has fewer than 30 cases.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Encodes the experimental designer's success/failure criteria directly into policy, making the collider check a first-class gate rather than a diagnostic run after the fact.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Prevents premature commitment to either the researcher's residual-axis mechanism or the skeptic's collider story by forcing an explicit stratum-level decision and refusing to act on underpowered parity claims.

cycles.question: Adversarially attack the usefulness of dry pullback semantics: construct the strongest alternative explanation. Prefer a concrete diagnostic over generic caution.

researcher.mechanism_claim: Dry pullback semantics are not a causal mechanism but a noisy, partly-undefined readout of underlying volatility/momentum regime; the apparent pullback signal is epiphenomenal to vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, and base_duration_weeks, which carry 1.5-2x the standardized contrast of pullback features.
evidence_for: Standardized deltas rank pullback_pct at only 0.64 and pullback_duration_weeks at -0.73, well below vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), mom_20 (-1.00), and up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19), so the pullback features are mid-pack at best.

Among the 6 selected_winners with B0=true, half (entity_ead73f4390, entity_b00579f203, entity_28a6ec4601, entity_90a828939a) have NULL pullback fields — the semantic is structurally undefined for the strongest winners, undermining any claim that observing the pullback is required for edge.

Conditional direction is counter to the 'healthy shallow base' thesis: false_negatives have a SHALLOWER pullback_pct (-7.3%) than selected_winners (-15.9%), i.e., winners pull back HARDER, so a 'dry' shallow pullback actually correlates with the wrong outcome class.

False_positive_ruins also split: 4 of 8 have null pullback (entity_3472243e0c, entity_84824e6a20, entity_b6bcccdf6a, entity_40ea0cfb3b), and the 3 with non-null pullbacks span -12.3% to -16.2% over 7 weeks — indistinguishable in magnitude from the 2c58cebc59 selected_winner at -25.1%/6w and 3adc078f01 at -42.3%/9w, so pullback depth alone does not separate ruin from large_win.
evidence_against: pullback_duration_weeks does show a moderate negative contrast (-0.73 std) suggesting shorter pullbacks trend toward false_negatives, which is at least directionally consistent with one version of the thesis; this is the strongest single counter-example and must be tested jointly with base_duration_weeks (which has -0.42 std, likely collinear).
The numeric_contrasts table is truncated; cannot rule out that pullback features in interaction (e.g., pullback_pct × up_day_ratio_20) carry joint signal not visible in marginal deltas.
falsifiable_predictions: Regressing W4 forward return on (vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, ma10_slope_5, base_duration_weeks, up_day_ratio_20) and then adding pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks will increase out-of-sample R² by <2% and leave ruin-vs-large_win AUC unchanged within ±0.01; if pullback semantics are causal the marginal R² should exceed 5%.

Stratifying B0 picks by vol_ratio_5_20 quintile, the partial effect of pullback_pct on ruin probability will flip sign across at least two quintiles (interaction with vol regime), confirming pullback is a vol-regime marker rather than an independent signal.

Within the pullback_null B0 subset, win rate will be statistically indistinguishable (binomial test, p>0.2) from the pullback_observed B0 subset once base_duration_weeks is matched, falsifying any claim that 'observing a defined dry pullback' is itself informative.
policy_implications: Drop pullback_pct and pullback_duration_weeks from the B0 scoring model; reallocate their weight to vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, and up_day_ratio_20, whose standardized contrasts are 1.5-1.9x larger and directionally cleaner.

Treat the pullback feature as a diagnostic overlay (for post-hoc explanation of why a B0 pick with strong vol/momentum failed) rather than a gating input; this preserves interpretability without letting a weak, partially-undefined feature suppress otherwise valid high-vol/momentum setups.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The prior conclusion that dry pullback semantics are 'epiphenomenal to vol/momentum regime' is a sampling-and-engineering artifact, not a refutation: (a) the pullback features suffer ~50% missingness (NULL in 4/6 strongest winners, 4/8 ruins, and ~half the false_negatives), so the reported 0.64/-0.73 standardized deltas are computed on an effective n roughly HALF that of vol_ratio_5_20's 1.05, making the 'mid-pack' ranking statistically uninterpretable; (b) vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20 are not independent causal drivers but PARTIAL MEDIATORS of the same regime the pullback features describe (a selloff expansion that drives both vol and the pullback_depth snapshot), so partialling them out first is a form of partialling-out-the-treatment; and (c) the 'dry' qualifier was never actually tested because the dataset has no pullback-conditioned volume feature (e.g., avg volume during pullback weeks / pre-pullback volume) — only a snapshot-level vol_ratio_5_20 that conflates pre-pullback vol expansion with pullback-specific dryness, so the entire argument is a category error attacking a shadow of the original claim.

attacks.issue: Apples-to-oranges comparison of standardized deltas across features with different missingness rates
attacks.why_it_matters: up_day_ratio_20 (delta -1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), and mom_20 (-1.00) are computed on 27 cases. pullback_pct (0.64) and pullback_duration_weeks (-0.73) are computed on roughly 13-14 cases (the rest are NULL). Standardized deltas from n≈13 have SE roughly √(27/13) ≈ 1.4× larger, meaning a 'real' effect of the same magnitude would appear as 0.64 when in fact the population effect could be ~0.9 — still mid-pack, but the conclusion that pullback is '1.5-1.9x weaker' is a missingness-driven illusion, not an effect-size finding.

attacks.issue: vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20 are mediating variables for the pullback process, not exogenous controls
attacks.why_it_matters: A pullback, by definition, is a price drawdown that occurs with vol expansion and momentum deterioration. The B0-snapshot vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20 partly REFLECT the pullback (or its absence) rather than being independent regime features. The prior researcher's recommended 'reallocation of weight away from pullback' is equivalent to recommending partialling out the treatment variable and then declaring the residual causally empty — a textbook over-controlling-for-mediator error.

attacks.issue: The 'dry' semantic was never operationalized; the test attacks a different feature than the claim
attacks.why_it_matters: The original thesis concerns 'dry' pullbacks — pullbacks occurring on declining/below-average volume. The dataset has no pullback-conditioned volume feature. The nearest available proxy is snapshot-level vol_ratio_5_20, which captures pre-pullback vol expansion (often elevated) and conflates it with the dryness that occurs DURING the pullback. Without a pullback-window volume feature (e.g., median volume in pullback weeks / median volume in pre-pullback 4 weeks), the 'dry' semantic is undefined in this evidence, and any null result on vol_ratio_5_20 cannot refute it.

attacks.issue: The marginal-vs-conditional contrast ignores the documented interaction of pullback features with up_day_ratio_20
attacks.why_it_matters: The prior researcher's own falsifiable_predictions list notes pullback_pct × up_day_ratio_20 as a candidate interaction, but the reported contrasts are purely marginal. In regime-classified features like pullback depth, the marginal effect is often near zero because the sign FLIPS across conditioning values (shallow pullback + strong tape = bull flag continuation; shallow pullback + weak tape = topping). A delta of 0.64 on pullback_pct is the average of a positive and negative conditional effect, not evidence of a small effect.

attacks.issue: The base/pullback family is broadly weak (base_depth_pct 0.19, dist_to_52w_high 0.16), suggesting the entire construction is undersampled, not that pullback specifically is epiphenomenal
attacks.why_it_matters: If the prior researcher's mechanism claim were correct (pullback is vol/momentum readout), then the underlying base features (base_depth_pct, dist_to_52w_high) should ALSO be weak, which is exactly what we see. But this is symmetric: the weakness of base features could equally reflect (i) the construction being noisy across snapshots, (ii) the n=27 sample underpowering all base/pullback contrasts similarly, or (iii) the labels themselves (false_negative defined by future W4 returns) being noisy. The argument is not 'pullback is weaker than momentum', it is 'everything in the base/pullback complex is undersampled' — which leaves the original claim's status UNRESOLVED, not refuted.

attacks.issue: Sample selection: snapshots cluster on a small set of dates (snap_71486ed83c and snap_d0d57b1e40 dominate the false_negative set), creating temporal confounding
attacks.why_it_matters: snap_71486ed83c alone contributes 6 of the 27 cases (5 of 7 false_negatives). If the underlying market regime on that date (e.g., a broad correction week) suppresses pullback_pct readings AND elevates false_negative rate, the median-delta comparison is a market-regime artifact, not a feature comparison. Any conclusion about 'pullback semantics' derived from a date-clustered sample is confounded with that date's regime.

attacks.issue: Circular label construction: 'false_positive_ruin' is defined by W4 outcomes that themselves depend on whether the pullback continued, reversed, or broke support
attacks.why_it_matters: If the B0 pick is selected on day T and the W4 forward return is ruin, the label 'false_positive_ruin' is partly determined by the realized path of the pullback during weeks T+1 to T+4. The pullback_pct snapshot at T is then 'explaining' a label that the subsequent pullback dynamics created. This is a partial look-ahead in the contrast table, not a clean test of whether observing the pullback at T is predictive.

counterexamples_to_seek: Within the pullback_observed subset, stratify by vol_ratio_5_20 tertile and report the ruin rate per cell — if the ruin rate is monotone in vol_ratio_5_20 within the pullback-observed group, then vol_ratio_5_20 is acting as a mediator and pullback's true causal effect is hidden behind it.

Extract a true 'dry' feature: for each B0 pick with a non-null pullback, compute (median volume during pullback weeks) / (median volume in the 4 weeks pre-pullback) and re-run the contrast — a value <1.0 would confirm the 'dry' semantic is real and measurable, while >1.0 would falsify it. This is the missing diagnostic the prior analysis needed.

Find B0 picks where pullback_pct is in the false_negative range (-5% to -10%) but the pick succeeded (small_win or large_win) — entity_df5478102d (pullback -5.0%, small_win) and entity_d8e8e7b814 (null pullback, small_win) are candidates; if the depth-overlap between false_negative and selected_winner is large, the marginal -7.3% vs -15.9% comparison is not a decision boundary, just a median artifact.

Identify the snapshot dates where vol_ratio_5_20 >1.5 and pullback_pct is null — these are 'vol-expansion-without-pullback' names. If they cluster in the selected_winner class, the null-pullback subset is not 'strong winners' but 'vol-expansion names that ran', which is a different population from the pullback-observed winners and cannot be pooled with them.

Examine entity_6618d3e80c (B0=true, pullback NULL, outcome=both false_positive_ruin AND selected_winner — a label that itself is contradictory) and entity_535a1beed7 (B0=false, pullback NULL, outcome=false_negative_big_winner|false_negative_relative) — the label structure reveals that the B0 selection itself is non-deterministic with respect to these features, and the contrast table is averaging over label noise.
what_would_change_my_mind: A re-extraction that adds a pullback-conditioned volume feature (volume-during-pullback / volume-pre-pullback) and shows that, conditional on vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20, this 'dry' feature has standardized delta <0.3 and does not interact with up_day_ratio_20 — this would operationalize the original claim and either confirm or refute it cleanly. Without this feature, the question is UNRESOLVED.

A regression of W4 forward return on the FULL pullback feature set (pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_volume_ratio IF extracted) with vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, and up_day_ratio_20 included but with the pullback features interacted (not additively) with vol_ratio_5_20 — if the interaction terms are jointly insignificant (p>0.1) AND the main effects of pullback remain near zero, the mechanism is genuinely vol/momentum-driven and I would concede the prior claim.

A matched-pair analysis: for each false_negative with observed pullback, find a selected_winner with observed pullback matched on (vol_ratio_5_20 ±10%, mom_20 ±5pp, base_duration_weeks ±2w) — if the ruin-vs-win split is then 50/50, pullback has no residual information; if it remains 70/30, the prior claim is wrong. This is the minimum decisive test and is feasible within the existing n=27.

Replication on a held-out snapshot set with n≥100 B0 picks, where pullback features have <20% missingness — the current n=27 with 50% pullback nulls has roughly 13 effective observations for pullback contrast, well below the threshold (~30) for a standardized delta to be informative.

A demonstration that removing the pullback_null B0 picks (i.e., re-running the contrast on the 13-14 cases with observed pullback) does NOT increase the vol_ratio_5_20 or mom_20 standardized deltas, proving those features carry independent information rather than mediating the pullback process.

tests.name: matched_pair_residual_pullback
tests.comparison: Within the pullback_observed subset only, pair each false_negative_big_winner|false_negative_relative case to its nearest selected_winner by Mahalanobis distance on (vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20) using ±0.15 vol / ±0.05 mom tolerance. Compute the paired median residual of pullback_pct (FN minus winner). Repeat for pullback_duration_weeks as a secondary residual.
tests.success_criterion: |paired median residual pullback_pct| > 5pp AND |paired median residual pullback_duration_weeks| > 1.5w (pullback retains independent information after removing vol/momentum regime).
tests.failure_criterion: |paired median residual pullback_pct| < 2pp AND |paired median residual pullback_duration_weeks| < 1w (pullback is mediator-only artifact; the researcher mechanism holds and reallocation of weight is justified).

tests.name: pullback_x_tape_signflip
tests.comparison: Within B0=true cases, split by up_day_ratio_20 median (0.55) AND vol_ratio_5_20 median (1.42) into four regime cells. In each cell compute median pullback_pct of false_positive_ruin vs selected_winner. Test for sign-flip of the (ruin - winner) pullback_pct gap across the four cells; require >=2 cells with opposite-signed gaps exceeding 4pp magnitude.
tests.success_criterion: Sign-flip confirmed (Kruskal-Wallis on regime-interaction term p<0.1) AND |gap| > 4pp in at least two cells with opposite signs -> pullback semantics are a regime-conditioned marker, not a direct signal (supports skeptic's regime-marker interpretation).
tests.failure_criterion: Gap direction is consistent across all four cells (Kruskal-Wallis p>0.3) AND |gap| < 3pp everywhere -> pullback carries a stable direct effect that is NOT vol/momentum-mediated (researcher's epiphenomenon claim is wrong).

leakage_checks: Confirm every feature is computed at or before snapshot timestamp; reject the test if pullback_pct or pullback_duration_weeks is derived from any price observation after the snapshot's date (PIT violation via forward-window pullback).

Confirm W4_return_bucket, outcome_label, and labels are used ONLY as the dependent variable, never as inputs to the matched-pair or interaction regressions (circular-label leakage flagged by the skeptic must be structurally excluded).

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The 'dry pullback' semantic is a conjunctive 3-dimensional construct (shallow depth × short duration × below-trend volume-during-pullback) but the available evidence schema captures only 1.5 dimensions: pullback_pct (full) and pullback_duration_weeks (partial, ~50% NULL). The 'dryness' qualifier — the volume-during-pullback-relative-to-pre-pullback ratio — is entirely absent; vol_ratio_5_20 is a snapshot-level feature that conflates pre-pullback vol expansion with pullback-specific dryness and therefore cannot stand in for it. Consequently, the Researcher's epiphenomenon claim and the Skeptic's mediator rebuttal are both arguing about a reduced-form 2D shadow of a 3D construct. Worse, the pullback_NULL subset (≈50% of B0 picks, including 4/6 of the strongest winners and 4/8 ruins) is not a missing-data problem to be imputed but a structurally different population — 'vol-expansion-without-pullback' names that ran away before a pullback could form — and pooling it with the pullback_observed subset in any contrast is the methodological root cause of both the Researcher's over-confident 'drop pullback' verdict and the Skeptic's equally over-confident 'UNRESOLVED because of missingness' verdict. A second-order problem: the Experimental Designer's matched-pair test is proposed on the pullback_observed subset (effective n≈13, with Mahalanobis tolerance yielding perhaps 5-7 viable pairs), giving paired-Wilcoxon power ≈0.4 to detect a 5pp median shift at α=0.05 — so the test is biased toward returning 'failure_criterion met' regardless of the true effect, meaning even a clean execution of the proposed protocol cannot resolve the question.
falsifiers: Compute pullback_volume_ratio = (median daily volume in pullback weeks) / (median daily volume in the 4 calendar weeks immediately preceding pullback onset) for every B0 pick with non-null pullback_pct; if, after controlling for vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20, this feature's standardized delta is <0.3 across the ≈13 observed cases AND it shows no sign-flip interaction with up_day_ratio_20, the 'dryness' semantic is empirically empty and the Researcher's epiphenomenon claim becomes default-true.

Run the matched-pair residual test on the pullback_observed subset ONLY (n≈13), but require power-calibrated minimum detectable effect of ≥8pp paired pullback_pct residual (not 5pp) and a binomial ruin-vs-win split of ≤60/40 within pairs; if both bounds are met, the regime-marker interpretation is supported and pullback semantics must be condition-gated, not dropped wholesale.

Stratify B0 picks into pullback_observed vs pullback_NULL cells and re-estimate vol_ratio_5_20's standardized delta within each cell separately; if the delta shrinks substantially (≥30% relative drop) within the pullback_NULL cell relative to the pooled estimate, the Researcher's claim that 'vol/mom dominate by 1.5-1.9x' is a population-mix artifact from conflating the two cells, and the 'vol/mom dominance' conclusion partially collapses.

Check temporal confounding: replicate the full contrast on a snapshot-stratified subsample that excludes snap_71486ed83c and snap_d0d57b1e40 (which together contribute 9/27 cases); if the pullback_pct standardized delta changes sign or magnitude by ≥0.4 std between the full sample and this date-balanced subsample, all prior contrast-based conclusions are regime-confounded and the verdict remains UNRESOLVED regardless of any matched-pair result on the full sample.

Construct a synthetic 'dry' label using the existing snapshot data (e.g., define dry := pullback_pct between -3% and -10% AND up_day_ratio_20 ≥ 0.5 AND vol_ratio_5_20 ≤ 1.4) and measure forward W4 return against the residual; if this constructed dry subset shows ruin rate within ±5pp of the B0-selected median, the operational definition of 'dry' is too loose to be load-bearing, and the original claim must be re-specified before any further test is informative.
actionable_design_principles: Never pool pullback_observed and pullback_NULL B0 picks in a single contrast; they are different populations (post-pullback consolidation vs pre-pullback breakout continuation) and pooling them is the root cause of every conclusion drawn so far. All future analyses must split on pullback_status as a first-class stratum.

Separate the gating question ('should presence/absence of an observed pullback be a hard filter?') from the weighting question ('how much should pullback_pct count in the within-observed-pullback scoring model?'). The evidence is sufficient to test the gating question (it is a population-selection effect, not a feature effect) but is NOT sufficient to test the weighting question without a new feature and a larger sample.

Construct pullback_volume_ratio (volume-during-pullback / volume-pre-pullback) in the snapshot ETL before any further debate about whether to drop or retain pullback semantics; without this feature the 'dry' qualifier is undefined in evidence and the question is structurally UNRESOLVED.

Pre-register the minimum detectable effect for any matched-pair test on the pullback_observed subset; given effective n≈13 with Mahalanobis matching, report power alongside the test result so that 'failure to reject' is not misread as 'evidence of null effect'.

When evaluating a feature with 50% structural NULLs, never report a single-feature standardized delta as if it were comparable to a fully-observed feature's delta; either report effective-n-adjusted confidence intervals or restrict the contrast to the observed subset with explicit sample-size disclosure.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Add a `requires_pullback_volume_ratio` declaration to the B0 scoring model schema; any model that references `pullback_pct` or `pullback_duration_weeks` as inputs must also declare a `pullback_volume_ratio` input sourced from the snapshot ETL, and the model is rejected at compile time if the feature is missing.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This is a structural enforcement of the 'dry' qualifier rather than a runtime check; it prevents the existing research failure mode in which a 3D construct is tested via a 1.5D proxy and the missing dimension is silently ignored.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Adds one new derived feature to the snapshot ETL and a schema-level constraint to the model DSL; does not change runtime scoring capacity but eliminates an entire class of silently-incorrect inferences.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Add a routing rule that partitions B0 picks into two scoring paths at evaluation time: `pullback_observed_path` (uses pullback_pct, pullback_duration_weeks, pullback_volume_ratio jointly) and `vol_expansion_no_pullback_path` (uses vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, up_day_ratio_20 only, with no pullback features permitted as inputs). The final score is a path-conditional output, not a pooled linear combination.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Unlike a pooled linear model with pullback features set to NULL-imputed values, this routing prevents the pullback_NULL population from contaminating the coefficient estimates of the pullback_observed population and vice versa; it makes the population-mix artifact structurally impossible rather than statistically detectable.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Requires the DSL to support conditional path evaluation; doubles the number of effective scoring models but each path operates on a cleaner population and can be trained on roughly half the data with sharper coefficients.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Add a snapshot-stratified audit log that, for every B0 pick, records (i) pullback_status ∈ {observed, null, shallow, deep}, (ii) the matched selected_winner entity's pullback_status, (iii) vol_ratio_5_20 and mom_20 at snapshot, and (iv) the snapshot date. This log enables the matched-pair and temporal-confounding falsifiers to be executed as scheduled re-tests rather than as one-off analyses, and surfaces date-clustering problems automatically.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This is observability infrastructure rather than a model change; it converts a static 27-case archaeology into a continuously-refreshable diagnostic that can detect when the population mix drifts over time.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Storage-only addition; no impact on scoring latency or model capacity, but enables falsifier #2 (matched-pair) and falsifier #4 (temporal confounding) to be re-run on every refresh without manual re-extraction.

cycles.question: Adversarially attack the benefit of distinct-1 diversification: construct the strongest alternative explanation. Prefer a concrete diagnostic over generic caution.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The benefit attributed to distinct-1 diversification is a confound with base-maturity quality, not an independent diversification effect. 'Distinct-1' labels proxy for stocks that have completed longer (base_duration_weeks median 52 vs 44) and slightly deeper bases (base_depth_pct median -29.5 vs -25.8). The numeric_contrasts table shows base_duration carries a standardized delta of -0.42 between false negatives and selected winners, comparable in magnitude to many of the surface-level technical features (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20). Once base quality is controlled for, distinct-1 should contribute zero marginal information; worse, enforcing distinct-1 as a portfolio constraint can force inclusion of inferior-base names to satisfy the 'distinctness' rule, diluting alpha.
evidence_for: 6 of 8 false_positive_ruin cases have null pullback_duration_weeks and null pullback_pct, indicating they never formed a proper corrective base — these are 'no-pullback extended' entries, not distinct-1 setups that failed on quality

Selected winners median pullback_pct is -15.9% vs -7.3% for false negatives (standardized delta +0.64), showing the surviving winners had substantially deeper, more corrective bases regardless of distinct-1 status
base_mbox_count median is 4.0 for false negatives vs 3.5 for selected winners — more choppy/wobbly bases correlate with skipping, suggesting base quality (not pattern distinctness) is the gatekeeper

Entity 6618d3e80c carries a dual label (false_positive_ruin|selected_winner) with vol_ratio_5_20=1.45 and px_vs_ma50=0.337 — the same setup produces both outcomes, implying base-quality thresholds (not distinctness) decide the label

The standardized deltas in numeric_contrasts rank up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), mom_20 (-1.00), px_vs_ma50 (-0.85) as top separators — none of these are 'distinct-1' attributes; they are all snapshot-quality descriptors

False negatives entity_de1c657364 (8-week pullback, -7.3%, big winner) and entity_535a1beed7 (no pullback, mom_20=0.028, large win) show that 'weak-base' snapshots occasionally produce large winners, undermining the implicit assumption that distinct-1 = base-quality
evidence_against: Sample is only n=27 with heavy missingness on pullback fields (≥8 nulls), too small to disentangle distinct-1 from base-quality via partial correlation

Selected winners are heterogeneous in pullback depth (entity_440e297253: -1.5% over 3 weeks vs entity_2c58cebc59: -25.1% over 6 weeks vs entity_3adc078f01: -42.3% over 9 weeks), so 'base quality' itself is multi-dimensional and not a single latent variable

Distinct-1 could still capture a real regime feature: stocks emerging from a first base after a long run often have different sector/market-cap exposure, providing genuine correlation reduction even after base-quality matching

The method_note defines false negatives relative to B0 selected medians, which embeds the distinct-1 / B0 selection logic into the outcome label itself — partial circularity that makes the 'confound' interpretation hard to refute from this evidence alone
falsifiable_predictions: In a hold-out of ≥200 breakout candidates, regressing W4 return on (base_depth_pct, base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count, mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20) plus a distinct-1 dummy will yield a partial R² for the distinct-1 dummy below 0.005 and a t-stat below 1.0

Within base-quality deciles, the cross-sectional dispersion of forward returns will not be lower for portfolios constructed under a distinct-1 constraint than for unconstrained same-quality portfolios, and the ruin rate difference will be inside the 95% bootstrap CI

Pairwise return correlations between distinct-1 cohort members will be statistically indistinguishable from correlations between randomly chosen same-base-quality non-distinct-1 members, with |Δρ| < 0.05 over rolling 13-week windows

Replacing the distinct-1 rule with a 'longest-base-wins' tiebreaker will produce a higher information ratio (predicted Δ ≥ 0.15) on the same discovery/train sample, with the improvement concentrated in names that the distinct-1 rule forced in (mom_20 < 0.05 cluster)

Drawdown depth during broad market selloffs (e.g., >-7% SPX weeks) will be similar across distinct-1 and matched-quality non-distinct-1 baskets, falsifying the claim that distinct-1 provides independent tail-risk hedging
policy_implications: Drop distinct-1 as a portfolio-construction primitive; replace with an explicit base-quality score (depth + duration + mbox_count + rs slope) and diversify across base-quality deciles rather than across pattern distinctness

If the diagnostic above shows distinct-1 is null, the current 'diversification' label is masking a base-quality bet and misleading risk attribution — reclassify the strategy as concentrated base-quality exposure

Implement a paired test in the next live cycle: run two parallel sleeves (distinct-1 constrained vs base-quality constrained with same expected position count) and compare realized Sharpe, max DD, and ruin rate over ≥40 trades per sleeve

Re-examine the 'no-pullback' subset (null pullback fields) — this is where 6/8 false positives cluster and where base quality fails to discriminate; consider a separate 'extended-entry' sub-strategy with tighter stops rather than forcing it into the distinct-1 framework

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The base-maturity confound hypothesis is the wrong direction. The data shows base_duration_weeks is only the 12th strongest separator (standardized delta -0.42) while the top four separators (up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50) are all snapshot-phase descriptors that are themselves downstream of 'first-base emergence.' The null-pullback cluster (6/8 false_positive_ruin with null pullback fields) is the EXACT regime distinct-1 is designed to filter, not the regime it should be judged on. The prior claim reverses causation: shallower subsequent pullbacks in winners are not a cause of correlation reduction, they are a downstream symptom of the same regime (fresh first-base emergence after dormancy/IPO) that drives the diversification. Treating base-depth as the 'true' driver is treating a proxy for a proxy.

attacks.issue: Ranking inversion: if base-maturity were the active ingredient, base_duration_weeks and base_depth_pct should be top-3 separators. They rank 12th and 11th respectively. The top four are all point-in-time momentum/participation features that are causally antecedent to base maturity, not downstream of it.
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher's whole confound story depends on base features dominating; if they are weaker than snapshot features, the natural alternative is that distinct-1 is a phase/regime label that *contains* the momentum information rather than being explained by base structure.

attacks.issue: Survivorship asymmetry: failure archaeology only observes errors. The silent successes (estimated 70-85% of B0 picks) are invisible. Distinct-1's primary benefit may be in the bulk, not in the error tail. A n=27 error sample cannot reject a real but modest effect concentrated in successful names.
attacks.why_it_matters: A negative finding on the error sample is consistent with distinct-1 working perfectly on the silent majority. The prior treats error archaeology as if it were a random sample of the strategy; it is not.

attacks.issue: Null-pullback cases are mis-classified as 'not distinct-1 setups.' Six of eight false_positive_ruin cases have null pullback fields precisely because they are in an 'extended no-base' regime. These are the canonical pattern that distinct-1 SHOULD exclude, and their presence as is_b0_pick=true (7/8) is evidence the system ALREADY had them in — i.e., that distinct-1 filtering is needed but not applied in the failure cases.
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher treats the null-pullback cluster as evidence against distinct-1, but it is actually a positive existence proof: the system is failing on the exact regime where distinct-1 is supposed to operate. A correct interpretation is 'distinct-1 was not enforced strictly enough,' not 'distinct-1 does not work.'

attacks.issue: Base_duration is a noisy proxy that conflates structurally different regimes. A 52-week 'maturing base approaching breakout' and a 52-week 'sideways chop that almost-formed-a-base' receive the same label. The +8-week median difference between false negatives and winners is well within this proxy's measurement noise floor.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the base-duration variable is itself a noisy proxy for 'true' base quality, then using it as the 'controlled-for' feature in the confound argument is not neutral — the confounder absorbs its own noise and the residual can look null even when distinct-1 is doing real work.

attacks.issue: Falsifiable prediction #1 (partial R² for distinct-1 dummy < 0.005 with t < 1.0) is calibrated to reject a real but modest effect. A genuine regime indicator in cross-sectional return regressions typically explains 0.3-0.8% of variance — below the proposed threshold. The prediction is structured to pass on a finding of zero rather than to discriminate between competing magnitudes.
attacks.why_it_matters: The prior's own diagnostic is asymmetric. A skeptic should demand a two-sided test: if the null is R²=0.005-0.01, the prior prediction cannot reject, and the conclusion 'no effect' would itself be poorly supported.

attacks.issue: The 'replace distinct-1 with longest-base-wins' proposal is biased toward older/worn-out bases. Fresh first-base breakouts (the very population distinct-1 targets) systematically have SHORTER base durations than second/third-base continuations. A longest-base rule would systematically underweight the distinct-1 population, so even if the proposal 'won' the comparison, it would not isolate the relevant counterfactual.
attacks.why_it_matters: The proposed counterfactual is not apples-to-apples; it stacks the deck. A proper test would be 'shortest-mature-base-wins' or 'freshest-pattern-wins,' which would also lose to distinct-1 for the same reason but more honestly.

attacks.issue: The researcher concedes that selected winners are heterogeneous in pullback depth (-1.5% to -42.3%) and treats this as evidence base quality is multi-dimensional. The alternative reading: these winners are heterogeneous because distinct-1 captures a regime indicator that allows BOTH shallow pullbacks (strong-trend continuation) and deep pullbacks (post-correction first-base). The heterogeneity is the diversification working, not a confound.
attacks.why_it_matters: If winners cluster into a low-correlation set precisely because they span different pullback regimes, distinct-1 is doing the work the researcher is trying to attribute to base quality. The diversity is the effect, not noise around it.

counterexamples_to_seek: Selected winners with base_duration_weeks > 60 (very long base) that underperform — would refute the 'longer base = better' version of the prior's mechanism and force a retreat to 'deeper base = better,' which is even weaker in the data

False_positive_ruin cases WITH non-null pullback fields (currently 2/8) — let us compare base_depth between failed and winning names within the SAME pullback regime, removing the null-cluster confounder

Sector/market-cap distribution of distinct-1 winners vs the broader B0 candidate pool. If distinct-1 winners are disproportionately in a sector or cap bucket that has lower correlation with the index, the diversification benefit is real but the prior is mis-attributing it to base features

Time-series rolling 13-week correlations: distinct-1 cohort vs non-distinct-1 cohort during SPX-trending vs SPX-choppy weeks. A regime indicator predicts lower correlation in choppy regimes; a quality proxy predicts similar correlation in both

Entity-level base-maturity trajectory: does mom_20 at entry LEAD or LAG base_duration_weeks? If lead, the snapshot features are causal and base features are downstream; if lag, the researcher's directionality might be right

The two false_negative_big_winner cases (entity_de1c657364, entity_535a1beed7) — both with weak pullback but large wins. Are their base features similar to distinct-1 winners? If yes, they should have been included; the fact they were excluded is the real failure mode, not the distinct-1 rule itself
what_would_change_my_mind: A matched-pairs analysis on n≥200 with exact matching on (base_duration_weeks within ±2 weeks, base_depth_pct within ±2pp, base_mbox_count, sector, market_cap_bucket) showing that within matched pairs, distinct-1 vs non-distinct-1 W4 returns are statistically indistinguishable (p > 0.5) AND ruin rates are within bootstrap CI

Demonstration that the distinct-1 cohort's average pairwise correlation with the non-distinct-1 B0 cohort exceeds 0.70 on rolling 13-week windows, and that the cross-correlation of the distinct-1 cohort with the SPX is NOT statistically different from the non-distinct-1 cohort's beta

Bootstrap CI on the base_duration standardized delta that excludes the range [-0.6, -0.3] — i.e., evidence the effect is both statistically real and substantially larger than the snapshot-feature effects. Currently the -0.42 estimate is too small and too noisy to dominate

A finding that within the discovery-train sample, the B0 pick rate conditional on base-quality decile is FLAT across deciles (i.e., base quality is not the selection criterion). This would invalidate the prior's claim that B0 selection is 'really' a base-quality filter

A backtest showing that a portfolio constructed WITHOUT any distinct-1 constraint but with an explicit base-quality score (depth + duration + mbox_count) achieves a HIGHER information ratio than the current distinct-1 rule over ≥200 trades with realistic transaction costs. Until this is shown, the confound hypothesis remains unproven

tests.name: Within-base-maturity strata, do snapshot-phase features still predict outcome?
tests.comparison: Stratify the 27 cases into base_duration_weeks tertiles. Within each tertile, compute median mom_20 for false_positive_ruin vs selected_winner. Researcher predicts mom_20 median gap collapses to <0.03 within every tertile. Skeptic predicts gap persists at >0.08 in at least one tertile.
tests.success_criterion: mom_20 median gap within every base_duration tertile is < 0.03 AND standardized gap < 0.3 (researcher wins: base-maturity fully explains the snapshot separation).
tests.failure_criterion: In any base_duration tertile, mom_20 gap remains >= 0.08 OR standardized gap >= 0.6 (skeptic wins: snapshot-phase info is independent of base maturity).

tests.name: Null-pullback cluster dissection: is the ruin-mode driven by snapshot quality or by lack of base?
tests.comparison: Among is_b0_pick=true cases, compare the 8 false_positive_ruin cases against the 11 selected_winner cases on a composite snapshot score = mean of (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20). Also split the 8 ruins into 6 with null pullback_pct vs 2 with non-null pullback_pct. Skeptic predicts snapshot composite separates ruin from winner within the null-pullback subset; researcher predicts it does not because the null-pullback group is structurally a different regime that no snapshot feature can rescue.
tests.success_criterion: Snapshot composite median for the 6 null-pullback ruins is within 0.5 SD of selected_winner median (i.e., the null-pullback ruins were not distinguishable by snapshot features, supporting the 'distinct-1 should have excluded them' reading).
tests.failure_criterion: Snapshot composite median for the 6 null-pullback ruins is >= 1.0 SD below selected_winner median (i.e., the ruins WERE low-snapshot-quality and a snapshot gate would have caught them, undermining the 'distinct-1 is needed' reading).

tests.name: Causality direction: does mom_20 at entry lead or lag base_duration_weeks?
tests.comparison: Test whether mom_60 + ma20_slope_5 jointly predict base_duration_weeks (researcher's direction: snapshot features -> base maturity) vs whether base_duration_weeks + base_depth_pct predict mom_20 (skeptic's direction: base maturity -> snapshot features). Use Spearman rank correlation on the 27 cases. Researcher predicts mom_60|ma20_slope_5 -> base_duration partial rho > 0.30. Skeptic predicts base_duration -> mom_20 partial rho > 0.30.
tests.success_criterion: Partial Spearman |rho| between mom_60 + ma20_slope_5 and base_duration_weeks (controlling for the other side) exceeds 0.30 in the direction mom_60 -> base_duration.
tests.failure_criterion: Reverse direction holds, OR both partial rhos are < 0.20 (i.e., no detectable causal ordering and the confound claim becomes unprovable from PIT features alone -> UNRESOLVED).

leakage_checks: Do not use is_b0_pick, w4_return_bucket, or outcome_label as a predictive feature; they are ground-truth labels and would leak the selection mechanism under test.
Do not use snapshot_anon or entity_anon as features; they are identity/cluster labels, not PIT market descriptors.

Do not use pullback_duration_weeks or pullback_pct as predictors in Test 2 (null-pullback cluster) — their nullness IS the regime being studied, so using them to predict inside the null subset would be circular.
priority_order: Within-base-maturity strata, do snapshot-phase features still predict outcome?
Null-pullback cluster dissection: is the ruin-mode driven by snapshot quality or by lack of base?
Causality direction: does mom_20 at entry lead or lag base_duration_weeks?

synthesizer.mechanism_summary: The distinct-1 benefit cannot be cleanly assigned to either 'base-maturity confound' (researcher) or 'regime indicator with independent information' (skeptic) from the available evidence, because the n=27 error-archaeology sample simultaneously satisfies three constraints that favor each interpretation and violates one critical assumption (base features rank only 11th-12th as separators, while snapshot-phase features rank top four). The null-pullback cluster (6/8 false_positive_ruin cases with null pullback fields) is the single strongest empirical regularity and is interpretable both ways: (a) it is exactly the regime distinct-1 was supposed to filter, so its failure rate is evidence the rule was not enforced strictly enough; (c) it represents a structurally different 'extended no-base' regime where base-quality controls cannot help and a distinct-1 gate is orthogonal. The selected-winners heterogeneity in pullback depth (-1.5% to -42.3%) is consistent with BOTH 'distinct-1 captures a regime that spans multiple base depths' (skeptic) and 'base quality is multi-dimensional and the single base_duration proxy is too coarse to capture it' (researcher). The survivorship asymmetry (only error archaeology visible) means a real but modest distinct-1 effect in the silent majority is invisible to the diagnostic. The causal direction (does mom_20 lead or lag base_duration_weeks?) is empirically resolvable but has not been tested. Net: distinct-1 is at minimum partially confounded with base-maturity, at maximum an independent regime label whose true effect is unestimable from errors alone.
falsifiers: RESEARCHER WINS if, within base_duration_weeks tertiles, the mom_20 median gap between false_positive_ruin and selected_winner collapses to <0.03 in EVERY tertile (Test 1 success criterion) AND the partial Spearman between mom_60+ma20_slope_5 and base_duration_weeks controlling for the reverse direction is <0.20 (Test 3 ambiguity). Under that result, base-maturity fully mediates the snapshot separation and distinct-1 has zero marginal information.

SKEPTIC WINS if, within base_duration_weeks tertiles, mom_20 gap remains >=0.08 in at least one tertile (Test 1 failure criterion) AND the partial Spearman from mom_60+ma20_slope_5 to base_duration_weeks exceeds 0.30 (Test 3 success criterion). Under that result, snapshot features are causally antecedent and distinct-1 captures leading regime information not reducible to base proxies.

BOTH LOSE (mechanism becomes genuinely UNRESOLVED) if base-maturity strata show heterogeneous results across tertiles (gap collapses in one tertile, persists in another) AND causality direction is indeterminate with both partial rhos <0.20. This would imply the relationship is non-monotonic and base-maturity is not a sufficient statistic for the underlying latent variable.

RESEARCHER'S CONFOUND REVERSES if a matched-pairs analysis on n>=200 with exact matching on (base_duration_weeks +/-2w, base_depth_pct +/-2pp, base_mbox_count, sector, cap_bucket) shows distinct-1 vs non-distinct-1 W4 returns are statistically indistinguishable (p>0.5) AND ruin rates within bootstrap CI. This is the cleanest test but requires a sample roughly 7x the current one.

SKEPTIC'S REGIME CLAIM SOLIDIFIES if the distinct-1 cohort's rolling 13-week pairwise correlations with non-distinct-1 B0 cohort average below 0.70 AND cross-correlation with SPX is statistically different from the non-distinct-1 cohort's beta, during choppy-regime weeks. This would prove distinct-1 acts as a regime diversifier independent of base features.

EXPERIMENTAL DESIGNER'S NULL-PULLBACK DISSECTION is the single highest-value test: if the 6 null-pullback ruin cases have snapshot-composite median within 0.5 SD of selected_winner median, distinct-1 is NOT reducible to a snapshot gate (skeptic gains ground); if their composite is >=1.0 SD below, distinct-1 IS replaceable by snapshot gating (researcher gains ground).
actionable_design_principles: Do NOT adopt either narrative as policy. The 'distinct-1 = base-maturity confound' story cannot be confirmed because base features rank poorly (11th-12th) and the 'longest-base-wins' replacement proposed by the researcher is structurally biased against the fresh first-base population distinct-1 targets. The 'distinct-1 = regime indicator with silent-majority effects' story cannot be confirmed because only error archaeology is visible and n=27 cannot reject modest magnitudes in the bulk.

Run the experimental designer's three tests on the FULL candidate pool (not just the n=27 error set) before changing live policy. Until then, treat both readings as live hypotheses and avoid irreversible commitments to either sleeve design.

Decouple portfolio-construction effects from selection-quality effects. The question 'does distinct-1 diversify the portfolio?' is mechanically different from 'does distinct-1 select better names?' and the failure archaeology only speaks to the latter. A distinct-1 constraint can win or lose on correlation-reduction grounds even when it has zero selection alpha.

Treat the null-pullback cluster (currently 6/8 false positives) as a SEPARATE REGIME with its own risk model, not as evidence for or against distinct-1. These cases fail because they entered without a corrective base; neither a distinct-1 rule nor a base-duration gate reliably rescues them, but a regime-specific stop/tightening rule might.

Require any replacement rule to be expressed as a CAPACITY-NEUTRAL counterfactual: same expected position count, same sector/cap exposure, same turnover. The researcher's 'longest-base-wins' and the skeptic's 'silent-majority argument' both fail this test (one biases toward worn-out bases, the other relies on unobservable bulk).

Add an explicit snapshot-quality composite (z-scored mean of up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50) as a PARALLEL gate that runs alongside distinct-1, not as a replacement. Coincident gating decisions (both agree to exclude) become high-confidence rejections; conflicting decisions (distinct-1 says keep, snapshot says skip, or vice versa) become the regime boundary where alpha lives.

Stop using outcome_label definitions that embed the distinct-1 / B0 selection logic into the label itself. The method_note creates partial circularity ('false negative relative to B0 selected median') that prevents any PIT feature from fully refuting the confound hypothesis. Reframe outcomes as forward returns and base-quality separately.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Within-base-maturity strata, conditional snapshot-quality veto: if mom_20 z-score (vs base_duration tertile median) is below -1.0 AND vol_ratio_5_20 z-score is below -0.5, exclude the candidate regardless of distinct-1 status. This operationalizes Test 1 directly: within-base strata, snapshot quality still separates ruin.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Implements a within-strata conditional gate that the experimental designer specified but the researcher and skeptic both talked around. Crucially, it does NOT replace distinct-1; it adds an additional filter that activates only in the snapshot-poor, base-acceptable quadrant.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Neutral — fires only inside the within-base tertile where snapshot quality is depressed; expected to filter 10-20% of B0 candidates without changing portfolio count materially.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Null-pullback separate regime flag: when pullback_duration_weeks IS NULL AND pullback_pct IS NULL, route the candidate to an extended-entry sub-strategy with a tighter trailing stop (e.g., -5% vs -8%) rather than either admitting it under distinct-1 or excluding it via base-quality gate. This removes the 6/8 false_positive_ruin cluster from being interpretable as distinct-1 evidence in either direction.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Neutralizes the single most contested empirical observation in the failure archaeology. Without this routing, every analyst will continue to over-interpret the null-pullback cluster. With it, the cluster's ruin rate becomes a property of the extended-entry regime, not of distinct-1.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Neutral-to-positive. Routes ruin-prone candidates to a regime where they may still contribute return with tighter risk controls; capacity impact depends on null-pullback frequency in the broader pool (currently 6/27 in error set, ~30%+).

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Partial-Spearman causal ordering audit: compute partial rho between (mom_60 + ma20_slope_5) and base_duration_weeks, controlling for the reverse direction, on a rolling 26-week window. Publish the sign and magnitude as a regime indicator. If rho flips sign across windows, distinct-1's information content is regime-dependent and the policy should be regime-conditional.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Directly operationalizes Test 3 (causality direction) and turns the abstract 'who leads whom' question into an observable, monitorable signal. A regime-conditional policy is more defensible than a static one and prevents overcommitting to either the researcher's or skeptic's causal story.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Informational only — does not alter position count but changes which sleeve receives incremental capital based on the rolling rho sign.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Capacity-matched sleeve competition: run two parallel sub-portfolios for >=40 trades each — one with the current distinct-1 constraint, one with distinct-1 REPLACED by a base-quality composite (depth + duration + mbox_count, equal-weighted z-score). Keep expected position count and sector/cap exposure matched. Compare realized Sharpe, max DD, ruin rate, and rolling 13-week pairwise correlation with the parent portfolio.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Forces a falsifiable, capacity-neutral comparison that resolves the central dispute without the circularity of the existing outcome_label definitions. If the base-quality sleeve wins on Sharpe with similar ruin rate, the researcher's replacement rule gains a real (not theoretical) footing. If the distinct-1 sleeve wins on correlation-reduction with similar Sharpe, the skeptic's regime story is empirically grounded.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: High relevance — this is the cleanest test of whether distinct-1's claimed benefit is a portfolio-construction effect or a selection effect, and it can run on the existing sample base if at least 40 trades per sleeve are available over the next live cycle.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Snapshot-composite parallel gate: compute z-scored snapshot composite = mean(z(mom_20), z(vol_ratio_5_20), z(up_day_ratio_20), z(px_vs_ma50)) for every candidate. Require BOTH a distinct-1 distinctness check AND a snapshot-composite above the bottom decile to enter the portfolio. Coincident-fail exclusions become high-confidence rejections; distinct-1-pass-snapshot-fail and distinct-1-fail-snapshot-pass become flagged boundary cases for manual review.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: Implements Test 2's snapshot-composite comparison as a live policy rather than a post-hoc diagnostic. Crucially, it does NOT collapse distinct-1 into a snapshot gate (which is the researcher's strongest read of the data); it makes the two decisions visible side by side, so the policy can be re-tuned based on which quadrant produces the most ruination.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Moderate-to-neutral — adds a gate that should filter ~10% of B0 candidates and produces a structured boundary-case category (~5-15% of candidates) that requires review bandwidth.

cycles.question: Adversarially attack the proposed adaptive-capacity direction: construct the strongest alternative explanation. Prefer a concrete diagnostic over generic caution.

researcher.mechanism_claim: The 'adaptive-capacity' cluster (mom_20, px_vs_ma50, px_vs_ma20, ma10/20_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20) is a single latent factor—extension above base— NOT independent capacity signals. Winners and ruins are drawn from the same high-extension bucket; false-negative wins come from the low-extension region. The model is identifying 'extended-state,' not capacity, and within the extended bucket it cannot separate winner from ruin.
evidence_for: False positives (ruins) and selected_winners occupy overlapping high-extension space (mom_20 0.07–0.32, px_vs_ma50 0.05–0.34 fully overlap); entity_6618d3e80c carries a mixed selected_winner|false_positive_ruin label at extreme extension (px_vs_ma50=0.337), evidencing non-monotonicity.

False-negative winners are systematically LESS extended on every one of these proxies (mom_20 median 0.058 vs 0.163, px_vs_ma50 0.056 vs 0.127, up_day_ratio 0.50 vs 0.625, vol_ratio_5_20 1.18 vs 1.42) and shallower pullbacks (–7.3% vs –15.9%); their wins are mean-reversion from quiet bases, the opposite of capacity.
evidence_against: Ten features show consistent median deltas in the same direction with standardized magnitudes 0.5–1.2σ, which is unusual for pure collinearity and could reflect a real multivariate capacity construct rather than a single extension axis.

Selected_winners have deeper prior pullbacks (–15.9%) than false_negatives (–7.3%), suggesting 'capacity' may proxy 'worked-off extension' (capacity = extension + prior correction) rather than extension alone.
falsifiable_predictions: Restricting to entries with mom_20>0.15 AND px_vs_ma50>0.10, the within-bucket AUC for winner-vs-ruin using any monotonic composite of these features is ≤0.55 (vs the apparent cross-bucket AUC).
Replacing the extension cluster with a single 'pullback_pct ≤ –20% AND base_duration ≥ 40w' rule recovers ≥70% of the missing false-negative winners without raising within-bucket ruin rate above 30%.
policy_implications: Collapse the capacity feature set to one composite (extension z-score) and stop allocating research budget to incremental slope/momentum variants; redirect capacity to base-quality and relative-strength features that discriminate inside the extended bucket.

If the within-bucket AUC test fails, retire the 'adaptive-capacity' framing in factor documents and re-label the strategy as 'extension-tilted breakout,' which has different sizing and stop-loss implications.

skeptic.strongest_counterclaim: The 'adaptive-capacity' cluster is not a latent factor — it is IBD's own relative-strength / breakout-compliance filter, restated. Because the 'selected_winner' label is defined conditional on B0 having picked the name and 'false_negative_relative' is defined conditional on B0 NOT having picked it, any feature IBD's B0 already uses (px_vs_ma50, mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, base_duration) will mechanically separate the two groups by construction. The 0.5–1.2σ median deltas are the expected footprint of selection-on-labels bias plus pullback MNAR (missing-not-at-random pullback fields concentrated in false_negatives), not evidence of an independent capacity construct.

attacks.issue: Label-construction selection bias: 'capacity' cluster is B0's filter, not a new signal
attacks.why_it_matters: Every feature in the proposed cluster (mom_20, px_vs_ma50, px_vs_ma20, ma10/20_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, base_duration_weeks, base_mbox_count) is a textbook IBD-style relative-strength / momentum-thrust ingredient. The two outcome classes are conditioned on B0 pick status itself, so they are guaranteed to differ on B0's inputs. Regressing mom_20 or px_vs_ma50 on is_b0_pick alone across the 27 cases will absorb most of the cross-bucket separation; whatever residual remains is not 'capacity' but unexplained B0 noise. The direction is therefore not adding information — it is rediscovering the filter that defines the labels.

attacks.issue: Within-snapshot heterogeneity refutes cross-bucket capacity claims
attacks.why_it_matters: snap_71486ed83c alone contains entity_2c58cebc59 (selected_winner, large_win, mom_20=0.32) sitting next to entity_bfb308b24a (false_negative_relative, loss, mom_20=0.027) and entity_de1c657364 (false_negative_big_winner, large_win, mom_20=0.058). If capacity were the operative axis, these should not coexist at overlapping feature levels inside one regime. They do. The cross-bucket deltas are dominated by between-snapshot regime (bull vs bear / sector rotation), not by an entity-level capacity factor. Any capacity model trained on this set will mostly be fitting snapshot_anon under a different name.

attacks.issue: Pullback_pct / pullback_duration_weeks are MNAR — the 8.6pp delta is partly 'pullbacks that get recorded get selected'
attacks.why_it_matters: Selected_winners show populated pullback fields with deeper medians (-15.9%); many false_negatives have null pullback_pct / pullback_duration_weeks (entity_ead73f4390, 4fdc3699fd, 2f86543bf6, etc.). Stocks that never corrected meaningfully do not generate a pullback observation, so they are absent from the pullback comparison by construction. The 'deeper pullback = capacity' interpretation collapses if a pullback_present_indicator alone predicts the outcome label — i.e., if the mechanism is 'having a recorded pullback stage gates selection,' not 'depth of pullback = capacity to extend.' No imputation sensitivity (multiple plausible values for the nulls) has been reported.

attacks.issue: Mixed-label case entity_6618d3e80c is data-quality failure, not capacity non-monotonicity
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_6618d3e80c (snap_d0d57b1e40) carries BOTH 'false_positive_ruin' AND 'selected_winner' — same entity, same W4 window, opposite outcomes under the labeling sub-rule. At px_vs_ma50 = 0.337 (the dataset maximum) the label is structurally ambiguous, and using this row as 'evidence that capacity is non-monotonic at extreme extension' is misreading a labeling bug as a theoretical finding. Any model that takes capacity seriously must first resolve or exclude this point; the researcher cited it in the opposite direction without auditing the sub-label time-resolution.

attacks.issue: Multiple-testing inflation on a 27-case, 11-vs-7 comparison
attacks.why_it_matters: Twenty-plus features are reported; the top standardized delta is 1.19σ on up_day_ratio_20 with n=18 vs n=7. After Bonferroni over 20 tests the effective threshold is roughly 2.5σ — none of the reported deltas clear it. The '10 features move in the same direction' claim is precisely what you expect when features are correlated and you report the consistent subset. With this sample size and this feature count, the cluster is statistically indistinguishable from correlated noise around the B0 filter.

counterexamples_to_seek: Within snap_71486ed83c and snap_d0d57b1e40, find any pair (one selected_winner, one false_negative_relative) whose mom_20 differs by <0.05 AND px_vs_ma50 differs by <0.03 — these are within-snapshot matched pairs that falsify 'capacity separates winners.'
Run pullback_present_indicator → outcome_label as a single-feature model; if AUC > 0.65 the pullback depth delta is just an MNAR proxy for 'having a recorded base,' not a capacity signal.

Decompose entity_6618d3e80c's W4 sub-path: what fraction of the four weeks triggered ruin vs winner sub-rules? If the mixed label is a time-resolution artifact (week-by-week reversal), the entire high-extension tail of the dataset is unreliable.

Regress each of the 10 cluster features on is_b0_pick alone across the 27 cases. If the marginal R² of the cluster exceeds 0.5, the direction is empirically redundant with B0 and adds nothing the model doesn't already have.

For each false_negative_relative entity, look up the IBD 'near-pick' from the same snapshot — does capacity discriminate between the picked and un-picked name within the snapshot? If not, capacity is between-snapshot regime in disguise.
what_would_change_my_mind: A within-snapshot, Mahalanobis-matched analysis showing the capacity cluster still separates selected_winners from false_negative_relatives at p < 0.05 after stratifying by snapshot_anon and using only snapshot-internal variance — this would rule out the regime-confound explanation.

Identification of even one predictive feature that is NOT in IBD's B0 toolkit (e.g., sector-relative RS, options skew, share-turnover percentile, institutional-flow divergence) showing a >0.7σ Bonferroni-corrected delta — this would prove capacity is not just B0's filter restated.

A multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis on the null pullback fields showing the 8.6pp pullback_pct delta survives under at least three plausible imputation models (e.g., MAR with base_depth_pct as predictor, worst-case flat imputation, hot-deck by sector).

A label-decomposition audit of entity_6618d3e80c and any other mixed-label rows demonstrating the W4 sub-rule conflict is a time-resolution artifact resolvable by weekly re-labeling — without this, the high-extension tail of every capacity claim is contaminated.

Replication on a held-out snapshot set (not in the 27 discovery rows) where the capacity composite's AUC for winner-vs-ruin within the extended bucket exceeds 0.60 — the researcher's own falsifiable prediction #1 stated ≤0.55, so seeing >0.60 out-of-sample would force retraction of this counterclaim.

tests.name: within_snapshot_capacity_discrimination
tests.comparison: Within each snapshot_anon stratum that contains >=1 selected_winner and >=1 false_negative_relative, compute a 3-feature z-score composite of mom_20, px_vs_ma50, vol_ratio_5_20; average the per-snapshot AUC for selected_winner vs false_negative_relative across strata. Snapshot_anon is used only as a stratification identifier, never as a predictor.
tests.success_criterion: Stratified-average AUC ≥ 0.65 with at least 3 contributing strata (supports capacity as a within-regime latent factor).
tests.failure_criterion: Stratified-average AUC ≤ 0.55 OR fewer than 3 strata contain both outcome classes (capacity is between-snapshot regime noise; the 0.5–1.2σ deltas dissolve once regime is held constant).

tests.name: b0_filter_redundancy_decomposition
tests.comparison: Across the 27 discovery rows, regress the 3-feature cluster composite (z-scored) on is_b0_pick as a single binary regressor; report adjusted R² and the residual AUC of the composite for outcome_label after partialling out is_b0_pick.
tests.success_criterion: Adjusted R² < 0.30 AND residual AUC within 0.05 of unadjusted AUC (cluster carries information orthogonal to B0's pick decision).
tests.failure_criterion: Adjusted R² ≥ 0.50 OR residual AUC drops by ≥ 0.10 after partialling out is_b0_pick (the cluster is the B0 filter restated; capacity direction is empirically redundant with the existing model).

tests.name: within_extended_bucket_auc_researcher_pred1
tests.comparison: Restrict to rows with mom_20 > 0.15 AND px_vs_ma50 > 0.10 (the extended bucket); compute AUC for selected_winner vs false_positive_ruin using the 3-feature composite. Mirrors the researcher's falsifiable prediction #1 with explicit feature budget.
tests.success_criterion: Within-bucket AUC ≥ 0.60 (capacity discriminates winners from ruins inside the extended bucket).
tests.failure_criterion: Within-bucket AUC ≤ 0.55 (researcher's own threshold is breached; capacity direction collapses to extension-tilted breakout with no within-bucket discrimination).

tests.name: pullback_present_vs_depth_discrimination
tests.comparison: Construct a derived pullback_present_indicator (= 1 if pullback_pct is non-null, else 0); compare (a) pullback_present_indicator alone predicting selected_winner vs false_negative_relative, (b) pullback_pct conditional on presence, (c) three null-imputation scenarios for pullback_pct: worst-case flat (0), hot-deck by base_depth_pct quartile, and multiple-imputation MAR using base_depth_pct + base_duration_weeks as predictors.
tests.success_criterion: Conditional pullback_pct AUC exceeds pullback_present_indicator AUC by ≥ 0.10 AND the 8.6pp median delta survives all three imputation scenarios within ±3pp.
tests.failure_criterion: pullback_present_indicator AUC ≥ 0.65 OR the median delta reverses sign under any imputation scenario (pullback depth is an MNAR proxy for 'having a recorded base stage,' not an independent capacity feature).

tests.name: mixed_label_entity_exclusion_sensitivity
tests.comparison: Recompute the within-extended-bucket AUC (researcher prediction #1) and the within-snapshot AUC (test 1) with and without entity_6618d3e80c (the snap_d0d57b1e40 row carrying the dual 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' label at the dataset-maximum px_vs_ma50 = 0.337).
